    Clean-room statement. This specification describes features, workflows and behaviour in Reviera's own words. Every input was publicly available: vendor online help, public blogs and tutorials, public forums and open-source repositories. All of it is listed with URLs and access checks in SOURCE_REGISTER.md. No proprietary, confidential, leaked or NDA-covered information was used. No vendor code, binaries, file formats or assets were examined or copied. Autodesk and Revit are trademarks of Autodesk, Inc. They are used here only to identify the functional reference. Reviera is not affiliated with or endorsed by Autodesk.

    0.1 Purpose and Scope

    Reviera is a parametric Building Information Modeling (BIM) authoring application for architecture, structural and MEP design, documentation and coordination. Its goal is functional parity with the main workflows of the reference product. It is built on open standards and open-source components:

    • Open data: IFC is the native file format, with no proprietary container.
    • Open collaboration: it can run as a client of the Open Source BIMserver.
    • Open automation: every operation can be driven from Lua scripts and by AI agents through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
    • Open licence: GPL-3.0-or-later.

    This document covers:

    Chapter Content
    0 Overview, architecture, glossary, requirement conventions, roadmap (this chapter)
    1 User interface shell
    2 Data model, families, parameters, project setup, file I/O, extensibility (Lua, add-ins, MCP)
    2a Reviera Extension Data (RXD): bespoke format and IFC embedding
    2b Live model store (SQLite) and crash recovery
    3 Architectural modeling and editing tools
    4 Structure, steel, concrete/precast, MEP systems, analysis
    5 Views, graphics, annotation, schedules, sheets, output
    6 Collaboration, linking and coordination (Local and BIMserver modes)
    7 Advanced features beyond the reference product: scene protocol, simulated walkthroughs, Godot translation layer for VR/AR, render bridges
    A Appendix A: requirement summary, shared commands, consolidated command index (1,938 commands; 762 requirements)

    Out of scope: - reproducing vendor-cloud services such as ACC/Forma and Autodesk Assistant (open alternatives are specified instead) - reading or writing the reference product's proprietary .rvt and .rfa formats - vendor content libraries

    0.2 Product Overview

    0.2.1 Users

    Persona Primary needs
    Architect / designer Model building elements quickly; produce plans, sections, elevations, 3D views and sheets
    BIM coordinator Shared models, linking, clash detection, IFC exchange, standards (templates, parameters)
    Structural engineer Physical structural model, analytical model, loads, rebar documentation
    MEP engineer Duct, pipe and electrical systems, sizing, circuits, panel schedules, spaces and loads
    Computational designer / developer Lua scripting, add-ins, MCP automation, data extraction
    AI agent (non-human) Complete, typed, permissioned access to model queries and edits through MCP

    0.2.2 Product principles

    1. Single source of truth. All drawings, schedules and 3D views are live views of one model. Changing an element anywhere updates it everywhere.
    2. Parametric relationships. Hosting, joins, constraints, formulas and datums propagate changes automatically.
    3. Open by construction, compatibility first. A Reviera project is a single, schema-valid IFC file. Information IFC can't express (parametric intent, drawings, standards) is stored as Reviera Extension Data (RXD), a published JSON format embedded as standard Reviera_* property sets. Other IFC tools keep it or safely ignore it. A clean-IFC export and an external sidecar carrier are also available (Chapter 2a).
    4. Everything is a command. Each operation is a typed, undoable command, available in the same way to the UI, Lua and MCP.
    5. Multi-core first. Regeneration, tessellation, hidden-line processing, schedules and export use all available cores.
    6. Familiar workflows, own expression. Experienced BIM users should find the workflow concepts familiar. Reviera's naming, visual design, icons and defaults are its own.

    0.3 System Architecture Summary

    The full rationale is in TECH_STACK.md.

    ┌──────────────────────────── wxWidgets UI (main thread) ─────────────────────────────┐
│ Ribbon · QAT · Properties · Project Browser · Views (GPU viewport) · Dialogs · AI pane│
└──────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
               │  invoke(command, params)          ▲ events (selection, model changed)
┌──────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                               Rust core (multi-core)                                 │
│  Command Registry ─ Transaction Manager/Undo ─ Element DB ─ Regeneration Graph       │
│        ▲        ▲                     │ ChangeSets ─► Live store (SQLite WAL, writer thread)│
│   LuaJIT VM   MCP server (rmcp)       ▼                        ▼                     │
│   scripts,    tools = commands   IfcOpenShell            OpenCASCADE                 │
│   add-ins     resources = model  (IFC schema, I/O)       (B-rep, booleans, HLR)      │
│                                       │                                              │
│                         ModelStore trait                                             │
│                ┌──────────────────────┴─────────────────────┐                        │
│        LocalStore (.ifc/.ifczip)              BimServerStore (JSON API, notifications)│
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    0.3.1 Command model (applies to every chapter)

    • A command has a stable dotted name (wall.create, view.duplicate, bimserver.checkin). It also has a parameter schema (JSON Schema), a result schema, an undoable flag, a permission class (read, edit, script, admin), and UI metadata (label, icon id, ribbon location, shortcut).
    • Every model-changing command runs inside a transaction. Interactive tools, such as drawing a wall chain, gather input and then issue one or more commands. A whole tool session can be grouped into one undo step.
    • Lua sees commands as reviera.<domain>.<verb>{...}. MCP sees each command as a tool named <domain>_<verb>. Read-only model access is provided as Lua query APIs and MCP resources (reviera://element/{guid}, reviera://view/{id}, reviera://schedule/{id}).
    • Each chapter ends with a command catalog. Appendix A merges them into one index.

    0.3.2 Operating modes

    • Local: the project is an .ifc or .ifczip file on disk, and one user edits it.
    • BIMserver client: the project is an Open Source BIMserver project. Reviera keeps an offline working copy, checks in revisions, gets the latest revision, merges changes by GlobalId and shows notifications. Chapter 6 maps the reference product's worksharing concepts (central/local, worksets, element borrowing, synchronise) onto this mode.

    0.3.3 Persistence summary

    Reference concept Reviera persistence
    Project file IFC4 (ADD2 TC1) .ifc / .ifczip; IFC4X3 optional
    Unsaved working state Live SQLite store *.rvlive in the per-user data directory, updated per transaction (Chapter 2b); local only, never exchanged
    Family file IFC library file (IfcProjectLibrary + type objects) with RXD families/<id> embedded
    Project template IFC file marked as a template (Reviera_ProjectTemplate)
    Categories IFC entity class + PredefinedType (+ Reviera_Category where finer granularity is needed)
    Types / instances IfcTypeObject subtypes / occurrence entities
    Parameter values Readable Psets/Qtos (standard Pset_* where defined, otherwise project-named Psets)
    Parameter definitions (formulas, groups, shared ids) RXD document standards/parameters
    Element recipes, sketches, owned constraints RXD element data in the Reviera_Element Pset on the element
    Cross-element constraints RXD document model/constraints
    Views, sheets, schedules, view templates, annotation RXD documents (Reviera_Doc:* Psets on IfcProject); optional IfcAnnotation export
    Worksets / phases / design options RXD documents and element membership (optional IfcGroup export)
    Live ownership / locks (BIMserver) BIMserver Extended Data, not in the model file

    0.4 Glossary

    Term Meaning in Reviera
    Element Any persistent object: a model element, datum, view, annotation, type or setting
    Category A classification of elements (Walls, Doors, …) that controls visibility, graphics and scheduling
    Family A named definition of a parametric object, with one or more types. System families (walls, floors and similar) are built into Reviera. Loadable families come from IFC library files. In-place families are one-off, project-specific definitions.
    Type A named set of parameter values shared by many instances (IfcTypeObject)
    Instance One placed occurrence of a type
    Host An element that another depends on and is cut by, such as a wall hosting a door
    Datum A reference element: level, grid, reference plane or scope box
    View A live graphical or tabular representation of the model: a plan, section, 3D view, schedule and so on
    View template A named, reusable set of view settings
    Sheet A printable layout holding views and schedules inside a title block
    Sketch mode An editing mode for drawing 2D boundary or path curves that define an element (floor, roof, stair)
    Regeneration Recomputing dependent elements and geometry after a change
    Transaction An atomic, undoable unit of model change
    Command A registered, typed operation, available through the UI, Lua and MCP
    Working copy The local copy of a BIMserver project being edited
    Check in / Get latest / Sync Upload a revision / download the newest revision / do both, with a merge
    Lua add-in A packaged Lua extension with a manifest that declares a GPL-compatible SPDX licence
    MCP Model Context Protocol: the interface through which AI agents call Reviera commands

    0.5 Requirement Conventions

    The full rules are in spec/00_conventions.md. - IDs have the form <AREA>-<FEATURE>-<NNN>. Area codes: UI, DM, ARC, STR, MEP, ANA, DOC, COL. - Priorities: - P0: MVP, a single-user architectural authoring tool - P1: v1.0, complete multi-discipline authoring with collaboration - P2: later, advanced discipline and analysis features - P3: deferred or not applicable - Each requirement uses "shall" language and has acceptance criteria written as testable check-boxes. - Each feature has a Ref: line pointing to the research section (and screenshot) it came from, so it can be traced back to the public source register.

    0.7 Non-functional Requirements

    ID Requirement Target
    NFR-PERF-001 Opening a 200 MB IFC4 model on an 8-core workstation ≤ 60 s to first interactive view
    NFR-PERF-002 Regenerating a single wall edit with 50 dependents (joins, hosted doors, room boundaries) ≤ 150 ms
    NFR-PERF-003 3D viewport navigation on a 1 M-triangle model ≥ 30 fps on a mid-range GPU
    NFR-PERF-004 Parallel scaling of full regeneration and export ≥ 5× speed-up on 8 cores versus 1
    NFR-REL-001 Crash safety Live SQLite store updated after every committed transaction (Chapter 2b). An application crash loses no more than 250 ms of committed work, and power loss no more than about 1 s. File writes are atomic.
    NFR-REL-002 Round-trip fidelity Saving an untouched IFC file loses no entities or properties (ids preserved)
    NFR-PORT-001 Platforms Windows 10 and later (x64); macOS 10.12 and later on Intel, macOS 11 and later on Apple silicon (universal binary); current Linux distributions (x64, X11/Wayland via GTK), shipped as a Flatpak that bundles its dependencies (TECH_STACK §5.4)
    NFR-ACC-001 Accessibility Full keyboard operation; screen-reader labels on all controls; HiDPI scaling at 100–300 %
    NFR-I18N-001 Localisation All UI strings externalised (gettext); metric and imperial units; RTL-safe layouts
    NFR-SEC-001 Scripting and MCP safety Permission classes enforced; Lua sandbox levels; MCP over HTTP requires authentication; credentials never exposed as MCP resources
    NFR-LIC-001 Licence compliance SPDX header in every source file; CI licence allow-list for dependencies; add-in loader enforces a GPL-compatible SPDX licence by default
    NFR-CR-001 Clean-room integrity No vendor assets, text, or file contents in the repository; contributions certify public-source provenance (DCO plus a provenance statement)

    1CHChapter 1: User Interface Shell

    Area code: UI · Status: Draft 1 · Date: 2026-10-12 · Licence of this document: GPL-3.0-or-later (as part of the Reviera source tree) Primary source: research/01_ui_shell.md (cited below as research/01 §n). Screenshots under screenshots/ui/ are internal reference only and are never shipped as Reviera assets.

    1.0 About this chapter

    1.0.1 Scope

    This chapter specifies the application shell of Reviera: every window region, palette, toolbar, menu, in-canvas control and interaction convention that a user meets before and while editing a model. It also specifies how the shell is built on wxWidgets, how every visible control is bound to the single command registry, how UI state is exposed to Lua and MCP, the built-in AI agent pane, the BIMserver-mode user interface, accessibility, HiDPI and persistence.

    The chapter does not specify the modelling behaviour behind the tools that appear in the ribbon. Each tool in the ribbon catalog (§1.8) names its owning chapter by area code and the command it invokes. The owning chapter is authoritative for that command's parameters, rules and IFC mapping.

    Owner code Owning chapter
    UI Chapter 1 (this chapter)
    DM Chapter 2 — Data model, families, parameters, project setup, file I/O, Reviera Extension Data (RXD), extensibility (Lua, add-ins, MCP)
    ARC Chapter 3 — Architectural modelling and modify tools (includes datums, work planes, sketching, generic modify tools)
    STR Chapter 4 — Structure, steel, concrete/precast
    MEP Chapter 4 — Mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fabrication
    ANA Chapter 4 — Analysis (structural analytical model, energy, loads, route, carbon)
    DOC Chapter 5 — Views, graphics, annotation, schedules, sheets, output
    COL Chapter 6 — Collaboration, linking, coordination, BIMserver

    1.0.2 Terminology used in this chapter

    Term Meaning in Reviera
    Shell The main application frame and everything in it except the content drawn inside a view.
    Command A typed, registered operation (§1.1.1). The only way the shell changes the model or the application state.
    Tool A UI affordance (button, menu item, gallery entry, key sequence) that is bound to a command.
    Tool session An interactive, multi-step collection of command arguments in the canvas (picks, sketches, typed values) that ends by invoking a command, or is cancelled.
    Context The combination of active document, active view, active tool session, selection set and edit mode (sketch, group edit, family edit) that drives what the shell shows.
    Contextual tab A ribbon tab that exists only while a given context holds (§1.9).
    Pane A dockable window managed by the docking manager (Properties, Project Browser, System Browser, Agent, …).
    View window A dockable document window that displays one view, sheet or schedule.
    Orientation Cube Reviera's 3D orientation widget (functional counterpart of the reference's cube widget).
    Navigation Wheel Reviera's cursor-following radial navigation menu (functional counterpart of the reference's wheel menus).
    Command Search Reviera's search box for commands, help, views and files (counterpart of the reference's title-bar help search).
    Theme token A named colour or metric (for example canvas.selection) used by all drawing code instead of literal colours.

    1.0.3 Design principles

    1. One registry, many surfaces. Ribbon, Quick Access Toolbar, menus, context menus, key sequences, Command Search, Lua and MCP all draw on the same command registry. Nothing in the shell performs model work directly.
    2. Context in, presentation out. A single context engine decides what the ribbon, Properties palette, status bar and in-canvas controls show. Surfaces are renderers of that state.
    3. Tool options are data. Options for an active tool are a declarative descriptor rendered by the shell into contextual ribbon panels and the Properties palette (§1.10). There is no separate Options Bar.
    4. Never block the UI thread. All model work runs on the core's worker pool through the command queue; the shell remains responsive and shows progress (TECH_STACK §3.3).
    5. Keyboard first, mouse friendly. Every command is reachable without a mouse (key sequence, keytips or Command Search); every key action has a visible equivalent.
    6. Own look. Reviera uses its own icon set, colours and wording. No reference artwork is used.
    7. Mode-agnostic shell. Local and BIMserver modes share the same shell; mode-specific elements appear only where behaviour differs (§1.32).

    1.1 Shell architecture

    1.1.1 Command descriptors and UI metadata

    ID: UI-ARCH-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §27 items 1–2; TECH_STACK §2

    Purpose. Give every registered command the metadata the shell needs to present it, so that UI surfaces are generated from the registry rather than hand-written.

    Behaviour & rules. - Every command in the registry shall carry a UI descriptor with the following fields. Fields marked req are required for any command that appears on a UI surface.

    Field Type Notes
    id req string domain.verb[.sub] Stable; never localised; used by shortcuts, QAT, Lua, MCP.
    label req localisable string Short name shown on buttons and menus.
    label_long localisable string Used in Command Search, the shortcut dialog and tooltips when label is ambiguous.
    icon icon key Resolves to an SVG in the active icon theme (§1.28).
    tooltip req localisable string One sentence (first tooltip stage, §1.25).
    tooltip_extended localisable rich text + optional illustration key Second tooltip stage.
    help_topic string Topic key into the offline help (F1).
    ribbon_paths list of tab/panel[/split] Zero or more locations. The ribbon is built from these plus the layout file (§1.8.1).
    default_shortcuts list of key bindings From the default map (§1.26.5).
    invocation req enum direct, interactive, toggle, dialog, menu (see UI-ARCH-002).
    availability req predicate id Evaluated by the context engine; decides enabled/disabled and visible/hidden.
    toggle_state state query id For toggle commands, returns on/off for highlighting.
    discipline set of discipline flags Used by discipline filtering (UI-RIB-007).
    priority_tier P0–P3 Builds can omit commands above a configured tier.
    exposure flags ui, lua, mcp Default all three. A few shell-internal commands are not exposed to MCP (for example agent.*, §1.31).
    undoable bool Mirrors the core definition; shown in catalogs and used by the agent pane.
    reserved_keys bool True when its shortcut is reserved (§1.26.3).
    • Commands contributed by Lua add-ins shall provide the same descriptor through their manifest; the shell treats them exactly like built-in commands.
    • A command without label, tooltip, invocation or availability shall be rejected at registration if it declares any ribbon_paths or default_shortcuts.

    Commands. ui.command.list(filter?) -> [descriptor], ui.command.describe(id) -> descriptor.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Removing a command from the registry removes it from the ribbon, QAT, menus, Command Search and shortcut dialog without any other code change. - [ ] A Lua add-in that registers a command with a ribbon_paths entry produces a working button on the next ribbon rebuild. - [ ] ui.command.describe("wall.create") over MCP returns the label, tooltip, shortcuts and ribbon paths.

    1.1.2 Invocation kinds and the UI-to-core path

    ID: UI-ARCH-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §6.1, §27 item 2; TECH_STACK §3.3

    Purpose. Define how activating a tool turns into a command execution.

    Behaviour & rules. - direct: the command runs immediately with arguments taken from the current context (for example element.delete with the current selection). The shell places a request on the core command queue and returns at once. - interactive: the shell starts a tool session (UI-ARCH-003). The session collects arguments from picks, sketches, typed values and tool options, and then submits one or more command requests. A session may stay active after a submission ("chain" or repeated placement) until the user presses Esc or picks another tool. - toggle: the command flips a boolean state (for example Thin Lines). The button is drawn in its pressed state while toggle_state is true. - dialog: the shell opens a dialog; the dialog's OK/Apply submits commands. Cancel submits nothing. - menu: the tool only opens a drop-down (for example a split button's arrow or a "Plan Views" drop-down). - Every model-changing submission runs inside a core transaction. A tool session that submits several commands as one user action (for example a wall chain finished with Esc) shall wrap them in one transaction group so a single Undo reverts the whole action. - While the core is executing a request, the shell shall stay responsive: navigation, hover highlighting and cancel remain available. If a request runs longer than 500 ms, the status bar shows a progress indicator with a Cancel button where the command supports cancellation. - Commands submitted from Lua or MCP while a UI tool session is active are queued; they do not interleave with an open transaction. The status bar shows "External request waiting" until the session ends or the user allows it to proceed (UI-API-006).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Clicking Delete with three elements selected produces one undo entry named after the command. - [ ] Drawing a four-segment wall chain and pressing Esc produces one undo entry. - [ ] During a 10-second regeneration the user can still orbit the active 3D view.

    1.1.3 Context engine

    ID: UI-ARCH-003 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §8, §10, §27 item 3

    Purpose. Compute, in one place, everything the shell needs to know about the current situation.

    Behaviour & rules. - The context engine holds: active document; active view window; active tool session (command id, step, tool-option values); selection set (element ids grouped by category); edit mode stack (none, sketch, group edit, in-place family edit, family editor document, view-on-sheet activation, reveal-hidden mode); selection option toggles (UI-SEL-004); operating mode (Local/BIMserver) and connection state. - On any change it publishes a context snapshot to all surfaces. Surfaces never query the model directly to decide visibility; they read the snapshot and evaluate command availability predicates against it. - Snapshots are immutable and versioned. The ribbon, Properties palette, status bar and canvas overlays shall update within one UI frame (≤ 16 ms budget for the shell side) after a snapshot is published for selections of up to 10 000 elements; larger selections may degrade the Properties palette to "computing…" while the common parameter set is computed off-thread. - The engine also exposes the snapshot to Lua and MCP (§1.30) and emits change notifications.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Selecting a wall shows the wall contextual tab, wall instance properties and wall drag controls, all from one snapshot change. - [ ] Selecting 50 000 elements by window does not freeze the UI; the Properties palette shows a progress state and then the common parameters.

    1.1.4 Tool option descriptors

    ID: UI-ARCH-004 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §9 (spec note), Figure 20 screenshots/ui/revit2027_options_bar_removed.png, screenshots/ui/options_bar.png

    Purpose. Represent per-tool options (height, location line, chain, offset, radius, and so on) as data so they can be rendered consistently.

    Behaviour & rules. - An interactive command declares a list of tool options, each with: key, label, value type (bool, enum, length, angle, number, element reference such as a level), default, persistence (session, user, none), and placement hint (ribbon, properties, both). - The shell renders options with placement ribbon or both as controls in contextual ribbon panels (§1.9.3), and options with properties or both as a "Tool Options" group at the top of the Properties palette. - Changing an option while the tool session is active affects the next submission; for options that alter an in-progress preview (for example Location Line) the preview updates immediately. - Option values with persistence user are remembered per command between sessions (§1.29). - Tool options are readable and writable from Lua and MCP while a tool session is running (tool.get_options, tool.set_option).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] The wall placement tool shows Height/Depth, top constraint, Location Line, Chain, Offset and Radius in a contextual panel, and the same values in the Properties "Tool Options" group; changing one updates the other. - [ ] Restarting Reviera keeps the last-used wall Location Line.

    Purpose. Fix how each shell element is built on wxWidgets (3.3 or later) so implementation choices are consistent.

    Behaviour & rules.

    Shell element wxWidgets realisation Custom work required
    Main frame wxFrame with native decorations; wxAuiManager owns all panes Frame-level DPI change handling

    File menu Custom-drawn "File" button at the left of the ribbon tab row opening a full-height wxPopupTransientWindow with a two-column layout; on macOS the native wxMenuBar also exposes File, Edit, View, Window and Help Split items, right pane switching
    Ribbon wxRibbonBar with wxRibbonPage, wxRibbonPanel, wxRibbonButtonBar, wxRibbonToolBar, wxRibbonGallery; a Reviera wxRibbonArtProvider subclass drawing from theme tokens Contextual pages (show/hide pages plus page highlight), slide-out pinning, panel floating, Ctrl-drag tab reorder, four minimise modes, keytips, embedded option controls

    • The Rust↔wxWidgets binding is wxDragon (TECH_STACK §3.4, §5); any extensions are kept as clean patches offered upstream. This chapter is written against a UI bridge interface: the Rust core publishes context snapshots and accepts command requests; the C++ or Rust-wrapped wx side renders. Neither option may let wx code reach into the element database directly.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] On Windows, Linux (GTK 3) and macOS the ribbon, docking, view tabs and Properties palette function identically apart from platform-native decorations. - [ ] No canvas overlay is implemented as a native child window over the GPU surface (verified by code review checklist).

    1.1.6 Threading and responsiveness

    ID: UI-ARCH-006 · Priority: P0 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.3, §3.7.1

    Purpose. Fix which thread does what, so that no model, network or script work can freeze the window and no worker thread can corrupt a widget.

    Behaviour & rules. - The wx event loop runs on the main thread and owns every widget. Core results reach the UI thread through a queued event (CallAfter equivalent); no core thread touches a widget. - Network operations (BIMserver, agent model provider, MCP over HTTP) run on the async runtime and report progress through the same mechanism. - Long-running UI-thread work (for example populating a 100 000-row Project Browser) shall be virtualised or chunked so that no single UI-thread slice exceeds 50 ms. - Thread roles.

    Thread Owns Never does
    Main (UI) wx widgets, input routing, tool-session state machine, context-snapshot rendering Model reads beyond the published snapshot; blocking I/O
    Core worker pool Command execution, regeneration, snapshot building, snap queries Widget calls
    Live-store writer Group-committing change sets to the local store (Ch. 2b) Anything on the UI's critical path
    Async runtime BIMserver, agent provider, MCP over HTTP, update checks Model writes except through the command queue
    Scripting Lua handlers and scripts Direct widget calls (it uses commands such as ui.notify)
    Renderer GPU submission for every canvas Blocking on regeneration (it draws the last committed scene)
    • Back-pressure. When more than 200 queued UI events from the core are pending, the bridge coalesces events of the same kind (snapshot, progress, notification) and keeps only the newest of each, so a burst of commits cannot flood the event loop.
    • Modal dialogs run a nested event loop on the main thread; core results that arrive meanwhile are still delivered and applied to non-modal surfaces.
    • Debug watchdog. Debug and test builds run a watchdog that samples the main thread every 50 ms and logs any stall above 250 ms with a stack trace. Release builds keep only a counter, visible in Help › About › Diagnostics.
    • Shutdown. app.exit asks the core to finish or cancel the running command, flushes the live store and waits at most 5 s for worker threads before closing windows; it never closes a widget while a worker could still post to it.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With a 500 MB model open, a UI watchdog in debug builds records no main-thread stall above 250 ms during open, select-all, and view switching. - [ ] A test that calls a widget method from a worker thread fails a debug assertion. - [ ] During a BIMserver download over a throttled 1 Mbit/s link, the user can pan, select and open the Options dialog. - [ ] Committing 1 000 small transactions from a Lua loop produces no more than one snapshot redraw per UI frame.

    Default layout (top to bottom).

    Behaviour & rules. - The layout is fully rearrangeable (§1.15) and restorable to this default with ui.layout.reset. - Every zone except the ribbon tab row and the centre can be hidden from View › Windows › User Interface (UI-DOCK-004). - Minimum supported window size: 1024 × 640 logical pixels; below that, the ribbon collapses panels (UI-RIB-002) and docks auto-hide. - Bookmarked layouts: the user can save the whole arrangement under a name and switch between saved arrangements instantly. This covers panes, ribbon, QAT, visible panels and, optionally, theme, scale and open views. Specified in §1.29.4 (UI-LAYOUT-001…006).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A fresh profile starts with the layout in the table above on all three platforms. - [ ] ui.layout.reset() restores that layout without restarting. - [ ] Saving the layout "Docs" with the Project Browser floating, then switching to "Default" and back, restores the floating browser (see also §1.29.4).

    1.3 Reviera Home

    1.3.1 Home screen

    ID: UI-HOME-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §2, §2.1, §2.2 · screenshots/ui/home_classic.png, screenshots/ui/home_new_recent.png, screenshots/ui/home_new_projects.png

    Purpose. Provide a start page for opening and creating models and families, and a place to return to between tasks.

    Workflow. 1. Reviera starts and shows Home in place of the ribbon and view area. 2. The user opens a recent item, browses for a file, creates a new model from a template, or connects to a BIMserver project. 3. Home closes and the ribbon and views appear. Ctrl+D or the QAT Home button returns to Home; the back arrow (or Ctrl+D again, or Esc) returns to the active model.

    UI. - Left rail: - Models: Open… (file.open), New… (file.new with the New Model dialog: template list from Options › File Locations, plus "Model / Model template" choice and schema choice IFC4 or IFC4X3 — the latter only in Local mode). - Families: Open… (family_doc.open), New… (family_doc.new, opens the family template chooser). - Pages: Recent, Servers (BIMserver mode entry point, §1.32.2), Samples & Learning (bundled sample models and the offline manual). - Footer links: What's New (local release notes), Manual (offline help), Community (project website), Report a Problem (opens the issue tracker URL in the browser), Licence & Source (GPL notice and source location). - Recent page (right area): - Grid view (thumbnails) or list view (columns: Name, Pinned, Modified, Location, Kind, Size, Mode). Columns can be shown/hidden and reordered. - Two groups: Models and Families. Server projects appear in Models with a server badge. - Search box filtering by name and location; Filter flyout by modified date (All / Today / Last 7 days / Last 30 days / Last 90 days) and kind (Models / Families / Templates). - Pin (keeps an item at the top and exempt from list truncation), Remove from list, Open containing folder, Open read-only (Local mode) and Open revision… (server items). - Missing files are shown greyed with a "Locate…" action. - Thumbnail source: the preview image that Reviera stores with the model's Reviera Extension Data at save (Ch. 2); when absent, a generic kind icon. Server items use a per-user local thumbnail cache.

    Behaviour & rules. - Home is shown at start-up unless the user launched Reviera with a file argument or chose "Reopen last session" in Options (UI-PREF-002). - The Recent list holds up to 50 items by default (configurable 0–200; 0 hides the list). It is stored per user, never inside a model. - While Home is visible, keyboard shortcuts for model commands are inactive except reserved file shortcuts (Ctrl+N, Ctrl+O) and Ctrl+D. - Home uses only local data plus configured servers; it never contacts any service the user has not configured. - There is no usage-analytics page (the reference's "insights" page is not reproduced; see §1.35).

    Commands. ui.home.show(), ui.home.hide(), ui.home.toggle(), ui.recent.list(kind?) -> [RecentItem], ui.recent.pin(path_or_uri, pinned), ui.recent.remove(path_or_uri), ui.recent.clear().

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Starting Reviera with no arguments shows Home; Ctrl+D with a model open toggles between Home and the model. - [ ] A pinned item remains at the top after 60 other files are opened. - [ ] Filtering by "Families" and "Last 7 days" shows only families modified in the last week. - [ ] A recent server project opens through the server login flow if no valid session token exists.

    1.4 File menu

    ID: UI-FILE-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §3 · screenshots/ui/file_tab_menu.png

    Purpose. Offer document-level operations (new, open, save, export, print, close), the recent/open document lists, Options and Exit.

    Workflow. 1. The user clicks File (left end of the tab row) or presses Alt, F. 2. A full-height panel opens. The left column lists item groups; hovering or clicking an item's arrow shows its sub-items in the right pane; clicking an item's main area runs its default. 3. Clicking outside or pressing Esc closes the panel.

    UI. Left column items, their default action and their sub-items:

    Item Default (click) Sub-items (right pane) Commands (owner) Pri
    New New Model dialog Model; Family; Conceptual Mass Family; Title Block; Annotation Symbol; Model Template file.new(kind, template?) (DM) P0 (mass/title block/symbol P1)
    Open Open dialog Model (IFC/IFCZIP); Family; From Server…; Sample Files; IFC open options… file.open(path, options?), family_doc.open, bimserver.open (COL), cde.select_documents (From CDE…, COL), file.ifc_open_options (DM) P0 (server P1, CDE P2)
    Save Save (writes the model using its current RXD carrier: embedded, or .ifc + .reviera sidecar written atomically) — file.save(document_id? (default: active)) -> status (DM) P0
    Save As Save As dialog with an Options… button (RXD carrier, below) Model; Family; Template; Library ▸ Family / Group / View file.save_as(document_id? (default: active), path, kind?, format?: ifc\|ifczip, carrier?: embedded\|external_file\|external_dir\|bundle) -> status, family.save_as, group.save, view.save_to_library (DM) P0 (library P1)
    Export — CAD ▸ DWG, DXF, DGN, SAT, STL; Images & Animations ▸ Image, Walkthrough, Sun Study; Reports ▸ Schedule, Room/Area Report; PDF; OBJ; FBX; glTF; gbXML; Family Types; Database (ODBC/SQLite); IFC ▸ (with Reviera data, Clean IFC (strip Reviera data), another schema or MVD); BCF; Export options ▸ (CAD export setups, IFC export setups) export.* (DOC/DM) PDF P0; CAD, image, schedule P1; others P2
    Print Print dialog Print; Print Preview; Print Setup; Batch Print print.* (DOC) P0 (batch P2)
    Server — (only shown when BIMserver features are enabled) Connect…; Publish to Server…; Check In…; Get Latest; Sync; Export Local Copy…; Disconnect server.* (COL) P1
    Close Close active model — file.close() (DM) P0
    • Right pane, default content: Recent Documents with a sort control (Most recent first, By name, By size, By kind) and pins; a toggle switches to Open Documents, which lists every open view of every open model; clicking a view activates it (view.activate).
    • Footer: Options (ui.options.open) and Exit Reviera (app.exit).

    Behaviour & rules. - File is not a ribbon page; it cannot be reordered or hidden. - Items are disabled when unavailable (for example Save with no model open; Check In when not connected). - Reviera Extension Data (RXD) handling (Local mode). Reviera-specific project data that plain IFC cannot express (Reviera Extension Data, "RXD"; format defined in 02a_extension_data_format.md, Ch. 2) is embedded in the IFC file as property sets by default, so a model is normally one .ifc file. An external sidecar <name>.reviera is an optional alternative carrier. The shell behaves as follows: - Save As options (Options… button in the Save As dialog, also in Options › File Locations as the default for new models): - RXD carrier: ( ) Embed Reviera data in the IFC (recommended) — default; ( ) Write separate sidecar file — writes <name>.ifc plus <name>.reviera. - The chosen carrier is remembered for the model and used by subsequent Save. With the sidecar carrier, Save writes both files as one atomic operation (both written to temporary files, then both replaced); if either write fails, neither original is replaced and an error dialog names the failing file. - Export clean IFC (File › Export › IFC › Clean IFC (strip Reviera data), export.ifc(strip_rxd=true, path, schema?), P0): writes a copy without any RXD property sets or entities, for exchange with tools that dislike unknown property sets. It never changes the open model's path or carrier, and the dialog states that parametric intent (constraints, sketches, view definitions and similar) will not be in the copy. - Open: RXD embedded in the IFC is read automatically. When the model uses the sidecar carrier, opening <name>.ifc also reads <name>.reviera when present; selecting a .reviera file in the Open dialog opens its paired IFC. - RXD missing (a foreign IFC with no RXD, or an expected sidecar not found): the model opens with default UI and documentation settings and a non-blocking notice in the notification area: "This model has no Reviera data; defaults are in use. It will be added when you save." For a missing sidecar the notice also offers "Locate data file…" (file.locate_rxd). - RXD stale (RXD records refer to GlobalIds that no longer exist, or its recorded model fingerprint differs, for example after the IFC was edited in another tool): Reviera opens the model, reconciles automatically by GlobalId (Ch. 2 rules), and shows a reconciliation report — a notice that opens a dialog listing what was kept, what was re-attached, what was dropped as orphaned (with element and record identifiers), and what was reset to defaults. The report offers Keep reconciled data (default; takes effect on next Save), Discard Reviera data and use defaults, and Save report… (text/CSV). When reconciliation would drop more than a threshold (default 10 % of records) the report opens automatically as a modal dialog instead of a notice. - Project-scoped UI data (open views and their tab/tile arrangement, Project Browser state, selection sets, browser organisation schemes) are RXD documents stored with the model through whichever carrier it uses (§1.29). Per-user preferences are never written into RXD. - Closing a model with unsaved changes prompts Save / Don't Save / Cancel; in BIMserver mode a further prompt offers Check In when there are local changes not checked in. - On macOS the same items are mirrored in the native menu bar's File menu; Options appears as the application "Settings…" item and Exit as "Quit Reviera".

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Clicking the main area of Open shows the Open dialog; clicking its arrow shows the Open sub-items without opening a dialog. - [ ] The Open Documents list contains every view window, including ones floated on a second monitor, and activating one brings its frame to front. - [ ] Every item in the table is reachable with keytips (§1.25.3). - [ ] A new model saved with default options produces a single .ifc file that reopens with its open views, browser state and selection sets restored. - [ ] Choosing "Write separate sidecar file" produces .ifc + .reviera; killing the process during a later Save leaves both previous files intact and mutually consistent. - [ ] Export clean IFC produces a file containing no RXD property sets, and the open model's carrier and path are unchanged. - [ ] Opening a foreign IFC without RXD shows the defaults notice and no modal dialog. - [ ] Opening a model whose RXD references 5 deleted GlobalIds shows a reconciliation report listing those 5 records as orphaned.

    1.6 QAT strip right side: Command Search, help and identity

    1.6.1 Command Search

    ID: UI-SEARCH-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §5 · screenshots/ui/infocenter_search.png, screenshots/ui/help_menu.png

    Purpose. One search box to find and run any command, open a view, open a recent file, or find a help topic. Replaces the reference's online-help search box with a local, broader tool.

    Workflow. 1. The user clicks the search box or presses Ctrl+K. 2. As the user types, results appear grouped as Commands, Views & Sheets (active model), Recent Files, Help Topics, Settings (Options pages). 3. Arrow keys move; Enter runs the command, activates the view, opens the file or help topic, or opens Options at that setting. Esc closes.

    Behaviour & rules. - Matching is case-insensitive, accent-insensitive and fuzzy over label, long label, command id, synonyms declared in descriptors, and the shortcut keys. Wildcards * and ? are honoured when present. - Each command result shows icon, label, ribbon path(s), shortcut(s) and whether it is currently available. Unavailable commands are listed but cannot be run; the reason ("needs a selection", "only in plan views") is shown. - Results are ranked by match quality, then by the user's recent usage (stored locally). - Help search runs against the offline manual index bundled with the application; no network request is made unless the user enables "Search online documentation" in Options.

    Commands. ui.command_search(query, limit?) -> [SearchResult].

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Typing "algn" ranks Align first; Enter starts the Align tool. - [ ] Typing a view name opens that view. - [ ] With networking disabled, search still returns help topics.

    1.6.2 Help menu and About

    ID: UI-HELP-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §5

    Behaviour & rules. - A Help button at the right of the QAT strip opens the offline manual. Its drop-down lists: Manual, What's New, Keyboard Shortcut Reference (generated from the live shortcut map), Lua API Reference (generated from the registry), MCP Tool Reference (generated), Report a Problem, Community, Check for Updates (only if enabled), About Reviera. - F1 opens context help: for the tool under the cursor when its tooltip is visible, for the active dialog, or for the active tool session. Help topics are looked up by help_topic in the command descriptor or by dialog id. - About Reviera shows version, build hash, licence (GPL-3.0-or-later) with the full text, third-party component licences, and where to obtain the corresponding source code (TECH_STACK §4.2 distribution duty).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] F1 while hovering the Wall button with its tooltip shown opens the wall help topic. - [ ] About shows the GPL text and a list of third-party licences that matches the build's dependency manifest.

    1.6.3 User identity

    ID: UI-IDENT-001 · Priority: P0 (Local) / P1 (server) · Ref: research/01 §5, §24.1

    Behaviour & rules. - In Local mode the user name comes from Options › General (default: the operating-system login name). It is written into change attribution and ownership data. - In BIMserver mode the user name shown and used for attribution is the account name of the active server session; the Options field is shown read-only with the note "Set by server login" while connected (§1.32). - There is no vendor account sign-in. The QAT strip shows a connection indicator only in BIMserver mode (§1.32.5). - Validation. The Local user name is 1–64 characters, trimmed, with no control characters; an empty field reverts to the operating-system login name on OK. The setting key is general.user_name. - Where the name is used. Undo and History entries (with the source, §1.30.6), live-store change sets (Ch. 2b), saved-selection and view-bookmark authorship, the default check-in comment template, and ownership claims. The IFC IfcOwnerHistory written on save uses the same name (Ch. 2). - Change during a session. A new name applies to entries created after OK; existing entries keep the name they were made with. Changing the name while elements are owned in Local mode shows a warning that ownership records keep the old name. - Agents and scripts. Changes made by a Lua script or an MCP session are attributed to "<user name> via <script or session name>", never to the script alone. - The user name is readable by scripts and agents with ui.user.get() -> {name, source: options|server, server_uri?}; it can only be changed through ui.options.set("general.user_name", …), which fails while a server session is active.

    Commands. ui.user.get() -> {name, source, server_uri?}.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing the user name in Options changes the name recorded on new undo entries and ownership claims in Local mode. - [ ] While connected to a server, the user-name field cannot be edited. - [ ] Clearing the field and pressing OK restores the operating-system login name. - [ ] A wall created by an MCP session named "planner" is attributed to "<user> via planner" in the History pane, and its Undo entry reads "Create wall — agent: planner" (§1.30.6).

    1.7 Ribbon behaviours

    1.7.1 Structure and control kinds

    ID: UI-RIB-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §6.1 · screenshots/ui/ribbon_contextual_tab.png

    Purpose. Organise commands as tabs → panels → tools.

    Behaviour & rules. - A tab holds panels; a panel holds tools and has a title strip along its bottom edge. - Supported tool kinds:

    Kind Description wx realisation
    Large button Icon above label wxRibbonButtonBar large button
    Small button Icon beside label; stacked 2 or 3 high wxRibbonButtonBar small/medium button
    Icon-only button Icon with tooltip wxRibbonToolBar tool
    Split button Main part runs the last-used member (remembered per user); arrow lists all members wxRIBBON_BUTTON_HYBRID + menu; last-used stored in ui-state.toml
    Drop-down button Arrow only; opens a menu wxRIBBON_BUTTON_DROPDOWN
    Toggle button Drawn pressed while on wxRIBBON_BUTTON_TOGGLE bound to toggle_state
    Embedded control Combo, numeric/length entry, check box inside a panel (mostly contextual option panels) wxRibbonPanel hosting a sizer with native controls
    Gallery Scrollable grid of choices with an expand arrow (type galleries, draw-shape gallery) wxRibbonGallery
    • Every tool is bound to exactly one command id (split and drop-down members each bound to their own).
    • Disabled tools remain visible and show the reason for unavailability in their tooltip.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] After choosing "Roof by Extrusion" from the Roof split button, the main part of the button runs Roof by Extrusion until another member is used, including after restart.

    1.7.2 Adaptive resizing

    ID: UI-RIB-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §6.1

    Behaviour & rules. - As available width shrinks, panels reduce in this order: large → small buttons; small → icon-only; finally the panel collapses into a single drop-down button that opens the full panel as a popup. Panels on the right collapse first; each panel may declare a collapse priority. - Growing the window reverses the process. - Collapsed panels stay keyboard- and keytip-reachable. - Reduction steps. Each panel declares, in ribbon-default.toml, an ordered list of size variants it supports (large, medium = small buttons with labels, small = icon-only, collapsed). Panels without a declaration get all four. The layout pass removes one step at a time from the panel with the highest collapse priority (default: rightmost first) until the tab fits, so the result is deterministic for a given width. - Fixed parts. The Select panel (§1.8.2) never collapses below small buttons. Embedded option controls (§1.10) shrink their label first, then become icon-plus-value, and only then move into the collapsed panel's popup. - Collapsed panel popup. The single button shows the panel's icon and title; clicking it opens the full panel as a popup that closes after a tool is chosen or on Esc. Split buttons keep their last-used member inside the popup. - Labels. When a large button becomes small or icon-only, its label moves into the tooltip; no label is truncated with an ellipsis inside the ribbon. - Hysteresis. Layout recalculation runs at most once per frame during a window drag and uses 16 px of hysteresis, so panels do not flicker between two sizes at a boundary width. - Font scale. The same algorithm runs after a UI font-scale or DPI change (§1.33.2, §1.33.3).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] At 1024 px wide the Architecture tab shows every panel, with at least one panel collapsed, and every tool can still be reached. - [ ] Narrowing the window by 1 px steps from 1920 to 1024 px never changes the panel layout twice for the same width, and widening back restores the full layout. - [ ] A collapsed panel's popup can be opened with keytips and its tools run from the keyboard. - [ ] No ribbon label is shown truncated at any width.

    1.7.3 Slide-out panels and dialog launchers

    ID: UI-RIB-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/01 §6.2, §6.3 · screenshots/ui/ribbon_expanded_panel.png, screenshots/ui/ribbon_expanded_panel_pinned.png, screenshots/ui/ribbon_dialog_launcher.png

    Behaviour & rules. - A panel may declare overflow tools. An arrow beside its title opens a slide-out showing them. The slide-out closes when the pointer leaves it or the user clicks elsewhere, unless the pin at its lower-left is set; a pinned slide-out stays open while its tab is active and is remembered per tab. - A panel may declare a dialog launcher command, drawn as a small corner button in the title strip (for example Mechanical Settings on the HVAC panel). Launchers are ordinary commands (shortcut-assignable, QAT-addable). - Opening a slide-out. Clicking the arrow, or pressing Down on a focused panel title, opens the slide-out directly below the panel at the panel's width or wider. It overlaps the canvas; it does not push the canvas down. Only one unpinned slide-out is open at a time. - Closing. An unpinned slide-out closes when the pointer has been outside it for 500 ms, after a tool in it is chosen, on Esc, or when another tab is activated. A pinned slide-out ignores pointer exit and tool choice; it hides when its tab is not active and reappears when the tab is activated again. - Pin state is stored per tab and panel in ui-state.toml and is part of the Ribbon part of a layout bookmark (UI-LAYOUT-001). It survives restart. - Minimised ribbon. In the minimised states (UI-RIB-004) a pinned slide-out behaves as unpinned, because the panel itself is a temporary overlay. - Floating panels (UI-RIB-005) show their overflow tools below the main tools with no slide-out. - Launcher rules. A launcher is drawn only if its command is available in the current context; otherwise it is shown disabled with the reason in its tooltip. A panel has at most one launcher. Launchers have keytips like any other tool.

    Commands. ui.ribbon.pin_slideout(tab_id, panel_id, pinned: bool) -> (); launchers run their own registered command.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Pinning the Room & Area slide-out keeps it open while switching between Architecture and Annotate tabs and returning. - [ ] An unpinned slide-out closes after a tool in it is chosen; a pinned one stays open. - [ ] Assigning a shortcut to the Mechanical Settings launcher command and pressing it opens the same dialog as the launcher button.

    1.7.4 Minimise states

    ID: UI-RIB-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/01 §6.4

    Behaviour & rules. - Ribbon states: Full, Tabs only, Panel titles only, Panel buttons only (one icon per panel). - A state button right of the last tab toggles between Full and the user's preferred minimised state; its arrow chooses the preferred state or "Cycle through all". - In minimised states, clicking a tab, title or panel button shows the content as a temporary overlay that closes after a tool is chosen. - Double-clicking a tab label toggles Full ↔ preferred minimised state. - Right-clicking empty ribbon space toggles Show panel titles. - State definitions. - Full: tabs and panels always visible (default). - Tabs only: only the tab row is shown; clicking a tab shows its whole panel area as an overlay. - Panel titles only: the tab row plus a strip of panel titles; clicking a title shows that panel as an overlay. - Panel buttons only: the tab row plus one icon per panel; clicking an icon shows that panel as an overlay. - Cycle. When the preferred state is "Cycle through all", the state button steps Full → Tabs → Titles → Buttons → Full. - Overlays. An overlay closes when a tool is chosen, on Esc, when the pointer has been outside it for 500 ms, or when the canvas is clicked. It never takes keyboard focus from an in-canvas text editor. - Contextual tabs in a minimised state. A contextual tab appears in the tab row as usual. When "Activate contextual tab on selection" is on (UI-RIB-006), its tab label is highlighted, but its panels are not opened automatically, so that the canvas stays uncovered. - Keytips work in every state; choosing a tab keytip opens its overlay. - The current state and the preferred minimised state are stored in ui-state.toml and in the Ribbon part of a layout bookmark. Focus mode (UI-DOCK-004) uses Tabs only temporarily without changing the stored preference.

    Commands. ui.ribbon.set_state(full|tabs|titles|buttons), ui.ribbon.cycle_state().

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Each of the four states can be selected, survives restart, and every tool remains reachable through overlays. - [ ] With the preferred state set to Panel titles only, the state button toggles between Full and Panel titles only. - [ ] In Tabs only, selecting a wall highlights the contextual tab label without opening an overlay.

    1.7.5 Rearranging tabs and panels

    ID: UI-RIB-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/01 §6.5

    Behaviour & rules. - Ctrl+drag a tab label to reorder tabs. File cannot move; contextual tabs always stay at the right end. - Drag a panel title to reorder panels within its tab, or drag it off the ribbon to create a floating panel (an always-on-top mini toolbar). Floating panels can be snapped to each other into a group and moved by a grip; hovering a floating panel shows a Return to Ribbon control. - Tabs and individual panels can be hidden from the ribbon right-click menu (Show Tabs ▸, Show Panels ▸). - Reset Ribbon (right-click menu and Options › User Interface) restores default order, visibility and states without touching the QAT; Reset All UI restores both.

    Commands. ui.ribbon.get_layout() -> RibbonLayout, ui.ribbon.move_tab(tab_id, index), ui.ribbon.move_panel(tab_id, panel_id, index), ui.ribbon.float_panel(tab_id, panel_id, pos?), ui.ribbon.dock_panel(panel_id), ui.ribbon.set_visible(tab_id, panel_id?, visible), ui.ribbon.reset().

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A floated Modify panel remains usable while the Annotate tab is active and returns to its original position with Return to Ribbon. - [ ] Reset Ribbon does not change the QAT.

    1.7.6 Tab-switching behaviour

    ID: UI-RIB-006 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §6.6

    Behaviour & rules. - On selection or tool start: when "Activate contextual tab on selection" is on (default on), the contextual tab becomes the active tab; when off, it appears but the current tab stays active. - After clearing a selection or finishing a tool: per user choice, either stay on the Modify tab or return to the tab that was active before (default: return to previous). Set separately for the model environment and the family editor. - Ctrl+** activates the first contextual tab when one exists. - Tab activation from the keyboard never changes the selection. - **Settings keys.**ui.ribbon.activate_contextual_on_selection(bool, default true),ui.ribbon.after_clear.modelandui.ribbon.after_clear.family(stay_on_modify|return_to_previous, defaultreturn_to_previous). All three are on Options › User Interface (UI-PREF-002) and can be part of a scenario's preference overlay (UI-SCEN-001). - **"Previous tab"** is the last permanent tab that was active before the contextual tab took focus. If that tab has since been hidden (by discipline filtering or the user), Reviera returns to Modify instead. - **Tool start from a ribbon button** keeps the user on the tab the tool came from while the tool's contextual tab is shown, unless the tool's option panels exist only on the contextual tab; then the contextual tab is activated whatever the setting, so the options can be seen. - **Changing selection category** (for example from walls to doors) while a contextual tab is active keeps the contextual tab active; its content is replaced (§1.9.1). - **Tool chaining.** Aftertool.repeat_lastor Create Similar, the tab-switching rules apply as for a fresh tool start. - **Ctrl+ with no contextual tab does nothing and shows "No contextual tab" in the status bar for 2 s. - Lua and MCP calls to ui.ribbon.activate_tab follow the same rules and fail with an error when the tab is hidden or unknown.

    Commands. ui.ribbon.activate_tab(tab_id), ui.ribbon.activate_contextual().

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With the option off, selecting a wall while on the Annotate tab shows the wall contextual tab but leaves Annotate active; Ctrl+` then activates it. - [ ] With "return to previous", selecting a wall from the View tab and pressing Esc returns to the View tab; with "stay on Modify" it stays on Modify. - [ ] The model and family-editor settings are independent: changing one does not change the other.

    1.7.7 Discipline filtering

    ID: UI-RIB-007 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/01 §6.7, §24.2

    Behaviour & rules. - Options › User Interface › Disciplines and tools offers check boxes: Architecture; Structure; Steel; Concrete & Precast; Structural analysis; Systems – mechanical; Mechanical analysis; Systems – electrical; Electrical analysis; Systems – piping; Piping analysis; Massing & Site; Energy analysis; Route analysis; Carbon analysis. - Clearing a box hides every command whose discipline set is fully covered by cleared boxes, and removes any tab left empty. - An organisation may lock this setting through the system defaults file (§1.29.3); the check boxes are then disabled with a "Managed by administrator" note. - Hidden commands remain available to Lua and MCP and through Command Search (shown as "hidden by discipline settings", runnable). - The ui.disciplines setting. The check boxes are stored as one per-user setting with the key ui.disciplines: a set of discipline flags, architecture, structure, steel, concrete, structural_analysis, mechanical, mechanical_analysis, electrical, electrical_analysis, piping, piping_analysis, massing_site, energy_analysis, route_analysis, carbon_analysis. The default is all flags set. This key is what an administrator locks (§1.29.3) and what a scenario's preference overlay may change (UI-SCEN-001). - What it filters. Ribbon tabs, panels and tools; QAT items (hidden, not removed, so they return when the discipline is re-enabled); context-menu entries; Properties-palette parameter groups that belong only to cleared disciplines (for example Structural when every structural flag is cleared); and the Options pages of cleared analysis features. It does not filter the Project Browser, Command Search, Lua, MCP, keyboard shortcuts or the model: elements of every discipline remain visible and editable. - Commands with no discipline set are treated as common and are never hidden. - Shortcuts to hidden commands still run them; the status bar adds "(hidden by discipline settings)". - At least one modelling discipline. Clearing every flag of Architecture, Structure and the three Systems disciplines is refused with the message "Keep at least one modelling discipline". - Changes take effect on OK without restart; the ribbon rebuilds once. - This filter is a UI preference. It is unrelated to the view discipline (Architectural, Structural, Mechanical, …) owned by Ch. 5.

    Commands. ui.disciplines.get() -> {enabled[], locked: bool}, ui.disciplines.set(enabled[]) -> () (fails when locked or when no modelling discipline would remain). Both are thin wrappers over ui.options.get/set("ui.disciplines").

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Clearing Structure, Steel, Concrete & Precast and Structural analysis removes the Structure, Steel and Concrete tabs and the structural tools on shared panels. - [ ] A locked discipline setting cannot be changed in Options. - [ ] With Structure cleared, typing the column shortcut still starts the column tool, and Command Search lists it as hidden but runnable. - [ ] Re-enabling a discipline restores the QAT items that were hidden by it, in their original positions. - [ ] ui.disciplines.set([]) returns an error and changes nothing.

    1.7.8 Add-in contributions

    ID: UI-RIB-008 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §7.13

    Behaviour & rules. - Lua add-ins declare tabs, panels and tools in their manifest (DM chapter defines the manifest). Add-in tools without their own tab go to Add-Ins › External Tools. - Add-in tabs are inserted after the Add-Ins tab by default; users can reorder them. - Add-in ribbon items are rejected if they reuse a built-in tab or panel id, except for the documented extension points addins/* and modify/addins. - An add-in that is not loaded (for example due to the licence check in TECH_STACK §4.2) contributes nothing to the ribbon. - Declared items. A manifest entry names a tab id (new, or the extension points), a panel id, and for each tool: command id, kind (§1.7.1), size variants, optional keytip and collapse priority. Icons are SVG files inside the add-in package; a missing icon falls back to a generic add-in glyph and logs a warning. - Id namespacing. Add-in tab and panel ids are prefixed with the add-in's namespace (addin.<namespace>.<id>), so two add-ins cannot collide. Two add-ins declaring the same display name get distinct tabs with the add-in name in the tooltip. - Validation. At load, every tool must reference a command the same add-in registers (or a built-in command); invalid entries are skipped and listed in the Add-in Manager's load report, and the rest of the add-in's ribbon still loads. - Discipline and priority. Add-in commands may declare discipline flags and are filtered by UI-RIB-007 like built-in ones. - Load and unload at run time. Enabling or disabling an add-in in the Add-in Manager (Ch. 2) rebuilds the ribbon without restart. User customisations that refer to an unloaded add-in (QAT items, moved panels, shortcuts) are kept and reappear when it loads again. - Limits. One add-in may contribute at most 3 tabs and 20 panels; extra entries are rejected with a load-report message.

    Commands. ui.ribbon.rebuild() -> () regenerates the ribbon from the registry, the default layout file and the user's customisations (used after add-in load/unload and by scripts); add-in ribbon entries themselves come from the manifest (Ch. 2).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Installing a sample add-in that declares a tab "Survey" with one panel shows that tab after Add-Ins on next start, and its button runs the add-in's command. - [ ] An add-in tool that names an unregistered command is skipped and reported, while the add-in's other tools appear. - [ ] Disabling the add-in removes its tab without restart; re-enabling it restores the tab and any QAT item the user had added from it.

    1.8 Ribbon catalog

    1.8.1 Catalog conventions

    ID: UI-RIBCAT-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §7 · screenshots/ui/ui_overview_annotated.png, screenshots/ui/ribbon_insert_tab_legacy.png, screenshots/ui/view_tab_windows_panel_canvas_theme.png

    Purpose. Define Reviera's default ribbon: its tabs, panels and tools, with the command each tool invokes and the owning chapter.

    Rules. - The ribbon default layout is a data file (ribbon-default.toml) shipped with Reviera and generated/validated against the registry at build time; a tool referencing an unknown command fails the build. - The tables below are normative for grouping and placement. Command ids for non-UI owners are the binding names the ribbon uses; if an owning chapter defines a different name, the owning chapter wins and this table is updated (tracked in §1.35). - Column meanings: Kind: L large, S small, I icon-only, Sp split member, Dd drop-down member, T toggle, G gallery, Dl dialog launcher, So slide-out item. Keys: Reviera default key sequence (§1.26.5). Pri: the tool's priority tier. P3 rows are listed only to record the decision not to ship them, with the open alternative. - Command arguments in braces (for example wall.create{structural}) mean "the same command with that preset argument". - Default tab order: File · Architecture · Structure · Steel · Concrete · Systems · Insert · Annotate · Analyze · Massing & Site · Collaborate · View · Manage · Add-Ins · Modify, then add-in tabs (after Add-Ins), then contextual tabs.

    1.9 Contextual tabs

    1.9.1 Contextual tab model

    ID: UI-CTX-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §8 · screenshots/ui/ribbon_contextual_tab.png, screenshots/ui/dark_theme_full_ui.png

    Purpose. Bring the tools relevant to the current selection or tool session to the ribbon automatically.

    Behaviour & rules. - A contextual tab appears whenever (a) one or more elements are selected, (b) an interactive tool session is active, or (c) an edit mode is active (sketch, group edit, in-place edit, reveal hidden, annotation isolation, viewport activation). - Its label follows the pattern "Modify · <Context>", where Context is the category name (plural) for selections ("Modify · Walls"), the tool name for placement ("Modify · Place Wall"), "Multi-Select" for mixed categories, or the edit mode name ("Modify · Edit Floor Boundary"). - The tab is drawn with the theme accent ribbon.contextual in both themes and remains at the right end of the tab row. Element-specific panels inside it carry the same accent on their title strip. - Content = the generic Modify panels (Select, Properties, Clipboard, Geometry, Modify, View, Measure, Create) filtered by availability, followed by context panels contributed by the owning chapters for that category, tool or mode, followed by tool option panels (§1.10). - Context panels are declared as data: each owning chapter registers (context selector, panel id, tools[]) entries. A context selector matches on category set, tool command id, or edit mode. The shell composes them; it does not hard-code any. - When selection and tool context change rapidly (for example dragging a crossing window), tab rebuilds are coalesced so the ribbon updates at most once per frame. - Generated contextual pages are cached by context key so that reselecting the same category does not rebuild widgets.

    Commands. ui.ribbon.get_contextual() -> {label, panels[]}, ui.ribbon.register_context_panel(selector, panel) (Lua add-ins, DM manifest).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Selecting a wall and a door shows "Modify · Multi-Select" with the Filter tool; selecting only doors shows "Modify · Doors" with the Host and Mode panels. - [ ] An add-in that registers a panel for the selector category = IfcWall sees its panel on "Modify · Walls".

    1.9.2 Default context panels

    ID: UI-CTX-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §8 table; Figure 20 screenshots/ui/revit2027_options_bar_removed.png

    The following context panels are part of the default layout. Owners are authoritative for their commands.
