    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] In any sketch mode, every non-sketch ribbon tool is disabled except navigation, view and the Mode panel; Esc twice or Cancel leaves the mode without changes.

    1.9.3 Edit modes and canvas feedback

    ID: UI-CTX-003 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §8 (final paragraph), §14

    Behaviour & rules. - Modal edit modes (sketch, group edit, in-place edit, family-in-context edit) take over the ribbon: only tools valid in the mode are enabled, and the mode's Finish/Cancel controls are always visible. - Elements not editable in the mode are drawn in the theme token canvas.editing_dimmed (a user-definable colour, default a desaturated tone of the background contrast colour) so the editable set stands out. - Leaving the mode by any route (Finish, Cancel, Esc twice, closing the view) is unambiguous; closing the view while in a mode prompts "Finish / Cancel / Stay". - Undo inside a mode undoes steps within the mode; after Finish, the whole mode session is one undo entry. - Mode stack. Modes can nest (for example a sketch inside a group edit). The context engine keeps them as a stack (UI-ARCH-003); Finish and Cancel act on the top mode only. The canvas label (§1.17.2) lists every level, innermost last, for example "Editing Group: Unit A › Edit Boundary". - What stays available. Navigation, view switching to views where the mode is valid, the View Control Bar, Properties of the edited object, Measure and the Modify tools that the mode declares. Commands that would change elements outside the mode are disabled with the reason "Not available while editing <mode>". Lua and MCP requests that would do so are queued (UI-API-006). - Esc handling. The first Esc ends the current drawing step; the second Esc, with no step active, asks the mode to cancel; if the mode has unsaved steps, a small in-canvas prompt "Discard changes? Esc again to discard, Enter to finish" appears rather than a dialog. - Finish validation. If the mode's owner rejects Finish (for example an open sketch loop), the mode stays active, the offending items are highlighted in canvas.alert, and the message from the owner is shown in the status bar and as a notice with "Continue editing" and "Cancel edit mode". - Crash recovery. Every edit mode is an interactive tool under §2.1 of the conventions; its micro-operations are journalled so that Resume sketch can restore it after a crash (UI-RECOV-001, DM-LIVE-015). - Model switching. Activating a view of a different model while in a mode prompts Finish / Cancel / Stay, as for closing the view.

    Commands. Finish and Cancel are owner commands (sketch.finish, sketch.cancel, group.finish, group.cancel, Ch. 3). The current mode stack is part of ui.get_state() (edit_mode, UI-API-002).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] During floor boundary sketching, walls are drawn in the dimmed editing colour and cannot be selected. - [ ] After Finish, one Undo removes the floor. - [ ] Finishing a floor sketch with an open loop keeps sketch mode and highlights the gap. - [ ] A sketch nested in a group edit shows both mode names in the canvas label; Finish ends only the sketch.

    1.9.4 Draw gallery

    ID: UI-CTX-004 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §7.14 (Draw)

    Behaviour & rules. - Tools that create curve-based elements or sketches show a Draw panel with: element line kinds valid for the context (Boundary Line, Model Line, Reference Line/Plane, Slope Arrow…), placement surface (Draw on Work Plane / Draw on Face) and a shape gallery: Line, Rectangle, Inscribed Polygon, Circumscribed Polygon, Circle, Start-End-Radius Arc, Centre-Ends Arc, Tangent End Arc, Fillet Arc, Spline, Ellipse, Partial Ellipse, Pick Lines, Pick Walls (or Pick Faces where valid). - The active shape is a tool option (shape) and is remembered per tool. - Shapes are drawing aids only: the submitted command receives curves (owner: ARC sketch.add_curve). - Availability. The owning tool declares which shapes it accepts. Shapes the tool cannot use are not shown (for example Spline is not offered for walls, Pick Walls is offered only where boundaries can follow walls). The default shape is the tool's first declared shape, normally Line. - Pick lines in the gallery create curves that keep a link to the picked edge where the owner supports it (shown by a lock glyph after picking); the tool option pick_lock (default off) makes that link a constraint. - Shape options. Each shape adds its own tool options (§1.10): number of sides and inscribed/circumscribed for polygons, radius on/off and value for arcs and fillets, Chain and Offset for open shapes, and Close loop for line chains. Options are remembered per tool and shape with persistence user. - Keyboard. The gallery is reachable through keytips; while a draw tool is active, Ctrl+Shift+O moves focus into the option controls (§1.10). Typed lengths and angles use listening dimensions (§1.22.1). - Micro-operations. Each click, typed value and shape change is recorded as a micro-operation of the active tool session, so an interrupted sketch can be replayed (conventions §2.1). - Placement surface. Draw on Work Plane uses the active work plane (Ch. 3); Draw on Face makes each pick select a face first. The choice is a tool option surface.

    Commands. tool.set_option("shape", line|rectangle|polygon_inscribed|polygon_circumscribed|circle|arc_3pt|arc_centre|arc_tangent|arc_fillet|spline|ellipse|ellipse_partial|pick_lines|pick_walls|pick_faces) and tool.get_options() while a draw tool is active; curves are submitted with the owner's commands.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Choosing Rectangle in Place Wall creates four joined walls with one click-pair. - [ ] Switching the floor sketch to Circle and back to Line keeps each shape's last radius and offset settings. - [ ] The wall tool's gallery does not offer Spline.

    1.10 Tool option presentation (no Options Bar)

    ID: UI-OPT-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §9 · screenshots/ui/options_bar.png, screenshots/ui/revit2027_options_bar_removed.png

    Purpose. Present the options of the active tool without a separate Options Bar row.

    Behaviour & rules. - Reviera has no Options Bar. Tool options (UI-ARCH-004) are rendered as: 1. Contextual ribbon panels, grouped by the option's group attribute (for example Placement, Constraint, Levels, Location). Controls are embedded wx controls sized for one-line use. 2. A Tool Options category at the top of the Properties palette, always expanded while a tool is active. - The two renderings are views of the same data; editing either updates the other immediately. - Options with keyboard relevance are reachable by keytips (for example Alt, then the option's keytip) and by Tab focus cycling from the canvas into the first option control with Ctrl+Shift+O (Reviera addition, returns to canvas on Enter or Esc). - A user preference "Show tool options in a strip below the ribbon" (P2) renders the same options as a single row for users who prefer that arrangement; it is off by default. - Lua and MCP read and write tool options with tool.get_options / tool.set_option.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Every option shown in the reference's Options Bar for wall, floor sketch, stair, tag, pipe and duct placement is available in the corresponding contextual panel. - [ ] Changing Location Line in the ribbon updates the Properties Tool Options row and the in-canvas preview. - [ ] With the P2 strip preference on, the same options appear in a single row and stay synchronised.

    1.11 Properties palette

    1.11.1 Palette structure and content rules

    ID: UI-PROP-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §10 · screenshots/ui/properties_palette_annotated.png, screenshots/ui/properties_filter_dropdown.png

    Purpose. View and edit the instance properties of whatever is in context, and reach type properties.

    UI (top to bottom). 1. Type Selector (§1.12). 2. Properties filter combo: "<Category> (n)", "Common (n)" for mixed selections, or "View: <name>" when nothing is selected. Choosing a category narrows the grid to that category without changing the selection. 3. Edit Type button: opens Type Properties for the shown entity's type. 4. Tool Options category (only while a tool session is active, §1.10). 5. Parameter grid: collapsible groups (Constraints, Construction, Graphics, Materials and Finishes, Dimensions, Identity Data, Phasing, Structural, Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing, Energy, Text, IFC, Other…) with two columns: name and value. 6. Footer: sort buttons (group order, A→Z, Z→A), Help link for the shown category, and Apply.

    What it shows.

    Context Content
    Nothing selected, no tool Active view's properties
    View selected in Project Browser That view's properties
    Tool session active Properties of the element about to be created (instance defaults) plus Tool Options
    One category selected Instance properties of the selection
    Several categories Only properties common to all; filter combo lists each category with counts
    Type selected in Project Browser Type properties, read-only, with an Edit Type button
    MEP element with Systems tab active System properties of its system
    Family editor document Family parameters for the active family
    Elements in a linked model Read-only instance properties, marked "Linked"

    Behaviour & rules. - Value editors: text; number with units (accepts unit suffixes and simple arithmetic like 3000+150 or 12'6", evaluated by the units service of Ch. 2); check box; enum combo (searchable as in §1.12); element reference combo (levels, phases, materials) with search; colour; "Edit…" buttons opening dialogs (Visibility/Graphics, View Range, Crop, Material); a small "associate global parameter" button on parameters that support it. - Read-only values are shaded and not focusable for editing; their tooltip states why ("computed", "controlled by view template", "owned by <user>"). - Mixed values show <varies> (text configurable in Manage › Additional Settings › Multiple Values Indication). Entering a value assigns it to all selected elements. - Parameters controlled by a view template show a lock badge and are read-only. - IFC group: shows GlobalId, IFC class and PredefinedType (read-only) and the property sets on the element, so users can see what will be exported. - Apply semantics: edits apply when the user presses Apply, presses Enter in the editor, or moves the pointer out of the palette (Auto-apply, default on; preference). Pending edits are marked with a change bar. Esc reverts pending edits. - Each Apply is one undo entry named "Edit properties (<n> elements)". - Zoom: Ctrl+wheel scales the grid font between 80 % and 200 %. - Sorting: in group order, project-defined parameters appear after built-in ones within each group, alphabetically by default (preference: creation order). - The palette is modeless and dockable (§1.15); hidden with PP, Ctrl+1, or View › User Interface.

    Data (IFC mapping). The palette displays and edits parameters as defined in Ch. 2 (property sets, quantities, and Reviera Extension Data). It adds no persistent data of its own.

    Commands. ui.properties.get(target?) -> PropertyGridModel (groups, rows, value, display string, editable flag, reason), ui.properties.set_filter(category|view), ui.properties.apply(), ui.properties.revert(). Property writes are performed by element.set_param(ids, {name: value}) (Ch. 2).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With nothing selected, the palette shows the active view's properties; selecting a view in the Project Browser shows that view's properties without activating it. - [ ] Selecting 3 walls with different heights shows <varies> for Unconnected Height; typing 3000 and Enter sets all three in one undo step. - [ ] Narrowing the filter to Doors in a mixed selection does not change the status-bar selection count. - [ ] Entering 2400+600 in a length field stores 3000 mm. - [ ] Moving the pointer out of the palette applies a pending edit when Auto-apply is on, and does not when it is off.

    1.11.2 Type Properties dialog entry points

    ID: UI-PROP-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §10 (Edit Type)

    Behaviour & rules. - Edit Type targets the type of the entity whose properties are shown (view type, tool's type, or selection's type). It is disabled when the selection contains more than one type, with a tooltip explaining why. - The ribbon's Type Properties button targets the selection's type or the type selected in the Project Browser. - The Type Properties dialog itself (duplicate, rename, preview, parameter grid) is owned by Ch. 2; the shell supplies only the entry points. - All entry points, each resolving the target type as stated:

    Entry point Target type
    Properties › Edit Type Type of the entity shown in the palette: the active tool's chosen type, the selection's single type, the browser-selected view's view type, or the active view's view type when nothing is selected
    Modify › Properties › Type Properties The selection's single type, or the type node selected in the Project Browser
    Project Browser › type node › Type Properties (or double-click when the double-click action is "Edit type properties", UI-SEL-005) That type
    Type Selector right-click › Type Properties The type under the pointer in the list
    Canvas right-click on a single-type selection › Type Properties The selection's type
    • Disabled cases, each with its reason in the tooltip: several types selected ("Selected elements have different types"); elements without types (for example model lines in some contexts: "This element has no type"); linked elements ("Types of linked models are read-only" — the dialog still opens read-only from the browser); BIMserver elements owned by another user (the dialog opens read-only, "Owned by <user>").
    • During a tool session, editing the type of the tool's chosen type affects the next placements; Duplicate in the dialog switches the tool to the new type on OK.
    • Undo. OK in the dialog is one undo entry; Cancel discards every change made in the dialog, including duplicates.
    • Narrowed filter. When the Properties filter is narrowed to one category of a mixed selection (UI-PROP-001), Edit Type targets the single type of that category, if there is one.

    Commands. type.edit_properties(type_id?) (Ch. 2; defaults to the type resolved above).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With two wall types selected, Edit Type is disabled and its tooltip says "Selected elements have different types". - [ ] With a door and a wall selected and the filter narrowed to Doors, Edit Type opens the door's type. - [ ] Duplicating a type from Edit Type during wall placement makes the next wall use the new type.

    1.12 Type Selector

    ID: UI-TYPE-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §10.1 · screenshots/ui/type_selector_search.png

    Purpose. Choose the type to place, or change the type of the selected elements.

    Behaviour & rules. - Shown at the top of Properties when a placement tool is active or the selection contains elements that can share a type. It displays a preview image, the family name and the type name. - Opening it focuses a search field. Words may be typed in any order; matching is case-insensitive and matched characters are highlighted. Results are grouped by family with thumbnails. - Keys: Down/Tab moves into the list; Up/Down/Tab/Shift+Tab move; Enter chooses; Esc first clears the search, then closes. Home/End/PageUp/PageDown move by item or page. - Choosing a type for a selection changes it immediately (no Apply) as one undo step; incompatible elements are skipped with a status-bar message. - The list shows recently used types at the top (last 5, per category, per user). - The same searchable-list control is used for every long combo in the shell (property enum values, dialog tables, category pickers). - Right-click menu: Add to Quick Access Toolbar (adds a compact type combo to the QAT) and Add to Modify Tab (adds a type gallery panel).

    Commands. ui.type_selector.list(category|tool) -> [TypeEntry]; type changes are performed by element.set_type(ids, type_id) (Ch. 2); for an active tool, tool.set_option("type_id", id).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Typing "200 conc" finds "Concrete 200mm" in a list of 300 wall types within 50 ms. - [ ] Changing the type of 20 selected doors is one undo step.

    1.13 Project Browser

    1.13.1 Tree, tabs and search

    ID: UI-PB-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §11 · screenshots/ui/project_browser_search.gif, screenshots/ui/ui_insert_tab_floor_plan.png

    Purpose. Navigate and manage every view, sheet, schedule, family, group and link in the model.

    UI. - Title: "Project Browser — <model name>". - Search box (Ctrl+F when the canvas or browser has focus): live filtering, matches highlighted at every tree level, arrow keys move through results, Enter opens. - Tab strip (icon toggles): All, Views, Legends, Schedules, Sheets, Families, Groups, Links; dynamic tabs Panel Schedules, Reports, Assemblies, Server Revisions (the last in BIMserver mode) appear when such items exist. Search covers all tabs. - Top-level nodes (All tab): Views (by current organisation scheme), Legends, Schedules/Quantities, Sheets, Families (category › family › type), Groups (Model, Detail), Links, Assemblies, Panel Schedules, Reports, Coordination Models. - The active view is bold. Sheet placement icons show whether a view is on a sheet, not placed, or (for schedules and legends) placed on several sheets; they can be turned off from the right-click menu.

    Interactions.

    Action Gesture Command
    Open view Double-click, Enter, or right-click › Open; multiple selected views open together after a confirmation (with "don't ask again") view.open (Ch. 5)
    Rename Slow double-click, F2, right-click › Rename view.rename (Ch. 5), type.rename, family.rename (Ch. 2)
    Open hosting sheet Right-click › Open Sheet (disabled when not placed or placed on several sheets) sheet.open_for_view (Ch. 5)
    Place view on sheet Drag view onto a sheet node or into an open sheet; or right-click a sheet › Add View; the viewport follows the cursor until clicked sheet.place_view (Ch. 5)
    Remove from sheet Right-click the view under a sheet › Remove from Sheet viewport.remove (Ch. 5)
    New sheet Right-click Sheets › New Sheet sheet.create (Ch. 5)
    Duplicate view Right-click › Duplicate View › Duplicate / With Detailing / As Dependent view.duplicate (Ch. 5)
    Find referring views Right-click › Find Referring Views view.find_referring (Ch. 5)
    Expand / collapse Right-click › Expand Selected, Collapse Selected, Expand All, Collapse All; keyboard Right/Left, * —
    List zoom Ctrl+wheel —
    Family type actions Right-click › Select All Instances (in View / in Project), Type Properties, Duplicate, Rename, Delete, Reload, Edit; drag a type into a view to place it selection.select_all_instances, type.*, family.* (Ch. 2), component.place
    Group actions Drag to place; right-click › Delete, Rename, Select All Instances, Properties, Duplicate, Reload, Save Group group.* (Ch. 3)
    Link actions Right-click › Add Link, Manage Links, Create Instance, Reload, Reload From, Unload (for everyone / for me) link.* (Ch. 6)
    Rendered images Drag onto a sheet sheet.place_image (Ch. 5)
    Delete Delete key or right-click › Delete (with confirmation listing dependent items) view.delete, sheet.delete (Ch. 5)
    • Find in Project Browser: from the canvas, right-click an element or view › Find in Project Browser (FF) reveals and selects its node (views, sheets, legends, families including nested families, groups, links, assembly views, view references and schedules on sheets).
    • Selecting a node shows its properties in the Properties palette without opening it (UI-PROP-001).
    • The browser is virtualised: models with 20 000 views and 5 000 family types must expand and filter interactively.

    Data. Expansion state, active tab and scroll position are project-scoped UI data stored as an RXD document (§1.29.2); organisation schemes are defined in Ch. 5 and stored as RXD per Ch. 2.

    Commands. browser.search(text) -> [node], browser.reveal(element_or_view_id), browser.expand(node_id, recursive?), browser.collapse(node_id|all), browser.set_tab(tab_id), browser.get_tree(tab_id?, depth?) -> tree, browser.get_selected() -> [node].

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Typing "lev" highlights "Level 1", "Level 2" and any family named "Leveller" in under 100 ms in a model with 5 000 views. - [ ] Dragging a floor plan onto a sheet node opens the sheet and attaches the viewport to the cursor. - [ ] FF on a selected door reveals its type node under Families › Doors. - [ ] Reopening a model restores the browser's expanded nodes from its RXD.

    1.13.2 Browser organisation dialog

    ID: UI-PB-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/01 §11 (Browser Organization)

    Behaviour & rules. - View › Windows › User Interface › Browser Organization opens a dialog with three tabs (Views, Sheets, Schedules), each listing organisation schemes with radio buttons for the active scheme and New / Edit / Rename / Delete. - Editing a scheme opens a two-page dialog: Filtering (up to 3 rules: parameter, operator, value, combined with AND) and Grouping & Sorting (up to 6 group levels, each with parameter, "use first N characters" option, and a final sort parameter and direction). Any view, sheet or schedule parameter, including project and shared parameters, may be used. - The top node of each list shows the active scheme name, for example "Views (by Discipline)". - The dialog is a front end to browser.create_organization, browser.set_organization and related commands defined in Ch. 5; scheme definitions are stored as RXD. Which scheme is active can be a project default (RXD) and a per-user override (user config). - Schemes transfer between models with Transfer Project Standards (Ch. 2).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A scheme grouping views by Discipline then by the first 2 characters of View Name reorganises the tree immediately on OK. - [ ] Switching active scheme is undoable when it changes the project default, and not undoable when it changes only the per-user override.

    1.14 System Browser

    ID: UI-SB-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/01 §12

    Purpose. Show MEP systems, zones and analytical systems as a tree, and find unassigned components.

    UI. - Opened with F9, View › User Interface › System Browser, or canvas right-click › Browsers › System Browser. Docked at the bottom of the centre area by default. - View selector: Systems | Zones | Analytical Systems. In Systems view, a discipline filter: All / Mechanical / Piping / Electrical. - Toolbar: Auto-fit columns (double-click a header also fits) and Column Settings (per discipline category: General, Mechanical, Piping, Electrical; show/hide and order). - Tree: System classification › System › Components, plus an Unassigned folder per discipline. - In Analytical Systems view: Add Zone Equipment, Add Air System, Add Water Loop (Ch. 4 commands).

    Behaviour & rules. - Hovering a row pre-highlights the element in every open view where it is visible. - Selection is synchronised both ways with the canvas; Ctrl/Shift multi-select works. - Row right-click: Expand / Expand All / Collapse / Collapse All; Select (in canvas); Show (opens or cycles through views containing the element, zooming to it); Delete; Properties. - The tree updates incrementally after each committed transaction.

    Commands. sysbrowser.get_tree(view: systems|zones|analytical, discipline?) -> tree, sysbrowser.show_element(element_id) (cycles views); system data commands are owned by Ch. 4.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A newly placed air terminal not connected to a duct appears under Unassigned › Mechanical within one second of placement. - [ ] Choosing Show on a pipe opens a view that contains it and zooms to it; choosing Show again moves to the next such view.

    1.15 Docking

    1.15.1 Dockable panes

    ID: UI-DOCK-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §13 · screenshots/ui/dockable_windows_grouped.png

    Purpose. Let users arrange palettes and browsers freely.

    Behaviour & rules. - Dockable panes: Properties, Project Browser, System Browser, Agent (§1.31), Notifications, Server Projects and Revision History (§1.32), Lua Console, BCF Issues, Fabrication Parts, P&ID Modeler, Reconcile Hosting, Background Tasks, and add-in panes declared in manifests. - Docking gestures: drag a pane by its caption; a translucent outline and dock guides show the landing position. Drop at a window edge to dock there; drop on another pane's caption to group as tabs; drop on the lower half of a pane to stack below it. Holding Ctrl while dragging suppresses docking. Double-clicking a caption toggles docked/floating. - Grouped panes show their tabs along the bottom of the group. - Panes and view windows cannot be grouped together. - Each pane has a caption menu: Float, Dock, Auto-hide (collapse to an edge tab that slides out on hover), Close. - Floating panes can be moved to any monitor and keep their position across sessions (§1.29).

    wx realisation. wxAuiManager with wxAuiPaneInfo per pane; grouping uses AUI notebook docking; the dock guides are the AUI "hint" window drawn with theme tokens.

    Commands. ui.pane.list() -> [{id, visible, docked, floating, rect, group}], ui.pane.show(id), ui.pane.hide(id), ui.pane.toggle(id), ui.pane.float(id, rect?), ui.pane.dock(id, side, position?), ui.pane.group(id, with_id).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Dragging Project Browser onto the Properties caption groups them as tabs; double-clicking the Properties tab caption floats only Properties. - [ ] Holding Ctrl while dragging Properties near the left edge leaves it floating.

    1.15.2 Hiding chrome

    ID: UI-DOCK-004 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §13 (Hiding chrome), §7.11

    Behaviour & rules. - View › Windows › User Interface lists check boxes for: Orientation Cube, Navigation Bar, Project Browser, System Browser, Properties, Status Bar, Status Bar – Worksets, Status Bar – Design Options, Agent, Notifications, Lua Console, plus discipline panes (Fabrication Parts, P&ID Modeler, Reconcile Hosting) and add-in panes. - Focus mode (Reviera addition, P1, Ctrl+Shift+F11): hides all panes, the status bar and collapses the ribbon to tabs; pressing again restores the previous arrangement. - Chrome element ids. Each check box maps to an id used by commands, layout bookmarks and scenarios: orientation_cube, navigation_bar, status_bar, status_bar.worksets, status_bar.design_options, view_control_bar, view_tabs, qat, plus every pane id of UI-DOCK-001 (properties, project_browser, system_browser, agent, notifications, lua_console, history, …). Panes are shown and hidden with ui.pane.*; the other ids with ui.chrome.set_visible. - What hiding does. Hiding a pane keeps its dock position and size, so showing it again restores it where it was. Hiding the Orientation Cube or Navigation Bar applies to every view window, including floating frames. Hiding the View Control Bar or view tabs is allowed only through ui.chrome.set_visible and the Presentation layout (UI-LAYOUT-002); the menu shows them so the user can bring them back. - Never hidden. The ribbon tab row and the canvas cannot be hidden (§1.2). The File button stays reachable with Alt, F. - Focus mode details. It remembers the exact pre-focus state, including floating panes and the ribbon state, in memory only. Leaving it (Ctrl+Shift+F11, Esc with nothing selected and no tool, or the "Exit focus mode" chip at the top-right of the canvas) restores that state. Applying a layout bookmark while in focus mode leaves focus mode first. Focus mode does not persist across restart. - Storage. Visibility flags are stored in layout.toml and are the Visible panels part of a layout bookmark (UI-LAYOUT-001).

    Commands. ui.chrome.get() -> {element_id: bool}, ui.chrome.set_visible(element_id, visible: bool) -> (), ui.focus_mode.toggle() -> (); panes use ui.pane.show, ui.pane.hide and ui.pane.toggle (UI-DOCK-001).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Unticking Status Bar hides it; re-ticking restores it at the same height. - [ ] Focus mode toggles twice back to the identical layout. - [ ] Hiding the Navigation Bar removes it from a floating view frame on a second monitor as well. - [ ] Hiding Properties, restarting, and showing it again restores it at its previous dock position and width.

    1.16 View windows: tabs, tiling, splits and multiple monitors

    1.16.1 Tabbed view windows

    ID: UI-VIEWWIN-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §13 · screenshots/ui/tab_views.png

    Behaviour & rules. - Every open view, sheet or schedule has its own tab showing a view-kind icon, the view name, a model badge when several models are open, and a close button. A view open in two windows is not allowed; activating an already-open view focuses its tab. - When tabs overflow, a drop-down at the right of the tab strip lists all tabs (searchable). - Drag tabs to reorder; drag a tab to a window edge or onto another tab group to split (left, right, top, bottom). - Tab right-click menu: Close, Close Others, Close All, Close All in This Model, Float, Move to New Window, Dock to Main Window, Find in Project Browser, Copy View Name. - Middle-click on a tab closes it. - Closing the last view of a model asks whether to close the model. - View switching order for Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab: tab position or most recently used (Options › User Interface). Ctrl+Tab cycles through all views including floating windows; holding Ctrl shows a switcher overlay listing views.

    Commands. view.activate(view_id, {new_window?: bool, float?: bool, monitor?: int}) -> window_id (opens the view if needed, via view.open of Ch. 5, then focuses it); view.close(view_id); view.close_inactive(); window.list() -> [{window_id, view_id, model_id, frame_id, rect, active}]; window.switch(view_id) (alias of view.activate for the Switch Windows menu); window.next(direction).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Opening 40 views shows an overflow drop-down that lists all 40. - [ ] With MRU order selected, Ctrl+Tab returns to the previously active view. - [ ] view.activate from MCP on a closed view opens and focuses it, returning its window id.

    1.16.2 Tile, tab-all and close-inactive

    ID: UI-VIEWWIN-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §13 · screenshots/ui/tile_views.gif

    Behaviour & rules. - Tile Views (WT) arranges all view windows docked in the main frame into a near-square grid; Tab Views (TW) merges all docked view windows back into one tab group. Neither affects floating windows. - Zoom All to Fit (ZA) fits every visible view window. - Close Inactive Views keeps, per model: the focused view in each tile, at least one view per open model or family, and all floating windows; everything else closes. - Editing in one tile updates all tiles live after the transaction commits. - Switch Windows lists open views grouped by model with a check mark on the active one. - Tile grid rule. For n docked view windows, Tile uses c = ceil(sqrt(n)) columns and r = ceil(n / c) rows, filled left to right in tab order; the last row's tiles share the full width. Each tile keeps its own View Control Bar and zoom. Tiling 1 view does nothing; tiling more than 16 views is allowed but each tile is clamped to a minimum of 240 × 180 logical pixels, and tiles beyond what fits stay as tabs in the last tile. - Tab Views keeps the active view active and orders tabs as they were before tiling. - Zoom All to Fit applies Zoom to Fit to every visible tile (including floating frames), not to hidden tabs; it adds one entry to each view's navigation history. - Close Inactive Views never closes a view with an active edit mode or tool session, and never closes the last view of a family editor document. Views it closes keep their RXD navigation state (§1.29.2). It shows "Closed n views" in the status bar. - Switch Windows with more than 30 open views adds a search field at the top of the list. - All four commands are presentation only: no undo entry, no modified flag.

    Commands. window.tile(), window.tab_all(), view.zoom_all_to_fit(), view.close_inactive(), window.switch(view_id) (UI-VIEWWIN-001).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With 4 views open, Tile Views shows a 2 × 2 grid; Tab Views restores a single tab group. - [ ] Close Inactive Views with 2 models open leaves at least one view per model. - [ ] With 5 views open, Tile Views gives 3 columns over 2 rows, and the two tiles in the second row share its full width. - [ ] Close Inactive Views does not close a view in which a floor sketch is active.

    1.16.3 Floating windows and multiple monitors

    ID: UI-VIEWWIN-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/01 §13 · screenshots/ui/multi_monitor_views.png

    Behaviour & rules. - Dragging a tab outside the main window (or choosing Float / Move to New Window) creates a secondary frame containing its own tab area, View Control Bar, Orientation Cube and Navigation Bar. Further tabs can be dropped into it. - Secondary frames have no ribbon; keyboard shortcuts and the main ribbon act on whichever view window has focus. - Secondary frames appear in the operating system's window list and task switcher as "Reviera — <view name>". - Dock to Main Window (tab menu) returns a view to the main frame. - Each frame handles its own DPI (§1.33.3). Moving a frame between monitors with different scale factors re-lays it out without restarting. - Layout persistence records each floating frame's monitor and rectangle; if that monitor is missing at restore, the frame is placed on the primary monitor at the same relative position, clamped to be fully visible.

    Commands. window.float(view_id, rect?, monitor?), window.dock_to_main(view_id), ui.monitors() -> [{index, rect, scale, primary}].

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A view floated onto a 200 %-scale second monitor renders sharply and its controls are correctly sized. - [ ] Disconnecting the second monitor and restarting places the floating frame on the primary monitor, fully visible.

    1.17 Canvas (drawing area)

    1.17.1 Canvas host and rendering contract

    ID: UI-CANVAS-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §14; TECH_STACK §3.2

    Purpose. Display views, sheets and schedules and host all direct-manipulation feedback.

    Behaviour & rules. - Each view window contains one canvas: a native child window handed to the wgpu renderer (TECH_STACK §3.2, §5.2). Schedules use a grid control instead of the GPU canvas (Ch. 5). - The renderer draws, in order: model and annotation content (Ch. 5); overlay pass for pre-highlight, selection, temporary dimensions, grips, snap glyphs, alignment lines, rubber-band rectangles, mode border and label, Orientation Cube, Navigation Bar, Navigation Wheel; then the in-canvas text editor (a native control positioned on top). - Overlay drawing never waits for model regeneration: during a long transaction the last committed scene remains navigable and overlays stay live. - Refresh (F5) redraws all views from current data. - Views not currently visible stay open with their state; their GPU resources may be released under memory pressure and recreated on activation. - Target interaction performance: ≥ 30 frames per second while navigating a 3D view of 1 million triangles on reference hardware (defined in Ch. 0 non-functional requirements), with "simplify during navigation" allowed to drop detail.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] During a 5-second regeneration, hovering elements still pre-highlights them from the last committed scene. - [ ] F5 redraws every visible view.

    1.17.2 Canvas colours and mode indicators

    ID: UI-CANVAS-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §14, §25 · screenshots/ui/temporary_hide_isolate.gif, screenshots/ui/dark_theme_full_ui.png, screenshots/ui/dark_theme_black_canvas_2023.png

    Behaviour & rules. - Canvas colours are theme tokens (§1.28): canvas.background, canvas.selection (with "semi-transparent" flag), canvas.preselection, canvas.alert, canvas.calculating, canvas.editing_dimmed, canvas.reveal_hidden, canvas.temp_mode_border, canvas.temp_view_props_border, canvas.reveal_constraints_border, canvas.displacement_border. - With a dark background, linework drawn in black (or near-black, luminance < 15 %) is displayed in the inverse colour; other colours are kept unless the user enables "adapt colours to background" (P1). - Mode indicators: whenever a view is in a temporary state, Reviera draws a coloured frame inside the view border and a text label in the top-left corner naming the state(s), so colour is never the only signal:

    State Border token Label text
    Temporary Hide/Isolate active canvas.temp_mode_border "Temporary Hide/Isolate"
    Reveal Hidden Elements canvas.reveal_hidden (hidden elements also drawn in this colour) "Reveal Hidden Elements"
    Temporary View Properties canvas.temp_view_props_border "Temporary View Properties"
    Reveal Constraints canvas.reveal_constraints_border "Reveal Constraints"
    Highlight Displacement Sets canvas.displacement_border "Displacement Sets"
    Isolate Annotations canvas.temp_mode_border "Annotations Isolated"
    Sketch / group / in-place edit none (dimming instead) mode name, e.g. "Editing Group: Unit A"
    • Several states stack: labels are listed one per line; the border shows the most recent.
    • Defaults are chosen to be distinguishable for common colour-vision deficiencies (§1.33).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Activating Temporary Isolate shows both the frame and the label; the label is read by the platform screen reader when the view gains focus. - [ ] Switching to the dark canvas draws black wall cut lines in white.

    1.18 View Control Bar

    ID: UI-VCB-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §15 · screenshots/ui/view_control_bar.gif, screenshots/ui/temporary_hide_isolate.gif

    Purpose. Per-view graphic controls, always at hand at the bottom-left of each view window.

    Behaviour & rules. - Shown at the bottom of every view window (main and secondary frames), left of the horizontal scroll bar. Contents depend on the view kind; controls whose property is governed by an applied view template are disabled with a tooltip naming the template. - Controls (owner of the underlying command in brackets):

    # Control Behaviour Command (owner) Pri
    1 Scale Text button ("1:100"); list of standard scales for the project's unit system plus Custom…; hidden in perspective views view.set_property(view, "Scale", v) (DOC) P0
    2 Detail Level Coarse / Medium / Fine view.set_property(…"DetailLevel") (DOC) P0
    3 Visual Style Wireframe, Hidden Line, Shaded, Shaded with Edges, Consistent Colours, Textures, Realistic, Path-traced (3D only, P2), Graphic Display Options… view.set_property(…"VisualStyle"), view.set_graphic_display (DOC) P0
    4 Sun Path On / Off / Sun Settings… view.set_property(…"SunPath"), sun.settings (DOC) P1
    5 Shadows On / Off view.set_property(…"Shadows") (DOC) P1
    6 Render Opens the render dialog (3D only) render.start (DOC) P2
    7 Crop View Toggle cropping view.set_property(…"CropEnabled") (DOC) P0
    8 Show Crop Region Toggle crop boundary visibility view.set_property(…"CropVisible") (DOC) P0
    9 Lock 3D View Save Orientation and Lock / Restore Orientation and Lock / Unlock view.lock_3d, view.restore_orientation (DOC) P1
    10 Temporary Hide/Isolate With a selection: Isolate Category (IC), Hide Category (HC), Isolate Element (HI), Hide Element (HH). While active: Reset (HR), Apply to View view.temp_isolate, view.temp_hide, view.temp_reset (UI); view.temp_apply (UI → DOC view.hide_elements) P0
    11 Reveal Hidden Elements Toggles reveal mode with its contextual tab view.reveal_hidden.toggle (UI) P0
    12 Collaboration Display BIMserver mode only: Off, Ownership Status, Owners, Model Updates (changed since my last Get Latest), Worksets, Settings… view.set_worksharing_display(mode) (COL) P1
    13 Temporary View Properties Enable, Temporarily Apply Template…, Restore View Properties, recent templates view.temp_properties.* (DOC) P1
    14 Show Analytical Model Structural/MEP analytical views view.set_property(…"ShowAnalytical") (ANA) P2
    15 Highlight Displacement Sets Toggle view.highlight_displacement (DOC) P2
    16 Reveal Constraints Toggle (CX) view.reveal_constraints.toggle (UI) P1
    17 Preview Visibility Family editor only family_doc.preview_visibility.toggle (DM) P1
    18 Thin Lines Mirror of the global toggle (TL) for quick access ui.thin_lines.toggle (UI) P0
    • Temporary hide/isolate is session state of the view window: it does not change the model, is not undoable, does not affect printing or export, and is cleared when the model closes unless converted with Apply to View (which becomes a normal undoable DOC command).
    • Reveal hidden mode draws hidden elements in canvas.reveal_hidden, adds the "Reveal Hidden Elements" contextual tab (§1.9.2), and is session state.
    • The bar's buttons are keyboard reachable (F6 cycles focus between ribbon, panes, canvas and the View Control Bar; arrow keys move within it).

    Commands. view.temp_isolate(view_id?, element_ids|category_ids, by: element|category), view.temp_hide(view_id?, element_ids|category_ids, by), view.temp_reset(view_id? (default: active)) -> (), view.temp_apply(view_id? (default: active)) -> (), view.reveal_hidden.toggle(view_id?), view.reveal_constraints.toggle(view_id?), view.get_temp_state(view_id?) -> {hidden[], isolated[], reveal, constraints}.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] HI on two selected walls isolates them in the active view only; printing that view prints all elements. - [ ] Apply to View converts the temporary state into permanent hidden elements in one undo step. - [ ] On a view with a template controlling Detail Level, the Detail Level control is disabled and its tooltip names the template.

    1.19 Navigation

    1.19.1 Mouse, keyboard and 3D input devices

    ID: UI-NAV-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §16.1

    Behaviour & rules. - Middle-drag pans; wheel zooms about the cursor; double-click middle zooms to fit. - Shift + middle-drag (3D) orbits about the pivot: the selection's centre if something is selected, else the model's visible extents centre, else a user-defined centre set with Define Centre of Rotation (R3, right-click in 3D). - Ctrl + Shift + middle-drag (3D, Reviera addition) looks around from the eye point in perspective views. - F8 starts orbit with the left button until Esc (for users without a middle button). A preference offers left-button navigation profile for trackpads: Alt+drag orbit, Alt+Ctrl+drag pan (P1). - Trackpads: two-finger scroll pans, pinch zooms, Shift+two-finger scroll orbits in 3D (P1). - Zoom commands: Zoom In Region (ZR), Zoom Out 2× (ZO), Zoom to Fit (ZF), Zoom All to Fit (ZA), Zoom Sheet Size (ZS), Previous Pan/Zoom (ZP), Next Pan/Zoom (ZN, Reviera addition). - Each view keeps a navigation history of up to 50 states for Previous/Next. - 3D mice (6-DoF devices) are supported through the open device protocol available on each platform (for example spacenavd on Linux) with modes 2D, Object, Walk and Fly (P2). - Navigation does not create undo entries and does not mark the model modified. The latest camera of each view is kept as view state: it goes to the live store at once (Ch. 2b), and is written to the RXD document views/state (latest camera and Home per view, by view id) along with the next save that happens for any other reason. A view's saved camera in views/<viewId> changes only through edits such as view.set_camera; when it changes after the latest navigation, the saved camera wins. Closing a model whose only changes are navigation does not prompt to save. An explicit view.set_camera call (from a script, an agent, or Save Orientation) is an ordinary undoable edit that marks the model modified. In BIMserver mode, navigation never causes a check-in, and the default 3D view is per user.

    Commands. view.zoom(view_id?, mode: in_region|out|fit|all_fit|sheet_size|previous|next, rect?), view.pan(view_id?, dx, dy), view.orbit(view_id?, yaw_deg, pitch_deg, pivot?), view.set_camera(view_id, eye, target, up, projection?: orthographic|perspective, fov?) -> (), view.get_camera(view_id) -> Camera, view.set_pivot(view_id, point), view.zoom_to_elements(view_id?, element_ids).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Wheel zoom keeps the model point under the cursor fixed to within one pixel. - [ ] Shift+middle-drag with a door selected orbits about the door. - [ ] view.zoom_to_elements from MCP frames the given elements in the active view.

    1.19.2 Orientation Cube

    ID: UI-NAV-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §16.2, §24.10 · screenshots/ui/viewcube.png

    Behaviour & rules. - Shown in a corner of 3D views (default top-right). Semi-transparent when idle (configurable inactive opacity), opaque on hover. - Clicking any of its 26 regions (6 faces, 12 edges, 8 corners) animates to that orientation; dragging orbits freely; in face views, roll arrows rotate 90° and adjacent-face arrows step to neighbouring faces. - A projection button (Reviera addition, owner request) shows the current projection, PERSP or ISO, and switches between perspective and isometric (parallel) projection with one click. The same toggle is in the View menu and in the right-click menu, and has the keyboard sequence PI. - A Home button returns to the view's home orientation; a compass ring below shows N/E/S/W (project north or true north per view setting); clicking a letter faces that direction; dragging the ring rotates about the vertical axis. - Right-click menu: Go Home; Save View (creates a named 3D view, DOC); Lock to Selection; Perspective / Orthographic; Set Current View as Home; Set Front to View ▸; Reset Front; Show Compass; Orient to View ▸ (any plan, elevation, section or 3D view; adds a section box when orienting to a plan or section); Orient to Direction ▸ (N, S, E, W, NE, NW, SE, SW, Top, Bottom); Orient to a Plane…; Help; Options…. - Face labels use the project's localisation; their content is generated text, not artwork. - Options (§1.27): show/hide; all 3D views or active only; position (4 corners); size (Auto, Tiny, Small, Normal, Large); inactive opacity (0–100 %); snap to closest view when dragging; fit to view on change; animated transitions (and their duration); keep scene upright; show compass. - Keyboard: when the canvas has focus, Alt+Home goes home; Alt+numpad keys choose faces (P1 accessibility addition).

    Commands. view.orient(view_id?, preset: top|bottom|front|back|left|right|ne_iso|…|home), view.orient_to_view(view_id?, source_view_id, add_section_box?), view.orient_to_direction(view_id?, dir), view.set_home(view_id?), view.set_projection(view_id?, perspective|orthographic).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Each of the 26 regions produces a distinct, correct orientation. - [ ] Orient to View › Level 1 plan produces a top-down 3D view with a section box matching the plan's view range. - [ ] With inactive opacity 0 %, the cube appears only on hover.

    1.19.3 Navigation Bar

    ID: UI-NAV-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/01 §16.3 · screenshots/ui/navigation_bar.png

    Behaviour & rules. - A slim vertical bar along one edge of each view window (drawn by the overlay pass) with: Orientation Cube toggle, Navigation Wheel (split: 2D, Full, View Object, Tour Building, mini variants), Pan Active View (only on an activated viewport on a sheet), Zoom (split with the zoom commands, last used remembered), 3D Mouse (when a device is present), Fly (perspective views). - Customise menu at the bottom: tick which tools show; Docking ▸ Link to Orientation Cube / Top / Bottom / Left / Right (top/bottom makes it horizontal); dragging along an edge also repositions it. - Hidden with View › User Interface › Navigation Bar. - Default. Shown in every 3D view and every 2D view window, docked to the right edge and linked to the Orientation Cube (it sits just below the cube in 3D views and at the top of the right edge in 2D views). Tools that do not apply to the view are hidden rather than disabled: the Orientation Cube toggle and Fly in 2D views, Pan Active View except on an activated viewport. - Split tools. Navigation Wheel and Zoom are split buttons whose main part runs the last-used member, remembered per user, as on the ribbon (UI-RIB-001). - Linked docking. When linked to the Orientation Cube, moving the cube to another corner moves the bar with it. When docked to the top or bottom edge, the bar is horizontal and its tools appear in the same order left to right. - Opacity. The bar uses the same inactive opacity as the Orientation Cube (§1.19.2) and becomes opaque on hover; it never covers the View Control Bar or scroll bars. - Keyboard. The bar's tools are commands with their own shortcuts (view.zoom modes, ui.nav.wheel, ui.nav.device_mode), so the bar is never the only way to reach them; it is skipped in the F6 focus cycle. - Persistence. Customise choices and docking position are per user, stored in settings.toml, and are part of the Canvas chrome part of a layout bookmark.

    Commands. ui.navbar.get() -> {tools[], dock: linked|top|bottom|left|right}, ui.navbar.set(patch) -> (); visibility with ui.chrome.set_visible("navigation_bar", …) (UI-DOCK-004).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Unticking Navigation Wheel in Customise removes it from every view's bar and persists. - [ ] Moving the Orientation Cube to the bottom-left corner moves a linked Navigation Bar to the left edge below the cube. - [ ] Docking the bar to the top makes it horizontal in every open view window. - [ ] A 2D plan view's bar shows no Orientation Cube toggle and no Fly tool.

    1.19.4 Navigation Wheel

    ID: UI-NAV-004 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/01 §16.4 · screenshots/ui/steeringwheel_full_navigation.png, screenshots/ui/steeringwheel_2d.png

    Behaviour & rules. - A radial tracking menu that follows the cursor. Wedges start a navigation tool on press, act while dragging and end on release. - Wheels: 2D (Zoom, Pan, Rewind) — the only wheel in 2D views; Full (Zoom, Rewind, Pan, Orbit, Centre, Walk, Look, Up/Down) big and mini; View Object (Centre, Zoom, Rewind, Orbit); Tour Building (Forward, Look, Rewind, Up/Down). - While a wheel is open, middle-drag pans, wheel zooms and Shift+middle orbits as usual. - Rewind shows a strip of thumbnails of earlier view states; dragging along it restores any of them. - Wheel right-click menu: switch wheel; Fit to Window; Restore Original Centre; Level Camera; Increase/Decrease Walk Speed; Orient to View; Orient to a Plane; Undo View Orientation Changes; Save View; Increase/Decrease Focal Length; Move/Re-centre Crop Boundary; Help; Options; Close Wheel. - Options (§1.27): text visibility (messages, tooltips, cursor text); big and mini size and opacity; invert look vertical axis; walk parallel to ground; walk speed factor; zoom by one step per click; keep scene upright when orbiting. - The wheel is drawn by the overlay pass in Reviera's own visual design; it shall not reproduce reference artwork.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Shift+W (or the Navigation Bar) opens the Full wheel at the cursor; dragging the Orbit wedge orbits; releasing ends the tool with the wheel still shown; Esc closes it. - [ ] Rewind restores a view state from 10 steps earlier.

    1.20 Status bar

    Purpose. Show prompts, progress, mode state and selection controls.

    Elements (left to right).
