    Active Option Only Restrict selection to the active design option selection.options.set{active_option_only} (UI) P1
    Exclude Options Exclude design-option elements from selection selection.options.set{exclude_options} (UI) P1
    Editable Only Restrict selection to elements the user may edit (ownership) selection.options.set{editable_only} (UI) P1
    Select Links / Underlay / Pinned / by Face / Drag on Selection Five selection toggles (§1.21.4) selection.options.set{…} (UI) P0
    Background Tasks Spinner while background tasks run (colour fills, analysis, background export, server sync); click lists tasks with progress and Cancel; warning icon when background processing is disabled ui.background_tasks (UI), F11 P0
    Agent activity Shows when an MCP/agent session is connected or running a command; click opens the Agent pane or the MCP sessions list §1.31 P1
    Selection count / Filter Funnel with the number of selected elements; click opens the Filter dialog selection.filter_dialog (UI) P0

    Behaviour & rules. - Hidden entirely with View › User Interface › Status Bar; the Workset and Design Options groups can be hidden separately. - The prompt is also exposed to screen readers as a live region (§1.33). - The status bar spans the main frame only; secondary frames show a compact prompt line at their bottom.

    Commands. ui.status.get() -> {prompt, progress?, selection_count, toggles}, ui.background_tasks() -> [Task], ui.background_tasks.cancel(task_id).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Hovering a door shows "Doors : <family> : <type>" in the prompt. - [ ] Clicking the selection count after a crossing selection opens the Filter dialog listing categories with counts.

    1.21 Selection

    1.21.1 Pre-highlight and picking

    ID: UI-SEL-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §18.1

    Behaviour & rules. - Hover pre-highlights the element under the cursor (heavier lines in canvas.preselection), shows its identity in the status bar, and after a delay (§1.25) shows an in-canvas tooltip. - Click selects it. The selection is model-wide: it shows in every view where the elements are visible and in the browsers. - Tab / Shift+Tab cycle forward/backward among candidates under the cursor before clicking: overlapping elements, chains of joined walls or lines, elements inside links, shape handles and snap candidates. The status bar shows "n of m" while cycling. - Right-click on a pre-highlighted element selects it (if not already selected) and opens the context menu. - Selection is not undoable and is not recorded in the model; it is session state. Commands record the selection they acted on for redo purposes. - Esc clears the selection; with a tool active, the first Esc ends the current step, the second ends the tool.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With three walls joined in a chain, hovering one and pressing Tab once highlights the chain; clicking selects all three. - [ ] Selecting a wall in a plan highlights it in an open 3D view.

    1.21.2 Multiple selection

    ID: UI-SEL-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §18.2

    Behaviour & rules.

    Gesture Effect
    Ctrl+click Add to selection (cursor shows +)
    Shift+click Remove from selection (cursor shows −)
    Drag left → right Window: solid rectangle; selects elements entirely inside
    Drag right → left Crossing: dashed rectangle; selects elements inside or touching
    Ctrl / Shift with a box Add / remove the boxed set
    Tab to a chain, click Select the whole chain (follows the smallest turning angle at junctions with more than two members)
    SA, or right-click › Select All Instances ▸ Visible in View / In Entire Project All instances of the selected types (in a design option: within the active option)
    Ctrl+Left, or right-click › Select Previous Restore the previous selection
    Ctrl+A (Reviera addition) Select all selectable elements visible in the active view, honouring the selection toggles
    Esc Clear
    • Box selection honours the selection option toggles (§1.21.4) and design-option/editability filters.
    • Tools that need several picks (for example "pick walls" modes) use an add/remove picking mode with Finish and Cancel on the contextual tab.

    Commands. selection.get() -> {ids[], by_category}, selection.set(ids[], mode?: replace|add|remove (default replace)) -> (), selection.clear(), selection.previous() -> (), selection.select_all_instances(type_ids? (default: types of the current selection), scope: view|project) -> element_ids[], selection.chain(element_id), selection.box(view_id?, rect, mode: window|crossing, combine: replace|add|remove), selection.select_all_visible(view_id?).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A left-to-right box around half a wall does not select it; right-to-left does. - [ ] selection.set([a, b]) from Lua updates the canvas, the Properties palette and the status-bar count. - [ ] Ctrl+Left after clearing restores the cleared selection.

    1.21.3 Filter dialog and saved selections

    ID: UI-SEL-003 · Priority: P0 (filter) / P1 (saved sets) · Ref: research/01 §18.3, §18.2 (saved selection sets), §7.12 (Selection panel)

    Behaviour & rules. - Filter dialog: list of categories in the selection with Count and a check box each; Check All / Check None; running total; OK keeps checked categories. - Saved selection sets (Manage › Selection, or the contextual Selection panel): Save (name), Load (replace or add), Edit (opens an editing mode where clicks add or remove members, with Finish/Cancel). Sets are stored with the model as RXD documents, so they travel with the IFC (Ch. 2); saving, editing and deleting a set are undoable. - Saved sets are also usable as view filter sources (Ch. 5).

    Commands. selection.filter_dialog(), selection.filter(category_ids[]) -> element_ids[] (keeps only those), selection.set_save(name, ids?) -> set_id, selection.set_load(set_id, mode: replace|add), selection.set_edit(set_id), selection.set_delete(set_id), selection.set_list() -> [set].

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Unchecking Furniture in the Filter dialog removes all furniture from the selection. - [ ] A saved set survives save, close and reopen; renaming it is undoable.

    1.21.4 Selection option toggles

    ID: UI-SEL-004 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §18.4, §17

    Behaviour & rules. - Global, per-user toggles shown in the Select panel drop-down and as status-bar icons: - Select Links — on: a link highlights as a whole and Tab reaches its elements; off: links cannot be selected but can still be snapped and aligned to. - Select Underlay Elements. - Select Pinned Elements — off: pinned elements cannot be picked or boxed (protects grids and links). - Select Elements by Face — on: clicking a face interior selects (not in wireframe); off: edges only. - Drag Elements on Selection — on: press-drag moves an element without selecting it first. - Active Option Only, Exclude Options, Editable Only (status bar). - Toggle states persist per user, not per model.

    Commands. selection.options.get() -> {links, underlay, pinned, by_face, drag_on_select, active_option_only, exclude_options, editable_only}, selection.options.set(name, value).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With Select Pinned off, a crossing box over a pinned grid does not select it. - [ ] Toggling Select Links in the ribbon updates the status-bar icon immediately.

    1.21.5 Double-click behaviour

    ID: UI-SEL-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/01 §18.5

    Behaviour & rules. - Options › User Interface › Double-click actions… sets, per element kind (Family instance, Sketched element, View inside a sheet, View outside a sheet, Assembly, Group, Stair/Railing, Schedule on sheet), one of: Do nothing / Edit type properties / Edit element (enter its edit mode) / Activate view / Open view. - Defaults: Family → Edit element (opens the family editor for loadable families); Sketched element → Edit element; Group → Edit element; View on sheet → Activate view; Schedule on sheet → Open view. - Remaining defaults. View outside a sheet (a view marker such as a section head or callout in another view) → Open view; Assembly → Edit element (assembly edit mode, Ch. 5); Stair/Railing → Edit element (component edit mode, Ch. 3). Each kind offers only the actions that make sense for it; for example Activate view is not offered for Family instance. - Deactivate. Double-clicking outside an activated viewport on a sheet deactivates it, whatever the settings; this is fixed behaviour, not an option. - Elements that cannot be edited (linked elements, elements owned by another user in BIMserver mode, pinned elements when Select Pinned is off) ignore the double-click and show the reason in the status bar. In-place families follow the Family instance setting but open in-place editing rather than the family editor. - Edit in place versus editor. For loadable families, Edit element opens the family editor as a separate document. If that family is already open in the editor, its window is activated instead. - Double-click timing follows the operating system's double-click interval and distance. - Storage. Options keys ui.double_click.<kind> (for example ui.double_click.group = "nothing"), per user. They can be locked by an administrator and changed by a scenario's preference overlay. - Dialog. The Double-click actions dialog is a two-column grid (Element kind, Action combo) with Restore defaults, OK and Cancel; OK applies immediately without restart.

    Commands. Read and write with ui.options.get/set("ui.double_click.<kind>", action); the dialog is a page of ui.options.open("user_interface", "ui.double_click").

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Setting Group to "Do nothing" makes double-clicking a group have no effect. - [ ] Double-clicking a loadable door with default settings opens the door family in the family editor; doing it again activates the same editor window. - [ ] Double-clicking a linked wall does nothing and the status bar says why.

    1.22 In-canvas controls

    1.22.1 Temporary dimensions and listening dimensions

    ID: UI-CTRL-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §19.1

    Behaviour & rules. - When placing or when one element is selected, Reviera shows temporary dimensions from the element to the nearest perpendicular references (walls, grids, levels, reference planes) according to the reference preferences in Manage › Additional Settings › Temporary Dimensions (walls: centreline / faces / core centre / core faces; doors and windows: centreline / opening edges). - Clicking a value opens an in-canvas editor; entering a new value moves or resizes the element accordingly (one undo step). Unit expressions are accepted as in the Properties palette. - Witness-line grips can be dragged to another reference, or clicked repeatedly to cycle the reference on that element (Edit Witness Lines, EW). - A make-permanent control under each value converts it into a permanent dimension (DOC dim.create_aligned). - While placing, the displayed length steps by snap increments chosen by zoom level (§1.23). - Listening dimensions: during a draw step, typing digits opens the editor pre-filled; Enter fixes the length (or angle when the tool expects one) along the current direction. - Appearance: text size and background (transparent/opaque) in Options › Graphics. - With several elements selected, temporary dimensions, pins and constraint padlocks are hidden until Activate Controls (AC) is toggled on.

    Commands. tempdim.list(element_id) -> [{index, ref_a, ref_b, value}], tempdim.set_value(element_id, index, value) (resolves to the owning move/resize command; undoable), tempdim.make_permanent(element_id, index) -> dimension_id, ui.controls.activate(on?), ui.temp_dim.settings().

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Clicking the temporary dimension between a selected wall and a grid and typing 1200 moves the wall so the distance is 1200 mm; one Undo reverts it. - [ ] While drawing a wall, typing 4500 and Enter makes a 4500 mm segment.

    1.22.2 Grips and shape handles

    ID: UI-CTRL-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §19.2

    Behaviour & rules. - End grips (filled dots) at the ends of curve-driven elements in plan: drag to lengthen, shorten or reorient within the work plane. In a selected chain, shared ends move together. Right-click an end grip of a wall: Allow Join / Disallow Join (ARC wall.set_join_allowed). - Shape handles (single arrows) in elevation and 3D: drag faces in one direction. Pressing Tab over one switches to moving the element rather than resizing. - Constrained handles (double arrows): move along a line (for example labelled dimensions in families). - Edge handles: Tab over an edge in elevation/3D picks the whole edge. - Dimension text grip: drags the text of a dimension away from its line. - Rotation handle: a draggable rotation grip with a movable, snapping centre (used by rotate-capable elements and the Rotate tool). - All grips are drawn in Reviera's own glyph style at a minimum hit target of 8 logical pixels (larger with the accessibility preference, §1.33). - Dragging produces a live preview; release submits one command and one undo step. Esc during the drag cancels.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Dragging a wall end grip to another wall's end joins them on release; Esc during the drag restores the original. - [ ] Every grip is reachable with Tab cycling when the pointer is over its element.

    1.22.3 Flip controls and Spacebar

    ID: UI-CTRL-003 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §19.3

    Behaviour & rules. - Flip controls (paired arrows) appear on selected elements that support flipping: walls (reverse layer orientation), doors and windows (Flip Facing and Flip Hand), and family-defined flips (single = 180° rotation, double = mirror; horizontal or vertical). - Spacebar with a selection flips or rotates it: free-standing components rotate 90° about their insertion point per press; doors and windows cycle facing/hand combinations; walls flip. If any selected element cannot respond, or the elements share no common direction, nothing happens and the status bar says why. - Spacebar during placement rotates the component preview by 90° (or aligns to the nearest wall/grid under the cursor, cycling).

    • Flip control placement. Controls are drawn on the side the flip would move to: for walls beside the exterior face, for doors and windows at the opening on the facing side (facing) and at the hinge side (hand). They are hit targets of at least 8 logical pixels (12 with the larger-targets preference, §1.33.2) and have tooltips "Flip facing", "Flip hand" or "Flip wall orientation".
    • Mixed selections. Clicking a flip control on one element flips only that element. Space applies to the whole selection only when every element supports the same flip; mixed doors and walls are refused ("Selected elements have no common flip").
    • Door cycle order for Space: original → flip hand → flip facing and hand → flip facing → original.
    • Rotation centre. Free-standing components rotate about their insertion point; a selection of several components rotates each about its own insertion point.
    • Hosted elements stay hosted when their host flips; how their facing responds is defined by the owning chapter (Ch. 3).
    • Undo. Each Space press or flip-control click is one undo entry named after the owner command, for example "Flip door hand".
    • Locked or pinned elements are skipped with a status-bar message; ownership in BIMserver mode is checked first.

    Commands. ui.flip_selection() (dispatches to the owner commands element.flip / insert.flip_facing / insert.flip_hand / element.rotate, Ch. 3).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Pressing Space four times with a door selected visits four distinct facing/hand combinations and returns to the start. - [ ] Space with a door and a wall selected changes nothing and the status bar explains why. - [ ] Clicking the flip control of a wall reverses its layer order in one undo step.

    1.22.4 Pins, locks and constraints

    ID: UI-CTRL-004 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §19.4

    Behaviour & rules. - Pinned elements show a pin glyph when selected; clicking it unpins (glyph shows struck-through); clicking again re-pins. PN pins, UP unpins. - Dimensions and alignments that can constrain show a padlock; clicking locks/unlocks the constraint (ARC/DOC constraint commands). Multi-segment dimensions show an EQ toggle. - Reveal Constraints (CX) shows all constraints in the view with the mode border (§1.17.2). - When glyphs show. Pin, padlock and EQ glyphs appear for a single selected element, or for several only after Activate Controls (UI-CTRL-001). A padlock also appears immediately after an Align operation, at the aligned reference, until the next command, so the user can lock the alignment in one click. - Pin rules. Unpinning by clicking the glyph is one undo entry ("Unpin"). Moving, deleting or changing a pinned element is refused with "Element is pinned" and an Unpin and continue action in the status bar; deleting a selection that includes pinned elements deletes the others and reports how many were skipped. Pinned state is model data owned by Ch. 3. - Padlock states. Open padlock = unconstrained; closed = constrained; a red padlock marks a constraint that cannot be satisfied after a change, with the failure reported by the owner chapter. Clicking a closed padlock removes the constraint. - EQ states. "EQ" struck through = not equal; "EQ" = equal; clicking toggles. While equal, the segment values may be shown as "EQ" text according to the dimension's display setting (Ch. 5). - Reveal Constraints is session state of the view window (like Temporary Hide/Isolate): it draws every locked dimension, alignment and equality constraint in canvas.reveal_constraints_border colour, is not undoable and is cleared when the view closes.

    Commands. element.pin, element.unpin (Ch. 3); constraint lock and equality commands are owned by Ch. 3 and Ch. 5; view.reveal_constraints.toggle(view_id?) (UI-VCB-001); ui.controls.activate(on?) (UI-CTRL-001).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Clicking a padlock on an aligned dimension locks it; moving the referenced grid then moves the constrained wall. - [ ] Trying to move a pinned grid shows "Element is pinned" and leaves it in place. - [ ] Right after an Align, clicking the padlock at the aligned reference creates the constraint in one undo step. - [ ] CX shows the mode border and label and draws every constraint in the view; CX again removes them.

    1.22.5 3D transform gizmo

    ID: UI-CTRL-005 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/01 §19.5

    Behaviour & rules. - In massing, family-form and displacement contexts, a triad with axis arrows and plane handles appears at the selection. Axis colours follow the theme tokens gizmo.x, gizmo.y, gizmo.z (default red/green/blue, distinguishable by arrowhead labels X/Y/Z as well as colour) and gizmo.local for local mode. - Spacebar toggles global/local orientation while the gizmo is active. - Handles. Three axis arrows (move along one axis), three plane squares (move in the plane of two axes) and, where the owner allows rotation, three arcs (rotate about one axis). Hovering a handle highlights it and shows its constraint as a dashed infinite line or plane. - Placement. The gizmo sits at the centroid of the selection, or at the selected point or edge midpoint when a sub-element (vertex, edge, face) is selected. It keeps a constant screen size (default 96 logical pixels) independent of zoom. - Local orientation aligns the axes with the selected element's own coordinate system (for a face, its normal is local Z). The current mode is shown as "Global" or "Local" next to the gizmo. - Precision. While dragging, snaps (§1.23) and listening dimensions (§1.22.1) work: typing a number and Enter moves exactly that distance along the active axis. Rotation steps by the angular snap increment. - Undo. One drag is one undo entry, submitted as the owner's move or rotate command (Ch. 3). Esc during the drag cancels it. - Micro-operations. A gizmo drag is a short interactive session; its start point, axis and typed value are journalled under conventions §2.1.

    Commands. ui.gizmo.toggle_orientation() -> global|local; the transforms themselves are element.move and element.rotate (Ch. 3).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Dragging the Z arrow moves the selection only vertically; the label "Z" is visible on the handle. - [ ] With a sloped face selected and Local mode on, the Z arrow follows the face normal. - [ ] Dragging the XY plane square and typing 1500 then Enter moves the selection 1500 mm along the drag direction in one undo step.

    1.23 Snaps and alignment

    ID: UI-SNAP-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §20

    Purpose. Make picks precise without typing coordinates.

    Behaviour & rules. - While drawing or placing, candidate snap points are shown with distinct glyphs (endpoint, midpoint, intersection, centre, quadrant, perpendicular, tangent, nearest, work-plane grid, point) and the snap kind is named in the status bar and next to the cursor. - Alignment lines (dashed) indicate inferences: collinear with existing lines, parallel and perpendicular tracking, horizontal/vertical lock near 0° and 90°, tangent continuation from arc ends, alignment with reference planes and same-category elements, and alignment with linked or imported CAD geometry. - Shift forces horizontal/vertical (orthogonal to the work plane axes) while held. - Tab / Shift+Tab cycle among coincident snap candidates. - Snaps dialog (Manage › Settings › Snaps): Snaps Off; length increment list (semicolon-separated, coarse to fine, chosen by zoom); angular increment list; check boxes for each object snap; Snap to Remote Objects; Snap to Point Clouds; Restore Defaults. Settings are per user (not per model) and persist. - Snap overrides apply to the next pick only, from the right-click menu › Snap Overrides or two-key sequences:

    Override Keys Override Keys
    Snaps Off SO Endpoints SE
    Midpoints SM Nearest SN
    Work Plane Grid SW Quadrants SQ
    Intersections SI Centres SC
    Perpendicular SP Tangents ST
    Points SX Remote Objects SR
    Point Clouds SY Close loop SZ
    Mid between two points S2 Turn override off SS
    • With Nearest off, jump snaps let the cursor pick snap points some distance away.
    • Snapping is computed in the core against a spatial index and returned to the overlay within one frame for typical views; the UI never blocks waiting for snap results (it shows the raw cursor until results arrive).

    Commands. snap.settings.get() -> SnapSettings, snap.settings.set(patch), snap.settings_dialog(), snap.override_next(kind), snap.query(view_id, point, tolerance_px?) -> [SnapCandidate] (used by Lua/MCP to compute precise points without a mouse).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Typing SM while drawing a wall makes the next click snap only to midpoints; the following click uses normal snaps again. - [ ] Holding Shift while drawing constrains the segment to horizontal or vertical. - [ ] Snap settings survive restart and are the same in every model.

    1.24 Context menus

    ID: UI-MENU-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §21

    Purpose. Offer relevant commands at the pointer.

    Behaviour & rules. - Context menus are generated from registered menu contributions (target selector, group, command id, order); owners and add-ins contribute; unavailable entries are hidden (not disabled) unless the entry declares otherwise. - Default contents:

    Target Items
    Canvas, nothing selected Cancel; Repeat <last command> (also Enter in idle); Recent Commands ▸; Select Previous; Find Referring Views; Zoom In Region; Zoom Out; Zoom to Fit; Previous/Next Pan/Zoom; Browsers ▸ (Project Browser, System Browser); View Properties; Open Sheet (if placed); Find in Project Browser; (on sheets) Activate View
    Canvas, element(s) selected Cancel; Repeat; Recent Commands ▸; Select Previous; Select All Instances ▸ (Visible in View, In Entire Project); Select Joined Elements; Delete; Hide in View ▸ (Elements, Category, by Filter); Override Graphics in View ▸ (Element, Category, Filter); Create Similar; Edit Family; Find in Project Browser; Find Referring Views; Zoom ▸; Properties; group items (Edit Group, Ungroup, Exclude, Move to Project, Restore Excluded); ownership items in BIMserver mode (Request Editing, Show Owner, Relinquish); "Ask Agent about selection" (when the Agent pane is configured)
    While a draw tool is active Cancel; Snap Overrides ▸; tool-specific items (for example Close loop)
    3D views Define Centre of Rotation (R3); Orient ▸
    Wall end grip Allow Join / Disallow Join
    Ribbon tool Add to Quick Access Toolbar; Assign Keyboard Shortcut…; Show Panel Titles; Show Tabs ▸; Show Panels ▸; Reset Ribbon
    QAT item Remove; Add Separator; Move Left/Right; Customize…
    Type Selector Add to Quick Access Toolbar; Add to Modify Tab
    View tab Close; Close Others; Close All; Float; Move to New Window; Dock to Main Window; Find in Project Browser; Copy View Name
    Project Browser, System Browser See §1.13, §1.14
    Orientation Cube, Navigation Wheel See §1.19.2, §1.19.4
    Pane caption Float; Dock; Auto-hide; Close
    • Menus open with right-click, the Menu key, or Shift+F10, at the pointer or (keyboard) at the focused element.
    • "Assign Keyboard Shortcut…" opens the shortcuts dialog filtered to that command.

    Commands. ui.context_menu.items(target_descriptor) -> [MenuItem] (for agents and tests), tool.repeat_last() -> session_id, tool.recent() -> [command_id].

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Right-clicking a selected door shows Edit Family and Select All Instances; right-clicking empty canvas does not. - [ ] Shift+F10 opens the canvas menu at the selection's screen centre.

    1.25 Tooltips and keytips

    1.25.1 Ribbon and control tooltips

    ID: UI-TIP-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §22 · screenshots/ui/tooltip_ribbon.png

    Behaviour & rules. - Two stages: after a short hover, the brief tooltip shows the label, the first-stage description and the first assigned shortcut in brackets (for example "Wall (WA)"). After continued hover, the extended tooltip adds the extended description, an optional illustration from Reviera's own help assets, the ribbon path, all shortcuts and "Press F1 for help". - Disabled tools show the unavailability reason in the brief tooltip. - Tooltip assistance level (Options › User Interface): None (no tooltips; F1 still works on focused controls), Minimal (brief only), Normal (default; brief then extended), High (both immediately). - Tooltips are also delivered as accessible descriptions of the control (§1.33). - Timing (Normal level): brief tooltip after 400 ms of hover; extended after a further 1 200 ms. Moving to an adjacent control while a tooltip is shown replaces it after 100 ms (no new delay). The tooltip hides on pointer exit, key press, click or after 20 s. At High, both stages appear together after 100 ms. Delays are settings keys ui.tooltips.delay_brief_ms and ui.tooltips.delay_extended_ms (range 0–5 000 ms) under the level key ui.tooltips.level (none | minimal | normal | high). - Content source. All text comes from the command descriptor (UI-ARCH-001): label / label_long, tooltip, tooltip_extended, default_shortcuts and the user's actual bindings, ribbon_paths. Illustrations are Reviera's own SVG or animated assets referenced by tooltip_extended; no video is streamed from the network. - Split buttons show the tooltip of the member under the pointer; for the main part, the last-used member. - Add-in tools show the add-in's name as a final line ("From add-in: Survey Tools"). - Placement. Below the control, clamped to the monitor's work area; never covering the control itself. Tooltips follow the UI theme and font scale. - Keyboard focus. When a ribbon tool gets keyboard focus (keytips, F6, arrow keys), its brief tooltip is shown after the same delay, so keyboard users get the same information. - F1 with a tooltip visible opens that command's help topic (UI-HELP-001), at every assistance level including None.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With Normal assistance, hovering Trim/Extend to Corner shows a brief tooltip within 500 ms and the extended tooltip within 2 s. - [ ] With None, no tooltip appears. - [ ] After reassigning Wall to WW, the Wall tooltip reads "Wall (WW)". - [ ] Moving the keyboard focus to the Door tool shows its brief tooltip.

    1.25.2 In-canvas tooltips

    ID: UI-TIP-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §22, §18.1

    Behaviour & rules. - Hovering an element shows "Category : Family : Type" (and for linked elements, the link name; for elements owned by others in BIMserver mode, the owner). - During tools, a cursor-adjacent hint shows the next step and the active snap. - The same text is shown in the status bar. - Element tooltip content, one line each, only when applicable: "Category : Family : Type"; mark or name if set; "Link: <link name>"; "Owned by <user>" (BIMserver mode); "Pinned"; "Design option: <set> › <option>" when not in the main model; "Hidden by temporary isolate" never appears (hidden elements are not hovered). - Delay. 600 ms of stillness over the same element (setting ui.tooltips.canvas_delay_ms); any pointer movement of more than 4 logical pixels hides it. Tab cycling (UI-SEL-001) updates the tooltip immediately to the cycled candidate. - Tool hints. The cursor hint shows at most two short lines: the step prompt from the tool (for example "Pick end point") and, while snapping, the snap name. Hints are suppressed while the in-canvas text editor is open. - Assistance level. None hides element tooltips and cursor hints (the status bar still shows the text); Minimal shows tool hints only; Normal and High show both. - Placement and look. Offset 16 logical pixels below-right of the cursor, flipped to stay inside the view window; drawn by the renderer's overlay pass in UI theme colours (not canvas colours), so it stays readable on light and dark canvases.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Hovering a linked wall shows the link name in the tooltip. - [ ] With Minimal assistance, hovering a wall shows no tooltip while the wall tool's "Pick start point" hint still appears. - [ ] Pressing Tab over overlapping elements changes the tooltip to each candidate in turn.

    1.25.3 Keytips

    ID: UI-TIP-003 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §22 · screenshots/ui/keytips.png

    Behaviour & rules. - Pressing and releasing Alt (or F10) overlays letter badges on File, QAT items, ribbon tabs and (on Reviera addition) the pane captions. Typing a badge opens that tab and shows badges for its tools; typing a tool's badge runs it or opens its menu; Esc steps back one level; any mouse click hides badges. - Keytips are generated: each tab/tool may declare a preferred keytip; conflicts are resolved automatically by adding a second letter. Localised builds generate keytips from localised labels. - While keytips are visible, key-sequence shortcuts are suspended. - Levels. Level 1: File (F), QAT items (digits 1–9, then 01–09 for items 10–18), ribbon tabs, contextual tabs and (Reviera addition) pane captions. Level 2: the tools of the chosen tab, including embedded option controls and dialog launchers. Level 3: members of a split or drop-down button, or items of a collapsed panel or slide-out. - Generation. A tool's keytip is its declared preference if free at that level; otherwise the first letter of the label, then the first letters of following words, then two-letter combinations from the label, then a two-character code. Assignments are stable: they depend only on the ribbon content, not on the order in which panels were loaded, so a user learns them once. Two-character keytips wait for the second key without a timeout. - Collapsed and hidden content. Collapsed panels (UI-RIB-002) get a panel keytip that opens the popup and continues at level 3. Tools hidden by discipline filtering (UI-RIB-007) get no keytip. - Badges. Drawn in UI theme colours at the bottom centre of each control, at least 16 logical pixels high; disabled tools show dimmed badges that do nothing when typed. - Exit. Esc steps back one level; Esc at level 1, Alt again, a mouse click, or focus leaving the main window hides all badges. Running a tool hides them. - Floating panels show badges only when the user presses Alt while pointing at them.

    Commands. ui.keytips.show(), ui.keytips.hide().

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Alt, then the Annotate tab keytip, then the Text keytip starts the Text tool. - [ ] No two badges visible at the same level are identical. - [ ] The same ribbon content produces the same keytips after a restart and after loading the panels in a different order. - [ ] A collapsed panel's tools can be run with three keytip presses.

    1.26 Keyboard shortcut system

    1.26.1 Shortcut model

    ID: UI-KEY-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §23.1

    Purpose. Let users run any command from the keyboard with short typed sequences or chorded keys.

    Behaviour & rules. - Two binding forms: 1. Key sequence: 1 to 5 alphanumeric keys (letters, digits and /, ;, ,, .) typed without modifiers while the canvas, ribbon or a non-text pane has focus. 2. Chord: one key with modifiers (Ctrl, Shift, Alt in combination; Alt alone with a letter is reserved for keytips; on macOS Ctrl maps to Cmd for reserved chords, while sequences are unaffected). - A command may have several bindings; a binding may be assigned to several commands (resolved by the status bar, §1.26.4). - Execution rule for sequences: a typed sequence runs as soon as it matches a binding and is not a prefix of any longer binding; if it is also a prefix of a longer binding, Reviera waits for the next key up to the sequence timeout (default 800 ms, configurable 300–3000 ms) and then runs the shorter match; Space runs the displayed match at once; Esc or Backspace edits/cancels the buffer. - Sequences are inactive while a text field has focus; chords stay active unless the focused control consumes them (for example Ctrl+C in a text field copies text). - Context scopes: a binding may be scoped to a context (for example text_editor, sketch_mode, schedule_view, rebar_placement); scoped bindings take precedence in their scope and do not conflict with global ones. - Shortcuts are stored per user in shortcuts.toml (§1.29) as a list of {command, keys, scope} entries and can be exported and imported in that format.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With CO and COL both bound, typing C, O runs CO after the timeout; typing C, O, L runs COL immediately. - [ ] Typing WA in the canvas starts the wall tool; typing WA inside a Properties text field enters text.

    1.26.2 Keyboard Shortcuts dialog

    ID: UI-KEY-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §23.2

    Behaviour & rules. - Opened with KS, View › User Interface › Keyboard Shortcuts, Options › User Interface › Customize…, or a ribbon tool's right-click "Assign Keyboard Shortcut…". - Search (case-insensitive substring over label, long label, command id and keys). - Filter: All, With shortcuts, Without shortcuts, Reserved, Conflicts, by ribbon tab, by owner chapter, Add-in commands. - Grid: Command | Shortcuts | Locations (ribbon paths) | Scope | Owner, sortable by any column. - Press keys field with Assign and Remove; conflicts are shown inline before assigning ("Also used by: …"), with the option to assign anyway or replace. - Reserved commands are shown greyed with their keys in angle brackets; their key field is disabled. Each reserved command has an assignable twin command id (for example file.save is reserved on Ctrl+S, and file.save may also get a sequence such as SV). - Import, Export, Reset to Defaults, Print / Save as HTML reference, OK, Cancel. - Changes take effect on OK without restart.

    Commands. ui.shortcuts.dialog(filter?), ui.shortcuts.list(filter?) -> [{command, keys[], scope, reserved}], ui.shortcuts.assign(command_id, keys, scope?), ui.shortcuts.remove(command_id, keys), ui.shortcuts.import(path, mode: merge|replace), ui.shortcuts.export(path), ui.shortcuts.reset().

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Assigning WW to Wall shows no conflict; assigning MV to Wall shows "Also used by: Move". - [ ] Export then Import on another machine reproduces the same map.

    1.26.4 Running sequences from the status bar

    ID: UI-KEY-004 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §23.4

    Behaviour & rules. - While a sequence is being typed, the status bar prompt shows the typed keys and the first matching command; Down/Right cycle to the next match, Up/Left to the previous; Space runs the shown match without typing further keys. - When a completed sequence is bound to several commands, Reviera does not run any: the status bar lists the candidates and the user picks with arrows and Space (or Enter). - This applies to sequences only, not chords. - Display format. The prompt area shows Keys: CO › Copy (CO) — 3 more; while cycling, the shown command, its full sequence and its availability. Unavailable matches (for example a tool that needs a selection) are listed in grey and are skipped by Space, which then runs the next available match. - Ordering of matches. Exact matches first, then longer sequences in alphabetical order of their keys; within the same keys, scoped bindings for the current context before global ones (UI-KEY-001). - Timeout interaction. Cycling with arrow keys stops the sequence timeout; the buffer stays until Space, Enter, Esc or 10 s without input. - Ambiguous completed sequences (several commands bound to the same keys in the same scope) show a numbered list; typing the digit 1–9 also picks a candidate. - No match. A key that makes the buffer match nothing is ignored, and the prompt shows "No command for <keys>" for 1.5 s; the buffer keeps its previous content. - Accessibility. The prompt is a live region, so screen readers announce the shown command at the chosen verbosity (§1.33.4). - Scripts and tests can resolve a sequence without typing it.

    Commands. ui.shortcuts.resolve(keys, scope?) -> [{command_id, exact: bool, available: bool}].

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Typing R then Down shows successive commands whose sequences start with R; Space runs the shown one. - [ ] With XY bound to two commands in the same scope, typing XY shows a numbered list and typing 2 runs the second command. - [ ] Typing a key that matches nothing shows "No command for …" and leaves the buffer unchanged. - [ ] ui.shortcuts.resolve("WA") returns the wall command as an exact match.

    1.26.5 Reviera default shortcut map

    ID: UI-KEY-005 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §23.5, §20

    Purpose. Provide a default map that is efficient and familiar to users of two-letter mnemonic schemes, defined by Reviera's command ids.

    Rules applied in building the map. - Two-letter mnemonics are used where they are widely known in the industry so that users can transfer muscle memory; Reviera's map is maintained as its own data file (shortcuts-default.toml) keyed by Reviera command ids. - No default sequence is bound to two commands. Where traditional mnemonics collide, Reviera gives the sequence to one command (the more frequent) and leaves the other unbound: RC → Repeat Last Command (coping removal has none); RG → Remove from Group (render gallery has none); PC → Check Pipe Systems (point-cloud snap override moves to SY); SZ → Close-loop snap (system-zone sketch has none); SE → Endpoint snap (Section has none); ME → Mechanical Equipment (Measure has none); ST → Tangent snap (Stair has none). - Additions not found in the traditional scheme: 3D default 3D view, ZN next pan/zoom, CI check in, FL floor, Ctrl+K Command Search, Ctrl+J Agent pane, Ctrl+Shift+L Lua Console, Ctrl+Shift+O focus tool options, Ctrl+Shift+F11 focus mode, Ctrl+A select all visible. - Scoped bindings (text editor, rebar placement) apply only in their scope.

    1.27 Options dialog

    1.27.1 Dialog structure

    ID: UI-PREF-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §24 · screenshots/ui/options_colors_tab_theme.png

    Purpose. Central place for application-wide, per-user preferences.

    Behaviour & rules. - Opened from File › Options, Command Search, or ui.options.open(page?, setting?). Available with or without a model open. - Left: page tree with a search box that filters pages and highlights matching settings. Right: the page. - Settings are per user and global (not per model), stored in settings.toml (§1.29). Settings locked by the administrator defaults file show a lock icon and are read-only. - OK applies and closes; Cancel discards; Apply applies without closing; each page has Restore page defaults. - Settings that need a restart are marked and the user is told on OK.

    Commands. ui.options.open(page?, setting?), ui.options.get(key) -> value, ui.options.set(key, value), ui.options.list(prefix?) -> [{key, value, default, locked, requires_restart}], ui.options.reset(prefix?).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Typing "opacity" in the search box shows the Orientation Cube and Navigation Wheel pages with the matching settings highlighted. - [ ] ui.options.set("ui.tooltips.level", "minimal") from Lua takes effect immediately.

    1.28 Themes

    ID: UI-THEME-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §25 · screenshots/ui/dark_theme_full_ui.png, screenshots/ui/dark_theme_black_canvas_2023.png, screenshots/ui/options_colors_tab_theme.png

    Purpose. Provide light and dark appearances for the UI and, independently, for the canvas.

    Behaviour & rules. - Two independent axes: 1. UI theme: Light, Dark, or Follow system (default). Covers the ribbon, QAT, panes, status bar, View Control Bar, view tabs, and all dialogs (no dialog is exempt). 2. Canvas scheme: Light (light background, dark linework) or Dark (dark background, light linework). Toggled with View › Windows › Canvas Theme or CA. - All colours come from theme tokens defined in theme files (themes/<name>.toml) shipped with Reviera; users may add custom theme files. Token groups: ui.* (window, panel, text, accent, focus ring, disabled), ribbon.* (tab, active tab, contextual accent, panel title), canvas.* (§1.17.2), gizmo.*, status.* (info, warning, error, success). - Platform realisation: on Windows, wxWidgets dark mode support (MSWEnableDarkMode / wxApp::SetAppearance); on macOS, the app appearance is set to light, dark or system; on Linux/GTK, Reviera requests the GTK dark or light variant at start-up and follows prefers-color-scheme portal changes when "Follow system" is chosen. Custom-drawn controls (ribbon art provider, overlays, status bar) read tokens and repaint on theme change. - Switching themes takes effect immediately without restart; icon bundles switch to the matching variant (light-on-dark or dark-on-light). - A High contrast theme pair (light and dark) is shipped (§1.33); when the operating system's high-contrast mode is on and the theme is Follow system, Reviera uses it. - Contextual tab accent, selection and pre-selection colours meet contrast requirements against both canvas schemes (§1.33.2).

    Commands. ui.theme.get() -> {ui, canvas, effective_ui}, ui.theme.set(ui: light|dark|system|<custom>), ui.canvas_theme.set(light|dark), ui.canvas_theme.toggle(), ui.theme.list() -> [name].

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With Follow system, changing the OS appearance switches Reviera's UI theme within 2 seconds without restart. - [ ] Dark UI with Light canvas and Light UI with Dark canvas both work; every dialog follows the UI theme. - [ ] A custom theme file overriding ribbon.contextual changes the contextual tab colour.

    1.29 UI persistence

    1.29.1 Per-user stores

    ID: UI-PERSIST-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §26, §6.5, §4

    Behaviour & rules. - Per-user configuration lives in the platform configuration directory: Linux $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/reviera/ (default ~/.config/reviera/), Windows %APPDATA%\Reviera\, macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Reviera/. Caches (thumbnails, server working copies, agent transcripts) live in the platform cache/data directory. - Files (all human-readable TOML, versioned with a schema_version key and migrated forward automatically):

    File Contents Reset command
    settings.toml Every Options value (§1.27), selection toggles, snap settings, tool-option memory, split-button last-used members, Type Selector recents ui.options.reset()
    ui-state.toml Ribbon layout (tab and panel order, hidden items, floating panels, pinned slide-outs, minimise state), QAT contents and position ui.ribbon.reset(), ui.qat.reset()
    shortcuts.toml Keyboard bindings (differences from the default map) ui.shortcuts.reset()
    layout.toml The current dock layout per monitor configuration fingerprint, the active bookmark and auto-switch rules. Bookmarks themselves are in layouts/*.toml (§1.29.4). Older named-workspaces ui.layout.reset()
    recent.toml Home recent list and pins ui.recent.clear()
    servers.toml Saved BIMserver connections (no secrets; tokens in the OS keychain) —
    agent.toml Agent provider configuration (no secrets) —
    • Each store can be reset independently from Options › User Interface or by deleting the file; a corrupt file is renamed *.bad and defaults are used, with a notice.
    • Writes are atomic (write temp, rename).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Deleting ui-state.toml resets ribbon and QAT but keeps shortcuts and options. - [ ] A truncated settings.toml produces a notice and default settings; the damaged file is kept as settings.toml.bad.

    1.29.2 Project-scoped UI data (RXD)

    ID: UI-PERSIST-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §26 (per-model row); TECH_STACK §3.7.3

    Behaviour & rules. - Project-scoped UI data are Reviera Extension Data documents stored with the model through its RXD carrier (embedded in the IFC by default, or the optional sidecar; Ch. 2 and 02a_extension_data_format.md): - UI document: starting view (Ch. 5 command), last session's open views with their tab/tile/split arrangement and per-view navigation state (when "Save view arrangement with model" is on, default on in Local mode), saved selection sets (§1.21.3). - Browser document: Project Browser expansion state and active tab, browser organisation scheme definitions and project-default active scheme (§1.13). - In BIMserver mode, the open-view arrangement and browser expansion state are kept per user in the local working-copy cache, not checked in, so users do not overwrite each other's layouts; selection sets, organisation schemes and the starting view are checked in as model data. - Changes that are purely presentational (expansion state, open views) mark the model as modified only for the RXD part and never create undo entries; they are saved with the next Save but never trigger a save prompt on their own (a preference can change this). - Per-user preferences are never stored in RXD. - Export clean IFC (§1.4) omits all of these.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Opening a model shows the views open at its last save, arranged as they were, when the preference is on. - [ ] Expanding browser nodes and closing without other edits does not prompt to save. - [ ] In BIMserver mode, user A's open-view layout is not changed by user B's check-in.

    1.29.3 Administrator defaults

    ID: UI-PERSIST-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/01 §26 (all-users template), §6.7 (locked disciplines)

    Behaviour & rules. - A system-wide defaults directory (Linux /etc/reviera/, Windows %PROGRAMDATA%\Reviera\, macOS /Library/Application Support/Reviera/) may contain settings.toml, ui-state.toml, shortcuts.toml and layout.toml used as defaults for new user profiles, and a locked list of setting keys users cannot change. - Locked settings apply to Lua and MCP too. - Directory contents.

    Entry Use
    settings.toml, ui-state.toml, shortcuts.toml, layout.toml Seed values copied into a new profile on first launch; never re-applied to an existing profile except for locked keys
    locked.toml keys = [ … ]: setting keys (exact, or a prefix ending in .*) that users cannot change, for example ui.disciplines, ai.mcp.*; the value in force is the one in the defaults settings.toml, or the built-in default if absent
    layouts/, scenarios/ Organisation layouts and scenarios, read-only for users (UI-LAYOUT-002, UI-SCEN-004)
    themes/ Extra theme files offered to every user (§1.28)
    • Override order, highest first: locked administrator value → scenario overlay (UI-SCEN-001) → user value → administrator seed → built-in default. A scenario that lists a locked key is shown as "not applied" for that key.
    • Existing profiles. At each launch Reviera re-reads locked.toml; locked keys take the administrator value for the session without overwriting the user's stored value, so unlocking later restores the user's own choice.
    • Visibility. Locked settings show a lock icon and the note "Managed by administrator" in Options; ui.options.list reports locked: true; ui.options.set on a locked key returns the error setting_locked and changes nothing.
    • Errors. A malformed defaults file is ignored with a notice to the user and a log entry naming the file and line; Reviera then starts with built-in defaults for the affected store and still applies any valid locked.toml.
    • Read-only location. Reviera never writes to the defaults directory; it only reads it.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A locked ui.disciplines setting is enforced for a new and an existing user profile. - [ ] Removing the key from locked.toml restores the user's previously chosen value at the next launch. - [ ] ui.options.set("ui.disciplines", …) from MCP returns setting_locked while the key is locked. - [ ] A seed shortcuts.toml is applied to a new profile and not to an existing one.

    1.29.4 Workspaces I: bookmarked layouts and personal layout preferences

    Workspace model (overview). The workspace is a high-level, user-owned customisation of how each person works, on top of the application's defaults and below any administrator locks. It has three building blocks: - layout bookmarks (§1.29.4): where things are on screen - workflow scenarios (§1.29.5): how the user works in a given process, as preferences, shortcuts and entry actions - view bookmarks (§1.29.5): where in the model they work

    All three are personal by default, portable between machines, switchable on demand or by context, and fully scriptable through Lua and MCP. Projects may only recommend; they never impose. Owner directive (2026-10-12). The UI shall support bookmarked layouts and personal preferences for UI layout choices. This is a Reviera addition: the reference product keeps one UI state per user, with no named layouts.

    UI-LAYOUT-001 — Saving and applying layout bookmarks

    ID: UI-LAYOUT-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: Owner directive 2026-10-12; research/01 §13 (docking), §26 (UI persistence)

    Purpose. Lets users switch the workspace between tasks with one action, for example modeling on two monitors, then sheet documentation, then coordination review on a laptop, and get back to a known arrangement after experimenting.

    What a bookmark can hold. Each part is optional. The user ticks the parts when saving, and parts left unticked are left alone when the bookmark is applied.

    Part Contents Default
    Dock layout Position, size, grouping and tab order of every pane (Properties, Project Browser, System Browser, History, Agent, Notifications, Server, Lua Console, add-in panes); docked, floating or auto-hidden; floating frames with their monitor ✔
    Visible panels Which panes and zones are shown or hidden (UI-DOCK-004) ✔
    Ribbon Minimise state, tab order, hidden tabs and panels, floating panels, pinned slide-outs, the active tab ✔
    Quick Access Toolbar Its contents and position (above or below the ribbon) ✔
    Status bar Which status-bar items are shown ✔
    Canvas chrome View-tab style, whether the Orientation Cube and Navigation Bar are shown, the selection toggles shown ✔
    Appearance Theme (light, dark or system), UI density (comfortable or compact), UI font scale ☐
    View arrangement The open views and their tab, tile and split arrangement. Views are matched by RXD view id in the current project (§1.29.2), so this part applies only when the same project is open. Missing views are skipped and listed in a notice. ☐

    Workflow. 1. Arrange the UI. 2. Choose View › Windows › Layouts ▾ › Save current layout…, or click the layout chip on the status bar and choose Save…. 3. Enter a name, tick the parts to include, and optionally pick an icon colour and a shortcut slot (1–9). 4. Apply it from any of: - the Layouts menu (split button: the main part re-applies the last layout, the arrow opens the list) - the status-bar layout chip - command search ("Layout: Documentation") - Ctrl+Alt+1…9 - Lua or MCP 5. Switch back (Ctrl+Alt+0) returns to the arrangement in use just before the last apply, even if it was never saved. 6. Update "<name>" saves the current arrangement over the bookmark. Rename, duplicate, delete and set as startup layout are available in Manage layouts….

    Behaviour & rules. - Applying is atomic and flicker-free. The frame is frozen while the AUI perspective, ribbon state and visibility are applied, then thawed. The target is under 300 ms, with no relayout flash. - Applying a layout never changes the model, never creates undo entries and never marks the project as modified. - Interactive sessions survive. Applying a layout during a sketch or tool session keeps the session and its contextual tab. The contextual tab stays visible even if the bookmark hides the ribbon tab it came from. - Add-in panes that a bookmark mentions but that aren't installed are skipped silently, and their state is kept for later. Panes that appeared after the bookmark was saved keep their current state. - The status-bar chip shows the active bookmark's name. It shows "<name> (modified)" once the user changes the arrangement afterwards, and the chip's menu then offers Update or Save as new.

    Data. Per user, one TOML file per bookmark in <config>/reviera/layouts/<slug>.toml, holding: - schema_version, name, icon_color, slot and parts - per-part data: the AUI perspective string, a ribbon state table, a QAT list, visibility flags and appearance keys - a [displays.<fingerprint>] table for each monitor setup it was saved on (UI-LAYOUT-003)

    These files are never stored in RXD or in the model. The one exception is UI-LAYOUT-006.

    Save layout dialog. Fields: Name (required, 1–64 characters, unique among personal layouts ignoring case; a clash offers Replace or Choose another name), the part check boxes of the table above with their defaults, Icon colour (eight theme colours), Shortcut slot (None, 1–9; choosing a slot already used shows which layout holds it and moves it on OK). Built-in and organisation names may be reused for personal layouts; the list then shows the badge to tell them apart.

    Manage layouts dialog (ui.layout.manage). A list in three groups (Built-in, Organisation, Personal), each row showing icon colour, name, slot, the parts it holds, and the display setups it has variants for. The right side shows the pane-position diagram (UI-LAYOUT-002). Buttons: - Apply, Update from current (personal only), Rename (personal only; same validation as Save), Duplicate (any; creates a personal copy), Delete (personal only; asks for confirmation and names any scenario or auto-switch rule that uses it, which then fall back to "no layout change"), Export… and Import… (UI-LAYOUT-005), Set as startup (UI-LAYOUT-002). - An Auto-switch tab for the rules of UI-LAYOUT-004, and a Display variants list per layout with Delete variant (UI-LAYOUT-003). - Changes are written immediately; the dialog has Close, not OK/Cancel.

    Commands. - ui.layout.save(name, parts[], slot?, icon_color?) -> layout_id - ui.layout.apply(layout_id | name | slot, parts?) -> report (applies all saved parts, or only the listed subset; the report names skipped panes and parts overridden by administrator locks) - ui.layout.load(name) -> (): kept as a short form of ui.layout.apply(name) for scripts; fails with not_found when no layout has that name - ui.layout.update(layout_id) -> status, ui.layout.switch_back() -> status - ui.layout.rename(layout_id, name) -> status, ui.layout.delete(layout_id) -> status (both refuse built-in and organisation layouts with read_only) - ui.layout.list(group?: builtin|org|personal) -> [LayoutInfo] (LayoutInfo = id, name, group, slot, icon_color, parts, display fingerprints, is_active, is_modified) - ui.layout.manage() -> () opens the Manage layouts dialog - ui.layout.reset() -> () restores the default arrangement of §1.2; it is not a bookmark and deletes none.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Save "Modeling" (two monitors, Properties floating on monitor 2) and "Docs" (one window, Project Browser on the right, ribbon minimised to tabs). Ctrl+Alt+1 and Ctrl+Alt+2 switch between them in under 300 ms, with no visible relayout flash. - [ ] Applying a bookmark saved without Appearance leaves the current theme unchanged. - [ ] Applying a layout during floor sketch mode keeps sketch mode and its contextual tab. - [ ] Switch back restores the unsaved arrangement that was in use before the last apply. - [ ] Applying a layout doesn't mark the project as modified.

    UI-LAYOUT-002 — Built-in, organisation and personal layouts

    ID: UI-LAYOUT-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: Owner directive 2026-10-12; §1.29.3

    • Built-in starter layouts (read-only; the user can duplicate one to customise it):
    Layout Arrangement
    Modeling the default layout (§1.2)
    Documentation Project Browser enlarged with the Sheets tab active, Properties narrow, the ribbon opening on the Annotate tab
    Coordination History, Notifications and Server panes docked on the right, the clash and BCF panes open
    Compact for screens 1440 px wide or less: ribbon minimised to panel titles, palettes auto-hidden at the edges
    Presentation minimal chrome: ribbon hidden, status bar reduced, canvas only
    • Organisation layouts are read from the administrator defaults directory (layouts/ under §1.29.3). They are listed with an Org badge and are read-only for users. An administrator can mark one as the startup layout for new profiles.
    • Personal layouts are the user's own. The startup layout preference sets what the UI uses at launch:
    Option Behaviour
    Last used (default) The arrangement from the end of the previous session
    A specific bookmark That bookmark, every launch
    Ask at launch The user picks from a list on the Home screen
    • Lists and locks.
    • The Manage layouts dialog lists the built-in, organisation and personal layouts in three groups, with a preview of each: a diagram of pane positions drawn from the saved data, not a screenshot.
    • Settings the administrator has locked (§1.29.3) are applied whatever the bookmark says. The dialog shows which parts were overridden.
    • Ask at launch. The Home screen shows a "Choose a layout" strip above Recent with one button per layout (built-in, organisation, personal), preselecting the last used; choosing nothing and opening a model uses the last used one.
    • Missing startup layout. If the startup layout has been deleted or its organisation file removed, Reviera falls back to Last used and shows a notice.

    Commands. ui.layout.duplicate(layout_id, name) -> layout_id (any group; the copy is personal), ui.layout.set_startup(last_used | layout_id | ask) -> status, ui.layout.list(group?) (UI-LAYOUT-001).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A fresh profile lists the five built-in layouts. Deleting one isn't possible; duplicating one creates an editable personal copy. - [ ] An organisation layout placed in the defaults directory appears with the Org badge. When set as the startup layout for new profiles, a new user's first launch uses it.

    UI-LAYOUT-003 — Multi-monitor and display-aware layouts

    ID: UI-LAYOUT-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/01 §13 (multiple monitors)

    • Variants per display setup. A bookmark keeps one variant per monitor configuration fingerprint: the count, arrangement, resolution and scale of the monitors.
    • Applying the bookmark uses the variant that matches the current displays exactly, if there is one.
    • Otherwise Reviera adapts the nearest variant:
      • Floating frames are mapped to the monitor in the same relative position.
      • Frames whose monitor no longer exists are docked into the right dock group, keeping their tab order.
      • Sizes are scaled by the DPI ratio and clamped to the work area.
    • A notice offers Save a variant for this display setup.
    • Display changes while running. When the monitor setup changes during a session (a laptop docked or undocked, a monitor unplugged), Reviera keeps windows on screen at once. It then re-applies the active bookmark's matching variant if one exists, or offers to save one.
    • No window off screen. After any apply, every frame must be at least 80 % visible on some monitor.
    • Fingerprint. A hash of the sorted list of (monitor position relative to the primary, resolution, scale factor). Monitor names and serial numbers are not used, so swapping one monitor for an identical model matches.
    • Variant management. Save a variant for this display setup stores the current arrangement as an extra variant of the active bookmark; Manage layouts lists the variants with Delete variant. A bookmark keeps at most 8 variants; saving a ninth replaces the least recently used one after a confirmation.

    Commands. ui.layout.save_display_variant(layout_id) -> status (stores the current arrangement as the variant for the current fingerprint); ui.monitors() (UI-VIEWWIN-003) returns the data the fingerprint is built from.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Apply a two-monitor bookmark with only the laptop screen connected: all panes are visible and floating panes are docked on the right. Reconnecting the second monitor restores the two-monitor variant automatically.

    UI-LAYOUT-004 — Context-bound layouts (auto-switch)

    ID: UI-LAYOUT-004 · Priority: P2 · Ref: Owner directive 2026-10-12

    • Rules. Users can bind a bookmark to a context in Manage layouts › Auto-switch. Available contexts:
    • the active view type is a sheet, a schedule, a 3D view or a drafting view
    • the Family Editor is active
    • the project is in BIMserver mode
    • a given monitor setup (fingerprint) is connected
    • the main window is narrower than a set width
    • Order. Rules are evaluated in user-set order, and the first match is applied when the context starts. When the context ends, the layout that was active before it is restored.
    • Manual changes win. A layout the user applies by hand stays until the context changes again. A global Auto-switch toggle in the chip menu turns all rules off.
    • Partial bookmarks are encouraged. A bookmark bound to a context should normally include only the parts that matter for that context, such as Ribbon and Visible panels, so switching feels light.
    • Auto-switch tab (in Manage layouts). A table of rules with columns Order, Context (combo of the contexts above, with a width value or a display setup picker where needed), Layout (combo; built-in, organisation or personal) and Enabled. Buttons: Add, Remove, Move up, Move down. Validation: a rule needs a context and a layout; two enabled rules with the same context are allowed but the later one is greyed with "Never reached". Rules are stored in layout.toml.
    • Debounce. A context must hold for 300 ms before its rule applies, so quickly tabbing through views does not cause a chain of switches.

    Commands. ui.layout.rules.list() -> [rule] and ui.layout.rules.set(rules[]) -> status where rule = {context, layout_id, order, enabled}; ui.layout.auto_switch(enabled: bool) -> status sets the global toggle.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Bind "Docs" to sheet view active. Opening a sheet applies "Docs"; activating a plan view returns to the previous layout. With Auto-switch off, nothing changes.

    UI-LAYOUT-005 — Personal preference profile: export, import and sync

    ID: UI-LAYOUT-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: Owner directive 2026-10-12; §1.29.1

    • Export profile… writes a .reviera-profile file: a ZIP of the user's chosen stores, from settings.toml, ui-state.toml, shortcuts.toml, layouts/*.toml and layout.toml. Secrets are never included (servers.toml is written without tokens), and machine-specific paths are made relative or dropped.
    • Import profile… previews what will change, then lets the user merge (incoming layouts are added and name clashes renamed) or replace.
    • Profile sync folder (optional preference): the user picks a folder, for example one synced by Nextcloud, Syncthing or a network share. Personal layouts and selected stores are mirrored to it, and changes are picked up at launch and when the window regains focus. Conflicts keep the newer file and save the older one as <name>.conflict.toml.
    • Share a single layout with Export layout… and Import layout… (one .toml file each), for example to give a colleague a documentation layout.
    • Import preview dialog. Lists each incoming store and layout with its action (Add, Replace, Rename to "<name> (2)", Skip: newer schema), and a count of setting keys that would change with a Show keys expander. The user can untick individual items. Import applies them in one step; nothing is written if the user cancels. Files with a newer schema_version than this build understands are skipped and listed.
    • Clash policy for single layouts (on_clash): rename (default; adds " (2)", " (3)", …), replace, or skip.
    • Sync folder validation. The folder must exist and be writable; Reviera writes a small reviera-sync.toml marker there. If the folder becomes unavailable (network share offline), syncing pauses with a status-bar notice and resumes when it returns.

    Commands. - ui.profile.export(path, stores[]) -> status, ui.profile.import(path, mode: merge|replace, preview?) -> ChangeSummary (with preview = true nothing is written; the summary lists what would change) - ui.layout.export(layout_id, path) -> status, ui.layout.import(path, on_clash: rename|replace|skip) -> layout_id - ui.profile.set_sync_folder(path | null) -> status (null turns syncing off; the folder's contents are left in place)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Export a profile on machine A and import it on machine B with merge: B's own layouts are kept and A's layouts are added. A clash on "Docs" becomes "Docs (2)". - [ ] An exported profile contains no BIMserver token or agent API key; a search of the archive finds no secret values.

    UI-LAYOUT-006 — Recommended project layout (team standard)

    ID: UI-LAYOUT-006 · Priority: P2 · Ref: §1.29.2

    • Recommending. A project can carry one or more recommended layouts, stored in the RXD document ui/state under recommended_layouts. Only the parts Dock layout, Visible panels, Ribbon and View arrangement can be recommended. Personal Appearance is never part of a project.
    • On open. When a user opens the project, the layout chip shows Project layout available. Applying it is always the user's choice; it never applies automatically. The user can also save it as a personal bookmark.
    • Who can set it. Recommended layouts are project data. In BIMserver mode, changing them requires edit rights and goes up with the next check-in.
    • Recommending workflow. In Manage layouts, a personal or organisation layout has Recommend for this project…. The dialog shows which parts will be copied (only the four allowed parts; others are listed as "not shared") and asks for an optional note shown to other users. The layout is copied into the RXD document, so later edits to the personal original do not change the project copy; Update recommendation copies it again.
    • Data. ui/state › recommended_layouts[]: {id, name, note, parts, perspective, ribbon, visible, view_arrangement, author, created}. The view arrangement uses RXD view ids, so it resolves in every copy of the project. Panes of add-ins that a user does not have are skipped as in UI-LAYOUT-001.
    • Undo and modified state. Recommending or removing a recommendation is an ordinary undoable edit of project data and marks the project modified. Applying a recommended layout is a personal action: not undoable, no modified flag.
    • Dismissal. The chip's "Project layout available" hint can be dismissed per project; it reappears only when the recommendation changes.
    • Limits. At most 5 recommended layouts per project; the first is the one offered by the chip, the rest are listed in its menu.
    • Clean IFC export (§1.4) drops these records with the rest of RXD.

    Commands. ui.layout.recommend(layout_id, remove?: bool) -> status (adds or updates the project copy; remove = true deletes it; undoable), ui.layout.list_recommended() -> [LayoutInfo] (the active project's recommendations, with group = project); applying uses ui.layout.apply with the returned id.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] User A sets "Coordination review" as recommended and checks in. When user B opens the project, the chip offers it; applying it doesn't change B's theme or personal bookmarks. - [ ] Editing A's personal "Coordination review" after recommending it does not change the project copy until Update recommendation. - [ ] Undo after Recommend for this project removes the recommendation.

    1.29.5 Workspaces II: workflow scenarios and view bookmarks

    Owner directive (2026-10-12). "Users can adjust the workspace to their liking, save it as a bookmark and switch on demand. Users define a preference for each work process and scenario, matching their optimal workflow and preferences."

    This builds on §1.29.4. A layout bookmark stores where things are. A workflow scenario stores how the user wants to work in a particular process: a layout plus preference, shortcut and view-bookmark overlays, switched on demand or automatically.

    UI-SCEN-001 — Workflow scenarios

    ID: UI-SCEN-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: Owner directive 2026-10-12; research/01 §24 (Options), §20 (snaps), §18 (selection)

    Purpose. Different work processes need different setups. Modeling, detailing, sheet documentation, coordination review, site work, MEP routing and client presentation each have their own best combination. Users can capture each one once and recall it with one action, instead of changing a dozen settings every time.

    What a scenario holds. Every part except Name is optional.

    Part Contents
    Name, icon colour, description, slot Slot 1–9 maps to Ctrl+Shift+1…9. Layout bookmarks keep Ctrl+Alt.
    Layout A reference to a layout bookmark (§1.29.4), or no layout change
    Preference overlay Any subset of user preferences (§1.27, §1.29.1). It changes only the keys it lists. Examples: snap types and distances; object-snap priorities; selection toggles (links, underlay, pinned, by face, drag); temporary-dimension reference (wall centre or faces); tool option defaults (wall location line, auto-join, chain); view navigation (zoom behaviour, orbit centre, mouse mapping); canvas graphics (anti-aliasing, shadows for performance, background); tooltip level; keytips; autosave and sync reminders; units display precision for temporary dimensions; and the default discipline filter for the ribbon.
    Shortcut overlay Bindings that apply only while the scenario is active. A detailing scenario might bind DL to detail line and RG to filled region, while modeling keeps its own uses. Conflicts are checked against the base map when the scenario is saved.
    View bookmarks A set of view bookmarks (UI-SCEN-002) that can be opened together when the scenario is applied, for example the plan, its 3D view and a section, tiled
    Entry actions (P2) Optional: set the active ribbon tab, open a pane (History, Agent), apply a temporary view property, or run a personal Lua macro from the user's script folder. Macros run at the user's chosen trust level; project-embedded scripts never run here.

    Overlay rules. - Base and overlay. The user's normal preferences are the base. Applying a scenario lays its overlays on top of the base, and switching to another scenario first removes the current overlay. The base is never overwritten. "No scenario" means base only. - Changing a setting while a scenario is active. Options shows the setting's source ("from scenario Detailing" or "personal default"). Changing it asks once, for this scenario or for everything (the base), and remembers the answer as a preference. - Administrator locks (§1.29.3) always win. The scenario editor marks locked keys as not applied. - Applying a scenario never touches the model or undo, never marks the project as modified, and keeps an interactive session that is already running (as in UI-LAYOUT-001).

    Switching on demand. - The status bar has a single Workspace chip, for example "Detailing · Docs layout". Clicking it lists scenarios, then layouts, then Switch back (Ctrl+Shift+0), Capture…, Manage… and the Auto-switch toggle. - Scenarios are also available from View › Windows › Workspaces ▾, from command search ("Scenario: Detailing"), with Ctrl+Shift+1…9, and from Lua or MCP. - Capture current setup as scenario… creates a scenario from where the user is now. It picks up the current layout, every preference that differs from the base, the current shortcut differences, and optionally the open views as view bookmarks. The user reviews the differences before saving.

    Built-in starter scenarios. These are read-only; the user can duplicate one to customise it.

    Scenario Layout Example overlay
    Modeling Modeling Default snaps, auto-join on, select-pinned off
    Detailing Documentation Snaps to endpoints and intersections only, selecting links and underlay off, detail-line shortcuts, Annotate tab active
    Sheet documentation Documentation Sheets tab active in the Project Browser, select-by-face off, temporary dimensions set to faces
    Coordination review Coordination Select links on, select pinned off, History and Notifications panes open, worksharing display on
    Site Modeling Larger snap distances, Massing & Site tab active
    MEP routing Modeling Systems tab active, System Browser open, connector snaps first
    Presentation Presentation Tooltips off, temporary dimensions hidden, smooth navigation, high-quality viewport graphics

    Capture dialog. Capture current setup as scenario… opens a review dialog with a Name field (same validation as layout names), a choice of layout (use the active layout, save the current arrangement as a new layout, or no layout change), and three lists with a check box per row: preferences that differ from the base (key, base value, current value), shortcut differences (keys, base command, current command), and open views (to become view bookmarks, off by default). Save creates the scenario with the ticked rows only.

    Commands. - ui.scenario.list(group?: builtin|org|personal|project) -> [ScenarioInfo] (id, name, group, slot, icon colour, layout id, counts of overlay keys, shortcuts and bookmarks, is_active) - ui.scenario.apply(scenario_id | name | slot) -> report (lists keys applied, keys skipped because locked, and missing view bookmarks) - ui.scenario.switch_back() -> status (returns to the scenario, or base, active before the last apply) - ui.scenario.capture(name, include: [layout, prefs, shortcuts, open_views]) -> ScenarioDraft (returns the differences for review; nothing is saved) - ui.scenario.save(ScenarioDef) -> scenario_id (saves a reviewed draft or a definition written by a script) - ui.scenario.update(scenario_id, from_current?: bool) -> status (with from_current, replaces the overlay with the current differences from the base) - ui.scenario.set_pref(key, value, target: scenario|base) -> status (the scripted equivalent of the "for this scenario / for everything" question; scenario needs an active scenario).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Create "Detailing" with select-links off and DL → detail line. Applying it changes only those two things; switching to "Modeling" restores select-links and the original DL binding. - [ ] With "Detailing" active, changing the snap distance and choosing for this scenario changes only "Detailing". Choosing for everything changes the base, and "Detailing" still overrides it if it lists that key. - [ ] Capture current setup lists exactly the settings that differ from the base, before it saves. - [ ] A scenario that sets a key the administrator has locked shows the key as not applied, and the locked value stays in force.

    UI-SCEN-002 — View bookmarks

    ID: UI-SCEN-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/01 §16 (navigation, saved home view), research/04 §1 (views); Chapter 6 (BCF)

    Purpose. Saved viewpoints inside views: a zoom region in a plan, or a camera and section box in a 3D view. The user can jump back to the exact place in the model they work on repeatedly.

    What a view bookmark holds. - the view id - in 2D views, the zoom and pan region - in 3D views, the camera, projection and section box - optional extras: temporary hide and isolate state, a temporary visual style override, the active workset or design option filter for display, and a selection set reference

    Workflow. 1. Choose Bookmark this view position (Ctrl+Shift+B, or the right-click menu on a view tab) and give it a name. (Ctrl+D is reserved for Reviera Home, §1.26.3.) 2. Bookmarks appear in a Bookmarks tab of the Project Browser, grouped by view, and in the Workspace chip's menu. 3. Double-click a bookmark (or use command search) to open its view and restore the position.

    Scope and storage. - Personal (default). Stored per user and per project in the user data directory, keyed by the project's DataId. Personal bookmarks are never stored in the model, so they don't clutter other users' projects. - Shared. Share with project moves a bookmark into the RXD document views/bookmarks, which travels with the model and through BIMserver. - BCF. A bookmark can be exported as a BCF viewpoint (camera, section box, visibility). A BCF viewpoint can be imported as a bookmark (Chapter 6, BCF). - Missing views. If a bookmark's view no longer exists, the bookmark is shown greyed out, with Re-target to view… and Delete. - Save dialog. Name (required, 1–80 characters, unique per view; default "<view name> 1", "… 2"), check boxes for the optional extras (off by default), and Personal / Shared with project (shared needs edit rights in BIMserver mode). Saving is presentation only for personal bookmarks; sharing is an undoable project edit. - Re-target. Re-target to view… offers views of a compatible kind (2D region bookmarks to 2D views, camera bookmarks to 3D views). The stored region or camera is reused as is; if it lies outside the new view's extents, Reviera zooms to fit and reports it. - Applying opens or activates the view (view.activate), restores the region or camera without adding an undo entry, and adds one entry to the view's navigation history so Previous Pan/Zoom returns to where the user was. Optional extras are applied as temporary view state (§1.18) and never change the view's saved properties. - BCF mapping. Export writes one BCF viewpoint with the camera (perspective or orthogonal), the section box as clipping planes, and the visibility of the temporary hide/isolate state as component visibility by IFC GlobalId. Import creates a personal 3D bookmark on the default 3D view, or on a chosen 3D view, and reports elements in the viewpoint that are not in the model. BCF version handling is owned by Ch. 6.
