    Commands. - view.bookmark.save(name, view_id?, include: [camera, section_box, temp_hide, visual_style, selection_set]) -> bookmark_id (default view: active) - view.bookmark.apply(bookmark_id) -> status - view.bookmark.list(view_id?, scope: personal|shared|all) -> [ViewBookmark] - view.bookmark.delete(bookmark_id) -> status (deleting a shared bookmark is an undoable project edit) - view.bookmark.share(bookmark_id) -> status (moves a personal bookmark into views/bookmarks; undoable) - view.bookmark.retarget(bookmark_id, view_id) -> status - view.bookmark.export_bcf(bookmark_id, path) -> status, view.bookmark.import_bcf(path) -> bookmark_id.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Bookmark a zoomed region of "Level 2" and a 3D camera with a section box. After closing and reopening the project, both bookmarks restore exactly. - [ ] A personal bookmark doesn't appear for another user of the same BIMserver project. A shared bookmark appears after their next sync. - [ ] Exporting a 3D bookmark as BCF and re-importing it reproduces the camera and section box.

    UI-SCEN-003 — Scenario triggers and precedence

    ID: UI-SCEN-003 · Priority: P2 (manual switching is P1, under UI-SCEN-001) · Ref: UI-LAYOUT-004

    • What can trigger a scenario.
    • The auto-switch rules from UI-LAYOUT-004 can target a scenario as well as a layout. The contexts are the same: view type, Family Editor, BIMserver mode, monitor setup and window width. Two more are added: the active ribbon tab or tool family (for example any Systems tool), and the project, meaning a personal default scenario per project.
    • Scenarios can also be started by script, through Lua or MCP (ui.scenario.apply), so a user's agent can, for example, prepare a review session.
    • Precedence, highest first:
    Rank Source Example
    1 Applied by hand Picked from the chip, a shortcut or command search
    2 Context rule, in rule order Sheet view active
    3 The user's per-project default —
    4 The project's recommended scenario Only if the user has opted in once per project
    5 The startup choice (UI-LAYOUT-002) —

    When a context ends, the scenario that was active before it is restored. - No ping-pong. A rule can't re-trigger within 2 s of the user overriding it by hand. An optional "notify on auto-switch" toast offers Undo switch. - Per-project default. Stored per user and per project (keyed by the project's DataId) in the user data directory, never in the model. It applies when the project's first view opens and is restored to the previous scenario when the project's last window closes. - Project recommendation opt-in. The first time a project with a recommended scenario is opened, the Workspace chip asks once: Use the project's scenario / Not now / Never for this project. The answer is stored with the per-project default.

    Commands. ui.scenario.set_project_default(scenario_id | null) -> status (for the active project; null clears it); context rules use ui.layout.rules.set with a rule target of either a layout id or a scenario id (UI-LAYOUT-004); ui.scenario.apply (UI-SCEN-001) starts a scenario from a script.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Rule Systems tool active → "MEP routing". Starting a duct tool applies the scenario. Finishing the tool and activating an architectural tool restores the previous scenario. A manual switch during the duct session isn't overridden.

    UI-SCEN-004 — Scenario editor, storage and portability

    ID: UI-SCEN-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: UI-LAYOUT-005

    • The editor. Manage workspaces… lists scenarios (built-in, organisation, personal) and layouts. For each scenario it has these tabs:
    • General: name, slot, icon, description
    • Layout
    • Preferences: only the overridden keys are listed. Add setting… searches every Options key. Remove returns a key to the base.
    • Shortcuts: the overlay bindings, with conflicts highlighted
    • View bookmarks
    • Entry actions
    • Triggers

    It also has Compare with base, showing the effective differences. - Storage. <config>/reviera/scenarios/<slug>.toml, which references layouts by id and view bookmarks by id. Organisation scenarios come from the defaults directory and are read-only, with an Org badge. - Portability. Scenarios are part of ui.profile.export and ui.profile.import and of the profile sync folder (UI-LAYOUT-005). They can also be shared one at a time; a scenario's referenced layout is bundled with it on export. - Team-recommended scenarios. A project can recommend a scenario in the same way as a layout (UI-LAYOUT-006). Its preference overlay is limited to non-personal keys, such as snaps and selection toggles. Appearance, mouse mapping and shortcuts are never pushed by a project. - Editor rules. Built-in and organisation scenarios open read-only, with Duplicate to edit. Edits to a personal scenario are saved when the editor closes or another scenario is selected; Revert discards edits since the editor opened. A scenario that is active while edited is re-applied on save. Validation: a unique name (1–64 characters), a slot not used by another scenario (a clash offers to move it), shortcut overlay conflicts shown in red and allowed only after confirmation, preference values checked against each key's type and range. - Delete. Deleting a personal scenario that is active returns to base first; rules and per-project defaults that name it are listed in the confirmation and are removed with it. - Import clash policy (on_clash): rename (default), replace, skip. A bundled layout that clashes follows the same policy. - Recommend. The stored copy goes to RXD document ui/state › recommended_scenarios[]; keys outside the allowed set are dropped with a list shown before saving.

    Commands. - ui.scenario.manage(scenario_id?) -> () opens Manage workspaces at the given scenario - ui.scenario.diff(scenario_id) -> [PrefDiff] (key, base value, scenario value, locked; the data behind Compare with base) - ui.scenario.duplicate(scenario_id, name) -> scenario_id, ui.scenario.delete(scenario_id) -> status - ui.scenario.save(ScenarioDef) -> scenario_id (also used by the editor) - ui.scenario.export(scenario_id, path) -> status, ui.scenario.import(path, on_clash) -> scenario_id - ui.scenario.recommend(scenario_id, remove?: bool) -> status (undoable project edit).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Export a scenario that references a personal layout. Importing it on another machine brings in both, and the scenario's layout reference resolves. - [ ] Compare with base lists the same keys that applying the scenario changes.

    1.30 UI state for Lua and MCP

    1.30.1 Exposure principle

    ID: UI-API-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: TECH_STACK §2, §3.5, §3.6; research/01 §27 item 2

    Purpose. Let scripts and AI agents see and drive what the user sees: active view, selection, open windows, tool state.

    Behaviour & rules. - Every UI command in this chapter is a registry command and therefore available as reviera.<id> in Lua and as an MCP tool, unless marked otherwise in the catalog (§1.34). - UI commands that only change presentation (view activation, zoom, selection, pane visibility) are not undoable and do not open model transactions; they run on the UI thread via the command queue and return once applied. - MCP permission levels (TECH_STACK §3.6): UI read commands (ui.get_*, selection.get, window.list, ui.screenshot) require read-only; UI write commands that change presentation only (view.activate, selection.set, view.zoom*) are allowed at read-only level by default but can be restricted in Options › AI & MCP ("Agents may change my view and selection": ask / allow / deny); commands that change persistent UI settings (ui.options.set, ui.shortcuts.*, ui.ribbon.*) require full-scripting level.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An MCP client at read-only level can call ui.get_active_view and selection.get but receives a permission error from ui.options.set.

    1.30.2 State queries

    ID: UI-API-002 · Priority: P0

    Commands. - ui.get_state() -> UiState with fields: mode (local|bimserver), documents[] (id, path or server URI, modified flags), active_document, active_view (id, name, kind), windows[] (as window.list), selection (ids, counts by category), tool (command id, step, options) or null, edit_mode stack, ribbon.active_tab, theme, home_visible, server (connection state, project, revision, pending changes). - ui.get_active_view() -> {view_id, name, kind, document_id, window_id}. - ui.get_active_document() -> {document_id, path|uri, schema, modified}. - tool.get_active() -> {command_id, step, prompt, options} | null. - ui.screenshot(view_id?, width?, height?, overlays: bool = false) -> PNG renders a view (offscreen if not visible) for agents that need to "see" the model; size is capped (default 2048 px longest side).

    Behaviour & rules. - Consistency. Every query answers from the latest published context snapshot (UI-ARCH-003), never from a half-applied state; each result carries the snapshot's version so a client can tell whether two answers belong together. - Size limits. selection in ui.get_state() returns at most 1 000 ids plus truncated: true and the full count; clients use selection.get() for the complete list. windows[] and documents[] are not truncated. - No model access. These queries never open a transaction and never wait for one; during a long command they answer immediately with the previous snapshot and busy: true. - Screenshot rules. Width and height default to the view window size (or 1280 × 960 when the view is not open) and are clamped to the cap; aspect ratio is kept when only one is given. With overlays = false no selection, pre-highlight, grips or mode borders are drawn. Rendering a closed view does not open it, does not add it to the recent list and releases its GPU resources afterwards. Views that are not graphical (schedules) return an error not_graphical. A screenshot respects temporary hide/isolate of the view's window if it is open. - Errors. Unknown ids return not_found; queries never return partial objects. - Permissions. All of these are read commands, allowed at the read-only MCP level (UI-API-001).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] ui.get_state() reflects a selection made by the user within one second. - [ ] ui.screenshot of a non-active view returns an image without changing the active view. - [ ] During a 10-second regeneration, ui.get_state() returns within 50 ms with busy: true. - [ ] With 5 000 elements selected, ui.get_state() reports a count of 5 000, 1 000 ids and truncated: true. - [ ] ui.screenshot of a schedule returns not_graphical.

    1.30.3 MCP resources and change notifications

    ID: UI-API-003 · Priority: P0

    Behaviour & rules. - MCP resources: reviera://ui/state, reviera://ui/active-view, reviera://ui/selection, reviera://ui/windows, reviera://ui/tool, reviera://view/{id}/image (screenshot). Clients may subscribe; Reviera sends resource-updated notifications on change, coalesced to at most 10 per second per resource. - Lua scripts subscribe with reviera.on("selection_changed" | "active_view_changed" | "tool_changed" | "document_opened" | "document_closed" | "theme_changed", fn); handlers run on the scripting thread and must not block (long handlers are cut off with a warning per the scripting chapter). - Resource contents. Each resource returns JSON of the same shape as the matching query: ui/state = ui.get_state(), ui/active-view = ui.get_active_view(), ui/selection = selection.get(), ui/windows = window.list(), ui/tool = tool.get_active(). view/{id}/image returns a PNG made with ui.screenshot(id) at default size and is regenerated only when read, never pushed. - Coalescing. Updates within a 100 ms window are merged into one notification that carries the latest snapshot version; a client that reads after the notification always gets the newest state, never an intermediate one. - Event payloads (Lua). selection_changed(ids, by_category), active_view_changed(view_id, previous_view_id), tool_changed(command_id | nil, step), document_opened(document_id), document_closed(document_id), theme_changed(ui, canvas). Events are delivered in the order they happened; a handler that raises an error is logged and kept subscribed; after 3 consecutive time-outs the handler is unsubscribed with a notice. - Unsubscribing. reviera.on returns a handle with :off(); MCP clients unsubscribe per resource. Subscriptions end when the session or script ends. - Permissions. Subscriptions are read access; a client at any MCP level may subscribe. The "Agents may change my view and selection" setting (UI-API-001) restricts only writes; it never blocks reading or subscribing.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A subscribed MCP client receives an update for reviera://ui/selection after the user clicks an element. - [ ] A crossing selection that changes the selection 40 times in one second produces at most 10 notifications, and the last one matches the final selection. - [ ] A Lua handler for active_view_changed receives the new and previous view ids.

    1.30.4 Driving the UI

    ID: UI-API-004 · Priority: P0

    Commands and rules. - view.activate(view_id, opts?), selection.set(ids[], mode?: replace|add|remove (default replace)) -> (), selection.highlight(ids, duration_ms?) (temporary pre-highlight to draw the user's attention; no selection change), view.zoom_to_elements(view_id?, ids), ui.pane.show(id), ui.ribbon.activate_tab(id), ui.notify(message, level: info|warning|error, actions?). - tool.start(command_id, type_id?, preset_args?) -> session_id starts an interactive tool session for the user to complete (for example an agent prepares a wall tool with a chosen type); tool.cancel(), tool.finish() -> (). - Agents and scripts should prefer non-interactive commands with explicit arguments; tool.start exists to hand over to the user. - Highlight. selection.highlight draws the elements in canvas.preselection with a pulsing outline (a steady outline when Reduce motion is on) for duration_ms (default 2 000, range 200–30 000). A new call replaces the previous highlight from the same session. Elements not visible in any open view are reported back as not_visible ids. - Notifications. ui.notify shows an in-app toast and adds the entry to the Notifications pane. actions is a list of up to 3 {label, command_id, args}; clicking one runs that command with the caller's permissions. Toasts from scripts and agents carry the source name ("From agent: planner"). More than 5 notifications per 10 s from one session are collapsed into one "n more messages" entry. - Tool hand-over. tool.start fails with busy when the user is already in a tool session or edit mode (it never interrupts the user). The started session belongs to the user; the caller is told when it ends through the tool_changed event (UI-API-003). tool.cancel and tool.finish act only on a session the same caller started, unless the caller has full-scripting permission. - Presentation-only rule. All commands here except tool.finish (which submits the tool's commands) are presentation only: not undoable, no modified flag; they follow the "Agents may change my view and selection" setting (UI-API-001) and the concurrency rules of UI-API-006. - Errors. Unknown ids return not_found; hidden or unknown ribbon tabs and panes return not_available; a denied presentation change returns permission_denied and shows nothing to the user.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] selection.highlight flashes the given elements in all visible views without changing selection.get() -> {ids[], by_category}. - [ ] ui.notify with an action "Open schedule" shows a toast whose button opens that schedule. - [ ] tool.start while the user is sketching returns busy and the sketch continues undisturbed. - [ ] With "Agents may change my view and selection" set to deny, view.activate from MCP returns permission_denied and the active view does not change.

    1.30.5 Interactive picks for scripts

    ID: UI-API-005 · Priority: P1

    Behaviour & rules. - ui.pick.point(prompt, view_id?, snap?: bool) -> Point3 | cancelled, ui.pick.elements(prompt, filter?, multiple?: bool) -> [id] | cancelled, ui.pick.box(prompt) -> Rect, ui.prompt.text(title, label, default?) -> string | cancelled, ui.prompt.choice(title, options[]) -> index | cancelled. - Picks show the prompt in the status bar with the requester's name ("Script 'Renumber' asks: pick the first door"); Esc cancels. - Over MCP these require an interactive user; they time out (default 120 s) and are refused when Reviera runs headless. - Pick sessions. Each call starts a short interactive session with its own contextual tab "Pick for <requester>" holding Finish (for multiple picks), Cancel and the prompt. Only one pick request is active at a time; further requests queue in arrival order and the status bar shows "n pick requests waiting". - Filters. filter accepts category (IFC class or Reviera category key), type id, view-visibility, editable_only and a list of allowed ids. Elements that fail the filter cannot be pre-highlighted; the cursor shows a "not allowed" badge over them. - Point picks use normal snapping unless snap = false; coordinate entry (§1.33.1) works. The returned point is in project coordinates (Ch. 2) and in internal units. - Box picks follow window/crossing by drag direction and return the rectangle in view coordinates with the view id. - Prompts. ui.prompt.text and ui.prompt.choice show small modal dialogs titled with the requester's name; text input is limited to 4 096 characters; choice shows up to 50 options with search when more than 10. - Interruptions. Closing the view, starting another tool or switching documents cancels the pick and returns cancelled. A timed-out request returns timeout. - No hidden picks. A script cannot pick on behalf of the user without the prompt being shown; picks are never satisfied by synthetic input.

    Commands. ui.pick.point, ui.pick.elements, ui.pick.box, ui.prompt.text, ui.prompt.choice as listed above.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A Lua script calling ui.pick.elements("Pick doors", {category="IfcDoor"}, true) lets the user pick only doors and returns their ids on Finish. - [ ] Two scripts asking for picks at the same time are served one after the other, each with its own prompt. - [ ] An MCP pick request with no answer for 120 s returns timeout.

    1.30.6 Concurrency with the user

    ID: UI-API-006 · Priority: P0 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.3

    Behaviour & rules. - Requests from Lua or MCP that would open a model transaction while the user is in a tool session or edit mode are queued; the status bar shows "External request waiting (n)" with a button that lists them and lets the user allow them now (ending the user's tool), defer, or reject. - Presentation-only requests (view.activate, selection.set, zoom) are applied immediately unless the user is in the middle of a drag or text edit, in which case they are applied when it ends. - While an agent operation runs, the status bar agent indicator shows its name; the user can stop it (cancelling the current command and rejecting queued ones from that session). - Undo history entries record their source (UI, Lua script name, MCP session/agent name).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An MCP wall.create request sent while the user is drawing a floor sketch waits until the sketch finishes or the user allows it. - [ ] The Undo drop-down shows "Create wall — agent: <session name>" for an agent-created wall.

    1.31 Agent pane

    1.31.1 Purpose and architecture

    ID: UI-AGENT-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/01 §5 ([2027] assistant palette) · screenshots/ui/revit2027_autodesk_assistant_button.png, screenshots/ui/revit2027_autodesk_assistant_panel.png

    Purpose. Offer a built-in, open, vendor-neutral AI assistant that works through Reviera's own MCP server, as Reviera's alternative to the reference's proprietary assistant.

    Behaviour & rules. - The Agent pane is a dockable pane (default: right dock, hidden) toggled with Ctrl+J, the QAT-strip Agent button, or View › User Interface › Agent. - It contains a built-in MCP client connected to Reviera's own MCP server through an in-process transport, plus optionally to additional MCP servers the user configures (for example a document-search server or a company standards server). Each server's tools are namespaced. - It talks to a model provider configured by the user: any provider reachable through a supported chat API, including locally hosted models; no provider is bundled or preconfigured, and nothing is sent anywhere until the user configures one. Keys are stored in the OS keychain. - Agent sessions are ordinary MCP sessions: they get the permission level chosen for the pane (default: model-edit with confirmation), and their commands go through the same queue, transactions and undo attribution as any other client (§1.30.6). - The pane is optional; builds without networking can omit the provider connectors while keeping the pane for local providers.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With no provider configured, the pane shows a setup page and makes no network connection. - [ ] Tools from Reviera's MCP server appear in the agent's tool list exactly as an external MCP client would see them.

    1.31.2 Conversation UI

    ID: UI-AGENT-002 · Priority: P1

    UI. - Header: provider/model selector, permission level badge, New conversation, History (list of past conversations with search and timestamps), Settings. - Transcript: user and assistant messages (rendered Markdown subset: paragraphs, lists, code, tables); tool-call cards showing tool name, arguments (collapsible JSON), status (pending approval, running, done, failed, undone), result summary, and for model-changing calls the undo entry name with an Undo button. - Context chips above the input: Active view, Selection (n elements), Screenshot of active view, Open schedule; each can be toggled before sending. Default attachments are set in Options. - Input: multi-line text; Enter sends, Shift+Enter new line; slash-commands for quick actions (/select, /explain-warnings, /schedule); a Stop button while the agent runs. - Suggested prompts on an empty conversation, generated from the current context (for example "Tag all untagged doors in this view"). - Canvas right-click "Ask Agent about selection" opens the pane with the Selection chip attached. - History list. The History button opens a list of past conversations for this user (newest first) with title (the first user message, editable), date, provider and model, number of model-changing calls, and the project it was held in. A search field filters by text in titles and messages. Actions: Open (read-only transcript; Continue starts a new turn in it if its provider is still configured), Rename, Delete, Export as Markdown…. Conversations whose retention has expired are not listed (UI-AGENT-003). - Stop. Stop cancels the provider request, cancels the running tool call where the command supports cancellation, and drops queued calls of that turn; calls already committed stay and can be undone with Undo agent turn.

    Commands. These commands are for Lua and the pane itself and are not exposed over MCP (§1.34 notes): - agent.conversation.new(provider?, model?) -> conversation_id - agent.send(conversation_id, text, attachments?) -> () (attachments are context-chip ids: active_view, selection, screenshot, open_schedule) - agent.stop(conversation_id) -> () - agent.history(filter?) -> [ConversationSummary] (filter by text, date range, project).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Each tool call the agent makes appears as a card before or as it runs; failed calls show the error. - [ ] Clicking Undo on a tool-call card undoes exactly that call's transaction (or reports that later changes depend on it).

    1.31.3 Approval, safety and undo

    ID: UI-AGENT-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.6 (safety)

    Behaviour & rules. - Approval policy (per conversation, default from Options): Ask for every model change (default), Ask for destructive changes only (delete, purge, check-in, overwrite), Allow all model changes this conversation. Read-only and presentation commands never ask unless the user chose so (§1.30.1). - execute_lua and full-scripting tools always ask, showing the full script. - Preview mode: for commands that support preview, the card offers Preview (temporary graphics in the active view) before Approve. - Each agent turn (one user message and the resulting tool calls) is wrapped in a transaction group so Undo agent turn reverts it in one step. - Model content (element names, parameter values, text notes, server comments) supplied to the agent is marked as data in the prompt envelope; the pane never executes instructions found in model content without the user's approval under the policy above. - Transcripts are stored per user in the data directory (retention configurable: never, 30 days, forever); never in the model and never checked in. - The pane shows which external services a conversation has used. - Approval card. A call that needs approval shows its tool name, a plain-language summary generated from the command descriptor ("Delete 3 elements: 2 walls, 1 door"), the arguments, and Approve, Reject, Preview (where supported) and Approve all like this in this conversation. The card does not time out; the agent waits. Reject takes an optional reason that is returned to the agent with the error. - Undo agent turn is offered on the last message of every turn with committed changes. If later edits depend on the turn's changes, the shell reports the conflicting undo entries and offers Undo back to here (which also undoes the later entries) or Cancel.

    Commands. agent.approve(call_id) -> () and agent.reject(call_id) -> () are UI-only: they are bound to the card buttons and are not callable from Lua or MCP, so no script or agent can approve a call. agent.undo_turn(conversation_id, turn_id) -> () (Lua and the pane) undoes the turn's transaction group.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Under the default policy, an agent's element.delete call waits for Approve; Reject returns an error result to the agent and changes nothing. - [ ] "Undo agent turn" after a turn that created 12 tags removes all 12 in one step. - [ ] With retention "never", closing the conversation leaves no transcript on disk.

    1.32 BIMserver-mode user interface

    1.32.1 Connect and log in

    ID: UI-SRV-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.7, §3.7.1

    Workflow. 1. Collaborate › Connect (or Home › Servers › Add server, or opening a recent server project). 2. Login dialog: Server (combo of saved connections plus "New…"), URL, user name, password, "Remember me" (stores the session token in the OS keychain; the password is never stored), Test connection, Log in. Shows server version, supported IFC schemas and deserialisers once reached. 3. On success the connection indicator turns to "Connected as <user>" and the Server Projects pane opens.

    Behaviour & rules. - TLS certificate problems show a clear dialog with certificate details and options Cancel / Trust this certificate for this server (pinned) — never a silent bypass. - Expired tokens trigger the login dialog pre-filled, without losing local work. - Credentials are never exposed to Lua or MCP (bimserver.login from scripts uses a saved connection id; the keychain lookup is internal). - Logout (bimserver.logout) keeps the working copy and switches to offline.

    Commands. ui.server.login_dialog(connection_id?); protocol commands bimserver.login, bimserver.logout are owned by Ch. 6.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Logging in with "Remember me" and restarting reconnects without asking for the password until the token expires. - [ ] A self-signed certificate is refused until the user explicitly trusts it.

    1.32.2 Server Projects pane and Home Servers page

    ID: UI-SRV-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/01 §2.2 (project browsing pattern) · screenshots/ui/home_new_projects.png

    UI. - A tree of servers › projects › sub-projects, with search; each project shows schema, last revision number, date and author. - Selecting a project shows its revisions list (number, date, user, comment, size) in the lower half, with filter by user and date and search in comments. - Actions: Open latest, Open revision…, Link into current model (Ch. 6), New project… (name, schema, parent), Publish current model here (bimserver.publish_local), Properties (project settings the user may edit), Refresh. - Opening a project downloads the revision into the local working copy with progress and Cancel; subsequent opens use the cache and only download newer revisions. - Home › Servers shows the same browser full-page, plus recently opened server projects.

    Commands. ui.server.browser(connection_id?); data commands (bimserver.list_projects, bimserver.list_revisions, bimserver.open, bimserver.create_project) are owned by Ch. 6.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Opening revision 12 of a project with 40 revisions opens that revision read-write in the working copy, and the title shows r12.

    1.32.3 Check In

    ID: UI-SRV-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.7 (check-in)

    Workflow. 1. Collaborate › Check In (CI), or QAT Sync › Sync with Options. 2. Check In dialog: comment (required; template from Options), change summary (counts of added/modified/deleted elements by category, expandable to a list with "zoom to"), option "Get latest first" (default on), option "Relinquish my ownership after check-in", and Check In / Cancel. 3. Progress shows serialise → upload → server processing; the UI remains usable for navigation (editing is paused until upload completes, with a status explanation). 4. Result: new revision number toast; failures show the server message and keep local changes.

    Behaviour & rules. - Comment validation. 1–2 000 characters after trimming; the template's placeholders ({user}, {date}, {changed_count}) are filled in before the dialog opens. The last 10 comments are offered in a drop-down. - Change summary comes from the live store's change sets since the last Get Latest or Check In (Ch. 2b). "Zoom to" activates a view containing the element and selects it without closing the dialog. RXD-only changes (for example a shared view bookmark) are listed under Project data. - Get latest first. When on and newer revisions exist, Reviera runs Get Latest (UI-SRV-004) first; if that produces conflicts, Check In stops at the conflict dialog and resumes after the conflicts are resolved. - Open edit modes. Check In is refused while an edit mode or tool session is active ("Finish or cancel <mode> first"). - Save first. The model is saved locally before upload so that a crash during upload leaves a consistent working copy. - Ownership. With "Relinquish my ownership" ticked, ownership is released only after the server confirms the new revision; on failure the user keeps it. - Cancel is possible during serialise and upload; it leaves the working copy and the server unchanged. During server processing Cancel is disabled with the explanation "The server is processing the revision". - Offline. In offline mode Check In is disabled with "Not connected".

    Commands. ui.server.checkin_dialog(comment?) -> () opens the dialog (pre-filling the comment when given); OK submits bimserver.check_in(comment) (Ch. 6), preceded by bimserver.get_latest() when "Get latest first" is on and followed by ownership.relinquish(scope: all) when chosen.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Check In is disabled with no local changes (tooltip "Nothing to check in"). - [ ] A failed upload leaves the working copy unchanged and offers Retry. - [ ] An empty comment disables the Check In button. - [ ] With a floor sketch active, Check In is refused with a message naming the mode. - [ ] With "Relinquish" ticked and a failed upload, the user still owns the elements.

    1.32.4 Get Latest and Sync

    ID: UI-SRV-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.7, §3.7.2

    Behaviour & rules. - Get Latest (RL) downloads newer revisions and merges them by GlobalId into the working copy. Sync = Get Latest, merge, then Check In (with the Check In dialog unless "Sync now" with a remembered comment is chosen). - After merging, a Merge report notice lists elements added, changed and removed by others, with "Show in view" (temporarily highlights them; uses the Collaboration Display "Model Updates" mode) and "Select". - Conflicts (an element changed locally and on the server) open the Conflict resolution dialog: per element or per category, choose Keep mine / Take theirs / Inspect (side-by-side property comparison and a highlight in the active view); bulk actions; the dialog can be left and resumed. Rules for what counts as a conflict are owned by Ch. 6. - Merge results are one undo-able step only before any later edit; after that, the server revision is the baseline.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] After another user moves a wall and checks in, Get Latest updates the wall and the merge report lists it. - [ ] A conflicting edit opens the conflict dialog; choosing Keep mine and checking in uploads the local value.

    1.32.5 Connection indicator and notifications

    ID: UI-SRV-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.7.1 (notification interfaces)

    Behaviour & rules. - Connection indicator in the QAT strip and status bar: Offline (grey), Connected (accent), Syncing (animated, with reduce-motion fallback), Error (warning colour + icon). It shows counts of local changes not checked in and of new server revisions. Clicking opens the Server pane. - Notifications: new revision events from the server (pushed; polling fallback at the configured interval) show an in-app toast "Revision 42 by Alex: <comment> — Get Latest / Dismiss" and, when Reviera is not focused, an OS notification (preference). Ownership requests, request responses and lock changes also notify. - All notifications are kept in the Notifications pane (with filters, mark read, and actions), and are available via ui.notifications.list. - Working offline: the indicator shows Offline; Save keeps working locally; Check In and Get Latest are disabled; on reconnect, a notice summarises what changed on the server.

    Commands. ui.notifications.list(filter?) -> [Notification], ui.notifications.dismiss(id|all), ui.notifications.act(id, action).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A check-in by another user produces a toast within 5 seconds when push notifications are available. - [ ] Disconnecting the network switches the indicator to Offline without an error dialog; local saves still succeed.

    1.32.6 Revision history

    ID: UI-SRV-006 · Priority: P1

    Behaviour & rules. - The Revision History pane lists the current project's revisions; actions: Open revision read-only in a new document, Compare with working copy / with another revision (Ch. 6 bimserver.compare; results shown as a colour-coded temporary view state plus a list), Download as .ifc, Copy revision URI. - Comparisons use the mode-border convention (§1.17.2) with the label "Comparing r40 ↔ working copy". - List columns. Revision number, date (UI locale), user, comment (first line, full text in a tooltip), size, and a marker for the revision the working copy is based on. Sort by any column; filter by user and date range; search in comments. The list loads 100 revisions at a time and fetches more on scroll. - Compare display. Added elements in status.success, changed in status.warning, removed shown as ghost outlines in status.error, each also with a distinct line pattern so colour is not the only signal (§1.33.2). A legend sits in the view's top-left under the mode label. The list beside it groups changes by category with counts; selecting a row selects and zooms to the element. Compare state is temporary view state: Esc or End comparison clears it, and it is never saved. - Open read-only opens the revision as a separate document whose title carries r<n> (read-only); editing commands are disabled in it, and it can be closed without a save prompt. - Restore. Make this the latest revision… (with a required reason) is offered to users with the server right to do so; it creates a new revision with the old content (Ch. 6) and never rewrites history. - Offline. The pane shows the cached list with "Offline — list may be out of date" and disables actions that need the server.

    Commands. ui.server.revisions(project?) -> () opens or focuses the pane; actions call bimserver.history(), bimserver.compare(roid_a, roid_b), bimserver.download_revision(server_id, roid, path) and bimserver.restore(roid, reason) (Ch. 6).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Comparing two revisions highlights added, changed and removed elements in distinct, labelled styles. - [ ] Opening r12 read-only leaves the working copy open and unchanged, and closing r12 asks nothing. - [ ] Ending a comparison restores the view's normal display with no undo entry.

    1.32.7 Ownership feedback

    ID: UI-SRV-007 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/01 §17 (Editing Requests, Editable Only), §15 (#12 worksharing display); TECH_STACK §3.7.2

    Behaviour & rules. - Elements owned by another user show the owner in tooltips and Properties (read-only reason "Owned by <user>"); attempting to edit offers Request editing (sends a request; status bar count updates for the owner). - Editing Requests dialog: incoming and outgoing requests with Grant / Deny / Withdraw. - Collaboration Display modes on the View Control Bar colour elements by ownership status, owner, or "changed since my last Get Latest", with a legend. - Edit attempt flow. When a command would change elements the user does not own, the command is not run. A dialog lists the blocking elements with their owners and offers Request editing (sends one request per owner, with an optional message), Select blocking elements, and Cancel. Elements owned by nobody are taken automatically (ownership.borrow) before the command runs, when the server allows it. - Waiting for a grant. Pending outgoing requests show in the status-bar Editing Requests count. When a request is granted, a toast offers Retry the last action; denied requests show the owner's message. - Incoming requests raise a toast for the owner with Grant, Deny and Open requests. The Editing Requests dialog lists incoming and outgoing requests (requester, elements with "zoom to", message, time, status) with Grant, Deny (with optional message) and Withdraw. - Properties palette. For elements owned by others, every editable row is read-only with the reason "Owned by <user>"; a banner at the top of the palette offers Request editing. - Relinquish. Collaborate › Relinquish All Mine, and right-click › Relinquish on owned elements; refused for elements with local changes not checked in ("Check in first"). - Offline. Ownership information shows the last known state, marked "may be out of date"; editing elements the user does not hold is refused until connected.

    Commands. Ownership and request commands are owned by Ch. 6: ownership.borrow, ownership.relinquish, ownership.query, editrequest.create, editrequest.grant, editrequest.deny, editrequest.retract, editrequest.manage (opens the Editing Requests dialog); Collaboration Display uses view.set_worksharing_display(mode).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Moving an element owned by another user is blocked with a message offering Request editing. - [ ] After the owner grants the request, Retry the last action moves the element. - [ ] Relinquishing an element with local changes not checked in is refused.

    1.33 Accessibility, HiDPI and localisation

    1.33.1 Keyboard operability

    ID: UI-A11Y-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/01 §22 (keytips), §23

    Behaviour & rules. - Every command is reachable without a pointer (sequences, keytips, Command Search). Every pane, dialog and the ribbon support full keyboard navigation with a visible focus ring (token ui.focus_ring, minimum 2 logical pixels). - F6/Shift+F6 cycles focus regions; within the canvas, Tab cycles candidates and arrow keys nudge the selection by the current snap increment (Shift+arrow: 10×) as a move command (P1). - Canvas picks can be made from the keyboard: coordinate entry (type x,y or @dx,dy or <distance<angle when a tool asks for a point; P1) and snap.query for scripts. - No feature depends on hover alone: hover information is also available for the selected element through Properties and the status bar. - Focus regions in F6 order: ribbon (with QAT), left dock panes, view window tabs, canvas, View Control Bar, right and bottom dock panes, status bar. Hidden regions are skipped. Each region remembers its last focused control. - Canvas keyboard selection. With the canvas focused and no tool active, Ctrl+Shift+Right and Ctrl+Shift+Left step through the elements visible in the view, nearest to the view centre first, pre-highlighting each (Tab keeps its meaning of cycling candidates under the pointer, UI-SEL-001); while an element is stepped to, Enter selects it and Ctrl+Enter adds it to the selection (otherwise Enter keeps its repeat-last meaning, §1.26.3). The status bar and the accessible summary name the current element. - Nudge. Arrow keys move the selection by the current snap length increment for the zoom level (Shift+arrow: 10×). Consecutive nudges within 1 s merge into one undo entry "Nudge". Nudging is refused for pinned or non-movable elements with a status-bar message. - Coordinate entry syntax: x,y (absolute, project coordinates), @dx,dy (relative to the last point), <distance<angle (polar from the last point, angle in degrees counter-clockwise from the view's X axis). Values accept unit suffixes as in the Properties palette. Invalid input is kept in the field and marked, with an explanation. - Dialogs. Every dialog has a default button (Enter) and a cancel button (Esc), visible mnemonics on labelled controls, and opens with focus on the first editable field. - No timing traps. No interaction requires a key to be pressed within a fixed time except sequence shortcuts, whose timeout is configurable (§1.26.1).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A test user can create, dimension and tag a wall without a mouse. - [ ] Every dialog in the shell passes an automated tab-order check (no traps, logical order). - [ ] Typing @3000,0 after the first wall point places the end point 3 000 mm along X. - [ ] Three arrow nudges within one second produce one undo entry.

    1.33.2 Visual accessibility

    ID: UI-A11Y-002 · Priority: P1

    Behaviour & rules. - UI text and essential icons meet a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 (text) and 3:1 (icons, focus rings, selection outlines against both canvas schemes) in the standard themes; the high-contrast themes meet 7:1 for text. - State is never conveyed by colour alone: mode borders carry labels; toggles have pressed shapes; status uses icons plus text; selection is drawn with thicker lines as well as colour. - A colour-vision-deficiency-safe canvas palette (preference) changes selection, pre-selection, alert and comparison colours to a palette distinguishable under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia. - UI font scaling 90–200 % without clipping; the ribbon re-lays out. - Reduce motion disables animated transitions (Orientation Cube, view changes, toasts). - Larger grips and hit targets preference (minimum 12 logical pixels).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Automated contrast checks on all theme files pass the thresholds above. - [ ] At 200 % UI font scale every ribbon label is readable or available in a tooltip, and no dialog clips text.

    1.33.3 HiDPI and multiple scale factors

    ID: UI-DPI-001 · Priority: P0

    Behaviour & rules. - All sizes are specified in logical (device-independent) pixels and converted with FromDIP/ToDIP; all icons are SVG via wxBitmapBundle (no raster-only icons). - Windows: per-monitor DPI awareness v2 in the manifest; handle wxEVT_DPI_CHANGED in every top-level frame and dialog. macOS: native backing scale. Linux: GTK scale factor and fractional scaling where the compositor supports it. - The canvas renders at native device resolution; line weights, text heights and grip sizes are scaled correctly so that printed-scale line weights look consistent across monitors; overlay hit-testing uses device pixels. - Moving a window between monitors with different scale factors updates layout, icons and canvas resolution without restart or blurring. - Supported scale range: 100 %–300 %.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] At 150 % and 200 % scale on Windows, Linux (Wayland and X11) and macOS, no icon is blurry and no control is clipped. - [ ] Dragging a floating view from a 100 % monitor to a 200 % monitor re-renders it sharply within one second.

    1.33.4 Assistive technology

    ID: UI-A11Y-003 · Priority: P1

    Behaviour & rules. - Native wx controls expose accessibility through the platform (UI Automation/MSAA on Windows, AT-SPI on Linux, NSAccessibility on macOS). Custom-drawn controls (ribbon, QAT strip, status bar toggles, View Control Bar, Type Selector list, keytips) implement accessible names, roles, states and descriptions (from the command descriptor's label and tooltip) through wxAccessible on Windows and equivalent bridge code on the other platforms. - The canvas exposes an accessible summary: active view name and kind, selection summary ("3 walls selected, 1 door"), active tool and prompt, and mode labels. Changes are announced through a live region at the verbosity chosen in Options. - The Properties palette is fully navigable by screen reader (group, name, value, read-only reason). - Agent pane transcripts and notifications are accessible text. - Verbosity levels (Options › Accessibility): Off (no canvas announcements; controls still have names), Brief (selection count and category, mode changes), Normal (default; adds tool prompts and the hovered or cycled element), Detailed (adds snap names and temporary-dimension values while drawing). Announcements of the same kind are throttled to one per second; the newest replaces a pending one. - Roles. Ribbon tabs are announced as tabs, panels as groups, split buttons as split buttons with their current member, toggles with pressed state, galleries as lists with the selected item. The Project Browser and System Browser are trees with level and expanded state. Toasts are announced politely without moving focus; error dialogs are announced assertively. - Canvas as a single object. The canvas is one accessible object with role "drawing", whose name is the view name and whose description is the accessible summary; individual elements are not exposed as accessible objects (the selection summary and the Properties palette carry their information). - Testing. Each platform build runs an automated accessibility tree dump of the main window and compares it with a stored reference, so missing names or roles fail the build. - The accessible summary is also available to scripts and tests.

    Commands. ui.a11y.summary() -> {view, selection, tool, prompt, modes[]} returns the same text the canvas exposes.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With a screen reader running, tabbing through the Modify tab announces each tool's name and shortcut. - [ ] Selecting elements announces the new selection summary. - [ ] With verbosity Off, selecting elements produces no announcement while ribbon controls are still named. - [ ] The accessibility tree dump shows no unnamed interactive control in the main window.

    1.33.5 Localisation

    ID: UI-L10N-001 · Priority: P1

    Behaviour & rules. - All user-visible strings are externalised (gettext catalogues via wxWidgets' translation support); command ids, Lua names and MCP tool names are never localised. - Number, unit and date formatting follow the model's unit settings (for values) and the UI locale (for dates in Home, revisions and notifications). - Right-to-left layouts are not required for v1.0 (noted in §1.35). - Keytips are regenerated per language; default key sequences are language-independent. - Language choice. Options › General › Language offers Follow system (default) and each installed catalogue; the key is general.language (a BCP 47 tag such as de-DE). A change takes effect after restart and is marked "requires restart" (UI-PREF-001). - Fallback. A missing translation falls back to British English per string, never to the command id; the build reports catalogue coverage, and a language with less than 80 % coverage is listed as "partial". - What is translated. Labels, tooltips, dialogs, messages, help index titles, built-in layout and scenario names (stored by id, so renaming in another language does not create a new layout). Not translated: command ids, setting keys, Lua and MCP names, IFC class names and property set names, file names, and user content (view names, parameter names defined in the model). - Model-level text. Category and built-in parameter display names in the UI follow the UI language; values written into IFC follow the IFC rules of Ch. 2, independently of the UI language. - Layout robustness. Dialogs use sizers so text up to 40 % longer than English fits without clipping; the ribbon uses the reduction rules of UI-RIB-002 for longer labels. - Search. Command Search matches both the localised label and the English label, so users can follow English tutorials. - Sources. Catalogues live in the source tree as .po files under the same licence; contributed translations follow the project's contribution rules.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Switching the UI language changes ribbon labels and tooltips after restart while all shortcuts and scripts keep working. - [ ] In a German UI, typing "Wall" in Command Search finds the wall tool. - [ ] A string missing from a catalogue is shown in English, not as an id.

    1.33.9 Crash recovery and live-store status

    ID: UI-RECOV-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: spec/02b_live_model_store.md §6.2 (owner directive, 2026-10-12)

    Purpose. This is the user interface for the live SQLite store (Chapter 2b). After a crash it offers to recover unsaved work. While the user works, it shows that their work is being kept safe.

    Workflow. 1. At startup, if recovery.list returns any project, the Recover unsaved work dialog opens before the Home screen. It shows one row per project: name or "Untitled", path, time of the last change, number of unsaved changes, and the last three undo labels. 2. Each row has Restore (the default button), Restore as copy…, Show changes, Discard and Decide later. Discard asks for confirmation inside the dialog itself. 3. A restored project opens with "(recovered)" in its title and is marked as unsaved. A notice bar in the view area says: "Recovered N changes from <time>. Save to keep them." It has Save and Show changes buttons.

    UI. - Status bar indicator. A small disk glyph shows the store's state: - Up to date: everything committed is on disk. - Writing…: change sets are pending, shown for more than 0.5 s only. - Recovery data unavailable: a write failed or the disk is full. Shown in red, and clicking it opens details and a Retry button. - Tooltip. Shows the time of the last durable commit and the store's location. - Settings. Options › General › Recovery has fields for durability mode (Normal/Full), group-commit window, store location, retention and disk quota (DM-LIVE-014). - Auto-save reminders. The existing save reminder (§1.29) remains, because the live store doesn't replace saving the IFC file. - Encryption. The indicator's tooltip shows "Recovery data encrypted" or "Recovery data not encrypted". Options › General › Recovery has the encryption switch and a Set recovery passphrase… button (DM-LIVE-016). - Resuming a sketch. For a recovered sketch or tool session, the notice bar shows Resume sketch and Discard sketch (DM-LIVE-015). - History panel. A dockable panel (View › Windows › History, Ctrl+Shift+H) with a timeline, origin filters, historical views and restore and revert actions, as specified in Chapter 2b §8.5 (DM-LIVE-017).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] After the process is killed, the next start shows the dialog listing the project. Restore reopens the project with the "(recovered)" title and the notice bar. - [ ] Filling the disk turns the indicator red within 2 s, and editing continues. - [ ] Screen readers announce the indicator's state changes, but no more than once every 10 s.

    1.35 Open questions / deviations from reference

    1.35.1 Intentional deviations

    # Reference behaviour Reviera behaviour Reason
    D1 Options Bar row below the ribbon (removed in the reference's 2027 release) No Options Bar; tool options rendered as contextual ribbon panels and a Properties "Tool Options" group from one descriptor; optional strip rendering (P2) Matches the reference's 2027 direction while keeping one data model; addresses users who prefer a strip
    D2 QAT embedded in a custom-drawn title bar QAT in a slim strip above the ribbon; native window decorations kept Cross-platform correctness (Wayland, macOS) and accessibility of native title bars
    D3 Title-bar online-help search box, vendor sign-in and app store Command Search (commands, views, files, offline help, settings); local user name or server login; no store Offline-first, no vendor accounts, faster command discovery
    D4 Vendor cloud items (cloud models, cloud rendering, cloud parameters, shared views, insights page, cloud documents on Home) Not provided (P3). Open alternatives: BIMserver mode, local rendering, shared parameters files, BCF Vendor-cloud features are out of scope (Ch. 0)
    D5 Proprietary AI assistant palette Built-in Agent pane: MCP client to Reviera's own MCP server, user-chosen model provider (local or hosted), explicit approvals, per-turn undo Open, vendor-neutral alternative; same command surface as every other client
    D6 Separate Precast tab plus reinforcement on Structure (later gathered on a Concrete Detailing tab) One Concrete tab from the start Follows the reference's newest grouping; avoids duplicated tools
    D7 Worksharing central/local files, sync with central BIMserver connect / check in / get latest / sync; Collaboration Display instead of worksharing display Collaboration model is BIMserver (TECH_STACK §3.7)
    D8 Some default key sequences bound to two commands Default map has no global-scope conflicts (RC, RG, PC, SZ resolved; SE, ME, ST kept for snaps/MEP) Predictable behaviour; users can still create duplicates
    D9 Shortcuts stored in a vendor XML file; UI state in a binary file Human-readable TOML stores, independently resettable; no import of the reference's shortcut file format is specified Clean-room rule (no reproduction of vendor files); transparency
    D10 Single-key-sequence execution only on final key Explicit prefix rule with configurable timeout Needed once users define overlapping sequences
    D11 Dark theme leaves some dialogs light (fixed late in the reference) Every dialog follows the UI theme from the first release; high-contrast themes shipped Consistency and accessibility
    D12 Selection-colour and view-mode states signalled mainly by colour Mode borders always carry text labels; colour-vision-safe palette option Accessibility (§1.33.2)
    D13 Macros and visual programming panels Scripting panel (Script Manager, Lua Console, Script Security, Add-in Manager); node-based programming deferred (P3) Lua is the scripting platform (TECH_STACK §3.5)
    D14 Project-scoped UI data inside the proprietary model file Stored as Reviera Extension Data (embedded in the IFC by default, optional sidecar); presentational state kept per user in BIMserver mode IFC is the source of truth; avoid users overwriting each other's layouts
    D15 Ctrl+A unused in the canvas Ctrl+A selects all visible elements in the active view Common platform expectation
    D16 No coordinate entry Optional typed coordinate entry for picks (P1) Keyboard accessibility

    1.35.2 Open questions

    # Question Proposed handling
    Q1 ~~Rust↔wxWidgets binding~~ Resolved (owner, 2026-10-12): wxDragon, with any extensions kept as clean patches offered upstream (TECH_STACK §3.4). The UI bridge interface (§1.1.5) is kept.
    Q2 wxRibbonBar lacks native support for contextual-tab colouring beyond page highlight, slide-out pinning, panel floating and four minimise states Prototype with a custom art provider; fall back to a Reviera-owned ribbon widget if wxRibbonBar cannot be extended cleanly
    Q3 ~~Command ids for tools owned by Ch. 2–6 in §1.8~~ Resolved (2026-10-12): every ribbon and shortcut command id now matches the owning chapter's catalog; tools/build_spec.py checks this.
    Q4 ~~Owner of phasing and design-option commands~~ Resolved: phase.* belongs to Ch. 2 (DM), designoption.* to Ch. 5 (DOC, §5.11), and element.demolish to Ch. 3 (ARC-MOD-024).
    Q5 ~~Clean IFC export and file.locate_rxd~~ Resolved: both are defined in Ch. 2a (§4, §13); export.ifc has one aligned signature across chapters (Appendix A.2).
    Q6 ~~Whether navigation marks the model modified~~ Resolved: no. Navigation is view state, saved with the next save; explicit view.set_camera is an undoable edit (§1.19.1, UI-NAV-001).
    Q7 Push notifications depend on the BIMserver notification interface being reachable through proxies Polling fallback specified; the target server is the latest stable BIMserver, currently 1.5.188 (TECH_STACK §5, decision 7)
    Q8 Right-to-left UI support Not required for v1.0; revisit for P2 Deferred to the post-Alpha/POC review (owner, 2026-10-12).
    Q9 Agent pane provider connectors: which chat APIs ship in-tree, and their licences (must be GPL-3.0-compatible) Decide with the dependency allow-list (TECH_STACK §4.2) Deferred to the post-Alpha/POC review (owner, 2026-10-12).
    Q10 Whether to offer a one-time importer for users' own shortcut exports from other applications Excluded from this specification pending a clean-room review Deferred to the post-Alpha/POC review (owner, 2026-10-12).
    • Deviation: bookmarked layouts (owner directive, 2026-10-12). The reference keeps one UI state per user. Reviera adds named, partial, display-aware layout bookmarks; built-in, organisation and personal layouts; context-based auto-switching; portable preference profiles; and recommended project layouts (§1.29.4, UI-LAYOUT-001…006).
    • Deviation: workflow scenarios and view bookmarks (owner directive, 2026-10-12). Reviera treats the workspace as a high-level, user-owned customisation of how each person works. Scenarios bundle a layout with preference, shortcut and view-bookmark overlays for each work process, and switch on demand or by context (§1.29.5, UI-SCEN-001…004). The reference has no equivalent beyond one global set of options.
