    2CHChapter 2: Data Model, Families, Parameters, Project Setup, File I/O and Extensibility

    Area code: DM · Status: Draft 1 (2026-10-12) · Primary source: research/05_data_model_platform.md · Architecture source: TECH_STACK.md · Extension data carrier: spec/02a_extension_data_format.md

    This chapter is the backbone of the Reviera specification. It defines what a Reviera model is, how it is stored, how it changes, how users and programs extend it, and how it moves in and out of the application. Other chapters (ARC, STR, MEP, ANA, DOC, COL) define particular element kinds and tools. They build on the element model, parameter system, transaction model, storage split and command registry defined here. Where this chapter and a domain chapter disagree about storage or identity, this chapter wins. Where this chapter and 02a_extension_data_format.md disagree about how extension data is physically carried, 02a wins.

    Storage design (owner decision, 2026-10-12; compatibility first). A Reviera project is a single valid IFC file (.ifc or .ifczip). 1. Standard IFC holds everything IFC can express: spatial structure, elements, types, geometry, materials and layer sets, standard Pset_*/Qto_*, the values of user parameters (as property sets that other tools can read), classifications, grids, openings and voids. 2. Reviera Extension Data (RXD) holds everything IFC cannot express: constraints, sketches, family parametric definitions, parameter definition metadata, views, sheets, schedules, view-specific annotation, phases, design options, worksets, revisions, links, styles, patterns and settings. RXD has two forms: - RXD element data: data scoped to one IFC element (its recipe, sketch, constraints, hosting detail and memberships). By default it is carried in a Reviera_Element property set on that element. - RXD documents: project-scoped documents (for example views, sheets, annotation, styles, families/<guid>). By default they are carried in Reviera_Document_* property sets on IfcProject. 3. An external .reviera sidecar is an alternative carrier for the same RXD. It is useful for git, or when a downstream tool strips unknown property sets.

    How RXD is encoded, chunked, compressed, versioned and validated, and how the sidecar carrier works, is defined in spec/02a_extension_data_format.md. This chapter defines what RXD holds, which element or document it belongs to, and how it refers to IFC. Document and key names used here are proposals for 02a; if 02a renames one, 02a wins.

    2.0 Reading guide

    2.0.1 Scope

    In scope Defined elsewhere
    Element model (category, family, type, instance) and its IFC4 mapping Behaviour of particular elements, such as walls or ducts (ARC, STR, MEP)
    The split between standard IFC and RXD, and the RXD contents for this chapter's data How RXD is carried, encoded and validated, and the sidecar carrier (02a)
    Identity, hosting, dependency graph, regeneration, transactions, failures View graphics, annotation behaviour, schedules and sheets (DOC). This chapter only states where they are stored.
    Family editor, family file format, the conceptual massing environment Worksharing, sync and BIMserver protocol details (COL)
    Parameters, formulas, units, the shared parameter library Ribbon layout and palette behaviour in general (UI)
    Project setup (Manage features), materials Analysis engines (ANA)
    File I/O, schema policy, import/export, migration
    Command registry, Lua API, add-ins, visual programming, MCP server

    2.0.2 Notation

    • Requirement keywords. "Shall" is mandatory. "Should" is recommended. "May" is optional.
    • Lua examples use the API surface defined in §2.13. JSON examples are informative; the normative JSON Schemas are published with 02a.
    • IFC entity names follow IFC4 ADD2 TC1. Where IFC4X3 differs (for example IfcBuildingElementType became IfcBuiltElementType), the difference is noted.
    • "RXD document x" means the data is stored in that RXD document. By default it is embedded in the IFC file as a Reviera_Doc:<path> property set; the external .reviera container is the alternative carrier (see 02a). Document names given here are proposals for 02a; if 02a renames a document, 02a wins.
    • Grammar is written in EBNF (ISO/IEC 14977 style, with |, [ ], { }).
    • Internal units are SI (§2.9). Any number in this chapter without a unit is in internal units.

    2.0.3 Glossary

    Term Meaning in Reviera
    Element Anything with identity in the model: physical objects, datums, annotation, views, sheets, types, settings. An element is an IFC entity, an RXD-only record, or an IFC entity with RXD element data.
    Category A fixed classification defined by the application. It sets default graphics, behaviour flags and the IFC entity class.
    Family A named definition that shares parameters, geometry logic and representation across a set of types.
    Type A named set of type-parameter values inside a family. It is stored as an IfcTypeObject subtype.
    Instance A placed occurrence of a type. It is stored as an IFC occurrence entity (IfcWall, IfcDoor, …).
    IFC-backed element An element whose primary record is an IfcRoot entity in the .ifc file (it may also have RXD element data).
    RXD-only element An element that has no IFC entity (views, sheets, annotation, phases, …). It exists only as a record in an RXD document. It still has a GUID in the same 22-character IFC format.
    RXD Reviera Extension Data: the data IFC cannot express, as RXD element data (on one IFC element) and RXD documents (project-scoped). Carriers are defined in spec/02a_extension_data_format.md (§2.4).
    Command A typed, registered operation. It is the only way to change the model (§2.12).
    Regeneration Recomputing derived values and geometry after a change, in dependency order (§2.6).
    Family package A family stored on disk as an .ifc type library carrying the family's RXD (§2.8.14).

    2.1 Architectural principles

    Model-wide principles

    ID: DM-CORE-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §1, §16.1, §16.9; TECH_STACK §1, §3.1, §3.7

    Purpose. These rules shape every other requirement in this chapter.

    Behaviour & rules. 1. IFC is the model of record for everything it can express. The in-memory building model is an IFC instance population, managed through IfcOpenShell. Reviera has no proprietary project format. RXD holds only what IFC cannot express. 2. One database per project. In memory, IFC entities and RXD records form one element store with one transaction system. Every view, schedule and sheet is a live query of it. A change made anywhere appears everywhere on the next regeneration. 3. Everything with identity is an element. Every element has an internal ID and a durable GUID (§2.5). IFC-backed elements use their GlobalId. RXD-only elements get a GUID in the same format. 4. IFC first. Data is stored in a standard IFC entity, attribute, relationship or buildingSMART property set (Pset_*, Qto_*) whenever one has the right meaning. Data goes to RXD only when IFC has no suitable construct (the split is in §2.4.2). 5. The building stands without RXD. The file shall be valid for its declared schema. A tool that ignores or strips every Reviera_* property set shall still see correct geometry, spatial structure, types, materials, standard properties and user parameter values. Losing RXD loses intent (constraints, views, annotation), not the building. 6. References by GUID only. RXD refers to IFC entities by GlobalId, never by STEP instance number (#123). 7. Integrity checks. 02a defines how Reviera detects RXD that is missing, stale or belongs to another project (for example, after a downstream tool rewrote the file). This chapter defines the user-facing reconciliation (§2.4.3). 8. Lossless pass-through. IFC entities, properties and relationships that Reviera does not understand are kept and written back unchanged, with the same GlobalId and values, unless the user edits or deletes their owner. Unknown RXD documents and unknown keys are also kept (02a). 9. Commands only. Every change goes through a registered command inside a transaction (§2.7, §2.12). The UI, Lua, add-ins and MCP have no other write path. 10. SI internal units. All stored quantities use SI base or derived units (metre, radian, kilogram, second, kelvin, …). Display units are a formatting layer (§2.9.5). 11. Deterministic results. For the same model and the same command sequence, regeneration gives the same geometry and values, whatever the number of threads (§2.6.4). 12. Mode independence. Everything in this chapter behaves the same in Local mode and BIMserver mode. Only open, save, sync and history differ. Because RXD is embedded in IFC by default, it travels with each BIMserver revision as ordinary properties (COL chapter; 02a).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A model saved by Reviera passes IfcOpenShell schema validation and the buildingSMART validation service's schema and normative rule checks for IFC4 ADD2 TC1. - [ ] Opening a third-party IFC4 file, then saving it without edits, keeps every entity's GlobalId, every property value and every relationship. A semantic diff with IfcOpenShell's diff tooling reports no differences except the header, IfcOwnerHistory/application entries and added Reviera_* property sets. - [ ] Stripping every Reviera_* property set from a saved project and opening it gives a model with all elements, types, materials and parameter values, plus a notice that views, annotation and constraints were not found. - [ ] No code path outside the command layer can mutate the element store. This is enforced by Rust visibility (the store's mutating API is crate-private to the transaction module).

    2.2 Element model

    2.2.1 Elements

    ID: DM-ELEM-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §1.1, §1.3, §16.1

    Purpose. To define the common shape of every stored object.

    Behaviour & rules. - Every element shall expose these common attributes, where they apply:

    Attribute Meaning Storage
    id Internal 64-bit ID (§2.5) RXD element data (identity)
    guid Durable GUID IfcRoot.GlobalId; for RXD-only elements, the record's guid
    category Category key (for example cat.walls) IFC class + PredefinedType (+ ObjectType); RXD element data (elements) only when not derivable
    subcategory For geometry parts IFC presentation layer assignment (§2.10.3)
    name Element or type name IfcRoot.Name
    description Free text IfcRoot.Description
    type_id Its type, for instances IfcRelDefinesByType
    level_id Reference level Spatial containment; RXD element data (elements) when the level is a non-storey level (§2.3.5)
    host_id Host element, for hosted instances IfcRelFillsElement / IfcRelVoidsElement / IfcRelConnectsElements; RXD element data (hosting) for the host reference detail
    owner_view_id Owning view, for view-specific elements RXD document views/annotation/<viewId>
    phase_created / phase_demolished Phasing RXD element data (phasing); derived Pset_*Common.Status in IFC (§2.3.11)
    design_option_id Design option membership RXD element data (membership)
    workset_id Workset membership RXD element data (membership) (COL)
    group_id Model/detail group membership IfcRelAssignsToGroup (model groups); RXD document model/groups
    location Point, curve or placement IfcObjectPlacement + Axis representation
    parameters All parameter values IFC attributes, Psets, Qtos (§2.9)
    geometry Evaluated geometry IfcProductDefinitionShape
    • Elements shall be grouped into these roles. The role controls where an element can appear and how it behaves on regeneration:
    • Model elements (IFC-backed). These are hosts (walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, toposolids, foundations, stairs) and components (doors, windows, furniture, columns, beams, equipment, and so on). Walls hosted on walls are allowed as hosts (ARC chapter).
    • Datum elements. Storey levels and grids are IFC-backed. Non-storey levels, reference planes and scope boxes are RXD-only (RXD document model/datums). In families, reference lines and points are in the family definition.
    • View-specific elements (RXD-only, RXD document views/annotation/<viewId>). Annotation (dimensions, tags, text, symbols, spot elevations, keynotes, revision clouds) and details (detail lines, filled and masking regions, detail components, repeating details, detail groups). Each has exactly one owner view.
    • Views and sheets (RXD-only). Every view kind, plus sheets, viewports and schedules (DOC chapter).
    • Type and family elements. Types are IFC-backed. A family's parametric definition is an RXD document (§2.8.14).
    • Settings elements. Materials and classifications are IFC-backed. Project information is IFC-backed (IfcProject, IfcSite, IfcBuilding, IfcPostalAddress). Units, phases, design options, worksets, line and fill patterns, line styles, object styles, filters, view templates, parameter definitions and bindings, and global parameters are RXD-only.
    • Elements shall be addressable by internal ID and by GUID through the same query API (§2.13.3), whatever file their primary record lives in.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Every element in a loaded model has a non-zero internal ID and a valid GUID. - [ ] A query category == cat.doors returns every door instance and no door types. A separate type query returns the door types. - [ ] Deleting a view deletes every element whose owner view is that view, in the same transaction.

    2.2.2 Categories and subcategories

    ID: DM-CATG-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §1.1, §9.2, §16.1

    Purpose. Categories give every element a fixed classification. That classification drives graphics, scheduling, tagging, filtering, behaviour flags and IFC export.

    Behaviour & rules. - Categories are defined by the application in a versioned category registry. Users cannot create categories. Add-ins may not add categories in v1. Instead they use cat.generic_models with an IFC ObjectType (see open question Q-DM-01). - Each category definition shall contain: - key (stable string, for example cat.walls), display name (localisable), discipline; - ifc_class, ifc_type_class and a default PredefinedType (RXD-only categories have ifc_class = none); - behaviour flags: is_model, is_annotation, is_cuttable, is_hostable_target (can be a host), requires_host, is_room_bounding_default, is_schedulable, is_taggable, is_tag_category (with target categories), allows_material, allows_subcategories; - default Object Style entries for projection and cut (line weight, colour, pattern, material) (§2.10.3); - built-in parameters and their IFC mapping (§2.9.2). - Subcategories are user- or family-defined children of a category, for example Doors › Frame/Mullion, Doors › Panel, Doors › Swing. They carry their own Object Style. Subcategories created in a family are added to the project when the family loads. Name clashes merge into the existing subcategory. - The category's internal numeric ID shall be negative and stable across releases. This keeps category IDs separate from element IDs (§2.5). - Subcategory definitions and their GUIDs are stored in RXD document standards/styles (§2.10.3). In IFC, geometry assigned to a subcategory is placed on an IfcPresentationLayerAssignment named <Category>|<Subcategory>, so other tools can toggle it.

    Category registry (normative baseline; domain chapters add rows).

    Category key IFC occurrence IFC type Default PredefinedType Notes
    cat.walls IfcWall IfcWallType STANDARD (layered), SOLIDWALL, PARTITIONING, SHEAR, ELEMENTEDWALL (curtain), PARAPET IfcWallStandardCase is never written for IFC4 (it is deprecated).
    cat.curtain_walls IfcCurtainWall IfcCurtainWallType USERDEFINED Aggregates panels and mullions (§2.3.9)
    cat.curtain_panels IfcPlate IfcPlateType CURTAIN_PANEL A door in a curtain panel is an IfcDoor aggregated by the curtain wall.
    cat.curtain_mullions IfcMember IfcMemberType MULLION
    cat.floors IfcSlab IfcSlabType FLOOR, BASESLAB, LANDING
    cat.roofs IfcRoof (aggregate) + IfcSlab ROOF parts IfcRoofType FLAT_ROOF, SHED_ROOF, GABLE_ROOF, HIP_ROOF, FREEFORM, … A single-face roof may be written as an IfcSlab ROOF (open question Q-DM-02).
    cat.ceilings IfcCovering IfcCoveringType CEILING
    cat.doors IfcDoor IfcDoorType DOOR, GATE, TRAPDOOR OperationType on the type
    cat.windows IfcWindow IfcWindowType WINDOW, SKYLIGHT, LIGHTDOME PartitioningType on the type
    cat.stairs IfcStair (aggregate) IfcStairType from shape, for example STRAIGHT_RUN_STAIR Runs IfcStairFlight, landings IfcSlab LANDING
    cat.railings IfcRailing IfcRailingType HANDRAIL, GUARDRAIL, BALUSTRADE
    cat.ramps IfcRamp IfcRampType STRAIGHT_RUN_RAMP, …
    cat.columns (architectural) IfcColumn IfcColumnType COLUMN + Pset_ColumnCommon.LoadBearing=false
    cat.structural_columns IfcColumn IfcColumnType COLUMN + LoadBearing=true STR chapter
    cat.structural_framing IfcBeam / IfcMember IfcBeamType / IfcMemberType BEAM, JOIST, BRACE STR chapter
    cat.structural_foundations IfcFooting / IfcPile IfcFootingType / IfcPileType PAD_FOOTING, STRIP_FOOTING, …
    cat.furniture IfcFurniture IfcFurnitureType USERDEFINED IFC4: IfcFurnishingElement subtype
    cat.casework IfcFurniture IfcFurnitureType USERDEFINED (ObjectType Casework)
    cat.plumbing_fixtures IfcSanitaryTerminal IfcSanitaryTerminalType WASHHANDBASIN, TOILETPAN, …
    cat.generic_models IfcBuildingElementProxy IfcBuildingElementProxyType USERDEFINED IFC4X3: IfcBuiltElement may be used
    cat.specialty_equipment IfcBuildingElementProxy IfcBuildingElementProxyType USERDEFINED (ObjectType SpecialtyEquipment)
    cat.mass IfcBuildingElementProxy IfcBuildingElementProxyType USERDEFINED (ObjectType Mass) Not exported to exchange MVDs by default (§2.11.4)
    cat.rooms IfcSpace IfcSpaceType INTERNAL, EXTERNAL Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities
    cat.areas IfcSpace — USERDEFINED (ObjectType Area:<scheme>) IfcZone for area groupings
    cat.levels IfcBuildingStorey (storey levels) — — Non-storey levels: RXD document model/datums (§2.3.5)
    cat.grids IfcGrid (axes are IfcGridAxis) — — §2.3.6
    cat.reference_planes, cat.scope_boxes — — — RXD document model/datums
    cat.openings IfcOpeningElement — OPENING, RECESS
    cat.toposolid IfcGeographicElement (IFC4) IfcGeographicElementType TERRAIN IFC4X3 may use IfcEarthworksFill / IfcGeotechnicalStratum
    cat.ducts, cat.pipes, … IfcDuctSegment, IfcPipeSegment, … matching types per MEP chapter MEP chapter
    cat.parts IfcBuildingElementPart IfcBuildingElementPartType INSULATION, PRECASTPANEL, USERDEFINED
    cat.assemblies IfcElementAssembly IfcElementAssemblyType USERDEFINED
    Annotation categories (cat.dimensions, cat.text_notes, cat.*_tags, cat.generic_annotations, cat.detail_items, cat.filled_regions, cat.revision_clouds, …) — — — RXD document views/annotation/<viewId> (optional IfcAnnotation on export, §2.11.4)
    cat.views, cat.sheets, cat.schedules, cat.viewports — — — RXD documents views/<viewId>, sheets, schedules

    Data (storage). The category registry itself is application data, not model data. For IFC-backed elements the category is derived from the IFC class, PredefinedType and ObjectType, using the table above. When that is ambiguous (for example furniture vs casework), the category key is in RXD element data (elements). If there is no RXD entry, the category is inferred from the IFC class.

    Commands. subcategory.create(parent_category, name) -> element_id · subcategory.rename(subcategory_id, name) · subcategory.delete(subcategory_id, reassign_to?)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Each IFC-backed row of the registry round-trips: create an element of the category, save, reopen. It comes back with the same category, and an IFC viewer shows the IFC class listed in the table. - [ ] Importing a third-party IfcDoor with no RXD assigns cat.doors. - [ ] Deleting a subcategory that geometry uses either reassigns that geometry to the parent category or to the named subcategory. Undo restores both the subcategory and the assignments.

    2.2.3 Families: system, loadable and in-place

    ID: DM-FAM-001 · Priority: P0 (system, loadable placement) / P1 (in-place, family editing) · Ref: research/05 §1.2, §4.9, §16.2

    Purpose. To define the three family kinds and where their definitions live.

    Behaviour & rules.

    Kind Definition lives in Created by Editable with Portability
    System family The application (geometry logic in Rust). Its types live in the project. Built in. Types are created with Duplicate in Type Properties. Specialised editors (for example the wall layer editor in ARC) Types move between projects only through Transfer Project Standards (§2.10.9) or copy/paste
    Loadable family A family package (§2.8.14). A full copy is embedded in each project that uses it. The Reviera Family Editor The Family Editor (opened from a package, or from the project with Edit Family) Saved and loaded as family packages
    In-place family The project only. It is single-use. Model In-Place inside a project The Family Editor tools, in an in-place session Not reusable. Copying makes an independent copy.
    • A loadable family embedded in a project shall carry its full definition (parameters, formulas, forms, constraints, nested families, lookup tables), not only the evaluated geometry. This lets the family be edited from the project and saved back out as a package.
    • Loading a family that already exists (same family GUID, §2.5) shall offer Keep project values or Overwrite parameter values from the family. In both cases, instance placements are kept. Types that were removed from the family file stay in the project until purged.
    • Loading a family with the same name but a different family GUID shall prompt the user to rename the incoming family or replace the existing one. Replacing remaps types by name and reports any instances whose types could not be remapped.
    • Nested shared families that are already in the project prompt Use project version / Use version from family (§2.8.10).

    Data (storage). - IFC: each loadable or in-place family is an IfcProjectLibrary (Name = family name) declared by the IfcProject through IfcRelDeclares. The family declares its types through a second IfcRelDeclares (§2.3.2). System families have no library object. Their types are declared directly by the IfcProject. - RXD document families/<id> holds the parametric definition (§2.8.14). RXD document families/index lists every family with kind (system/loadable/in_place), system-family key (for example basic_wall, stacked_wall, curtain_wall), template, category, version and the GUIDs of its types.

    Commands. family.load(path, type_names?, overwrite_values=false) -> family_id · family.reload(family_id, path?, overwrite_values=false) · family.save_as(family_id, path) · family.edit(family_id) -> family_document_id · family.rename(family_id, name) · family.delete(family_id) · family.create_in_place(category, name) -> family_document_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Load a door family, place three instances, edit the family from the project to change frame depth, and reload it. All three instances update and keep their positions and hosts. - [ ] Save As on an embedded family produces a family package that loads into a second, empty project with the same types and parameter values. - [ ] Loading with Keep project values leaves type-parameter values that were changed in the project unchanged. Overwrite resets them to the file's values.

    2.2.4 Types

    ID: DM-TYPE-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §1.1, §7.6; screenshots/platform/family_types_dialog_parameter_groups.png

    Purpose. A type is a named, reusable set of type-parameter values.

    Workflow. 1. Select an instance. In the Properties palette, choose Edit Type. 2. In Type Properties, choose Duplicate, enter a name and edit the values. Choose Rename to rename the type. 3. Choose OK. All instances of the type regenerate.

    UI. Properties palette › type selector and Edit Type button. The Type Properties dialog has: Family drop-down, Type drop-down, Duplicate, Rename, a grouped parameter grid (Parameter | Value, with a formula indicator), Preview, and a link to the family's editor (for loadable families) or assembly editor (for system families).

    Behaviour & rules. - Type names are unique within a family. Duplicating a type copies every type-parameter value, plus its material assignments and layer structure. - Editing a type parameter shall regenerate every instance of that type in a single transaction. - Changing the type of an instance (type swap) keeps every instance parameter that has the same definition (same GUID or same built-in key) in both types. It keeps named references that dimensions and constraints point to (§2.8.3). It reports dimensions or constraints that could not be kept as warnings. - A type can be deleted only when it has no instances, or after confirming that its instances will be deleted too. - Type Properties dialog (type.edit_properties(type_id?)). With no argument it opens on the type of the current selection; if the selection holds several types it opens on the first and the Type drop-down lists the others; with nothing selected it opens on the type chosen in the Properties palette type selector. It refuses with type.none_selected when there is no type in context. - The dialog edits a working copy. Values are checked as they are typed (data type, unit parsing §2.9.5, min/max, enum), and an invalid cell is outlined with the error in its tooltip. OK and Apply are disabled while any cell is invalid. - Apply commits all changed values as one transaction named "Edit Type: <type name>" (a sequence of type.set_param calls) and keeps the dialog open; OK applies and closes; Cancel discards uncommitted edits. - Duplicate asks for a name, proposes "<name> 2" (next free number), and refuses a name already used in the family. Rename follows the same rule. Both act immediately as their own transactions and switch the dialog to the result. - Formula-driven, reporting and read-only parameters are greyed. Parameters associated with a global parameter show the association and are read-only (§2.9.6). - Preview (toggle) shows a live thumbnail of the type in a plan, elevation or 3D view of the user's choice; it regenerates from the working copy so the effect of an unapplied value is visible. - The dialog reports how many instances use the type ("Used by 128 instances"), so the user knows the reach of an edit.

    Data (storage). IfcXxxType (§2.3.2). Type-parameter values live in property sets in IfcTypeObject.HasPropertySets. IfcTypeProduct.Tag holds the type mark. Duplicating creates a new type entity with a new GlobalId. Type data IFC cannot hold (for example wall core boundaries and wrapping) is in RXD element data (types), keyed by the type's GlobalId.

    Commands. type.duplicate(type_id, new_name) -> type_id · type.rename(type_id, name) -> () · type.delete(type_id, delete_instances=false) · type.set_param(type_id, param, value) -> () · type.edit_properties(type_id?) (opens the Type Properties dialog) · instance.change_type(element_ids[], type_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] In Type Properties, typing "abc" into a Length cell outlines it with a parse error and disables OK; correcting it re-enables OK, and OK changes the value of every instance in one undo item. - [ ] Duplicating a wall type and changing a layer's thickness in the copy does not affect walls of the original type. - [ ] Swapping a door between two types of the same family keeps its Mark, host and position, and keeps dimensions that point to the "Left" and "Right" named references. - [ ] The IFC export of a duplicated type shows two distinct IfcDoorType entities, each linked to its own instances through IfcRelDefinesByType.

    2.2.5 Instances

    ID: DM-INST-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §1.1, §2.2

    Purpose. An instance is one placed occurrence of a type, with its own location and instance-parameter values.

    Behaviour & rules. - Placement modes come from the family template (§2.8.1). They are: level-based (elevation is taken from a level plus an offset), work-plane-based, face-based, host-based (wall, floor, ceiling, roof), line-based, two-level-based, adaptive (N points), and view-specific (annotation and detail). - A parameter is either a type parameter or an instance parameter in a given family (§2.9.1). Instance parameters do not override type parameters. - Flip, mirror and rotation state are instance properties: facing_flipped, hand_flipped, mirrored, plus a rotation about the placement Z axis. - Every instance shall report computed, read-only parameters: area, volume, length and perimeter where they apply, host, level and room. These are refreshed by regeneration.

    Data (storage). IFC: the occurrence entity, with ObjectPlacement (an IfcLocalPlacement relative to the storey placement, or to the host for hosted elements) and Representation. The body is usually an IfcMappedItem of the type's RepresentationMap, whose transform includes any mirroring (§2.3.10). RXD element data (placement) keeps the flip flags and work-plane reference (02a §6.4); RXD element data (elements) keeps the level offset to a non-storey level and the room-calculation point. These cannot be recovered reliably from the transform.

    Commands. instance.place(type_id, placement, host_id?, level_id?, params?) -> element_id · instance.place_adaptive(type_id, points[], hosts?[]) -> element_id · instance.flip(element_id, axis: "facing"|"hand"|"work_plane") · instance.pick_new_host(element_id, host_id, face_ref?)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A level-based instance moved to another level keeps its absolute elevation if "keep elevation" is chosen, or keeps its offset if not. - [ ] Flipping a door's facing changes the exported geometry and the RXD flag. The opening and fill relationships stay intact.

    2.2.6 Groups, assemblies, parts and links (storage)

    ID: DM-ELEM-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §1.4, §7.6

    Purpose. To fix how compound elements are stored. Their tools are defined in ARC (groups, parts), DOC (assemblies, Ch 5 §5.16) and COL (links).

    Behaviour & rules. - Model and detail groups. A group type is an element that holds a template of member elements. Each group instance holds real member elements that are kept in step with the group type. Parameters bound with "values vary by group instance" may differ between instances. Parameters bound with "values aligned per group type" are forced equal (§2.9.3). - Assemblies. A named set of elements with a naming category. Assembly views are defined in DOC. - Parts. Elements derived from layers of layered hosts. They can be divided, merged and excluded. - Links. A link type references an external model (a file path or a BIMserver project/revision). A link instance places it with a transform. Linked elements are read-only.

    Data (storage).

    Concept IFC RXD
    Model group instance IfcGroup (ObjectType = group type name) + IfcRelAssignsToGroup (members), so other tools see the grouping RXD document model/groups: group types (member template), instance → type, per-instance variations
    Detail group — RXD document model/groups + members in RXD document views/annotation/<viewId>
    Assembly IfcElementAssembly + IfcRelAggregates (members) RXD document model/assemblies (naming category, assembly views)
    Parts IfcBuildingElementPart aggregated by the host through IfcRelAggregates RXD element data parts on the host (division sketches, exclusions)
    Link type / instance Optional IfcDocumentReference through IfcRelAssociatesDocument on IfcProject RXD document project/links (source URI, revision, transform, visibility)

    Commands. Defined in ARC, DOC and COL. This chapter reserves the command namespaces group.*, assembly.*, part.* and link.*.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A model with two instances of a group type round-trips. After reopening, editing one member in one instance and choosing "apply to group type" updates the other instance.

    2.3 IFC4 mapping

    2.3.1 Schema baseline and header

    ID: DM-IFC-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §11.1, §12.1; TECH_STACK §3.1, §3.7.3

    Behaviour & rules. - The default project schema is IFC4 ADD2 TC1 (FILE_SCHEMA(('IFC4'))). Projects may be created in, or converted to, IFC4X3_ADD2 in Local mode. In BIMserver mode this is allowed only when the server advertises a matching deserializer (COL chapter). - Reading is supported for IFC2X3 TC1, IFC4 and IFC4X3_ADD2. An IFC2X3 file is upgraded in memory to the project schema (§2.11.8). The user is told that saving writes the new schema, and that "Export IFC2X3" (§2.11.4) remains available. - The header written by Reviera shall contain: - FILE_DESCRIPTION(('ViewDefinition [DesignTransferView]'),'2;1'); - FILE_NAME with the application name Reviera, the version, the author and organisation from Project Information, and a UTC timestamp; - FILE_SCHEMA(('IFC4')) or FILE_SCHEMA(('IFC4X3_ADD2')). - IfcOwnerHistory is optional in IFC4. Reviera shall write it on IfcRoot entities only when the project setting "Write owner history" is on (default: off in Local mode, on in BIMserver mode). Change attribution is otherwise kept in RXD element data (identity) (§2.5). - IfcProject.RepresentationContexts shall contain a Model context (3D) with sub-contexts Body, Axis, Box, FootPrint, Clearance and Reference, and a Plan context (2D) with sub-contexts Annotation (PLAN_VIEW, SECTION_VIEW, ELEVATION_VIEW) and Body/Axis. TrueNorth and WorldCoordinateSystem follow §2.10.7. - IfcProject.UnitsInContext shall declare SI units for every measure Reviera writes. It shall use IfcSIUnit (METRE, SQUARE_METRE, CUBIC_METRE, RADIAN, …), even when display units are imperial. Display units are kept in RXD document project/settings (§2.9.5).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A new project file has exactly one IfcProject, one IfcUnitAssignment in SI, and the representation contexts listed above. - [ ] Converting a project from IFC4 to IFC4X3_ADD2 and back produces a model with the same element count, GUIDs and RXD content. Entity renames (for example IfcBuildingElementType → IfcBuiltElementType) are listed in the migration report.

    2.3.2 Types and occurrences

    ID: DM-IFC-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §1.1, §1.2; TECH_STACK §3.1

    Behaviour & rules. - Every Reviera type shall be an IfcTypeObject subtype matching its category (§2.2.2). Its Name is <FamilyName>:<TypeName>, the convention other tools use to split family and type. Its ElementType is <TypeName>. Its Tag holds the type mark. - PredefinedType shall be set from the category default, or from the family's IFC classification family parameter (§2.8.2). When it is USERDEFINED, the type's ElementType and the occurrence's ObjectType shall carry the user-defined value. - Every instance shall be linked to its type through exactly one IfcRelDefinesByType (RelatingType = type, RelatedObjects = all its instances). Reviera keeps one relationship per type and updates its RelatedObjects set, rather than creating one relationship per instance. - Shared geometry. A type's evaluated geometry for the default parameter state is written once as IfcTypeProduct.RepresentationMaps (an IfcRepresentationMap with Body, and also Axis, FootPrint or plan Annotation maps where they exist). An instance whose geometry equals the type's geometry under a rigid transform (plus mirroring) shall use an IfcMappedItem referencing that map. An instance with unique geometry (because of instance parameters, joins or cuts) shall have its own representation. - An occurrence's PredefinedType shall be NOTDEFINED, or equal to its type's value. Reviera writes NOTDEFINED on occurrences when the type is set, so the value is not duplicated. - Families have no IFC class. A loadable or in-place family is an IfcProjectLibrary declared by the IfcProject through IfcRelDeclares, and it declares its types (§2.2.3). This is valid IFC4 and lets other tools see which types belong together.

    Example (informative, STEP fragment).

    #100= IFCPROJECTLIBRARY('3vB2…',$,'Single-Flush Door',$,$,$,$,$,$);
#101= IFCRELDECLARES('0Lw9…',$,$,$,#1,(#100));             /* project declares the family */
#110= IFCDOORTYPE('1xH4…',$,'Single-Flush Door:0915 x 2134',$,$,(#120,#121),(#130),'D1','0915 x 2134',.DOOR.,.SINGLE_SWING_LEFT.,.F.,$);
#111= IFCRELDECLARES('2Qa8…',$,$,$,#100,(#110));           /* family declares its types   */
#140= IFCDOOR('0aZ1…',$,'Single-Flush Door:0915 x 2134:301245',$,$,#141,#142,'D-104',2.134,0.915,.NOTDEFINED.,$,$);
#150= IFCRELDEFINESBYTYPE('3pR7…',$,$,$,(#140,#160,#170),#110);

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] In a model with 500 instances of 3 door types, the file has 3 IfcRelDefinesByType relationships, and a viewer groups the doors by type. - [ ] Identical furniture instances share a single IfcRepresentationMap. The file size grows by less than 2 KB per extra identical instance. - [ ] An instance with a unique instance-parameter value (for example a different width) gets its own representation, and keeps its type relationship.

    2.3.3 Property sets and quantity sets

    ID: DM-IFC-003 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §7, §12.2; screenshots/platform/ifc_property_mapping_2027.png

    Purpose. Parameter values are stored as IFC properties, so other tools can read them. Parameter definitions (data type, group, formula, GUID, tooltip, binding) are RXD (document parameters, §2.9).

    Behaviour & rules. - Type parameters live in property sets attached to the type through IfcTypeObject.HasPropertySets. Instance parameters live in property sets attached to the occurrence through IfcRelDefinesByProperties. - When an occurrence has a property set with the same Name as one on its type, IFC treats the occurrence's property as the override. Reviera never writes the same property on both type and occurrence for one parameter, because a parameter is either type or instance (§2.9.1). When reading third-party files, Reviera follows IFC: the occurrence value wins, and the property is shown as an instance parameter. - Each parameter has exactly one IFC home (pset_name, property_name), taken from its definition (§2.9.2). The order of preference is: 1. a direct IFC attribute (for example Name, Description, Tag, OverallHeight); 2. a buildingSMART property set for the entity (Pset_WallCommon, …); 3. a buildingSMART quantity set (Qto_*BaseQuantities), for computed quantities; 4. the property set named in the parameter definition (project, shared and family parameters; §2.9.2); 5. for built-in parameters with no standard home, a property set named after the parameter's group (for example Identity Data, Constraints, Other), with the property named after the parameter (see Q-DM-03). - Quantity sets are written as IfcElementQuantity with MethodOfMeasurement = 'BaseQuantities' from regenerated geometry on each save. They are read-only in Reviera. If a user edits a quantity in a third-party file, the edit is kept as an "imported quantity" until the element is regenerated. - Property values shall use the IFC measure type of the parameter's data type (§2.9.4). Enumerations shall use IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue with a shared IfcPropertyEnumeration. Element references (material, family type, element) shall use IfcPropertyReferenceValue. - A property set with no values is not written. A bound parameter with no value is written as a property with a null NominalValue, so schedules in other tools can see the field.

    2.3.4 Spatial structure

    ID: DM-IFC-004 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §1.3, §9.1, §9.8

    Behaviour & rules. - Each project shall have this decomposition, using IfcRelAggregates: IfcProject → one or more IfcSite → one or more IfcBuilding → zero or more IfcBuildingStorey. A new project contains one site ("Default Site"), one building ("Building 1") and two storeys ("Level 1", "Level 2"). - Every model element that has a reference level shall be in exactly one IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure, whose RelatingStructure is the storey for that level (§2.3.5). Elements without a level are contained in the building or, for site elements, in the site. - Elements that are parts of another element (curtain panels, stair flights, roof slabs, assembly members, shared nested components) shall not be contained in a spatial structure directly. They are reached through IfcRelAggregates from the parent, as IFC requires. - Rooms (IfcSpace) shall be aggregated by their storey through IfcRelAggregates, not contained. - Elements that span several storeys (for example a multi-storey column or a curtain wall) are contained in their base storey. The other storeys are listed through IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure. - Reviera may support several buildings on one site. level.create takes an optional building.

    Commands. site.create(name) -> element_id · building.create(site_id, name) -> element_id · spatial.reassign(element_ids[], container_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Validation finds no element contained in more than one spatial structure, and no aggregated part that is also contained. - [ ] A two-storey column is contained in Level 1 and referenced in Level 2.

    2.3.5 Levels

    ID: DM-IFC-005 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §1.3, §2.2; TECH_STACK §3.1

    Behaviour & rules. - A level marked Building Storey (default on) shall be an IfcBuildingStorey, aggregated by its building. Its Elevation attribute and its placement Z shall both equal the level elevation relative to the building's zero. - A level marked as not a storey (for example "Top of Parapet") has no IFC construct with the right meaning. It is a RXD-only datum in RXD document model/datums. Elements whose reference level is a non-storey level are contained in the nearest storey below it. Their reference level and offset are kept in RXD element data (elements), so offsets keep their meaning. - Toggling the storey flag converts between the two forms in a single transaction. The GUID is preserved (the RXD record takes over the storey's GlobalId, and vice versa). Spatial containment is reassigned. - Level data that IFC cannot hold (elevation base Project/Survey, structural flag, computation height, level head type, 2D/3D extents per view) is in RXD document model/datums.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing a level's elevation moves every element whose base is constrained to that level, in the same transaction, and updates IfcBuildingStorey.Elevation. - [ ] A non-storey level is not listed as a storey by a third-party viewer. Elements referencing it appear in the storey below.

    2.3.6 Grids

    ID: DM-IFC-006 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §1.3; TECH_STACK §3.1

    Behaviour & rules. - Reviera treats each grid line as its own element (selectable, with its own name, type and extents). IFC groups axes into an IfcGrid. The mapping is: - each grid system (default: one per building, or one per user-defined grid group) is one IfcGrid, contained in the lowest storey, or in the building; - each Reviera grid line is one IfcGridAxis in UAxes, VAxes or WAxes. Reviera assigns U to lines within ±45° of project X, V to the rest, and W to arcs and multi-segment grids; - IfcGridAxis.AxisTag is the grid name, and AxisCurve is the 2D curve. Multi-segment grids use an IfcCompositeCurve. - IfcGridAxis is not an IfcRoot, so it has no GlobalId. Per-axis identity is kept in RXD document model/datums. Each record holds {grid_guid, axis_tag, axis_guid, internal_id, grid_type, extents, bubble_visibility}, keyed by the IfcGrid GlobalId plus the axis tag. - Renaming a grid updates AxisTag and the RXD key in the same transaction. The axis GUID is unchanged.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Six orthogonal grid lines produce one IfcGrid with three U axes and three V axes, and a third-party viewer shows their tags. - [ ] After renaming a grid from "A" to "A1" and reopening, the grid keeps its GUID, and dimensions to it are still attached.

    2.3.7 Openings, voids and fillings

    ID: DM-IFC-007 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §2.2, §4.4; TECH_STACK §3.1

    Behaviour & rules. - When a hosted component cuts its host (doors, windows, wall openings, shafts, and components with an "opening cut" void), Reviera shall create an IfcOpeningElement (PredefinedType = OPENING or RECESS). It is linked to the host by IfcRelVoidsElement (RelatingBuildingElement = host, RelatedOpeningElement = opening). - When a component fills that opening, IfcRelFillsElement (RelatingOpeningElement = opening, RelatedBuildingElement = component) shall link it. - The opening's placement shall be relative to the host. The component's placement shall be relative to the opening (or to the host), so that moving the host in a third-party tool keeps the door in place. - The host's Body representation written to IFC shall be the uncut body. Other tools apply the opening, as IFC intends. Reviera's own display uses the cut body (computed by OCCT). For coordination exports, the option "Write cut host geometry" (default off) writes the cut body instead. - Voids that cut several hosts (for example a shaft through floors) produce one IfcOpeningElement per host. RXD element data (hosting) on each opening records which source element made each opening. - Non-cutting hosting (a face-hosted light fixture on a ceiling, or a wall-hosted cabinet without a cut) shall be written as IfcRelConnectsElements (no connection geometry) between host and hosted element, so other tools can see the link. The host reference detail (stable reference string §2.8.3, face UV, offset) is in RXD element data (hosting).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A door in a wall produces exactly one opening, one voids relationship and one fills relationship. - [ ] A third-party viewer shows the wall with a hole at the door, using only the IFC relationships. - [ ] Deleting the wall deletes its doors (after a confirmation that lists them) together with the opening entities and both relationships.

    2.3.8 Materials, layer sets and profile sets

    ID: DM-IFC-008 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §1.2, §4.8, §10; TECH_STACK §3.1

    Behaviour & rules. - Layered system types (basic walls, floors, roofs, ceilings) shall have an IfcMaterialLayerSet attached to the type through IfcRelAssociatesMaterial. Each layer is an IfcMaterialLayer with: - Material (IfcMaterial), LayerThickness, IsVentilated (for air layers); - Name = layer function (Structure, Substrate, ThermalInsulation, Membrane, Finish1, Finish2); - Category = LoadBearing / Insulation / Finish, following buildingSMART recommendations; - Priority = join priority (0–100), mapped from Reviera's layer priority (ARC chapter). - Each instance of a layered type shall have an IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage attached through IfcRelAssociatesMaterial. It records: - LayerSetDirection = AXIS2 for walls and AXIS3 for slabs, roofs and ceilings; - DirectionSense = POSITIVE or NEGATIVE, depending on flip state; - OffsetFromReferenceLine = the signed distance from the wall location line (or slab reference plane) to the first layer; - ReferenceExtent = the wall height, where it applies. - Layer data IFC cannot hold (core boundaries, wrapping at inserts and ends, "variable" layer flags, structural-material flag, stacked-wall and sweep/reveal definitions) is in RXD element data (types), keyed by type GlobalId (ARC chapter). - Profiled types (beams, columns, mullions, braces) shall use IfcMaterialProfileSet on the type and IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage on the instance. CardinalPoint maps from the Reviera justification. - Components with several materials (doors, furniture) shall use IfcMaterialConstituentSet on the type. There is one constituent per material parameter (for example "Frame", "Panel", "Glass"), and its Name is the parameter name. - Instance material overrides (a material bound to an instance parameter) shall be written as a constituent set on the occurrence. - <By Category> materials take the subcategory or category material from Object Styles (§2.10.3), and that resolved material is the one written.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 3-layer exterior wall type round-trips with identical layer order, thicknesses, materials and core boundaries. - [ ] Flipping a wall instance flips DirectionSense. A third-party viewer that renders layers shows the finish on the other side. - [ ] A door family with "Frame Material" and "Panel Material" parameters exports an IfcMaterialConstituentSet with two constituents named after the parameters.

    2.3.9 Other relationships

    ID: DM-IFC-009 · Priority: P0 (joins, aggregation) / P1 (others) · Ref: research/05 §1.4, §2.2, §2.3

    Reviera relationship IFC RXD

    2.3.10 Geometry representation

    ID: DM-IFC-010 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §1.1, §4.4, §4.7; TECH_STACK §3.2

    Behaviour & rules. - Body representations shall use the simplest IFC form that is exact: 1. SweptSolid (IfcExtrudedAreaSolid, IfcRevolvedAreaSolid) for extrusions and revolves; 2. Clipping (IfcBooleanClippingResult with IfcHalfSpaceSolid) for walls cut by roofs or sloped tops; 3. CSG / boolean results for simple void cuts inside families; 4. AdvancedSweptSolid (IfcSurfaceCurveSweptAreaSolid, IfcSweptDiskSolid, IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid) for sweeps; 5. Brep (IfcFacetedBrep) or AdvancedBrep (IfcAdvancedBrep) for blends, lofts and free forms; 6. Tessellation (IfcPolygonalFaceSet, IfcTriangulatedFaceSet) for mesh imports and as a fallback. - Axis (Curve2D/Curve3D) shall be written for walls, beams, columns, members, ducts and pipes. FootPrint shall be written for slabs and spaces. Box (IfcBoundingBox) shall be written for every product. - Plan-symbolic geometry of types (door swings, plan-only symbols) shall be written in the Plan context Annotation sub-context as IfcAnnotationFillArea/IfcPolyline/IfcIndexedPolyCurve on the type's RepresentationMaps. This is building content that IFC can express, so it stays in IFC. The visibility rules that choose which symbolic geometry to show are in the family definition (RXD). - Detail-level variants (Coarse/Medium/Fine) are a Reviera concept. The Fine body is written to the Body sub-context. Coarse and Medium bodies, where they differ, are written as additional IfcShapeRepresentations with RepresentationIdentifier = 'Body' in additional sub-contexts named Body-Coarse / Body-Medium (target view MODEL_VIEW). This keeps all geometry in IFC. Reviera reads them back by sub-context name. - Styling. Surface styles come from materials (§2.10.5) through the material's IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation, or through IfcStyledItem on body items. - Precision. IfcGeometricRepresentationContext.Precision = 1e-5 m. OCCT tolerances are set from it (§2.6.5).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A straight wall without cuts is written as IfcExtrudedAreaSolid, not as a B-rep. - [ ] A family with Coarse/Fine variants round-trips both variants. - [ ] A third-party viewer that does not understand the extra sub-contexts displays the Fine body only.

    2.3.11 Phases, design options and worksets (storage)

    ID: DM-IFC-011 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §2.4; TECH_STACK §3.1, §3.7.2

    Behaviour & rules. - Phases and phase filters are RXD-only: RXD document project/phases holds the ordered phases, the phase filters and the project's current phase. Each element's created/demolished phase is element data phasing. - The IFC Status property of each element's Pset_*Common shall be derived on save from the element's phases relative to the current phase: NEW (created in it), EXISTING (created earlier, not demolished), DEMOLISH (demolished in it), TEMPORARY (created and demolished in it). On reading a file with no RXD, phases are inferred from Status: EXISTING → phase "Existing", everything else → phase "New Construction". - Design option sets and options are RXD-only (RXD document project/design_options; each element's membership is element data membership). On save, the IFC file contains elements of the main model and of every option. Non-primary option elements are listed in RXD so Reviera can hide them. On export to an exchange MVD (§2.11.4), only the main model and primary options are written, unless the user chooses otherwise. - Worksets and ownership are RXD-only (RXD document project/worksets, element data membership; COL chapter).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With the current phase set to "New Construction", a wall created in "Existing" and demolished in "New Construction" exports Status = DEMOLISH. - [ ] Opening the .ifc alone in a third-party viewer shows elements of secondary design options. Opening it in Reviera hides them in views set to show the primary option.

    2.4 Storage split: standard IFC and Reviera Extension Data (RXD)

    2.4.1 Principles

    ID: DM-RXD-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §2.3, §13.1 (extensible storage), §16.9; TECH_STACK §3.1, §3.7; spec/02a_extension_data_format.md

    Purpose. IFC cannot hold parametric intent: constraints, sketches, family formulas, view and sheet definitions, or the meaning of annotation. RXD stores that intent with the model.

    Behaviour & rules. - Physical carriage (property-set names, JSON or compressed chunks, sizes, schema versions, validation, the alternative .reviera sidecar carrier) is defined in spec/02a_extension_data_format.md. This chapter does not redefine it. - Scope rule. Data about one IFC element, which is meaningless without that element, is RXD element data on that element. Everything else is a record in a project-scoped RXD document. Examples: - a floor's sketch, a wall's attach constraints, a door's flip flags, an element's phase and design-option membership → RXD element data; - a view, a sheet, a dimension, a phase definition, an object style, a family recipe → RXD document records. - References. Every RXD reference to an IFC element shall use its GlobalId. References to non-rooted IFC resources (grid axes, materials, profiles) use a composite key (for example <IfcGrid GlobalId>/<AxisTag>) or the RXD GUID assigned to that resource (§2.5). RXD-only elements reference each other by their GUID. - References to sub-element geometry (a face of a wall, the "Left" reference of a door) use stable reference strings (§2.8.3). - Ownership. Each RXD document record has exactly one owner: an IFC element GUID, or an RXD-only element GUID. When the owner is deleted, its records are deleted in the same transaction. Element data is deleted with its element automatically. This keeps BIMserver merges by GlobalId correct (COL chapter). - Orphans. On open, RXD records whose owner GUID is missing from the IFC (for example, because another tool deleted the element) shall be listed in an Extension Data Reconciliation report. The user can drop them (default) or keep them, inactive, for a later merge. - Edits outside Reviera. For each IFC-backed element with intent, RXD element data keeps a BLAKE3 hash of its IFC placement and body (identity.geometry_hash). If another tool changed the IFC so that the hash no longer matches, Reviera shall flag the element as "edited outside Reviera" and offer to keep the IFC (dropping conflicting intent, for example a sketch) or to reapply intent (regenerating from RXD and overwriting the outside edit). - Forward compatibility. Unknown documents and unknown keys are kept and written back unchanged (02a).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Deleting a floor in a third-party tool and reopening in Reviera removes its element data with it. Constraints in RXD documents that referenced it are listed as orphans, and dropping them leaves no dangling references. - [ ] A floor whose extrusion depth was changed in another IFC editor is flagged on open, and both resolutions work.

    2.4.2 What goes where

    ID: DM-RXD-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §1–§10; spec/02a_extension_data_format.md

    Data Standard IFC RXD (element data key, or document name; 02a is authoritative)
    Spatial structure, storeys ✔ document datums (non-storey levels, level display data)
    Grids ✔ IfcGrid/IfcGridAxis document datums (axis identity, extents, bubbles)

    User parameter values ✔ (as property sets) —
    Parameter definitions (data type, group, formula, GUID, tooltip, bindings) — document parameters
    Global parameters (definitions, values, formulas, associations) — document parameters
    Classifications ✔ IfcClassification/IfcClassificationReference —
    Openings, voids, fills ✔ element data hosting
    Joins ✔ (connection relationships) element data joins
    Constraints, locks, EQ, labelled dimensions — element data constraints (IFC owner) or the owning record in document annotation (dimension owner)
    Sketches and edit-sketch recipes — element data sketch

    Lookup tables — inside the family document (or an RXD asset, 02a)

    Sheets, viewports, title-block instance data, sheet collections — document sheets
    Schedules — document schedules
    View-specific annotation and details — document annotation
    Revisions — document revisions
    Object styles, line weights, line styles, line patterns, fill patterns — document styles

    Design options Elements only document design_options (sets, options); element data membership
    Worksets, ownership — document worksets (definitions); element data membership (COL)

    Location: geo-referencing ✔ IfcMapConversion, IfcProjectedCRS, IfcSite lat/long, TrueNorth document location (named shared-coordinate sites, weather)

    2.4.3 Reconciliation

    ID: DM-RXD-003 · Priority: P0 · Ref: spec/02a_extension_data_format.md; TECH_STACK §3.7

    Behaviour & rules. - On every open, Reviera shall run the integrity checks that 02a defines. Their outcomes are shown to the user like this: - RXD present and consistent: open normally. - No RXD found (a third-party file, or a file whose Reviera_* property sets were stripped): open as an IFC-only model (§2.11.1) and tell the user. If an external .reviera sidecar for this file is found beside it, offer to attach it. - RXD belongs to another project (identity mismatch as defined in 02a): refuse to bind it. Offer to open IFC-only, or to choose another sidecar. - RXD stale or partial (for example, IFC edited by another tool after the last Reviera save): open with the RXD, then run reconciliation (§2.4.1) and show which elements and documents are affected. - The reconciliation report lists orphans, hash mismatches and documents that failed schema validation. Each item has a resolution, and every resolution can be undone.

    Commands. rxd.status() -> {present, carrier, schema_version, orphans, mismatches, invalid_documents} · rxd.reconcile(mode: report|apply, drop_orphans?=true) -> report · rxd.attach_sidecar(path) · rxd.export_sidecar(path)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A project saved by Reviera, then re-saved by a tool that strips unknown property sets, opens as IFC-only. Attaching the sidecar exported before the strip restores views and annotation. - [ ] Pairing a project's IFC with another project's sidecar is refused.

    2.4.4 Constraints

    ID: DM-RXD-004 · Priority: P0 (locks, alignments, level constraints) / P1 (equality, labelled dimensions, global-parameter links) · Ref: research/05 §2.3, §4.5

    Behaviour & rules. - Constraints are stored with their owner: as RXD element data constraints when the owner is an IFC element, or inside the owning record (for example a dimension in RXD document views/annotation/<viewId>). Each record has this shape (informative; the schema is in 02a):

    {
  "id": "1kP0…",                    // GUID of the constraint (22-char IFC format)
  "owner": "0aZ1…",                 // owning element GUID (IFC or RXD-only)
  "kind": "align|distance|equal|angle|attach_top|attach_base|level_offset|host|parallel|tangent|fixed",
  "refs": ["0aZ1…#face:exterior", "2Hq…#ref:Left"],  // stable references, §2.8.3
  "value": 0.0,                     // distance (m) or angle (rad)
  "param": "CorridorWidth",         // optional: label (family, project or global parameter)
  "locked": true,
  "reporting": false
}
    • The owner is chosen like this: a dimension owns its distance, equality and label constraints. The moving element owns an alignment lock (the one that was aligned onto the target). A wall owns its attach and level constraints.
    • When a referenced element is deleted, its constraint records are removed in the same transaction. The removal is reported as a warning (§2.7.4) when the constraint was locked.

    2.4.5 Sketches

    ID: DM-RXD-005 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §2.3, §4.4

    Behaviour & rules. - RXD element data sketch holds, for every sketch-based element (floor, roof, ceiling, opening, filled region, stair boundary, in-place form), keyed by the owning element GUID: - plane: the work plane, as a reference or an explicit plane; - curves: each with an id, a kind (line, arc, circle, ellipse, spline, point), geometry in sketch-plane coordinates, and flags (is_reference, defines_slope, slope, offset, overhang) that the owning element interprets; - loops: an ordered list of curve IDs with orientation; - constraints: the same record format as §2.4.4, with references of the form #curve:<id>:<start|end|mid>; - picked_from: for curves created with "Pick Walls" or "Pick Lines", a reference to the source, so the curve follows it. - The evaluated result is in IFC (for example, the slab's IfcArbitraryProfileDefWithVoids). If the RXD sketch is missing (for example, a downstream tool stripped it), Edit Boundary rebuilds a sketch from the IFC profile, without constraints or picked-from links. - Sketch validation (closed loops, no self-intersection, no overlapping loops where they are not allowed) runs on Finish Sketch. Errors keep the user in sketch mode (§2.7.4).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A floor sketched with "Pick Walls" follows the walls when they move, after the project has been saved and reopened. - [ ] With the RXD stripped from the file, Edit Boundary on that floor gives an editable sketch that matches the slab outline.

    2.5 Element identity

    Internal ID and GlobalId

    ID: DM-ID-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §2.1, §16.1; TECH_STACK §3.3

    Purpose. Every element needs a fast in-process key and a durable, globally unique key.

    Behaviour & rules. - GUID. Every IFC-backed element uses its GlobalId. This is a 128-bit UUID encoded as IFC's 22-character base-64 string (alphabet 0-9A-Za-z_$). RXD-only elements get a GUID in the same encoding, so tools handle every GUID the same way. - New GUIDs shall be random UUID v4, or UUID v7 when the setting "time-ordered GUIDs" is on (this improves locality in BIMserver). - A GUID is never reused, and never changes over the life of the element. That includes save, reopen, schema upgrade, type swap, move between levels, conversion between storey and non-storey level, and BIMserver sync. - Copy, paste, duplicate, mirror-copy and array create new GUIDs. The source GUID is kept in element data identity (source_guid). - Non-rooted IFC resources (materials, profiles, styles, grid axes) have no GlobalId in IFC. Reviera gives them an RXD GUID, mapped in RXD document project/identity to a resource key (for example material:<Name> or <IfcGrid GlobalId>/<AxisTag>). Renaming a material updates the key, not the GUID. - Internal ID (ElementId) is an unsigned 64-bit integer, unique within one model and never reused within it: - It is persisted in element data identity (for IFC-backed elements) or in the element's record (for RXD-only elements). The next free value is in RXD document project/identity. - On opening a file with no RXD (a third-party file), IDs are assigned in ascending order of STEP instance number. This makes them deterministic for that file. - On merging another revision, or pasting from another model, any clashing internal IDs in the incoming elements are reassigned. A remap table is reported to Lua/MCP (model.id_remap event), so scripts holding IDs can update them. The GUID is the only key that is guaranteed across models. - IDs 1–999 are reserved for model singletons (project information, project settings). Negative values are reserved for categories and built-in parameters. - STEP instance numbers (#123) are never used as identity. They may change on every save. - The UI shall offer IDs of Selection (shows internal ID and GUID, both copyable) and Select by ID (accepts either).

    Commands. element.get_ids(element_ids[]) -> [{id, guid}] · element.select_by_id(ids_or_guids[]) -> element_id[] · element.find_by_guid(guid) -> element_id?

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] 10,000 elements created, saved, reopened, saved again and reopened all keep identical GUIDs and internal IDs. - [ ] Copying 50 elements creates 50 new GUIDs and IDs, each with source_guid pointing at its source. - [ ] Merging two BIMserver revisions that each created an element with internal ID 5001 leaves both elements in the model, with distinct IDs, and emits a remap event. - [ ] Select by ID accepts 3vB2Qe… (22 characters) and 5001, and selects the same element.

    Version stamps

    ID: DM-ID-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §2.1 (document version)

    Purpose. Caches, add-ins, agents and exporters need a cheap way to ask "has anything changed since I last looked, and what?" without diffing the model.

    Behaviour & rules. - The model shall keep a model version: a 128-bit episode GUID (new on each open or session start) plus a monotonically increasing transaction counter. Add-ins and MCP clients can read it to detect changes cheaply (model.version). - The counter increases by exactly 1 for every committed transaction, including undo, redo, journal replay and merged BIMserver revisions. Rolled-back transactions and read-only commands do not change it. Undo does not restore an earlier counter value: undoing is itself a new change. - Each element shall keep the transaction counter of its last change (in memory), and last_modified_txn / last_modified_by / last_modified_at in element data identity (persisted as <episode>:<counter>). - "Change" means any facet of the element changed: parameters, placement, geometry after regeneration, type, host, memberships or its RXD element data. An element touched by regeneration only because a dependency was re-evaluated, but whose results are identical, is not marked changed. - Deleted elements are tracked as tombstones (internal ID, GUID, counter of deletion) for the current episode, so a change query can report deletions. - A version from a different episode (for example after reopening the file) cannot be compared element by element. element.changed_since then returns {stale_episode: true} and the caller must re-read everything. Within an episode, versions are totally ordered. - last_modified_by holds the origin of the transaction (user, lua:<script>, addin:<id>, mcp:<client>, sync:<author>), never credentials.

    Data (storage). The episode GUID and counter are in memory and in the live store (Ch 2b). Per-element stamps are persisted in RXD element data identity for IFC-backed elements, and in each record for RXD-only elements. They are not written to exchange exports (§2.11.4).

    Commands. model.version() -> {episode, counter} · element.changed_since(version) -> {changed[], deleted[], stale_episode}

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] element.changed_since(v) called right after model.version() returns empty lists. After a move, changed holds exactly the moved and regenerated elements. - [ ] Undoing that move increases the counter again, and element.changed_since with the post-move version returns the same elements. - [ ] Deleting a door reports its ID as deleted in the next element.changed_since call; calling with a version from before the last file open returns stale_episode: true. - [ ] Changing a type parameter that does not affect the geometry of a dependent tag leaves the tag out of the changed list.

    2.6 Hosting, the parametric dependency graph and regeneration

    2.6.1 Hosting and dependent elements

    ID: DM-HOST-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §2.2, §4.1

    Purpose. Hosted elements follow their hosts, and deleting a host deals with its dependents in a predictable way.

    Behaviour & rules. - Hosting modes (fixed by the family template, §2.8.1): wall-, floor-, ceiling-, roof-, face-, line-, work-plane-, level- and two-level-based, and adaptive. - Moving or changing a host moves or re-evaluates its hosted elements in the same transaction. A face-hosted element follows its host face through its stable reference (§2.8.3). If that face no longer exists after the change, the element becomes orphaned. It keeps its last world position and gets a warning, and the user can use Pick New Host. - Deleting a host shall show a dialog listing its dependents, before the transaction commits: - hosted components and openings: deleted; - tags and view-specific annotation that refer only to deleted elements: deleted; - dimensions that refer to a deleted element: the reference is removed, and the dimension is deleted if it has fewer than two references left; - constraints: removed (with a warning for locked ones); - sketch lines picked from the host: unlinked, and their geometry kept. - Elements hosted on linked model faces keep their position when the link is unloaded. They are flagged "host not available" until the link is reloaded (COL). - Walls hosted on walls, attachments to roofs and floors, and other host rules come from domain chapters, and are expressed through the same dependency graph.

    Commands. element.dependents(element_ids[]) -> {element_id, action}[] · element.delete(element_ids[], confirm_dependents?=true) -> element_ids[] · host.rehost(element_id, host_id, reference?)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Deleting a wall with 2 doors, 1 tag per door and a dimension to the wall face shows all 5 dependents with their actions, and Cancel leaves the model unchanged. - [ ] Changing a host wall's thickness keeps hosted doors centred in the wall, or at the same offset from the reference face, as the family's placement rule says.

    2.6.2 The dependency graph

    ID: DM-REGEN-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §2.3, §3, §16.5; TECH_STACK §3.3

    Purpose. "A change anywhere is a change everywhere" is put into practice by an explicit graph that records which derived values depend on which inputs.

    Behaviour & rules. - The core shall maintain a directed dependency graph in memory. It is rebuilt from the model on open, and kept up to date by every transaction. The graph is not saved to disk. Its sources (constraints, hosting, sketches, formulas) are saved in IFC and RXD. - Nodes are fine-grained facets of elements, not whole elements. This avoids recomputing more than needed:

    Facet Example
    params(e) Evaluated parameter values of element e, including formula results
    placement(e) Location point, curve or transform
    shape(e) Uncut solid of e (OCCT B-rep)
    cut_shape(e) Shape after joins, openings and void cuts
    profile(e) 2D boundary (sketch-based elements, rooms)
    quantities(e) Area, volume, length, Qto values
    annotation(a) Text values and geometry of annotation a
    view_cache(v) Visibility and display lists of view v (DOC)
    • Edges say "B must be recomputed when A changes". They come from: 1. type → instance (params(type) → params(instance), shape(instance)); 2. formulas (each referenced parameter → the formula's parameter); 3. global parameters → the parameters and dimensions associated with them; 4. constraints (§2.4.4): references → constrained element placement; 5. hosting: shape(host) → placement(hosted); placement(hosted) → cut_shape(host) (openings); 6. joins: shape(a), shape(b) → cut_shape(a), cut_shape(b); 7. level and datum constraints: placement(level) → base and top of constrained elements; 8. room bounding: cut_shape(bounding elements) → profile(room) → quantities(room); 9. annotation references: referenced facets → annotation(a); 10. view dependencies: any visible facet → view_cache(v) (lazily, only for open views).
    • Cycles. The graph must stay acyclic. A command that would create a cycle (for example, a formula A = B + 1 when B = A * 2, or two walls each attached to the other) shall be rejected before commit. The error names the elements and parameters in the cycle (§2.7.4).
    • Strongly coupled groups. Some inputs must be solved together (for example the reference planes and labelled dimensions in one family, or the curves of one sketch with their constraints). Each such group is a single solver node. Its members are solved together by the constraint solver (§2.6.3).
    • The graph shall be inspectable for debugging: regen.explain(element_id) returns the upstream inputs and downstream dependents of an element's facets.

    Commands. regen.explain(element_id, facet?) -> {upstream[], downstream[]}

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing one door type's width recomputes only that type's instances, their host walls' cut_shape, the affected rooms and the open views showing them. Instrumentation shows that no other elements were recomputed. - [ ] Creating a circular formula reference is rejected with a message naming both parameters, and the model is unchanged.

    2.6.3 Constraint solving

    ID: DM-REGEN-002 · Priority: P0 (1-D dimensional constraints) / P2 (general 2D solver) · Ref: research/05 §2.3, §4.5, §16.5

    Purpose. To solve locks, alignments, equalities and labelled dimensions.

    Behaviour & rules. - v1 solver (P0/P1): a 1-D solver, like the reference product. Constraints act on distances along a direction between parallel references (planes, lines, faces). Each solver node is split into independent axis groups (for example X, Y, Z, and each family-local direction). Each group is solved as a sparse linear system, with locked or labelled values as equations and current positions as soft targets (least change). Angular constraints on reference lines are solved in a second pass, with the same method on angles. - Over-constrained or inconsistent systems shall be reported as an error that names the conflicting constraints and highlights them in the view. That is a clear improvement on a generic "constraints are not satisfied" message. Resolutions offered: Remove constraint(s) (choose which), Unjoin, Cancel. - Under-constrained systems are allowed. Free references keep their current position. - P2: a general 2D sketch solver (points, lines, arcs, with coincident, tangent, perpendicular, parallel, distance, radius and angle constraints). It is based on an open solver, for example the PlaneGCS solver (LGPL-2.1+) or SolveSpace's solver (GPL-3.0). It applies inside sketches and the family editor. - The solver shall be deterministic. For the same inputs it returns bit-identical results.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A family with Width and Depth labelled dimensions, plus an EQ constraint about the centre plane, flexes correctly through 20 random values in the valid range. - [ ] Locking two contradictory distances between the same pair of planes reports an error naming both dimensions, and Remove constraint on either one resolves it.

    2.6.4 Parallel regeneration

    ID: DM-REGEN-003 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §3, §15.1 (single-threaded regeneration in the reference); TECH_STACK §3.2, §3.3

    Purpose. To use all CPU cores for geometry, where the reference product mostly does not.

    Behaviour & rules. - When. Regeneration runs inside every transaction, before commit (§2.7.1). Lua scripts and commands may also call regen.now() part-way through a transaction to read updated values. - Algorithm. 1. Mark every facet that the transaction's changes touched as dirty, then propagate dirtiness downstream. 2. Order the dirty subgraph into topological levels (Kahn's algorithm). Ties are broken by element internal ID, so the order is deterministic. 3. Evaluate each level in parallel with rayon (par_iter over the level's facets). Each task reads only committed or already-evaluated upstream results, and writes its result into a per-task output slot. Tasks never write to shared state. 4. After each level, merge the slots into the transaction's staging area in internal-ID order. 5. After the last level, check the warnings and errors (§2.7.4). If there are no blocking errors, swap the staging area into the committed store atomically, in a single ArcSwap-style pointer swap per store partition, so readers (the UI, MCP resource reads) see either the old state or the new state, never a mix. - Determinism. Parallel results shall not depend on thread count or scheduling. Floating-point reductions that cross tasks (for example the total area of a room from several boundary segments) shall be done in a fixed order after the parallel step. - Granularity. Very small facets (parameter evaluation) are batched, so each rayon task does at least about 50 µs of work. Large booleans may themselves use OCCT's internal parallelism (§2.6.5). - Cancellation. Long regenerations shall check a cancellation token between levels and inside long OCCT operations (Message_ProgressRange user break). Cancelling rolls the transaction back. - Progress. Regenerations longer than 300 ms report progress to the UI status bar and to MCP progress notifications. - Background view work. View caches (view_cache(v)) for views that are not visible are recomputed lazily, when a view is activated. They are not part of the transaction.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Regenerating a 20,000-element benchmark model after changing a shared wall type is at least 3× faster on 8 cores than on 1 core (same machine). - [ ] The same benchmark, run with 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 threads, produces identical geometry hashes (element data identity.geometry_hash) for every element. - [ ] Cancelling a long regeneration leaves the model exactly as it was before the command.

    2.6.5 OCCT threading rules

    ID: DM-REGEN-004 · Priority: P0 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.2

    Purpose. OCCT is not uniformly thread-safe. These rules make parallel use of it safe.

    Behaviour & rules. 1. No shared mutable shapes. A TopoDS_Shape that is being built or modified is owned by exactly one task. Shapes in the committed store are immutable. A task that needs to change one first copies it (BRepBuilderAPI_Copy) or builds a new shape from it. 2. Read-only sharing is allowed only for committed, immutable shapes, and only for operations documented as read-only (for example bounding boxes or point classification on an already-meshed shape). Every operation that writes caches into a shape (for example triangulation stored on faces, or BRepMesh_IncrementalMesh) shall run on a task-owned copy. 3. Per-thread tools. Algorithm objects (BRepAlgoAPI_*, BRepOffsetAPI_*, BRepMesh_*, ShapeFix_*) are created per task, never shared or reused across threads. 4. No global state changes during regeneration. Global OCCT settings (for example BRepAlgo fuzzy values via static setters, Standard:: allocator settings, message gravity) are set once at start-up and never changed while workers run. 5. Memory manager. OCCT shall be configured to use the system allocator in its thread-safe mode (MMGT_OPT=0 or the build's equivalent; verify for the chosen OCCT version), set before the first OCCT call. 6. Handles across threads. Handle(Standard_Transient) reference counts are atomic in current OCCT releases, so passing handles of immutable objects between threads is allowed. This shall be confirmed by a stress test for the OCCT version that is pinned. 7. Internal parallelism. Boolean and meshing algorithms support SetRunParallel(true). Reviera shall enable it only when the current regeneration level has fewer tasks than the number of worker threads, to avoid oversubscription.
