OCCT's thread pool (OSD_ThreadPool) shall be sized to the rayon pool size. 8. Tolerances. Fuzzy values and tolerances come from the project precision (1e-5 m, §2.3.10). Boolean failures are retried once with a fuzzy value 10× larger. If that also fails, the element gets a warning, and the uncut shape is shown. 9. Isolation of crashes. OCCT exceptions (Standard_Failure) are caught at the FFI boundary and become element warnings. A failure in one task never aborts other tasks.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A ThreadSanitizer/stress test runs 1,000 random boolean regenerations on 16 threads with no data races reported in Reviera code or in the FFI layer. - [ ] A deliberately failing boolean (coincident faces) produces one element warning, and the other 999 elements regenerate normally.

    2.7 Transactions, undo/redo, warnings and errors

    2.7.1 Transactions

    ID: DM-TXN-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §3, §16.6; TECH_STACK §3.3

    Purpose. Every change is atomic, named and undoable.

    Behaviour & rules. - Transaction. Every command runs in exactly one top-level transaction, named after the command (for example "Wall", "Move", "Modify type attributes"). A transaction has the states Started → (Regenerating) → Committed | RolledBack. - Sub-transaction (savepoint). A transaction may create nested savepoints. Each can be rolled back on its own, without ending the outer transaction. Savepoints do not appear in the undo history. - Transaction group. A group bundles several transactions: - Assimilate merges them into a single undo item with the group's name (for multi-step tools such as "Create stair", or an MCP agent's multi-step task). - Commit keeps them as separate undo items. - Rollback undoes all of them. - Serialisation. Only one transaction can be open on a document at a time. Requests from the UI, Lua and MCP are queued on the command queue and run in order (TECH_STACK §3.3). Read-only queries do not need a transaction, and run concurrently against the last committed snapshot. - Contents. A transaction records a change set: elements added, modified (per facet and per parameter, with before and after values) and deleted, plus RXD records added, changed and removed. This change set drives undo, events, updaters (§2.13.5) and BIMserver sync (COL). - Failure → rollback. An unhandled error, a panic in a command, a Lua error or a blocking failure (§2.7.4) rolls the transaction back completely. - Read-only mode. Commands declared effect = read (§2.12) run without a transaction. Trying to write from them is an error.

    Commands. These are internal primitives, exposed to Lua (§2.13.4) and MCP (§2.16.4), not as stand-alone tools: txn.begin(name), txn.commit(), txn.rollback(), txn.savepoint() -> sp, txn.rollback_to(sp), txn.group_begin(name), txn.group_end(mode: "assimilate"|"commit"|"rollback").

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A Lua script that creates 10 walls and then raises an error leaves no walls in the model, and no undo item. - [ ] A group of 3 transactions assimilated as "Create stair" shows as one undo item, and one undo removes all three transactions' changes. - [ ] During a long transaction started by MCP, a read-only MCP resource read returns the last committed state without waiting.

    2.7.2 Undo and redo

    ID: DM-TXN-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §3

    Purpose. Multi-level undo and redo of named operations.

    UI. Quick Access Toolbar › Undo and Redo split buttons. Each drop-down lists the transaction names, newest first, and each entry shows its source (UI, Lua script name, add-in ID or MCP client name). Choosing an entry undoes or redoes everything up to and including it. Shortcuts: Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y (UI chapter).

    Behaviour & rules. - Undo is stored as inverse change sets (not full snapshots). Memory use is bounded by a setting (default 512 MB, or 100 items, whichever is reached first). The oldest items are dropped when the limit is reached. - Undo survives save in Local mode (a difference from the reference product). - Undo is cleared by: closing the document; Get latest / Sync in BIMserver mode (the merge changes the base); purge with "compact undo"; and schema conversion. The user is warned before each of these. - Any new transaction clears the redo stack. - Undo and redo are themselves transactions for events and updaters: document.changed fires with undo = true. Updaters do not run on undo or redo, because their effects are already part of the recorded change set. - Every undo item records its origin: {source: "ui"|"lua"|"addin"|"mcp", actor, session_id}. MCP undo tools can only undo items from their own session, unless they have the full permission level (§2.16.5).

    Commands. edit.undo(steps=1) · edit.redo(steps=1) · edit.history() -> [{name, origin, time}]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] After 50 mixed edits, undo of all 50 returns the model to a state whose IFC export is semantically identical to the original. - [ ] Undo after save, in Local mode, works, and the model shows as modified again. - [ ] An MCP session with model-edit permission cannot undo a UI user's transaction.

    2.7.3 Change journal and recovery

    ID: DM-TXN-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §11.1 (journals, backups)

    Behaviour & rules. - Reviera shall write a session journal: an append-only log of every executed command with its parameters, its origin and its result. It is in JSON Lines (journal-<date>-<pid>.jsonl in the user's state directory). It is used for diagnostics and crash recovery. MCP tool calls are logged with the client name. - Crash recovery. Reviera writes an autosave of the model every N minutes (default 10) to a recovery file, in the background, from a committed snapshot. On the next start after a crash, it offers to restore the autosave and replay the journal entries since the autosave. - Journal replay can also be used as a macro recording source (§2.13.8). - Journals never contain credentials or MCP authentication tokens.

    Commands. journal.replay(path, stop_on_error=true)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Killing the process after 20 edits and restarting offers recovery. Accepting gives a model that matches the state after the 20th edit.

    2.7.4 Warnings, errors and failure handling

    ID: DM-FAIL-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §2.3, §3

    Purpose. Problems found during a transaction are reported consistently and can be resolved by users or by code.

    Behaviour & rules. - Every problem is a failure message created from a failure definition in a registry. Each definition has a stable ID (for example dm.constraint.unsatisfied, arc.wall.overlap, dm.regen.boolean_failed), a severity, a message template, the elements involved and the resolutions it offers. - Severities:

    Severity Effect Stored Example
    Info Shown briefly in the status area No "Family loaded with 3 types"
    Warning Transaction commits. A non-modal warning pop-up lists the warnings and their elements. Yes, in RXD document project/warnings Overlapping walls; room not enclosed; boolean failed
    Error Transaction cannot commit until it is resolved. A modal dialog offers the resolutions and Cancel. No Constraints cannot be satisfied; sketch not closed; circular reference
    Fatal Transaction rolls back. No resolution. No Internal invariant broken
    • Resolutions are typed actions, such as Remove constraint, Unjoin elements, Delete element(s), Disallow join, Keep editing (sketch). Applying a resolution re-runs regeneration inside the same transaction.
    • Stored warnings are re-checked on every regeneration of the elements involved. A warning disappears when its condition is gone. The warnings of a model are listed in Review Warnings (Manage › Inquiry): grouped by definition, with element IDs, Show (zooms to the elements), Delete checked and Export (HTML/CSV).
    • Programmatic handling.
    • Lua and add-ins can register a failure preprocessor for a transaction. It receives every failure before the UI does, and can dismiss a warning, resolve an error with one of its resolutions, or let it continue to the UI.
    • In MCP and other non-interactive contexts there is no UI: warnings are returned in the tool result, and errors fail the call with their resolutions listed. The agent can then call again with failure_policy: {"<failure-id>": "<resolution>"}.
    • Each command result shall include warnings[] (ID, message, element IDs) so that scripts can react.

    UI. Warning pop-up (bottom right, non-modal, with "Show", "More info", "Expand"). Error dialog (modal, with resolution buttons). Manage › Inquiry › Review Warnings. A warning count badge in the status bar.

    Data (storage). Stored warnings: RXD document project/warnings (failure definition ID, element GUIDs, first-seen time, dismissed state).

    Commands. warnings.list(filter?: {kind?, severity?, element_ids?}) -> warning[] · warnings.show(warning_id) · warnings.dismiss(warning_ids[]) (sets the same stored acknowledged state in project/warnings as Chapter 6's warnings.acknowledge; the two are aliases) · warnings.export(path, format: html|csv) -> () · failure.set_policy(policy) (per transaction or per session)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Two overlapping walls produce a stored warning that is listed in Review Warnings, survives save and reopen, and disappears when one wall is moved away. - [ ] An MCP tool call that causes a dm.constraint.unsatisfied error fails, lists the resolutions, and leaves the model unchanged. Repeating the call with failure_policy: {"dm.constraint.unsatisfied": "remove_constraints"} succeeds and reports which constraints were removed. - [ ] A Lua failure preprocessor that dismisses arc.wall.overlap lets a batch script create overlapping walls with no pop-ups, and the warnings are still stored.

    2.8 The Reviera Family Editor

    The Reviera Family Editor is a document mode for creating and editing loadable families. It opens a family document. That is an in-memory model of the same kind as a project, with its own transactions and undo, but holding one family definition instead of a building. In-place families use the same tools inside a project (§2.2.3).

    2.8.0 Family Editor environment

    ID: DM-FED-000 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §4 (intro), §4.9; screenshots/platform/family_types_dialog_parameter_groups.png, screenshots/platform/family_types_cabinet_variations_2026.png

    Purpose. A dedicated environment that looks like the project environment but offers family-authoring tools.

    Workflow. 1. File › New › Family, then choose a family template (§2.8.1). Or open a family package. Or select an instance in a project and choose Edit Family. 2. Draw reference planes, add dimensions and label them with parameters, and create forms locked to the planes. 3. Open Family Types, create types, and flex the parameters. 4. Choose Load into Project (or Load into Project and Close), or Save to a family package.

    UI. - The document opens in its own view windows, with a Project Browser listing the family views: Ref. Level plan, ceiling plan, Front/Back/Left/Right elevations, and a default 3D view. Its title-bar badge reads "Family: <name>". - Create tab panels: - Properties: Family Types, Family Category and Parameters, Type Properties; - Forms: Extrusion, Blend, Revolve, Sweep, Swept Blend, and Void Forms (the same five as voids); - Model: Model Line, Component (nest), Model Text, Opening (host templates only), Model Group; - Control: Flip Control; - Connectors: Electrical, Duct, Pipe, Cable Tray, Conduit (MEP templates); - Datum: Reference Plane, Reference Line, Reference Point (conceptual and adaptive); - Work Plane: Set, Show, Viewer; - Family Editor: Load into Project, Load into Project and Close. - Annotate tab: Aligned/Angular/Radial/Diameter/Arc-length dimensions, Label (annotation families), Symbolic Line, Detail Component, Filled Region, Masking Region, Text. - Modify tab: the standard modify tools (ARC chapter) plus Align/Lock, Array (with a count parameter), Cut/Uncut Geometry, Join/Unjoin Geometry, and Visibility Settings for the selected geometry. - The Properties palette shows the selected form's properties (extents, Visible, Visibility Settings, Material, Subcategory, Solid/Void). The "=" button beside a property associates it with a family parameter. - There is no Options Bar. Placement and drawing options are in the contextual tab (UI chapter; matches the reference's 2027 direction).

    Behaviour & rules. - A family document has the same transaction, undo, warning and regeneration behaviour as a project (§2.6, §2.7). - Load into Project pushes the current definition into one or more open projects or family documents, chosen in a dialog. It uses the reload rules in §2.2.3. A family document opened from a project with Edit Family offers the source project first. - Several family documents and projects may be open at once.

    Commands. family_doc.new(template_path) -> document_id · family_doc.open(path) -> document_id · family_doc.save(document_id, path?) · family_doc.load_into(document_id, target_document_ids[], overwrite_values=false)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A user can create a parametric table family (four legs and a top driven by Width, Depth and Height), flex it through 3 types, load it into a project and schedule its types, without leaving the application. - [ ] Undo in a family document never affects an open project, and the reverse is also true.

    2.8.1 Family templates

    ID: DM-FED-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §4.1, §11.1

    Purpose. Templates fix a family's category, hosting behaviour, default references and dimensionality before any geometry exists.

    Behaviour & rules. - A family template is a family package (§2.8.14) with the template flag set in its family-package manifest (02a). By convention the file is named <Name>.familytemplate.ifc. Opening one always creates a new, untitled family document. - A template fixes: - category (it can be changed later only within the template's compatibility set; for example Generic Model ↔ Furniture is allowed, Door → Window is not); - placement mode: level, work_plane, face, wall_hosted, floor_hosted, ceiling_hosted, roof_hosted, line, two_level, adaptive, pattern_panel, view_specific, profile, title_block, annotation, mass. This cannot be changed after creation, except that level families may be switched to work_plane with the Work Plane-Based flag (§2.8.2); - dimensionality: 3D, 2D detail, 2D annotation, 2D profile, title block, conceptual (CME, §2.8.13); - default references and parameters: for example Left/Right/Front/Back/Centre planes and Width/Depth labels; or, for door templates, a host wall with a default opening and Width/Height parameters. - Reviera shall ship its own templates. They shall be authored from scratch (not copied from the reference product's content) and cover these groups:

    Group Templates (metric and imperial variants)
    Generic Generic Model; Generic Model (face-based, line-based, wall-, floor-, ceiling- and roof-hosted, two-level-based); Generic Model Adaptive; Generic Model Pattern-Based
    Architecture Door; Door (curtain wall); Window; Window (curtain wall); Furniture; Furniture System; Casework; Plumbing Fixture; Specialty Equipment; Entourage; Planting; Baluster; Baluster Post; Baluster Panel; Railing Support; Railing Termination; Curtain Wall Panel; Column; Parking; Site
    Structure Structural Framing (beams and braces); Structural Framing (complex and trusses); Structural Column; Structural Foundation; Structural Stiffener; Structural Connection; Structural Truss (STR chapter)
    MEP Mechanical Equipment; duct and pipe fittings (elbow, tee, cross, transition, union, cap); Air Terminal; Electrical Equipment; Electrical Fixture; Lighting Fixture (ceiling, wall, linear); device templates (communication, data, fire alarm, security, nurse call); cable tray and conduit fittings (MEP chapter)
    2D Detail Item; Detail Item (line-based); Profile; Profile (hosted); Profile (rail); Profile (mullion); Profile (stair nosing); Profile (reveal)
    Annotation Generic Annotation; Generic Tag; Multi-Category Tag; category tags (Door, Window, Room, Area, Space, Wall, …); Material Tag; Keynote Tag; Section Head; Elevation Mark; Level Head; Grid Head; Callout Head; View Title; Spot Elevation Symbol; Revision Tag; North Arrow; Stair Path; Span Direction Symbol
    Title blocks ISO A0–A4; ANSI A–E; ARCH A–E; Custom Size
    Conceptual Mass; Generic Model Adaptive; Curtain Panel Pattern-Based (rectangle, rhomboid, triangle bent/flat, hexagon, octagon, arrows, zigzag, half/third step)
    • Template search paths: the shipped template folder, the user template folder, and any folder listed in settings (UI chapter). Template sets are installed per locale, with the metric set as the default.
    • Users can save any family document as a template (Save As › Family Template). The template keeps the family's category, placement mode, references and parameters. Geometry is kept only if the user chooses to keep it.

    Commands. family_template.list(locale?) -> template[] · family_doc.save_as_template(document_id, path, keep_geometry=false)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Each shipped template opens, flexes its default parameters without errors, and loads into an empty project, where its placement mode works (for example, a wall-hosted template places only on walls). - [ ] An attempt to change a Door family's category to Windows is refused, and the message explains why.

    2.8.2 Family category and family parameters

    ID: DM-FED-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §4.2

    Purpose. Family-level behaviour flags that apply to the whole family and cannot vary by type.

    Workflow. 1. In a family document, Create › Properties › Family Category and Parameters (family_doc.category_params()). 2. Pick a category in the tree. The flag grid below refreshes to the flags that apply to it, keeping the values of flags both categories share. 3. Set flags. Choose OK to apply the category change and all flag changes as one transaction, or Cancel.

    UI. Create › Properties › Family Category and Parameters: a category tree (filtered to the compatible set) and a property grid of family parameters. Only the flags that apply to the category are shown. - The tree has a discipline filter (All, Architecture, Structure, Mechanical, Electrical, Piping) and a search field. Categories outside the template's compatibility set (§2.8.1) are not listed; a note under the tree says why ("Door templates can only be Doors"). - Each flag row shows its name, value control (check box, drop-down or text) and a tooltip with its meaning. Flags that the template fixes (for example work_plane_based for face-based templates) are shown greyed with the reason.

    Validation. - Changing the category is checked before it is applied. If geometry is assigned to subcategories of the old category, the dialog lists them and offers to move them to same-named subcategories of the new category (created if missing) or to the new category itself. Nested shared components and tag targets are unaffected. - ifc_class / ifc_predefined_type drop-downs list only values allowed for the category (§2.2.2). USERDEFINED requires a non-empty text value, otherwise OK is disabled. - classification_code must exist in a loaded classification system when one is active (§2.10.10); an unknown code is accepted only after confirmation and is flagged in the family's warnings. - Turning shared off on a family that is nested as shared in an open project warns that its instances will stop being schedulable there after reload.

    Behaviour & rules. These family parameters shall be supported:

    Flag Applies to Meaning
    work_plane_based Level-based 3D families Instances host on a work plane or face when placed
    always_vertical Work-plane- and face-based The instance stays vertical on a sloped host (default on for most categories)
    cut_with_voids_when_loaded 3D Voids in other families and in-place elements may cut this family
    shared All When nested, instances are separate, selectable, taggable and schedulable elements in projects (§2.8.10)
    room_calculation_point Furniture, equipment, doors, windows, … Shows a movable point that sets which room or space the instance belongs to. Doors and windows also report To Room/From Room.
    part_type MEP and structural Normal, Elbow, Tee, Cross, Transition, Cap, Union, Multi-port, Damper, Panelboard, Switchboard, Transformer, … (MEP/STR chapters)
    classification_code / classification_title All A classification reference (§2.10.10)
    ifc_class / ifc_predefined_type Model families Overrides the category's default IFC class and PredefinedType within the allowed set (§2.2.2)
    visible_in_plan / show_precut_in_plan Doors, windows, … Plan representation behaviour
    maintain_annotation_orientation 3D Nested annotation stays readable when the host is rotated in elevation
    can_host_rebar Structural STR chapter
    structural_material_type, symbolic_cutback, stick_symbol_location Structural framing STR chapter
    rotate_with_component, fixed_rotation Tags and annotation Annotation behaviour
    load_classification, default_elevation, round_connector_dimension MEP MEP chapter
    lock_rotation, moves_with_nearby_elements Some categories Placement behaviour

    Data (storage). RXD document families/<id> (flags). ifc_class/ifc_predefined_type and the classification also go to IFC: the type's entity class, PredefinedType and IfcRelAssociatesClassification.

    Commands. family_doc.set_category(category) · family_doc.set_flag(flag, value) · family_doc.category_params() (opens the dialog; its OK runs the two commands above inside one transaction)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing a Generic Model family with a "Frame" subcategory to Furniture offers to move the geometry to "Furniture › Frame"; accepting creates that subcategory, and one undo restores the category and the assignments. - [ ] A furniture family with shared = on, nested in a "Desk Set" family, gives individually schedulable furniture instances in a project. With shared = off, it gives none. - [ ] Setting ifc_predefined_type = USERDEFINED with value "Kiosk" exports the type with PredefinedType=USERDEFINED and ElementType='Kiosk'.

    2.8.3 Reference planes, reference lines and stable references

    ID: DM-FED-003 · Priority: P1 (planes, lines, named references) / P0 (stable reference strings, needed by projects) · Ref: research/05 §4.3, §4.5; screenshots/platform/reporting_parameters_angles_2026.png

    Purpose. References are the skeleton of a parametric family, and the anchor points that project dimensions and constraints attach to.

    Behaviour & rules. - Reference planes have: name (used to set the work plane and as a stable reference name), is_reference, defines_origin, wall_closure (door and window templates: where host layers wrap), subcategory. - is_reference values:

    Value Project behaviour
    not_a_reference Invisible to project dimensioning and snapping
    weak Can be dimensioned. Lower priority for temporary dimensions.
    strong Highest priority for temporary dimensions and snapping in projects
    left, center_lr, right, front, center_fb, back, bottom, center_elev, top Named references. They are strong, and are preserved across type swaps and family swaps (dimensions to "Left" survive a swap to any family that also has "Left").
    • defines_origin: the three planes (one per axis) with this flag set define the insertion point. Changing them moves the geometry relative to the placement point. Placed instances keep their placement point when the family is reloaded.
    • Reference lines have two ends, and four implied work planes (two along the line, one normal at each end). They can be driven by length and angle parameters, and are used for hinged and rotating rigs. In the CME they are references for forms (§2.8.13).
    • Reference points (CME and adaptive families): free, hosted on a curve or face (parameterised by normalised length or UV), or driving (adaptive points, §2.8.13).
    • Stable reference strings. Anything outside a family or element (project dimensions, constraints, hosted elements, tags) shall refer to sub-element geometry through a stable reference string. That string is not a geometry index. Its grammar:
    stable_ref   = element_guid , "#" , ref_kind , ":" , ref_name , [ "/" , occurrence ] ;
ref_kind     = "ref"      (* named reference plane/line of a family: Left, Right, Center_LR, or a user name *)
             | "face"     (* semantic face of a system element: exterior, interior, core_exterior, core_interior, top, bottom, start, end *)
             | "edge" | "vertex"
             | "axis"     (* location line or axis *)
             | "form"     (* a face of a family form: <form-id>.<face-role> *)
             | "curve"    (* sketch curve: <curve-id>[:start|:end|:mid] *)
             | "point"    (* adaptive or reference point: <index or name> *) ;
ref_name     = name_char , { name_char } ;
occurrence   = digit , { digit } ;   (* nth occurrence, for repeated features *)

    System elements publish their semantic faces (domain chapters list them: for example, walls publish exterior, interior, core_exterior, core_interior, top, bottom, start, end, axis). Family forms publish face roles derived from the form recipe (for example an extrusion's start, end and side.<sketch-curve-id>). These do not change when topology changes, unless the recipe changes. - Reference resolution failure (for example, a named reference that is missing after a family swap) shall produce a warning. The dependent constraint or dimension is removed or detached, as §2.6.1 describes.

    Data (storage). RXD document families/<id> (references[]). Stable reference strings appear in RXD wherever references are stored.

    Commands. family_doc.reference_plane.create(p1, p2, view_id, name?, is_reference="weak") -> element_id · family_doc.reference_line.create(p1, p2, view_id?) -> element_id · family_doc.reference.set(element_id, name?, is_reference?, defines_origin?, wall_closure?) · reference.resolve(stable_ref) -> {element_id, geometry}

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A project dimension from a door's "Left" reference to a grid survives swapping the door to another door family that has a "Left" reference, and moves to the new reference position. - [ ] Moving the planes that define the origin moves the family geometry relative to placed instances' insertion points, and each instance keeps its placement point after reload.

    2.8.4 Forms: extrusion, blend, revolve, sweep, swept blend, and voids

    ID: DM-FED-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §4.4, §4.7; screenshots/platform/formula_driven_sunshade_family_2026.png

    Purpose. The five solid form types, plus their void counterparts, built from sketches and profiles.

    Workflow (example: extrusion). 1. Create › Forms › Extrusion. Set the work plane if prompted. 2. Sketch one or more closed loops (the sketch-mode contextual tab offers line, rectangle, polygon, circle, arc, spline, pick lines, pick references). Lock sketch lines to reference planes with the padlock. 3. Set Extrusion Start and End in Properties, or with shape handles. 4. Finish (✓). The form is created and can be selected. Its handles can be locked to reference planes.

    Behaviour & rules.

    Form Inputs Parameters OCCT build (indicative) IFC result
    Extrusion One work plane, one or more closed loops (nested loops become holes) start, end (along the plane normal) BRepPrimAPI_MakePrism IfcExtrudedAreaSolid
    Blend Base sketch and top sketch on parallel planes (one closed loop each), editable vertex mapping first_end, second_end, vertex connections, twist BRepOffsetAPI_ThruSections (ruled) IfcAdvancedBrep or IfcFacetedBrep
    Revolve Closed profile loop(s) plus an axis line in the same plane start_angle, end_angle BRepPrimAPI_MakeRevol IfcRevolvedAreaSolid
    Sweep Path (sketched or picked: lines, arcs, splines; open or closed; 2D in v1, 3D in CME) plus one profile (sketched, or a loaded profile family and type) profile angle, flip, horizontal/vertical offset, trajectory_segmentation, max_segment_angle BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipe / MakePipeShell IfcSurfaceCurveSweptAreaSolid / IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid, or B-rep
    Swept blend One path segment plus two profiles (one at each end) profile angles, offsets, vertex mapping BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipeShell with two sections IfcAdvancedBrep
    Void (each of the above) Same Same Same, then boolean cut Boolean result, or IfcOpeningElement when it cuts the host (§2.3.7)
    • Every form has these properties: visible (Yes/No, can be associated with a Yes/No parameter); visibility settings (§2.8.11); material (fixed, <By Category>, or associated with a Material parameter); subcategory; solid_or_void; and the extents above, each of which can be associated with parameters.
    • Voids cut the solids in the same family that they intersect, automatically. Cut Geometry and Uncut Geometry control cutting explicitly, including cutting of nested shared components. In hosted templates, a void with "Cut host" creates an opening cut in the host (§2.3.7).
    • Join Geometry inside a family merges solids for display (no seam lines) and for IFC export (one solid where the materials match).
    • Each form's sketches use the sketch model and constraints of §2.4.5.
    • Shape points display (family_doc.shape_points.toggle(), View Control Bar in family documents). Shows or hides, in the active family view, the glyphs of points that shape forms: sketch vertices of selected forms, blend vertex-mapping points, profile insertion points on sweep paths, reference points and adaptive points (with their index numbers, §2.8.13). It is view state only: not undoable, not saved in the family, and not shown in projects. It is on by default in the conceptual environment and off elsewhere. Hidden points can still be picked with Tab.
    • Other family modelling tools: Model Line, Model Text (font, size, depth, text parameter), Opening (host templates), Array (linear and radial; count can be an Integer parameter, including 0 and 1), Flip Control (an arrow that flips the instance in projects), Component (nesting, §2.8.10), Detail Component, Filled Region, Masking Region, Symbolic Line (§2.8.11).

    Data (storage). RXD document families/<id> (forms[], each with a recipe: kind, sketch IDs, path, profile reference, parameters, visibility, material, subcategory). The evaluated geometry for each type is in IFC (RepresentationMaps; §2.8.14).

    Commands. family_doc.form.extrusion(sketch, start, end, solid=true) -> element_id · family_doc.form.blend(base_sketch, top_sketch, first_end, second_end, vertex_map?, solid=true) -> element_id · family_doc.form.revolve(sketch, axis, start_angle, end_angle, solid=true) -> element_id · family_doc.form.sweep(path, profile, profile_options?, solid=true) -> element_id · family_doc.form.swept_blend(path, profile_start, profile_end, options?, solid=true) -> element_id · family_doc.form.set(element_id, props) · family_doc.geometry.cut(cutting_id, target_id) · family_doc.geometry.uncut(cutting_id, target_id) · family_doc.geometry.join(a_id, b_id) · family_doc.geometry.unjoin(a_id, b_id) · family_doc.array.create(element_ids[], kind: "linear"|"radial", count, spacing_or_angle, count_param?) -> element_id · family_doc.model_text.create(text, position, font, size, depth) -> element_id · family_doc.control.create(position, direction: "single_h"|"double_h"|"single_v"|"double_v") -> element_id · family_doc.shape_points.toggle() -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Each of the five form types and their voids can be created, locked to reference planes, flexed through parameters, and exported to IFC with the representation type listed in the table (or a valid B-rep). - [ ] A void extrusion in a wall-hosted family, marked "Cut host", cuts the host wall in the project and creates an IfcOpeningElement. - [ ] An array whose count is driven by an Integer parameter flexes through 0, 1 and 10 without errors.

    2.8.5 Dimensions, labels, locking, flexing and reporting parameters

    ID: DM-FED-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §4.5; screenshots/platform/reporting_parameters_angles_2026.png

    Purpose. Dimensions with labels turn geometry into parameters.

    Behaviour & rules. - Aligned, linear, angular, radial, diameter and arc-length dimensions can be placed between references (planes, lines, form faces, edges). - Label a dimension with an existing parameter of matching data type, or create a new parameter from the dimension. The label is shown on the dimension text ("Width = 900"). - EQ on a multi-segment dimension makes its segments equal (an equality constraint). - Lock (padlock) makes a dimension's value fixed, or locks an alignment created by Align or by sketching onto a reference. - Reporting parameters. A labelled dimension can be marked reporting. It then reads the geometry instead of driving it, and its value can be used in formulas. A reporting parameter that reads host geometry (for example host wall thickness in a wall-hosted family) is always an instance parameter. Reporting parameters cannot be given formulas. - Flexing. In the Family Types dialog (§2.8.6), Apply regenerates the family with the current values. Solver errors are reported as in §2.6.3, naming the conflicting constraints. A Flex Test command runs every type, plus optional random values in declared ranges, and reports failures. - Parameter ranges. Numeric parameters may declare min/max (a Reviera addition). Values outside the range are refused in Properties and in commands, with an error. Flex Test uses the ranges.

    Commands. family_doc.dimension.create(refs[], kind, view_id, position) -> element_id · family_doc.dimension.label(dimension_id, param_name | new_param_def) · family_doc.dimension.set_eq(dimension_id, on) · family_doc.constraint.lock(dimension_or_alignment_id, on) · family_doc.align(target_ref, moving_ref, lock=false) · family_doc.flex_test(random_samples=0) -> report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A labelled dimension marked reporting (host wall thickness) updates as the host wall type changes in the project, and drives a formula for frame depth. - [ ] Flex Test on a family with a deliberate over-constraint reports the failing type and names both conflicting constraints.

    2.8.6 Family parameters and the Family Types dialog

    ID: DM-FED-006 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §4.6, §7.1; screenshots/platform/family_types_dialog_parameter_groups.png, screenshots/platform/family_types_cabinet_variations_2026.png

    Purpose. To manage a family's parameters, types and formulas in one place.

    UI. Create › Properties › Family Types dialog: - Type name drop-down, with New, Rename, Delete and Duplicate type buttons; - a search field; - a grid grouped by parameter group (§2.9.2), with columns Parameter | Value | Formula | Lock. Instance parameters show "(default)" after the name. Formula-driven values are read-only and greyed. Reporting parameters are marked; - a toolbar: New, Edit, Delete and Duplicate parameter; Move Up/Down; Sort A–Z/Z–A; Manage Lookup Tables (§2.8.8); Add from Parameter Library (§2.9.7); Flex Test; - Apply (regenerates and flexes) and OK / Cancel.

    Workflow (dialog). 1. Create › Properties › Family Types (family_doc.types()), or double-click a label in the canvas. The dialog opens on the current type. 2. Pick or create a type, edit values and formulas, add or edit parameters. 3. Apply commits the pending edits as one transaction ("Family Types") and flexes the geometry while the dialog stays open, so the user sees the result. OK applies and closes. Cancel rolls back everything applied since the dialog opened, after a confirmation when anything was applied.

    Validation. - Values are parsed per data type and unit (§2.9.5) as they are typed. A formula is checked with formula.validate on each keystroke pause (300 ms): syntax, unknown names, unit dimension mismatch and cycles are shown under the cell, and Apply/OK are disabled while any formula is invalid. - Type names are unique within the family; empty names and names containing : are refused (: separates family and type names in IFC, §2.3.2). - Parameter names are unique within the family and must not clash with a built-in parameter of the family's category. A deleted parameter that is used in formulas, labels, associations or lookup-table calls lists those uses and is refused until they are removed. - If flexing fails (§2.6.3), Apply rolls back that step, keeps the dialog open, selects the offending type and names the conflicting constraints.

    Behaviour & rules. - Parameter Properties dialog (new or edit): kind (Family parameter or Shared parameter, chosen from the library §2.9.7); name; discipline and data type (§2.9.4); group; Type or Instance; Reporting; tooltip (up to 500 characters); min/max; IFC home (property set and property name, §2.9.2, defaulting to a set named after the family's category, for example Doors Parameters, configurable; see Q-DM-03); for Family Type parameters, the category. - Family parameters are not schedulable or taggable in projects. Shared parameters are (they carry a GUID; §2.9.7). A family parameter can be converted to shared (choosing a library definition with a matching data type), and back to family. Values and formulas are kept. - Parameters can be duplicated, which creates a copy with the suffix " (copy)". - Type parameter formulas cannot reference instance parameters. Instance parameter formulas may reference type parameters (§2.8.7). - Lock fixes a dimension-driven parameter's value during flexing of others. It applies only to dimension labels. - Type changes. New types copy the current type's values. Renaming a type in a family that is loaded in projects renames it there on reload. Deleted types are kept in projects until purged (§2.2.3).

    Commands. family_doc.param.add(def: {name, data_type, group, is_instance, shared_guid?, reporting?, tooltip?, min?, max?, ifc_home?}) -> param_id · family_doc.param.edit(param_id, changes) · family_doc.param.delete(param_id) · family_doc.param.duplicate(param_id) -> param_id · family_doc.param.to_shared(param_id, library_guid) · family_doc.param.to_family(param_id) · family_doc.param.set_formula(param_id, formula | null) · family_doc.type.create(name) -> type_id · family_doc.type.rename(type_id, name) · family_doc.type.delete(type_id) · family_doc.type.set_value(type_id, param_id, value) · family_doc.type.set_current(type_id) · family_doc.types() (opens the Family Types dialog)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Entering the formula Width + Height for an Area parameter shows a unit-dimension error under the cell and disables OK. - [ ] A family with 12 parameters in 4 groups shows them grouped as defined. Search "wid" filters to the Width parameters. - [ ] Converting a family parameter "Leaf Width" to a shared parameter keeps its formula and values, and the parameter becomes available in project schedules after reload. - [ ] Entering a value below min is refused with a message showing the allowed range.

    2.8.7 The formula language

    ID: DM-FRM-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §4.6, §7.4, §16.4

    Purpose. A small, unit-aware expression language for family parameters, global parameters and calculated values (schedules and labels; DOC chapter). It works like the reference product's formulas, with clear improvements: <=/>=, text concatenation, explicit unit rules, references to global parameters, and table lookups with interpolation.

    Behaviour & rules.

    (a) Grammar (normative).

    formula      = expression ;
expression   = concat ;
concat       = comparison , { "&" , comparison } ;              (* text concatenation *)
comparison   = additive , [ comp_op , additive ] ;              (* non-associative *)
comp_op      = "=" | "==" | "<>" | "!=" | "<" | ">" | "<=" | ">=" ;
additive     = term , { ( "+" | "-" ) , term } ;
term         = unary , { ( "*" | "/" ) , unary } ;
unary        = [ "-" | "+" ] , power ;
power        = primary , [ "^" , unary ] ;                       (* right-associative *)
primary      = quantity | text | boolean | reference | call | "(" , expression , ")" ;
quantity     = number , [ unit ] | feet_inches ;
number       = digits , [ "." , digits ] , [ exponent ] | "." , digits , [ exponent ] ;
digits       = digit , { digit } ;
exponent     = ( "e" | "E" ) , [ "+" | "-" ] , digits ;
feet_inches  = digits , "'" , [ [ "-" ] , inch_part , '"' ] ;     (* e.g. 5'  5'-6"  5' 6 1/2" *)
inch_part    = digits , [ ( " " , digits , "/" , digits ) | ( "." , digits ) ] | digits , "/" , digits ;
unit         = unit_symbol ;                                     (* from the unit catalogue §2.9.5: mm cm m km in ft ° deg rad grad m² m2 m³ m3 kg t N kN Pa kPa MPa s min h K °C W kW V A Hz lx lm cd … *)
text         = '"' , { text_char | '""' } , '"' ;
boolean      = "true" | "false" ;
reference    = [ "@" ] , ( name | "[" , bracket_name , "]" ) ;   (* "@" marks a global parameter *)
call         = function_name , "(" , [ expression , { "," , expression } ] , ")" ;
name         = name_start , { name_char } ;                      (* longest match against defined parameter names; may contain inner spaces *)
    • Formulas are locale-independent: the decimal mark is always . and the argument separator is always ,. The UI shows a hint when the user's locale uses a decimal comma.
    • Names. A reference may be written bare when it matches a defined parameter name exactly. The tokenizer tries the longest defined name at each position, so names with spaces (Frame Width) work without brackets. Names that collide with function names, units or keywords, or that contain operator characters, must be written in brackets: [Width-2], [mm]. Name matching is case-sensitive. A case-insensitive near-miss produces a "did you mean" hint.
    • Reserved words: true, false, and all function names.

    (b) Types and units. - Value types: Quantity (a number with a physical dimension, which may be dimensionless), Integer, Boolean, Text, ElementRef (material, family type, image, …). - Every quantity carries a dimension vector over (length, mass, time, current, temperature, amount, luminous intensity, angle, currency). Values are held in SI internally (§2.9.5). - +, - and comparisons require equal dimensions. * and / combine dimensions. ^ requires a dimensionless, constant exponent when the base has a dimension. The result must have integer dimension exponents (so sqrt(Area) is a Length, and sqrt(Length) is an error). - Unit literals are converted to SI at parse time: 1200 mm is 1.2 m; 30° is π/6 rad. - Unit-less literals in dimensioned contexts (compatibility rule). A bare number added to, subtracted from or compared with a dimensioned quantity is read in the project display unit for that dimension (for example Width + 50 with display unit mm means Width + 50 mm). It produces a lint warning formula.unitless_literal with a one-click fix that adds the unit. A formula whose overall result is dimensionless, assigned to a dimensioned parameter, is read in that parameter's display unit, with the same lint. This keeps formulas that users bring from other tools working, while steering them towards explicit units. - Angles. The angle is a dimension. Trigonometric functions accept angles, or dimensionless numbers read as radians. Inverse functions return angles. - Assignment. The result must match the target parameter's data type: - Integer targets round half away from zero (warning if the fraction is greater than 1e-9); - Yes/No targets need a Boolean; - Text targets accept Text, or any value formatted with the target's display format; - ElementRef targets accept only if(...) results whose branches are ElementRefs of the right kind, or references to parameters of the same kind. - Integer arithmetic. Integers promote to dimensionless quantities in arithmetic. / always gives a quantity. Use rounddown(a / b) for integer division.

    (c) Functions (normative set).

    Function Signature Notes
    if if(cond, a, b) Lazy: only the chosen branch is evaluated. a and b must have the same type and dimension.
    and, or and(b1, b2, …), or(b1, b2, …) Two or more Boolean arguments, short-circuit
    not not(b)
    abs, sign abs(x), sign(x) sign returns −1, 0 or 1 (dimensionless)
    min, max min(x1, x2, …) Same dimension
    clamp clamp(x, lo, hi)
    mod mod(a, b) Result has the sign of b. Same dimension.
    sqrt sqrt(x) Halves dimension exponents (must be even)
    exp, ln exp(x), ln(x) Dimensionless only
    log log(x) or log(x, base) Base 10 by default. Dimensionless only.
    round, roundup, rounddown round(x), round(x, increment) Half away from zero / towards +∞ / towards −∞. Without an increment, a dimensioned x rounds to whole display units (compatibility). With an increment, it rounds to multiples of the increment (same dimension).
    sin, cos, tan sin(a) Angle or radians
    asin, acos, atan asin(x) Return an angle
    atan2 atan2(y, x) Same dimension for y and x. Returns an angle.
    pi pi()
    lookup lookup(table, column, default, key1, …) Exact match (relative tolerance 1e-9). Returns default if no row matches (§2.8.8).
    lookup_nearest lookup_nearest(table, column, default, key1, …) Nearest row by normalised key distance
    lookup_interp lookup_interp(table, column, default, key) Linear interpolation on one numeric key, clamped at the ends
    size_lookup as lookup Alias accepted for compatibility
    len len(t) Character count (Unicode scalar values)
    upper, lower, trim upper(t)
    left, right, mid left(t, n), mid(t, start, n) start is 1-based
    contains contains(t, s) Boolean
    text text(x) or text(x, "format") Formats a value. Format strings: "0.00", "#,##0", or a unit spec such as "unit:mm;dp:0;symbol" (§2.9.5).
    number number(t) or number(t, unit) Parses text. Error if not numeric.
    value_in value_in(x, unit) The number of units in x, dimensionless (for example value_in(Width, mm))
    count_true count_true(b1, b2, …) Integer count of true values

    (d) Scope and evaluation. - Family formulas may reference parameters of the same family, and global parameters with @Name. Global references are resolved in the project the family is loaded into. In the family document, and in projects without that global, the default value declared in the family is used. That default is part of the parameter's "global input" declaration. This is a Reviera extension (P2). - Type parameter formulas may reference only type parameters (and globals). Instance parameter formulas may reference type and instance parameters. - Global parameter formulas may reference other global parameters (P1) and the project information parameters (P2). - Formulas are compiled once into a typed expression tree with constant folding. They are evaluated in Rust, not in Lua, for speed and determinism. Evaluation order follows the dependency graph (§2.6.2). Cycles are rejected. - Errors (unknown name, type or dimension mismatch, division by zero, a table not found, a function argument out of domain) mark the parameter as in error. The error message includes the character position. A family that has formula errors cannot be loaded into a project.

    (e) Examples (informative).

    Leaf Width          = Width - 2 * Frame Width
Handle Height       = clamp(Height * 0.45, 900 mm, 1100 mm)
Number of Panels    = rounddown(Width / 600 mm)
Is Wide             = Width >= 1200 mm
Description Text    = "Door " & text(Width, "unit:mm;dp:0") & " x " & text(Height, "unit:mm;dp:0")
Fin Angle           = if(@Orientation = "South", 35°, 15°)
Elbow Radius        = lookup_interp(ElbowRadii, "Radius", 1.5 * Diameter, Diameter)

    Commands. formula.validate(context_id, param_id | null, text) -> {ok, type, dimension, errors[], lints[]} · formula.evaluate(context_id, text) -> value (evaluates without storing)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] The parser accepts every example in (e), and a conformance test suite of at least 300 cases covering each grammar rule and function (with expected values or errors). - [ ] Width + 50, with display units in mm, evaluates as Width + 0.05 m and produces the formula.unitless_literal lint. The quick-fix rewrites it to Width + 50 mm. - [ ] sqrt(Length) is rejected with a dimension error that points at character 1. - [ ] A type formula referencing an instance parameter is rejected with a message that names both parameters. - [ ] Formula results are identical on all supported platforms (bit-exact for +, −, ×, ÷ and sqrt; within 1 ulp for transcendental functions, using a portable libm).

    2.8.8 Lookup tables

    ID: DM-LUT-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §4.6

    Purpose. To drive parameters from tabular data (for example fitting dimensions by nominal size), embedded in the family.

    UI. Family Types › Manage Lookup Tables: a list of tables, with Import, Export, Rename, Delete and an embedded grid editor (edit cells, add and remove rows and columns, check types).

    Behaviour & rules. - Tables are embedded in the family. Files are only used for import and export. - Reviera table format (CSV, RFC 4180, UTF-8, , separator, . decimal mark): - The first header cell is the row label (it is not used for lookup). - Every other header cell is ColumnName[spec] or ColumnName[spec:unit], where spec is a data-type key from §2.9.4 (length, area, angle, number, integer, text, yes_no, …) and unit is a unit key from §2.9.5 (default: SI). - Each data row has a label, then one value per column, in the declared unit. Empty cells are null.

    Label,ND[length:mm],Radius[length:mm],Socket Depth[length:mm],Material[text]
DN15,15,22.5,16,Copper
DN20,20,30,19,Copper
DN25,25,37.5,22,Copper
    • Import also accepts the widely used Name##spec##unit header style, so tables can be migrated from other tools. Unknown spec or unit tokens produce a mapping dialog.
    • Lookup semantics are defined by the lookup* functions (§2.8.7). Key columns are matched by the order of the key arguments. If a table has duplicate keys, the first matching row wins, and a warning is shown on import.
    • Size limit: 100,000 rows × 64 columns per table (bigger tables are refused, with a message).

    Data (storage). RXD document families/<id> (lookup_tables[], in a typed, columnar form). Very large tables may be RXD assets (02a).

    Commands. family_doc.lookup_table.import(path, name?) -> table_id · family_doc.lookup_table.export(table_id, path) · family_doc.lookup_table.rename(table_id, name) · family_doc.lookup_table.delete(table_id) · family_doc.lookup_table.set_cell(table_id, row, column, value)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Importing the example table and using lookup(Pipes, "Radius", 0 mm, ND) gives 30 mm when ND = 20 mm. - [ ] Exporting and re-importing a table gives byte-identical CSV (except line endings, which are normalised to LF). - [ ] A Name##length##millimeters header imports with the right spec and unit.

    2.8.9 Type catalogs

    ID: DM-TCAT-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §4.6, §11.1

    Purpose. Families with hundreds of sizes (for example steel sections) are loaded with only the types that a project needs.

    Behaviour & rules. - A family package may contain many types (as IFC types). When it holds more than a threshold (default 20 types), or has a companion type catalog, loading it shows the Specify Types dialog: a table of types with sortable, filterable parameter columns and multi-select. Only the selected types are copied into the project. - Companion type catalog (optional, for families whose types are defined as data rather than in the package): a CSV file with the same base name as the family package plus .types.csv (for example HEA.family.ifc + HEA.types.csv). It uses the header grammar of §2.8.8, with the first column being the type name. Each row becomes a type. Its values override the family defaults for the listed parameters. - Reload with a catalog keeps the types already in the project and offers to add more. - Export Family Types: writes the family's current types to a catalog file. - Import Family Types (Insert › Import › Import Family Types; family.import_types(family_id?, path)) creates types from a catalogue file for a family that is already in the document, without reloading the family package. - In a family document family_id is omitted: the rows become types of the open family (family_doc.type.create plus family_doc.type.set_value for each value). - In a project, family_id names a loaded family. The command first opens the Specify Types dialog on the catalogue rows so the user can pick which rows to import; through Lua and MCP all rows are imported unless the call is preceded by family.list_types and a filtered catalogue. - The family is identified by the user's pick or, when family_id is omitted in a project, by the catalogue's base name matching a loaded family name; no match fails with family.not_found. - A row whose type name already exists asks Overwrite values, Skip or Import as "<name> (2)" (one choice for all, or per row). Through commands the default is Skip, and the result lists skipped rows. - Columns are matched to family parameters by name, then by shared GUID when the header carries one (§2.8.8). Unknown columns, values that fail unit parsing, and values outside a parameter's min/max are reported per row and cell; the row is still imported with those cells left at the family default. - Formula-driven and reporting parameters cannot be set from a catalogue; such columns are reported and ignored. - The whole import is one transaction ("Import Family Types"); its report lists created, overwritten, skipped and failed rows. - Both the Reviera .types.csv grammar and the reference product's catalogue header grammar (Name##LENGTH##MILLIMETERS style) are accepted on import, so existing catalogues can be reused.

    Commands. family.list_types(path) -> [{type_name, values}] (reads a package or catalog without loading it) · family.load(path, type_names[]) (see §2.2.3) · family.export_types(family_id, path) · family.import_types(family_id?, path) -> type_id[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A package with 400 types loads in under 2 s when 3 types are selected, and the project then contains only those 3 types. - [ ] A type catalog with a column that is not a parameter of the family reports that column and ignores it. - [ ] Importing a 10-row catalogue into a loaded "HEA" family whose project already has 2 of those types creates 8 types, skips 2 (by default), and one undo removes all 8. - [ ] A catalogue written with the reference product's ##-typed header imports into a Reviera family with the same values (within unit-conversion tolerance).

    2.8.10 Nested and shared nested families

    ID: DM-NEST-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §4.10

    Purpose. Families built from other families: door hardware, casework assemblies, curtain panels with doors, tags with symbols.

    Behaviour & rules. - Nesting. Component places an instance of a loaded family inside the family document. The nested family's definition is embedded in the parent. - Associated parameters. Any parameter of a nested instance (or nested type) can be associated with a parent parameter of the same data type, with the "=" button in Properties. The child's value then follows the parent's. Associations are type-to-type, or instance-to-instance/type. - Family Type parameters. A parent parameter of data type Family Type (§2.9.4), restricted to a category, can drive which nested type is used. In projects, users can swap the nested type through that parameter. The candidates are the nested family's types and, optionally, all loaded families of that category. - Shared nested families. If the child has shared = on (§2.8.2): - in projects, nested instances become real elements: selectable with Tab, taggable, schedulable, and with their own GUID; - in IFC they are separate occurrences, aggregated by the parent occurrence through IfcRelAggregates (§2.3.9), and typed by their own IfcTypeObject; - their GUIDs are stable across regeneration: each shared nested instance's GUID is derived deterministically, as UUID v5 of (parent GUID, nested-instance path). The same parent therefore always gets the same nested GUIDs, even after reload; - when a shared nested family is already loaded in the project with the same family GUID, loading asks Use project version or Use version from family. - Non-shared nested families are merged into the parent's geometry. In IFC they appear as part of the parent type's RepresentationMap (as IfcMappedItems of the child type's maps). - Nesting depth limit: 8 levels. Recursive nesting (a family nesting itself, directly or indirectly) is refused.

    Data (storage). RXD document families/<id> (nested[]: child family GUID, type or Family Type parameter, placement, associations, visibility). The child's own definition is a separate families/<child-guid> document.

    Commands. family_doc.component.place(family_id, type_id, placement) -> element_id · family_doc.param.associate(nested_element_id, child_param, parent_param_id | null)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A shared nested chair in a "Table and Chairs" family schedules as 4 chairs per table in a project. Their GUIDs are unchanged after reloading the family. - [ ] A Family Type parameter "Handle Type" lets a project user swap the nested handle on a door type, and the change exports as a different nested type.

    2.8.11 Visibility, detail levels, symbolic geometry and materials in families

    ID: DM-FED-007 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §4.7, §4.8

    Behaviour & rules. - Visibility settings of each form, model line, nested component, filled region and symbolic line: - Detail levels: Coarse, Medium, Fine (any combination); - View directions: Plan/RCP; Front/Back; Left/Right (for 3D families); - Only when cut in plan or section. - Visible may be bound to a Yes/No parameter (for example "Show Handle"). - Symbolic lines and 2D elements in 3D families appear only in views parallel to the plane they were drawn in. They are used for door swings and plan-only symbols. - Draw order of 2D elements in 3D families is controllable (bring to front, send to back). - Plan pre-cut behaviour comes from the family flags (§2.8.2). - Preview Visibility (View Control Bar in family documents; family_doc.preview_visibility.toggle(view_id?)). When on, the family view draws only what a project view of the same kind, direction and detail level would show: elements hidden by their visibility settings, symbolic lines drawn in other planes, and visible parameters that are false for the current type are hidden; elements that would be cut only when cut are drawn as cut. A banner shows "Preview visibility: on". It is view state only, not undoable and not saved; elements hidden by it cannot be selected until it is turned off. The default is off. - Materials. A form's material can be fixed, <By Category>, or bound to a Material parameter (type or instance). When a family is loaded, the materials it uses are copied into the project. If a project material with the same name exists, the project's version wins, unless the user chose Overwrite parameter values on load. - IFC: the visibility and detail-level variants are written as in §2.3.10. Plan symbolic geometry goes in the type's plan Annotation representation map.

    Commands. family_doc.visibility.set(element_ids[], {coarse, medium, fine, plan, front_back, left_right, only_when_cut, visible_param?}) · family_doc.draw_order(element_ids[], "front"|"back"|"forward"|"backward") · family_doc.preview_visibility.toggle(view_id?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A door family whose panel is visible only at Medium and Fine, and whose swing symbolic line is in Plan only, shows the correct geometry at all three detail levels in a project plan and elevation. - [ ] With Preview Visibility on in the family's Ref. Level plan at Coarse, the same door shows exactly what a Coarse project plan shows, and turning it off shows all elements again.

    2.8.12 Special family kinds

    ID: DM-FSPEC-001 … 006 · Priority: see table · Ref: research/05 §5.1–§5.8; screenshots/platform/edit_label_dialog_2026.png

    ID Kind Priority Requirements
    DM-FSPEC-001 Annotation families: tags and symbols P0 (shipped tag families, used as is) / P1 (editing) 2D families with lines, filled regions, text and labels. A label binds text to one or more parameters, each with prefix, suffix, sample value, spaces before it, line break after it, and optional unit-format override. Labels may contain calculated values (formulas, §2.8.7, over the tagged element's parameters). Tag families have a target category. Multi-category tags read shared and built-in common parameters from any category, and can be the default tag for Tag by Category and Tag All Not Tagged. Families set rotate-with-component and fixed-rotation flags. Leader behaviour is defined in DOC. Edit Label dialog: category parameters on the left; label parameters (Spaces, Prefix, Sample Value, Suffix, Break) on the right.
    DM-FSPEC-002 Title block families P0 (shipped title blocks) / P1 (editing) Sheet-size templates. They contain border lines, images (logos, RXD assets) and labels bound to Sheet, Sheet Collection and Project Information parameters (including shared parameters). They can have an embedded revision schedule (DOC), several types, and Yes/No-driven visibility. A type property overrides the "As indicated" scale text. Title-block parameters are available to sheet list schedules (DOC).
    DM-FSPEC-003 Profile families P1 2D closed loops used by sweeps, wall sweeps and reveals, slab edges, fascias, gutters, railings, mullions (several loops allowed), stair nosings and custom structural sections. Profiles may have types and parameters. Loops must be closed, non-self-intersecting and drawn in the template's single plane; open or crossing loops are refused on save with the offending curves highlighted. The template's origin is the insertion point used by hosts. A profile usage type parameter (generic, mullion, rail, nosing, reveal, slab edge) filters which tools list the profile. In IFC, a profile type used by a profiled element becomes an IfcArbitraryClosedProfileDef (or IfcArbitraryProfileDefWithVoids) referenced from IfcMaterialProfile.
    DM-FSPEC-004 Detail item families P1 2D, category Detail Items, placed in views. Contents: detail lines, filled and masking regions, text, labels and nested detail items, with types and parameters. Line-based detail items stretch between two picked points and support repeating details (DOC). Draw order inside the family and against other view elements is kept (§2.8.11). Detail items can be tagged, keynoted and scheduled. They never appear in 3D or in IFC exchange exports. Storage: RXD documents (families/… for the definition; views/annotation/<viewId> for placed instances).
    DM-FSPEC-005 MEP connectors P1 Connector elements in families: duct, pipe, cable tray, conduit and electrical. Each has system classification, shape (round, rectangular, oval), size linked to parameters, flow configuration (calculated, preset, system), flow direction (in, out, bidirectional), loss method, and electrical properties (voltage, poles, apparent load, power factor). One connector may be primary. Connectors can be linked for pass-through flow. In IFC: IfcDistributionPort nested in the type (IfcRelNests) with FlowDirection, PredefinedType and SystemType, plus Pset_DistributionPortCommon and the port-type psets. The detailed behaviour is in the MEP chapter.
    DM-FSPEC-006 Mass families P2 Built in the CME (§2.8.13), as loadable families or in-place masses. In projects: Show Mass toggle, mass floors by level (one per selected level that cuts the mass), gross floor area, volume and surface area reported as read-only parameters, and by-face creation of walls, floors, roofs and curtain systems, with Update to Face (ARC chapter). Masses are hidden in views unless shown, and are excluded from exchange exports by default (§2.11.4). Mass floor areas feed area schedules and energy analysis (ANA).

    Commands. family_doc.label.create(position, params[{param, prefix?, suffix?, sample?, spaces?, break?}], text_type_id) -> element_id · family_doc.label.edit(label_id, params[]) · family_doc.connector.create(kind, face_ref | work_plane, props) -> element_id · family_doc.connector.set(connector_id, props)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A door tag family with a label "Mark" plus a calculated value text(Width, "unit:mm;dp:0") & "x" & text(Height, "unit:mm;dp:0") shows "D-104" and "915x2134" for a tagged door. - [ ] A title block label bound to a shared project-information parameter "Client Reference" shows the project's value on every sheet. - [ ] A pipe elbow family with two pipe connectors linked to a "Nominal Diameter" parameter exports two IfcDistributionPorts nested in its type.

    2.8.13 Adaptive components and the conceptual massing environment (CME)

    ID: DM-CME-001 … 005 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/05 §5.5, §5.6, §6; screenshots/platform/adaptive_component_repetition_2026.png, screenshots/platform/conceptual_divided_surface_patterned_2026.png, screenshots/platform/conceptual_uv_grid_2026.png

    Purpose. A 3D-first environment for masses, adaptive components and pattern-based panels, used for façades, trusses and complex repeated geometry.

    DM-CME-001 — Conceptual environment

    • Uses 3D levels and work planes, reference points (free, hosted on curves or faces, driving), a 3D snapping system, a 3D move gizmo (drag along or across axes) and X-Ray mode (shows the form's profiles, path and edges).
    • Create Form (solid or void) from selected curves and references. It infers the form type:
    • one closed profile → extrusion (one open profile → surface);
    • two or more profiles on non-intersecting planes → loft;
    • profile + path → sweep;
    • profile + line in the same plane → revolve;
    • several profiles along a path → swept blend. If several results are possible, a chooser appears (thumbnails of the options).
    • Direct editing: push and pull faces, edges and vertices with the gizmo. Add Edge, Add Profile, Dissolve (back to profiles), Rebuild.
    • Forms are either reference-based (driven by references and parameters) or unconstrained (directly editable).
    • OCCT: lofts use BRepOffsetAPI_ThruSections (smooth); sweeps use BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipeShell; surfaces use BRepFill/GeomFill. IFC: IfcAdvancedBrep (B-spline surfaces); IfcTriangulatedFaceSet as a fallback.
    • Workflow. (1) Create a family from the Mass, Generic Model Adaptive or pattern-based template; the document opens in a 3D view with two reference planes and a level. (2) Draw model or reference lines on a work plane or on 3D levels, or place reference points. (3) Select curves and choose Create Form › Solid or Void. (4) Edit the result with the gizmo, or add profiles and edges. (5) Flex parameters in Family Types (§2.8.6) and load into a project.
    • Work planes in 3D. Clicking on a face, level or reference plane makes it the active work plane for the next sketch (Set work plane automatically, default on). Reference points host their own three work planes. The 3D snapping set adds face, edge, point-on-curve and mid-point snaps.
    • Model lines vs reference lines. Forms built on model lines consume them (the lines become form edges). Forms built on reference lines stay driven by them, so moving the reference line or changing a parameter on it reshapes the form.
    • Edge cases. Self-intersecting or zero-area profiles are refused with the curve highlighted. A loft whose profiles have different vertex counts uses automatic vertex matching, which the user can edit in X-Ray. A form that fails to rebuild after a parameter change keeps its last valid shape and raises a warning naming the failing step (§2.7.4).
    • Data. RXD document families/<id> (forms[] with kind cme_form, the referenced curves and points, and whether each form is reference-based or unconstrained); evaluated geometry per type in IFC as in §2.8.14.
    • Acceptance. Moving a reference line that drives a loft reshapes the loft in the same transaction; deleting a model line used by a form is refused with a message naming the form.

    DM-CME-002 — Divided surfaces and paths

    • Divide Surface creates a UV grid on a face. Each direction is set by number, or by distance (with justification, grid rotation and belt offset). Alternatively, the surface is divided by intersecting references (levels, reference planes, lines), and the Face Manager edits which references are used.
    • Divide Path places nodes along curves (by number, distance, or intersections).
    • Surface representation controls show and hide the original surface, nodes, U/V grid lines, pattern lines and pattern fill.

    DM-CME-003 — Patterns and pattern-based panels

    • Built-in patterns for divided surfaces: Rectangle, Rectangle Checkerboard, 1/2 Step, 1/3 Step, Arrows, Hexagon, Octagon, Octagon Rotate, Rhomboid, Rhomboid Checkerboard, Triangle (bent and flat), Triangle Checkerboard (bent and flat), Zigzag.
    • Pattern-based panel families (template Curtain Panel Pattern-Based) define a tile with adaptive corner points. Applied to a divided surface, they populate each tile, adapting to the node positions. Border tiles: Partial, Overhanging, Empty (per surface).

    DM-CME-004 — Adaptive components

    • Family template Generic Model Adaptive. Reference points can be made adaptive: they are numbered placement points, plus optional shape handle points. Geometry is built between them from reference lines and forms. Orientation options for each point: global, host, instance, and their combinations.
    • Placement: the user clicks N points in a project, on a divided-surface node, on a divided-path node or on any surface. The instance adapts to them. The command form is instance.place_adaptive (§2.2.5).
    • Repeat distributes an adaptive component across a divided path or a surface node grid, following the pattern of the first placement. The repeater is one element with a repeater type.
    • In IFC, each placed adaptive instance is an occurrence with its own representation (geometry is unique per placement). Its adaptive point positions are RXD element data (adaptive).

    DM-CME-005 — Masses in projects

    • See DM-FSPEC-006. Energy-analysis use of masses is in the ANA chapter.

    Commands. cme.form.create(curve_refs[], solid=true, choice?) -> element_id · cme.form.push_pull(subelement_ref, vector) · cme.form.add_edge(face_ref, p1, p2) · cme.form.add_profile(form_id, parameter) · cme.form.dissolve(form_id) · cme.divide_surface(face_ref, {u, v} | {references[]}) -> element_id · cme.divide_path(curve_refs[], spec) -> element_id · cme.surface.set_pattern(divided_surface_id, pattern, border_tiles?) · cme.surface.apply_component(divided_surface_id, panel_type_id) · cme.point.create(position | host_ref, adaptive=false) -> element_id · cme.point.make_adaptive(point_id, index?) · cme.repeat(adaptive_instance_id) -> element_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A loft created from three closed profiles on parallel planes can be dissolved back to the profiles and re-formed with the same result. - [ ] A curved façade divided 20 × 10 and populated with a 4-point adaptive panel produces 200 panels that follow the surface when its control profile moves. - [ ] A 2-point adaptive beam repeated along a 50-node divided path creates 49 instances, and these export to IFC as occurrences with unique geometry.

    2.8.14 Family package file format

    ID: DM-FFMT-001 · Priority: P0 (reading packages for placement) / P1 (writing from the Family Editor) · Ref: research/05 §4.9, §11.1, §16.9; TECH_STACK §3.1; spec/02a_extension_data_format.md

    Purpose. Families are stored as IFC type libraries, so that any IFC tool can use a family's types and geometry, while Reviera keeps the full parametric definition as RXD.

    Behaviour & rules. - A family package is a valid IFC4 file (IFC4X3 optional, matching the target project schema). Recommended names: <Family>.family.ifc for one family, <Library>.library.ifc for a collection, <Name>.familytemplate.ifc for templates. .ifczip is allowed. - IFC content. The package shall contain: 1. one IfcProject (Name = the family or library name), with SI units and the representation contexts of §2.3.1. It contains no spatial structure, and no occurrences except as noted below; 2. one IfcProjectLibrary per family (the primary family, plus every nested family it needs), declared by the project with IfcRelDeclares; 3. each family's types, as IfcTypeObject subtypes declared by the family's library with IfcRelDeclares. Each type carries: - its type-parameter values as property sets (§2.3.3); - its evaluated geometry for that type's values: RepresentationMaps for Body (Fine, plus Body-Coarse/Body-Medium when different), Axis, FootPrint, plan Annotation; - its material assignments: IfcMaterialLayerSet, IfcMaterialProfileSet or IfcMaterialConstituentSet; - its ports (IfcDistributionPort, nested) for MEP families; - its classification (IfcRelAssociatesClassification); 4. every IfcMaterial used, with its properties and styles (§2.10.5); 5. for annotation, title block, detail and profile families, which have no IFC type class: no IFC types. Their whole definition is RXD. - RXD content (carried as 02a defines; logical content only here): - an RXD document families/<id>/package (the package manifest): - package format version and minimum Reviera version; - the primary family GUID and the list of contained families; - the template flag and the source template GUID; - a preview image (RXD asset, PNG, 512 × 512); - author, licence (an SPDX expression, optional for content but recommended), description and keywords; - one RXD document families/<id> per family, holding: name, category, template, placement_mode, flags (§2.8.2), parameters[] (§2.8.6, with formulas), types[] (name, values, link to the IFC type GUID), references[] (§2.8.3), sketches[], forms[] (§2.8.4), dimensions[] and constraints[] (§2.8.5), symbolic[] (2D elements with view orientation), nested[] (§2.8.10), arrays[], controls[], connectors[], labels[] (annotation families), lookup_tables[] (§2.8.8), adaptive_points[], divided_surfaces[] (CME), subcategories[], views[] (family views and their settings). - Informative skeleton of families/<family-guid>:

    {
  "schema": "reviera.family", "schema_version": "1.0.0",
  "guid": "3vB2…", "name": "Single-Flush Door", "category": "cat.doors",
  "template": "door", "placement_mode": "wall_hosted",
  "flags": { "shared": false, "room_calculation_point": true, "ifc_predefined_type": "DOOR" },
  "parameters": [
    { "id": "p1", "name": "Width",  "data_type": "length", "group": "dimensions", "instance": false,
      "ifc_home": ["Pset_DoorCommon", null], "attribute": "OverallWidth" },
    { "id": "p2", "name": "Frame Width", "data_type": "length", "group": "construction", "instance": false },
    { "id": "p3", "name": "Leaf Width", "data_type": "length", "group": "dimensions", "instance": false,
      "formula": "Width - 2 * Frame Width" }
  ],
  "types": [ { "name": "0915 x 2134", "ifc_type": "1xH4…", "values": { "p1": 0.915, "p2": 0.05 } } ],
  "references": [ { "id": "r1", "name": "Left", "is_reference": "left", "plane": { "origin": [-0.4575,0,0], "normal": [1,0,0] } } ],
  "forms": [ { "id": "f1", "kind": "extrusion", "sketch": "s1", "start": 0, "end": { "param": "p5" },
               "material": { "param": "p9" }, "subcategory": "Panel",
               "visibility": { "coarse": false, "medium": true, "fine": true } } ],
  "nested": [], "lookup_tables": [], "connectors": []
}
    • Consistency rule. On save, the IFC types and their geometry shall be regenerated from the RXD definition, so the two always agree. On load, if the RXD is missing (for example, the package was re-saved by a tool that strips unknown property sets), the family loads as a static family. Its types and geometry are usable, but parametric editing is unavailable, and the user is told why.
    • Third-party type libraries. Any IFC file whose IfcProject declares an IfcProjectLibrary with types (or declares types directly) can be loaded as static families, one family per library, or per type class when there is no library.
    • Embedding. Inside a project, an embedded family is exactly the same content: an IfcProjectLibrary + types in the project's IFC, plus the families/<guid> RXD document. Save Family As writes a package from it unchanged.
    • Versioning. Each family has a family_version (semver) that increases on every save from the Family Editor. On load, Reviera compares family GUID and version (§2.2.3).

    Commands. family.package.inspect(path) -> {families[], types[], has_rxd, version, licence} · plus family.load, family.save_as (§2.2.3) and family_doc.save (§2.8.0).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A family package saved by Reviera passes IFC4 schema validation. It opens in at least two other open-source IFC tools (for example IfcOpenShell-based Bonsai, and one web viewer), which show its types with correct geometry and property values. - [ ] Re-saving a package through a tool that strips unknown property sets, then loading it, gives a static family with all types, and the user is told that parametric editing is unavailable. - [ ] Save Family As from a project, followed by loading into a new project, gives types and instances that match the original exactly (the same geometry hashes).

    2.8.15 Library browser

    ID: DM-LIB-001 · Priority: P1 (local folders) / P2 (organisation libraries over HTTPS or git) · Ref: research/05 §4.9 (load family, content library), §11.1, §16.2; spec/01 (Insert › Load from Library)

    Purpose. Find, inspect and load families and types from local folders and from organisation libraries without knowing file paths. It is the open counterpart of a vendor cloud content library.

    Workflow. 1. Insert › Load from Library › Browse Library (library.browse(query?, source?)), or Load Family… › Browse library in the file dialog. The Library panel opens docked to the right (it can float). 2. Pick a source in the tree, or search across all sources. Narrow the results with filters. 3. Select a result. The preview pane shows the family, its types and its key parameters. 4. Choose Load (opens Specify Types when the family has many types, §2.8.9), Load and Place (loads, then starts placement with the chosen type), or Open (opens the package in the Family Editor; not available for read-only sources unless saved as a copy).

    UI. - Sources tree: Reviera Library (shipped content), My Libraries (user folders), Organisation (configured remote libraries and network folders), Favourites, Recently loaded.
