Each source shows its state (indexed, indexing n %, offline, error). - Search box with free text over name, type names, category, keywords and description; filters for category, placement mode (§2.8.1), IFC class, discipline, licence, author or publisher, and "has types matching" (for example Width >= 900 mm, using the collector's operators, §2.13.3). - Results as a thumbnail grid or a list (Name, Category, Types, Source, Version, Licence, Modified), sortable, with the count of matches. - Preview pane: an interactive 3D preview (orbit, zoom; plan and front views for 2D families) rendered locally from the package geometry; the type list with each type's values for up to 8 key parameters chosen by the family's author (default: the dimension group); the licence (SPDX), author, version and description from the package manifest (§2.8.14); and warnings (for example "Static family: no parametric data", "Requires Reviera 1.3"). - Context menu: Add to / Remove from Favourites, Show in folder, Copy path or URL, Properties.

    Behaviour & rules. - Indexing. Each source is indexed in the background into a per-user cache (<cache_dir>/reviera/library-index.sqlite). The index stores, per family: package path or URL, content hash, family GUID and version, name, category, placement mode, type names and key values, keywords, licence and the 512 × 512 preview image from the manifest. Re-indexing is incremental by modification time and hash. A 10,000-family folder indexes once and is searchable within 200 ms per query afterwards. - Library files. A <Library>.library.ifc holding several families shows one result per family. Third-party IFC type libraries are indexed as static families (§2.8.14) and marked so. - Organisation libraries (P2). A remote library is a static JSON index (reviera.library-index, version 1) at an HTTPS URL or in a git repository: one entry per package with URL, SHA-256, family GUID, version, licence and preview URL. Packages are downloaded on demand into the cache and verified against the checksum; a mismatch is refused. Sources can be pre-configured by an administrator policy file, and those cannot be removed by the user. No vendor service is needed. - Duplicates. When the same family GUID appears in several sources, results group them and show the highest version first; the user can pick another version. - Loading uses family.load (§2.2.3) with its reload rules: if the family is already in the project, the comparison of GUID and version is shown before loading. - Licence display. Packages without a licence are shown with "Licence not stated". A package whose licence forbids redistribution is still loadable for private use, but a notice is shown once per package. - Offline. Cached remote packages remain loadable offline; uncached ones are listed but greyed.

    Data (storage). No model data. Sources, favourites and the index are per-user application data (UI chapter, preferences). Loaded families are embedded as usual (§2.2.3). The source URL and package hash are recorded in families/index so Reload from library can find a newer version.

    Commands. library.browse(query?, source?) (opens the panel) · library.search(text?, filters?, source?, limit=100) -> library_item[] · library.source.add(path_or_url, name?) -> source_id · library.source.remove(source_id) · library.refresh(source_id?) · library.load(item_ref, type_names?, place=false) -> family_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Adding a local folder of 2,000 family packages indexes it in the background without blocking editing; a search for "door 900" then returns matching door families within 200 ms. - [ ] Selecting a result shows a rotatable 3D preview and its types without loading the family into the project (the model version is unchanged). - [ ] A remote library whose package checksum does not match its index entry is refused with an error naming the package, and nothing is loaded. - [ ] Load and Place on a door with 30 types opens Specify Types, then starts door placement with the chosen type.

    2.9 Parameters and units

    2.9.1 Kinds of parameters

    ID: DM-PARAM-001 · Priority: P0 (built-in, project) / P1 (family, shared, global) · Ref: research/05 §7.1, §7.6

    Purpose. Parameters carry all element data. This section defines their kinds and how each kind is identified.

    Behaviour & rules.

    Kind Defined in Identity Schedulable / taggable Typical use
    Built-in The application's parameter registry Stable key (for example wall.base_offset) with a negative internal ID Mostly yes Mark, Comments, Level, Base Offset, Area, Volume, Fire Rating
    Family A family definition Name, unique within the family No Driving geometry and formulas inside a family
    Shared A parameter library (§2.9.7) GUID Yes, including tags and title blocks Firm-wide data fields used in families and projects
    Project The project, bound to categories Name (if local) or GUID (if shared) Schedules yes. Tags only if shared. Project-specific data on many categories
    Global The project GUID of the global parameter Not directly (they can be shown through calculated values) Driving dimensions and values project-wide
    Key schedule A key schedule (DOC) Name Yes Pick-list values that set several parameters at once
    IFC-native A third-party IFC file (Pset name, property name) Yes Properties Reviera found in imported files that do not match any definition
    • Every parameter value is either a type value (stored on the type) or an instance value (stored on the instance). The definition's binding decides which (§2.9.3). It is never both.
    • Read-only computed parameters (Area, Volume, Length, Perimeter, Count, Host, Room) are produced by regeneration. They are shown greyed out, and commands that try to set them fail with a clear error.
    • IFC-native parameters. When Reviera opens an IFC file, every property that does not match a built-in, shared or project definition becomes an IFC-native parameter. It is shown in Properties under its property-set name, can be edited and scheduled, and is written back to the same property set. The user can promote one to a project or shared parameter. Promotion keeps the values and adds a definition.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A third-party IFC file with a custom property set ACME_Asset (property AssetTag) shows AssetTag in Properties and in the schedule field list. Edits are written back to ACME_Asset.AssetTag.

    2.9.2 Parameter definitions

    ID: DM-PARAM-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §7.1, §7.7, §16.3

    Purpose. Parameter definitions are first-class objects with a fixed set of fields.

    Behaviour & rules. A parameter definition shall have these fields:

    Field Meaning
    id Internal ID
    guid Required for shared, global and project parameters. Built-in parameters use their key.
    name Display name (unique among the definitions bound to a category)
    data_type A data-type key (§2.9.4), for example length, yes_no, family_type:cat.doors
    group A parameter group key (below)
    discipline common, structural, hvac, electrical, piping, energy, infrastructure
    tooltip Up to 500 characters
    visible Hidden parameters are kept but not shown (for add-in use)
    user_modifiable If false, only code can change values
    hide_when_no_value Hidden in Properties when empty
    min / max Optional range (numeric types)
    enum Optional allowed-values list (text and integer types). Written to IFC as IfcPropertyEnumeration.
    ifc_home Property-set name and property name (and, for built-in parameters, an IFC attribute) used to store the value (§2.3.3)
    formula Family and global parameters only
    reporting Family and global parameters only
    • Parameter groups (the "group under" list; keys are stable and display names are localisable): analysis_results, analytical_model, constraints, construction, data, dimensions, division_geometry, electrical, electrical_circuiting, electrical_lighting, electrical_loads, electrical_analysis, energy_analysis, fire_protection, forces, general, graphics, green_building, identity_data, ifc_parameters, layers, materials_and_finishes, mechanical, mechanical_flow, mechanical_loads, model_properties, moments, other, phasing, photometrics, plumbing, primary_end, rebar_set, releases_member_forces, secondary_end, segments_and_fittings, set, slab_shape_edit, structural, structural_analysis, text, title_text, visibility, carbon (Reviera addition).
    • Default IFC home for user parameters: a property set named by the binding's configured property-set name. The default is <Project or Library name> Parameters, for example "ACME Parameters". Parameters may be given a specific property set name and property name, so that they map onto a buildingSMART property (for example a shared parameter "Acoustic Rating" mapped to Pset_WallCommon.AcousticRating for walls and Pset_DoorCommon.AcousticRating for doors). The IFC home can differ per bound category.
    • No collisions. Built-in parameters keep their established names and their IFC homes (for example built-in Fire Rating owns Pset_<Class>Common.FireRating). A user parameter may not take a built-in's name for a bound category (§2.9.3), and may not be mapped onto an IFC home that a built-in or another parameter already uses for that category (param.home_clash). User parameters that map onto a standard property are named after that property, as above.
    • Built-in parameter registry. The application ships a registry of built-in parameters: key, name, data type, group, the categories it applies to, type/instance, read-only flag and IFC home. Domain chapters add rows. Examples:
    Key Name Data type Type/Instance IFC home
    elem.mark Mark text Instance IfcElement.Tag
    elem.comments Comments text Instance group-named set Identity Data.Comments (§2.3.3)
    type.type_mark Type Mark text Type IfcTypeProduct.Tag
    type.description Description text Type IfcRoot.Description (type)
    type.fire_rating Fire Rating text Type Pset_<Class>Common.FireRating
    type.manufacturer Manufacturer text Type Pset_ManufacturerTypeInformation.Manufacturer
    type.model Model text Type Pset_ManufacturerTypeInformation.ModelLabel
    type.cost Cost currency Type Identity Data.Cost (IfcMonetaryMeasure)
    type.classification_code Classification Code text Type IfcClassificationReference.Identification
    type.keynote Keynote text Type Identity Data.Keynote
    elem.level Level element:level Instance Spatial containment
    elem.phase_created Phase Created element:phase Instance RXD element data phasing
    wall.base_offset Base Offset length Instance RXD element data constraints (and the evaluated geometry)
    wall.unconnected_height Unconnected Height length Instance Qto_WallBaseQuantities.Height (as a derived value) + RXD
    door.width Width length Type IfcDoor.OverallWidth (instance attribute, written from the type) + IfcDoorType property

    Commands. param.definition(param_ref) -> definition · param.list(category?, element_id?) -> definition[] · param.set_ifc_home(param_ref, category?, pset_name, property_name)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Mapping a shared parameter "Acoustic Rating" to Pset_WallCommon.AcousticRating for walls and to Pset_DoorCommon.AcousticRating for doors writes each value to the right standard property set. - [ ] Mapping a project parameter onto Pset_WallCommon.FireRating for walls is refused with param.home_clash, naming built-in Fire Rating. - [ ] param.list("cat.walls") returns every built-in, project and shared parameter bound to walls, with its data type and IFC home.

    2.9.3 Project parameters and category bindings

    ID: DM-PARAM-003 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §7.3, §7.6; screenshots/platform/parameter_properties_shared_project_parameter.png, screenshots/platform/manage_tab_settings_panel.png

    Purpose. To add data fields to project elements by category.

    Workflow. 1. Manage › Settings › Project Parameters. The list is sorted A–Z and has a search field. 2. Add: choose Project parameter (enter name, data type, group) or Shared parameter (pick from the parameter library). Choose Type or Instance. For instance parameters, choose Values aligned per group type or Values can vary by group instance. Choose the categories on the right (a filterable tree with Check all / Check none, and Hide unchecked). Optionally set the IFC property-set name. 3. OK. Every existing element in the chosen categories gets the parameter, with no value. 4. Modify changes the binding (categories, group, IFC home). Remove deletes the definition and all its values, after a confirmation that shows how many values will be lost.

    Behaviour & rules. - A binding is (definition, categories, type or instance, group behaviour). A definition can have only one binding in a project. - Changing a binding from instance to type (or back) is allowed. Reviera asks how to resolve values that differ between instances of the same type (take the most common value, take the first value, or clear). The resolution is reported. - Parameters can also be created from the schedule-field dialog (DOC) and from the Family Types dialog (as family parameters). Those are the same definitions. - A project or shared parameter with the same name as a built-in parameter of a bound category is refused; built-in names follow established convention and take precedence (§2.9.2, No collisions). - Project Parameters dialog (param.project.manage()). The list shows every project and shared parameter binding with Name, Data type, Type/Instance, Group, Categories (count, with the list in a tooltip), Source (Project, or the library name for shared ones) and IFC property set. Buttons: Add, Modify, Remove and Duplicate (copies a project parameter's definition and binding under a new name and GUID, without values; it is param.project.add with the copied definition). A search field filters by name, and a drop-down filters by category. - The Parameter Properties sub-dialog validates before OK is enabled: a name is required, at most 255 characters, unique among definitions bound to any of the chosen categories, and free of [ ] { } | ; < > (characters reserved by formulas and naming rules); a data type is required; at least one category must be ticked; a property-set name, if given, must not start with Pset_ or Qto_ unless it maps onto that standard set's existing property (§2.9.2), and must not start with Reviera_. - Changes made in the dialog (several adds, modifies and removes) are applied together on OK as one transaction named "Project Parameters"; Cancel discards them. - Removing a binding used by schedules, filters, tags, view templates or formulas lists those uses first.

    Data (storage). Definitions and bindings: RXD document standards/parameters. Values: IFC property sets (§2.3.3).

    Commands. param.project.add(def, categories[], is_instance, group_behavior: "aligned"|"vary", pset_name?) -> param_id · param.project.modify(param_id, changes) · param.project.remove(param_id) · param.get(element_id, param_ref) -> value · param.set(element_ids[], param_ref, value) · param.set_many(changes: [{element_id, param_ref, value}]) · param.clear(element_ids[], param_ref) · param.project.manage() (opens the Project Parameters dialog)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] In the Project Parameters dialog, adding "Fire Rating" bound to Doors (where a built-in Fire Rating exists) is refused with the clash named, and OK stays disabled until the name is changed. - [ ] Adding an instance text parameter "Room Finish Code" to Rooms and Areas makes it appear in both categories' Properties and schedules, and in IFC under the configured property set. - [ ] Changing a parameter from instance to type, when instances of the same type disagree, shows the resolution dialog and applies the choice. - [ ] param.set on a read-only computed parameter fails with error param.read_only.

    2.9.4 Data types and IFC measure types

    ID: DM-PARAM-004 · Priority: P0 (common) / P1 (discipline types) · Ref: research/05 §7.7, §8

    Purpose. A fixed, versioned catalogue of data types. Each type maps to an IFC measure type and an SI internal unit.

    Behaviour & rules. - Each data type has a key (for example length) and a versioned ID (reviera:spec/length@1). Keys are used in formulas, tables and APIs. Versioned IDs are stored in RXD, so that a future change in meaning can be migrated. - The catalogue (normative baseline; domain chapters may add types, but not change existing ones):

    Key Discipline Storage IFC value type SI internal unit
    text common string IfcLabel (≤ 255 chars) or IfcText —
    multiline_text common string IfcText —
    integer common i64 IfcInteger —
    number common f64 IfcReal —
    yes_no common bool IfcBoolean —
    url common string IfcURIReference —
    date / datetime common ISO 8601 IfcDate / IfcDateTime —
    length common f64 IfcLengthMeasure (IfcPositiveLengthMeasure when min > 0) m
    distance common f64 IfcLengthMeasure m
    area common f64 IfcAreaMeasure m²
    volume common f64 IfcVolumeMeasure m³
    angle common f64 IfcPlaneAngleMeasure rad
    rotation_angle common f64 IfcPlaneAngleMeasure rad
    slope common f64 IfcRatioMeasure (rise/run) —
    ratio / percentage common f64 IfcRatioMeasure / IfcPositiveRatioMeasure —
    currency common f64 IfcMonetaryMeasure (with IfcMonetaryUnit from project currency) currency unit
    mass common f64 IfcMassMeasure kg
    mass_density common f64 IfcMassDensityMeasure kg/m³
    mass_per_length common f64 IfcMassPerLengthMeasure kg/m
    time common f64 IfcTimeMeasure s
    duration common ISO 8601 IfcDuration —
    speed common f64 IfcLinearVelocityMeasure m/s
    cost_per_area common f64 IfcReal + unit in the template (no IFC measure) currency/m²
    material common element ref IfcPropertyReferenceValue → IfcMaterial —
    image common asset ref IfcPropertyReferenceValue → IfcImageTexture / IfcURIReference —
    fill_pattern common element ref IfcLabel (pattern name) —
    family_type:<category> common element ref IfcPropertyReferenceValue → IfcTypeObject (or IfcLabel name) —
    element:<kind> common element ref IfcPropertyReferenceValue → IfcObjectDefinition / IfcLabel GUID —
    load_classification electrical element ref IfcLabel —
    force structural f64 IfcForceMeasure N
    linear_force structural f64 IfcLinearForceMeasure N/m
    area_force structural f64 IfcPlanarForceMeasure N/m²
    moment structural f64 IfcTorqueMeasure N·m
    linear_moment structural f64 IfcLinearMomentMeasure N·m/m
    stress structural f64 IfcPressureMeasure (IfcModulusOfElasticityMeasure for moduli) Pa
    unit_weight structural f64 IfcReal (no IFC measure) N/m³
    thermal_expansion structural f64 IfcThermalExpansionCoefficientMeasure 1/K
    section_area / section_modulus / moment_of_inertia / warping_constant structural f64 IfcAreaMeasure / IfcSectionModulusMeasure / IfcMomentOfInertiaMeasure / IfcWarpingConstantMeasure m² / m³ / m⁴ / m⁶
    point_spring / line_spring / area_spring / rotational_spring structural f64 IfcLinearStiffnessMeasure / IfcModulusOfLinearSubgradeReactionMeasure / IfcModulusOfSubgradeReactionMeasure / IfcRotationalStiffnessMeasure N/m, N/m², N/m³, N·m/rad
    acceleration structural f64 IfcAccelerationMeasure m/s²
    frequency structural/electrical f64 IfcFrequencyMeasure Hz
    temperature hvac/piping f64 IfcThermodynamicTemperatureMeasure K
    temperature_difference hvac f64 IfcThermodynamicTemperatureMeasure (difference flag in the template) K
    pressure hvac/piping f64 IfcPressureMeasure Pa
    airflow / flow hvac/piping f64 IfcVolumetricFlowRateMeasure m³/s
    velocity hvac/piping f64 IfcLinearVelocityMeasure m/s
    power / heat_gain / cooling_load / heating_load hvac/electrical f64 IfcPowerMeasure W
    power_density hvac/electrical f64 IfcHeatFluxDensityMeasure W/m²
    energy energy f64 IfcEnergyMeasure J
    thermal_conductivity energy f64 IfcThermalConductivityMeasure W/(m·K)
    heat_transfer_coefficient energy f64 IfcThermalTransmittanceMeasure W/(m²·K)
    thermal_resistance energy f64 IfcThermalResistanceMeasure m²·K/W
    specific_heat energy f64 IfcSpecificHeatCapacityMeasure J/(kg·K)
    thermal_mass energy f64 IfcReal (heat capacity per area; no IFC measure) J/(m²·K)
    permeability energy f64 IfcVaporPermeabilityMeasure kg/(s·m·Pa)
    dynamic_viscosity hvac/piping f64 IfcDynamicViscosityMeasure Pa·s
    roughness hvac/piping f64 IfcLengthMeasure m
    duct_size / pipe_size / conduit_size / cable_tray_size / bar_diameter mep/structural f64 IfcPositiveLengthMeasure m
    current electrical f64 IfcElectricCurrentMeasure A
    electrical_potential electrical f64 IfcElectricVoltageMeasure V
    apparent_power electrical f64 IfcPowerMeasure (VA; apparent flag in the template) VA
    illuminance electrical f64 IfcIlluminanceMeasure lx
    luminous_flux electrical f64 IfcLuminousFluxMeasure lm
    luminous_intensity electrical f64 IfcLuminousIntensityMeasure cd
    luminance electrical f64 IfcReal (no IFC measure) cd/m²
    efficacy electrical f64 IfcReal lm/W
    color_temperature electrical f64 IfcThermodynamicTemperatureMeasure K
    resistivity electrical f64 IfcElectricResistanceMeasure × m (as IfcReal) Ω·m
    number_of_poles electrical i64 IfcCountMeasure —
    demand_factor electrical f64 IfcRatioMeasure —
    global_warming_potential carbon (Reviera) f64 IfcMassMeasure (kg CO₂e) kg CO₂e
    gwp_per_mass / gwp_per_volume / gwp_per_area carbon (Reviera) f64 IfcReal (unit in the template) kgCO₂e/kg, /m³, /m²
    • Where IFC has no measure type, the value is written as IfcReal. The unit is given in the matching IfcSimplePropertyTemplate.PrimaryUnit when templates are exported (§2.11.4). Reviera reads the unit from the definition, not from the value.
    • Changing the data type of an existing definition is not allowed for shared parameters (it would break GUID identity). For project and family parameters it is allowed only between compatible types (for example number ↔ integer, text ↔ multiline_text), with a preview of the converted values.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] For every row, setting a value, saving and reopening gives the same value, and the IFC property uses the listed value type. - [ ] A third-party file with a property stored as IfcThermalTransmittanceMeasure is recognised as heat_transfer_coefficient, and displayed in the project's chosen unit.

    2.9.5 Units

    ID: DM-UNIT-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §8; screenshots/platform/project_units_dialog.png

    Purpose. SI internally, any reasonable unit for display and input, set per discipline and per data type.

    Behaviour & rules. - Internal units are SI: metre, radian, kilogram, second, kelvin, ampere, mole, candela and their derived units. This differs from the reference product, which uses decimal feet internally. Conversion happens only at input (parsing) and output (formatting). - Unit catalogue. Every unit has a key (millimetre), a versioned ID (reviera:unit/millimetre@1), symbols (mm), the data types it applies to, and an exact conversion to SI (scale + offset, held as rationals where possible, for example 1 in = 0.0254 m exactly). It shall include at least: mm, cm, dm, m, km, in, ft, ft-in (with fractional and decimal inch forms), yd, mi; mm², cm², m², ha, km², in², ft², ac; mm³, cm³, L, m³, in³, ft³, yd³, gal (US/UK); °, rad, grad, % slope, rise/run (1:n), rise per 12 in; kg, t, g, lb, kip; N, kN, lbf, kip-force; Pa, kPa, MPa, bar, psi, in H₂O, in Hg; °C, °F, K, °R (with offsets); L/s, m³/h, CFM, GPM; W, kW, BTU/h, ton of refrigeration; lx, fc; V, A, VA, kVA; and the project currency. - Project Units (Manage › Settings › Project Units; shortcut UN): - a discipline selector (Common, Structural, HVAC, Electrical, Piping, Energy, Infrastructure); - per data type, a format: unit, rounding (number of decimal places, or a custom increment such as 5 mm or 1/16″), unit symbol (none, or one of the unit's symbols), and the flags suppress trailing zeros, suppress 0 feet, suppress 0 inches, show + for positive values, use digit grouping, suppress spaces; - decimal symbol and digit grouping (123,456.78, 123.456,78, 123 456,78, 12,34,567.89). - Format overrides. Dimension types, schedule fields, tag labels and parameters may override the project format (Use project settings off). - Input parsing. Value fields accept any unit of the right dimension (3' 6", 1067, 1.067 m, 42 in). A bare number uses the field's display unit. Simple arithmetic is accepted (=1200/2 + 50 mm) through the formula evaluator (§2.8.7). - Presets. Metric (mm), Metric (m), Imperial (ft-in), Imperial (decimal ft). Project templates store their unit set. - IFC. IfcUnitAssignment stays SI (§2.3.1). Display formats are in RXD document project/settings. On export to third-party exchanges, an option lets the user write the project's display length unit as IfcSIUnit with a prefix (for example millimetre) or as IfcConversionBasedUnit (inch, foot), with values converted. This is for receivers that expect it.

    UI. The Project Units dialog: discipline drop-down; a list of data types with their current format sample; a Format button for each, which opens the Format dialog (unit, rounding, symbol, flags, with a live sample); and decimal and grouping settings. Ref: screenshots/platform/project_units_dialog.png.

    Workflow (Project Units dialog, units.edit()). 1. Manage › Settings › Project Units (UN). The dialog opens on the Common discipline. 2. Optionally choose a preset from the drop-down at the top (Metric (mm), Metric (m), Imperial (ft-in), Imperial (decimal ft)); this fills every format and can still be edited row by row. 3. Click a row's Format button. In the Format dialog choose the unit (only units whose dimension matches the data type are listed), the rounding, the symbol and the flags. The sample shows a fixed test value per data type (for Length, 1.2345678 m) formatted live. 4. OK in the Format dialog returns to the list; OK in Project Units applies every change as one transaction ("Project Units"). Cancel discards all.

    Validation. - A custom rounding increment must be positive and expressed in a unit of the same dimension; it is stored in SI and shown in the chosen unit. - Decimal places range 0–12. Fractional-inch rounding offers 1/2 to 1/256 only for ft-in and in units. - The decimal symbol and the digit-grouping symbol must differ; choosing the same character is refused. - Flags that do not apply to the unit (for example suppress 0 feet for millimetres) are hidden, not just disabled. - A row whose format is overridden somewhere (dimension types, schedule fields) shows the number of overrides; changing the project format does not change those overrides.

    Data (storage). RXD document project/settings (formats per data type, decimal symbol, grouping, overrides catalogue). Overrides on dimension types or schedules are kept with those objects (DOC).

    Commands. units.get() -> unit_settings · units.set_format(data_type, format) · units.set_preset(preset) · units.set_number_format(decimal_symbol, digit_grouping, indian_grouping?) · units.format(value, data_type, format?) -> text · units.parse(text, data_type) -> value · units.edit() (opens the Project Units dialog)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] In Project Units, setting both the decimal symbol and digit grouping to "," is refused; setting Length to millimetres with 0 decimals shows "1235" as the sample, and OK creates one undo item. - [ ] With Length set to feet and fractional inches, rounded to 1/16″, units.format(1.0, "length") returns 3' - 3 3/8", and parsing that string gives a value within 1/32″ of 1.0 m. - [ ] Changing the display unit from mm to m changes no stored value. An IFC diff before and after shows only RXD changes. - [ ] units.parse("5' 6\"", "length") returns 1.6764 m (exact to 1e-12).

    2.9.6 Global parameters

    ID: DM-GPAR-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §7.4, §2.3

    Purpose. Named project-wide values that drive dimensions and element parameters.

    Workflow. 1. Manage › Settings › Global Parameters: New, Edit, Delete, Duplicate. Sort and filter. Each row shows Name, Value, Formula, Reporting. 2. Create "CorridorWidth" (Length, group Dimensions) = 1800 mm. 3. Select a dimension between two corridor walls. In the dimension's contextual tab, choose Label › CorridorWidth. The walls move to satisfy the value. 4. Select doors. In Properties, use the small "=" button beside Sill Height to associate it with the global "DoorSillHeight".

    Behaviour & rules. - A global parameter has a name, data type (any numeric type, plus yes_no, text, integer, material), group, an optional formula (over other globals), a reporting flag and a tooltip. - A driving global can label instance dimensions (as an equality constraint, §2.4.4) and can be associated with instance parameters of matching data type (but not with type parameters or read-only parameters). - A reporting global is set from a labelled dimension. It reads the measured value, and can be used in other globals' formulas. It cannot label more than one dimension. - Deleting a global used by dimensions or parameters shows how many uses there are. The uses become plain values (dimensions are unlabelled, and parameters keep their current value). - Associations are shown in Properties (the "=" button turns blue, and the value is greyed). Select elements on a global highlights everything it drives. - Global Parameters dialog (global.manage(), shortcut GL): - a grid grouped by parameter group, with columns Name | Value | Formula | Reporting | Uses; formula-driven values are greyed; reporting rows show the dimension they read; - a toolbar: New and Edit (both open the Global Parameter Properties sub-dialog: name, discipline, data type, group, reporting, tooltip), Duplicate, Delete, Move Up/Down, Sort A–Z/Z–A, Select elements, and a search field; - values and formulas are edited in the grid; Apply commits pending edits as one transaction ("Global Parameters") and keeps the dialog open, OK applies and closes, Cancel discards uncommitted edits. - Validation. Names are unique (case-insensitive) among globals, at most 255 characters, and may not contain [ ] { } | ; < > @ (the @ prefix is how formulas refer to globals, §2.8.7). Formulas are checked with formula.validate against the other globals: unknown names, unit dimension mismatch and cycles are shown under the cell and block Apply. The data type of a global cannot change once it has associations. A reporting global cannot be given a formula or a typed value. Deleting shows the use count first.

    Data (storage). RXD document standards/parameters (globals[]: definition, value, formula, reporting, list of associations as element GUID + parameter key or dimension GUID).

    Commands. global.create(name, data_type, value | formula, group?, reporting=false) -> global_id · global.set(global_id, value | {formula}) · global.delete(global_id) · global.associate(global_id, element_ids[], param_ref) · global.dissociate(element_ids[], param_ref) · global.label_dimension(global_id, dimension_id) · global.list() -> global[] · global.select_driven(global_id) -> element_id[] · global.manage() (opens the Global Parameters dialog)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing "CorridorWidth" from 1800 mm to 2000 mm moves the labelled walls in one transaction, and undo restores both the value and the walls. - [ ] A global formula CorridorWidth * 2 + 300 mm updates when CorridorWidth changes. A cycle between two globals is rejected. - [ ] 200 doors associated with "DoorSillHeight" update together when it changes.

    2.9.7 Parameter libraries (shared-parameter equivalent)

    ID: DM-SPAR-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §7.2, §7.5, §16.7; screenshots/platform/edit_shared_parameters_dialog.png

    Purpose. GUID-identified parameter definitions shared across projects and families, in an open, diff-friendly format of Reviera's own design.

    Behaviour & rules. - A Reviera parameter library is a UTF-8 JSON file with the extension .rplib.json. It is validated by a published JSON Schema (reviera.paramlib, version 1). A library contains groups (for organising only) and definitions. Several libraries may be active at once. Each has a stable library ID, so definitions from different libraries never clash. - Format (normative).

    {
  "schema": "reviera.paramlib",
  "schema_version": "1.0.0",
  "library": {
    "id": "6f1c9d2e-8a4b-4c1e-9f0a-2b7d3e5c1a90",
    "name": "ACME Practice Parameters",
    "version": "2026.3.0",
    "publisher": "ACME Architects",
    "license": "CC-BY-4.0",
    "default_pset": "ACME_Common"
  },
  "groups": [
    { "id": "g-identity", "name": "Identity" },
    { "id": "g-acoustic", "name": "Acoustics" }
  ],
  "definitions": [
    {
      "guid": "3b0d2a4e-5f61-4c7a-9e2b-1d0c8f6a7b51",
      "name": "Acoustic Class",
      "data_type": "text",
      "enum": ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
      "group": "g-acoustic",
      "param_group": "identity_data",
      "discipline": "common",
      "tooltip": "Sound reduction class according to the practice standard.",
      "visible": true,
      "user_modifiable": true,
      "hide_when_no_value": false,
      "ifc": { "pset": "ACME_Common", "property": "AcousticClass" },
      "labels": ["acoustics", "doors", "walls"],
      "deprecated": false,
      "superseded_by": null
    }
  ]
}
    • Rules.
    • guid is a canonical UUID string. It is the identity. name, tooltip, group, labels and ifc may change between library versions. data_type may not change.
    • Definitions are never deleted from a published library. They are marked deprecated, optionally with superseded_by.
    • The ifc mapping is the default IFC home. Projects can override it per category (§2.9.2).
    • Files are written with sorted keys and 2-space indentation, so they diff well in version control.
    • Embedding. When a shared definition is used in a project or family, a full copy of it (with the library ID and version) is stored in the project's RXD document standards/parameters. Projects therefore never depend on the library file being present.
    • Conflicts. If a project already has a definition with the same GUID but different metadata (for example a newer name), loading a family or importing a library offers Keep project or Update from source. If the data types differ, the newer definition is refused with an error that names both sources.
    • UI: Manage › Settings › Parameter Libraries:
    • the active libraries list (Add file, Add URL, Remove, Create new);
    • for the selected library: a group tree and a definitions grid (search, filter by label or data type, show deprecated);
    • New, Edit and Deprecate definition; New and Rename group; Export to IFC templates (§2.11.4).
    • Read-only libraries (opened from a URL or a read-only file) show a lock.
    • The dialog (paramlib.manage()) edits library files, not the model, so its changes are not undoable in the project. Edits are held in memory per library and written on Save library or on OK (an atomic write, with sorted keys and 2-space indentation as the rules above require); Cancel discards unsaved edits after confirmation. A library changed on disk by another program while open is reloaded on request, with a notice if local edits would be lost.
    • Definition editor validation: a name is required (at most 255 characters, unique within its group, free of [ ] { } | ; < >); a data type is required and is locked once the definition has been saved; enum values must be unique and valid for the data type; min must not exceed max; the IFC property set must not start with Reviera_, and a Pset_ home must name a property that exists in that standard set; superseded_by must name a non-deprecated definition with the same data type.
    • A column In project marks definitions already embedded in the active project, and Add to project… opens Project Parameters with the definition pre-selected (§2.9.3).
    • Team distribution (open alternative to a vendor cloud service). A library can be opened from an HTTPS URL or a git repository path. Reviera caches it, and checks for updates on start-up and on demand. Firms publish their standard library as a versioned file in their own repository or web server. No vendor service is needed.
    • Import of the reference product's shared-parameter text files is supported for migration. GUIDs, names, groups, data types (mapped to §2.9.4 keys), visibility and descriptions are preserved. Unknown data-type tokens go to a mapping dialog. Export to that text format is P2, for interoperability with firms that still use it.
    • IFC templates. A library can also be written as an IFC file containing an IfcProjectLibrary with IfcPropertySetTemplate and IfcSimplePropertyTemplate entities. Each template's GlobalId is the definition GUID (encoded to 22 characters), with PrimaryMeasureType and units from §2.9.4. This is a read/write interchange form, for tools that use IFC templates.

    Commands. paramlib.open(path_or_url) -> library_id · paramlib.create(path, name) -> library_id · paramlib.close(library_id) · paramlib.definition.add(library_id, def) -> guid · paramlib.definition.edit(library_id, guid, changes) · paramlib.definition.deprecate(library_id, guid, superseded_by?) · paramlib.group.add(library_id, name) -> group_id · paramlib.group.rename(library_id, group_id, name) · paramlib.import_legacy(path, target_library_id) · paramlib.export_ifc_templates(library_id, path) · paramlib.search(text?, labels?, data_type?) -> definition[] · paramlib.manage() (opens the Parameter Libraries dialog)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A library with 500 definitions opens in under 200 ms, and its JSON Schema validation passes. - [ ] Importing a reference-product shared-parameter file with 50 parameters gives 50 definitions with identical GUIDs. A family using one of them, after round-tripping through Reviera, schedules in the same column as a project parameter with that GUID. - [ ] Changing data_type of an existing GUID in a library file is reported as a validation error on open. - [ ] A project that uses shared parameters opens and schedules correctly with every library file removed from the machine.

    2.9.8 Extended properties (external data)

    ID: DM-PARAM-005 · Priority: P3 (vendor cloud equivalent) / P2 (open alternative) · Ref: research/05 §7.1 (extended properties, 2027), §12.1

    Purpose. Showing data from external systems (for example asset registers or coordination models) next to element parameters, without copying it into the model.

    Behaviour & rules. - The vendor-cloud feature is out of scope (P3). - Open alternative (P2): an add-in API (§2.13) for external property providers. A provider registers a namespace, and answers get_properties(guid[]) -> {name, value, data_type}[] (read-only). Results are shown in Properties under the provider's name, and are available in schedules as external fields. They are never written to IFC unless the user chooses Materialise, which copies them into a property set. - Registration. reviera.external_props.register{namespace, name, fields = {{name, data_type, unit?}}, get_properties = fn, refresh_interval_s?}. The declared fields list is what schedules and filters offer before any value is fetched. A provider needs trust level standard or higher when it reads files or the network (§2.13.7). - Fetching and caching. Values are requested in batches of at most 1,000 GUIDs, on a worker coroutine (§2.13.6), never on the UI thread. They are cached per session with the time fetched. Properties shows cached values immediately, marked with the provider's icon and a "fetched hh:mm" tooltip; Refresh (per provider, or on the palette's context menu) re-fetches. A provider that times out (default 10 s per batch) or raises an error shows "unavailable" in its rows; the rest of the UI is unaffected. - Matching. Providers key on IFC GlobalId by default. A provider may declare key = {param = "<param_ref>"} instead (for example an asset tag), in which case Reviera sends that parameter's values. - Use in documentation. External fields can be shown in schedules, used in schedule filters and sorting, and in view filters (DOC). They cannot be edited, used in family formulas, or drive geometry. A schedule that uses an external field shows a "live data" note with the fetch time, and PDF export prints the fetch time in the schedule footer. - Materialise. Copies the current values into a user property set as one undoable transaction, creating project parameter bindings if needed (§2.9.3). Data types are preserved; unknown types become text. - Data (storage). Nothing is stored in the model unless materialised. The list of providers a schedule uses is kept in that schedule's RXD document, so opening the project without the add-in shows the columns as "provider missing".

    Commands. external_props.list_providers() -> provider[] · external_props.materialise(provider, element_ids[], pset_name)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A sample Lua provider that reads a CSV keyed by GUID shows its values in Properties for matching elements, and Materialise writes them to the chosen property set. - [ ] A provider that sleeps for 30 s does not freeze the UI; its rows show "unavailable" after the 10 s timeout, and other parameters remain editable. - [ ] A schedule with an external field, opened without the provider's add-in, keeps the column and shows "provider missing" instead of failing.

    2.10 Project setup and the Manage features

    2.10.1 Manage tab

    ID: DM-SET-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §9 (intro); screenshots/platform/manage_tab_settings_panel.png, screenshots/platform/manage_tab_visual_programming_panel.jpg

    Purpose. One ribbon tab for project-wide settings and model-management tools.

    UI. Ribbon Manage tab, with these panels (each tool is a registered command; shortcuts are in the UI chapter):

    Panel Tools
    Settings Materials · Object Styles · Snaps · Project Information · Project Parameters · Parameter Libraries · Global Parameters · Transfer Project Standards · Purge Unused · Project Units · Structural Settings ▾ · MEP Settings ▾ · Panel Schedule Templates ▾ · Additional Settings ▾ (Line Styles, Line Weights, Line Patterns, Fill Patterns, Material Assets, Analysis Display Styles, Sheet Issues/Revisions, Arrowheads, Temporary Dimensions, Detail Level, Halftone/Underlay, Assembly Code, Keynoting, Classification Systems, Area and Volume Computations, Color Fill Schemes)
    Project Location Location · Coordinates ▾ · Position ▾
    Design Options Design Options · Pick to Edit · Add to Set (ARC chapter)
    Manage Project Manage Links · Manage Images (§2.10.14) · Starting View · Decal Types (§2.10.15)
    Phasing Phases (§2.10.12)
    Numbering Rule-Based Numbering (§2.10.16)
    Selection Save · Load · Edit (UI chapter)
    Inquiry IDs of Selection · Select by ID · Review Warnings · Extension Data Status (§2.4.3)
    Scripts Script Manager · Run Script… · Script Security (§2.13.7, §2.13.8)
    Add-ins Add-in Manager (§2.14)
    Visual Programming Reviera Graph · Graph Player (§2.15, P2)
    AI Agents MCP Server status · Permissions · Session log (§2.16)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Every tool in the table runs a registered command, and so is callable from Lua and MCP with the same result as from the ribbon.

    2.10.2 Project information

    ID: DM-SET-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §9.1

    Purpose. A single record of project identity, used by title blocks, schedules and exports.

    Behaviour & rules. - The Project Information dialog edits these fields, and any project parameters bound to the Project Information category:

    Field IFC home
    Project Name IfcProject.LongName (with IfcProject.Name holding the project number, the usual convention)
    Project Number IfcProject.Name
    Project Status / Phase IfcProject.Phase
    Project Issue Date Identity Data.ProjectIssueDate on IfcProject (IfcDate)
    Client Name IfcActor (role CLIENT) with IfcRelAssignsToActor → IfcProject
    Project Address IfcPostalAddress on IfcBuilding.BuildingAddress (and IfcSite.SiteAddress)
    Building Name IfcBuilding.Name / LongName
    Organisation Name / Description IfcOrganization (owning organisation; also IfcOwnerHistory when written)
    Author FILE_NAME author, and IfcPerson
    Energy settings, route-analysis settings RXD document project/settings (ANA chapter)
    • Project information is one element (a singleton, internal ID 1). It cannot be deleted.
    • Project Information dialog (project.info.edit(); Manage › Settings › Project Information). A property grid grouped as Identity Data (organisation, author, building name), Project (name, number, status, issue date, client), Address and Other, followed by every project parameter bound to the Project Information category under its own group.
    • Project Address opens a structured address editor (address lines, town, region, postal code, country) that writes IfcPostalAddress; a free-text address from a third-party file is shown in the first line and kept unchanged until edited.
    • Energy Settings and Route Analysis Settings rows open their own dialogs (ANA chapter).
    • Validation. Project Number may be empty but, when set, must be at most 255 characters (IfcLabel). Issue Date accepts ISO 8601 or the user's locale format and is stored as IfcDate. Text fields over 255 characters are refused, except the description fields, which are IfcText. Shared parameters bound to Project Information use their own data-type validation (§2.9.4).
    • OK applies all changed fields as one transaction ("Project Information"); Cancel discards them. The dialog is also reachable from Properties when nothing is selected and the active view is a sheet.
    • In BIMserver mode, project information is an ordinary element for ownership: editing it takes its advisory lock (COL).

    Commands. project.info.get() -> info · project.info.set(fields) · project.info.edit() (opens the Project Information dialog)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Setting Client Name to "City of Example" produces an IfcActor with role CLIENT assigned to the project, and a title-block label bound to Client Name shows it. - [ ] Entering an address in the structured editor writes an IfcPostalAddress with separate Town, PostalCode and Country, which a third-party viewer shows; an issue date typed as 12/10/2026 in a UK locale is stored as 2026-10-12.

    2.10.3 Object styles and subcategories

    ID: DM-OBJS-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §9.2

    Purpose. Default graphics for every category and subcategory.

    UI. Manage › Settings › Object Styles. Tabs: Model Objects, Annotation Objects, Analytical Model Objects, Imported Objects. A tree grid (category with subcategories) with columns: Line Weight Projection, Line Weight Cut (only for cuttable categories), Line Colour, Line Pattern, Material. Buttons: Modify Subcategories (New, Delete, Rename), Select All / None / Invert, filter by discipline.

    Behaviour & rules. - Object styles are the lowest layer of graphic precedence. View-level overrides (visibility/graphics, filters, view templates; DOC chapter) take precedence over them. - Built-in subcategories (for example Doors › Frame/Mullion, Glass, Opening, Panel, Plan Swing, Elevation Swing; Walls › Common Edges, Hidden Lines; Windows › Sill/Head, Trim; Imported Objects › one subcategory per imported layer) are created automatically. They cannot be deleted. - Imported CAD layers become subcategories of Imported Objects › <file name> (§2.11.5). - IFC. For other tools, each category and subcategory used by model geometry is written as an IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle. Its name is <Category> or <Category>|<Subcategory>, and it has LayerOn = TRUE and LayerStyles = an IfcCurveStyle (projection colour and width). The AssignedItems are the representation items of that subcategory. Cut weights, patterns and materials are only in RXD.

    Data (storage). RXD document standards/styles (object_styles[]: category or subcategory key and GUID, projection/cut weight, colour, pattern, material GUID).

    Commands. object_style.set(category_or_subcategory, {projection_weight?, cut_weight?, color?, pattern?, material?}) · object_style.get(category_or_subcategory) -> style (plus subcategory.create/rename/delete, §2.2.2)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Setting Walls cut line weight to pen 5 changes the cut walls in every plan view that has no override, and leaves views with an override unchanged. - [ ] A third-party viewer lists layers "Doors|Panel" and "Doors|Frame/Mullion", and toggling them hides the matching parts of the doors.

    2.10.4 Line weights, line patterns, line styles and fill patterns

    ID: DM-LINE-001 (line weights, patterns, styles) · DM-PAT-001 (fill patterns) · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §9.3

    Behaviour & rules. - Line weights (Manage › Additional Settings › Line Weights). There are 16 pens, on three tabs: - Model line weights are scale-dependent. They form a table of pen thickness (mm on paper) by view scale. Columns 1:10 … 1:5000 can be added and removed. Weights for scales between columns are taken from the nearest column at a larger scale. - Perspective line weights are scale-independent. - Annotation line weights are scale-independent. - Line patterns: named sequences of dash, dot and space lengths (paper units). Defaults: Solid, Dash, Dot, Dash Dot, Hidden, Centre, Phantom, Overhead, Demolished, … Editing a pattern updates every use. - Line styles (Manage › Additional Settings › Line Styles): subcategories of the Lines category, each with weight, colour and pattern. Built-in styles: Thin Lines, Medium Lines, Wide Lines, Hidden Lines, Overhead Lines, <Sketch>, <Room Separation>, <Area Boundary>, <Space Separation>, <Centerline>, <Demolished>, <Beyond>, <Insulation Batting Lines>. Users may add styles. Built-in styles cannot be deleted. - Fill patterns (Manage › Additional Settings › Fill Patterns): - Drafting patterns are defined in paper units, and keep the same size at any scale. - Model patterns are defined in real-world units, align to geometry, and can be moved and rotated on faces. - Each pattern is simple (parallel lines or crosshatch, with angle and spacing), custom (a grid of line families with angle, origin, offset, shift and dash sequence), or solid fill. - Patterns may be rotated (custom patterns too). - Double fill: filled regions, materials and overrides may use a foreground and a background pattern, each with its own colour. - Pattern files. Reviera reads and writes .pat files (the widely used, publicly documented hatch format used by many CAD tools) for import and export. Its own storage is the RXD form. Reviera ships its own default pattern set, authored from scratch.

    Data (storage). RXD document standards/styles (line_weights, line_patterns[], line_styles[], fill_patterns[]). In IFC, a material's cut and surface patterns are also written as IfcFillAreaStyle with IfcFillAreaStyleHatching (simple and crosshatch patterns), so other tools can draw them (§2.10.5).

    Commands. line_weight.set(kind: "model"|"perspective"|"annotation", pen, scale?, thickness_mm) · line_weight.add_scale(scale) · line_weight.remove_scale(scale) · line_pattern.create(name, segments[]) -> id · line_pattern.edit(id, segments[]) · line_pattern.delete(id, replace_with?) · line_style.create(name, weight, color, pattern) -> id · line_style.edit(id, props) · line_style.delete(id, replace_with?) · fill_pattern.create(name, kind: "drafting"|"model", definition) -> id · fill_pattern.edit(id, definition) · fill_pattern.delete(id, replace_with?) · fill_pattern.import_pat(path, names?[], kind) -> id[] · fill_pattern.export_pat(ids[], path)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Pen 3 in the model table at 1:100 = 0.35 mm, and at 1:200 = 0.25 mm. A wall drawn with pen 3 prints at those widths in PDFs at each scale (DOC). - [ ] A .pat file with 5 patterns imports, renders the same as a reference rendering within a tolerance of 1 px at 300 dpi, and exports back to an equivalent .pat. - [ ] A double fill (foreground diagonal in red, background solid in light grey) shows both layers in a filled region and in a material's cut pattern.

    2.10.5 Materials

    ID: DM-MAT-001 … 007 · Priority: P0 (identity, graphics, basic appearance) / P1 (physical, thermal, libraries) / P1 (carbon) · Ref: research/05 §10, §4.8; screenshots/platform/material_browser_appearance_tab_2026.png, screenshots/platform/material_browser_physical_asset_annotated_2026.png, screenshots/platform/material_carbon_information_2027.png

    Purpose. A material combines identity, drawing graphics, rendering appearance, and physical, thermal and carbon data.

    DM-MAT-001 — Material element and IFC mapping (P0)

    • Each material is an IfcMaterial (Name, Description, Category = the material class, for example concrete, steel, wood, masonry, glass, gypsum, insulation, plastic, following buildingSMART recommendations). It has a RXD GUID (§2.5).
    • Material data is spread across IFC and RXD like this:
    Tab Data IFC RXD (document materials)
    Identity Name, description, class, comments, keywords, manufacturer, model, cost, URL, keynote, mark IfcMaterial attributes; IfcMaterialProperties Pset_MaterialCommon (where it applies) plus a material property set Identity Data (manufacturer, model, cost, URL, keynote, mark); IfcExternalReferenceRelationship for library origin comments, keywords
    Graphics Shading colour and transparency ("use appearance colour"), surface pattern (foreground/background, colour, alignment), cut pattern (foreground/background, colour) IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation → IfcStyledRepresentation → IfcSurfaceStyle (IfcSurfaceStyleShading/Rendering), plus IfcFillAreaStyle for patterns pattern references and alignment
    Appearance Rendering asset (§DM-MAT-002) IfcSurfaceStyleRendering (diffuse colour, transparency, specular, reflectance method), IfcSurfaceStyleWithTextures / IfcImageTexture the full PBR asset
    Physical Structural asset (§DM-MAT-003) Pset_MaterialMechanical, Pset_MaterialCommon, Pset_MaterialSteel, Pset_MaterialConcrete, Pset_MaterialWood (as IfcMaterialProperties) asset identity and sharing
    Thermal Thermal asset (§DM-MAT-004) Pset_MaterialThermal, Pset_MaterialHygroscopic, Pset_MaterialOptical, Pset_MaterialEnergy asset identity and sharing
    Carbon Embodied carbon (§DM-MAT-005) material property set Carbon (GWP values) database link and record metadata
    • Assets (appearance, physical, thermal, carbon) are separate, shareable records in RXD document standards/materials. Several materials may share one asset. The UI shows a sharing indicator with the user count, and offers Duplicate asset to make a private copy. When written to IFC, shared asset values are copied into each material's property sets.
    • Names. Material names are unique in a project (case-insensitive) and at most 255 characters. Because IFC identifies non-rooted materials by name, renaming updates the RXD resource key (§2.5) and every IfcMaterial.Name, layer set and constituent set that uses it, in one transaction.
    • Default material. Every project has a built-in Default material, used where an element or family form says <By Category> and the category's object style has no material (§2.10.3). It cannot be deleted or renamed, but its values can be edited.
    • Third-party materials. An IfcMaterial found in an opened file with no RXD becomes a Reviera material: its IfcMaterialProperties populate the matching asset fields, its surface style populates Graphics and Appearance, and properties with no Reviera home are kept as IFC-native parameters of the material (§2.9.1). Two third-party materials with the same name are kept apart by suffixing " (2)" on the second, and the change is reported.
    • Where materials are used. Materials are assigned to layers of layered types, to profile sets, to family forms (fixed or by parameter), to painted faces (ARC) and through object styles. material.list reports, per material, the number of types and instances that use it, which the browser shows as a count.
    • Acceptance. Renaming "Concrete C30" to "Concrete C30/37" changes the name in every layer set of the exported IFC and keeps the material's RXD GUID; opening a third-party file with an IfcMaterial "Brick" carrying Pset_MaterialCommon.MassDensity = 1800 shows 1800 kg/m³ on the Physical tab.

    DM-MAT-002 — Appearance (P0 basic, P2 full rendering)

    • The appearance model is a physically based (metal/roughness) material, compatible with glTF 2.0 PBR, so export to glTF (§2.11.5) is lossless. Fields:
    • base colour or texture;
    • metallic, roughness;
    • normal and bump map;
    • occlusion;
    • emissive colour and strength;
    • transmission and IOR (glass);
    • opacity and cutout map;
    • texture transform (scale in real-world units, offset, rotation);
    • tint.
    • Schema presets (Generic, Ceramic, Concrete, Glazing, Hardwood, Masonry, Metal, Metallic Paint, Mirror, Plastic, Solid Glass, Stone, Wall Paint, Water) are templates that set sensible PBR values. They are UI presets, not separate schemas.
    • Textures are RXD assets. When "Embed textures in IFC" is on (default for textures ≤ 1 MB), they are also written as IfcBlobTexture (PNG/JPEG). Otherwise they are written as IfcImageTexture with a relative URL.
    • Thumbnails are rendered locally (sphere, cube or plane swatch).

    DM-MAT-003 — Physical (structural) asset (P1)

    • Behaviour: isotropic, orthotropic or transversely isotropic.
    • Basic thermal: thermal expansion coefficient (by direction).
    • Mechanical: Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, shear modulus (by direction), density.
    • Strength: yield strength, tensile strength, and per-class fields (concrete compressive strength, lightweight flag, shear strength modification; wood species, grade, bending, compression parallel/perpendicular, shear, tension; steel resistance/reduction factors).
    • IFC: Pset_MaterialMechanical (YoungModulus, ShearModulus, PoissonRatio, ThermalExpansionCoefficient), Pset_MaterialCommon (MassDensity, Porosity), Pset_MaterialSteel (YieldStress, UltimateStress, …), Pset_MaterialConcrete (CompressiveStrength, MaxAggregateSize, …), Pset_MaterialWood (Species, StrengthGrade, …). Values with no standard home go to the material property set Physical.

    DM-MAT-004 — Thermal asset (P1)

    • Fields: thermal conductivity, specific heat, density, emissivity, permeability, porosity, reflectivity, electrical resistivity, transmits light (Yes/No), and for gases and liquids, compressibility and viscosity.
    • IFC: Pset_MaterialThermal (ThermalConductivity, SpecificHeatCapacity), Pset_MaterialCommon (MassDensity, Porosity), Pset_MaterialOptical (emissivity as ThermalIrEmissivityFront/Back; reflectance), Pset_MaterialHygroscopic (VaporPermeability). The rest go to the material property set Thermal.
    • Assembly thermal values. Layered types compute Heat Transfer Coefficient (U), Thermal Resistance (R) and Thermal Mass from their layers and thicknesses (with standard surface resistances, configurable per project in Energy Settings). These are written to Pset_*Common.ThermalTransmittance on the type (§2.3.3).

    DM-MAT-005 — Carbon asset (P1)

    • Fields:
    • database (free text, with presets such as "ÖKOBAUDAT", "ICE", "EC3", "Manual") and record ID / URL;
    • declared unit (kg, m³, m², piece);
    • GWP A1–A3 (kg CO₂e per declared unit), and optional A4, A5, B, C1–C4, D stages;
    • biogenic carbon, reference service life, EPD validity date, notes.
    • The carbon asset is used by carbon reporting (ANA chapter). Element-level results are calculated from material quantities (volume × density → mass, then × GWP/kg, or area × GWP/m²). They are written to Pset_EnvironmentalImpactIndicators.ClimateChangePerUnit and the related properties of the element type, when Write carbon results to IFC is on.
    • Data connectors to online EPD databases are add-ins (§2.14), not built in. The open data sets that Reviera may bundle shall be checked for licence compatibility before inclusion.

    DM-MAT-006 — Material Browser and libraries (P0 basic, P1 libraries)

    • Material Browser (Manage › Settings › Materials; shortcut MAT):
    • left top: project materials (search, filter by class, list or thumbnail view);
    • left bottom: library panel (shipped Reviera library, Favourites, user libraries; tree by class);
    • right: the editor, with tabs Identity / Graphics / Appearance / Physical / Thermal / Carbon;
    • toolbar: New, Duplicate, Rename, Delete, Add to Favourites, Add from library to project (also by drag-and-drop), Create/Open/Remove library;
    • each asset tab has Replace asset (opens the Asset Browser), Duplicate asset, Remove asset;
    • batch operations: select several materials and change a shared field (for example class, cut pattern) at once.
    • Material libraries are IFC files (<Name>.materials.ifc). The file has one IfcProject that declares an IfcProjectLibrary named after the library. Each material is associated with the library through IfcRelAssociatesMaterial, so the file is valid IFC. Assets and other RXD go in the library's RXD documents (materials), carried as 02a defines. Textures are RXD assets.
    • Reviera ships a starter library authored from scratch, with appearance textures under compatible licences (for example CC0).
    • Deleting a material in use asks for a replacement material. Purge removes unused materials and assets (§2.10.11).
    • Browser workflow (material.browser(material_id?)). The browser opens on the given material, on the material of the selected element's first layer or form, or on the last material viewed. Selecting a project material loads it into the editor. Edits on the editor tabs are held as pending changes; Apply commits them as one transaction ("Edit Material: <name>"), OK applies and closes, Cancel discards pending changes. Switching to another material with pending changes asks Apply, Discard or Cancel.
    • Project list. Search matches name, description, class, keywords and comments. Filters: class, Used in project / Unused, Has appearance texture, Has carbon data. Each row shows a swatch, the name and a use count. Multi-selection enables the batch edit described above; fields that differ across the selection show "<varies>".
    • Library panel. The tree lists each open library by class. Library materials can be previewed in the editor read-only; Add to project copies the material with its assets (material.library.add_to_project). If a project material with the same name exists, the user chooses Replace values (keeps the project GUID), Add as "<name> (2)" or Skip. Read-only libraries (shipped, or opened from a read-only location) show a lock; dragging a project material onto an editable library adds it there (material.library.add_from_project).
    • Validation. Name rules as in DM-MAT-001. Numeric asset fields are unit-parsed (§2.9.5) and range-checked (for example density > 0, Poisson's ratio between −1 and 0.5, transparency 0–100 %, roughness 0–1); invalid fields block Apply. Pattern pickers list only drafting patterns for Cut and both kinds for Surface (§2.10.4).

    Commands. material.create(name, class?, from_library?) -> material_id · material.duplicate(material_id, name, share_assets=true) -> material_id · material.rename(material_id, name) · material.delete(material_id, replace_with?) · material.set(material_id, {identity?, graphics?, appearance?, physical?, thermal?, carbon?}) · material.asset.duplicate(material_id, asset_kind) -> asset_id · material.asset.replace(material_id, asset_kind, asset_id) · material.library.open(path) -> library_id · material.library.create(path, name) -> library_id · material.library.add_to_project(library_id, material_names[]) -> material_id[] · material.library.add_from_project(library_id, material_ids[]) · material.list(filter?) -> material[] · material.browser(material_id?) (opens the Material Browser)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A material with a red concrete appearance, a diagonal cut pattern, and density 2400 kg/m³ exports to IFC with IfcSurfaceStyleRendering (red), an IfcFillAreaStyleHatching, and Pset_MaterialCommon.MassDensity = 2400. A third-party viewer renders the wall in red. - [ ] Two materials sharing a physical asset both update when the asset's density changes. After Duplicate asset on one, they are independent. - [ ] A wall type with layers 15 mm gypsum (λ = 0.25), 100 mm mineral wool (λ = 0.035) and 15 mm gypsum reports U ≈ 0.32 W/(m²·K) (with Rsi + Rse = 0.17 m²K/W), and writes it to Pset_WallCommon.ThermalTransmittance. - [ ] A material with carbon GWP A1–A3 = 0.15 kg CO₂e/kg and density 2400 kg/m³, used for 10 m³ of wall, reports 3,600 kg CO₂e for those walls. - [ ] A material library saved by Reviera opens as valid IFC4, and its materials can be added to a second project, keeping all assets.

    DM-MAT-007 — Asset Browser and asset editing (P1)

    ID: DM-MAT-007 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §10; screenshots/platform/material_browser_physical_asset_annotated_2026.png

    Purpose. Assets (appearance, physical, thermal, carbon) are shared records that several materials can use. The Asset Browser finds and swaps them, and the asset tabs edit them safely.

    Workflow. 1. On an asset tab of the Material Browser choose Replace asset, or open Manage › Additional Settings › Material Assets (material.assets(material_id?)). The Asset Browser opens filtered to the asset kind of the tab (or, from the Manage menu, to all kinds). 2. Browse the Project assets and each library's assets by kind and class (for example Physical › Concrete), or search by name, keyword or property value (for example "density > 2000 kg/m³"). 3. Select an asset to preview its values (and, for appearance, a rendered swatch). 4. Replace in material swaps the material's asset for the chosen one (material.asset.replace), or Add to project copies a library asset without assigning it.

    UI. Asset Browser: kind tabs (Appearance, Physical, Thermal, Carbon); a tree of sources (Project, Reviera library, user libraries) and classes; a results list (name, class, users, source); a preview pane. Toolbar: Replace in material, Add to project, Duplicate, Rename, Delete (project assets only), Show users.

    Behaviour & rules. - An asset tab shows the asset's name and a sharing indicator ("Shared by 4 materials"). Editing a shared asset asks first whether to edit it for all users or to Duplicate asset for this material only (material.asset.duplicate). The choice can be remembered for the session. - Assets have names unique per kind within the project; library assets keep their library identity so a later Add to project of the same asset is recognised and not duplicated. - An asset with no users is kept until purged (§2.10.11). Deleting an asset in use is refused; the user must replace it in each material first (Show users lists them). - Physical and thermal assets whose values have a standard IFC home are written into each user material's property sets on save (DM-MAT-001); an asset edit therefore marks every user material as changed. - Appearance assets with textures show texture size and source; a missing texture file shows a broken-link badge and offers Reload from… (§2.10.14).

    Data (storage). Assets are records in RXD document standards/materials with kinds per asset type, referenced by GUID from each material; IFC carries copies of their standard values (DM-MAT-001).

    Commands. material.assets(material_id?) (opens the Asset Browser) · material.asset.duplicate(material_id, asset_kind) -> asset_id · material.asset.replace(material_id, asset_kind, asset_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Editing the density on a physical asset shared by 3 materials, and choosing Duplicate asset, changes only the edited material; the other two keep the old value and the indicator on the edited one reads "Not shared". - [ ] Deleting an asset used by 2 materials is refused with both material names listed. - [ ] Searching the Asset Browser for "density > 2000 kg/m³" lists only physical assets whose density exceeds that value.

    2.10.6 Additional settings (annotation and computation)

    ID: DM-SET-003 · Priority: P0 (temporary dimensions, detail level, area/volume) / P1 (others) · Ref: research/05 §9.4

    Behaviour & rules. These settings are project-wide. Their behaviour is defined in the chapters named. This chapter only defines their storage (RXD document project/settings, or styles for graphic styles) and their commands:

    Setting Behaviour defined in Command
    Arrowheads (Arrow, Dot, Diagonal, Heavy end tick, Datum triangle, Elevation target, Loop, Box, Kink, …) DOC settings.arrowhead.create/edit/delete
    Temporary dimensions (walls: centreline, faces, core centre, core faces; doors and windows: centreline, openings) UI settings.temporary_dimensions.set(walls, doors_windows)
    Detail level by view scale (Coarse/Medium/Fine thresholds) DOC settings.detail_level_by_scale.set(table)
    Halftone and underlay DOC settings.halftone.set(props)
    Area and volume computations (room area at wall finish, centre, core layer, core centre; volume computation on/off; area schemes) ARC settings.area_volume.set(props)
    Colour fill schemes DOC (DOC chapter)
    Sun settings DOC/ANA (DOC chapter)
    Callout, elevation and section tags; spot dimension settings DOC (DOC chapter)
    Keynoting settings (file path, numbering) DOC settings.keynoting.set(path, numbering)
    Assembly code / classification tables §2.10.10 —
    Structural settings (symbolic cut-backs, brace symbols, load cases and combinations, analytical settings, boundary-condition symbols, rebar cover) STR (STR chapter)
    MEP settings (mechanical, electrical, piping, load classifications, demand factors, building and space types) MEP (MEP chapter)
    Panel schedule templates MEP (MEP chapter)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing room area computation from "at wall finish" to "at wall centre" recomputes every room area in one transaction.

    2.10.7 Project location, coordinates and position

    ID: DM-LOC-001 · Priority: P0 (internal origin, base points, true north, lat/long) / P1 (map search, weather, named sites, acquire/publish) · Ref: research/05 §9.8; screenshots/platform/location_and_site_dialog_2026.png

    Purpose. To place the project on Earth, and relate its internal coordinates to survey and shared coordinates.

    UI. Manage › Project Location › Location opens the Location, Weather and Site dialog: - Location tab: Define location by — a map search (an address search and map, using an open map service such as OpenStreetMap/Nominatim; configurable, with no vendor service), or a city list (bundled, open data) with latitude, longitude, time zone and daylight saving. - Weather tab: heating and cooling design temperatures, clearness number. Use the nearest weather station (from an open data set such as the ASHRAE climate design conditions or EnergyPlus EPW metadata, subject to licence checks), or enter values. - Site tab: named sites (shared-coordinate positions of this model in a larger context), each with an angle from project north to true north. Make current, Duplicate, Rename, Delete.

    Coordinates ▾: Acquire Coordinates (from a link), Publish Coordinates (to a link), Specify Coordinates at Point, Report Shared Coordinates. Position ▾: Relocate Project, Rotate True North, Rotate Project North, Mirror Project.

    Behaviour & rules. - Three reference points: - Internal origin: fixed, the origin of internal coordinates. It is never moved. - Project base point: a user-placed point that defines project coordinates (and, optionally, the zero for level elevations). - Survey point: a user-placed point linking the project to a real-world coordinate system. - IFC mapping: - IfcSite.RefLatitude, RefLongitude (as IfcCompoundPlaneAngleMeasure) and RefElevation; - geo-referencing with IfcMapConversion (Eastings, Northings, OrthogonalHeight, XAxisAbscissa, XAxisOrdinate, Scale) from the model's context to an IfcProjectedCRS (Name = an EPSG code such as EPSG:25832, plus GeodeticDatum, VerticalDatum, MapProjection, MapZone and MapUnit where known), calculated from the survey point; - project north and true north through the context's TrueNorth direction; - the project base point is written as the IfcSite placement (default) or as the world coordinate system, chosen in the IFC export setup (§2.11.4). - Named sites, the base point and survey point positions, clipped/unclipped state, and weather data are in RXD document project/location. - Relocate, Rotate True North and Mirror change the coordinate transforms (and, for mirror, the geometry). They are single transactions, and are undoable. - A CRS database (PROJ, MIT licence) is used to validate EPSG codes and, optionally, to convert latitude and longitude to map coordinates.

    Commands. location.set(lat, lon, elevation?, time_zone?, dst?) · location.search(address) -> candidates[] · location.weather.set(props | {station_id}) · site.position.create(name) -> id · site.position.set_current(id) · site.position.rename(id, name) · site.position.delete(id) · coordinates.set_survey_point(point, shared_coords) · coordinates.set_project_base_point(point, angle_to_true_north?) · coordinates.set_crs(epsg_code) · coordinates.acquire(link_instance_id) · coordinates.publish(link_instance_id, site_position_id) · coordinates.report(point) -> {internal, project, shared, lat_lon?} · position.relocate(translation, rotation?) · position.rotate_true_north(angle) · position.rotate_project_north(angle, align_views=false) · position.mirror(axis)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Setting the survey point to E 500000, N 5700000 with CRS EPSG:25832 writes an IfcMapConversion and IfcProjectedCRS, and a third-party geo-aware viewer places the model at that location. - [ ] Rotating true north by 30° changes TrueNorth and the shadow direction of sun studies, but no element coordinates. - [ ] Report Shared Coordinates at a picked point gives values consistent with the survey point within 0.1 mm.

    2.10.8 Snaps

    ID: DM-SET-004 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §9.5

    Purpose. Consistent, predictable snapping for every pick, in every tool, with user control over what snaps and at what increments.

    UI. Manage › Settings › Snaps dialog: Snaps Off master switch; Dimension snaps with two lists (length increments and angular increments, each a semicolon-separated list such as 1000; 100; 20; 5 mm and 90; 45; 15; 5; 1 °); an Object snaps check list with each snap's override shortcut beside it; Check all / Check none; Snap to remote objects and Snap to point clouds; Restore defaults; and, when the user has rights, Save as project default.

    Behaviour & rules. - Settings: dimension snap increments (length and angle), which depend on zoom (a list of increments). Object snaps: endpoints, midpoints, nearest, work plane grid, quadrants, intersections, centres, perpendicular, tangents, points, snap to remote objects, snap to point clouds. Each snap has a two-letter override shortcut (UI chapter). - Snap settings are per user (application preferences). An optional project default can be stored in RXD document project/settings. - Increment choice. The increment used at a given moment is the smallest one in the list whose on-screen size is at least 10 pixels (configurable 4–40) at the current zoom, so snapping becomes finer as the user zooms in. - Priority. When several snaps are within the pick tolerance (default 8 pixels), the order is: forced override, endpoint, intersection, centre, midpoint, perpendicular, tangent, quadrant, point, nearest, work-plane grid. The candidate glyph and a tooltip name the snap; Tab cycles among candidates (UI chapter). - Overrides. A two-letter shortcut (the list is owned by the UI chapter; for example SE endpoint, SM midpoint, SI intersection, SC centre, SN nearest, SP perpendicular, ST tangent, SQ quadrant, SX point, SW work-plane grid, SR remote, SO snaps off for the next pick, SS turn override off) applies to the next pick only, even if that snap is switched off. - Validation. Increment lists accept units (§2.9.5); entries must be positive, are de-duplicated and sorted descending on OK; an empty list disables that kind of dimension snap. Angular increments must divide 360° into a whole number of steps or are refused. - Project default. When a project carries a snaps default and the user has never changed their own settings, the project default is used; otherwise the user's settings win. Opening a project never silently overwrites a user's settings. - Snapping is computed by the view's pick service from the visible geometry cache, so remote snaps and point-cloud snaps are limited to what is displayed (and to loaded point-cloud tiles).

    Commands. snaps.get() -> settings · snaps.set(settings) (settings = {enabled, length_increments[], angle_increments[], object_snaps: {name: bool}, remote, point_clouds, pixel_threshold?, scope?: "user"|"project_default"}; neither scope creates an undo item: the user scope is a preference, and the project default is written to project/settings and marks the project modified)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Turning off "Midpoints" stops midpoint snapping in all views. The per-snap shortcut still forces it for the next pick. - [ ] With length increments 1000; 100; 10 mm, drawing a wall at a zoom where 100 mm is 15 pixels snaps lengths to 100 mm; zooming in until 10 mm is 12 pixels snaps to 10 mm. - [ ] Entering an angular increment of 7° is refused with a message; entering "2 ft; 6 in" as length increments is stored as 0.6096 m and 0.1524 m.

    2.10.9 Transfer project standards

    ID: DM-XFER-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §9.6

    Purpose. To copy settings and system-family types from one open project (or template) to another.

    Workflow. 1. Open the source and the target projects. Make the target active. 2. Manage › Settings › Transfer Project Standards. Choose the source project. 3. Tick the item kinds to copy. Each kind expands to show individual items, so selection can be granular. 4. OK. If items with the same name exist, choose Overwrite, New only or Cancel. A summary lists what was copied, renamed or skipped.

    Behaviour & rules. - Transferable kinds include at least: wall, floor, roof, ceiling, stair, railing, ramp, curtain-wall, mullion and panel types; dimension and text types; arrowheads; fill patterns; line patterns; line styles; line weights; materials (with assets); object styles; project information; project units; parameter definitions and bindings; global parameters; view templates; view filters; phase settings and phase filters; print and export setups; keynote and classification settings; colour fill schemes; MEP settings (pipe and duct types, segments, sizes, fluids, system types, electrical settings, load classifications); structural settings; title-block and annotation type settings. - Dependencies are copied too (for example a wall type brings its materials and their fill patterns). Dependencies that already exist are matched by GUID first, then by name. - Overwrite keeps the target's GUIDs, and only replaces values, so references in the target stay valid.

    Commands. standards.list(source_document_id) -> {kind, items[]}[] · standards.transfer(source_document_id, selection[{kind, item_ids?}], on_conflict: overwrite|new_only|rename) -> transfer_report
