    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Transferring one wall type copies it with its 3 materials and 2 fill patterns, which the target did not have, and the report lists all 6 items. - [ ] Transferring with Overwrite a material that exists in the target keeps the target material's GUID and changes its values.

    2.10.10 Classification systems and keynotes

    ID: DM-CLS-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §4.2 (classification code), §11.1 (keynote and classification files), §9.4

    Behaviour & rules. - Classification systems (for example Uniclass 2015, OmniClass, MasterFormat, Uniformat II, CCI, or national systems) are loaded from files into the project. They are stored in IFC as IfcClassification (Source, Edition, Name, Location), with the referenced codes as IfcClassificationReference (Identification, Name, ReferencedSource for hierarchy). They are associated with types or occurrences through IfcRelAssociatesClassification. - Reviera reads classification tables from CSV (code,parent_code,title) and from IFC files that contain IfcClassification trees, and from the buildingSMART Data Dictionary (bSDD) API when online (P2). - The Classification Code / Assembly Code fields in Properties open a searchable tree picker for the active system. More than one system may be used at once (one code per system per element). - Keynotes are tab-separated text files (key, text, parent_key). The path is relative to the project, or absolute. Keynote tags (DOC) read them. Keynote values on elements and materials are parameters (§2.9.2).

    Commands. classification.load(path_or_url, name?) -> system_id · classification.assign(element_ids[], system_id, code) · classification.unassign(element_ids[], system_id) · keynotes.load(path) · keynotes.reload()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Assigning Uniclass Ss_25_10_30 to a wall type writes an IfcClassificationReference with Identification Ss_25_10_30, linked to an IfcClassification named "Uniclass 2015".

    2.10.11 Purge unused

    ID: DM-PURGE-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §9.7

    Purpose. To remove unused content and keep projects lean.

    UI. Manage › Settings › Purge Unused. A tree grouped by kind (families › types, materials, assets, groups, view templates, filters, line patterns, fill patterns, line styles, text and dimension types, unplaced views (optional, off by default), parameter definitions without values, classification systems, RXD orphans), with Check all, Check none, Expand/Collapse and a count per group. OK purges the checked items.

    Behaviour & rules. - "Unused" means: no element, type, view, template, setting or formula refers to the item (computed from the dependency graph and RXD references). - Purge runs multiple passes automatically: removing a family can make its nested families and materials unused. The dialog shows the final result of all passes. It offers a Show items freed by this selection preview. - Items owned by another user (BIMserver advisory locks; COL) cannot be purged and are shown greyed out. - Built-in and system items (built-in line styles, the default material, built-in subcategories) are never offered. - Purge is one transaction, so it can be undone. The option "compact undo after purge" clears the undo stack to free memory.

    Commands. purge.list(include_unplaced_views=false) -> {kind, items[]}[] · purge.run(item_ids[], compact_undo=false) -> report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] In a project with one loaded but unused family that nests two others and uses three materials, a single purge removes all six items, and undo brings them all back.

    2.10.12 Phases and design options (settings)

    ID: DM-PHASE-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §2.4

    Purpose. Define the project's construction sequence, how each phase status is drawn, and which statuses each view shows.

    Workflow. 1. Manage › Phasing › Phases (phase.manage()). The dialog opens on Project Phases. 2. Add phases with Insert Before / Insert After on the selected row; rename in place; give each a description. 3. On Phase Filters, create filters and set each status to By category, Overridden or Not displayed. 4. On Graphic Overrides, set the look of each status. 5. OK applies all changes as one transaction ("Phases"); Cancel discards them.

    Behaviour & rules. - Manage › Phasing › Phases dialog, with three tabs: - Project Phases: an ordered list (earliest first) with columns Number, Name, Description and a Current marker (Set as current chooses the project's current phase, which drives the IFC Status of §2.3.11; the default is the last phase); insert before or after, combine with previous or next, rename; - Phase Filters: New, Existing, Demolished and Temporary states, each set to By category, Overridden or Not displayed; - Graphic Overrides: per phase status, projection and cut line style, fill pattern, halftone, material. - Defaults: phases "Existing" and "New Construction"; phase filters "Show All", "Show Complete", "Show Demo + New", "Show New", "Show Previous + Demo", "Show Previous + New", "Show Previous Phase". - Element status in a view is derived from the view's phase: New (created in the view's phase), Existing (created earlier, not demolished), Demolished (demolished in the view's phase), Temporary (created and demolished in the same phase). Elements created in a later phase are not shown. - Combining phases moves elements of the removed phase into the remaining phase. Views, schedules and rooms whose phase was removed move to the remaining phase too. An element whose created and demolished phases become the same becomes Temporary, and the dialog reports how many. - Validation. Phase and filter names are unique and non-empty. At least one phase must exist; the last phase cannot be combined away. A phase cannot be deleted directly, only combined, so no element is ever left without a phase. The four built-in statuses cannot be renamed. Built-in phase filters can be edited but not deleted; a user filter used by views lists those views before it can be deleted, and they switch to "Show All". - New elements take the active view's phase as Phase Created; demolishing (ARC's Demolish tool) sets Phase Demolished to the view's phase. element.set_phase refuses a demolished phase earlier than the created phase. - IFC. Phases are not IFC entities; on save each element's status relative to the project's current phase is written to Pset_*Common.Status (NEW, EXISTING, DEMOLISH, TEMPORARY) and exchange exports use the phase chosen in the setup (§2.3.11, §2.11.4). - Design options are managed in the ARC chapter. Their storage is §2.3.11.

    Data (storage). RXD document project/phases: kinds phase (name, description, order, GUID), phase.filter (per-status presentation) and phase.override (per-status graphics). Element membership is RXD element data (membership/phasing).

    Commands. phase.create(name, after_phase_id?) -> phase_id · phase.rename(phase_id, name) · phase.combine(phase_id, with: "previous"|"next") · phase_filter.create(name, states) -> id · phase_filter.edit(id, states) · phase.graphic_overrides.set(status, overrides) · element.set_phase(element_ids[], created?, demolished?) · phase.manage() (opens the Phases dialog)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Combining "Phase 2" with "Phase 1" moves every element created in Phase 2 into Phase 1, and views whose phase was Phase 2 change to Phase 1. - [ ] Trying to combine away the only remaining phase is refused; renaming a phase to an existing phase name is refused. - [ ] A wall created in "Existing" and demolished in "New Construction" exports with Pset_WallCommon.Status = DEMOLISH, and a view with phase "New Construction" and filter "Show Demo + New" draws it with the Demolished overrides.

    2.10.13 Starting view and project templates

    ID: DM-SET-005 (starting view) · DM-TMPL-001 (project templates) · Priority: P1 / P0 · Ref: research/05 §9.12, §11.1

    Behaviour & rules. - Starting view: the view opened when the project opens (default: the last view used). It is stored in RXD document project/settings. - Images are managed as described in §2.10.14, and decal types in §2.10.15. - Project templates (DM-TMPL-001, P0). A project template is a project marked as a template in its RXD manifest (02a). By convention it is named <Name>.template.ifc. New Project creates a copy with new GUIDs for everything (project, site, building, storeys, views, types, …), so projects made from the same template never share element GUIDs. Exception: definitions with intended global identity (shared parameter GUIDs, family GUIDs, material RXD GUIDs) keep their GUIDs. - Reviera ships these templates, authored from scratch: Architectural (metric), Architectural (imperial), Multi-discipline (metric), Multi-discipline (imperial), Construction, and Empty.

    Commands. project.new(template_path?) -> document_id · project.save_as_template(path) · settings.starting_view.set(view_id | "last")

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Two projects created from one template have no GlobalId in common for spatial elements, views or system types, but share family GUIDs and shared parameter GUIDs.

    2.10.14 Image management

    ID: DM-IMG-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §9.12; web: Manage Images Dialog; spec/06 COL-LNK-005

    Purpose. One place to see, add, replace and remove every raster image and PDF page image the project holds, whatever uses it: title blocks, drafting views and sheets, schedules (image parameters), materials (textures), decals and family image parameters.

    Workflow. 1. Insert › Import › Manage Images, or Manage › Manage Project › Manage Images (image.manage()). 2. Select an image to see where it is used. Add, reload, replace, place or delete as needed. 3. Each action runs immediately as its own transaction; Close closes the dialog.

    UI. A table with columns Preview (thumbnail), Name (file name with extension), Kind (imported, linked, rendering, texture), Pixel size, File size, Count (placements plus parameter and material uses) and Path (source path; "in project" for images with no external source, such as saved renderings). A Path type switch (Relative to project / Absolute) controls how source paths of linked images are stored. Buttons: Add…, Reload, Reload From…, Place Instance, Show users (lists each view, sheet, element, type or material using the image, with Go to), Delete. Sorting by any column; search by name.

    Behaviour & rules. - Storage and de-duplication. Imported images are RXD assets, de-duplicated by SHA-256 hash: adding the same file twice stores it once (COL-LNK-005). Linked images keep only their path and are re-read on open and on Reload. - Add imports PNG, JPEG, TIFF (first page), BMP and WebP files, and single PDF pages rasterised at a chosen resolution (150–600 dpi, default 300). Images above 16,384 × 16,384 pixels are refused with image.too_large and a downscale offer. - Reload re-reads the image from its recorded path; Reload From points it at another file and replaces the content. Every user keeps its size, position and crop. A missing source keeps the last embedded content (for imported images) or shows a "not found" placeholder (for linked images). - Place Instance places the selected image in the active drafting view, legend or sheet, at its native size (from its dpi, 96 dpi if none), and starts the placement tool (image.place). Placement is one click (native size) or two clicks (opposite corners, with Lock proportions on by default); the tool declares its micro-operations (pick corner, pick opposite corner, toggle proportions) and a replay function, as every interactive tool must (Ch 2b §6.5, DM-LIVE-015). - Delete of an unused image removes it. Deleting an image in use offers to delete its placements too, or to replace it with another image (replace_with), which keeps every placement's size and position and every parameter or material reference. An image parameter value can be cleared without deleting the image (the None choice in the image parameter's picker, §2.9.4). - Changing Path type rewrites the stored paths of all linked images in one transaction; images whose path cannot be made relative (another drive) stay absolute and are listed. - Purge offers unused images (§2.10.11).

    Data (storage). Imported images: RXD assets with hash, original name, pixel size and dpi; placements are view- or sheet-owned records (views/annotation/<viewId>); linked images are kind link.image in project/links (Ch 6). Image parameters hold an asset reference (§2.9.4); material textures are written to IFC as described in DM-MAT-002.

    Commands. image.manage() (opens the dialog) · image.list() -> image[] · image.add(path, page?, dpi?) -> image_id · image.reload(image_id, path?) (no path: re-read the recorded source) · image.place(image_id, view_id, position, width?) -> element_id · image.set_path_type(mode: "relative"|"absolute") -> report · image.delete(image_ids[], replace_with?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Adding the same PNG twice creates one image row whose Count rises as it is placed; the IFC/RXD stores one asset. - [ ] Reload From on a logo used in a title block and two drafting views changes the picture in all three without changing their sizes or positions. - [ ] Deleting an image used as a material texture and in one sheet, with replace_with set, leaves the material and the sheet pointing at the replacement; undo restores the original.

    2.10.15 Decal types

    ID: DM-DECAL-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/05 §9.12; web: Decal Type Properties; web: Decal Attributes

    Purpose. Decals put images (signs, posters, screens, labels) on model faces for rendered and realistic views without modelling them. A decal type holds the image and its rendering attributes; placing it is a DOC tool.

    Workflow. 1. Manage › Manage Project › Decal Types, or Insert › Decal › Decal Types (decal.types()). 2. Create new decal (enter a name), then choose an image source (an existing project image or a new file, §2.10.14) and set its attributes. 3. Choose OK. Place decals with Insert › Decal › Place Decal (decal.place, Chapter 5, DOC-OUT-011).

    UI. Decal Types dialog: a list of decal types on the left (search, New, Duplicate, Rename, Delete); on the right the selected type's attributes with a live preview swatch rendered with the current attributes. The type's identity fields (Type Mark, Manufacturer, Model, Keynote, Description, Type Comments, URL, Cost, Assembly Code) are edited in its Type Properties (§2.2.4).

    Behaviour & rules. - Attributes of a decal type:

    Attribute Range / values Default
    Image A project image (PNG, JPEG, BMP; alpha is used as transparency) — (required)
    Brightness 0–10, a multiplier on the image's luminance 1.0
    Reflectivity 0–1 0.1
    Transparency 0–1 0
    Finish Matte, Satin, Glossy, Polished (sets PBR roughness 0.9 / 0.5 / 0.2 / 0.05) Matte
    Luminance 0–100,000 cd/m², with presets (none, dim screen, LCD screen, lit sign) 0
    Bump pattern None, or a project image used as a height map None
    Bump amount 0–1 0.3
    Cut-outs None, Rectangular, Oval, or an image whose alpha or luminance masks the decal None
    • The attributes map onto the PBR appearance model of DM-MAT-002 (base colour texture, roughness, emissive, opacity, normal or bump), so decals render through the same pipeline as materials and export losslessly to glTF.
    • Editing a type changes every placed decal of that type. Types are unique by name; a type with placements cannot be deleted until its decals are deleted, which the dialog offers.
    • Placing (Chapter 5): decal.place(view_id, decal_type_id, face_ref, position, width?, height?) -> element_id puts a rectangle on a planar or cylindrical face; Lock proportions is on by default. Decals follow their host face when it moves and are deleted with it. They show as a placeholder outline in non-rendered visual styles and as the image in Realistic and rendered views.
    • Decal types and placed decals can be copied between projects with Transfer Project Standards and copy/paste (§2.10.9).
    • IFC. Decals are not building elements. They are not written to exchange exports; with Export IFC with documentation (02a §4) a decal may be written as an IfcAnnotation with a textured surface (P3).

    Data (storage). Decal types: records in RXD document standards/materials (kind decal.type, proposed for 02a), referencing an image asset. Placed decals are stored as Chapter 5 defines for decal.place (DOC-OUT-011): a record holding the type, the host GUID and a stable face reference (§2.8.3).

    Commands. decal.types() (opens the dialog) · decal.type.create(name, image_id, attributes?) -> type_id · decal.type.edit(type_id, attributes) · plus type.duplicate, type.rename and type.delete (§2.2.4), which work on decal types.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A decal type with a PNG with alpha, placed on a wall, renders with the transparent pixels showing the wall material; changing its Brightness to 2 brightens every placed decal of that type. - [ ] Deleting a decal type with 3 placements is refused until the placements are deleted, and the dialog offers to delete them in the same transaction. - [ ] A glTF export of a 3D view with a decal contains a textured quad on the wall face using the decal image.

    2.10.16 Rule-based numbering

    ID: DM-NUM-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/05 §14 (2027: rule-based numbering); web: What's New in Revit 2027 (Symetri); web: Revit 2027 (BIM Pure)

    Purpose. Number elements automatically and consistently from rules, such as "doors numbered per room as <Room Number>-A, -B", or "columns per level as L2-C001", instead of typing marks by hand or running scripts.

    Workflow. 1. Manage › Numbering › Rule-Based Numbering (numbering.rule_based()). The dialog lists the project's numbering rules. 2. New (+): name the rule, for example "Doors by room". 3. Elements: choose one or more categories, then optionally a filter: an existing view filter, or rules built in place with the same rule editor as view filters (parameter · operator · value, nested AND/OR sets). Elements that match can also be excluded by a condition (for example Comments equals "Exclude"). The matching count is shown live. 4. Target: choose the parameter that receives the number. Default: Mark for instance rules, Type Mark for type rules. Any writable text or integer instance parameter (built-in, project or shared) that is bound to every chosen category may be used. 5. Partition (optional): choose one or more parameters, for example Level, or To Room: Number. Each distinct combination of values forms its own sequence, numbered independently. With no partition, all matching elements form one sequence. 6. Matching (optional): choose when elements count as "the same" and share one number: None (default), Same type, Same values of chosen parameters, or Same type and geometry. 7. Format: build the number from segments, with a live sample: literal text, the value of a parameter (from the element, its type, its level or room), and the counter. The counter is digits (minimum width with leading zeros), upper-case letters or lower-case letters (A…Z, AA…; with an optional skip list, default I and O). Set the start value (default 1 or A) and the increment (default 1); a start may be overridden per partition value. 8. Order: choose how elements in a sequence are ordered: Creation order (default), By location (left to right then top to bottom, or by distance along a picked path), or Sorted by up to three parameters. 9. Review the preview table (element, sequence, current value, proposed value, conflicts). Choose Apply now to number, and tick Apply automatically to keep numbering new and changed elements. 10. OK saves the rules; the changes and any numbering applied are one transaction ("Rule-Based Numbering").

    UI. Left: the ordered list of rules (name, categories, target, enabled, auto) with New, Duplicate, Rename, Delete, Move Up/Down. Right: the rule editor in five sections (Elements, Target, Partition and Matching, Format, Order). Bottom: the preview table with filters (Changes only, Conflicts only) and a Select in model button. A rule with an error shows a red marker and the reason.

    Behaviour & rules. - Sequences. A sequence is identified by the rule and the partition values. An element with no value for a partition parameter goes into a "(none)" sequence of its own. Within a sequence, matched elements always get the same number and unmatched elements never share one. - Automatic mode. Enabled rules with Apply automatically run as a built-in updater (§2.13.5) inside the transaction that adds elements, or that changes a partition, filter or matching parameter. New elements get the next free number of their sequence; an element that moves to another sequence (for example to another room) gets the next free number there. Changes are part of the user's undo item. Automatic mode never renumbers elements that keep their sequence, so numbers stay stable as the model grows. - Apply now offers two modes: Fill missing (only elements with an empty target) and Renumber all (recomputes every element in the rule's scope by its order, closing gaps). Renumber all shows the number of changed values before applying. - Manual edits. When a user edits the target value of a numbered element by hand, the element is marked manually numbered for that rule and is skipped by automatic mode; its value still counts as taken in its sequence. Reset to rule clears the mark. - Gaps. Deleting an element leaves a gap; automatic mode does not reuse it (to keep issued numbers stable) unless the rule's Reuse gaps option is on. - Several rules. Rules are evaluated in list order. If two enabled rules would write the same target parameter of the same element, the later one is skipped for that element and the dialog shows an overlap warning on both rules. Rules writing different targets may overlap freely. - Uniqueness check. After numbering, duplicate values of the target within a sequence (possible after manual edits) raise a warning (§2.7.4) that names the elements. - Groups and linked models. Elements inside group instances are numbered only when the target is bound with values can vary by group instance (§2.9.3); otherwise they are skipped and reported. Elements in linked models are never numbered. - BIMserver mode. Numbers assigned locally may collide with numbers assigned by another user in the same sequence. After a sync, colliding elements in automatic rules are renumbered in order of creation time then GUID, and the sync report lists every changed value. - Validation. A rule needs a name (unique), at least one category and a target parameter bound to every chosen category; the format must contain exactly one counter segment; the start must be valid for the counter kind; partition and order parameters must exist on the chosen categories. Invalid rules can be saved disabled but cannot be applied.

    Data (storage). Rules: records of kind numbering.rule in RXD document project/settings (proposed for 02a): name, order, enabled, auto, categories, filter (a filter.rule reference or an inline rule), target parameter, partition parameters, matching mode, format segments, start overrides per partition value, order mode, gap policy. Per-element state (the rule ID that last numbered it and the manual flag) is RXD element data elements (numbering). Numbers themselves are ordinary parameter values, so they reach IFC through the target parameter's IFC home (for Mark, IfcElement.Tag).

    Commands. numbering.rule_based() (opens the dialog) · numbering.rule.create(def) -> rule_id · numbering.rule.edit(rule_id, changes) · numbering.rule.delete(rule_id) · numbering.rule.reorder(rule_ids[]) · numbering.preview(rule_id | def, element_ids?) -> [{element_id, sequence, current, proposed, conflict?}] · numbering.apply(rule_id?, mode: "fill_missing"|"renumber_all", element_ids?) -> report · numbering.reset_manual(element_ids[], rule_id?)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A rule "Doors by room" (doors; target Mark; partition To Room: Number; format <To Room: Number>-<letters A>) numbers the three doors of room 101 as 101-A, 101-B, 101-C and the door of room 102 as 102-A. - [ ] With Apply automatically on, placing a fourth door into room 101 sets its Mark to 101-D in the same undo item as the placement; moving it into room 102 changes it to 102-B. - [ ] Two identical chairs of the same type, with matching Same type and geometry, get the same number; a third chair of another type gets the next number. - [ ] A door whose Mark was typed by hand keeps it through Fill missing and automatic numbering, and Reset to rule brings it back under the rule. - [ ] A rule whose format has no counter segment cannot be applied, and the dialog names the error.

    2.11 File I/O

    2.11.0 Creating new documents

    ID: DM-FILE-006 · Priority: P0 (model, model template, family) / P1 (title block, annotation symbol, conceptual mass) · Ref: research/05 §4.1, §9.12, §11.1; spec/01 (File › New, Reviera Home)

    Purpose. One entry point to start any kind of Reviera document from a template.

    Workflow. 1. File › New (Ctrl+N), or New… on Reviera Home (file.new(kind, template?, schema?)). The New dialog opens for the chosen kind (Model by default). 2. For a model: choose a project template from the list (from the template folders in Options › File Locations, plus Browse… and None), choose Create new: Model or Model template, and, in Local mode, the IFC schema (IFC4, default, or IFC4X3). 3. For a family, title block, annotation symbol or conceptual mass: the family template chooser opens, filtered to that kind (§2.8.1). 4. OK creates an untitled document and opens its starting view. The document is saved only when the user saves.

    Behaviour & rules. - Kinds. model copies the chosen project template with new GUIDs (DM-TMPL-001; the same operation as project.new). model_template does the same, but the result is flagged as a template, so its first save defaults to <Name>.template.ifc. family, title_block, annotation_symbol and mass_family call family_doc.new with a template of that kind; template is then a family template path, and a template of the wrong kind is refused with file.template_kind_mismatch. - No template. template omitted for a model uses the default template set in Options; None creates an empty project with one site, one building, one storey ("Level 1", elevation 0), SI units in IFC, the Metric (mm) display preset and the built-in standards (line weights, patterns, object styles). Families always need a template. - Schema. schema applies to models only. IFC4X3 is offered only in Local mode and when the template's schema allows it; a template saved in IFC4 is converted on creation (§2.11.3) with the usual report. In BIMserver mode the schema is the server project's schema. - Untitled documents get a live store at once (Ch 2b §2), so work is recoverable before the first save. The title bar shows "Untitled 1", "Untitled 2", … per session. - Missing or invalid templates (not found, not a Reviera template, newer RXD major version) are reported in the dialog with the reason, and the user picks another; a template from an older RXD version is migrated in memory (§2.11.8). - New documents take the project information defaults from the template, with Project Issue Date set to today and Author set to the user name from Options.

    Data (storage). Nothing is written until the first save. The new project's Reviera_Manifest records the source template's name and DataId for traceability (02a).

    Commands. file.new(kind: model|model_template|family|title_block|annotation_symbol|mass_family, template?, schema?: IFC4|IFC4X3) -> document_id (plus project.new, §2.10.13, and family_doc.new, §2.8.0, which it calls)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] file.new(kind="model") with no template and no default creates a project with one storey "Level 1" that saves as a valid IFC4 file. - [ ] file.new(kind="family", template="Door.familytemplate.ifc") opens a family document with the door template's references and parameters; passing a title-block template with kind="family" fails with file.template_kind_mismatch. - [ ] A new untitled model, edited and then killed before any save, is offered in the recovery dialog on restart.

    2.11.1 Opening models

    ID: DM-FILE-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §11.1, §11.2, §12.1; TECH_STACK §3.1, §3.7

    Purpose. To open any IFC file, whether written by Reviera or by another tool, and make it editable.

    Workflow. 1. File › Open (Ctrl+O), choose an .ifc or .ifczip file. Or choose a recent file on Reviera Home (UI chapter), or a BIMserver project (COL chapter). 2. A progress bar shows the stages: parse → build element store → RXD binding and checks (§2.4.3) → regeneration of view caches for the starting view. 3. If the file needs a schema upgrade, or has RXD warnings, a summary dialog lists them before editing begins.

    Behaviour & rules. - Parsing uses IfcOpenShell. The file is parsed on a worker thread. The UI stays responsive, and Cancel is available. - Geometry is not recomputed from RXD on open. The IFC geometry is used as is (tessellated with OCCT, in parallel). Regeneration only runs for elements that are edited later, or flagged by reconciliation. This keeps open times proportional to file size. - Foreign elements. Elements without RXD (from other tools) become IFC-native elements: - they can be selected, moved, copied, rotated, mirrored, deleted, scheduled and tagged; - their properties can be edited; - their geometry is fixed (treated like a direct shape). - Recognise (Modify › Recognise, P1) converts them to parametric Reviera elements where possible: walls with an IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage and an extruded or clipped body become basic walls; extruded slabs become floors with a sketch; storey-contained doors and windows in openings become placed instances of static families made from their types. Recognition never changes the GUIDs. It reports elements it could not convert. - Large models (P1). Partial open: choose storeys, disciplines (by IFC class) or worksets to load; unloaded elements stay in the file untouched and are written back on save. Incremental open (P2): show the model while geometry is still being tessellated, coarse first. - Read-only open is available (for example, for files on read-only media). Save is disabled, and Save As is offered. - Files from a newer Reviera follow §2.11.8. - IFC open options (File › Open › IFC open options…; file.ifc_open_options(options?) -> options). A per-user dialog that sets the defaults used when opening IFC files; called without arguments it opens the dialog, with options it sets them and returns the result. Settings: - Partial open: always open everything (default), or always ask with the storey, IFC-class and workset chooser; - Incremental open (P2): on or off; - Third-party files: run Recognise automatically on open (off by default), and which classes to try (walls, slabs, doors and windows); - Unit conversion report: show, or only log; - Tessellation quality for third-party B-rep and swept geometry: coarse, normal (default), fine (chordal deviation 5 mm / 1 mm / 0.2 mm, angular 20° / 10° / 5°); - Schema upgrade: for IFC2X3 files, open as an upgraded copy (default) or read-only; - Missing RXD sidecar: look for it silently, or always ask (§2.4.3). Values are validated on OK (for example a chordal deviation must be between 0.05 mm and 50 mm). The options apply to the next open; the File › Open dialog shows the active options in a summary line with a link to change them for that one open.

    Commands. file.open(path, {partial?: {storeys?, classes?, worksets?}, read_only?}) -> document_id · file.close(document_id, save?: "ask"|"yes"|"no") · element.recognise(element_ids[]) -> report · file.ifc_open_options(options?) -> options

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 500 MB IFC4 file from another authoring tool opens in under 60 s on the reference machine (8 cores, 32 GB), and every element is selectable, schedulable and exportable. - [ ] Recognise on 200 third-party walls with layer-set usages converts at least 95% to basic walls with the same layers and GUIDs, and reports the rest with a reason. - [ ] Opening a file with partial load (one storey), editing it and saving keeps the unloaded storeys' entities byte-equivalent in a semantic diff. - [ ] Setting Partial open to always ask in IFC open options makes the next File › Open show the storey chooser; the setting persists across application restarts.

    2.11.2 Saving

    ID: DM-FILE-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §11.1, §11.2; TECH_STACK §3.1

    Behaviour & rules. - Save (Ctrl+S) writes the project in its current schema to .ifc (STEP, ISO 10303-21) or .ifczip (a ZIP holding one .ifc file, as buildingSMART defines). RXD is written with it, in the carrier set for the project (embedded by default; 02a). - Atomic write. Saving writes to a temporary file in the same folder, flushes it to disk, then renames it over the original. A failure or crash during save never damages the original file. - Background save. Saving serialises a committed snapshot on a worker thread. The user can keep working. Edits made during the save are included in the next save. - Deterministic output. For an unchanged model, two saves produce identical files except the header timestamp. Entity order is stable: by kind (project and contexts, units, spatial structure, types, elements, relationships, resources), then by GlobalId (or by owner for non-rooted entities). STEP instance numbers are reassigned in that order. This makes .ifc files usable in version control and keeps diffs small. - Backups. Local saves keep N previous versions (default 3), as <name>.<nnnn>.ifc in a <name>_backup folder next to the project. Each backup is a full copy (with its RXD). - Save As can change the file name, the format (.ifc ↔ .ifczip) and the RXD carrier (embedded, sidecar, or both; 02a). It cannot change the schema. Use Convert Schema for that (§2.11.3). - File locking. In Local mode, Reviera creates a lock file (.~lock.<name>#) while a project is open, and warns if another user or process has the file open. It then offers read-only open. - Compression. .ifczip uses DEFLATE (level 6 by default). STEP text for large models typically compresses by 80–90%.

    Commands. file.save(document_id? (default: active)) -> status · file.save_as(document_id? (default: active), path, kind?, format?: ifc|ifczip, carrier?: embedded|external_file|external_dir|bundle) -> status · file.backups(document_id) -> backup[] · file.restore_backup(document_id, backup_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Killing the process at a random point during save (tested 100 times) never leaves a corrupt or truncated project file. The original or the new file is always intact. - [ ] Saving the same unchanged model twice gives byte-identical files except the FILE_NAME timestamp. - [ ] Editing during a background save of a 300 MB model is possible, and the next save includes the edit.

    2.11.3 IFC schema policy and conversion

    ID: DM-FILE-003 · Priority: P0 (IFC4 read/write, IFC2X3 read) / P1 (IFC4X3 projects, IFC2X3 export) · Ref: research/05 §11.2, §12.1, §12.2; TECH_STACK §3.1, §3.7.3

    Behaviour & rules.

    Schema Open Native project schema Export
    IFC2X3 TC1 ✔ (upgraded in memory to IFC4) ✘ ✔ (Coordination View 2.0)
    IFC4 ADD2 TC1 ✔ ✔ default ✔ (Reference View, Design Transfer View)
    IFC4X3 ADD2 ✔ ✔ (Local mode; BIMserver mode only if the server supports it) ✔ (Reference View)
    IFC-XML / IFC-JSON (.ifcxml, .ifcjson) P3 ✘ P3
    IFC5 (alpha) Watch list ✘ ✘
    • Convert Schema (File › Convert Schema) upgrades IFC4 → IFC4X3 or downgrades IFC4X3 → IFC4. Both directions keep GUIDs. Entities that have no counterpart in the target schema (for example IFC4X3 infrastructure classes in IFC4) are converted to IfcBuildingElementProxy with ObjectType set to the source class name. The original class is kept in RXD element data, so a later upgrade can restore it. A report lists every conversion.
    • IFC2X3 open upgrades with the same mapping as IfcOpenShell's schema-migration tooling (for example IfcWallStandardCase → IfcWall; type ApplicableOccurrence and owner history handled as IFC4 requires; property names updated where buildingSMART renamed them). Elements and properties that cannot be mapped are kept as proxies and listed in the report.
    • Units on open. Files in non-SI units (for example millimetres or feet) are converted to SI on open. Saving writes SI (§2.3.1). The conversion is reported once.

    Commands. file.convert_schema(document_id, target: "IFC4"|"IFC4X3_ADD2") -> report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An IFC2X3 sample set (at least 20 files from public buildingSMART and open-source test suites) opens with no crash, and with all IfcProduct entities present after upgrade. - [ ] IFC4 → IFC4X3 → IFC4 keeps every GUID, and every property value.

    2.11.4 IFC export setups (exchange exports)

    ID: DM-FILE-004 · Priority: P0 (basic Reference View export) / P1 (setups, property mapping) / P2 (IDS validation) · Ref: research/05 §12.1, §12.2, §12.3; screenshots/platform/ifc_property_mapping_2027.png

    Purpose. The native file is already IFC. Export produces a derived IFC file for a specific exchange (a Model View Definition, a client requirement, a coordination platform), leaving the native file unchanged.

    UI. File › Export › IFC. The dialog has a named setup drop-down (New, Duplicate, Rename, Delete, Import/Export setup as JSON) and these tabs: - General: - schema and MVD: IFC4 Reference View; IFC4 Design Transfer View; IFC2X3 Coordination View 2.0; IFC4X3 Reference View; - phase to export; - design options (primary only, or all); - space boundaries (none, first level, second level); - coordinate base (internal origin, project base point, survey point, shared site); - split walls, columns and ducts by storey; - file format (.ifc, .ifczip). - Content: - export only elements visible in a chosen view; - include RXD (off for exchange exports; it makes a "native" copy when on); - export annotation as IfcAnnotation (P2); - export rooms, areas and zones; - base quantities on or off; - material layer, profile and constituent sets on or off; - classification systems to include; - export parameter templates (IfcPropertySetTemplate) for user parameters; - level of detail (Coarse, Medium, Fine) for the Body; - Reviera-only categories (masses, reference planes): exclude by default. - Property Mapping (P1): - a tree of IFC classes on the left, with a filter; - for the selected class, a grid of property sets and properties: include on/off; target property set and property name; data type; source (a Reviera parameter, a formula over parameters, or a constant); and reset to default per row; - pre-defined groups: IFC common property sets, Base quantities, User parameters; - mapping profiles can be saved per setup, and exported or imported as JSON. - This takes the place of a mapping text file. Ref: screenshots/platform/ifc_property_mapping_2027.png. - Validation (P2): - validate the result against IFC schema and normative rules (IfcOpenShell validator); - validate against an IDS file (buildingSMART Information Delivery Specification 1.0), with a report linking failing elements back to the model.

    Behaviour & rules. - Exports run on a committed snapshot in the background, with progress and cancel. - An export never changes GUIDs. The same element has the same GlobalId in the native file and in every export. Elements that are split by storey get derived GUIDs, as UUID v5 of (element GUID, storey GUID), and are aggregated under an IfcElementAssembly that carries the original GUID. - Setups are stored in RXD document project/settings (ifc_export_setups[]). Shipped default setups: IFC4 Reference View, IFC4 Design Transfer View, IFC2X3 Coordination View 2.0, IFC4X3 Reference View.

    Commands. export.ifc(path, setup? (name, id or inline settings), settings_override?, schema?, strip_rxd?=false, documentation?, background?) -> job_id · export.ifc_setup.save(setup) · export.ifc_setup.delete(name) · export.ifc_setup.list() -> setup[] · validate.ifc(path?) -> report · validate.ids(ids_path, scope?) -> report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An IFC4 Reference View export of the sample project passes the buildingSMART validation service with no errors. - [ ] A property mapping that sends parameter "Acoustic Class" to Pset_DoorCommon.AcousticRating for doors produces that property in the export, and leaves the native file unchanged. - [ ] Every GUID in the export also exists in the native file (except split-element GUIDs, which are derived deterministically). - [ ] An IDS requiring Pset_WallCommon.FireRating on all external walls reports the 3 walls with no value, and each report row selects the wall in the model.

    2.11.5 Import and link formats

    ID: DM-IMP-001 … 012 · Priority: see table · Ref: research/05 §12.1, §12.3

    Behaviour & rules. - Insert › Import brings content into the model, as an import element in a view (2D), or as model geometry (3D). Insert › Link keeps a reference to the external file, reloaded on open or on demand (COL chapter for links of IFC and Reviera models). - Common options for CAD imports: - positioning: auto centre-to-centre, auto origin-to-internal-origin, by shared coordinates, or manual; - units: auto-detect, or a chosen unit; - current view only (2D); - layer selection: all, visible, or chosen; - colours: preserve, invert, or black and white; - correct lines slightly off axis. - Imported CAD becomes an import instance with an Imported Objects subcategory per layer (§2.10.3). Import instances can be exploded (partially or fully) into detail lines, text and filled regions, or into model lines. They are stored as RXD assets (the source file, or a converted cache) plus an RXD document views/annotation/<viewId> record (2D) or an IfcBuildingElementProxy with tessellated geometry (3D, ObjectType = ImportedGeometry). - Open libraries only. Every format is implemented with GPL-3.0-compatible libraries. Formats that need proprietary SDKs are P3, with an open alternative noted.

    ID Format Import Link Priority Library (licence) Notes
    DM-IMP-001 IFC (2X3, 4, 4X3) ✔ (open, or merge into the current model) ✔ P0 (open) / P1 (merge, link) IfcOpenShell (LGPL-3.0) Merge keeps GUIDs. Clashing GUIDs get new ones, with a report. Merge options: target storeys (by name match, by elevation within 1 mm, or a chosen storey), IFC classes to include, and whether to bring property sets for unknown definitions. Merged elements without RXD are IFC-native (§2.11.1) until recognised. Linking an IFC keeps it read-only and reloads it on change (COL). The merge is one transaction.
    DM-IMP-002 DXF (R12–2018) ✔ ✔ P1 LibreDWG (GPL-3.0+) DXF reader, or a Rust DXF crate (MIT) Layers, blocks (as nested import groups), text, hatches, dimensions (as exploded geometry). Units come from $INSUNITS, or the chosen unit when it is missing. Splines are kept as NURBS, arcs and ellipses as exact curves; proxy and unsupported entities are listed in the import report. Layer visibility and colour can be overridden per view (DOC).
    DM-IMP-003 DWG (R13–2018 and later where the library supports it) ✔ ✔ P1 LibreDWG (GPL-3.0+) Coverage depends on LibreDWG. Unsupported entities are listed in a report. Same options and results as DXF. Xrefs are resolved from the DWG's folder and imported as nested groups, or skipped with a warning. Files saved by versions newer than the library supports are refused with the version found and a suggestion to save as DXF from the source tool.
    DM-IMP-004 PDF (as underlay) ✔ ✔ P1 PDFium (BSD-3/Apache-2.0) Choose a page, resolution, and vector snapping to the PDF's path geometry. Pages are rendered at 72–600 dpi (default 150) for display; vector paths are extracted once into a snapping cache. Scale is set by the page's declared size or calibrated by two picked points of known distance. Password-protected PDFs are refused. Placed in plan, drafting and sheet views.
    DM-IMP-005 Images (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, BMP, WebP) ✔ ✔ P1 image crate (MIT/Apache-2.0) Placed in views, or on sheets. Images are RXD assets de-duplicated by hash, or linked by path (§2.10.14, COL-LNK-005). Native size comes from the image's dpi (96 dpi if none); maximum 16,384 × 16,384 pixels. Draw layer background or foreground; scale calibration by two points; alpha transparency kept.
    DM-IMP-006 OBJ, STL, PLY ✔ (project or family) — P1 Rust crates (MIT/Apache-2.0) Mesh. Optional decimation, and conversion to IfcTriangulatedFaceSet. Options: units (auto from file, or chosen), up-axis (Y or Z), merge coplanar triangles, decimate to a target triangle count, and category. Into a family, the mesh becomes a non-parametric form; into a project, a direct shape (§2.13.10). Non-manifold meshes are accepted for display and flagged.
    DM-IMP-007 glTF 2.0 / GLB ✔ (project or family) — P2 gltf crate (MIT/Apache-2.0) Mesh with PBR materials (mapped to §2.10.5). Each glTF material becomes a Reviera material (matched by name to existing ones, or created) with its textures as RXD assets. Node hierarchy becomes nested groups or one element per node (option). Animations and cameras are ignored with a note.
    DM-IMP-008 STEP AP203/AP214/AP242, IGES, BREP ✔ (project or family) — P1 OCCT (LGPL-2.1 + exception) Exact B-rep, used for manufacturer content in families. Solids keep exact faces (IfcAdvancedBrep on export); assemblies can be imported as one element or one element per part. Units come from the file. Colour and layer attributes (AP214/AP242) set materials and subcategories. Healing (sewing, small-edge removal) runs with a report.
    DM-IMP-009 3DM (Rhino) ✔ — P2 openNURBS (licence to be checked) Only if the licence check passes; otherwise P3. Imports breps, extrusions and meshes with layer names as subcategories; NURBS surfaces kept exact. Block instances become nested groups. Units from the file.
    DM-IMP-010 Point clouds: E57, LAS/LAZ, PLY — ✔ P2 libE57Format (BSL-1.0), las/laz crates (MIT/Apache-2.0) Indexed into an octree cache stored on disk next to the project (not part of IFC or RXD; rebuilt if missing). The link itself is in RXD document project/links. Snapping to points. Indexing runs in the background with progress; display uses level-of-detail streaming within a point budget (default 5 million points). Colour by RGB, intensity, elevation or classification. Clipped by section boxes and view ranges.
    DM-IMP-011 BCF 2.1 / 3.0 (.bcfzip) ✔ — P1 Built in (XML, ZIP) Topics, viewpoints and comments, linked to elements by IFC GUID (COL chapter). Viewpoints restore camera, section planes, visibility and selection. Components with GUIDs not found in the model are listed. Re-importing the same file updates topics by GUID instead of duplicating them.
    DM-IMP-012 gbXML ✔ (as masses or spaces) — P3 — The ANA chapter covers export. Import would create masses or spaces from Campus/Building/Space surfaces; it stays P3 because round-tripping analytical geometry rarely helps authoring.
    — SKP, DGN (V8), SAT, FBX, NWC/NWD, RVT/RFA, ADSK, AXM — — P3 No open library with acceptable licence and coverage Open alternative: export to IFC, DXF, glTF or STEP from the source tool. DGN V7 might be reachable through GDAL/OGR (MIT), which is a P3 candidate.
    • Reference-product models. There is no open reader for the reference product's native files. The supported migration path is: export IFC4 from the reference product (its exporter is open source); import the shared-parameter file (§2.9.7); import lookup tables and type catalogs (§2.8.8, §2.8.9); then use Recognise (§2.11.1). The migration guide shall document recommended exporter settings.

    Commands. import.cad(path, view_id?, options) -> import_id · link.cad(path, view_id?, options) -> element_id · import.explode(import_id, mode: partial|full) -> element_ids[] · import.pdf(path, page, view_id, options) -> element_id · import.image(path, view_id, placement) -> element_id · import.mesh(path, target: "project"|"family", category?, options) -> element_id · import.step(path, target: "project"|"family", category?) -> element_id · link.point_cloud(path, placement) -> element_id · import.bcf(path) -> topic_id[] · import.ifc_merge(path, options) -> report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A DXF R2018 file with 50 layers, blocks and hatches imports into a plan view. Each layer appears as an Imported Objects subcategory, and Explode produces detail lines on matching line styles. - [ ] A STEP AP214 file of a manufacturer's product imports into a Generic Model family as an exact B-rep, and exports from a project as IfcAdvancedBrep. - [ ] A vector PDF underlay offers snapping to its line endpoints.

    2.11.6 Export formats

    ID: DM-EXP-001 … 012 · Priority: see table · Ref: research/05 §12.2

    ID Format Source Priority Library (licence) Notes
    DM-EXP-001 PDF (vector) Sheets and views P0 Defined in DOC (own vector pipeline; for example pdf-writer, MIT/Apache-2.0) Combined or separate files, naming rules, print order, raster fallback for shaded views. Fonts are embedded as subsets; text stays selectable and searchable. Sheet size, orientation and margins come from the title block; line weights from the line weight table at the view scale (§2.10.4). PDF/A-2b output is an option. Details in DOC.
    DM-EXP-002 IFC (exchange) Model P0/P1 IfcOpenShell §2.11.4. Exchange exports never change the native file. Clean IFC (strip_rxd) and IFC with documentation are options of the same command (02a §4). Setups, property mapping and IDS validation as in §2.11.4.
    DM-EXP-003 DXF Views and sheets (2D), 3D views (3D) P1 Own writer, or LibreDWG Layer mapping by category and subcategory, using layer standard tables (for example ISO 13567, AIA, BS 1192). Text, hatches, dimensions as entities or exploded. Versions R2000–R2018 selectable. Sheets export with views as model-space xrefs or flattened into paper space (option). Colours by layer or by entity; line patterns as linetypes. Fill patterns become hatches using the .pat definitions (§2.10.4).
    DM-EXP-004 DWG Views and sheets P2 LibreDWG (GPL-3.0+) DWG output depends on LibreDWG write support (check version coverage). DXF is the recommended fallback. Same setups, layer mapping and naming as DXF. If the chosen version cannot be written, the job fails for that file with a message suggesting DXF, and the rest of the batch continues.
    DM-EXP-005 Images (PNG, JPEG, TIFF) Views and sheets P1 image crate Resolution, size, visual style, crop. Size by pixel width or height, or by dpi at the sheet's paper size; maximum 16,384 pixels per side. Background white, transparent (PNG) or as shown. Each view or sheet becomes one file named by the naming rule.
    DM-EXP-006 glTF 2.0 / GLB 3D views P1 gltf crate PBR materials (§2.10.5), element GUIDs and selected parameters in extras, one node per element, instancing for repeated types. Options: binary GLB or glTF with separate files, Draco mesh compression (on or off), texture size limit, which parameters to include, and coordinate base (internal origin, survey point). Only elements visible in the view are exported.
    DM-EXP-007 OBJ (+MTL) 3D views P1 Own writer One object per element (named by GUID), MTL materials with diffuse colour and base texture; units in metres; Y-up or Z-up option. Hidden elements in the view are skipped.
    DM-EXP-008 STL Selection, or 3D view P2 Own writer For 3D printing. Watertight check. Binary or ASCII STL; scale factor and units chosen; a report lists open edges and self-intersections per element before writing.
    DM-EXP-009 gbXML Spaces and analytical model P2 Own writer Defined in the ANA chapter. Written from rooms or spaces and the energy analytical model, with constructions and openings.
    DM-EXP-010 BCF 2.1 / 3.0 Issues P1 Built in COL chapter. Writes the selected topics with viewpoints (camera, section planes, visible and selected components by IFC GUID) and comments.
    DM-EXP-011 CSV / TSV / XLSX Schedules P0 (CSV) / P1 (XLSX) rust_xlsxwriter (MIT/Apache-2.0) DOC chapter. Exports the schedule as shown: headers, grouping rows and totals optional; values formatted (display units) or raw (SI). XLSX keeps column widths and number formats.
    DM-EXP-012 SQLite parameter database Model parameters P2 rusqlite (MIT) Open alternative to ODBC export: one table per category with every parameter, keyed by GUID. Re-import of edited values (P2) by GUID. Extra tables hold types, levels, rooms and the parameter definitions (data type, unit); values are stored in SI with a unit column. Re-import updates only writable parameters, as one transaction with a change report, and ignores rows whose GUID is not in the model.
    — STEP AP242 Selection P2 OCCT Exact solids for fabrication
    — SVG Views and sheets P2 Own writer
    — USD 3D views P3 OpenUSD (licence compatibility to be checked) Open alternative: glTF
    — DWF/DWFx, NWC, FBX, ADSK — P3 Proprietary Open alternatives: PDF, IFC, glTF
    • Bulk export (DM-EXP-013, P1). File › Export › Batch Export: choose sheets and views, and one or more formats (PDF, DXF/DWG, images, IFC, glTF). Each output has a naming rule built from parameters (for example {Sheet Number}-{Sheet Name}-{Current Revision}). Batch export runs in the background, with a report. Batch-export sets are saved in RXD document project/settings.

    2.11.7 Headless and command-line operation

    ID: DM-FILE-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §13.3 (cloud batch processing), §11.2 (batch upgrade)

    Purpose. An open, local equivalent of cloud batch processing: run Reviera without a UI for upgrades, exports, checks and configurators.

    Behaviour & rules. - reviera --headless [--script <file.lua>] [--command <name> --args <json>] [--trust <level>] <model.ifc> … runs commands or Lua scripts against one or more models, then exits. The exit code is 0 for success and non-zero for failure, and a JSON report goes to stdout or to a file. - reviera --mcp-stdio [model.ifc] starts the MCP server on stdio without a UI (§2.16.2). - Headless mode uses the same command registry and transactions. Commands that need user interaction (picks, dialogs) fail with ui.required, unless their parameters are fully given. - Typical scripts: batch schema conversion, batch IFC/PDF export, model checking, parameter updates from CSV, and family package upgrades.

    Commands. (process-level, not registry commands) — documented in the user manual.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] reviera --headless --command export.ifc --args '{"path":"out.ifc","setup_name":"IFC4 Reference View"}' model.ifc produces the same file as the UI export. - [ ] Running a headless script on 100 files in a loop uses all cores when invoked as several processes, and leaks no memory between files within one process.

    2.11.8 Versioning, upgrade and migration

    ID: DM-MIG-001 · Priority: P0 (rules) / P1 (save to previous RXD version) · Ref: research/05 §11.2, §16.9

    Purpose. To avoid the reference product's one-way, yearly file-format break.

    Behaviour & rules. - Two version axes: 1. the IFC schema (governed by buildingSMART; §2.11.3); 2. the RXD schema version (semver, set by Reviera; 02a). The application version is recorded too, but it does not by itself make files incompatible. - Compatibility promise: - Same RXD major version: any Reviera release opens and saves the file without loss. Newer minor versions add optional keys. Older releases keep unknown keys (§2.4.1) and warn that "some features were created in a newer version and are shown read-only". - Newer RXD major version: older releases open the file as IFC-only plus read-only RXD. Building elements and parameters are editable. RXD documents that cannot be read are kept unchanged on save, and are flagged as stale for reconciliation when the newer release reopens the file. - Older RXD major version: newer releases migrate on open, using a chain of migration steps (vN → vN+1 → …). Each step is a pure function over RXD documents, with a unit test and sample files. The original file is never overwritten until the user saves, and a backup of the pre-migration file is kept. - Save to previous version (P1). File › Save As › Previous Version writes RXD at the previous major version, when the model uses no features that exist only in the newer one. If it does, the dialog lists those features, and they are dropped (or turned into static IFC geometry) on export. - Family packages follow the same rules. A batch upgrade of a folder of families is available through the headless mode (§2.11.7) and the family.package.upgrade command. - Release policy. RXD major versions should change at most once every two years, with at least one year of overlap where the previous major version can still be written.

    Commands. file.save_previous_version(document_id, path) -> report · family.package.upgrade(paths[], in_place=false) -> report · rxd.migration_report(document_id) -> report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A project saved by release N (RXD 1.4) opens in release N−1 (RXD 1.2) with no data loss on save. The 1.4-only keys are kept and the user is warned. - [ ] A project with RXD 2.0 opened in a 1.x release keeps all 2.0 RXD documents byte-identical through an edit and save of building elements. - [ ] Each migration step has a test that migrates a sample file, and checks the result against the target JSON Schema.

    2.12 The command registry

    2.12.1 Command definitions

    ID: DM-CMD-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §13.1 (external commands), §16.11; TECH_STACK §2, §3.5, §3.6

    Purpose. Every operation is defined once, as a typed command. The UI, Lua, add-ins, MCP, the journal and the documentation are all generated from that definition.

    Behaviour & rules. - A command definition (Rust: a struct implementing a Command trait, registered at start-up with a macro; Lua add-ins register commands through the same registry, §2.14) shall contain:

    Field Meaning
    name domain.verb or domain.sub.verb, lower snake case (for example wall.create, family_doc.form.extrusion). Unique and stable.
    version Integer, increased on any breaking change to parameters or result
    summary / description One line, and a paragraph (localisable). Used for tooltips, Lua docs and MCP tool descriptions.
    params A JSON Schema (draft 2020-12), generated from Rust types (schemars). It includes units (x-reviera-data-type: "length"), element-reference kinds (x-reviera-element: {category: "cat.walls"}), defaults and enums.
    result A JSON Schema for the result
    effect One or more of read, edit, file_read, file_write, network, script, ui, destructive, settings
    undoable Whether it creates an undo item (false for read, file and UI-only commands)
    transaction_name Default undo name
    availability A predicate over the context: document kind (project, family, family kind), active view kind, selection (count, categories), mode (Local or BIMserver), sketch mode, edit mode
    interactive Whether it can prompt for picks and dialogs when parameters are missing (UI only), and which parameters can be picked
    ui Optional ribbon placement (tab, panel, order), icon ID, default shortcut, context-menu placement
    permissions The minimum MCP permission level (§2.16.5) and Lua trust level (§2.13.7), derived from effect unless overridden
    deprecated Optional: replacement command and removal version
    examples Example calls (used in documentation, MCP descriptions and tests)
    • One execution path. Every caller (a ribbon button, a shortcut, Lua, MCP, journal replay) calls registry.execute(name, args, context). That call validates args against the schema, checks availability and permissions, opens the transaction, runs the command, regenerates, commits or rolls back, and returns {result, warnings[], changed: {added[], modified[], deleted[]}}.
    • Units in arguments. Numeric arguments with a data type accept either a number in SI, or a string with a unit ("1200 mm"), which is parsed with §2.9.5.
    • Element references in arguments accept an internal ID (integer) or a GUID (string), and are normalised before the command runs.
    • Errors are typed: {code, message, details, resolutions?}. Codes are stable strings (for example param.read_only, ui.required, availability.wrong_view, failure.unresolved).
    • Generated outputs: the Lua binding (§2.13.2), MCP tools (§2.16.3), ribbon and shortcut bindings, the command-reference documentation (Markdown and HTML), JSON Schemas for each command (published with each release), and conformance test stubs.

    Commands. registry.list(filter?) -> command_summary[] · registry.describe(name) -> definition · registry.execute(name, args) (the generic entry point; exposed to Lua as reviera.run and to MCP as run_command)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A CI check fails if any pub model-mutating function in the core can be reached other than through a registered command. - [ ] For every registered command, the generated Lua function, MCP tool and documentation entry exist and agree with the schema (checked by a CI test that compares them). - [ ] Calling wall.create with "height": "3000 mm" and with "height": 3.0 gives identical walls.

    2.12.2 Command naming and stability

    ID: DM-CMD-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: TECH_STACK §2

    Behaviour & rules. - Domains are reserved per chapter: ui.*, view.*, sheet.*, schedule.*, annotate.* (DOC); wall.*, floor.*, roof.*, door.*, modify.* (ARC); str.* (STR); mep.* (MEP); analysis.* (ANA); bimserver.*, link.*, workset.* (COL); and the DM domains defined in this chapter (element, instance, type, family, family_doc, cme, param, paramlib, global, units, material, object_style, line_*, fill_pattern, project, location, coordinates, position, site, building, spatial, phase, standards, purge, classification, keynotes, file, import, link, export, validate, rxd, edit, warnings, failure, regen, registry, script, addin, graph, mcp, model, settings, snaps, image, pset, qto, host, subcategory, formula, journal, external_props, library, numbering, decal). - Add-in commands are named <addin-id>.<verb> (for example org.example.roomtools.renumber). They cannot use reserved domains. - Stability. A command's name and version form its contract. Breaking changes need a new version, and the previous version stays callable for at least one RXD major cycle (§2.11.8), through an adapter. Deprecations are announced in release notes and in registry.describe.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Registering an add-in command named wall.create is refused at load time with an error naming the reserved domain.

    2.13 Lua scripting API

    2.13.1 Runtime

    ID: DM-LUA-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §13.1, §13.4, §13.7; TECH_STACK §3.5

    Behaviour & rules. - LuaJIT is embedded through mlua (feature luajit). The language level is Lua 5.1 plus LuaJIT extensions. Scripts shall not rely on Lua 5.3+ features (integers, goto in 5.1 mode, utf8 library). Reviera provides a reviera.utf8 helper, and 64-bit integer IDs are exposed as LuaJIT int64_t cdata or as strings, as chosen by reviera.config.id_mode (default: strings for GUIDs, Lua numbers for internal IDs below 2^53, which covers all IDs in practice). - States: - a main state runs on the command thread. It runs macros, add-ins, updaters and event handlers. It has full access to the API (subject to trust level); - worker states (optional) run pure-computation functions in parallel (for example geometry calculations for many elements). They have no access to the model or to I/O. They receive copied data and return values. They are pooled. - Each add-in gets its own environment (a separate global table) in the main state, so add-ins cannot overwrite each other's globals. Add-ins at trust level native may use their own state on request. - Platform check. On platforms where the LuaJIT JIT is not reliable (to be checked per release; for example some ARM64 macOS builds), Reviera runs LuaJIT in interpreter mode (jit.off()). Results stay the same, but some scripts run more slowly.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Two add-ins that both define a global config do not see each other's value. - [ ] A worker-state function that tries to call reviera.query fails with lua.no_model_access.

    2.13.2 Module map

    ID: DM-LUA-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §13.1; TECH_STACK §3.5

    Behaviour & rules. The global table reviera contains:

    Module Contents Generated?
    reviera.<domain>.<verb>(args) One function per registered command (for example reviera.wall.create{...}). Takes a table of named arguments, and returns the result table. Raises a Lua error with a typed error object on failure. Yes, from the registry
    reviera.run(name, args) Generic command call by name —
    reviera.doc The active document: id, kind, path, title, is_family, version(), documents() (all open documents), activate(id) —
    reviera.query The element collector (§2.13.3) —
    reviera.element(id_or_guid) Returns an element proxy (read-only properties, plus convenience writes that call commands) —
    reviera.txn Transactions (§2.13.4) —
    reviera.events Events (§2.13.5) —
    reviera.updaters Updaters (§2.13.5) —
    reviera.post, reviera.timer, reviera.async Deferred and asynchronous execution (§2.13.6) —
    reviera.geom Read-only geometry access, and value types XYZ, UV, Transform, BBox, Curve, Plane, Solid (§2.13.10) —
    reviera.units parse, format, convert, data-type constants Wrappers of units.*
    reviera.ui Selection, picks, task dialogs, forms, ribbon and dockable panels (§2.13.9) —
    reviera.fs, reviera.http File and network access, subject to trust level (§2.13.7) —
    reviera.json, reviera.csv, reviera.utf8, reviera.log Utilities —
    reviera.addin The calling add-in's ID, version, data folder and settings store —
    • Element proxies. reviera.element(x) returns a proxy with fields id, guid, category, name, type (a proxy), level, host, owner_view, location, bbox, and methods:
    • :param(name_or_guid_or_key) returns {value, display, data_type, is_read_only, is_type};
    • :params() returns all parameters;
    • :set(name, value) calls param.set, and therefore needs an open transaction;
    • :geometry(options), :dependents(), :is_valid(). Proxies always read the current state of the document as the calling script sees it (inside a transaction, uncommitted changes are visible).

    Example (informative).

    -- Number all doors on Level 1 by room, inside one undoable transaction.
local doors = reviera.query()
  :of_category("cat.doors")
  :instances()
  :on_level("Level 1")
  :to_list()

reviera.txn.run("Renumber doors", function()
  for i, d in ipairs(doors) do
    local room = d:param("To Room").value or d:param("From Room").value
    local num  = room and reviera.element(room):param("Number").value or "X"
    d:set("Mark", string.format("%s-%02d", num, i))
  end
end)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Every registered command is callable as reviera.<name> with a table argument, and the result matches the MCP tool result for the same arguments. - [ ] The example above runs on the sample project, creates one undo item named "Renumber doors", and changes only Mark values.

    2.13.3 Element queries (the collector)

    ID: DM-LUA-003 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §13.1 (filtered element collector); TECH_STACK §3.5

    Purpose. A fast, chainable way to find elements. It is the Reviera counterpart of a filtered element collector.

    Behaviour & rules. - reviera.query([doc]) starts a query over a consistent snapshot: the committed state, or the transaction's current state when called inside a transaction. Filters are chained, and the query is lazy: nothing runs until it is iterated or a terminal method is called. - Quick filters use indexes in the element store (category, class, type, level, owner view, workset, design option, bounding-box R-tree, GUID). Slow filters need element data (parameter values, geometry intersection, Lua predicates). The query planner always applies quick filters first, whatever order they were written in.

    Method Kind Meaning
    :of_category(key, …) quick One or more categories (subcategories included)
    :of_ifc_class(name, …) quick IFC class, including subclasses (for example "IfcBuildingElement")
    :instances() / :types() quick Instances only, or types only
    :of_type(type_id) / :of_family(family_id) quick
    :on_level(level) quick By reference level (name, ID or GUID)
    :in_view(view_id) quick Visible in a view (uses the view's visibility cache)
    :owned_by_view(view_id) quick View-specific elements of a view
    :in_workset(id) / :in_design_option(id) / :in_phase(id, status?) quick
    :in_bbox(min, max, mode) quick mode = intersects, inside or contains (R-tree)
    :ids(list) / :guids(list) quick Restrict to a set
    :where(param, op, value) slow op: ==, ~=, <, <=, >, >=, contains, begins, ends, has_value, no_value. Unit-aware, for example :where("Width", ">=", "900 mm").
    :where_rule(rule) slow A filter rule in the same format as view filters (DOC), including AND/OR nesting
    :intersects_element(id) / :intersects_solid(solid) slow Exact geometric intersection (OCCT)
    :host_of(id) / :hosted_by(id) / :in_room(id) slow Relationship filters
    :filter(fn) slow A Lua predicate
    :excluding(ids) quick
    :sort_by(param_or_fn, desc?) terminal helper
    :to_list(), :ids(), :first(), :count(), :each(fn), :iter() (for for el in q:iter() do) terminal
    :group_by(param) terminal Returns {value → list}
    :explain() terminal Returns the query plan (index used, estimated rows)
    • Query results are proxies. They are invalidated if the elements are deleted later. :is_valid() checks this.
    • The same query model is used by the MCP query_elements tool (§2.16.4). Its JSON form is {category?, ifc_class?, instances?, type?, level?, view?, bbox?, where?: [{param, op, value}], limit?, offset?, fields?: []}.

    Commands. element.query(spec) -> {ids[], total, fields?} (the registry form, used by MCP)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] On a 100,000-element model, query():of_category("cat.walls"):count() takes under 5 ms, and :where("Fire Rating","==","EI 60") over 10,000 walls takes under 50 ms. - [ ] Chaining :filter(fn) before :of_category gives the same results, with the same plan, as the reverse order. - [ ] :explain() shows the index used for of_category and in_bbox.

    2.13.4 Transactions from Lua

    ID: DM-LUA-004 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §3; TECH_STACK §3.3, §3.5

    Behaviour & rules. - reviera.txn.run(name, fn) opens a transaction, runs fn, and commits. If fn raises an error, or returns false, the transaction is rolled back. It returns true, result, or false, err. - reviera.txn.savepoint(fn) runs fn inside a savepoint. An error inside it rolls back the savepoint only, and the error is returned instead of raised. - reviera.txn.group(name, mode, fn) runs fn inside a transaction group. mode is "assimilate", "commit" or "rollback" (rollback is useful for "what-if" calculations). - Explicit forms txn.begin/commit/rollback exist for advanced use. A transaction that is still open when the script ends is rolled back, with a warning. - Write outside a transaction. Calling an edit command outside a transaction opens and commits an implicit transaction for that single command (one undo item per call). This is convenient for interactive use. Scripts should use txn.run to group changes. - reviera.txn.on_failure(fn) registers a failure preprocessor for the current transaction (§2.7.4). fn(failures) returns a table of actions: {id = "dismiss" | "<resolution>" | "continue"}. - reviera.regen.now() runs regeneration part-way through the transaction (§2.6.4).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] txn.run with a function that errors after creating 3 elements leaves 0 elements and no undo item, and returns false with the error. - [ ] A transaction group with mode rollback that moves 100 elements and reads their new room assignments leaves the model unchanged, and returns the values read.

    2.13.5 Events and updaters (dynamic model update)

    ID: DM-LUA-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §3 (events, updaters), §13.1

    Purpose. Scripts can react to changes after they are committed (events), or inside the transaction that made them (updaters), so that dependent data stays correct automatically.

    Behaviour & rules. - Events (handlers run after commit, read-only by default; a handler may start its own transaction with reviera.post, §2.13.6):

    Event Payload
    app.started, app.closing —
    document.opened, document.closing, document.saved, document.saving (can cancel), document.activated document ID, path
    document.changed {txn_name, origin, added[], modified[{id, facets[], params[]}], deleted[], undo?, redo?}
    view.activated, selection.changed view ID / element IDs
    family.loaded, family.reloaded family ID
    model.id_remap {old → new} (§2.5)
    bimserver.revision_available, bimserver.synced COL chapter
    command.before, command.after command name, args, result. command.before can cancel (trust level standard and above; §2.13.7).
    failure.processing the failure list (as for preprocessors)
    app.idle — (fired after 100 ms of no input, at most 10 times per second)
    • Updaters (the equivalent of dynamic model update):
    reviera.updaters.register{
  id       = "org.example.roomtools.door-room-sync",   -- unique, stable
  name     = "Copy room number to door",
  triggers = {
    { query = { category = "cat.doors", instances = true }, change = "geometry" },
    { query = { category = "cat.rooms" },                  change = { param = "Number" } },
    { query = { category = "cat.doors" },                  change = "added" },
  },
  priority = 100,          -- lower runs first; ties broken by id
  optional = true,         -- if the add-in is missing, the model still opens without prompts
  run = function(ctx)      -- runs INSIDE the triggering transaction, before commit
    for _, id in ipairs(ctx.affected("cat.doors")) do
      local d = reviera.element(id)
      local room = d:param("To Room").value
      if room then d:set("Room Number", reviera.element(room):param("Number").value) end
    end
  end,
}
    • Change kinds: added, deleted, geometry (placement or shape facet changed), type_changed, {param = <ref>}, any.
    • Updaters run after the command, before regeneration finishes. Their changes become part of the same transaction and undo item. Regeneration then runs again for what they changed.
    • Loop control: an updater's own changes can trigger other updaters, but not itself again in the same pass. The whole updater phase runs at most 10 passes. If it does not settle, the transaction fails with updater.no_convergence, naming the updaters involved.
    • Time budget: each updater has a soft limit (default 200 ms per transaction). Going over it is logged and shown in the Add-in Manager. An updater that raises an error is disabled for the session, a warning is shown, and the transaction continues without its changes (default), or fails (when the updater is registered with on_error = "fail").
    • Updaters do not run on undo, redo, or merges of incoming BIMserver revisions (where the changes already include the updater results).
    • Model declaration. When a document is saved with an active updater that made changes, the updater's ID and the add-in ID are recorded in RXD document project/settings (updaters_used). On open without that add-in: if optional = true, nothing happens; otherwise, the user is warned that "data maintained by add-in X may become out of date if you edit".

    Commands. events and updaters are API-level, not registry commands. Introspection: addin.updaters() -> [{id, addin, triggers, enabled, stats}] · addin.updater.enable(id, on)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] The example updater sets "Room Number" on a door when the door is moved into another room. The door move and the parameter change are one undo item. - [ ] Two updaters that keep changing each other's trigger parameters fail the transaction with updater.no_convergence after 10 passes, and the model is unchanged. - [ ] A document.changed handler receives the exact added, modified and deleted IDs of each transaction.

    2.13.6 Deferred, asynchronous and modeless execution

    ID: DM-LUA-006 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §3 (modeless contexts, external events)

    Purpose. Modeless UIs, timers, network calls and long computations must change the model safely. This is the equivalent of external events.

    Behaviour & rules. - The model can only be changed on the command thread, in a transaction. Code running in other contexts (dockable-panel callbacks, timers, HTTP callbacks, worker states) cannot change the model directly. Instead it uses: - reviera.post(fn, opts?) queues fn to run on the command thread, in the next free slot, with full API access. opts.name labels it in the journal. opts.coalesce = key replaces a pending call with the same key. Returns a handle with :cancel() and :status(). - reviera.timer(ms, fn, {repeat?}) runs fn through post after a delay. - reviera.async(fn) runs fn as a coroutine on the command thread. Inside it, reviera.await(x) suspends without blocking the UI until x (an HTTP request, a worker-state job, a timer, or a user pick in the UI) completes. It then resumes on the command thread. Transactions cannot be held open across an await. Trying to do so fails with txn.await_in_transaction. - reviera.workers.map(fn_source, items, opts) runs a pure function over items in worker states, in parallel, and returns the results to the coroutine. - The UI never waits for Lua code to finish. Long-running script steps show a progress bar with Cancel. Cancel raises lua.cancelled at the next API call or yield point.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A dockable panel button that calls reviera.post to create a wall works while the user is orbiting a 3D view, and the wall appears as one undo item. - [ ] An async script that awaits an HTTP request of 5 s does not freeze the UI. The user can keep editing, and the script's transaction runs after the response.

    2.13.7 Sandbox and trust levels

    ID: DM-LUA-007 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §13.2 (load prompts), §13.4 (macro security); TECH_STACK §3.5

    Purpose. To run scripts from many sources safely. LuaJIT's FFI gives native memory access, so access must be limited by trust.

    Behaviour & rules.

    Level Name Model Files Network OS / processes ffi, debug, load of bytecode Typical use
    0 read_only Queries only. No transactions. ✘ ✘ ✘ ✘ MCP execute_lua at read-only permission, document scripts not yet trusted
    1 model Read and write through commands ✘ (except the add-in's own data folder) ✘ ✘ ✘ Most add-ins and macros
    2 standard As level 1, plus events that can cancel Read and write in user-chosen paths (through file dialogs, or paths declared in the manifest and approved), and the add-in data folder HTTPS to hosts declared in the manifest ✘ ✘ Add-ins that import and export data
    3 trusted As level 2 Any path the user can access Any host os.execute/io.popen with a confirmation prompt the first time ✘ Firm-internal tools
    4 native As level 3 Any Any Any ✔ ffi, debug, bytecode loading Add-ins that bind native libraries. Requires explicit user approval with a strong warning.
