    • Removed or wrapped globals at levels 0–2: io, os (except os.time, os.clock, os.date), require of C modules, package.loadlib, load/loadstring with bytecode (text chunks are allowed), dofile/loadfile (replaced by reviera.addin.require for files inside the add-in package), debug, ffi, jit (except jit.status), collectgarbage("stop").
    • Resource limits (all levels except native, configurable):
    • wall-clock limit per synchronous call (default 30 s, then a prompt to continue or cancel);
    • instruction-count hook, for interrupting runaway loops (the JIT is disabled for level-0 scripts so the hook is reliable; at higher levels the check also runs on every API call);
    • memory limit per add-in, through a custom allocator where the binding supports it, and otherwise by monitoring.
    • Granting trust.
    • The add-in's manifest requests a level (§2.14.1). The user grants it on first load, through a dialog that lists the capabilities.
    • Grants are remembered per add-in ID and content hash. A changed add-in asks again.
    • Signed add-ins from publishers the user trusts (OpenPGP or minisign keys in the trust store) skip the prompt, up to level 3.
    • Level 4 always asks.
    • Document scripts (stored in a model's RXD, §2.13.8) run at level 0 until the user trusts that document's scripts. Trust is per document GUID and script hash.
    • Script Security settings (Manage › Scripts): enable or disable application scripts and document scripts, ask before running, and the trust store (keys, granted add-ins, revocations).
    • Script Security dialog (script.security()), with three tabs:
    • Scripts: Application scripts — Enabled / Ask before each run / Disabled; Document scripts — Disabled until trusted (default) / Ask when a document with scripts opens / Always disabled; the maximum trust level a user may grant (default trusted; native only when the user ticks a separate, warned box); the wall-clock and memory limits (wall clock 5–600 s, default 30 s; memory 16 MB–4 GB per add-in, default 256 MB).
    • Trusted publishers: the list of OpenPGP and minisign public keys, with fingerprint, name, added date and the highest level their signed add-ins get without a prompt (at most trusted). Buttons: Import key…, Remove, Show fingerprint. A key must parse and have a valid fingerprint to be added.
    • Grants: every remembered grant (add-in ID, version hash, level, date) and every trusted document (document GUID, title, script hashes, level, date), with Revoke. Revoking takes effect for the next load or run; a running add-in is not interrupted.
    • Settings are per user. An administrator policy file can lock any of them (shown greyed with "set by your organisation"), for example to force Document scripts: Always disabled or to cap the maximum level. Policy always wins over user settings.
    • OK saves the settings (not undoable; they are not model data); Cancel discards them.

    Commands. script.security() (opens the Script Security dialog); trust decisions for add-ins use addin.trust.grant / addin.trust.revoke (§2.14.3) and for document scripts rxd.trust_scripts (02a).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A level-1 script calling io.open("/etc/passwd") fails with lua.sandbox.denied, and the attempt is logged. - [ ] A level-0 script running while true do end is interrupted within the configured limit, with no UI freeze longer than 1 s after the user chooses Cancel. - [ ] Changing one byte of a trusted add-in's code makes it ask for trust again on next load. - [ ] A document script in a downloaded project cannot write to the model until the user trusts it. - [ ] With a policy file that sets Document scripts: Always disabled, the Script Security dialog shows that option greyed, and rxd.trust_scripts fails with lua.policy.denied.

    2.13.8 Scripts (macros), the Script Manager and document scripts

    ID: DM-LUA-008 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §13.4, §13.7; screenshots/platform/macro_manager_and_vscode_2026.png, screenshots/platform/macro_vscode_editor_2026.png

    Purpose. Lightweight automation without packaging an add-in.

    UI. Manage › Scripts › Script Manager: - tabs: Application (user scripts in the user script folder) and Document (scripts stored in the model); - each tab is a tree of modules (Lua files) and entry points (functions marked with an annotation comment, for example --@macro "Renumber doors"); - buttons: New module, New macro, Edit, Rename, Delete, Run, Step into (debugger), Import, Export, Open folder; - Edit opens the built-in script editor: a dockable panel with syntax highlighting, completion generated from the registry, inline docs, a console (REPL) with result inspection, breakpoints and a variable view. Or it opens an external editor chosen in settings (any editor; Reviera provides a Language Server for completion, reviera-lua-ls, and writes type stub files for common Lua language servers).

    Behaviour & rules. - Application scripts live in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/reviera/scripts (or the platform equivalent) and are available in every document. - Document scripts are stored in RXD document scripts/<name> and travel with the model. They are subject to §2.13.7. - Recording (P2). Record captures the commands the user runs (from the journal, §2.7.3) into a new Lua macro, with literal arguments. The user can then edit it. - Quick-access shell. A Lua console panel (View › User Interface › Lua Console) runs one-line commands against the active document, at trust level model, or higher if granted. - Script Manager dialog (script.manager()). It is modeless, so the user can keep working while it is open. - Each module row shows its name, scope, last modified time, trust status (document modules: Not trusted / Trusted at level n) and load errors. Each entry point shows its display name (from the --@macro annotation), description (the comment block above it) and an optional --@args schema, from which Run builds a parameter form. - New module asks for a name (a valid Lua module name: letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, unique in the scope) and creates it from a template with one sample entry point. New macro adds an annotated function to the selected module. Rename renames a module or entry point and updates shortcut and Quick Access Toolbar bindings. Delete asks for confirmation and lists bindings that will be removed. - Modules are syntax-checked on save and on refresh; a module with a syntax error is listed with the line and message and its entry points are disabled. - Changes to document modules are model changes (one undoable transaction each, stored in scripts/<name>); changes to application modules are file operations and are not undoable. - Run executes the entry point at the module's granted trust level; document modules that are not trusted run only after the trust prompt (§2.13.7). Output and errors go to the console panel. - Run Script… (Manage › Scripts, and Add-ins › External; script.run_file(path, entry?, args?)) runs a Lua file from disk once, without adding it to the Script Manager. The first run of a file with an unknown hash shows a prompt naming the file and its SHA-256 hash, offering to run it at level model (default) or at a higher level up to the user's maximum (§2.13.7); the choice is remembered per hash, like add-in grants, and a changed file asks again. Without entry, the file's main chunk runs; with entry, that global function is called with args. The most recent 10 files are offered in a list. Its transactions follow §2.13.4, so a script that changes the model creates undo items named by the script.

    Commands. script.run(module, entry, args?) · script.list(scope: "application"|"document") -> script[] · script.create(scope, module, source) · script.delete(scope, module) · script.import(scope, path) · script.export(scope, module, path) · script.record_start() · script.record_stop(module_name) -> source · script.manager() (opens the Script Manager) · script.run_file(path, entry?, args?)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A macro created in the Script Manager appears in the Run list immediately, and can be bound to a keyboard shortcut and a Quick Access Toolbar button. - [ ] A document script survives save and reopen, and is listed under Document after reopening. - [ ] The built-in editor offers completion for reviera.wall.cr… with the parameter list of wall.create. - [ ] script.run_file on a file that calls wall.create asks for trust once, creates one undo item, and on a second run with the same file hash runs without asking. - [ ] A document module with a syntax error is shown in the Script Manager with its line number, and its entry points cannot be run.

    2.13.9 UI extension API

    ID: DM-LUA-009 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §13.1 (ribbon, dockable panes, dialogs, selection)

    Behaviour & rules. - Ribbon. Add-ins declare ribbon items in their manifest (§2.14.1) or at runtime with reviera.ui.ribbon.add{tab, panel, items}. Items are push buttons, split buttons, pull-downs, toggles, combo boxes and text boxes. Each one calls a registered command, with an availability predicate. Add-ins get their own tab by default, or their own panel in the Add-ins tab. - Selection and picks. reviera.ui.selection() and reviera.ui.select(ids). reviera.ui.pick_object{filter, prompt}, pick_objects, pick_point{snap, work_plane}, pick_box, pick_face, pick_edge. Picks work inside reviera.async coroutines (§2.13.6) and in synchronous commands. - Dialogs. - reviera.ui.task_dialog{title, main, content, buttons, commands, checkbox} shows a task dialog; - reviera.ui.form{title, fields = {...}} builds a declarative form, with fields such as text, number with unit, element picker, drop-down, check box, table and file picker, plus validation; - forms are rendered in native wxWidgets controls. - Dockable panels. reviera.ui.panel.register{id, title, default_dock, build = function(p) … end} uses the same declarative controls, plus a list or table view, a tree view and an HTML view. The HTML view is a sandboxed web view with no access to the API except through a message channel that calls registered commands. - Transient graphics. reviera.ui.overlay draws temporary lines, points, text and meshes in views (not saved, cleared on command end or on request), for previews and analysis display.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An add-in that declares a ribbon tab with 3 buttons shows them on start-up. Each button is greyed out when its command's availability predicate is false (for example, when no wall is selected). - [ ] A form with a length field accepts 3' 6" and returns 1.0668 m.

    2.13.10 Geometry API

    ID: DM-LUA-010 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §13.1 (geometry, direct shapes, ray casting)

    Behaviour & rules. - Value types (immutable, in reviera.geom): XYZ, UV, Transform, Plane, BBox, Curve (line, arc, ellipse, NURBS, polyline), CurveLoop, Solid, Mesh. - Access: element:geometry{detail = "fine", view = id?, include_symbolic?} returns solids, curves and meshes in world coordinates, with stable references for faces and edges (§2.8.3). - Operations (pure, run on OCCT copies): - boolean union, difference and intersection; - extrude, revolve, sweep, loft; - section by plane; - volume, area and centroid; - point containment, distance, closest point; - ray cast against the model (reviera.geom.raycast{origin, direction, filter} returns hits with element ID, face reference and distance). - Direct shapes. reviera.direct_shape.create{category, geometry, name?, type?} creates a non-parametric element of a category from solids or meshes. It is stored as an IFC element with that geometry (§2.11.1 "IFC-native element" behaviour).

    Commands. direct_shape.create(category, geometry, name?, type_id?) -> element_id · direct_shape.set_geometry(element_id, geometry) · geom.raycast(origin, direction, filter?) -> hit[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] geom.raycast from inside a room towards +X returns the first wall hit, with the face reference #face:interior.

    2.13.11 API versioning and documentation

    ID: DM-LUA-011 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §13.1 (API changes by release), §16.11

    Purpose. Add-ins and scripts must keep working across Reviera releases, and authors must know exactly what changed. This avoids the forced rebuilds that the reference product's runtime changes caused (Appendix A).

    Behaviour & rules. - The Lua API has a semver API version, separate from the application version. Add-ins declare a compatible range (§2.14.1). Minor versions only add features. Major versions may remove features, after one minor release of deprecation warnings. - What the API version covers: every reviera.* module function and its arguments, the element proxy fields and methods, event names and payloads, updater trigger kinds, error codes, and the command versions visible to Lua (§2.12.2). A command's own version changing is an API change: a breaking command change bumps the API major version, unless the old command version stays callable through an adapter (in which case it is a minor change). - Range check at load. The add-in's reviera_api range (Cargo-style semver syntax: ^, ~, >=, <, comma for AND) is checked against the running API version before its entry runs. Outside the range, the add-in is not loaded and the Add-in Manager shows both versions. Scripts without a manifest (Script Manager, script.run_file) may declare --@reviera_api "^1.2" on their first line; without it they run against the current version with no check. - Deprecations. A deprecated function or command still works and logs one warning per add-in per session, naming the replacement and the removal version. reviera.api.deprecations() lists the deprecated items an add-in has called in this session; the Add-in Manager shows a count per add-in. - Feature probing. reviera.api.version (a string), reviera.api.has(name) (true if a module function or command exists in this build) let scripts adapt to optional features (for example BIMserver mode, P2 commands). - Documentation. Generated reference documentation (HTML and Markdown) lists every module, function, command and event, with examples. It is published per API version, and shipped offline with the application. Each entry shows the version that introduced it, and deprecated entries show their replacement. A changelog per API version lists additions, deprecations and removals, generated from the registry and the Lua binding definitions and checked in CI. - Lua type stubs (for common Lua language servers) are generated per API version. - Support window. Each API major version is supported (bug fixes, no removals) for at least two years after the next major version ships, matching the RXD policy (§2.11.8).

    Commands. None of its own; registry.describe (§2.12.1) reports each command's version and deprecation, and the documentation is served as MCP resources reviera://docs/{topic} (§2.16.6).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An add-in that declares reviera_api = "^1.2" loads on API 1.5, and is refused on API 2.0 with a message naming the incompatibility. - [ ] Calling a deprecated function logs exactly one warning per session for that add-in, naming the replacement, and the call still succeeds. - [ ] The generated changelog for a release lists every command whose version changed, and CI fails if a command's schema changed without a version change. - [ ] reviera.api.has("bimserver.connect") returns false in a build without BIMserver support and true otherwise.

    2.14 Add-ins

    2.14.1 Add-in manifest

    ID: DM-ADDIN-001 · Priority: P0 (manifest, licence check) / P1 (UI, signing, registry) · Ref: research/05 §13.2; TECH_STACK §4.2

    Purpose. A declarative description of an add-in. It is used for discovery, licence policy, trust, command registration and UI placement.

    Behaviour & rules. - An add-in is a folder (or a .revieraaddin ZIP of that folder) containing reviera-addin.toml, Lua sources, resources, a LICENSE file and, optionally, README, icons, translations and tests. - Manifest format (normative; TOML 1.0):

    manifest_version = 1

[addin]
id          = "org.example.roomtools"      # reverse-DNS, unique, stable
name        = "Room Tools"
version     = "1.4.2"                      # semver
license     = "GPL-3.0-or-later"           # REQUIRED: SPDX license expression
authors     = ["Jane Doe <jane@example.org>"]
description = "Renumbering and room-door synchronisation."
homepage    = "https://example.org/roomtools"
source      = "https://git.example.org/roomtools"   # REQUIRED for registry submission
reviera_api = "^1.2"                       # semver range of the Lua API (§2.13.11)
entry       = "main.lua"                   # run on load; returns an init function
min_reviera = "1.0.0"                      # optional

[trust]
level = "standard"                         # requested level (§2.13.7)
network_hosts = ["api.example.org"]        # for level "standard"
paths = ["~/Documents/RoomTools"]          # extra file paths requested (approved by the user)

[[commands]]                                # registered in the command registry (§2.12)
name        = "org.example.roomtools.renumber"
function    = "commands.renumber"          # Lua path inside the add-in
summary     = "Renumber rooms along a path"
effect      = ["edit"]
params_schema = "schemas/renumber.json"    # JSON Schema; exposed to MCP automatically
mcp         = true                         # expose as an MCP tool (default true; false hides it)

[[ribbon]]
tab = "Room Tools"
panel = "Numbering"
items = [ { command = "org.example.roomtools.renumber", label = "Renumber", icon = "icons/renumber.svg" } ]

[[updaters]]
id = "org.example.roomtools.door-room-sync"
module = "updaters.door_room"
optional = true

[[panels]]
id = "org.example.roomtools.browser"
title = "Room Browser"
module = "ui.browser"

[dependencies]
"org.example.common" = "^2.0"

[signature]                                 # optional
key_id = "minisign:<publisher public key>"     # signature file: reviera-addin.toml.minisig
    • license is mandatory. Its value must be a valid SPDX license expression (SPDX 2.3 syntax, including AND, OR, WITH and +).
    • Required files: LICENSE (the licence text). For registry submission, the source is required as well.
    • Validation happens on discovery. An invalid manifest stops the add-in from loading, and the Add-in Manager shows the field errors.

    Commands. addin.validate(path) -> {ok, errors[], license_status}

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A manifest missing license, id, version or reviera_api fails validation, and each missing field is named. - [ ] A manifest whose [[commands]] entry refers to a missing JSON Schema file fails validation. With a valid schema, the command appears in registry.describe and as an MCP tool with that schema.

    2.14.2 Discovery, licence policy and loading

    ID: DM-ADDIN-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §13.2; TECH_STACK §4.2

    Behaviour & rules. - Locations (searched in this order; a later location never overrides an add-in ID already found, and duplicates are reported): 1. per user: $XDG_DATA_HOME/reviera/addins/<id>/ (Linux), %APPDATA%\Reviera\addins\<id>\ (Windows), ~/Library/Application Support/Reviera/addins/<id>/ (macOS); 2. all users: a system-wide, admin-writable location (for example /usr/share/reviera/addins/, %ProgramFiles%\Reviera\addins\). It is not user-writable, for security; 3. folders listed in settings (for example a firm network share), which can be marked trusted by an administrator policy file. - Licence check (as required by TECH_STACK §4.2). The loader parses the SPDX expression and evaluates it against the GPL-compatible allow-list: - allowed identifiers: GPL-3.0-only, GPL-3.0-or-later, LGPL-2.1-or-later, LGPL-3.0-only, LGPL-3.0-or-later, AGPL-3.0-only, AGPL-3.0-or-later, MIT, MIT-0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, Apache-2.0, MPL-2.0, Zlib, 0BSD, Unlicense, CC0-1.0, BSL-1.0, Artistic-2.0, X11, Python-2.0, and others that a maintainer adds after review; - the allow-list is a versioned data file shipped with Reviera and updated with releases; - evaluation: an OR is compatible if any branch is compatible; an AND is compatible if all parts are; WITH <exception> is compatible if the base licence is and the exception is on the allowed-exceptions list (for example Classpath-exception-2.0, LLVM-exception); - GPL-2.0-only (without an OR to a compatible licence), proprietary, LicenseRef-*, "non-commercial" and missing licences are not compatible. - Not compatible → not loaded by default. The Add-in Manager lists the add-in as Blocked (licence), showing its expression and why it failed. - User override. The user can enable a clearly labelled override per add-in ("Load this add-in anyway. I understand that it is not GPL-compatible, and that I may not distribute it with Reviera"). Overrides are remembered per add-in ID and version. The GPL does not restrict private use, so this matches TECH_STACK §4.2. - Load order. Dependencies first (topological). Cycles are refused. Each add-in's entry runs in its own environment at its granted trust level (§2.13.7). Its returned init(ctx) is called. Its commands, ribbon items, panels and updaters are registered. - Unload and reload (P1): an add-in can be disabled or reloaded without restarting. Its commands, ribbon items, panels and updaters are removed, and its handlers are unregistered. This is useful for development (a hot-reload button). - Failure isolation. An error in an add-in's entry disables that add-in only, and the error is shown in the Add-in Manager.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An add-in with license = "MIT OR Proprietary-ACME" loads (the MIT branch is compatible). One with license = "GPL-2.0-only" is blocked. One with no license field is blocked, with "missing license". - [ ] With the override enabled for a blocked add-in, it loads, and the Add-in Manager shows an "override" badge. - [ ] An add-in whose entry raises an error does not prevent other add-ins or the application from starting.

    2.14.3 Add-in Manager, packaging and registry

    ID: DM-ADDIN-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/05 §13.2, §13.7

    UI. Manage › Add-ins › Add-in Manager: a list with name, ID, version, licence (with compatibility status), granted trust level, source location, enabled/disabled, load time and errors. Buttons: Enable/Disable, Reload, Install from file…, Install from registry…, Uninstall, Update, Show commands, Show updaters (with run statistics), Open folder, Review trust.

    Add-in Manager dialog (addin.manage()). It is modeless. - List. Status badges: Loaded, Disabled, Blocked (licence), Blocked (API version), Failed (with the error), Override (licence override in effect), Update available. Filters: All, Enabled, Problems, Updates. Search by name, ID or command name. Sorting by any column. - Details pane for the selected add-in: manifest fields (description, authors, homepage, source, licence expression and why it passed or failed, requested and granted trust level, network hosts and paths), dependencies with their resolved versions, registered commands (name, effect, MCP exposure), ribbon items, panels, updaters with statistics (runs, average and maximum time, errors), deprecation warnings (§2.13.11), and the last 50 log lines. - Actions and their rules. - Enable/Disable (addin.enable) takes effect at once (unload or load, §2.14.2). Disabling an add-in that others depend on lists the dependants and disables them too after confirmation. - Uninstall (addin.uninstall) is possible only for per-user add-ins; all-user and policy-folder add-ins show why not. It removes the folder after unloading and keeps the add-in's data folder unless Remove settings and data is ticked. - Install from file… (addin.install) validates the package (manifest, signature, licence, API range, dependency availability) and shows a summary before extracting. An ID that is already installed is treated as an update; a lower version asks for confirmation (downgrade). - Update (addin.update) downloads from the registry the add-in came from, verifies checksum and signature, and asks for trust again when the requested level or content hash changed. - Licence override (addin.set_override) is shown only for blocked add-ins, behind the warning text of §2.14.2. - Review trust opens the grant for this add-in (addin.trust.grant / addin.trust.revoke). - Changes made here are application settings, not model changes, and are not undoable. - An add-in that registered updaters which made changes in the active project shows a "used by this project" marker (from updaters_used, §2.13.5), and disabling it warns that data it maintains may become out of date.

    Behaviour & rules. - Packaging. .revieraaddin is a ZIP of the add-in folder. Install from file verifies the manifest and the optional signature, shows the requested trust level and licence, then extracts the archive to the per-user location. - Registry (P2). An optional public registry is an index of add-ins: a static Git-hosted JSON index of package URLs and checksums, which anyone can mirror. It only accepts add-ins whose licence is compatible and whose source is public, as TECH_STACK §4.2 requires. Each entry records the SPDX expression, the source URL, checksums and signatures. The application can browse, install and update from configured registries. - Developer tools. reviera addin new <id> creates a template add-in with a manifest, LICENSE (GPL-3.0-or-later by default), tests and type stubs. reviera addin pack validates and packs. reviera addin test runs tests headless (§2.11.7).

    Commands. addin.list() -> addin[] · addin.enable(id, on) · addin.reload(id) · addin.install(path_or_registry_id) -> id · addin.uninstall(id) · addin.update(id) · addin.set_override(id, on) · addin.trust.grant(id, level) · addin.trust.revoke(id) · addin.manage() (opens the Add-in Manager)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Installing a signed add-in from a trusted key needs no trust prompt up to level 3. Installing an unsigned one shows the prompt with the requested capabilities. - [ ] Reloading an add-in after editing its Lua code updates its commands without restarting, and its ribbon buttons keep working. - [ ] Disabling an add-in on which two others depend lists both and, after confirmation, disables all three; their commands disappear from registry.list and from the MCP tool list. - [ ] Uninstalling an add-in from the all-users location is refused with a message explaining that it needs an administrator.

    2.15 Visual programming (future)

    2.15.1 Reviera Graph

    ID: DM-VPL-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/05 §13.5, §13.6; screenshots/platform/dynamo_interface_library_canvas.jpg, screenshots/platform/dynamo_revit_node_library.jpg, screenshots/platform/dynamo_documentation_browser_2026.png

    Purpose. A node-based visual programming environment for users who do not write code. It is built on the command registry and Lua, and does not need a separate runtime.

    Behaviour & rules. - Graph files (.rgraph.json, JSON, validated by a JSON Schema) contain nodes, typed ports, wires, groups, notes, graph inputs and outputs, and metadata (name, description, licence, required add-ins, API version). - Node library (searchable tree, with documentation for each node): - Registry nodes: one node per registered command, generated automatically. Inputs come from the parameter schema; outputs from the result schema. - Query nodes: built from the collector (§2.13.3), for example All Elements of Category and Filter by Parameter. - Core nodes: math, logic, lists (map, filter, zip, flatten, group, sort), strings, dictionaries, units, geometry value types (§2.13.10). - Script nodes: a Lua code block, and a formula node (§2.8.7). - Custom nodes: sub-graphs saved as .rgraphnode.json. - Package nodes: from add-ins. - Execution. - The graph is compiled to Lua, and runs at the graph's granted trust level (§2.13.7). - Each run is one transaction (or a group, when nodes ask for it). - Run modes: Manual, Automatic (re-run on input change, with a debounce), Periodic. - Element binding: a re-run updates the elements that the previous run created (tracked in RXD element data graph_binding by graph ID and node path), instead of creating duplicates. - Canvas. Pan and zoom, wire routing, node preview bubbles, a background 3D preview of geometry values, run status per node (OK, warning, error), and a linter (unused inputs, missing licences, unsafe trust).

    Commands. graph.open(path) -> graph_id · graph.run(graph_id, inputs?) -> outputs · graph.save(graph_id, path?) · graph.compile(graph_id) -> lua_source

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A graph "All walls of category → Filter by Fire Rating = EI 60 → Set Comments 'checked'" runs as one undo item, and running it again changes nothing. - [ ] A graph that creates 10 columns on grid intersections updates the same 10 columns (the same GUIDs) when the grid moves and the graph runs again.

    2.15.2 Graph Player

    ID: DM-VPL-002 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/05 §13.5; screenshots/platform/dynamo_player_inputs_2026.png

    Purpose. Let users who never open the graph editor run published graphs with their own inputs.

    Workflow. 1. Manage › Visual Programming › Graph Player. The panel lists graphs from the configured folders. 2. Select a graph; its marked inputs appear as a form, with the author's defaults. 3. Set inputs (pick elements in the model where asked) and choose Run. 4. Read the status, warnings and outputs; select output elements with Select in model.

    Behaviour & rules. A dockable panel that lists graphs from configured folders. Each graph shows its marked inputs (number with unit, slider, drop-down, element picker, file picker, Boolean) and outputs. Run executes it with status and warnings. Users who do not edit graphs can run them. Graph Player shows the graph's required trust level, and refuses graphs that need a higher level than the user has granted. - Folders. The user folder plus any folders in settings (for example a firm share); an administrator policy can add read-only folders. Subfolders appear as groups. Search filters by name and description. - Inputs. Only nodes the author marked Is input are shown, in the author's order, with their names and tooltips. Values are validated against the node's type and range before Run is enabled; element pickers state the expected categories and count. Input values are remembered per user per graph (Reset to defaults restores them). - Running. A run is one transaction named after the graph (or a group, if the graph asks), like graph.run (§2.15.1). Progress and Cancel are shown; cancelling rolls the run back. Automatic mode is not available in the Player; each run is explicit. - Outputs. Nodes marked Is output show their values (numbers with units, text, lists truncated to 100 items, element lists with Select in model). - Errors. A graph that fails to load (schema error, missing add-in, newer API) is listed with the reason and cannot be run. A run that fails shows the failing node's name and message, and the model is unchanged.

    Commands. graph.player.list(folder?) -> graph_summary[] · (runs through graph.run)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A graph with a length input and an element-picker input can be run from Graph Player without opening the graph editor. - [ ] Entering a value outside the input's declared range disables Run and names the range. - [ ] A graph that needs an add-in that is not installed is listed with "requires org.example.tools" and cannot be run.

    2.15.3 Design-space exploration

    ID: DM-VPL-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/05 §13.6

    Purpose. Generate and compare many design alternatives from a graph, then apply the chosen one. It is a local, open alternative to vendor cloud services.

    Workflow. 1. In the graph editor, mark inputs as variables (with min, max and step, or a list of values) and outputs as goals (minimise or maximise) or constraints (bounds that an outcome must meet). 2. Create Study, choose a solver and a budget (number of outcomes), and Generate. 3. Explore the results; pick an outcome; Apply to model.

    Behaviour & rules. A study is a graph with variable inputs (ranges) and goals (outputs to minimise or maximise) plus constraints. Solvers: Randomise, Cross product, Optimise (NSGA-II, implemented in Rust), Like this (local search around a chosen outcome). Outcomes run in parallel in headless worker documents (copies of the model in memory, §2.11.7). They are shown in a scatter plot and a parallel-coordinates chart, with thumbnails, and any outcome can be applied to the model as one transaction. This is a local, open alternative to vendor cloud services. - Budget and parallelism. The number of parallel workers defaults to the number of physical cores minus one, limited by memory (each worker holds a model copy; the study estimates memory before starting and lowers parallelism if needed). Cross product refuses budgets larger than the product of the variable steps and says so. - Determinism. Each study stores its random seed; re-running with the same seed, graph and model version gives the same outcomes. - Constraints. Outcomes that break a constraint are kept but marked infeasible and excluded from the Pareto set. - Results. Each outcome stores its variable values, goal values, constraint status, a thumbnail of a chosen view, and the run time. Results can be filtered by brushing axes, sorted, and exported as CSV. Apply re-runs the graph with that outcome's inputs on the live model (one transaction), so the applied result is real model content, not a copy of the worker's geometry. - Failure. An outcome whose run fails is recorded with its error and does not stop the study. Cancel keeps the outcomes finished so far. - Storage. Studies (definition, seed, outcomes) are saved next to the graph as <graph>.study.json; they are not model data. Thumbnails are stored in the same folder.

    Commands. study.create(graph_id, variables, goals) -> study_id · study.run(study_id, solver, budget) -> outcomes · study.apply(study_id, outcome_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An Optimise study over 2 variables and 2 goals with a budget of 200 runs returns a Pareto set, uses all cores, and applying an outcome reproduces its reported goal values. - [ ] Running the same study twice with the same seed gives identical outcome tables. - [ ] An outcome that breaks a constraint is shown as infeasible and is not in the Pareto set.

    2.16 The MCP server

    2.16.1 Overview

    ID: DM-MCP-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/05 §12.3 (AI assistant using MCP tool calls), §16.11; TECH_STACK §3.6

    Purpose. Every Reviera operation is available to AI agents through the Model Context Protocol. This is achieved by construction, from the command registry.

    Behaviour & rules. - The MCP server is built into the application with the official Rust MCP SDK (rmcp). It follows the current published MCP specification (protocol version negotiated at initialisation). The supported revision is listed in the release notes. - It exposes tools (generated from the registry, plus a few compound tools), resources (model data) and prompts (task templates). It supports notifications (resource updates, tool-list changes), progress and cancellation. - The server is off by default. The user turns it on in Manage › AI Agents (or with a command-line flag) and chooses the transports and the permission level. - Agents have no write path of their own. Their changes go through the same command queue, transactions, undo and warnings as user actions (§2.7).

    2.16.2 Transports and authentication

    ID: DM-MCP-002 · Priority: P0 (stdio) / P1 (streamable HTTP) · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.6

    Behaviour & rules. - stdio. reviera --mcp-stdio [model.ifc] runs Reviera headless (§2.11.7) as an MCP server on stdin/stdout, for local agents that start it as a sub-process. Trust follows the user who started it. The permission level comes from a command-line flag (default read_only). - Streamable HTTP (when the UI is running). The server listens on 127.0.0.1 (default port 47800, configurable). Binding to other interfaces requires TLS and an explicit setting. - Authentication: bearer tokens created in Manage › AI Agents › New client token. Each token has a name, a permission level, an optional expiry and an optional document scope. Tokens are stored hashed. Remote deployments may use OAuth 2.1 authorisation as the MCP specification describes (P2). - The Origin header is checked to prevent DNS rebinding attacks. CORS is closed by default. - Status UI. An AI Agents panel shows connected clients, their permission levels, active sessions, recent tool calls (from the journal), and a Disconnect / Revoke button for each one. A status-bar icon shows when an agent is connected, and pulses while an agent is running a tool.

    Commands. mcp.start(transport, options) · mcp.stop() · mcp.token.create(name, level, expiry?, document_scope?) -> token · mcp.token.revoke(token_id) · mcp.sessions() -> session[] · mcp.session.disconnect(session_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With the HTTP transport on, a request without a valid token gets HTTP 401, and a request from a disallowed Origin gets HTTP 403. - [ ] Revoking a token disconnects its sessions within 1 s. - [ ] Credentials (BIMserver passwords, tokens) never appear in any tool result, resource or log.

    2.16.3 Tool catalogue: generation from the registry

    ID: DM-MCP-003 · Priority: P0 · Ref: TECH_STACK §2, §3.6

    Behaviour & rules. - One tool per command. For each registered command (core and add-in, unless mcp = false): - tool name = the command name (for example wall.create). For clients that do not accept . in tool names, the setting MCP tool name style = underscore maps it to wall_create; - description = summary + description + key examples, plus the data types and units of numeric arguments; - inputSchema = the command's parameter JSON Schema. Arguments with a data type also accept unit strings (§2.12.1); - outputSchema = the result schema. Results are returned as structured content, plus a short text summary; - annotations, derived from effect: readOnlyHint (effect is only read), destructiveHint (destructive or delete), idempotentHint (declared per command), openWorldHint (network). - Toolsets. Hundreds of tools overwhelm agents, so tools are grouped into toolsets, derived from command domains: core (query, inspect, select, param get/set, undo), modeling, documentation, families, materials, project_setup, io, collaboration, analysis, scripting, admin, and one toolset per add-in. - By default a session exposes core plus the toolsets chosen in the client token's configuration. - Agents can list and enable toolsets at runtime with toolsets.list / toolsets.enable / toolsets.disable. The server then sends notifications/tools/list_changed. - Discovery tools (always available): - find_commands(query, limit?) does a semantic and keyword search over the entire registry, including disabled toolsets, and returns names, summaries and schemas; - describe_command(name); - run_command(name, arguments) calls any command that the session's permission level allows, even when its toolset is not enabled. - The tool list is generated at start-up, and regenerated when add-ins load or unload.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] For every registered command, find_commands can find it by its summary text, and run_command can execute it with the same result as the specific tool. - [ ] Loading an add-in that registers 2 commands sends tools/list_changed, and the new tools appear with their schemas. - [ ] Every tool marked readOnlyHint=true is in fact read-only (verified by a test that runs each read-only tool and checks that the model version is unchanged).

    2.16.4 Compound and session tools

    ID: DM-MCP-004 · Priority: P0 (query, inspect, undo) / P1 (others) · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.6

    Tool Purpose Permission
    query_elements(spec) The collector query in JSON form (§2.13.3), with fields to return chosen parameters, plus paging read_only
    get_element(id_or_guid, fields?) The element summary: category, type, level, host, all parameters with display values, bounding box read_only
    get_selection() / set_selection(ids) The user's current selection read_only / model_edit
    get_view_image(view_id, width, height, options) A PNG render of a view (returns image content), so an agent can see what it did read_only
    execute_lua(source, args?) Runs Lua for compound operations, at the trust level allowed for the session (level 0 for read_only, level 1 for model_edit, as configured for full_scripting). The result is the returned value (as JSON) plus captured log output. full_scripting (level 0 version: read_only)
    batch(calls[], atomic=true) Runs several commands in order. With atomic, they run in one transaction, and are all rolled back if any fails. model_edit
    session.begin_group(name) / session.end_group(mode) A transaction group around several tool calls, so that one undo reverts an agent's multi-step task (§2.7.1) model_edit
    undo(steps?) / redo(steps?) / history() Limited to the session's own items, unless the level is full_scripting model_edit
    preview(command, arguments) Runs a command in a transaction that is then rolled back. Returns the change set, the warnings and, optionally, a view image. model_edit
    confirm(preview_token) In confirm mode, destructive commands return a preview token instead of running. The user (in the AI Agents panel), or the agent if the policy allows, confirms it. model_edit
    toolsets.list / toolsets.enable / toolsets.disable See §2.16.3 read_only
    find_commands, describe_command, run_command See §2.16.3 (as the target command)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An agent creates 4 walls and a floor inside session.begin_group("Create room") … end_group("assimilate"). The UI shows one undo item named "Create room (agent: <client>)", and one undo removes everything. - [ ] preview("element.delete", …) returns the dependents that would be deleted, and leaves the model unchanged (same model version). - [ ] get_view_image returns a PNG that matches the view's current state after the agent's last transaction.

    2.16.5 Permissions and safety

    ID: DM-MCP-005 · Priority: P0 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.6

    Behaviour & rules. - Permission levels (per token or stdio session):

    Level Allowed command effects Lua (execute_lua)
    read_only read Trust level 0
    model_edit read, edit, settings, ui (selection, view activation). file_write limited to export into a configured output folder. Trust level 0
    full_scripting All, including file_read/file_write anywhere, network, script, destructive without confirmation (unless confirm mode is forced) Up to the level set in the token (default 1; never native unless the user enables it explicitly)
    • Confirm mode (default on for model_edit): commands with effect destructive (delete, purge, schema conversion, overwrite on load, BIMserver check-in) need confirmation (§2.16.4).
    • Attribution. Every transaction made by an agent records origin = {source: "mcp", actor: <client name>, session_id}. It appears in the undo list, the journal and, in BIMserver mode, in the check-in comment and element change stamps (RXD element data identity.last_modified_by).
    • Limits. Per-session rate limit (default 20 write calls per second). A maximum result size, with paging for queries. A maximum wall time per call (default 120 s; long operations report progress and support cancellation).
    • Isolation. A session can only act on the documents in its token's scope. File paths are checked against allowed folders. Agents cannot read or change the MCP configuration, tokens or trust store.
    • Human visibility. The AI Agents panel can show a running feed of tool calls. Pause agents holds the command queue for agent calls (they wait or time out) until resumed.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A read_only session calling wall.create gets an error permission.denied with the required level, and the model is unchanged. - [ ] With confirm mode on, element.delete from a model_edit session returns a preview token, and nothing is deleted until it is confirmed. - [ ] After Pause agents, a pending agent write is not executed until Resume.

    2.16.6 Resource catalogue

    ID: DM-MCP-006 · Priority: P0 (element, type, view, project, categories, commands) / P1 (others) · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.6

    Behaviour & rules. Resources are read-only JSON (or other stated MIME types). Resource templates use RFC 6570 URI templates. {doc} defaults to the active document when omitted (reviera://element/{id} = reviera://doc/active/element/{id}).

    URI template MIME Content
    reviera://documents application/json Open documents (ID, title, path or BIMserver project, kind, schema, mode)
    reviera://doc/{doc}/project application/json Project information, units summary, location, phases, current phase
    reviera://doc/{doc}/element/{id_or_guid} application/json Element summary (as get_element)
    reviera://doc/{doc}/element/{id_or_guid}/geometry{?detail,format} model/gltf-binary or application/json The element's geometry (glTF, or a JSON B-rep summary)
    reviera://doc/{doc}/type/{id_or_guid} application/json Type with parameters and instance count
    reviera://doc/{doc}/family/{id_or_guid} application/json Family summary, types and parameters (definitions, with formulas when allowed)
    reviera://doc/{doc}/categories application/json Categories used in the model, with counts and subcategories
    reviera://doc/{doc}/levels, …/grids application/json Datums with elevations and positions
    reviera://doc/{doc}/views, …/view/{id} application/json View list, or one view's definition (type, scale, level, template, crop, filters)
    reviera://doc/{doc}/view/{id}/image{?w,h} image/png Rendered view image
    reviera://doc/{doc}/sheets, …/sheet/{id} application/json Sheets and placed viewports
    reviera://doc/{doc}/schedule/{id}{?format} application/json or text/csv Schedule data
    reviera://doc/{doc}/parameters application/json Parameter catalogue: built-in, project, shared and global definitions with bindings
    reviera://doc/{doc}/materials application/json Materials and assets (summaries)
    reviera://doc/{doc}/warnings application/json Stored warnings
    reviera://doc/{doc}/selection application/json Current selection (subscribable)
    reviera://doc/{doc}/history application/json Undo history with origins
    reviera://commands, reviera://command/{name} application/json The registry (summaries), or one definition with its schemas
    reviera://units application/json Data types and unit catalogue (§2.9.4, §2.9.5)
    reviera://docs/{topic} text/markdown Built-in documentation pages (API reference, how-tos)
    • Subscriptions. Clients can subscribe to element/{id}, selection, warnings and history. The server sends notifications/resources/updated after commits that affect them (coalesced, at most 5 per second per resource). notifications/resources/list_changed is sent when documents open or close.
    • Resources never include credentials. They include RXD content only as summarised fields, never raw RXD carrier data.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Reading reviera://element/{guid} for a door returns its category, type, host wall GUID, level and all parameters with display values in project units. - [ ] A client subscribed to selection receives an update within 200 ms of the user changing the selection.

    2.16.7 Prompts

    ID: DM-MCP-007 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/05 §12.3

    Purpose. Give agents ready-made, well-tested task templates, so common jobs use the right tools in the right order.

    Behaviour & rules. The server offers MCP prompts as task templates, for example: Audit model (warnings, unplaced views, missing parameters); Prepare IFC export (check against an IDS); Create sheets from views; Explain this element; Colour views by parameter. Prompts are generated from documented Lua and graph templates. Add-ins can contribute prompts in their manifest. - Definition. A prompt has a name, title, description, typed arguments (with descriptions, required flags and allowed values) and a message template. Templates may embed resources (§2.16.6), for example the current selection or the warnings list, which are resolved when prompts/get is called. - Tool references. A prompt names the tools it expects the agent to use. At start-up, and when add-ins load, every prompt is checked against the current tool catalogue; a prompt that refers to a missing tool is withdrawn from prompts/list and logged. notifications/prompts/list_changed is sent when the list changes. - Permissions. A prompt declares the permission level its tools need; prompts/list for a session shows only prompts the session's level can complete. - Add-in prompts are declared in the manifest ([[prompts]] with name, file and arguments) and are namespaced <addin-id>/<name>. - Localisation. Prompt titles and descriptions follow the application language; message templates are written in English unless the add-in supplies translations.

    Commands. (protocol-level, prompts/list and prompts/get)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] prompts/list returns the built-in prompts with argument descriptions, and prompts/get("Audit model") returns a message sequence that refers only to existing tools. - [ ] A read_only session does not see Create sheets from views in prompts/list. - [ ] Disabling an add-in that contributed a prompt removes it from prompts/list and sends list_changed.

    Appendix A — Reference evolution (release history and version notes)

    Ref: research/05 §14, §15, §13.1, §11.2 · screenshots/platform/wall_tool_ribbon_no_options_bar_2027.png, screenshots/platform/autodesk_assistant_2027.png

    The reference product releases once a year, each spring, with point updates during the year. Its file format changes with each yearly release, and older versions cannot read newer files. The table summarises what each release added in the areas this chapter covers (and some others), and what that means for Reviera's priorities. This summary is informative. It guides priorities, and is not a feature list to copy.

    Reference release Notable additions (summarised) Implication for Reviera
    2020 (Apr 2019) PDF and image underlays with snapping; elliptical walls; egress path analysis; double fill patterns; multiline text and image parameters; visual programming installed by default; internal origin made visible Double fill patterns, image and multiline parameters, and PDF underlay snapping are now baseline expectations (DM-PAT-001, DM-PARAM-004, DM-IMP-004). Internal origin, base point and survey point are P0 (DM-LOC-001).
    2021 (Apr 2020) Slanted walls; generative design studies; real-time realistic views; 3D rebar; systems analysis; tags rotating with elements Design-space exploration is P2 and runs locally (DM-VPL-003).
    2022 (Apr 2021) Native vector PDF export; tapered walls; the new unit API (versioned spec and unit IDs) replacing old enumerations; nested AND/OR filter rules; coordination-model link (a clash-review format); Rhino import PDF export is P0 (DOC). Versioned data-type and unit IDs are adopted from the start (DM-PARAM-004, DM-UNIT-001), avoiding a later API break.
    2023 (Apr 2022) New independent structural analytical model; cloud parameter service (preview, then GA in 2023.1); duplicate family parameters; filled regions in 3D families; IFC element mapping; Infrastructure units discipline The parameter library with URL/git distribution (DM-SPAR-001) is the open counterpart of the cloud parameter service. Duplicate parameters and the Infrastructure discipline are included.
    2024 (Apr 2023) Toposolid; dark theme; Project Browser search; one simplified default template; 2D draw order in 3D families; relocatable collaboration cache Draw order in families (DM-FED-007), and a small set of shipped templates (DM-TMPL-001).
    2025 (Apr 2024) Move to a new .NET runtime (add-ins rebuilt); sheet collections; family arrays of 0 or 1 elements; mullion profiles with several loops; macros edited in an external code editor; bulk export of several formats Arrays with count 0/1 (DM-FED-004), multi-loop profiles (DM-FSPEC-003), an external editor and language server for scripts (DM-LUA-008), and bulk export (DM-EXP-013). A stable, semver-versioned Lua API (DM-LUA-011) avoids forced rebuilds.
    2026 (Apr 2025) GPU-accelerated graphics (preview); shared parameters on view markers; title-block "As indicated" override; sheet-collection parameters; compound structures without a core; add-in dependency isolation and add-in manager settings; built-in add-in manager UI Per-add-in environments and an Add-in Manager from v1 (DM-LUA-001, DM-ADDIN-003). Cores are optional in layered types (§2.3.8).
    2027 (7 Apr 2026) Rule-based numbering; built-in AI assistant (preview) that calls MCP tools; Options Bar removed (options moved into the contextual ribbon and Properties); walls hosted on walls; multi-category tags as defaults; tag leader control; carbon asset on materials; IFC property-mapping dialog; extended properties from external data; new .NET runtime; Windows 11 only Confirms the direction of several Reviera design choices: MCP as a first-class interface (§2.16, P0), no Options Bar (UI chapter), a carbon asset (DM-MAT-005), a property-mapping UI (DM-FILE-004), and walls as hosts (§2.6.1). Extended properties get an open provider API (DM-PARAM-005).
    2027.1 (Jun 2026) Rotatable custom fill patterns; AI assistant reliability (MCP tool calls logged in journals); ambient shadows Pattern rotation (DM-PAT-001); every MCP call is logged in the session journal (DM-TXN-003, DM-MCP-005).
    2027.2 (Jul 2026) Tag by example; view-title snapping; incremental model open option Partial and incremental open (DM-FILE-001, P1/P2).

    Version and platform notes that shape Reviera: 1. One-way upgrades. Each yearly release changes the native format. There is no "save as previous version", and families must be upgraded too. → Reviera uses IFC plus a semver-versioned RXD, with a documented compatibility promise and save-to-previous (DM-MIG-001). 2. Mostly single-threaded regeneration (the reference's own hardware guidance favours high single-core clock speed). → Parallel regeneration is a core differentiator (DM-REGEN-003). 3. Runtime churn for extensions. The reference changed .NET runtimes in 2025 and again in 2027, so add-ins had to be rebuilt each time. → The Lua API is versioned separately from the application (DM-LUA-011). Lua add-ins need no compilation. 4. Late add-in isolation and security moves. Dependency isolation arrived in 2026, and all-user add-ins moved to a protected program folder in 2027. → Reviera has isolated environments, admin-only system add-in folders, trust levels and signing from v1 (DM-LUA-007, DM-ADDIN-002). 5. Windows-only, Windows 11 only from 2027. → Reviera targets Windows 10 and later, macOS 10.12 and later, and current Linux distributions through Flatpak (TECH_STACK §5.4). 6. Product tiers. The reference's lower-cost tier lacks the API, macros, visual programming, the conceptual massing environment and IFC import. → Reviera has no feature tiers. Everything in this chapter is available to every user. 7. Vendor cloud services (cloud parameters, cloud worksharing, content libraries, issue tracking, AI assistant service) → P3. Open alternatives are noted where they exist: parameter libraries over git/HTTPS (DM-SPAR-001), BIMserver (COL), BCF (DM-IMP-011), and MCP with any agent (§2.16).

    Open questions and deviations from the reference

    Open questions

    ID Question Proposed answer / next step
    Q-DM-01 Should add-ins be able to define new categories? Not in v1. Use cat.generic_models with ObjectType, or a registry extension in v2 once IFC mapping rules for custom categories are agreed. A v2 design would let an add-in register addin.<namespace>.<key> categories that must name an IFC class and PredefinedType (usually USERDEFINED plus ObjectType), default object styles and behaviour flags; projects using them would still open without the add-in, falling back to Generic Models. Deferred to the post-Alpha/POC review (owner, 2026-10-12).
    Q-DM-02 Roofs: always IfcRoof with IfcSlab parts, or a single IfcSlab ROOF for one-face roofs? Default to IfcRoof aggregate (more consistent); make the simple form an export option. Check with downstream tools. Test plan: export both forms from five roof shapes (flat, mono-pitch, gable, hip, freeform), open them in at least three viewers and two quantity take-off tools, and record which form gives correct areas and classification. Decide before P1 roof work starts.
    Q-DM-03 Property-set naming for built-in parameters that have no buildingSMART home (group-named sets such as Identity Data), and the default set for user parameters (<Project> Parameters / <Category> Parameters). Needs owner confirmation. The alternative is one vendor-neutral set name (for example Common). Must align with 02a, which owns the Reviera_* names. Criteria: names must not collide with buildingSMART Pset_/Qto_ prefixes, must be stable across languages (not localised group names), and must be readable in third-party schedules. A sample file with both conventions will be reviewed with two downstream users.
    Q-DM-04 Is IfcProjectLibrary declared by IfcProject (families inside a project) accepted by the buildingSMART validation service and by common viewers? Test with sample files before P1. Fallback: declare types directly on IfcProject and keep the family grouping in RXD only. Test: a project with three families as IfcProjectLibrary objects, validated by the buildingSMART validation service and opened in at least three viewers and BIMserver. If any rejects or loses the types, use the fallback and record the finding in 02a.
    Q-DM-05 Detail-level geometry in extra sub-contexts (Body-Coarse/Body-Medium): do other tools ignore them safely? Test with at least three viewers. Fallback: keep Coarse/Medium in RXD as recipes only. Also check file-size impact on a 50 MB model (extra maps for families with detail-level variants) and whether BIMserver stores the extra sub-contexts. Decide before the P1 Family Editor milestone.
    Q-DM-06 Sizes of embedded RXD documents in BIMserver (large IfcText values) and their effect on server performance. Measure with a 100-sheet project. 02a defines chunking. COL owns BIMserver specifics. Measurements to record: check-in time, server storage, download time and query speed with embedded RXD versus the external carrier, at 10, 100 and 500 sheets. If embedded documents slow the server noticeably, the BIMserver default carrier becomes external.
    Q-DM-07 OCCT thread-safety details (memory manager mode, handle reference counting) for the pinned OCCT version. Stress tests in CI (DM-REGEN-004). Run the parallel regeneration suite under ThreadSanitizer-equivalent checks and a long-running soak test (10,000 random edits) per OCCT upgrade; document the memory-manager mode and any operations that must be serialised. Any crash or data race blocks the OCCT upgrade.
    Q-DM-08 General 2D constraint solver choice (PlaneGCS vs SolveSpace solver) and its licence fit. Decide before P2. Both are GPL-3.0-compatible as stated, but this must be verified. Compare on a benchmark of 200 sketches from shipped families: solve time, robustness with redundant constraints, quality of conflict reports, and Rust binding effort. The licence check goes to the dependency licence register.
    Q-DM-09 Licence and coverage checks for LibreDWG (DWG read/write versions), openNURBS (3DM), OpenUSD and bundled open data (weather, cities, EPD sets, textures). Track in the dependency licence register (cargo-deny plus a data licence list). Each format or data set gets an owner, a licence verdict and a coverage note (versions read and written). Formats that fail the check move to P3 with the open alternative stated in §2.11.5 and §2.11.6.
    Q-DM-10 MCP tool names containing .: accepted by all target MCP clients? Default to dotted names, with the underscore style setting as a fallback (DM-MCP-003). Revisit when the MCP naming guidance changes. Test the five most used MCP clients at each release and record which need the fallback; the setting can be chosen per client token.
    Q-DM-11 ~~RXD document and key names used here~~ Resolved: aligned with the Name Registry and Object Kind Registry in 02a §6.4–§6.5, which are authoritative. New names proposed by this chapter (kinds numbering.rule and decal.type, element-data key elements.numbering) are listed for 02a to register.
    Q-DM-12 LuaJIT on ARM64 macOS, and LuaJIT memory limits through mlua. Validate per platform. Fall back to interpreter mode and to memory monitoring (DM-LUA-001, DM-LUA-007). The CI matrix runs the Lua test suite with JIT on and off on Windows x64, Linux x64 and arm64, and macOS arm64; any platform with failures ships with the JIT off until fixed.
    ### Intentional deviations from the reference
    Area Reference behaviour Reviera behaviour Reason
    Native format Proprietary compound file, one-way yearly upgrades A single valid IFC file, with RXD embedded as standard property sets (or an optional sidecar); semver RXD; save to previous version Openness, longevity, version-control friendliness (§2.1, DM-MIG-001)
    Internal units Decimal feet SI (metres, radians, …) Matches IFC, and avoids conversion error (DM-UNIT-001)
    Regeneration Largely single-threaded Parallel by dependency level with rayon; deterministic Use of modern CPUs (DM-REGEN-003)
    Over-constraint errors A generic "constraints not satisfied" message Names and highlights the conflicting constraints Usability (DM-REGEN-002)
    Undo after save Cleared in some situations, such as synchronisation Kept across local saves Usability (DM-TXN-002)
    Formula language No <=/>=, no text concatenation, implicit units, no global references in families <=/>=, & concatenation, explicit unit rules with a compatibility rule, @Global references, interpolating lookups, text functions Expressiveness and safety (DM-FRM-001)
    Shared parameters One active UTF-16 text file per session; or a vendor cloud service Several JSON parameter libraries, versioned, distributable by git/HTTPS; import of legacy text files Openness, diffs, team distribution without a vendor cloud (DM-SPAR-001)
    Lookup tables and type catalogs ##-typed header CSV, .txt catalogs Name[spec:unit] header CSV, .types.csv; legacy header import Own, readable format (DM-LUT-001, DM-TCAT-001)
    Family files Proprietary container IFC type library + RXD; usable as static types by any IFC tool Interoperability (DM-FFMT-001)
    Add-ins Compiled .NET assemblies; XML manifest; runtime rebuilds on .NET changes Lua packages; TOML manifest with a mandatory SPDX license; GPL-compatibility check; trust levels GPL policy (TECH_STACK §4.2); safety; no rebuilds (§2.14)
    Macros C# with an external IDE and SDK install Lua, built-in editor, optional external editor with a language server; recording Lower barrier (DM-LUA-008)
    Visual programming A separate bundled application Built on the command registry and Lua, compiled to Lua One API surface (DM-VPL-001)
    AI integration A vendor-hosted assistant (preview) Built-in MCP server for any agent; per-token permissions; confirm mode; attribution Openness and control (§2.16)

    2aCHChapter 2a: Reviera Extension Data (RXD): Format and IFC Embedding

    ID prefix: DM-RXD · Priority: P0 · Status: Draft 0.2 · 2026-10-12

    Owner directive (2026-10-12): "Full interoperability using IFC, with any additional information held in a bespoke format. If it can be embedded in a custom IFC data section that would be optimal. Priority is compatibility."

    Decision. - Reviera project data is IFC first. - Information IFC cannot express is held in one bespoke format, Reviera Extension Data (RXD): versioned JSON documents defined by JSON Schemas. - By default, RXD is embedded inside the IFC file using only standard, schema-valid IFC constructs: custom property sets with text values. - An external sidecar (.reviera) is a second carrier for exactly the same documents. It is used when embedding isn't wanted or a downstream tool removes unknown data.

    1. Principles (in priority order)

    # Principle
    1 Compatibility first. Every file Reviera writes is a valid IFC file under its declared schema, and passes the buildingSMART schema and normative-rule checks. Reviera never writes custom entities, non-standard sections or comments that carry data.
    2 IFC holds everything it can express. This includes spatial structure, elements, types, materials and layer sets, openings, ports, systems, zones, grids, classifications, standard Psets and Qtos, and the values of user-defined parameters, which go in readable Psets. Other tools see the complete building without knowing about Reviera.
    3 RXD holds only what IFC can't. This includes parametric intent (constraints, sketches, generation recipes, family definitions, formulas), documentation (views, sheets, schedules, view-specific annotation, graphic standards), and authoring organisation (phases, design options, worksets, browser organisation, project UI state).
    4 References go one way. RXD points into IFC by GlobalId. IFC content never depends on RXD.
    5 Degrades safely. If a tool removes RXD, the IFC model is still complete and correct; only drawings and parametric intent are lost. If a tool edits elements, Reviera detects it and reconciles (§7).
    6 Open format. The JSON Schemas are published under the MIT licence, together with this document, so any tool can read and write RXD.

    2. Why Property Sets (the evaluation behind "custom IFC data section")

    IFC has no official extension section for arbitrary vendor data. The candidate mechanisms were evaluated for compatibility:

    Mechanism Valid IFC? Survives other tools? Verdict
    Custom entity types ❌ invalid against the schema ❌ Rejected
    STEP comments /* … */ Valid ❌ removed by parsers and writers Rejected
    Custom HEADER entities / Part 21 Ed.3 sections Doubtful ❌ not supported by mainstream IFC tools Rejected
    IfcDocumentReference to an external file ✅ Only the link survives; the content is outside the file Used only for the external-sidecar carrier (§5)
    Repurposing IfcBlobTexture and similar binary fields Formally valid Semantically wrong; tools may strip or alter them Rejected
    Custom property sets (Reviera_*) with IfcText values ✅ IFC2X3/IFC4/IFC4X3; custom Pset names without the Pset_ prefix are allowed ✅ property sets are the most widely kept part of IFC across viewers, checkers, model servers (including BIMserver's object storage) and authoring tools Chosen

    Two further benefits of property sets: - Data attached to the element it describes moves with that element through partial exports, model splitting, federation and BIMserver's object-level storage. - The design works unchanged for every IFC encoding: STEP (.ifc), .ifczip, ifcXML, and future JSON-based IFC.

    3. Embedded Carrier (default)

    3.1 Placement

    RXD scope Attached to Property set name
    Manifest IfcProject Reviera_Manifest
    Project-level document (views, sheets, schedules, standards, phases, …; §6) IfcProject Reviera_Doc:<document-path> (one Pset per document, e.g. Reviera_Doc:views/index)
    Element data (recipe, sketch, owned constraints, phase/option/workset membership) The element itself, e.g. IfcWall, IfcStair Reviera_Element
    Type data (family linkage, type parameter formulas) The IfcTypeObject Reviera_Type
    Family recipe (shared by all its types) IfcProject (project) or IfcProjectLibrary (family file) Reviera_Doc:families/<familyId>

    All are attached through standard relations: IfcRelDefinesByProperties, or HasPropertySets for type objects.

    3.2 Property layout

    Reviera_Manifest (one per file):

    Property IFC type Content
    Format IfcLabel reviera-rxd
    FormatVersion IfcLabel 1.0
    DataId IfcIdentifier UUID that identifies this model's RXD set
    DataRevision IfcInteger Increments on every save
    Writer IfcLabel Reviera 0.4.0
    Carrier IfcLabel embedded, or external (see §5)
    Index IfcText A JSON document index with path, kind, schema version, sha256 and object count for each document

    Reviera_Doc:<path> and Reviera_Element / Reviera_Type:

    Property IFC type Content
    Kind IfcLabel Document kind (for example views.index). For element data, a comma-separated list of the sections present (for example identity,sketch,recipe); see §6.4.
    SchemaVersion IfcLabel For example 1.0
    Encoding IfcLabel json or zstd+base64
    Sha256 IfcIdentifier Hash of the decoded JSON bytes
    Rev IfcInteger Object/document revision, used for merging
    GeomHash IfcIdentifier Element data only. Hash of the element's canonical IFC representation as Reviera last generated it. Used to detect edits made by other tools (§7).
    Data IfcText Payload, when it fits in one chunk
    Data_0001 … Data_nnnn IfcText Payload chunks, when it doesn't

    3.3 Encoding rules (compatibility-driven)

    1. Choosing an encoding: - Payloads of 8 KiB or less are stored as json: readable in any IFC property viewer. - Larger payloads are stored as zstd+base64: compact, and base64 is plain ASCII.
    2. ASCII only. JSON is written with every non-ASCII character escaped as \uXXXX. Every payload string is therefore 7-bit ASCII, which avoids differences between tools in handling STEP \X2\ encodings. STEP string escaping (doubled ' and \\) is applied by the IFC writer (IfcOpenShell).
    3. Chunk size. Each chunk holds at most 32,000 characters, configurable, chosen to stay clear of string-buffer limits in older parsers. Chunks are joined in numeric order before decoding.
    4. Canonical JSON. Keys are sorted, the representation is deterministic and there is no insignificant whitespace. This makes Sha256 stable and diffs small.
    5. Size guard. If one document would exceed a configurable limit (default 64 MiB encoded), Reviera warns and suggests the external carrier.

    3.4 Example (STEP excerpt)

    #5021=IFCPROPERTYSINGLEVALUE('Kind',$,IFCLABEL('identity,recipe'),$);
#5022=IFCPROPERTYSINGLEVALUE('Encoding',$,IFCLABEL('json'),$);
#5023=IFCPROPERTYSINGLEVALUE('GeomHash',$,IFCIDENTIFIER('b3f1c09e…'),$);
#5024=IFCPROPERTYSINGLEVALUE('Data',$,IFCTEXT('{"identity":{"iid":48213},"recipe":{"kind":"recipe.stair","riserHeight":0.175,"runs":[{"end":[3.6,0],"risers":12,"start":[0,0]}],"treadDepth":0.28}}'),$);
#5025=IFCPROPERTYSET('1hQ$…',#5,'Reviera_Element',$,(#5021,#5022,#5023,#5024));
#5026=IFCRELDEFINESBYPROPERTIES('2aX0…',#5,$,$,(#4800),#5025);   /* #4800 = IFCSTAIR */

    4. Exports for Exchange

    Command Result
    Save (default) IFC with embedded RXD: full fidelity, and still fully standard IFC
    Export clean IFC (export.ifc{strip_rxd=true}) IFC with all Reviera_* Psets removed, for recipients who want no vendor-specific properties. The building model is identical.
    Export IFC with documentation (export.ifc{documentation=true}) Also writes documentation in standard IFC form for consumers that support it: annotation as IfcAnnotation (IfcGeometricCurveSet, IfcTextLiteralWithExtent), worksets and design options as IfcGroup, phase status as Pset_*Common.Status. This is an export; RXD remains the authoritative store.
    Save with external sidecar See §5

    5. External Carrier (.reviera sidecar), the alternative

    The external carrier holds the same RXD documents in a file outside the IFC. Use it when: - the project is version-controlled in git (directory form gives one JSON file per document, so diffs are clean) - a downstream tool in the round-trip strips unknown Psets - documents exceed the embedding size guard

    Forms. - X.reviera: a ZIP holding manifest.json (stored first, uncompressed) plus <document-path>.json. - X.reviera/: an unpacked directory with the same layout. - X.rvb: a bundle ZIP holding model.ifc and reviera/….

    Binding. In external mode the IFC file still carries Reviera_Manifest, with Carrier = external, its DataId and DataRevision, and an IfcDocumentReference to the sidecar file name. Element-level Reviera_Element and Reviera_Type Psets are still embedded, because they are small and travel with their elements. Only Reviera_Doc:* documents move out of the file.

    Lookup on open. Use embedded documents if present. Otherwise look for X.reviera (file or folder), then a .rvb containing the IFC. If nothing is found, open with default standards and show a notice.

    6. Object Model and Document Catalogue

    6.1 Object envelope

    All RXD objects share one envelope:

    { "id": "0192a3f5-1b2c-7d3e-8f40-112233445566", "kind": "view.plan", "rev": 7,
  "name": "Level 1", "data": { }, "ext": { } }
    • id is a UUIDv7 for objects that exist only in RXD.
    • Element data uses the element's GlobalId as its identity.

    6.2 References

    Target Form Example
    IFC object ifc:<GlobalId> ifc:3vB2YO$MX4xv5uCqZZG05x
    RXD object rv:<uuid> rv:0192a3f5-…
    Named geometric sub-reference ifc:<GlobalId>#<ref> #face:core.ext, #edge:top.start, #refplane:Left, #end:1
    Linked model element link:<linkId>/ifc:<GlobalId> —

    Sub-references are named, never index-based. The geometry engine resolves them after each regeneration. Units are SI (metres, radians). 3D coordinates are in the IFC project world coordinate system. View annotation coordinates are in the view's own plane coordinate system.

    6.3 Documents (format version 1.0)
