The typed value is recorded in the tool's micro-operation log as an explicit point ({op: "point", xyz, typed: "<text>"}), so crash recovery (§2.1 of the conventions) replays the exact coordinates rather than re-parsing.

    Commands. No command of its own. The resolved point is passed to the running tool exactly as a click would be; scripts call the creation command (for example wall.create) with explicit coordinates.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Wall tool, first click, type 5000, Enter: the result is a wall exactly 5.000 m long along the cursor direction. - [ ] In an imperial project, typing 8 6 produces 2.5908 m. - [ ] Typing 1200+600 in a metric project draws a line 1.800 m long; typing (2*900)/2 draws 0.900 m. - [ ] Typing -300 or abc keeps the box open with an error and creates nothing. - [ ] Moving the mouse after the box has opened does not change the direction of the committed segment.

    3.1.8 Snapping, alignment lines and constraint keys

    ID: ARC-SNAP-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §2.4, §16

    Purpose. Precise cursor input.

    Behaviour & rules. - Snap kinds: endpoints, midpoints, nearest, work-plane grid, quadrants, intersections, centres, perpendicular, tangents, points, remote objects and point clouds. Each kind can be switched on or off in Manage › Snaps. - Length and angle increments depend on zoom level. Each zoom band has a configurable increment. - Two-letter one-shot overrides apply to the next pick only: SE endpoint, SM midpoint, SN nearest, SI intersection, SC centre, SP perpendicular, ST tangent, SQ quadrant, SW work-plane grid, SX points, SR remote objects, PC point cloud, SO snaps off and SS override off. - Alignment lines are dashed temporary lines drawn through the endpoints of nearby geometry, extended in parallel and perpendicular directions. They snap the cursor when it is within 6 px. - Shift held while drawing constrains input to orthogonal directions in the view or work plane. - A snap marker shows the kind of snap with a glyph and a tooltip.

    Commands. snap.set_options(kinds, increments?). Snapping is interactive only. Scripted commands always take exact coordinates.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With all snaps switched off except Midpoint, the cursor snaps only to midpoints. - [ ] SO disables snapping for exactly one pick.

    3.1.9 Tab and Spacebar behaviours

    ID: ARC-KEY-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §2.4, §4.2, §5.2, §5.4, §8.2, §15.3

    Purpose. Two keys with consistent, context-dependent meanings.

    Behaviour & rules. - Tab cycles the pre-selection candidate under the cursor. The candidates come from a ranked list: 1. Overlapping elements under the cursor, frontmost first. 2. The connected chain of the hovered element (walls joined end to end, lines in a chain, or slab edges along a perimeter). 3. Sub-elements of the hovered element: curtain panel, grid or mullion; stacked sub-wall; stair run, landing or support; group member; shape-edit vertex or edge; layer boundary in Edit Assembly. 4. Alternative references for Align, dimensions and temporary dimensions.

    The status bar names the current candidate. Shift+Tab cycles backwards. - Spacebar, while placing: - walls (including By Room and By Segment): flips the exterior side about the location line; - doors: flips the hand; - windows: no action; - components: rotates the preview 90° about Z, or aligns it to the nearest wall when one is within snap distance; - stair winders: rotates the turn direction. - Spacebar with a selection flips walls, cycles doors and windows through their four facing/hand combinations, and rotates free-standing components by 90° (ARC-FLIP-001). - Spacebar in Rotate (§3.12) picks a new centre of rotation. - Elliptical walls ignore the Spacebar flip.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Hovering a wall joined in a closed rectangle and pressing Tab once highlights all four walls, and a click selects them all. - [ ] Spacebar while drawing a wall from left to right puts the exterior face below the wall line in plan.

    3.1.10 In-canvas element controls

    ID: ARC-CTRL-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §2.5

    Purpose. Direct manipulation of selected elements in the view.

    Behaviour & rules. Each selected element shows the controls its kind supports: - blue endpoint drag dots (curve-driven elements); - shape handles (triangular arrows that drag a face or an extent); - flip arrows; - a pushpin (pinned state); - padlocks (locked constraints); - the make-permanent dimension icon; - an Allow/Disallow join glyph at each wall end, in plan and in 3D; - an end-wrap toggle at each wall end, in plan; - Configure Grid Layout (curtain faces); - a 3D/2D extent toggle, a bubble-visibility checkbox and an Add Elbow control (datums); - direct-manipulation arrows (stairs, §3.7).

    Dragging a control issues the matching command once, on mouse-up. The preview during the drag uses the same regeneration code path with a scratch transaction.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Dragging a wall end dot regenerates its joins live and commits a single undo step. - [ ] A pinned element shows its pushpin, and its drag controls are disabled.

    3.2 Datums

    3.2.1 Levels

    ID: ARC-LVL-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §3.1 · screenshots/architecture/levels_in_elevation_view.png

    Purpose. Named horizontal planes that host level-based elements and define stories.

    Workflow. 1. The user opens a section or elevation view. The tool is unavailable in other views. 2. The user starts Architecture › Datum › Level (LL). Draw choices are Line and Pick Lines (with Offset). 3. While the cursor moves, level ends align with the ends of existing levels, and a temporary vertical dimension to the nearest level is shown. The user clicks the start and then the end. 4. Reviera names the level by incrementing the trailing number or letter of the previous name: Level 2 → Level 3, L02 → L03, A → B. 5. Clicking the name label renames the level. Reviera then asks whether to rename the associated views. Clicking the elevation label edits the elevation.

    UI. Placement-panel controls: Make Plan View (on by default) and Plan View Types… (Floor Plan, Ceiling Plan, Structural Plan, and so on). Instance and type parameters are listed below.

    Behaviour & rules. - A story level has Building Story = true and its own plan views. A reference level has neither. Make Plan View creates the selected plan view types. - Copying or arraying a level always creates reference levels without views. View › Plan Views lists the levels that have no views yet. - Changing the elevation moves every element whose base or top constraint refers to the level. This happens through datum edges; offsets are kept. - Deleting a level deletes its views and every element hosted on it, after a confirmation dialog that lists the counts by category. - Instance parameters: Elevation, Name, Story Above (used for IFC export height), Computation Height (the height at which room areas are measured, default 0), Scope Box, Structural, Building Story, Design Option (read-only). - Type parameters: Elevation Base (Project Base Point or Survey Point), Line Weight, Colour, Line Pattern, Symbol (head with bubble, head without bubble, or none), Symbol at End 1 Default and Symbol at End 2 Default. - Datum extents and head controls follow ARC-DATUM-001.

    Regeneration. A level is a root node. Its outgoing datum edges go to all level-based elements (walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, components, rooms, stairs and so on) and to the views associated with it.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Story level: IfcBuildingStorey, aggregated under IfcBuilding (IfcRelAggregates). Elevation is set from the level elevation in the building's coordinate system, and ObjectPlacement is relative to the building. Pset_BuildingStoreyCommon holds AboveGround and EntranceLevel where the user has set them. - Reference level: IfcAnnotation with ObjectType = "ReferenceLevel", contained in the nearest story level below it, with a 3D Axis representation (a horizontal line). (4X3: IfcAnnotation.PredefinedType = USERDEFINED.) - Parameter values (Elevation, Computation Height, Story Above, Structural, Building Story) are stored as IFC properties on the level. The level type is an IfcTypeObject with ApplicableOccurrence = "IfcBuildingStorey", and its graphic parameters are stored as properties on that type. - RXD element data (recipe.datum): the 3D extent, the per-view 2D extents keyed by view GlobalId, bubble flags, elbows, end locks and the scope box assignment.

    Commands. - level.create(elevation, name?, type_id?, make_plan_views?: bool, plan_view_types?: [view_type_id], extent?: Line) -> element_id - level.set_elevation(level_id, elevation) - level.rename(level_id, name, rename_views?: bool) - level.set_story(level_id, is_building_story) - level.create_plan_views(level_ids, view_type_ids) -> [view_id]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing a level's elevation by +300 mm raises every wall based on it by 300 mm and changes the height of every wall whose top constraint is that level. - [ ] Copying a level produces a reference level with no plan views, and it is exported as IfcAnnotation, not as a storey. - [ ] Deleting a level shows the dependent-element count before it commits.

    3.2.2 Grids

    ID: ARC-GRID-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §3.2 · screenshots/architecture/grid_type_properties_dialog.png

    Purpose. Vertical datum planes that organise the design. Columns can follow them.

    Workflow. 1. The user starts Architecture › Datum › Grid (GR) in a plan view, or in a section or elevation to adjust vertical extents. 2. Draw choices: Line, Start-End-Radius Arc, Center-Ends Arc, Pick Lines, and Multi-Segment. Multi-Segment opens a sketch in which the user draws a connected chain of lines and arcs and then presses Finish. 3. The user clicks the start and the end. The label increments automatically: numbers follow numbers and letters follow letters, and renaming the first grid to a letter switches the series to letters. 4. Grid ends align with parallel grids and show a lock (ARC-DATUM-001).

    UI. Selected-grid controls: bubble checkboxes at each end, the 2D/3D extent toggle, Add Elbow, end locks, and centre-segment handles when Center Segment is None or Custom.

    Behaviour & rules. - Type parameters: Symbol, Center Segment (Continuous, None or Custom) with its weight, colour and pattern, End Segment weight, colour and pattern, End Segments Length (in paper space), plan-view symbol defaults for each end, and the non-plan-view symbol default (Top, Bottom, Both or None). - Instance parameters: Name and Scope Box. - Grid names must be unique in the project. A duplicate name is rejected with a warning. - A multi-segment grid is edited only through Edit Sketch. It cannot have different scopes for different segments, and Copy/Monitor (COL chapter) cannot monitor it. - Arc grids appear only in plan views. A grid appears in a section or elevation only where the view plane crosses it.

    Regeneration. Root node, with outgoing datum edges to columns that have Moves With Grids on, to grid-locked constraints, and to dimensions.

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcGrid is contained in the ground story. By default Reviera writes one per scope box plus one for the grids that have no scope box. Each grid line is an IfcGridAxis with AxisTag = Name, AxisCurve set to IfcPolyline / IfcTrimmedCurve / IfcCompositeCurve (for multi-segment grids), and SameSense. - U/V assignment. Reviera clusters the axes by direction: the largest cluster becomes UAxes, the cluster most nearly at right angles to it becomes VAxes, and everything else (radial and multi-segment axes) goes to WAxes. IFC4 requires VAxes to be non-empty; see Open questions. - Per-axis data goes in RXD element data (recipe.datum) on the IfcGrid, keyed by the named sub-reference #axis:<uuid>, with the AxisTag as a cross-check. It holds the type reference, the 3D extent, the per-view 2D extents, bubble flags, elbow offsets and the scope box. - Grid type: IfcTypeObject (ApplicableOccurrence = "IfcGrid") whose graphic parameters are stored as properties on the type.

    Commands. - grid.create(curve | segments: [curve], name?, type_id?, scope_box_id?) -> element_id - grid.rename(grid_id, name) - grid.set_curve(grid_id, curve)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Ten grids drawn in sequence get the names 1–10. When the first grid of a new run is renamed "A", the next ones are named B, C, and so on. - [ ] A column with Moves With Grids follows the grid when the grid is moved, and stays put when the setting is off. - [ ] Every grid line round-trips through IFC with the same name, curve and extents.

    3.2.3 Reference planes

    ID: ARC-REFP-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §3.3

    Purpose. Infinite construction planes for alignment, dimensioning, hosting work planes, sketch guides and family skeletons.

    Workflow. The user starts Work Plane › Ref Plane (RP) and either draws a line with two clicks or uses Pick Lines (with Offset and Lock). The plane passes through the line and is at right angles to the view plane.

    Behaviour & rules. - A reference plane is shown as a green dashed line in every view to which it is perpendicular, with extent handles. - Properties: Name (named planes appear in the Work Plane dialog list), Subcategory (user-defined, for visibility control) and Scope Box. In families: Is Reference (Not a Reference, Strong, Weak, Left, Center (Left/Right), Right, Front, Back, Bottom, Top, …) and Defines Origin. - 2D and 3D extents work as described in ARC-DATUM-001. The plane itself is unbounded for hosting and alignment purposes.

    Regeneration. Root node, with datum edges to elements whose work plane is this plane and to aligned or locked references.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcAnnotation with ObjectType = "ReferencePlane", Name = the plane's name and an Axis representation (the defining line). Subcategory, Is Reference and Defines Origin are parameter values stored as properties. The plane's normal, extents and scope box are stored in RXD element data (recipe.datum).

    Commands. refplane.create(p0, p1, view_normal | normal, name?, subcategory?) -> element_id, refplane.rename(id, name).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A named reference plane appears in the Work Plane › Name list, and a model line can be sketched on it. - [ ] A reference plane drawn in plan is invisible in a 3D view and visible in any section cut at right angles to it.

    3.2.4 Datum extents

    ID: ARC-DATUM-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §3.1, §3.2, §3.5

    Purpose. Control how far levels, grids and reference planes extend, either in all views or in one view.

    Behaviour & rules. - 3D (model) extents are the datum's real extent and are shared by every parallel view. 2D (view-specific) extents override them in one view. A grip label toggles between "3D" and "2D". - Right-click › Reset to 3D Extents removes the 2D override. Maximize 3D Extents extends the datum to the model's bounding box. - Propagate Extents (Modify | Grids/Levels › Datum panel) copies the current view's 2D extents to the selected parallel views. - Alignment locks. Aligned datum ends show a padlock. When it is locked, dragging one end drags all the aligned ends. - Add Elbow inserts a jog near the bubble, with two draggable vertices. The jog is per view. - Each end has a bubble-visibility flag, per view. - A datum appears in a view only if its 3D extent (or its scope box, if it has one) crosses the view's cut plane or crop region. Datums that are not perpendicular to the view appear only where they cross it.

    Commands. - datum.set_extent(datum_id, view_id?, end, point) (no view_id means the 3D extent) - datum.reset_to_3d(datum_ids, view_id) - datum.maximize_3d(datum_ids) - datum.propagate_extents(datum_ids, source_view_id, target_view_ids) - datum.set_bubble(datum_id, view_id, end, visible) - datum.add_elbow(datum_id, view_id, end)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Dragging a grid end in 2D mode in plan view A does not change it in plan view B. Propagating the extents to B does. - [ ] Locked aligned level ends move together. After unlocking, they move independently.

    3.2.5 Scope boxes

    ID: ARC-SCOPE-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §3.4 · screenshots/architecture/scope_boxes_in_plan.png

    Purpose. Named 3D boxes that control where datums are visible and what their extents are, and that drive consistent view crops.

    Workflow. 1. The user starts View › Create › Scope Box. This works only in plan views. The user sets Name and Height on the contextual tab and clicks two opposite corners. 2. The box can then be resized with its handles in plan or 3D, and rotated with its rotate control or the Rotate tool. 3. The user assigns datums to the box (Properties › Scope Box) and assigns views to the box (view property Scope Box).

    Behaviour & rules. - A datum assigned to a box appears only in views whose cut plane or view plane crosses the box. Its 3D extents are set to the box faces plus a margin of 2 mm in paper space. Moving or resizing the box moves the datum ends. - A view assigned to a box gets a crop region equal to the box footprint (rotated if the box is rotated) and an unlocked crop. Changing the box updates the crop. - Views Visible (an instance property with an Edit dialog) lists the views in which the box itself is drawn. - Deleting a box clears all assignments. Datums keep their current extents.

    Regeneration. Root node, with datum edges to assigned datums and to the crop regions of assigned views.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcAnnotation with ObjectType = "ScopeBox", Name = the box name and a Box representation (IfcBoundingBox, oriented by ObjectPlacement). RXD element data (recipe.datum) on the box holds the Views Visible list. Datums and views record their box assignment in their own RXD data.

    Commands. - scopebox.create(name, rectangle: {corner_a, corner_b, rotation?}, height, level_id?) -> element_id - scopebox.set_extents(id, min, max, rotation?) - datum.assign_scope_box(datum_ids, scope_box_id | null) - view.assign_scope_box(view_ids, scope_box_id | null) (DOC owns views, and this command is listed here for completeness)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Rotating a scope box by 30° rotates the crop region of every assigned view by 30°. - [ ] A grid assigned to a box that does not reach Level 3 is not shown on the Level 3 plan.

    3.2.6 Work planes

    ID: ARC-WP-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §3.6 · web: Edit with the Workplane Viewer; Zoom to Fit Workplane Viewer

    Purpose. Every view has an active work plane, which is used for sketching, placing work-plane-based families, model lines and text, and for in-plane Rotate and Mirror in 3D.

    Workflow. 1. The user opens Work Plane › Set. The Work Plane dialog shows the current plane (with Show and Dissociate) and offers four ways to specify a new one: - Name: choose a level, grid or named reference plane; - Pick a plane: any planar dimensionable face, including faces in linked models; - Pick a line: use the plane the line was sketched on; - Pick a new host: available only when a work-plane-based element is selected; the user then chooses Vertical Face, Face or Work Plane. 2. If the chosen plane is perpendicular to the current view, a Go To View dialog lists suitable views and opens the one the user chooses.

    UI. - Show toggles a translucent plane with a grid, whose spacing is the work plane's Work Plane Grid Spacing property. - Viewer opens the Work Plane Viewer (below), a temporary view looking straight at the active plane. - Set › Pick a Plane is available as a direct shortcut.

    Work Plane Viewer. Architecture › Work Plane › Viewer, also on the Work Plane panel of the Modify | <Element> tab for work-plane-based elements and sketch-based forms (sweeps, swept blends, in-place and mass forms). - Which plane. With a work-plane-based element or a profile selected, the viewer looks at that element's plane. Otherwise it looks at the active work plane of the view it was started from (the last active view). If that view has no work plane (an elevation or section where none has been set), Reviera asks for one first, as for any work-plane tool. - What it is. An orthographic view whose view direction is the plane's normal and whose up direction is the plane's Y axis (or world +Z projected onto the plane when the plane is horizontal). It opens in a new tab or floating window, zoomed to the extents of the model; ordinary zoom and pan then apply. It has no crop and no far clip, and uses the Medium detail level and the source view's visual style. - Temporary. It is not listed in the Project Browser, cannot be placed on a sheet, renamed or saved, and is discarded when closed or when the project closes. Only one viewer exists per project window; starting it again re-aims the existing one. - Editing. All modify and sketch tools work in it. Edits are ordinary transactions, so they appear in every other view at once and undo as usual. Its work plane is the plane it looks at. - Data. Nothing is written to IFC or RXD; the viewer is session state only.

    Behaviour & rules. - The default work plane of a plan view is its associated level. Elevations and sections have no default and must be set before a work-plane tool can run; if none is set, Reviera asks the user for one. - A work-plane-based element stores its host plane. Moving the host moves the element. The element exposes the Work Plane instance parameter, Edit Work Plane and Pick New. - Dissociate fixes the element in place: it keeps its current world position and loses the host.

    Regeneration. datum edge from the hosting plane (level, grid, reference plane or face) to every work-plane-based element.

    Data (IFC mapping). View work planes are view data (DOC chapter). Each element's work-plane host (GlobalId plus face key, origin, X direction and normal) is stored in RXD element data (placement). The element's placement is written as an IfcLocalPlacement relative to the host's placement when the host is a product, or to the storey otherwise.

    Commands. - workplane.set(view_id, by: Name(datum_id) | Face(host_ref) | Line(element_id) | Plane(origin, normal, xdir)) -> plane - workplane.show(view_id, on) - workplane.viewer(view_id? (default: the active view)) -> view_id opens or re-aims the Work Plane Viewer and returns its transient view ID, which is valid only for the session - element.set_work_plane(element_ids, plane | host_ref) - element.dissociate_work_plane(element_ids)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Model text placed on a named reference plane moves with the plane when the plane is moved. - [ ] Choosing a vertical plane in a plan view offers Go To View with at least one section or elevation. - [ ] With a sweep's profile plane selected, Viewer opens a view normal to that plane, zoomed to the model extents. Editing the profile there updates the open 3D view without a refresh, and closing the viewer leaves no new entry in the Project Browser.

    3.3 Walls

    3.3.1 Wall kinds and function

    ID: ARC-WALL-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §4.1

    Purpose. Define which kinds of wall Reviera supports and how each one is classified.

    Kind Description Priority Spec
    Basic wall A single compound assembly of layers, optionally with vertical regions P0 §3.3.2–§3.3.15
    Stacked wall Basic sub-walls stacked vertically in one element P1 ARC-STKW-001
    Curtain wall A grid, panel and mullion system P1 §3.5
    In-place wall A free-form in-place family in the Walls category P1 ARC-INPL-001
    Wall by face A basic wall generated from a mass or generic-model face P2 ARC-MASS-003

    Behaviour & rules. - The type parameter Function takes one of Interior, Exterior, Foundation, Retaining, Soffit or Core-Shaft. Filters, schedules and analysis export use it, and it sets the IFC classification shown below. - Architecture › Build › Wall offers: Wall: Architectural (WA), Wall: Structural (the same tool with Structural = true; STR chapter), Wall by Face, Wall: Sweep and Wall: Reveal.

    Data (IFC mapping). Each wall is an IfcWall with an IfcWallType. The IFC4 exporter can write IfcWallStandardCase for a wall that is vertical, has a line or arc axis, has constant thickness, uses IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage and has an unedited profile. The default is plain IfcWall, which is valid in both IFC4 and 4X3.

    Function PredefinedType (IFC4) (4X3) Pset_WallCommon.IsExternal
    Interior STANDARD (PARTITIONING when Structural = false and the type is flagged as partition) same FALSE
    Exterior STANDARD same TRUE
    Foundation USERDEFINED, ObjectType FOUNDATIONWALL same TRUE
    Retaining SOLIDWALL RETAININGWALL TRUE
    Soffit USERDEFINED, ObjectType SOFFIT same FALSE
    Core-Shaft SHEAR if structural, otherwise STANDARD same FALSE
    Stacked (parent) ELEMENTEDWALL same from sub-walls

    Pset_WallCommon.LoadBearing is set from Structural, and Pset_WallCommon.ExtendToStructure from whether the wall's top is attached.

    Commands. See ARC-WALL-002 and later blocks.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A Retaining-function wall exports with SOLIDWALL in IFC4 and RETAININGWALL in IFC4X3.

    3.3.2 Placing walls

    ID: ARC-WALL-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §4.2 · screenshots/architecture/walls_by_room_by_segment.png

    Purpose. Create walls from drawn or picked curves.

    Workflow. 1. The user starts Architecture › Build › Wall › Wall: Architectural (WA) in a plan or 3D view. Slanted and tapered types can also be drawn in elevation and section views. 2. The user chooses a type and, optionally, edits the New Walls instance properties (Base Constraint, Location Line, Room Bounding and so on). 3. The user sets the contextual-tab options listed in the table below. 4. The user draws with Line, Rectangle, Inscribed or Circumscribed Polygon, Circle, the arc tools, Ellipse, Partial Ellipse, Pick Lines (model lines, reference planes and element edges; Tab picks a chain) or Pick Faces (vertical mass or generic-model faces; Tab picks all of them). 5. Spacebar flips the exterior side while drawing. With no flip, the exterior is on the left of the drawing direction, so a wall drawn from left to right has its exterior face on the upper side in plan. 6. The user finishes with Esc or Modify.

    UI. Options on the contextual tab:

    Control Values
    Level Base level. Shown only in 3D views; non-story levels are allowed
    Height / Depth Height draws upward from the base. Depth draws downward, and the top is then the base level
    Top constraint A level, or Unconnected plus a value
    Location Line Wall Centerline (default), Core Centerline, Finish Face: Exterior, Finish Face: Interior, Core Face: Exterior, Core Face: Interior
    Chain On or off
    Offset Distance of the location line from the input curve. Not available for ellipses
    Radius Automatic fillet between chained segments
    Join Status Allow (default) or Disallow. Kept for the session
    Auto Join / Auto Join & Lock Placement-panel toggles (ARC-WALL-015)
    Place By Segment / Place By Room Placement-panel modes (ARC-WALL-014)
    Hosted Wall Constraint-panel toggle, used with By Segment and By Room (ARC-WALL-016)
    Room Bounding Pre-set in New Walls properties

    Behaviour & rules. - Each drawn segment becomes one wall. In a chain, consecutive walls are joined end to end (ARC-JOIN-001). A Radius value inserts an arc wall between each pair of segments. - Ellipse and partial-ellipse walls require Location Line = Wall Centerline and ignore Spacebar. - A wall shorter than TOL_SHORT, or shorter than its own width when Join Status is Allow, is rejected with "Wall is too short". - Pick Faces creates walls whose location line lies on the face, according to the Location Line option, and records Related to Mass (ARC-MASS-003). - Location line persistence. - The location line stays in place through type changes. - Changing the Location Line parameter of a placed wall leaves its geometry where it is. Reviera recomputes the stored location-curve offset so that the body does not move. - Flipping mirrors the wall about its current location line. - The blue end dots are drawn on the location line.

    Regeneration. Edges into the wall: datum from the base and top levels; join from its join nodes; type from the wall type; attach from attach targets; host from the host wall (hosted walls). Edges out of the wall: host to its inserts; bound to rooms on the levels the wall spans; cut to embedded curtain-wall hosts.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Placement and axis. ObjectPlacement puts the local X axis along the start tangent, with the origin at the start point of the wall centreline at the base elevation. The Axis representation is the location centreline as an IfcPolyline (straight walls) or IfcTrimmedCurve on an IfcCircle / IfcEllipse. - Body. The Body representation follows §3.0.4. - Layer usage. IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage with LayerSetDirection = AXIS2. The exterior is at local +Y. Layers are listed from exterior to interior, so an unflipped wall has DirectionSense = NEGATIVE and OffsetFromReferenceLine = +d_ext, where d_ext is the distance from the centreline to the exterior finish face. A flipped wall has DirectionSense = POSITIVE and OffsetFromReferenceLine = -d_ext. ReferenceExtent is the unconnected height. - Parameter values. Base and top constraints are stored as storey GlobalIds and offsets; Room Bounding, Cross-Section, Angle and the others are IFC properties (DM property sets). - RXD. Element data (recipe.wall) holds the location-line choice, flip state and per-end join status. RXD document model/constraints holds the join-node overrides.

    Commands. - wall.create(type_id, curve, base_level, top_constraint: Level(id) | Unconnected(height), base_offset?, top_offset?, location_line?, flip?: bool, structural?: bool, structural_usage?, room_bounding?: bool, join_status?: Allow|Disallow, auto_join?: Off|Join|JoinAndLock) -> element_id - wall.create_chain(type_id, curves: [curve], closed?: bool, fillet_radius?, ...same as wall.create) -> [element_id] - wall.create_from_faces(type_id, face_refs, base_level, location_line, ...) -> [element_id] - wall.set_location(wall_id, curve) - wall.set_location_line(wall_ids, location_line) - wall.flip(wall_ids)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A rectangle drawn clockwise in plan produces four walls whose exterior faces all point outward, and a counter-clockwise rectangle puts the exterior faces inward (exterior on the left). - [ ] Changing a placed wall's Location Line from Centerline to Finish Face: Exterior does not move any face. A flip after that change mirrors the wall about the exterior face. - [ ] A 250 mm wall, unflipped, with its centreline as the location line, exports OffsetFromReferenceLine = 0.125 and DirectionSense = NEGATIVE, and an independent IFC viewer shows the layers on the correct sides.

    3.3.3 Wall instance parameters

    ID: ARC-WALL-003 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §4.3

    Group Parameters Notes
    Constraints Location Line; Location Line Offset (only when the wall is used as a curtain panel); Base Constraint; Base Offset; Base Is Attached (RO); Base Extension Distance; Top Constraint; Unconnected Height; Top Offset; Top Is Attached (RO); Top Extension Distance; Room Bounding; Related to Mass (RO); Hosted (RO); Offset from Host The extension distances are enabled only when the type has extendable layers (ARC-CMPD-004). The host fields apply to hosted walls only
    Cross-Section Cross-Section = Vertical, Slanted or Tapered; Angle From Vertical (Slanted, −90° to +90°); Enable Angle Overrides; Exterior Angle; Interior Angle (Tapered) ARC-WALL-005
    Structural Structural; Enable Analytical Model; Structural Usage STR chapter
    Dimensions Length, Area, Volume (RO) Exported as Qto_WallBaseQuantities (Length, Width, Height, GrossSideArea, NetSideArea, GrossVolume, NetVolume)
    Identity Image, Comments, Mark Name = Mark if one is set, Description = Comments
    Phasing Phase Created, Phase Demolished DM chapter

    Behaviour & rules. - Height computation. z_base = elev(BaseConstraint) + BaseOffset. z_top = elev(TopConstraint) + TopOffset, or z_base + UnconnectedHeight when the wall is unconnected. The result must satisfy z_top − z_base > TOL_SHORT; otherwise Reviera reports the error "Wall top below base" and leaves the wall unregenerated (its last valid body is kept and the wall is flagged). - Length is measured along the location centreline after joins are resolved, as the reference product does at the wall's computation length. - Area is measured on the exterior face (finish exterior), net of openings.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With Top Constraint = Level 2 (elevation 3.0) and Top Offset = −0.2, the wall height equals 2.8 m minus the base offset.

    3.3.4 Wall type parameters

    ID: ARC-WALL-004 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §4.4

    Behaviour & rules. Type parameters: - Structure (opens Edit Assembly); - Wrapping at Inserts (Do not wrap, Exterior, Interior or Both); - Wrapping at Ends (None, Exterior or Interior); - Width (RO, the sum of the layer thicknesses); - Function; - Default Exterior Angle and Default Interior Angle (tapered walls); - Width Measured At (Top or Base, tapered walls); - Coarse Scale Fill Pattern and Coarse Scale Fill Colour; - identity data (Keynote, Model, Manufacturer, Type Comments, URL, Description, Assembly Code, Type Mark, Fire Rating, Cost); - analytical properties (Heat Transfer Coefficient U, Thermal Resistance R, Thermal Mass, Absorptance, Roughness).

    R and U are computed from the layer materials' thermal assets: R = Rsi + Σ tᵢ/λᵢ + Rse, using the surface resistances set in the project's energy settings (ANA chapter).

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcWallType (PredefinedType as in ARC-WALL-001). - Pset_WallCommon on the type: FireRating, ThermalTransmittance (U), IsExternal, AcousticRating where it is set. - Pset_ConcreteElementGeneral and similar sets where the material calls for them. - Identity data uses Pset_ManufacturerTypeInformation and the classification references for the assembly code (IfcClassificationReference through IfcRelAssociatesClassification). - The wrapping settings are stored in RXD type data (recipe.compound).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A type with a 100 mm brick layer (λ 0.77), a 50 mm insulation layer (λ 0.035) and a 100 mm block layer (λ 0.5), with Rsi 0.13 and Rse 0.04, reports R ≈ 1.93 m²K/W.

    3.3.5 Compound structure model (shared)

    ID: ARC-CMPD-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §1 (2026 changes), §4.5, §17.3 · screenshots/architecture/wall_edit_assembly_layers_2026.png

    Purpose. One layered-structure data model shared by walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, building pads (on import) and toposolids.

    Behaviour & rules. - A compound structure is an ordered list of layers. Walls are listed from exterior to interior. Floors, roofs, ceilings and toposolids are listed from top to bottom. - Each layer has these fields: - function ∈ {Structure, Substrate, Thermal/Air, Finish 1, Finish 2, Membrane}; - priority (an integer 1–9, where 1 is the highest; independent of function); - material; - thickness; - wraps (bool); - structural_material (bool; at most one layer, and that layer must be in the core); - variable (bool; at most one layer). - Default priorities apply when a layer is created: Structure 1, Substrate 2, Thermal/Air 3, Finish 1 4, Finish 2 5, Membrane 0. Membrane means zero thickness and no part in priority cleanup. The user may change any non-membrane priority. - Core. Two boundary markers, core_start and core_end, are layer indices with 0 ≤ core_start ≤ core_end ≤ n. The core is the layer range [core_start, core_end) and may be empty (core_start = core_end). When the core becomes empty, every dimension and constraint that referenced a core face is deleted, after a warning that lists them. - Validation: - Every non-membrane layer must be at least 1/8" thick (3.2 mm). - Membrane layers must have thickness 0. - Core layers must have thickness greater than 0. - Priorities must not ascend from the core outward: on each side of the core, walking from the core boundary toward the face, each layer's priority number must be greater than or equal to the previous one (lower or equal priority). Membranes are exempt. - At most one layer may be variable. A variable layer is required for tapered walls and allowed for shape-edited slabs. - A type with a variable layer cannot use vertical-structure editing (ARC-CMPD-003). - The Default Wrapping settings (At Inserts and At Ends) are type parameters that the Edit Assembly dialog edits.

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcMaterialLayerSet is associated with the type. Each layer is an IfcMaterialLayer with: - Material; - LayerThickness; - IsVentilated (TRUE for an Air layer, FALSE otherwise, UNKNOWN for a membrane); - Name = the function name; - Category = LoadBearing (Structure), Insulation (Thermal), Finish (Finish 1/2), Membrane or Substrate; - Priority = 100 − 10·(p−1), clamped to 0–100, with membranes written as 0. IFC's priority runs the other way (higher means stronger), so Reviera reverses the scale on export. - The occurrence carries IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage. - RXD type data (recipe.compound): the exact Reviera priority, wraps, variable and structural flags per layer (keyed by a named layer sub-reference, not by index), core_start and core_end, the vertical regions, the type-level sweeps and reveals, and the default wrapping. - Import without RXD. When a type has no RXD data (for example, it was created by another tool), Reviera infers the core as the contiguous LoadBearing layers and the priorities from Category.

    Commands. - compound.set_layers(type_id, layers: [{function, priority?, material_id, thickness, wraps?, structural_material?, variable?}], core_start, core_end) - compound.insert_layer(type_id, index, layer) - compound.delete_layer(type_id, index) - compound.move_layer(type_id, index, delta) - compound.duplicate_layer(type_id, index) - compound.set_default_wrapping(type_id, at_inserts, at_ends)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A type whose layers are all outside the core (empty core) saves, regenerates and round-trips through IFC and RXD. - [ ] Setting a Finish layer to priority 1 while it lies between a priority-3 layer and the core fails validation with a message naming both layers. - [ ] Reading an IFC with Priority 100/90/80 and no RXD data yields Reviera priorities 1/2/3.

    3.3.6 Edit Assembly dialog

    ID: ARC-CMPD-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §4.5 · screenshots/architecture/wall_edit_assembly_layers_2026.png

    Purpose. The UI for editing a compound structure.

    UI. - Header: Family, Type, Total thickness, Resistance R, Thermal Mass and Sample Height (the height of the wall preview). - Layers grid, with exterior (or top) at the top: Function, Priority, Material (opens the Material Browser), Thickness, Wraps, Structural Material and Variable. Two locked rows mark the core boundaries ("Core Boundary — above" and "Core Boundary — below"), and the user can move them with Up and Down. - Buttons: Insert, Delete, Duplicate, Up and Down. - Default Wrapping drop-downs (walls only). - Modify Vertical Structure (walls only, enabled when the preview is set to Section): Modify, Merge Regions, Assign Layers, Split Region, Sweeps… and Reveals…. - Preview pane with a View choice of Floor Plan or Section, which renders the real join-free geometry of a sample wall.

    Behaviour & rules. The dialog edits a copy of the type. OK commits one transaction that updates the type and regenerates every instance. Cancel discards the copy. Validation (ARC-CMPD-001) runs on OK, and its errors are shown inline next to the offending row.

    Commands. The compound.* commands, applied as a batch.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing a layer's material and pressing OK updates all instances. Cancel leaves them untouched.

    3.3.7 Vertically compound walls (regions)

    ID: ARC-CMPD-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §4.5

    Purpose. Wall types whose material changes with height, for example a brick plinth below render.

    Behaviour & rules. - Region model. The wall cross-section in the type's sample plane (the thickness direction against height) is divided into rectangular regions. Each region is assigned to one layer row, which defines its function, priority and material. Region boundaries are horizontal or vertical segments. A horizontal boundary carries a distance from the base or from the top of the wall, and a padlock marks which of the two it is. - Split Region. Hovering a vertical layer border previews a horizontal split at the cursor height, and hovering a horizontal border previews a vertical split. A click commits the split, and both new regions keep the material they had. - Merge Regions. The user clicks a border, and an arrow shows which region absorbs the other. - Assign Layers. The user selects a row and then clicks regions to assign that row to them. - Modify. Selecting an outer vertical boundary shows a temporary dimension that sets the thickness. Selecting the top or bottom edge of a layer shows a padlock: an unlocked layer is extendable (ARC-CMPD-004). - Rules: - Rows must be contiguous from left to right. - A row cannot appear on both sides of the core. - Core boundaries and membranes cannot step. - Only layers that run the full height can have a thickness. - Moving one exterior edge moves every exterior edge. - Instance geometry. At height z within the wall, each region resolves to an absolute interval [z0, z1]. The base or top distance is measured from the instance's base or top. If the wall is shorter than the type's fixed regions, regions are clipped from the end opposite their anchor. The variable region (the one with no fixed distance) absorbs the remaining height.

    Data (IFC mapping). IFC4 has no region concept. The type's IfcMaterialLayerSet describes the full-height layers. Regions are stored in RXD type data (recipe.compound). The exported Body is the true geometry, and with the export option Parts per layer/region (P2) each region is also exported as an IfcBuildingElementPart aggregated under the wall, carrying its own IfcMaterial.

    Commands. - compound.split_region(type_id, region_key, orientation: Horizontal|Vertical, position) - compound.merge_regions(type_id, region_a, region_b, keep: A|B) - compound.assign_layer(type_id, region_keys, layer_index) - compound.set_region_anchor(type_id, boundary_key, from: Base|Top, distance)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A type with a 600 mm brick region anchored to the base shows the brick from 0 to 600 mm on a 3 m wall and on a 1 m wall alike. On a 0.5 m wall the brick region is clipped at 0.5 m.

    3.3.8 Extendable layers

    ID: ARC-CMPD-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §4.3, §4.5

    Purpose. Let some layers of a wall run past the wall's base or top, for example a brick skin that drops below the slab edge or a parapet finish that rises above the roof line.

    Workflow. 1. In Edit Assembly (ARC-CMPD-002) with the preview set to Section, the user clicks Modify, selects the top or bottom edge of a layer and clicks its padlock to unlock it. The type now marks that layer edge as extendable. 2. In the project, the user sets Top Extension Distance or Base Extension Distance on wall instances, or selects a wall in a section, elevation or 3D view, presses Tab until the extendable edge's shape handle is highlighted, and drags it.

    Behaviour & rules. - Layers whose top (or bottom) edge is unlocked in the type are extendable, and unlocked layers must be adjacent to each other. - Type rules. Top and bottom are unlocked independently. The unlocked set at each end is one contiguous run of layers; unlocking a layer that would split the run is refused with "Extendable layers must be adjacent". Membranes follow their neighbours and cannot be unlocked on their own. A layer inside a vertical region (ARC-CMPD-003) can be unlocked only when the region touches that end of the wall. - The instance parameters Top Extension Distance and Base Extension Distance move the extendable layers' top or bottom edges by that amount, which can be positive or negative. In section, elevation and 3D views, Tab exposes shape handles for the same edges. - Limits. A negative extension may not shorten the extendable layers to less than TOL_SHORT in height ("Layer extension exceeds wall height"). There is no upper limit for positive values. When the type has no extendable layer at an end, that end's parameter is read-only and 0. - Geometry. Each extendable layer's solid is built from the wall's layer solid with its top or base face moved along the wall's vertical direction (along the slant direction for slanted walls, ARC-WALL-010). The move happens after joins and before insert voids, so doors and windows still cut the extended layers. At a corner, two joined walls with equal extensions on the same layer functions produce a clean extended corner; unequal extensions leave a step. - Rooms and joins. Extended parts take part in layer cleanup with joined walls of the same function and priority (ARC-JOIN-001). They do not change the wall's room-bounding trace, because rooms are computed at the computation height (ARC-ROOM-002). - Extension is disabled while the wall's top or base is attached (ARC-WALL-008). Its parameters become read-only and are ignored.

    Data (IFC mapping). The extended geometry is part of the wall's Body. IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage cannot express per-layer heights, so the extension values are written as property values and stored in RXD element data (recipe.wall); the unlocked edges are flags per layer in RXD type data (recipe.compound).

    Commands. - compound.set_extendable(type_id, index, top?: bool, base?: bool) sets or clears the padlock state of a layer edge in the type. - wall.set_extension(wall_ids, top?: f64, base?: f64).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With an extendable brick layer and Base Extension Distance = −300 mm, the brick stops 300 mm below the wall base, while the other layers stay at the base. - [ ] Unlocking the bottom edges of layers 1 and 3 but not layer 2 is refused with a message naming the layers. - [ ] A window placed in a wall whose brick layer extends 500 mm above the top still cuts the brick, and attaching the wall top to a roof makes Top Extension Distance read-only.

    3.3.9 Layer wrapping

    ID: ARC-WRAP-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §4.4, §4.5 (Wrapping), §5.5

    Purpose. Finish layers turn into the jambs of openings and around the free ends of walls.

    Behaviour & rules. - Conditions. A layer wraps when all of these hold: its Wraps flag is set; the type's wrapping setting for that side is on; the wall is not tapered; and the host is a wall (floors and roofs never wrap). - For inserts, wrapping is controlled by Wrapping at Inserts (Exterior, Interior, Both or Do not wrap). The insert family's Wall Closure type parameter, if set, overrides it. - For ends, wrapping is controlled by Wrapping at Ends (Exterior, Interior or None). Each end of each wall can override it ("By type", "Exterior", "Interior" or "None"), and that override is stored in the wall's RXD element data (recipe.wall). - Insert-wrapping algorithm. It runs per insert, in the wall's local frame: u along the wall, v through the thickness from the exterior face (v = 0) inward, and z up. 1. Let R be the rough-opening profile of the insert projected onto the wall's elevation plane (u, z), taken from the family's opening-cut geometry. 2. Let c be the closure depth: the v coordinate of the family's Wall Closure reference plane. If the family has none, c is the core's exterior face. 3. For the exterior side, let W = [w₁ … w_k] be the wrapping layers between v = 0 and the core, ordered from the face inward, with thicknesses t₁ … t_k, and let T_j = Σ_{i≤j} tᵢ. 4. Lay out the jamb lining. Wrapping layer w_j occupies the ring Offset(R, T_j) \ Offset(R, T_{j−1}) (a 2D outward offset of the profile) over the depth v ∈ [v_start(w_j), c], where v_start is the layer's own starting depth. The outermost face layer therefore lines the jamb surface directly. 5. Every non-wrapping layer, and every layer deeper than the wrapping layers on that side, loses the volume Offset(R, T_k) × [0, c] (the "wrap pocket"). 6. The insert's void R × [0, wall width] is then cut from all layers. 7. The interior side is handled the same way from v = width with depths mirrored. Both applies the two sides independently, each up to its own closure depth: the exterior up to c, and the interior up to c_int (a second closure plane in the family, or the interior core face). 8. Curved walls. The 2D operations in steps 4 and 5 are done in the developed (u, z) space of the location curve at each layer's offset radius and then mapped back onto the cylinder. OCCT builds the ring solids with BRepOffsetAPI_MakeOffset (planar wire offset, GeomAbs_Intersection joins) followed by BRepPrimAPI_MakePrism for straight walls. For curved walls the developed faces are mapped through BRepBuilderAPI_GTransform approximations and the solid is built with BRepOffsetAPI_ThruSections. - End-wrapping algorithm. At a wall end that is not joined to anything: - Exterior: the wrapping exterior layers continue around the end face. Each wrapping layer w_j forms an L: its band along the wall, plus a cap across the end at distance T_{j−1} … T_j beyond the core's end face. The cap runs from the exterior face to the interior face of the core. Interior-side layers stop flush with the outer face of the cap. - Interior: the same, mirrored. - The core end face is the reference. Non-wrapping layers on the wrapping side are shortened by T_k so that the caps fit within the original end position. - Wrapping is recomputed when the insert moves, when the insert family's closure changes, or when the layers change.

    Regeneration. Edges host (insert → wall) and type (wall type → wall). The wrap pocket is part of the wall body, so the wall regenerates whenever any insert in it changes.

    Data (IFC mapping). The result is part of the wall Body. The insert's IfcOpeningElement stays the rough opening (R extruded through the full width). Wrapped layers are only visible in the body and in layer-wise parts (when exported).

    Commands. wall.set_end_wrap(wall_id, end: Start|End, mode: ByType|Exterior|Interior|None), plus the type commands in ARC-CMPD-001 and ARC-WALL-004.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 12.5 mm plasterboard layer with Wraps on, and Wrapping at Inserts = Interior, lines all four sides of a window opening up to the window's closure plane. In a plan cut the board turns into the jamb. - [ ] A free wall end with Wrapping at Ends = Exterior shows the exterior render wrapping around the end and stopping at the interior face of the core. - [ ] A tapered wall ignores all wrapping settings without error.

    3.3.10 Slanted and tapered walls

    ID: ARC-WALL-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §4.3, §4.5 · screenshots/architecture/tapered_walls_section.png

    Purpose. Walls whose faces are not vertical.

    Behaviour & rules. - Slanted walls (Cross-Section = Slanted). - Angle From Vertical α ∈ (−90°, +90°). A positive angle tilts the wall top toward the right of the drawing direction, which is the interior side when the wall is unflipped. - The cross-section is a parallelogram: at height h above the base, every layer is offset by h·tan α along the wall normal. - In-canvas dot controls at the top let the user set the angle or the top offset, snapping to 1° increments. - Inserts and sweeps stay vertical unless their Orientation instance parameter is set to Vertical, Perpendicular to Face or Parallel to Ground. - Only butt joins are allowed (no miter or square-off), and reveals are not allowed. - Split with Gap along a vertical plane is not allowed. - Attach targets must cover the wall's complete footprint in plan. - Tapered walls (Cross-Section = Tapered). The type needs a variable layer. - Exterior Angle αₑ and Interior Angle αᵢ default from the type, and an instance can override them with Enable Angle Overrides. A positive angle tilts the top of that face inward. - The type's thickness is measured at the base or at the top, as Width Measured At says. - The variable layer absorbs the difference, so its thickness at height h is t_v(h) = t_v0 − h·(tan αₑ + tan αᵢ) when measured at the base. - If t_v(h) ≤ 0 anywhere within the wall height, Reviera reports "Variable layer thickness would reach zero" and does not commit the change. - Layers on the exterior side of the variable layer stay parallel to the exterior face, and layers on the interior side stay parallel to the interior face. - Geometry. Each layer is the region between two ruled surfaces. Straight walls are built as a prism of the layer's 2D cross-section polygon, in the plane normal to the wall axis, along the wall length (BRepPrimAPI_MakePrism). Curved walls are built as a sweep of the cross-section along the location curve (BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipeShell with a fixed binormal of +Z, which keeps the faces conical).

    Data (IFC mapping). The body is an IfcExtrudedAreaSolid of the parallelogram or trapezoid profile along the wall axis for straight walls, and an IfcSurfaceCurveSweptAreaSolid or Brep for curved walls. IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage still applies, and for tapered walls IFC4 has IfcMaterialLayerWithOffsets (OffsetDirection AXIS3, with the offset values at the top). Reviera writes it for tapered walls.

    Commands. wall.set_cross_section(wall_ids, mode: Vertical|Slanted|Tapered, angle?: f64, exterior_angle?: f64, interior_angle?: f64, override_angles?: bool).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 3 m slanted wall at +10° has its top face displaced by 0.529 m toward the interior. - [ ] A tapered type with a 200 mm variable layer, measured at the base, with 1° on each face, built 3 m high, has a variable layer 0.0953 m thick at the top. With 2° on each face the variable layer would reach −0.0095 m within the height, and the change is rejected.

    3.3.11 Stacked walls

    ID: ARC-STKW-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §4.6

    Purpose. One element that stacks several basic wall types vertically.

    Behaviour & rules. - Type structure: - Offset reference, one of Wall Centerline, Core Centerline, Finish Face (Ext/Int) or Core Face (Ext/Int). It becomes each sub-wall's location line. - Sample Height. - Rows from top to bottom. Each row has a basic wall type, a Height (exactly one row is Variable), an Offset from the reference (positive toward the exterior), Top and Base extensions (when the sub-type's layers are extendable) and a Flip flag. - Buttons: Insert, Delete, Up, Down and Variable. - Instance layout. For wall height H, each fixed row takes its own height, and the variable row takes H − Σ fixed. If that would be ≤ 0, Reviera reports "Stacked wall too short for its fixed rows". - Sub-walls are real child elements. They are selectable with Tab and expose a subset of instance parameters (Room Bounding, Structural, phasing, Mark). - Joins: each sub-wall joins with whatever is at its own height, using the join algorithm (§3.3.12) once per height interval. - Ellipse stacked walls need Offset = Wall Centerline and every row's offset set to 0. - A stacked wall can be split only by a vertical plane. - Break Up turns the stacked wall into independent basic walls and keeps their positions and joins.

    Data (IFC mapping). The parent is an IfcWall (ELEMENTEDWALL) with an IfcWallType (ELEMENTEDWALL), and it aggregates (IfcRelAggregates) one IfcWall per sub-wall, each with its own type and layer set usage. The parent has no Body of its own. The row table is stored in RXD type data (recipe.stacked_wall).

    Commands. - stackedwall.set_rows(type_id, offset_reference, rows: [{wall_type_id, height | Variable, offset, flip, top_ext?, base_ext?}]) - wall.break_up(stacked_wall_ids) -> [element_id]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A stacked wall with a 900 mm fixed base row and a variable upper row, drawn 2.7 m high, has sub-walls 0.9 m and 1.8 m high. - [ ] Break Up produces two basic walls whose IFC GlobalIds are those of the former sub-walls.

    3.3.12 Wall joins and layer cleanup

    ID: ARC-JOIN-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §1 (2025/2026), §4.5 (Layer join rules), §4.7, §17.4 · screenshots/architecture/compound_layer_priority_joins.png

    Purpose. Walls that meet are connected cleanly, and their layers are resolved by priority.

    Workflow. - Walls join automatically when they are drawn or moved so that an end comes within TOL_JOIN of another wall. They do not join if the end's Join Status is Disallow. - Wall Joins (Modify › Geometry): the user clicks inside the grey square that marks a join, or draws a window around several joins, and then chooses: - Butt (default), Miter or Square off; - Previous / Next, which cycles the join order (single join only); - Display: Use View Setting, Clean Join or Don't Clean Join; - Allow Join / Disallow Join. - In-canvas glyph. At each selected wall end, in plan and 3D, a glyph toggles Allow/Disallow. A disallowed end stops square at its own location point.

    Behaviour & rules.

    A. Join detection. Detection runs per join node. 1. For each wall end E (point P_E on the location curve, tangent d_E pointing out of the wall) whose status is Allow, Reviera queries an R-tree of wall footprints at P_E with radius TOL_JOIN. 2. End-to-end candidates. Another wall end F with |P_E − P_F| ≤ TOL_JOIN, or whose extended location lines cross within max(w_E, w_F) of both endpoints, forms an L/corner node. A third or fourth end joins the same node when it lies within TOL_JOIN of the node point. 3. End-to-span candidates. If P_E, extended along d_E by at most w_other/2 + TOL_JOIN, lands inside another wall's footprint away from that wall's ends, the result is a T node (E abuts the continuous wall). 4. Two walls whose spans cross with neither end involved get no automatic join. The user can create one with Join Geometry. 5. Conditions for a node: - The walls' vertical extents overlap. - The walls are on the same level band, with their base levels within the overlap. - The angle between the location lines is above 1°. Parallel overlapping walls only join through Join Geometry. - The number of ends in an L node is at most 4. With more, Reviera reports "Too many walls at one join" and leaves the extras unjoined. 6. The node's join order is a list of the wall ends in it. By default the first wall drawn comes first. Previous and Next rotate the list. 7. Mid-end faces. Vertical faces created by an edited profile or by a wall opening (ARC-WALL-009, ARC-OPEN-003) are join targets just like wall ends. A wall end that abuts a notch face forms a T node against that face.

    B. Layer bands. For each wall W at height interval I (see C), Reviera builds the plan bands: - Each layer j occupies the strip between two offset curves of the location centreline, at signed distances a_j and b_j. Positive distances are toward the exterior, and the values follow from the layer thicknesses and the flip. - Every band carries (wall, layer index, priority p, in_core flag, material). - Membrane layers have zero width. They take no part in the cleanup and are re-inserted afterward as zero-thickness boundaries. - Arc walls produce concentric arcs. Elliptical walls produce offset curves (Geom2d_OffsetCurve), which are approximated by B-splines to within 0.01 mm where an exact type is needed.

    C. Height intervals. The join is solved separately in each vertical interval in which the set of participating bands is constant. 1. Collect breakpoints: the base and top of each wall in the node (after attachment, sampled at the node location), every region boundary (ARC-CMPD-003) and every extension boundary (ARC-CMPD-004). 2. Sort the breakpoints. Each pair of consecutive breakpoints defines an interval I = [z₀, z₁]. 3. Inside each interval, run step D with the bands present there. A wall whose extent does not cover I is absent from that interval, so the other walls' ends behave as free ends there (and get end wrapping, if it applies).

    D. Priority painting (the cleanup core). This step works on one node and one interval. 1. Extend. Each joining wall end is extended along its own direction until its bands reach the far face of the farthest other wall in the node. Bands are kept as 2D regions. 2. Cells. In the overlap zone, compute the arrangement of all band boundaries. Each cell is the intersection of one band from the arriving wall A with one band from the other wall B. For three or four walls, cells are intersections of bands from every wall that covers that point. 3. Reach rule. Band a of the arriving wall A reaches cell (a, b) when two conditions hold: - every band of B that lies between B's face on A's side and band b (exclusive) has a priority number strictly greater than p_a (that is, a is stronger than each one); and - p_b ≥ p_a.

    Core override: if a is in the core and b is not, a reaches b whatever their priority numbers. If b is in the core and a is not, a never reaches beyond B's core face. 4. Ownership. - If exactly one of a and b reaches the cell, that band owns it. - If both reach the cell, which happens only when p_a = p_b: in an L node the cell is divided by its miter diagonal, the segment from the cell corner where the bands' outer boundaries meet to the corner where their inner boundaries meet. Each half goes to the band on its side. In a T node the continuous wall's band owns the cell, so the arriving band stops at the cell boundary. - If neither reaches the cell, the cell goes to the band of the wall that is first in the join order. This is what the user sees as the join order changing with Next and Previous. 5. Join type adjustments: - Butt. Steps 1–4 as written. - Miter. Allowed only for L nodes of two walls. Step 4 is replaced: every cell is split by the node miter line, which joins the intersection of the two exterior faces to the intersection of the two interior faces. Each wall owns the side that faces its own body. Priorities are ignored. - Square off. Allowed for L nodes. The first wall in the join order is extended to the far face of the second wall and owns every cell. The second wall is trimmed at the first wall's near face. No layer interpenetration takes place. - Slanted walls allow only Butt. A wall abutting the interior face of another (a T node) allows only Butt. 6. Trim. Every part of an extended band that lies beyond the cells it owns is discarded. The final plan region of band a is its original strip, plus the cells it owns, minus the cells owned by other bands. 7. Merge for display. Adjacent regions from different walls are merged into one display region when they have the same material and the view's Wall Join Display allows it. Clean all wall joins merges always. Clean same type wall joins merges only when both walls have the same type. The Display override on the node takes precedence. Merging affects plan cut graphics only and never the solids. 8. Multi-wall nodes (3–4 walls). Walls are processed in join order. The first two form an L or T resolution. Each later wall is then resolved as a T into the combined footprint of the walls already processed, and its bands use the priority and core rules against whichever band of the combined footprint they meet.

    E. 3D realisation. For vertical walls, each band region of each interval is extruded from z₀ to z₁ (BRepPrimAPI_MakePrism). The pieces of one layer are fused (BRepAlgoAPI_Fuse with SetRunParallel(true) and the fuzzy value, followed by ShapeUpgrade_UnifySameDomain to remove the interval seams). Slanted and tapered walls use termination surfaces in place of 2D painting: - The termination of band a is the layer interface surface of wall B at which step D's reach rule stops it. That surface is a ruled plane when B is slanted. - The band's swept solid is split with BRepAlgoAPI_Splitter, using that surface (limited to B's vertical extent) as the tool, and the piece on A's side is kept. - Above or below B's extent, the band ends at its own end plane.

    F. Interaction with other operations. - Attach clipping (ARC-WALL-008) is applied after the join, to each wall's own solid. - Profile edits (ARC-WALL-009) are applied before the join, as a prism mask in the wall's plane. They therefore change the breakpoints in C. - Inserts and wrapping (ARC-WRAP-001) are applied last. - The R-tree, detection and painting results are cached per node. A node is marked dirty when any of its walls changes curve, type, height, flip, location line or join override.

    Regeneration. Each node is a graph node with join edges to and from its walls. When a node is re-solved, every wall in it regenerates, and nodes that share no wall regenerate in parallel (rayon). A wall end that moves can change node membership. In that case detection runs again for the old node and the new node in the same transaction.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Each pairwise connection is an IfcRelConnectsPathElements with RelatingConnectionType and RelatedConnectionType ∈ {ATSTART, ATEND, ATPATH} (L: ATSTART/ATEND pairs; T: ATEND to ATPATH). - RelatingPriorities and RelatedPriorities list the layer indices of each wall that pass through, in IFC layer order, as the IFC definition expects. They are computed from step D for the interval that contains the walls' common base. - The join type, join order and display override of each node are stored in RXD document model/constraints. Allow/disallow per end is owned by the wall and stored in its RXD element data (recipe.wall). - The resolved body is in each wall's Body representation.

    Commands. - wall.join_set_type(node_ref | wall_end_refs, type: Butt|Miter|SquareOff) - wall.join_cycle_order(node_ref, step: +1|-1) - wall.join_set_display(node_ref, display: ViewSetting|Clean|DontClean) - wall.set_join_allowed(wall_id, end: Start|End, allowed: bool) - wall.joins_query(wall_id) -> [JoinNode] (query)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Figure-8 test from the reference behaviour. Wall A is a CMU priority-1 core with insulation (3), an air gap (3) and brick (4). It meets wall B, a stud priority-1 core with finishes. A's CMU passes through B's finish layers and stops at B's core. A's insulation stops at B's air gap. A plan cut matches the ownership diagram in screenshots/architecture/compound_layer_priority_joins.png. - [ ] Two identical walls in an L corner, with Butt, show continuous exterior finish around the corner with one miter-diagonal seam, and no line between same-material cores when Clean all wall joins is set. - [ ] Miter on an L of a 300 mm wall and a 200 mm wall places the seam along the line joining the outer-face intersection and the inner-face intersection. - [ ] Disallowing the join at one end leaves that wall ending square at its location point, with a visible gap. - [ ] A T join of a 100 mm partition into a 300 mm external wall stops the partition's finishes at the external wall's interior finish, and the partition's core at the external wall's core face. - [ ] Walls of different heights: above the shorter wall's top, the taller wall's layers end as a free end. They do not extend into empty space. - [ ] Regenerating 1 000 independent L corners runs on at least four cores at once. Measured by a regeneration benchmark, the speed-up over single-threaded is at least 2.5×.

    3.3.13 Attach Top/Base and Detach

    ID: ARC-WALL-008 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §4.8, §7.1, §7.4

    Purpose. A wall's top or base follows a roof, floor, ceiling, reference plane or another wall.

    Workflow. 1. The user selects one or more walls and chooses Modify Wall › Attach Top/Base. 2. The user chooses Top or Base on the contextual tab. 3. The user picks the target. 4. Detach Top/Base works the same way: the user picks targets to detach, or uses Detach All.

    Behaviour & rules. - Valid targets: floors, roofs (including extrusion roofs), ceilings, non-vertical reference planes, the walls directly above or below, in-place floors and roofs, toposolids (base only), and elements in linked models (attach base only, read-only). - Top attach. Let S be the target's solid. The wall body is clipped by the upward shadow of the target's bottom faces: Tool = Prism(BottomFaces(S) ∩ WallFootprintXY, +Z, ∞) ∪ S, and Wall := Wall − Tool. Reviera uses the underside faces (those whose normal has Z < 0) and extrudes them up to the scene's bounding box (BRepPrimAPI_MakePrism with a finite vector). - Only the part of the wall under the target is affected. Partial overlap therefore attaches only the overlapped part, and the rest keeps its own top constraint. - A reference plane counts as an infinite half-space. - Base attach works the same way with the downward shadow of the target's top faces. - Height before clipping. The wall's nominal top is raised to the maximum height of the target over the wall's footprint, so that the wall can grow up to a high ridge. The Top Is Attached flag then becomes true. The nominal top and the stored constraint are kept for detaching. - Slanted walls. The target must cover the wall's whole plan projection. Otherwise Reviera reports "Attach target does not cover the slanted wall". - Reference planes. Attaching to a second reference plane on the same end replaces the first. - Extendable layers are disabled while the wall is attached. - After a floor or roof is finished, Reviera offers to attach the walls directly below to it (ARC-FLR-001, ARC-ROOF-001).

    Regeneration. An attach edge runs from the target to the wall. A cycle (for example, a roof whose footprint is locked to a wall that is attached to the same roof) is permitted because the footprint lock reads only the wall's plan curve, which does not depend on the attachment. The graph splits the wall node into a plan stage and a body stage so that no real cycle exists (§3.15).

    Data (IFC mapping). An IfcRelConnectsElements with Name = "AttachTop" or "AttachBase" (RelatingElement = target, RelatedElement = wall). The clipped body is written as an IfcBooleanClippingResult when the target is planar (with an IfcHalfSpaceSolid or IfcPolygonalBoundedHalfSpace), and as a Brep otherwise. The attach relation is also stored in RXD document model/constraints, which is authoritative.

    Commands. - wall.attach(wall_ids, end: Top|Base, target_id) - wall.detach(wall_ids, end: Top|Base, target_ids? ) (no targets means Detach All)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Walls attached to a 30° gable roof follow the roof underside, giving a triangular gable-end wall profile. - [ ] A wall half under a floor is clipped only under the floor, and the other half keeps its unconnected height. - [ ] Moving the roof up 500 mm raises the attached wall tops by 500 mm. - [ ] Detaching restores the original top constraint.

    3.3.14 Edit Profile (elevation profile)

    ID: ARC-WALL-009 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §4.9 · screenshots/architecture/wall_profile_mid_end_faces.png

    Purpose. Change a straight wall's elevation outline: gables, notches and holes.

    Workflow. 1. The user selects a straight wall and chooses Mode › Edit Profile. In a plan view Reviera offers Go To View. 2. The wall outline appears as sketch curves, together with dashed reference planes that show the original rectangle: the base, the top and the two ends. 3. The user edits: deletes, splits or adds lines, draws arcs, and adds inner closed loops for holes. 4. Finish applies the profile. Reset Profile restores the rectangle.

    Behaviour & rules. - Sketch curves that snap to a reference plane are locked to it and move when the wall's height or length changes. Unlocking them frees them. - Validation (ARC-SKCH-002) requires exactly one outer loop and any number of hole loops. - Geometry. The profile Π (in the wall's local u–z plane) is turned into a mask solid M = Prism(Π, normal, ±(width/2 + margin)). The wall's layers are intersected with M before the join step, which uses the profile's z range for its breakpoints. - Mid-end faces. Every vertical edge of Π that is not at the wall's two ends produces a vertical face, which is a join target (ARC-JOIN-001 A.7). - Not available for arc or elliptical walls. Those use Wall Opening instead.

    Data (IFC mapping). The body is written as an IfcExtrudedAreaSolid of the plan footprint, intersected (IfcBooleanResult INTERSECTION) with an IfcExtrudedAreaSolid of Π, or as a Brep. The profile sketch is stored in RXD element data (sketch, role profile).

    Commands. wall.edit_profile(wall_id, loops), wall.reset_profile(wall_ids).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A notch 1 m deep and 1 m high in the top corner creates a mid-end face, and a perpendicular wall drawn to that face joins it. - [ ] Raising the wall's top constraint moves the locked top line, and the notch keeps its depth.

    3.3.15 Wall sweeps and reveals

    ID: ARC-WALL-010 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §4.5 (Sweeps/Reveals), §4.10

    Purpose. Additive profiles (cornices, skirting) and subtractive profiles (grooves) along walls.

    Workflow (instance level). 1. The user starts Architecture › Build › Wall › Wall: Sweep or Wall: Reveal in a 3D or elevation view. 2. The user chooses the type and, on the Placement panel, Horizontal or Vertical. 3. Hovering a wall previews the sweep, and a click places it. Reviera pre-selects the same height on adjacent joined walls so that a click continues the run. 4. Restart starts a separate run. Clicking empty space ends the tool. 5. Selected sweeps offer Add/Remove Walls, Modify Returns (Straight or Angled) and end drag handles.

    Behaviour & rules. - Type parameters: Profile (a profile family), Material, Cuts Wall, Cut by Inserts, Default Setback, and Subcategory. - Instance parameters: Wall Offset, Level, Offset from Level, Length. - Type-level sweeps and reveals (Edit Assembly): rows with Profile, Material, Distance, From (Top or Base), Side (Exterior or Interior), Offset, Flip, Setback, Cuts Wall and Cuttable. They run the full wall length and are part of the wall element. - Geometry. The profile (a closed 2D wire from the profile family) is placed in the plane normal to the wall path at the start, with its origin at the wall face plus the offset, at height z = level + offset. It is swept along the face path (the location curve offset to the face) with BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipeShell (fixed binormal +Z for horizontal runs). - Across joined walls, the path is the face chain with miter corners: the shell is built per wall and trimmed by the bisector planes. - Cuts Wall: the sweep's solid is subtracted from the wall layers it overlaps (for example, to recess a cornice). - A reveal is always subtracted, and Cut by Inserts subtracts insert voids from the sweep. - Returns at the ends: Straight caps the end with a planar face. Angled sweeps the profile around a 90° turn into the wall face. - Vertical sweeps run from the wall base to the wall top at a distance along the wall. - Slanted walls. Reveals are not allowed. Sweeps take the Orientation setting (Perpendicular to Face or Parallel to Ground).

    Data (IFC mapping). - Instance sweep: IfcCovering with PredefinedType = MOLDING, linked to the wall through IfcRelCoversBldgElements, and a body of IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid (profile = IfcArbitraryClosedProfileDef, directrix = the face path) or a Brep. - Reveal: IfcOpeningElement with PredefinedType = RECESS, voiding the wall through IfcRelVoidsElement. - Type-level sweeps are part of the wall body, and the row table is stored in RXD type data (recipe.compound).

    Commands. - wallsweep.create(type_id, wall_ids, orientation: Horizontal|Vertical, offset_from_level | distance_along, side?) -> element_id - wallreveal.create(...) (same parameters as wallsweep.create) - wallsweep.add_walls(sweep_id, wall_ids) - wallsweep.remove_walls(sweep_id, wall_ids) - wallsweep.set_returns(sweep_id, end, mode: Straight|Angled) - walltype.set_sweeps(type_id, rows) - walltype.set_reveals(type_id, rows)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A cornice placed on one wall of a closed rectangle extends to all four walls on click, with mitered corners. - [ ] A reveal 20 mm deep cuts every layer it reaches and appears as an IfcOpeningElement (RECESS).

    3.3.16 Split, Split with Gap and horizontal split (walls)

    ID: ARC-WALL-011 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §4.12, §13

    Purpose. Divide one wall into two or more walls.

    Behaviour & rules. - Split Element (SL): a click at a point on the wall divides it there. - The two new walls keep the type, constraints and parameters. The original GlobalId stays with the part that contains the wall's start point, and the other part gets a new GlobalId. - The new ends are joined to each other with a butt join, so they look continuous. - Inserts go to whichever part contains their centre. - With Delete Inner Segment on, the user clicks two points and the middle segment is deleted. - Horizontal split. In elevation or 3D, hovering near a vertical edge previews a horizontal split line, which snaps to levels. The lower wall gets Top Constraint = that level, or an unconnected height. The upper wall gets Base Constraint = that level, or a base offset. Stacked walls cannot be split horizontally. - Split with Gap. The Joint Gap is between 1.6 mm and 305 mm. A click cuts out a gap of that width centred on the click. The two new ends get Disallow Join, and a locked dimension between them records the gap. To close the gap, the user unlocks the dimension, allows the joins and drags the ends together. A slanted wall cannot be split by a vertical plane.

    Commands. - element.split(element_id, point, delete_inner?: point2?) -> [element_id] (shared with ARC-MOD-010) - wall.split_horizontal(wall_id, z | level_id) -> [element_id] - element.split_with_gap(element_id, point, gap) -> [element_id]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Splitting a 10 m wall at 4 m gives walls of 4 m and 6 m. A door at 2 m stays hosted on the first wall, and the IFC export contains the original GlobalId exactly once. - [ ] Split with Gap of 20 mm leaves exactly 20 mm between the faces of the new ends, held by a locked dimension.

    3.3.17 Wall openings

    ID: ARC-WALL-012 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §4.11, §9

    Purpose. A plain rectangular hole through a wall, without a door or window family. The full specification of the opening element is ARC-OPEN-003; this block states what the wall side of the relation does.

    Workflow. 1. In an elevation, section or 3D view, the user chooses Modify | Walls › Modify Wall › Wall Opening (or Architecture › Opening › Wall) and picks a straight or arc wall. 2. The user drags a rectangle on the wall face. Two clicks set opposite corners; temporary dimensions show the distances to the wall ends and to the base level. 3. The opening is created at once. Selecting it shows drag controls on its four edges and temporary dimensions; it can be moved along the wall with Move or by dragging.

    Behaviour & rules. - Valid hosts. Basic walls, straight or arc, vertical or slanted. Stacked walls are cut through every sub-wall the rectangle covers. Curtain walls, elliptical walls and in-place walls are not valid hosts ("Wall Opening cannot be placed in this wall"). - Extent. The rectangle is limited to the wall's elevation outline. Dragging an edge past the wall end or top clips it to the outline, and the opening becomes a notch. - Wall faces. The cut creates mid-end faces: the wall's layer structure is closed on the opening sides like a wall end, so finish layers wrap into it when the type's Wrapping at Inserts applies (ARC-WRAP-001).
