Dimensions and Align can reference those faces. - Following the wall. The opening keeps its position along the wall (as a distance from the wall start) and its base and top constraints. Moving, lengthening or changing the type of the wall keeps the opening; if the wall becomes shorter than the opening's start position, the opening is deleted with a warning. - Copying and deleting. Copying the wall copies its openings. Deleting the wall deletes them. Splitting the wall (ARC-WALL-011) moves the opening to the part that contains its centre, and an opening that straddles the split point is clipped on each part. - Rooms. The opening does not connect rooms on either side, because room boundaries use the uncut wall body (ARC-ROOM-002).

    Data (IFC mapping). An IfcOpeningElement (PredefinedType = OPENING) with an extruded rectangular body through the wall thickness, related through IfcRelVoidsElement, with no fill. The u range and constraints are stored in RXD element data (recipe.opening).

    Commands. opening.create_wall(wall_id, u0, u1, base: {level_id, offset}, top: Level{id,offset} | Unconnected(h)) -> element_id (ARC-OPEN-003); element.move and element.set_param edit it afterwards.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 1.2 × 2.1 m wall opening in a plastered block wall shows the plaster returned into the reveal when the type wraps at inserts. - [ ] Shortening the wall so that its end lies inside the opening turns the opening into a notch; shortening it past the opening's start deletes the opening and reports it. - [ ] Rooms on both sides of a wall opening stay separate.

    3.3.18 Embedded curtain walls

    ID: ARC-WALL-013 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §4.13, §6.2

    Behaviour & rules. - A curtain wall whose type has Automatically Embed on, and which is drawn parallel to a basic wall (within TOL_ANGLE) with its location line within 152.4 mm (6") of that wall's location line and overlapping it in plan and in height, embeds in that wall. The host wall is then cut by the curtain wall's outline extruded through the host's thickness, as if it were an insert. - Nesting. A curtain wall embedded in a curtain-wall panel of type wall is allowed. - Editing the embedded wall's profile updates the host opening. - The embedding is a cut edge from the curtain wall to the host.

    Data (IFC mapping). An IfcOpeningElement voids the host (IfcRelVoidsElement), and the curtain wall fills it (IfcRelFillsElement).

    Commands. No command of its own. Embedding is automatic on create or move. geometry.cut (ARC-MOD-016) forces a cut manually.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Drawing a storefront along a brick wall cuts a matching opening, and moving the storefront moves the opening.

    3.3.19 Walls by Room and by Segment

    ID: ARC-WALL-014 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §1 (2026), §4.2 · screenshots/architecture/walls_by_room_by_segment.png

    Purpose. Generate finish walls (linings) against existing walls, columns or room boundaries.

    Workflow. 1. The user starts the Wall tool and chooses a lining type, then Place By Segment or Place By Room. 2. By Segment. Hovering a wall or column segment previews a new wall placed against the face on the cursor side. Tab toggles whether columns are included in the chain. A click creates the wall. 3. By Room. Hovering a room or any closed area previews walls along its whole boundary. A click creates them all. 4. Spacebar, before the click, flips which side of the new wall faces the target.

    Behaviour & rules. - Only targets cut by the plan view's level are eligible. Curtain walls, ellipse walls, face-based walls, in-place walls and room separation lines are not. - Targets in linked models are allowed. The target does not need to be room-bounding. - The new wall's location line is set to the finish face that touches the target. Its base and top come from the New Walls properties. - Each boundary segment produces one wall. Consecutive walls are joined to each other. The new wall is joined to the target (Auto Join, ARC-WALL-015) only when it is a hosted wall or when Auto Join is on. - With Hosted Wall on, every new wall is hosted on its target (ARC-WALL-016). Structural walls and curtain walls cannot be hosts during this creation, but can be picked as hosts afterwards. - Boundary source. By Room uses the room boundary computed at the room's computation height (ARC-ROOM-002), at the finish-face rule, regardless of the project's area rule.

    Commands. - wall.create_by_segment(type_id, target_ref, side: Left|Right, include_columns?: bool, hosted?: bool, base_level?, top_constraint?, ...) -> [element_id] - wall.create_by_room(type_id, room_id | point, flip?: bool, hosted?: bool, ...) -> [element_id]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] By Room in a rectangular room with a column in one corner creates a lining that wraps the column's two exposed faces when columns are included. - [ ] By Segment against a wall in a linked model creates the lining in the host model, with no hosting relationship.

    3.3.20 Auto Join and Auto Join & Lock

    ID: ARC-WALL-015 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §1 (2025), §4.2

    Behaviour & rules. - When a new wall overlaps an existing parallel wall face to face (for example, a lining placed against a core wall), Auto Join creates a Join Geometry relation between them. Inserts placed in either wall then cut both. - Auto Join & Lock also creates an alignment-lock constraint between the touching faces, so the two walls move together. - Neither option applies to structural, face-based, stacked or curtain walls, or to Pick Faces placement. - Slanted walls get Auto Join only, never the lock. - Inserts with complex cuts (non-prismatic voids) cut only the first wall.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcRelConnectsElements (Name "JoinGeometry"), and the lock in RXD document model/constraints.

    Commands. The option is passed to wall.create(type_id, curve, base_level, top_constraint: Level(id) | Unconnected(height), base_offset?, top_offset?, location_line?, flip?: bool, structural?: bool, structural_usage?, room_bounding?: bool, join_status?: Allow|Disallow, auto_join?: Off|Join|JoinAndLock) -> element_id. Afterward, geometry.join and constraint.lock_alignment apply.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A door placed in a core wall that was auto-joined to a lining cuts both walls.

    3.3.21 Hosted walls

    ID: ARC-WALL-016 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §1 (2027), §4.13

    Purpose. A lining or finish wall that follows its host wall.

    Behaviour & rules. - A hosted wall stores (host_wall, side, offset_from_host ≥ 0). - Its location curve is recomputed from the host's face curve on that side, offset by offset_from_host. It therefore follows the host's movement, rotation and changes to the host's cross-section (slanted or tapered). - It follows the host even when it is pinned. - If the offset is ≤ 152.4 mm and Auto Join is on, inserts in the host also cut the hosted wall. - Linked walls cannot be hosts. - A host cannot be aligned to its own hosted wall, because that would be a cycle and the command is rejected. - Commands on the contextual tab: Select Main Host, Remove Hosted Relationship (the wall becomes free and stays in place) and Pick New Host. - The read-only Hosted parameter is filterable and schedulable ("Walls Hosted = Yes").

    Regeneration. A host edge from the host wall's plan stage to the hosted wall.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcRelConnectsElements (Name "HostedWall", Relating = host). The relation and offset are owned by the hosted wall and stored in its RXD element data (recipe.wall), and Hosted is written as a property value.

    Commands. - wall.set_host(wall_id, host_wall_id, side, offset) - wall.remove_host(wall_ids) - wall.select_main_host(wall_id) -> element_id (query)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Rotating the host 15° rotates a hosted lining with it and keeps the offset. - [ ] Removing the relationship leaves the lining exactly in place.

    3.3.22 Other wall behaviours

    ID: ARC-WALL-017 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §4.13

    Purpose. Smaller wall behaviours that do not need a block of their own.

    Behaviour Rule
    Flip arrows Same as wall.flip: mirrors the wall about its location line. The layer order is reversed, so the exterior face moves to the other side; the location line, length, height and joins stay. When the location line is not the wall centreline, the body moves across it (for example, Finish Face: Exterior stays put and the wall swings to its other side). Hosted doors and windows keep their world position and their facing and hand; their voids are recomputed for the new layer order. Room boundaries at the finish rule move with the body. Flipping is refused on a pinned wall and on a wall in a group instance outside the group editor (ARC-MOD-000). Elliptical walls have no flip control. See also ARC-FLIP-001
    Spacebar With walls selected, Spacebar flips them as the flip arrows do (ARC-KEY-001). During placement it flips the side of the wall that is drawn as exterior
    Change type Keeps the location line (ARC-WALL-002). The joins are re-solved for the new thickness, inserts stay hosted (an insert whose void no longer fits reports "Cannot cut instance out of wall" and stays), and dimensions to faces that still exist (matched by face role: exterior finish, core face, centreline) stay attached. Dimensions to faces that no longer exist are deleted with a warning. Changing to a curtain or stacked type is allowed only when the wall has no profile edits that the new kind cannot represent
    Moves With Nearby Elements A component or line whose Moves With Nearby Elements is on, and which lies parallel to a wall within 300 mm, keeps its perpendicular distance when the wall moves. The relation is stored in RXD document model/constraints and re-detected on each move. Only straight walls and straight model lines or component reference lines take part; moving the wall along its own direction does not move the follower. The follower moves even if it is pinned (ARC-MOD-000)
    Disjoin on move ARC-MOD-004: moving a wall with Disjoin breaks its end joins first, so the joined walls do not stretch

    Data (IFC mapping). A flip changes IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage.DirectionSense (and OffsetFromReferenceLine when the location line is not the centreline) and the explicit body. The Moves With Nearby Elements flag is a property value on the follower.

    Commands. wall.flip(wall_ids), element.set_type(element_ids, type_id) and element.set_param(element_ids, "MovesWithNearbyElements", true); element.flip (ARC-FLIP-001) dispatches to wall.flip for walls.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Flipping a wall drawn on Finish Face: Exterior keeps that face's line in place and reverses the layers; a door in the wall keeps its swing side. - [ ] Changing a 200 mm wall to a 300 mm type with the location line on the core centreline keeps the centreline and re-cleans both end joins. - [ ] A model line 200 mm from a wall, with Moves With Nearby Elements on, stays 200 mm away when the wall is moved 1 m perpendicular to itself, and does not move when the wall is moved along its length.

    3.4 Doors, windows, components and architectural columns

    3.4.1 Hosting model for loadable families

    ID: ARC-HOST-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §5.1, §17.5

    Purpose. One hosting model for every loadable family.

    Hosting kind Valid hosts Placement behaviour
    Wall-hosted Basic and stacked walls; curtain-wall panels only after the panel has been swapped to a wall type Hovering a wall shows a preview; the family's opening void cuts the host
    Floor-, ceiling- or roof-hosted That category Hovering a host of that category shows a preview
    Face-based Any planar or curved face, including linked and imported faces Placement panel: Place on Vertical Face, Place on Face or Place on Work Plane
    Work-plane-based The active work plane Place on Work Plane
    Level-based (non-hosted) A level plus an offset. The element may rest on the infinite plane of a floor's top face A click places it; Spacebar rotates
    Line-based A work plane Two clicks define the length

    Behaviour & rules. - Cutting. A wall-hosted family carries an opening cut (a void solid in the family's coordinate system). - On placement, Reviera transforms the void into the host's coordinates and creates an IfcOpeningElement whose body is the void, clipped to the host's thickness plus 1 mm on each side. - The host body is then cut (BRepAlgoAPI_Cut), and wrapping applies (ARC-WRAP-001). - If the void does not reach through the full host width (for example, a recess), the opening's PredefinedType is RECESS. - Constraint along the host. An insert can only move along its host's surface and keeps its offset from the host face. Moving it off the host requires Disjoin (ARC-MOD-004) or Pick New Host. - Rehosting. Pick New Host (Modify | <category> › Host panel): - a level-based element can move to another level, floor or surface (in section or elevation); - a face-based or work-plane-based element can move to another face or plane. - Host deletion. Deleting a host deletes its hosted inserts. Face-based elements on a deleted face become orphaned: they stay where they are, report "Lost host" and can be rehosted. - Joined walls. An insert in a wall that is joined (Join Geometry or Auto Join) to a parallel wall also cuts that wall when its void reaches it. - Slanted walls. Inserts keep their Orientation setting (Vertical or Slanted). Slanted orientation tilts the family to match the wall angle.

    Regeneration. - Edges into the insert: host (the host's plan and body stages) and datum (the level). - Edge out of the insert: cut to the host body (and to joined walls). - The insert's void is computed from the insert alone, so the host never waits on the insert's full geometry. This avoids a cycle.

    Data (IFC mapping). The host is related to its opening through IfcRelVoidsElement (RelatingBuildingElement = host, RelatedOpeningElement = opening). The opening is related to the insert through IfcRelFillsElement. The insert is contained in the host's storey. For face-based elements, the host is recorded in RXD element data (placement), and in IFC through IfcRelConnectsElements (Name "HostedBy").

    Commands. - element.pick_new_host(element_ids, host_ref, placement?: VerticalFace|Face|WorkPlane) - element.host_query(element_id) -> host_ref (query)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A door moved along its wall stays in the wall. When the wall moves, the door moves with it. - [ ] Deleting the host wall deletes its doors after a warning that gives the count. - [ ] Each wall-hosted insert exports an IfcOpeningElement with matching void and fill relationships, and an IFC checker (IfcOpenShell validate) reports no errors.

    3.4.2 Doors

    ID: ARC-DOOR-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §5.2

    Purpose. Place door families in walls.

    Workflow. 1. The user starts Architecture › Build › Door (DR). It works in plan, section, elevation and 3D views. 2. The user picks a type, or uses Load Family. 3. Optionally, the user turns on Tag on Placement (Tag panel) and sets orientation (Horizontal or Vertical), Leader, leader length and Tags…. 4. Hovering a wall shows a preview with temporary dimensions (ARC-DIM-001). Moving the cursor toward one face of the wall or the other sets the facing (the swing side). Spacebar flips the hand. 5. A click places the door, and the tool repeats until Esc.

    UI. Selected doors show Flip hand (horizontal arrows) and Flip facing (vertical arrows) controls, which are also in the right-click menu. Which controls appear depends on the family's flip settings.

    Behaviour & rules. - Instance parameters: Level, Sill Height (changing it moves the door; it does not resize it), Head Height (= sill + height), Orientation (slanted walls), Frame Type, Frame Material, Finish, Comments, Mark, phasing, From Room and To Room (RO). - Mark. Each new door gets the next Mark in its category ("1", "2", … or the last Mark's increment). - Type parameters: Width, Height, Thickness, Rough Width, Rough Height, Function (Interior or Exterior), Wall Closure, Construction Type, materials, Fire Rating, Type Mark, Operation and Cost. - From/To Room. Two points are sampled 0.3 m apart along the facing normal from the family's room calculation point, at the room's computation height. Each point is located in the room set of the door's phase (ARC-ROOM-002). To Room is on the facing side. The Flip commands swap the two values. Both values are recomputed whenever rooms or doors regenerate. - Edge cases: - A door cannot be placed in a curtain panel (use a curtain-wall door, ARC-CW-006). - A door wider than its host segment gives "Cannot cut instance out of wall": the door stays and its void is not applied. - A door in one of a pair of parallel walls cuts the other only when the walls are joined.

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcDoor with OverallHeight, OverallWidth, PredefinedType = DOOR (GATE or TRAPDOOR where the family says so) and OperationType from the family (for example SINGLE_SWING_LEFT), written on both the occurrence and the type (IfcDoorType.OperationType), with UserDefinedOperationType when the value is USERDEFINED. - IfcDoorType with IfcDoorLiningProperties and IfcDoorPanelProperties derived from family parameters where it can map them. - Pset_DoorCommon holds Reference (Type Mark), FireRating, IsExternal (Function), HandicapAccessible and similar where they are set. - Hand and facing are expressed by the placement's mirrored axis. A mirrored instance has a negative determinant, and Reviera writes IfcCartesianTransformationOperator3DnonUniform in the mapped representation, so viewers show it correctly. - From/To Room are written as IfcRelSpaceBoundary (for the door) and as property values.

    Commands. - door.place(type_id, host_wall_id, point_along: f64 | point, sill_height?, flip_hand?: bool, flip_facing?: bool, tag?: {orientation, leader, leader_length}) -> element_id - insert.flip_hand(element_ids) - insert.flip_facing(element_ids)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Placing a door 900 mm wide with its centre 600 mm from a perpendicular wall face, using temporary-dimension settings set to Faces, gives a temporary dimension of exactly 600 mm. - [ ] Flipping facing swaps From Room and To Room. - [ ] Ten doors placed in sequence are numbered 1 to 10.

    3.4.3 Windows

    ID: ARC-WIN-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §5.3

    Purpose. Place window families in walls, and skylights in roofs.

    Workflow. The user starts Architecture › Build › Window (WN). The same tag and temporary-dimension behaviour as doors applies. Spacebar has no effect; after placement, flip controls flip facing and hand where the family allows it.

    Behaviour & rules. - Instance parameters: Level, Sill Height (defaults to the type's Default Sill Height), Head Height, Orientation, Mark, Comments and phasing. - Type parameters: Width, Height, Default Sill Height, Wall Closure, Window Inset, Construction Type and materials. - Roof-hosted window families cut roofs at right angles to the roof face (a skylight). - Window Inset moves the family's glazing plane in from the exterior face. It is applied as a translation along the wall normal before the void is computed.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcWindow (PredefinedType = WINDOW, SKYLIGHT for roof-hosted, LIGHTDOME where flagged) with OverallHeight and OverallWidth. IfcWindowType with PartitioningType from the family. Pset_WindowCommon holds IsExternal, FireRating, ThermalTransmittance and similar values. Openings and fills are as in ARC-HOST-001.

    Commands. window.place(type_id, host_id, point_along | point, sill_height?, flip_facing?) -> element_id.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing a window type's Default Sill Height does not move windows that are already placed. It changes only the default for new ones. - [ ] A skylight in a 30° roof cuts an opening at right angles to the roof face.

    3.4.4 Components

    ID: ARC-COMP-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §5.4

    Purpose. Place any loadable family: furniture, fixtures, equipment, planting, specialty items and so on.

    Workflow. 1. The user starts Architecture › Build › Component › Place a Component (CM). The tool is available only in views that suit the family (for example, plan or 3D for furniture). 2. The user picks a type, or uses Load Family. For face-based and work-plane-based families, the user picks a placement option; the last choice is remembered. 3. Spacebar cycles the rotation in 90° steps, or aligns the preview to the nearest wall. Rotate after placement (on the ribbon) asks for an angle after each click. 4. A click places the component.

    Behaviour & rules. - Instance parameters (typical): Level or Host, Offset or Elevation from Level, Moves With Nearby Elements, Work Plane, Schedule Level, Mark, Comments and phasing. - The context menu offers Pick New Host (ARC-HOST-001) and Edit Family (DM chapter). - With Moves With Nearby Elements on, Reviera records the nearest parallel wall within 300 mm at placement time, and the component keeps its offset from that wall (ARC-WALL-017).

    Data (IFC mapping). The IFC entity is chosen from the family's category through the category mapping table (DM chapter). Examples: Furniture → IfcFurniture; Casework → IfcFurniture (PredefinedType = SHELF or USERDEFINED); Plumbing Fixtures → IfcSanitaryTerminal; Planting → IfcGeographicElement (4X3: VEGETATION); Generic Models → IfcBuildingElementProxy. The geometry is an IfcMappedItem of the type's RepresentationMap, with the family geometry built once per type.

    Commands. component.place(type_id, point | host_ref, rotation?: f64, level_id?, offset?, placement?: VerticalFace|Face|WorkPlane) -> element_id.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Three chairs placed with Spacebar pressed once each are rotated 0°, 90° and 180° relative to the first. - [ ] Twenty instances of one type share a single IfcRepresentationMap in the IFC.

    3.4.5 Architectural columns

    ID: ARC-COL-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §5.5

    Purpose. Non-structural columns: casings, pilasters and decorative columns.

    Workflow. 1. The user starts Architecture › Build › Column › Column: Architectural in a plan or 3D view. 2. The user sets the options: Rotate after placement, Level (3D views only), Height/Depth, Level/Unconnected plus a value, and Room Bounding. 3. A click places the column. Its two centre reference planes can be aligned to grids or walls.

    Behaviour & rules. - An architectural column that is joined to walls takes the wall's material (the core material of the joined wall). - The wall's wrapping layers wrap around the column faces that face away from the wall. Reviera treats the column's section as a mid-span obstacle and applies end-wrapping (ARC-WRAP-001) to the wall pieces that meet it. - Structural columns behave differently and are covered in the STR chapter. - With Moves With Grids on, a column at a grid intersection keeps its offsets from both grids. - Attach Top/Base (Modify | Columns): - Attach Column: Top or Base. - Attachment Style: Cut Column, Cut Target or Do Not Cut. - Attachment Justification: Minimum Intersection, Intersect Column Midline or Maximum Intersection. - Offset from Attachment. - Valid targets: roofs, floors, ceilings, reference planes, structural framing, isolated foundations, foundation slabs and levels. - The column's top is moved to the height given by the justification: the lowest, middle or highest point where the target surface crosses the column's footprint. Then, if the style is Cut Column, the column is cut by the target's shadow (as in ARC-WALL-008). If the style is Cut Target, the target is cut by the column. - Detach Top/Base reverses the operation. - Instance parameters: Base Level, Base Offset, Top Level, Top Offset, Moves With Grids, Room Bounding, Top/Base Is Attached (RO), Attachment Justification at Top/Base, Offset From Attachment at Top/Base, Comments, Mark and phasing.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcColumn with PredefinedType = COLUMN (PILASTER where the family is flagged) and Pset_ColumnCommon.LoadBearing = FALSE. A property value marks it as architectural. Attach relations are IfcRelConnectsElements ("AttachTop" or "AttachBase") and are recorded in RXD document model/constraints.

    Commands. - column.place_architectural(type_id, point, base_level, top_constraint, base_offset?, top_offset?, rotation?, room_bounding?) -> element_id - column.attach(column_ids[], end: top|base, target_id, style?, justification?, offset?) -> () - column.detach(column_ids[], end: top|base, target_ids?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A column attached at its top to a sloping roof with Maximum Intersection reaches the highest point where the roof crosses the column's footprint. With Minimum Intersection it reaches the lowest. - [ ] A column joined to a plastered wall takes the plaster finish on its faces.

    3.4.6 Flip controls and mirrored state

    ID: ARC-FLIP-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §2.4, §2.5, §4.13, §5.2, §5.3, §13 (Edge cases) · web: About Flip Controls; Flip Elements

    Purpose. One set of rules for flipping elements in place (the paired-arrow controls, the context menu and the Spacebar) and for recording the resulting orientation, including mirroring, so that it survives IFC round trips.

    Workflow. 1. The user selects one or more elements. Each element that supports flipping shows its flip controls (ARC-CTRL-001). 2. The user clicks a control, chooses Flip Hand or Flip Facing from the right-click menu, or presses Spacebar. 3. The element flips at once; each click or key press is one undo step.

    UI. - Doors and windows show Flip hand (horizontal paired arrows, at the insert's centreline on the facing side) and Flip facing (vertical paired arrows, across the wall). The family decides which of the two exist. - Walls show one pair of arrows on the exterior side (ARC-WALL-017). Fascias, gutters and slab edges show horizontal and vertical arrows (ARC-SLED-001, ARC-ROOF-004). Stairs show their up/down arrow while being edited (ARC-STAIR-002). - Other family instances show the flip controls defined in the family editor (DM chapter). Each control is single or double and horizontal or vertical: a single control turns the instance 180° about the vertical axis through the control's point; a double control mirrors the instance across the plane through the control's axis. - The right-click menu lists the same actions with their names (Flip Hand, Flip Facing, Flip Work Plane, or the family control's label).

    Behaviour & rules. - Definitions. For a hosted insert, facing is the side of the host towards which the family's facing direction points (a door's swing side), and hand is the side of the family's centreline on which its hinge or handle lies. Flip facing reflects the instance across the vertical plane that contains the insertion point and is parallel to the host face; flip hand reflects it across the vertical plane through the insertion point at right angles to the host face. Doing both is equivalent to a 180° rotation. - Spacebar on a selection: walls flip; doors and windows cycle through the four combinations in the order (facing, hand) = (0,0) → (1,0) → (1,1) → (0,1) → (0,0); free-standing components rotate 90° about their insertion point; work-plane-based instances with a Flip Work Plane control flip to the other side of their plane. If the selection mixes kinds that respond differently, each element does its own action. If an element cannot respond (no control, pinned, or locked by a constraint), nothing changes for it and the status bar says why. - Hosted constraints. A flipped insert stays in its host at the same position along the host and the same sill height. Its opening void is recomputed; the host is cut again, and wrapping is reapplied. Door From Room and To Room swap when facing flips (ARC-DOOR-001). - References. Dimensions and alignments attached to named family references (for example Left, Right, Exterior) stay attached to the same named reference, which may now lie in a different position; constraints are re-solved (ARC-CNST-002). If a locked dimension would change, the flip is refused with "Constraints are not satisfied". - Pins and groups. A flip is a geometric modification: pinned elements and members of group instances outside the group editor are refused (ARC-MOD-000). - Mirrored state. Flip hand and flip facing do not set Mirrored. Mirrored (read-only, schedulable, filterable) is true when the instance's net transform has been reflected an odd number of times by the Mirror tool (ARC-MOD-003) or by a family mirror (double) control. Mirroring a door or window with the Mirror tool is recorded as the matching flip when the mirror plane is parallel or perpendicular to the host face, and sets Mirrored, so a mirrored door can be found in a schedule even though its hand looks the same as a flipped one. - Elements without flip support. In-place families, model text, groups and rooms have no flip control; element.flip reports "Element cannot be flipped" for them and changes nothing.

    Data (IFC mapping). - The flags facing_flipped, hand_flipped and mirrored (DM-INST-001) are stored in RXD element data (placement) and written as property values (FacingFlipped, HandFlipped, Mirrored) in the instance property set defined by the DM chapter. - Geometry. IFC placements (IfcAxis2Placement3D) cannot reflect, so the net transform T = placement · F_facing · F_hand · M is split: when det(T) > 0 (no flip, both flips, or two mirrors), the reflection pairs are folded into a rotation of the ObjectPlacement; when det(T) < 0, the IfcMappedItem.MappingTarget is an IfcCartesianTransformationOperator3DnonUniform with Scale = −1 on the reflected axis (X for hand, Y for facing), and the placement carries the rest. - Doors and windows. IfcDoor.OperationType swaps …_LEFT and …_RIGHT values when the effective hand changes (for example SINGLE_SWING_LEFT ↔ SINGLE_SWING_RIGHT); the type keeps its own value, and the occurrence value wins. The swing side is visible in the geometry and in the IfcRelSpaceBoundary of the door. - On import without RXD, Reviera derives the flags from the mapping transform's determinant and axis signs and marks them as inferred.

    Commands. - insert.flip_hand(element_ids) and insert.flip_facing(element_ids) flip doors, windows and other hosted inserts that have the matching control. - element.flip(element_ids, control?: Facing|Hand|WorkPlane|Family(control_key)) -> () is the generic entry point used by the flip controls, the context menu and ui.flip_selection (UI chapter). Without control, walls call wall.flip, fascias, gutters and slab edges flip horizontally (hostsweep.flip), inserts flip facing, and family instances use their first family control. Elements that do not support the control are skipped and listed in the result warning. - element.flip_state(element_id) -> {facing_flipped, hand_flipped, mirrored, controls: [control_key]} (query).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Pressing Space four times with a door selected visits four distinct facing/hand combinations and returns to the start; each press is one undo step. - [ ] Flipping the facing of a door between two rooms swaps its From Room and To Room values and moves its swing to the other side of the wall without moving its centreline. - [ ] A door flipped on both axes exports with a positive-determinant placement (no reflection operator); a door flipped on one axis exports an IfcCartesianTransformationOperator3DnonUniform with one negative scale, and IfcOpenShell renders it with the swing on the correct side. - [ ] A right-hand door mirrored with the Mirror tool and a right-hand door changed with Flip Hand look identical, but only the mirrored one reports Mirrored = true in a schedule. - [ ] element.flip on a pinned window changes nothing and returns "Element is pinned".

    3.5 Curtain walls and curtain systems

    3.5.1 Curtain element model

    ID: ARC-CW-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §6.1 · screenshots/architecture/curtain_wall_rendered.png

    Purpose. A curtain element is a surface divided by grids into cells. Each cell is filled by a panel, and mullions are swept along the grid segments and the borders.

    Behaviour & rules. - Hosts. Curtain walls (a wall kind), curtain systems (on faces) and sloped glazing (a roof type) all share one model: - a curtain surface (planar, or faceted-cylindrical for arc walls) with local axes U (along) and V (up), or Grid 1 and Grid 2 for systems and sloped glazing; - a set of grid lines, each with segments that can be turned off; - cells; - panels; - mullions. - Default types: a plain type with no grids and no mullions; a glazing type with preset grids; and a storefront type with preset grids and mullions. - Grid lines. Grid lines are either type-driven (generated by the layout rules and pinned) or independent, which happens when the user adds one or unpins one. Independent grid lines keep their absolute position when the wall is resized. - Panels have one of these types: - a system panel (Glazed, Solid or Empty); - a loadable curtain-panel family; - any basic or stacked wall type; - a nested curtain wall type; - a curtain-wall door or window family.

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcCurtainWall with an IfcCurtainWallType aggregates (IfcRelAggregates) its parts: - panels as IfcPlate (PredefinedType = CURTAIN_PANEL), or as IfcWall, IfcDoor or IfcWindow when the panel is one of those; - mullions as IfcMember (PredefinedType = MULLION). - The IfcCurtainWall itself has an Axis representation (its base line) and no body. - Grid lines (U/V positions, segment on/off, pin state, independent flag) are stored in RXD element data (recipe.curtain_grid). The type's layout rules are stored in RXD type data (recipe.curtain_type).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 6 m × 3 m curtain wall with three vertical grid lines and one horizontal grid line exports one IfcCurtainWall aggregating 8 IfcPlate and the matching IfcMember parts, and it opens in an independent viewer with every part present.

    3.5.2 Creating curtain walls

    ID: ARC-CW-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §6.2

    Workflow. The user starts the Wall tool with a curtain-wall type. Line, Pick Lines and Pick Faces work, as do Spacebar and listening dimensions.

    Behaviour & rules. - Arc curtain walls are faceted at their vertical grid lines: each panel is a planar chord, and mullions sit on the arc. With no vertical grid lines, the panel is curved (a cylindrical panel) only if its type allows that. Otherwise Reviera adds a facet every 15° and warns. - For non-rectangular outlines, the user can edit the profile (ARC-WALL-009) or attach the top (ARC-WALL-008). Cells that cross the outline are clipped to it, panels take the clipped shape, and border mullions follow the outline. - Embedding is described in ARC-WALL-013.

    Commands. wall.create with a curtain type. curtain.set_profile(wall_id, loops) is an alias of wall.edit_profile.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An arc curtain wall with vertical grid lines every 1 m has planar panels whose corners lie on the arc.

    3.5.3 Grid layout solver

    ID: ARC-CW-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §6.3, §17.6 · screenshots/architecture/curtain_grid_layout_controls.png

    Purpose. Compute type-driven grid positions from layout rules.

    Behaviour & rules. - Inputs for each direction (vertical grids along U; horizontal grids along V): - Layout L ∈ {None, Fixed Distance, Fixed Number, Maximum Spacing, Minimum Spacing}; - Spacing S; - Number n (instance, 1–200); - Justification J ∈ {Beginning, Center, End} (instance); - Angle θ (instance); - Offset o (instance); - Adjust for Mullion Size (type). - Measurement frame. Grid lines run at angle θ from the V axis (for vertical grids). Positions are measured along the direction perpendicular to the lines, d. The surface's extent along d is [d_min, d_max] (taken from the outline's corners), with length D = d_max − d_min. The justification origin d₀ is d_min (Beginning), (d_min + d_max)/2 (Center) or d_max (End), plus o. - Algorithm: - Fixed Distance: let r = D − ⌊D/S⌋·S be the leftover. The lines are at d_min + o + k·S (Beginning), d_max + o − k·S (End) or d_min + r/2 + o + k·S (Center), for every integer k for which the line lies strictly inside (d_min, d_max) by more than TOL_POINT. Center justification therefore leaves equal leftovers at the two ends. - Fixed Number: n is the number of interior grid lines. Positions are d_min + k·D/(n+1) for k = 1…n. Justification and offset do not apply. - Maximum Spacing: panel count m = ceil(D / S), positions d_min + k·D/m for k = 1…m−1. - Minimum Spacing: panel count m = max(1, floor(D / S)), positions d_min + k·D/m. - None: no type-driven lines. - Adjust for Mullion Size. When it is on, the spacing applies to the clear panel width, measured between mullion faces, instead of between centrelines. Reviera solves for line positions x_k such that x_{k+1} − x_k − (w_k + w_{k+1})/2 = S_clear, using the actual widths of the interior mullions w_k and border mullions (w_b) for this layout. For Max/Min Spacing and Fixed Number, the effective length becomes D − Σ mullion widths before dividing. - Independent lines keep their absolute positions. Type-driven lines that fall within 1 mm of an independent line are suppressed. - The solver runs in O(n) and is a pure function of its inputs, so it can be unit-tested.

    UI. Configure Grid Layout is an in-canvas control on a selected curtain face. It shows a justification-origin arrow for each direction (which the user can click to cycle Beginning, Center and End) and angle and offset fields for each direction.

    Commands. curtain.set_layout(element_id, direction: U|V, justification?, angle?, offset?, number?) and curtaintype.set_layout(type_id, direction, layout, spacing?, adjust_for_mullion?: bool).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Fixed Distance 1.5 m on a 10 m wall: Beginning justification gives lines at 1.5, 3.0 … 9.0, with a 1.0 m remainder at the end. Center justification gives 6 full panels with 0.5 m left at each end. - [ ] Maximum Spacing 1.2 m on a 10 m wall gives 9 equal panels of 1.111 m. - [ ] With Adjust for Mullion Size on, 50 mm interior mullions, 100 mm border mullions and Fixed Distance 1.0 m, every clear panel width is 1.000 m.

    3.5.4 Manual curtain grids

    ID: ARC-CW-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §6.4

    Workflow. 1. The user starts Architecture › Build › Curtain Grid in an elevation or 3D view. 2. The user picks a Placement mode: All Segments, One Segment, or All Except Picked (click segments to exclude, then Finish). 3. Hovering near a vertical edge previews a horizontal grid line, and hovering near a horizontal edge previews a vertical one. The preview snaps to the midpoints and thirds of panels, to visible levels, grids and reference planes, and to grid lines on curtain walls that share a corner. A click places the grid line.

    Behaviour & rules. - A selected grid line offers Add/Remove Segments: clicking a segment removes it, which merges the two adjacent cells into one panel, and clicking a dashed (removed) segment restores it. - Temporary dimensions are shown to the neighbouring grid lines, and the line has a pin control. - Manual lines are independent.

    Commands. - curtain.add_grid(element_id, direction: U|V, position, mode: All|One(segment)|AllExcept([segment])) -> grid_key - curtain.set_grid_segments(element_id, grid_key, segments_on: [bool]) - curtain.move_grid(element_id, grid_key, position) - curtain.delete_grid(element_id, grid_key)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Removing the middle segment of a vertical grid line merges two panels into one panel of twice the height. Restoring the segment splits it again, and the original panel type is kept.

    3.5.5 Mullions

    ID: ARC-CW-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §6.4

    Workflow. The user starts Architecture › Build › Mullion and picks a Placement mode: Grid Line (the whole line), Grid Line Segment or All Grid Lines. The same modes apply to border edges.

    Behaviour & rules. - Mullion types: - Rectangular: profile, thickness, width on side 1 and side 2, and offset; - Circular: radius; - Corner L: leg lengths and thickness; - Corner V; - Corner Trapezoid: centre width and depth; - Corner Quad: depth 1 and 2, which gives a kite, rectangle or square. - Custom profiles come from profile families. Closed multi-loop profiles (for example, hollow sections) are accepted, and open loops are rejected. - Instance parameters: Angle, Offset (locked when the mullion is type-driven), Length and Mark. - Generation: 1. A mullion is created for each grid segment that is on, and for each border edge that has a border mullion type. 2. Continuity at each grid intersection. Precedence, highest first: a per-mullion override (Make Continuous or Break at Join); then the type's Join Condition (Vertical Grid Continuous, Horizontal Grid Continuous, Border and Vertical Continuous, Border and Horizontal Continuous; for systems and sloped glazing, Grid 1 or Grid 2 Continuous); and then, with Not Defined, the vertical direction. 3. The continuous mullion runs through the intersection. The others are trimmed at the continuous mullion's faces: each end is cut by planes offset ±(width/2) from the continuous line. 4. The geometry is a sweep of the profile along the segment's straight line (BRepPrimAPI_MakePrism, or BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipe on faceted arcs). The profile is centred on the line, offset by the mullion offset along the surface normal, and rotated by the Angle. 5. Corner mullions sit at the shared vertical edge of two curtain walls that meet at angle φ. Their cross-section is built from φ and the type's dimensions (L: two legs along the two faces; V: two legs mirrored about the bisector; trapezoid and quad: the polygon from their parameters). - Type-driven mullions are pinned. Deleting one requires unpinning it first.

    Commands. - mullion.add(element_id, target: GridLine(key) | Segment(key, idx) | AllGridLines | Border(edge), type_id) -> [element_id] - mullion.set_continuity(mullion_id, mode: Continuous|Break) - curtaintype.set_mullions(type_id, interior_v, border1_v, border2_v, interior_h, border1_h, border2_h)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With Join Condition = Horizontal Grid Continuous, the horizontal mullions are unbroken and the vertical mullions stop at their faces. - [ ] A Make Continuous override on one vertical mullion wins over the type setting at that mullion's intersections only. - [ ] A hollow two-loop mullion profile produces a solid with an inner void.

    3.5.6 Panels and curtain-wall doors

    ID: ARC-CW-006 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §6.5

    Workflow. 1. The user hovers a panel's edge and presses Tab until the panel is highlighted, then selects it. 2. If the panel is pinned, the user unpins it. 3. The user changes its type in the Type Selector.

    Behaviour & rules. - A panel can take any of the panel kinds listed in ARC-CW-001. - A wall-type panel has Categorize as = Panel or Wall, which controls scheduling. - Panels cannot be resized directly. Moving grid lines resizes them. - Each cell polygon is used as follows: - system panel: a planar plate of the panel's thickness, offset along the surface normal; - family panel: an instance driven by width and height (the cell's bounding rectangle) and clipped to the cell if the cell is not rectangular; - wall-type panel: a wall whose location line is the cell's bottom edge and whose profile is the cell. - Curtain-wall door. Only door families made for curtain walls can replace a panel. The door fills the cell. The sill mullion is not removed automatically: the user unpins and deletes it. Switching back to a panel type reverts the change. Curtain-wall doors are tagged and scheduled as doors. - Inserts in wall-type panels are positioned relative to the curtain wall as a whole, so they do not follow the panel when grid lines move.

    Data (IFC mapping). A panel is an IfcPlate, IfcWall, IfcDoor or IfcWindow aggregated in the curtain wall (ARC-CW-001).

    Commands. curtain.set_panel_type(panel_ids, type_id). Pin and unpin are covered by ARC-MOD-013.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Swapping a glazed panel for a curtain-wall door turns that cell into an IfcDoor aggregated in the IfcCurtainWall, and it appears in the door schedule.

    3.5.7 Curtain systems by face

    ID: ARC-CW-007 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/02 §6.6, §12.1

    Workflow. 1. The user starts Massing & Site › Model by Face › Curtain System by Face and chooses a type. 2. With Select Multiple (on by default), the user clicks faces to add or remove them, or drags a pick box over a whole form. Clear Selection empties the set. 3. Create System builds the system.

    Behaviour & rules. - Each face gets its own UV grid (Grid 1 and Grid 2, each with angle and offset). - Curved faces are tessellated at the grid lines into planar panels. - A curtain system has no editable sketch. It updates only through Update to Face (ARC-MASS-003). - Manual grid lines snap to boundary intersections and reference planes.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcCurtainWall with ObjectType = "CurtainSystem", aggregating the same parts as a curtain wall.

    Commands. curtainsystem.create_by_face(type_id, face_refs) -> element_id.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A curtain system on the four faces of a mass box produces four grids whose corner mullions meet.

    3.5.8 Sloped glazing

    ID: ARC-CW-008 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §6.1, §7.4

    Purpose. Glazed roofs and skylights built from the curtain-element model (grids, mullions and panels) on the planes of a footprint or extrusion roof.

    Workflow. 1. The user creates a footprint roof (ARC-ROOF-001) or an extrusion roof (ARC-ROOF-002), or selects an existing one. 2. In the Type Selector the user picks a Sloped Glazing type. The roof becomes a set of glazed planes. 3. The user adds grids with Architecture › Build › Curtain Grid (Tab switches between Grid 1 and Grid 2 while placing), then mullions and panel changes as on a curtain wall.

    Behaviour & rules. - Changing a footprint or extrusion roof to a Sloped Glazing type replaces its body with a curtain surface on each roof plane. - Sketch kept. The roof keeps its footprint or profile sketch, slopes, cutoff and joins. Edit Footprint / Edit Profile still work, and the glazing regenerates from the new planes. - Grid directions. On each plane, Grid 1 lines run parallel to the plane's eave (its lowest horizontal edge; for an extrusion roof, the extrusion direction) and Grid 2 lines run up the slope, at right angles to Grid 1. Type layout rules (Fixed Distance, Fixed Number, Maximum Spacing, justification and angle, ARC-CW-003) are measured on the sloped plane, from the eave for Grid 1 and from the plane's justification point for Grid 2. - Grids follow the Grid 1 and Grid 2 rules. When placing a grid line, Tab switches between the two directions. - Edges. Hips, valleys and ridges are plane boundaries. The type's border mullions are placed on them once, shared by both planes and mitred to the bisector of the dihedral angle. Eaves and gables get the type's border mullions. - Mullions and panels behave as described in ARC-CW-005 and ARC-CW-006. - Type parameters are those of a curtain type (panel, join condition, grid layouts, interior and border mullions), plus the roof's Rafter Cut and Fascia Depth, which apply to the border mullions at the eave. - Changing back to a basic roof type discards the grids, mullions and panel overrides after a warning that gives their count. The roof sketch is unchanged. - Hosting. Sloped glazing is not a valid host for roof-hosted windows (use panels instead); walls can still attach to it (ARC-WALL-008), using its glazing plane.

    Data (IFC mapping). An IfcRoof aggregating one IfcCurtainWall (ObjectType = "SlopedGlazing") per roof plane, each with its own IfcPlate and IfcMember parts. The grid layout is stored in RXD element data (recipe.curtain_grid) per plane, keyed by the plane's sketch-edge sub-reference so it survives sketch edits that keep that edge.

    Commands. element.set_type(roof_id, sloped_glazing_type_id) followed by the curtain.* commands.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A hip roof changed to sloped glazing produces four glazed planes whose hip mullions sit on the hip lines. - [ ] With Grid 1 at a fixed distance of 1.5 m, a 30° plane whose slope length is 6 m gets three interior Grid 1 lines measured along the slope. - [ ] Changing the slope of one footprint edge from 30° to 45° regenerates that plane's grid and keeps manually added grid lines on the other planes. - [ ] Changing the roof back to a basic type warns with the number of mullions and panels to be removed and keeps the footprint.

    3.6 Floors, slab edges, ceilings, roofs, shape editing and parts

    3.6.1 Floors

    ID: ARC-FLR-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §7.1

    Purpose. Horizontal or sloped layered slabs defined by a sketched boundary.

    Workflow. 1. The user starts Architecture › Build › Floor › Floor: Architectural (the drop-down also offers Floor: Structural (SB), Floor by Face and Floor: Slab Edge). 2. In the sketch (Modify | Create Floor Boundary), the user draws: - Boundary Line: Pick Walls (default), lines and shapes, or Pick Lines; - Slope Arrow; - Span Direction (structural decks).

    Options: Offset, and Extend into wall (to core). 3. Outer loops define the floor, and inner loops define holes. Finish. 4. If walls below end at this floor's level, Reviera asks whether to attach them to the floor's underside. If the floor overlaps walls, it asks whether to join geometry so that the floor cuts them.

    Behaviour & rules. - Instance parameters: Level, Height Offset from Level, Room Bounding, Related to Mass (RO), Structural, Curved Edge Condition (shape-edited), Slope Angle (adjusts the slope-defining line without editing the sketch), Perimeter, Area, Volume, Elevation at Top, Elevation at Bottom, Elevation at Core Top, Elevation at Core Bottom, Thickness (RO, or editable when shape-edited with a variable layer), Comments, Mark and phasing. - Type parameters: Structure (ARC-CMPD-001), Default Thickness (RO), Function (Interior or Exterior), Coarse Scale Fill, Structural Material, analytical and thermal properties, and identity data. - Reference. The top of the floor is at level + offset, and the layers stack downward. - Slopes. A slope can come from a slope arrow, from two parallel boundary lines with different Offset from Base values, or from one line with Defines Slope and a Slope value. All three produce a tilted reference plane P. The top surface lies on P, with the pivot at the slope-defining line or the arrow's tail. - Geometry. The boundary loops are mapped to a face on P. Each layer is a prism of thickness t_j along −n_P, where n_P is the normal of P, so the layers stay perpendicular to the sloped face (BRepPrimAPI_MakePrism, then fused per layer). If the floor is shape-edited, ARC-SHAPE-001 applies. - Cuts. Floors cut walls with which they have Join Geometry. Shafts and openings cut floors (§3.8).

    Regeneration. - Edges into the floor: datum (level), sketch-lock (picked walls) and type. - Edges out of the floor: attach (walls attached to it), bound (rooms above and below, for volume), host (floor-hosted families) and cut (Join Geometry pairs).

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcSlab (PredefinedType = FLOOR; BASESLAB when the floor is structural and its function is foundation, STR chapter) with an IfcSlabType. - IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage with LayerSetDirection = AXIS3, DirectionSense = NEGATIVE and OffsetFromReferenceLine = 0, so the layers hang down from the top. - Body. An IfcExtrudedAreaSolid (profile IfcArbitraryProfileDefWithVoids, depth = thickness, ExtrudedDirection = (0,0,−1)) in a placement tilted to P for sloped floors, or an IfcFacetedBrep when the floor is shape-edited. When the floor has more than one outer loop, the body has one solid per loop. - Quantities. Qto_SlabBaseQuantities: Width (thickness), Perimeter, GrossArea, NetArea, GrossVolume, NetVolume. - Properties. Pset_SlabCommon: IsExternal, LoadBearing, PitchAngle. - The sketch is stored in RXD element data (sketch).

    Commands. - floor.create(type_id, loops, level_id, offset?, slope?: {line_key|curve, slope} | {arrow: SlopeArrow}, structural?, span_direction_edge?, room_bounding?, attach_walls_below?: bool, join_overlapping_walls?: bool) -> element_id (one element per call, unless the caller passes split_loops = true) - floor.edit_boundary(floor_id, loops, slope?) - floor.set_slope_angle(floor_id, angle)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A floor sketched with Pick Walls and Extend into wall (to core) on has its edges on the walls' core faces. - [ ] A floor with a 1:50 slope arrow 10 m long rises 0.2 m from tail to head, and its layers are perpendicular to the slope. - [ ] Answering Yes to the attach prompt attaches the walls below, and their tops follow the floor's underside.

    3.6.2 Slab edges

    ID: ARC-SLED-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §7.2

    Purpose. Profiles swept along slab edges, such as thickened edges and curbs.

    Workflow. 1. The user starts Floor › Floor: Slab Edge and hovers the horizontal edges of floors (or of toposolids and model lines). A click adds an edge. Edges picked one after another form one mitered run. 2. Restart Slab Edge starts a new run that is not mitered to the previous one. Modify ends the tool.

    Behaviour & rules. - Selected-element tools: Add/Remove Segments, horizontal and vertical flip arrows, and end drag handles. - Instance parameters: Vertical Profile Offset, Horizontal Profile Offset, Angle, Length, Volume, Mark and phasing. - Type parameters: Profile and Material. - Geometry. The profile is placed on the edge's normal plane, with its origin on the edge and its X axis pointing away from the slab. It is offset and rotated by the instance values and swept along the edge chain (BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipeShell). Corners are mitered by bisector planes. - The run cuts its host where the two overlap. This is the default join rule for host sweeps (ARC-MOD-017).

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcSlab with PredefinedType = USERDEFINED and ObjectType = "SLABEDGE", connected to its host through IfcRelConnectsElements. The body is an IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid or a Brep. See Open questions for the alternatives considered.

    Commands. - slabedge.create(type_id, edge_refs: [ref], ...offsets) -> element_id - hostsweep.add_segments(id, edge_refs) - hostsweep.remove_segments(id, edge_refs) - hostsweep.flip(id, axis: Horizontal|Vertical)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A slab edge picked along the four edges of a rectangular floor forms one closed, mitered run, and its volume equals the profile area times the centroid path length within 0.5%.

    3.6.3 Ceilings

    ID: ARC-CEIL-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §7.3

    Purpose. Ceilings at a height above a level, placed automatically in a room or sketched.

    Workflow. 1. The user starts Architecture › Build › Ceiling in a reflected ceiling plan. 2. Automatic Ceiling (default): hovering inside a closed loop of walls highlights the loop, and a click creates the ceiling. Room separation lines are ignored. 3. Sketch Ceiling: the user draws boundary lines (outer loop plus hole loops) and optionally a slope arrow, then presses Finish.

    Behaviour & rules. - Automatic loop detection uses the room-boundary arrangement (ARC-ROOM-002) at the ceiling height (level + offset). Only walls are used, with the area rule fixed to at wall finish. The arrangement face that contains the cursor becomes the boundary. - Slopes work as for floors (slope arrow, two parallel lines with different offsets, or one line that defines slope). A ceiling slopes in one direction only. - Instance parameters: Level, Height Offset From Level, Room Bounding, Slope, Perimeter, Area, Volume, Comments, Mark and phasing. - Types: a Basic Ceiling (one material and a thickness, with no layers) or a Compound Ceiling (Edit Assembly). - Reference. The ceiling's bottom face is at level + offset, and the layers stack upward. - Model pattern alignment. The ceiling's surface pattern (a model pattern from its material) can be selected with Tab and then aligned, rotated or moved. Each face stores the pattern's origin and angle.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcCovering with PredefinedType = CEILING and an IfcCoveringType. The covering is related to the rooms it covers through IfcRelCoversSpaces, computed from the room footprint overlap. A compound ceiling has IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage (AXIS3, POSITIVE). Qto_CoveringBaseQuantities holds Width, GrossArea and NetArea.

    Commands. - ceiling.create_auto(type_id, level_id, point, offset?) -> element_id - ceiling.create(type_id, loops, level_id, offset?, slope?) -> element_id - ceiling.edit_boundary(ceiling_id, loops, slope?) - surfacepattern.align(element_id, face_ref, origin?, angle?)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Clicking inside a room enclosed by four walls creates a ceiling whose edges lie on the walls' interior finish faces. - [ ] Each ceiling exports as IfcCovering(CEILING) with an IfcRelCoversSpaces link to the room it covers.

    3.6.4 Roof by footprint

    ID: ARC-ROOF-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §7.4 · screenshots/architecture/roof_footprint_sketch_mode.png · screenshots/architecture/roof_different_eave_heights_render.png

    Purpose. Pitched, hipped, gabled and flat roofs generated from a plan footprint and per-edge slopes.

    Workflow. 1. The user starts Architecture › Build › Roof › Roof by Footprint in a plan or reflected ceiling plan view. If the active level is the lowest level, Reviera offers to move the roof to the level above. 2. The user draws the footprint with Pick Walls (default), lines or shapes, and optionally slope arrows. Options: Defines slope (applies to each new line), Overhang (Pick Walls) and Extend to wall core. 3. The footprint must be one closed outer loop, with optional inner loops for openings. A triangle symbol marks each slope-defining edge. Edges that do not define slope become gables. 4. On Finish, Reviera offers to attach the walls under the roof.

    Behaviour & rules. - Footprint curve properties: Defines Roof Slope, Slope, Overhang, Plate Offset from Base, Offset from Roof Base, Extend into wall (to core) and Length. - Instance parameters: Base Level, Base Offset From Level, Room Bounding, Related to Mass, Cutoff Level, Cutoff Offset, Rafter Cut (Plumb Cut, Two Cut – Plumb, Two Cut – Square), Fascia Depth (between 0 and the thickness), Rafter or Truss, Maximum Ridge Height (RO), Slope (applied to every slope-defining edge), Thickness (RO), Volume, Area, Comments, Mark and phasing. - Type parameters: Structure, Default Thickness, coarse fill and analytical properties. - Align Eaves (in the sketch): the user selects eave lines and chooses Adjust Height (each edge's plate offset is changed) or Adjust Overhang. Reviera then computes the change for each edge so that all the selected eave lines end at the same height.

    Roof generation algorithm (geometry kernel; runs per roof): 1. Edge data. For each footprint edge e (in counter-clockwise order), let: - L_e be the plate line: the sketch line, offset to the wall's interior face when Rafter or Truss = Truss, or to the exterior face when it is Rafter. The offset is relative to the measured wall face when the edge is locked to a wall; otherwise the sketch line itself is the plate line. - h_e = z_base + PlateOffset_e be the plate height, where z_base = elev(BaseLevel) + BaseOffset. - s_e = tan(slope_e) be the gradient. A gable edge has s_e = ∞. - o_e ≥ 0 be the overhang. 2. Edge planes. Each slope-defining edge carries the plane P_e(p) = h_e + s_e · δ_e(p), where δ_e(p) is the signed horizontal distance from L_e toward the inside of the footprint. Each gable edge carries the vertical plane through L_e. An edge with a slope arrow carries the arrow's plane (ARC-SKCH-003) and is treated as slope-defining with that plane. 3. Eave polygon. Each slope-defining edge line is moved outward by o_e, and its eave height becomes h_e − s_e·o_e. Gable edges are moved outward by their overhang at the same plate height. The eave polygon E is the closed loop of these lines, with consecutive lines intersected. 4. Wavefront propagation (generalised weighted straight skeleton). Reviera treats the roof as a wavefront that rises in z. - At height z, the active edge e is the contour line of P_e at height z: the set of points where P_e(p) = z. For edges that are parallel to their plane's contour, this is the edge line moved inward by (z − h_e)/s_e. For a slope-arrow plane, it is a line perpendicular to the arrow. Gable edges do not move. - Starting from z₀ = min over e of the eave heights, Reviera processes events in increasing z: - edge events: an active edge shrinks to zero length, its two neighbours become adjacent, and a skeleton node is created; - split events: a reflex vertex of the wavefront hits an opposite edge, the polygon splits, and a node is created; - vertex events: several reflex vertices meet at once, which is handled as simultaneous split events, with ties broken by edge index for determinism. - Event times are the solutions of three-plane intersections (P_a ∩ P_b ∩ P_c), solved in f64 with a relative tolerance of 1e-9. Coincident events within TOL_POINT are merged. - Propagation stops when every wavefront component has collapsed, or at the cutoff height z_c = elev(CutoffLevel) + CutoffOffset. At the cutoff, the remaining wavefront polygon becomes a flat top face (or an opening, if the Cutoff option says to leave it open for a second roof). - Each footprint edge e produces one roof face: the region swept by its active edge, which lies on P_e. Gable edges produce vertical gable faces, which become the gable walls' attach target and are not part of the roof's top surface. - Reference implementations. The classic straight-skeleton event algorithm (Aichholzer and Aurenhammer, and its weighted generalisation) and the procedural-extrusion model by Kelly and Wonka (2011) are published references for this approach. Reviera implements it itself in Rust. CGAL's straight-skeleton package is GPL-3.0-or-later and compatible, but it is not a required dependency. - Convex footprints. For a convex footprint with all edges slope-defining and no arrows, the result must equal the lower envelope z(p) = min_e P_e(p). The test suite uses this as a cross-check. 5. Inner loops (openings). Inner loops cut vertical holes through the finished roof. Their edges do not take part in the skeleton. 6. Surface to solid. - The skeleton faces form the roof's reference surface: the underside of the roof at the plate line. - Each layer is the shell between this surface offset by T_{j−1} and by T_j along the face normals (upward). OCCT builds these with BRepOffsetAPI_MakeThickSolid / BRepOffsetAPI_MakeOffsetShape using GeomAbs_Intersection joins, so hip and valley seams stay planar intersections. - Eave cut (the vertical-normal plane through each eave line): - Plumb Cut: the solid is cut by the vertical plane through the eave line. - Two Cut – Plumb: a vertical cut of height Fascia Depth, measured down from the top surface, followed by a horizontal cut. - Two Cut – Square: a cut perpendicular to the roof face of height Fascia Depth, followed by a horizontal cut. - Gable edges get a vertical cut at the eave polygon. - Every cut is a BRepAlgoAPI_Cut with a half-space or with a prism of the cut polygon. 7. Joins. - Join/Unjoin Roof (ARC-ROOF-006) extends this roof's picked edge face until it meets the target roof's face, and Reviera clips it there. - Walls attached to the roof use its underside (ARC-WALL-008). - Roof–roof overlaps that are not joined stay overlapping. Reviera does not merge them silently. 8. Validation. - If the skeleton fails (for example, because of degenerate input), Reviera reports "Roof cannot be generated from this footprint" and names the edges involved. The previous valid geometry is kept. - A slope steeper than 89.9° is an error. - A footprint that is not closed, or that intersects itself, fails sketch validation.

    Regeneration. - Edges into the roof: datum (base and cutoff levels), sketch-lock (picked walls; plan stage only, §3.15) and type. - Edges out of the roof: attach to walls and columns, host to skylights, cut (Join/Unjoin Roof, Dormer), and bound to rooms.

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcRoof with an IfcRoofType aggregates (IfcRelAggregates) one IfcSlab (PredefinedType = ROOF) per skeleton face. Each slab has IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage (AXIS3, POSITIVE from the reference surface) and a body that is an IfcExtrudedAreaSolid along the face normal, clipped by IfcBooleanClippingResult half-spaces for the eave cuts and neighbouring planes. When clipping would need more than eight half-spaces, the body is an IfcFacetedBrep instead. - IfcRoof.PredefinedType is classified from the resolved faces: - all faces horizontal → FLAT_ROOF; - one sloped face → SHED_ROOF; - two opposed faces with gables → GABLE_ROOF; - all footprint edges slope-defining and four or more faces meeting at ridges → HIP_ROOF; - hips combined with gables → HIPPED_GABLE_ROOF; - a cutoff with a flat top over hips → MANSARD_ROOF; - all faces meeting at one apex → PAVILION_ROOF; - otherwise FREEFORM. - Pset_RoofCommon holds IsExternal and ProjectedArea, and Qto_RoofBaseQuantities holds GrossArea, NetArea and ProjectedArea. - The footprint sketch is stored in RXD element data (sketch), and the cut options in RXD element data (recipe.roof).

    Commands. - roof.create_footprint(type_id, loop: [{curve, defines_slope, slope?, overhang?, plate_offset?, offset_from_base?, extend_to_core?, lock_ref?}], holes?, base_level, base_offset?, cutoff?: {level_id, offset}, rafter_cut?, fascia_depth?, rafter_or_truss?, slope_arrows?: [SlopeArrow], attach_walls?: bool) -> element_id - roof.edit_footprint(roof_id, ...) (same parameters) - roof.align_eaves(roof_id, edge_keys, mode: AdjustHeight|AdjustOverhang) - roof.set_slope(roof_id, slope, edge_keys?)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 10 m × 6 m rectangle with all four edges at 30° gives a hip roof whose ridge is 4 m long, at a height of 3·tan 30° = 1.732 m above the plate. - [ ] The same rectangle with the two short edges as gables gives a gable roof whose 10 m ridge is at 1.732 m. - [ ] An L-shaped footprint with all edges at 35° gives a valley along the bisector of the reflex corner. Every face is planar, and the faces meet without gaps within TOL_POINT. - [ ] Edges with different slopes (30° and 45°) on the same rectangle give a ridge that is offset toward the steeper side, matching the analytic result. - [ ] A cutoff at 1.0 m above the plate on a 30° hip produces a flat top face, and PredefinedType = MANSARD_ROOF. - [ ] Two footprint roofs at different plate heights joined with Join/Unjoin Roof reproduce the figure in screenshots/architecture/roof_different_eave_heights_render.png (different eave heights on one building). - [ ] For convex footprints, the faces match the lower-envelope cross-check within 0.01 mm on 1 000 randomly generated cases.

    3.6.5 Roof by extrusion

    ID: ARC-ROOF-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §7.4

    Workflow. 1. The user starts Roof › Roof by Extrusion in an elevation, section or 3D view. 2. The user picks a vertical work plane (Work Plane dialog). 3. In the Roof Reference Level and Offset dialog, the user picks the level (the highest level by default) and an offset. A non-zero offset creates a reference plane at that height. 4. The user sketches an open profile of lines and arcs and presses Finish.

    Behaviour & rules. - Geometry. The open profile wire W is the top surface's section. It is offset downward by the roof thickness: BRepOffsetAPI_MakeOffset with IsOpenResult = true gives the parallel curve, and the two are joined at the ends with perpendicular segments to make a closed face, which is then extruded along the work-plane normal from Extrusion Start to Extrusion End (BRepPrimAPI_MakePrism). - Layers are offset bands of the profile. - The default extrusion depth spans the walls under the profile, or 6 m if there are none. - Instance parameters: Work Plane, Extrusion Start, Extrusion End, Reference Level, Level Offset, Rafter Cut, Fascia Depth, Slope (RO, for straight profiles) and the same identity and phasing parameters as footprint roofs. - The roof can be rehosted with Edit Work Plane.

    Data (IFC mapping). An IfcRoof aggregating one IfcSlab(ROOF) per profile segment (straight segments) or one slab for an arc (curved). Each body is an IfcExtrudedAreaSolid with the closed profile as an IfcArbitraryClosedProfileDef.

    Commands. roof.create_extrusion(type_id, work_plane, profile: [curve], ref_level, level_offset?, start, end) -> element_id.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An arc profile extruded 8 m gives a barrel roof (PredefinedType = BARREL_ROOF) of uniform thickness.

    3.6.6 Roof by face

    ID: ARC-ROOF-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/02 §7.4, §12.1 · web: Create a Roof from a Mass Face; Update Face Selections for Roofs and Curtain Systems

    Purpose. Roofs on free-form surfaces, generated from the faces of a mass or of an in-place or loadable generic model.

    Workflow. 1. The user opens a view that shows the mass (Show Mass must not hide it, ARC-MASS-001) and starts Massing & Site › Model by Face › Roof by Face. 2. The user picks a roof type and, on the contextual tab, the Level (default: the active view's level, or in 3D the highest level at or below the lowest picked face). 3. With Select Multiple on (the default), each click toggles a face in the pick set; the cursor shows + or −. Clear Selection empties the set; Create Roof builds the roof. With Select Multiple off, one click creates a roof on that face at once. 4. Later, Edit Face Selection (Modify | Roofs › Model by Face) re-enters the pick mode with the current faces selected, and Recreate Roof rebuilds the roof from the new set.

    Behaviour & rules. - The user picks non-vertical faces of a mass (Select Multiple, Clear Selection, Create Roof). - Valid faces. Planar or curved faces of masses and generic models whose normal is nowhere horizontal (at every sample point the normal is at least 1° away from the horizontal plane). All faces of one roof must belong to the same mass or generic-model instance ("Faces must belong to one element"). - Picked Faces Location = Top or Bottom of the roof at the face. The roof is offset from the face by its thickness in the matching direction (BRepOffsetAPI_MakeOffsetShape). - One roof cannot mix upward-facing and downward-facing faces. The user can split the mass face first (ARC-MOD-019) and build one roof from each part. - Several faces. Adjacent picked faces form one continuous roof: the layer solids are offset per face and the offset surfaces are intersected at the shared edges, so there is no gap or overlap. Faces that do not touch give one roof element with several disjoint bodies. - Layers. The compound structure is offset layer by layer, normal to the face (ARC-CMPD-001). A type with a variable layer is refused ("Variable layers are not supported for roofs by face"). Slope, Cutoff and Rafter Cut are not available; the slope is whatever the face gives. - Openings and joins. Vertical, by-face and shaft openings (ARC-OPEN-001, ARC-OPEN-002, ARC-OPEN-004) cut it, and walls can attach to it (ARC-WALL-008). Join/Unjoin Roof (ARC-ROOF-006) does not apply. - The roof records Related to Mass and updates only through Update to Face (ARC-MASS-003). - Mass removed. If the mass is deleted, the roof keeps its last geometry, Related to Mass becomes false, and Update to Face and Edit Face Selection are no longer offered.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcRoof (PredefinedType = FREEFORM unless the type says otherwise) aggregating one IfcSlab (PredefinedType = ROOF) per connected body, each with IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage. Curved bodies are written as IfcAdvancedBrep and planar ones as IfcFacetedBrep. The face references and pick location are stored in RXD element data (recipe.roof).

    Commands. - roof.create_by_face(type_id, face_refs, location: Top|Bottom, level_id) -> element_id - element.edit_face_selection(element_id, add?: [face_ref], remove?: [face_ref]) changes the face set of a roof by face or a curtain system by face (ARC-CW-007) and rebuilds it (the Recreate step). - element.update_to_face(element_ids) (ARC-MASS-003).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Mixing an upward-facing face and a downward-facing face in one selection is rejected with a clear message. - [ ] A roof by face on the curved top of a half-cylinder mass, with Picked Faces Location = Bottom, has its underside on the face within TOL_POINT and exports an IfcAdvancedBrep body. - [ ] Adding an adjacent face with Edit Face Selection and Recreate Roof gives one continuous roof with no gap at the shared edge. - [ ] Picking faces of two different masses for one roof is refused.

    3.6.7 Fascia, gutter and soffit

    ID: ARC-ROOF-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §7.4

    Behaviour & rules. - Fascia and Gutter (host sweeps, built as in ARC-SLED-001): - The user picks roof edges, soffit edges, the edges of other fascias, or model lines. Gutters accept horizontal edges only. - Consecutive picks form one continuous mitered sweep. Restart starts a new sweep, and clicking empty space finishes. - Selected sweeps offer Add/Remove Segments, flip, Modify Mitering (Vertical, Horizontal or Perpendicular to the edge), and end handles. - Instance parameters: Vertical Profile Offset, Horizontal Profile Offset, Angle, Length. - Type parameters: Profile, Material. - Gutter end caps are separate families. - Soffit (a sketch): - Pick Roof Edges creates sketch lines locked to the roof's eave edges. - Pick Walls uses the walls' outer faces. - The user trims the lines into a closed loop and presses Finish. - A soffit can be sloped with a slope arrow or line properties, like a floor. - It stays associated with the roof and walls unless it was drawn with plain lines. - Its type has a compound structure.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Fascia: IfcCovering (PredefinedType = USERDEFINED, ObjectType = "FASCIA"). - Gutter: IfcPipeSegment (PredefinedType = GUTTER). - Soffit: IfcCovering (USERDEFINED, ObjectType = "SOFFIT") with IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage. - All three are linked to the roof through IfcRelCoversBldgElements (fascia and soffit) or IfcRelConnectsElements (gutter).

    Commands. - fascia.create(type_id, edge_refs, mitering?) -> element_id - gutter.create(type_id, edge_refs) -> element_id - soffit.create(type_id, loops, level_id, offset?, slope?) -> element_id - hostsweep.set_mitering(id, mode)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A gutter picked along the four eaves of a hip roof forms one continuous mitered sweep, and it exports as IfcPipeSegment(GUTTER). - [ ] A soffit made with Pick Roof Edges follows the eave when the roof overhang changes.

    3.6.8 Slope arrows in roofs

    ID: ARC-ROOF-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §7.4 · web: Slope Arrow Properties

    Purpose. Slope a roof plane from an edge that is not slope-defining, so that gables, dormers and planes whose fall is not perpendicular to an edge can be modelled in one footprint.

    Workflow. 1. In the footprint sketch (Edit Footprint), the user clears Defines Roof Slope on the edge that should be driven, splitting it first with Split Element if only part of it should be. 2. The user chooses Draw › Slope Arrow and clicks the tail (snapped onto that edge) and then the head (inside the footprint). 3. In the Properties palette the user sets Specify and its values (ARC-SKCH-003). The Length is read-only. 4. Finish Edit Mode regenerates the roof.

    Behaviour & rules. - Values. Specify = Height at Tail uses Level at Tail, Height Offset at Tail, Level at Head and Height Offset at Head; the slope is (head height − tail height) / arrow length in plan. Specify = Slope uses Level at Tail, Height Offset at Tail and Slope. The defaults are the roof's base level, an offset equal to the edge's Plate Offset from Base, and the roof type's default slope. Negative offsets are allowed. - Placement rules. The tail must lie on a boundary edge (within TOL_POINT), and that edge must not be slope-defining; the head must lie inside the footprint or on its boundary. A zero-length arrow, an arrow whose head equals its tail, or a Height at Tail arrow with equal heights over a gable edge is reported on Finish ("Slope arrow does not define a slope"). - Several arrows on one edge. Each arrow drives the portion of the edge between its tail and the nearest split points; two arrows on the same unsplit edge are an error ("Only one slope arrow per edge segment"). - Interaction with cutoff. The cutoff level (ARC-ROOF-001) clips arrow-driven planes as it clips any plane. - A slope arrow is placed on a footprint edge that is not slope-defining (ARC-SKCH-003). Typical uses: - four-sided gable: an arrow from a gable edge to the ridge; - dormer without side walls: split a footprint line twice, clear the slope-defining flag of the middle segment, and draw two arrows from its ends to its midpoint; - tapered ramps and slabs. - In the skeleton, the arrow's plane replaces the edge's plane (ARC-ROOF-001, step 2). - Different eave heights on one building are modelled as two roofs at different plate heights, using cutoff levels, joined with Join/Unjoin Roof. - Floors and ceilings use the same arrow element (ARC-SKCH-003); there it tilts the whole slab, and at most one arrow is allowed per slab.

    Data (IFC mapping). Arrows are sketch curves with role slope_arrow in RXD element data (sketch); their values are per-curve properties. The resulting planes are part of the explicit roof body.

    Commands. In a sketch session, sketch.add_curve(session_id, Line{tail, head}, role: "slope_arrow", props: {specify, level_tail, offset_tail, level_head?, offset_head?, slope?}) -> curve_key and sketch.edit_curve for later changes; non-interactively, the slope_arrows: [SlopeArrow] parameter of roof.create_footprint and roof.edit_footprint (ARC-ROOF-001).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A dormer made with two arrows from the ends of a 3 m segment to its midpoint, rising 1 m, gives two triangular faces that meet the main roof faces without gaps. - [ ] On a 10 × 6 m footprint with only the two long edges slope-defining, an arrow from the middle of one short edge to the ridge with Specify = Slope 30° turns that gable into a hip plane at 30°. - [ ] An arrow whose tail is not on a boundary edge, or that sits on a slope-defining edge, is reported on Finish and the sketch stays open.

    3.6.9 Join/Unjoin Roof

    ID: ARC-ROOF-006 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §7.4, §9

    Workflow. The user starts Modify › Geometry › Join/Unjoin Roof, picks the edge of the roof to extend, and then picks the face of the roof or wall to join to.

    Behaviour & rules. - The picked edge's face plane P_e is extended until it meets the target surface. The extended face is then clipped by the target's surface (BRepAlgoAPI_Splitter), and the part beyond is removed. - Targets: any roof face, or a wall face (for wall targets, only footprint roofs can be joined). A roof with several top faces cannot be a target. - Join Geometry must not be used for dormers. - Unjoin restores the edge's original termination. - The relation is a cut / attach edge from the target to the joined roof.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcRelConnectsElements (Name "JoinRoof"), with the relation stored in RXD document model/constraints.
