Switching volumes off makes every room's Volume read "Not Computed". - [ ] A door in a bounding wall does not merge the rooms on its two sides. - [ ] A 300 × 300 mm column inside the room reduces the area by 0.09 m² and adds 1.2 m to the perimeter. - [ ] A separation line that stops 1 m short of the opposite wall leaves a single room, and the area does not change. - [ ] With the computation height set to 1.2 m, one bounding wall slanted 10° outward increases the area by approximately 1.2·tan 10° × that wall's length (ignoring corner effects), compared with a computation height of 0. - [ ] A room under a sloped ceiling that bounds it has a volume equal to the analytic prism-minus-wedge value within 0.1%. - [ ] Moving one wall recomputes only the rooms on that wall's levels. An unrelated level is not recomputed; this is measured by an instrumentation counter.

    3.9.3 Areas and area plans

    ID: ARC-AREA-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §10.1 (Area Schemes), §10.2

    Purpose. Areas defined per scheme (for example gross, rentable or a regulatory scheme), each with its own boundaries and rules.

    Workflow. 1. Manage the schemes in Area and Volume Computations › Area Schemes (create, rename, delete). The defaults are Gross Building and Rentable. 2. Room & Area › Area › Area Plan opens a dialog: Type (scheme), levels (multi-select), Do not duplicate existing views, and Scale. Reviera then asks whether to create area boundary lines automatically along the closed loops of exterior walls. (Curtain systems must be sketched by hand.) 3. Area Boundary (Room & Area › Area): Draw, or Pick Lines with Apply Area Rules (the line's position follows the area-type rules; an area must be placed before its type is known) or with an Offset. Picked boundaries follow their walls; drawn ones are fixed. 4. Area tool: Tag on Placement, orientation, Leader, and Area: New or Unplaced. A click inside boundaries places an area. An area can be placed unbounded and bounded later. 5. Areas are made visible through V/G › Area › Interior Fill and Reference (DOC chapter).

    Behaviour & rules. - Area boundary computation. This is ARC-ROOM-002 steps 4–8, with the candidates replaced by the scheme's area boundary lines on the level. Walls and columns are not used directly. - Area types and rules. Each scheme has area types. A rule table maps the pair of area types on the two sides of a picked boundary to a boundary position: exterior face, interior face, wall centreline, face toward side A or B, or glass line. Defaults for the two built-in schemes: - Gross Building: Gross Building Area ↔ outside → the exterior face. Exterior Area ↔ Gross Building Area → the exterior face. Exterior Area ↔ Exterior Area → the wall centreline. - Rentable: Office ↔ Office → the centreline. Office ↔ Exterior → the face on the office side. Office ↔ Building Common → the centreline. Store ↔ any → the centreline. Major Vertical Penetration ↔ any → the face on the penetration side. When a window is taller than 50% of the wall height, the boundary moves to the glazing plane of the window (the "glass line"). - The rule table is editable per scheme and stored in RXD document model/rooms. - Dynamic boundaries. A picked boundary with Apply Area Rules is recomputed whenever its wall moves or the area type on either side changes. - Areas can be tagged (Tag Area), unplaced and deleted like rooms. Area schedules are per scheme.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Each area is an IfcSpace: PredefinedType = GFA for the Gross Building scheme and USERDEFINED (ObjectType = the scheme name) for other schemes. It is aggregated under the storey and marked as an area (not a room) by a property value. - Each scheme is an IfcZone (ObjectType = "AreaScheme") whose members (IfcRelAssignsToGroup) are that scheme's areas. - Area boundary lines are IfcVirtualElement (4X3: BOUNDARY) with the scheme recorded as a property. - Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities.GrossFloorArea holds the area.

    Commands. - areascheme.create(name, description?) -> id - areascheme.set_rules(scheme_id, rules: [{type_a, type_b, position}]) - areaplan.create(scheme_id, level_ids, scale, auto_boundaries?: bool) -> [view_id] - areaboundary.create(view_id, curves | picks: [ref], apply_rules?: bool, offset?) -> [element_id] - area.place(view_id, point, area_type?, name?, number?) -> element_id - area.unplace(ids)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A Gross Building area plan created with automatic boundaries has its boundary on the exterior faces of the exterior walls, and the area equals the building footprint. - [ ] In the Rentable scheme, two Office areas separated by a 200 mm wall share a boundary on the wall centreline. Changing one of them to Exterior Area moves the boundary to the office-side face.

    3.9.4 Colour schemes

    ID: ARC-CLR-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §10.3 · screenshots/architecture/room_color_scheme_by_value.png · screenshots/architecture/room_color_scheme_by_range.png

    Purpose. Colour rooms, areas, spaces, zones and MEP elements by the value of one of their parameters.

    Workflow. 1. Room & Area › Color Schemes (or selecting a colour fill legend and choosing Edit Scheme) opens the Edit Color Scheme dialog: - Category: Rooms, Areas (per scheme), Spaces, HVAC Zones, Ducts or Pipes; - Schemes: Duplicate, Rename or Delete; - Title; - Color: the parameter to colour by; - By value or By range; - the rows table: Value, Visible, Color, Fill Pattern, Preview and In Use; - Include elements from links. 2. By range rows have At least (editable), Less than (RO, derived from the next row), Caption and Edit Format. 3. Apply. The view property Color Scheme, with Color Scheme Location = Background or Foreground, applies the scheme. Placing a Color Fill Legend (Annotate › Color Fill › Legend; DOC chapter) also applies it. Schemes work in plans and sections.

    Behaviour & rules. - By value. The row list is the set of distinct values of the parameter among elements of the category in the project (plus links, when included). Rows for values that no longer exist stay, marked as not In Use. New values get a colour from a pastel palette by default: Reviera's palette, the HSV wheel at saturation 0.35 and value 0.95, assigned by golden-ratio hue steps. - By range. Rows are sorted by At least, and an element falls in the row with the largest At least ≤ its value. Units follow the parameter. - An element whose value is not in a visible row is not coloured. - Graphics. The fill draws the element's footprint (rooms and areas: Ω from ARC-ROOM-002) with the row's colour and pattern. In sections it draws the cut of the room solid. - Legend. Type properties: swatch size, font, title text, opaque or transparent background, and Values Displayed = By View (only the values present in the view) or All.

    Data (IFC mapping). Scheme definitions are stored in the RXD views documents (DOC chapter). When the IFC export option Export colour fills as styles is set, the colour of each room's FootPrint is also written as an IfcStyledItem in the plan annotation context.

    Commands. - colorscheme.create(name, category, parameter, mode: value|range, ranges?) -> scheme_id - colorscheme.set_rows(scheme_id, rows: [{value | at_least, color, pattern?, visible, caption?}]) - colorscheme.duplicate(scheme_id, name) -> id - view.set_color_scheme(view_id, category, scheme_id? (none clears), location?: background|foreground) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Colouring by Department with five departments produces five rows, each with a distinct colour. Renaming one room's department to a new value adds a sixth row automatically. - [ ] Colouring by Area with ranges at 0, 10, 20 and 50 m² puts a 20.0 m² room in the 20–50 row.

    3.10 In-place models, model text and model lines

    3.10.1 Model In-Place

    ID: ARC-INPL-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §11.1

    Purpose. Unique, free-form elements modelled in the context of the project.

    Workflow. 1. The user starts Architecture › Build › Component › Model In-Place (it is also on the Structure and Systems tabs). 2. The user picks a category in the Family Category and Parameters dialog. The category decides where the element appears in the Project Browser and how it is scheduled, shown and exported. The user then gives it a Name. 3. The in-place family editor opens inside the project. Other elements are shown in half-tone but can still be snapped to. The available tools are: - solid forms: Extrusion, Blend, Revolve, Sweep and Swept Blend; - void forms of the same five kinds; - Model Line, Component, Model Text, Opening, Reference Line and Reference Plane; - Set Work Plane; - Family Types (parameters) and Category & Parameters; - Cut Geometry and Join Geometry with project elements. 4. Finish Model (or Cancel Model).

    Behaviour & rules. - An in-place family has exactly one type. Copying an in-place instance creates a new in-place family, because each in-place instance is unique. - Room bounding, hosting and attaching all work for in-place elements: - elements in the Walls, Floors, Roofs and Ceilings categories can be room-bounding; - in-place walls can host doors and windows; - walls can attach to in-place roofs and floors. - Form geometry in OCCT: - Extrusion: BRepPrimAPI_MakePrism of the sketch face between the start and end offsets. - Blend: BRepOffsetAPI_ThruSections between the base and top sketches, with vertex mapping set by the user. - Revolve: BRepPrimAPI_MakeRevol about the axis line, between the start and end angles. - Sweep: BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipeShell of the profile along a sketched or picked path. - Swept Blend: BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipeShell with two profiles and a law. - Voids are subtracted from all solids of the same family, and from project elements given in Cut Geometry pairs. - Edit In-Place re-opens the editor.

    Data (IFC mapping). - The occurrence uses the IFC class of its category (for example, Walls → IfcWall, Roofs → IfcRoof, Casework → IfcFurniture, Generic Models → IfcBuildingElementProxy). It has a unique IfcTypeProduct of the matching type class. - Body. It is written as CSG wherever IFC4 can express it: - IfcExtrudedAreaSolid (extrusion); - IfcRevolvedAreaSolid (revolve); - IfcExtrudedAreaSolidTapered (blends with matching topology); - IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid (sweeps); - IfcBooleanResult DIFFERENCE (voids).

    Any other form is written as an IfcAdvancedBrep or IfcFacetedBrep. - The form recipe is stored in RXD document families/<id>, flagged as in-place.

    Commands. - inplace.begin(category, name) -> session_id - inplace.add_form(session_id, kind: Extrusion|Blend|Revolve|Sweep|SweptBlend, solid: bool, params) -> key - inplace.finish(session_id) -> element_id - inplace.cancel(session_id) - inplace.edit(element_id) -> session_id

    All family-editor commands from the DM chapter can be used inside the session.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An in-place wall made from an extrusion can host a door, and it bounds rooms. - [ ] Copying an in-place element produces a second family with a new name, and editing one copy does not change the other.

    3.10.2 Model text

    ID: ARC-MTXT-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §11.2

    Workflow. 1. The user sets the work plane. 2. The user starts Architecture › Model › Model Text and enters multi-line text in the Edit Text dialog. 3. The preview follows the cursor, and a click places the text.

    Behaviour & rules. - Instance parameters: Work Plane, Text, Horizontal Align (Left, Center or Right), Material, Depth (0 means flat, which is recommended for performance), Comments, Mark and phasing. - Type parameters: Text Font, Text Size, Bold and Italic. - Model text is edited with Edit Text, moved and rotated like any element, and rehosted with Edit Work Plane. - Glyph geometry. The glyph outlines are taken from the font through FreeType (FTL/GPL-2.0+ dual licence; Reviera uses it under the GPL-2.0+ option, which is compatible). The quadratic and cubic contours become B-spline wires. They are built into faces, with holes found by contour orientation and nesting, and extruded by Depth (BRepPrimAPI_MakePrism). Text with Depth 0 is a set of planar faces.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Depth > 0: IfcBuildingElementProxy (ObjectType = "ModelText") whose body is an IfcPolygonalFaceSet of the tessellated glyphs, or Brep when the export precision is set to high. - Depth = 0: IfcAnnotation with an IfcTextLiteralWithExtent in a 3D annotation context, plus a tessellated IfcAnnotationFillArea copy. - In both cases the text, font and alignment are stored as property values.

    Commands. modeltext.create(text, work_plane, point, type_id, h_align?, material_id?, depth?) -> element_id and modeltext.set_text(element_id, text).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] The text "ABC" at depth 50 mm produces a solid with three lumps. The "A" has an enclosed hole.

    3.10.3 Model lines

    ID: ARC-MLIN-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §11.3

    Workflow. 1. The user starts Architecture › Model › Model Line (LI) and chooses a Line Style on the Line Style panel. Line style is not available for sketch lines. 2. The user draws with any shape from the Draw gallery. The options are Placement Plane (a level or plane from the list, or Pick…), Chain, Offset and Radius. 3. Listening dimensions work for length, radius, ellipse radii and polygon size.

    Behaviour & rules. - Model lines are 3D curves, lying on work planes, and visible in every view. By contrast, detail lines (DOC chapter) belong to a single view. - Convert Lines (Modify | Lines) turns model lines into detail lines and back. - Model lines can be picked with Pick Lines when placing walls, gutters, fascias and slab edges.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcAnnotation (ObjectType = "ModelLine"; in 4X3, PredefinedType = USERDEFINED) whose Annotation representation is a 3D curve (IfcPolyline, IfcTrimmedCurve or IfcBSplineCurveWithKnots), styled with the line style (IfcStyledItem with IfcCurveStyle). The work plane is stored in RXD element data (placement).

    Commands. modelline.create(curves: [curve], work_plane, line_style_id?) -> [element_id] and line.convert(element_ids, to: Model|Detail, view_id?) -> [element_id].

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A model line drawn on Level 1 appears in the floor plan, in elevations and in 3D. Converting it to a detail line in the plan removes it from the other views.

    3.11 Massing and site

    3.11.1 Masses

    ID: ARC-MASS-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/02 §12.1 · web: Control Visibility of Mass Instances

    Purpose. Conceptual volumes for early design and for model-by-face.

    Workflow. 1. On the Massing & Site tab, the Show Mass drop-down sets how masses are displayed (see Show Mass below). 2. In-Place Mass: the user names the mass, and the conceptual design environment opens. 3. The user draws profiles (lines, reference lines, points, arcs and splines, closed or open), selects them and chooses Create Form (Solid or Void). Reviera infers the form from the selection:

    Selection Form OCCT construction
    One closed loop Extrusion BRepPrimAPI_MakePrism
    Profile plus a coplanar axis line Revolve BRepPrimAPI_MakeRevol
    Path plus one profile Sweep BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipeShell
    Path plus several profiles Swept blend BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipeShell with sections
    Stacked closed profiles Loft BRepOffsetAPI_ThruSections(solid=true)
    One open profile Surface BRepPrimAPI_MakePrism of the wire (a face)
    1. Editing tools: a 3D gizmo that drags faces, edges and vertices; X-Ray (shows the defining profiles and path); Add Edge; Add Profile; Dissolve (back to profiles); and Rebuild. Divide Surface (UV grids, patterns and adaptive components) is P3 (see Deviations).
    2. Finish Mass.
    3. Place Mass inserts loadable mass families.

    Behaviour & rules. - Join masses (Join Geometry) to remove overlapping volume from the gross figures. - Show Mass. Mass is a model category that is hidden by default in new views. The Show Mass drop-down has four modes: - by View Settings (default): masses and their subcategories (Form, Mass Floor, pattern lines) display as each view's Visibility/Graphics settings say. This is the only mode that affects printing and export. - Form and Floors: mass forms and mass floors display in every view, even where the Mass category is off, so that the user can work with them without changing views. Printing, export and view templates still follow the view settings. - Surface Types and Zones and Shades: display mass surfaces, or energy-analysis zones and shading surfaces, so that they can be selected and given energy settings. Both are available only after an energy model has been created (ANA chapter); otherwise they are disabled with a tooltip saying why. The mode is session state of the project window, not model data: it is not saved, is not part of undo, and other users and BIMserver clients do not see it. When view_id is given, the mode applies to that view only until the view is closed, which lets scripts render a view with masses without changing the user's global mode. - Masses in views. A mass that is hidden by the current mode cannot be selected; model-by-face tools (ARC-MASS-003) switch the mode to Form and Floors for their duration and restore it afterwards. - Instance parameters: Gross Floor Area, Gross Surface Area, Gross Volume, Mass Floors (levels), Phase, Design Option and Workset.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcBuildingElementProxy (ObjectType = "Mass", 4X3 PredefinedType = USERDEFINED) with an IfcAdvancedBrep body. The form recipe is stored in RXD document families/<id>. Masses are excluded from the default IFC export view (Export masses option, off by default).

    Commands. - mass.begin_inplace(name) -> session_id - mass.create_form(session_id, curve_refs: [ref], solid: bool) -> key - mass.edit_form(session_id, key, op: MoveSub{ref,vector}|AddEdge|AddProfile|Dissolve|Rebuild) - mass.finish(session_id) -> element_id - mass.place(type_id, point, rotation?, level_id?) -> element_id - mass.show(view_id?, mode: by_view_settings|form_and_floors|surface_types|zones_and_shades) -> () sets the Show Mass mode (display setting, not undoable)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Selecting three stacked closed profiles and choosing Create Form produces a lofted solid, and its gross volume matches an independent OCCT calculation. - [ ] In a plan view whose Mass category is off, Form and Floors shows the mass and lets it be selected; printing that view to PDF does not include the mass; switching back to by View Settings hides it again and leaves the undo stack unchanged.

    3.11.2 Mass floors

    ID: ARC-MASS-002 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/02 §12.1 · web: Create Mass Floors; About Mass Floors at the Top of a Mass; About Mass Floors at the Bottom of a Mass

    Purpose. Slice a mass at project levels to get floor areas, perimeters, façade areas and volumes per storey for early design analysis, and to drive Floor by Face.

    Workflow. 1. The user selects one or more masses in any view and chooses Modify | Mass › Model › Mass Floors. 2. The Mass Floors dialog lists every story and reference level with a checkbox, sorted by elevation, plus Select All and Select None. With several masses selected, a box that differs between them shows as indeterminate; leaving it so keeps each mass's own choice. 3. OK creates, keeps or deletes mass floors to match the ticks, in one transaction.

    Behaviour & rules. - The user selects a mass and chooses Mass Floors, then ticks the levels. - For each ticked level L, Reviera computes the planar section of the mass at elev(L) (BRepAlgoAPI_Section), builds faces from it, and creates a mass floor. - Ticked levels that miss the mass are remembered but produce no floor. If the mass is later changed so that it crosses such a level, the floor appears automatically; if it stops crossing, the floor disappears (and comes back when it crosses again). Mass floors, unlike elements by face, always follow their mass. - Levels added later that cross the mass get mass floors automatically when the mass has all levels selected. - Top and bottom. No mass floor is created at a level that coincides (within TOL_POINT) with a top face of the mass, because nothing lies above it. A floor is created at a level that coincides with the bottom face. Any part of the mass below the lowest mass floor is not counted in any mass floor's figures; the mass's own Gross Volume and Gross Surface Area still include it. - Properties: Floor Perimeter, Floor Area, Exterior Surface Area (the mass's side surface between this level and the next), Floor Volume (the mass volume between this level and the next), Level, Usage and Mark. - Band definition. "The next" level is the next ticked level above that crosses the mass, or the top of the mass. The topmost floor's Exterior Surface Area therefore also includes the roof faces of the mass above it, and can be noticeably larger than the floors below. The bottom face of the mass is never part of any floor's exterior surface area. - Several section loops. A level that cuts the mass into separate islands gives one mass floor whose area is the sum of the islands; holes are subtracted. - Joined masses (Join Geometry) are sliced as their union, so overlapping volume is counted once. - Usage is a free-text instance parameter used for grouping in schedules. Mark is user-set. - Mass floors can be scheduled and tagged. - Deleting a level deletes its mass floors; unticking a level in the dialog deletes the mass floor and any tag on it after a warning. Floors made from a mass floor (Floor by Face, ARC-MASS-003) are not deleted; they lose their link.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcSpace (PredefinedType = GFA, ObjectType = "MassFloor") aggregated under the storey, with Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities. (GrossFloorArea, GrossPerimeter, GrossVolume; the exterior surface area is written as a property value.) The ticked levels (including those that currently miss the mass) are stored in the mass instance's RXD element data (elements). Mass floors are exported only with the Export masses option (ARC-MASS-001).

    Commands. mass.set_floors(mass_id, level_ids | All).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 20 × 30 × 12 m box mass with levels every 3 m creates four mass floors of 600 m² each, and each has a floor volume of 1800 m³. - [ ] With a level at the top face of that mass also ticked, no fifth floor is created, and the fourth floor's exterior surface area is 300 m² (sides) + 600 m² (roof) = 900 m². - [ ] Ticking a level 3 m above the mass creates nothing; stretching the mass to 15 m creates the floor at that level without reopening the dialog.

    3.11.3 Model by face and Update to Face

    ID: ARC-MASS-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/02 §4.1, §12.1

    Behaviour & rules. - Wall by Face (non-horizontal faces; options Level, Height and Location Line), Floor by Face (picks mass floors), Roof by Face (ARC-ROOF-003) and Curtain System by Face (ARC-CW-007) all work the same way: with Select Multiple (on by default), the user clicks faces to add or remove them, can use Clear Selection, and then chooses Create. - The new elements record Related to Mass and do not update automatically. Selecting one and choosing Update to Face regenerates it from the current face. Update to Face has no effect on walls with explicit top constraints, and it discards sketch edits. - Select elements based on a mass selects the dependent elements again. - Implementation. Each element stores (mass GlobalId, face sub-reference). Face sub-references are named from the form recipe (for example #face:extrusion1.side3) and stay stable while the recipe's topology is unchanged. When a face cannot be resolved, Update to Face reports "Face no longer exists".

    Commands. - wall.create_by_face(type_id, face_refs, level_id, location_line, height?) -> [element_id] - floor.create_by_mass_floor(type_id, mass_floor_ids) -> [element_id] - element.update_to_face(element_ids) - mass.select_dependents(mass_id) -> [element_id] (query)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] After the mass is stretched, Update to Face makes a wall by face match the new face. Before Update to Face, the wall stays unchanged.

    3.11.4 Toposolid

    ID: ARC-TOPO-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §1 (2024, 2026), §12.2 · screenshots/architecture/toposolid_site_plan_and_3d.png · web: Toposolid Smooth Shading; Toposolid Enhancements (2025)

    Purpose. A solid, layered terrain element that can be shape-edited, sub-divided, excavated, split and graded, and that can host site elements.

    Workflow. - Create from Sketch (Massing & Site › Model Site › Toposolid): 1. Sketch a closed boundary and Finish. 2. Use Shape Editing › Add Point (Along Surface or Absolute; Elevation Base = Current Level, Project Base Point, Survey Point or Internal Origin; Elevation). 3. Use Modify Sub Elements to drag points (blue arrow for vertical, red square for horizontal) or type elevations. - Create from Import: from 3D points or contour polylines in an imported or linked DWG, or from a points file (CSV or TXT: x, y, z with a header-row option). The number of points is capped by the setting toposolid.max_points (default 20 000, allowed range 10 000–50 000). For linked civil topography, toposolid.link_max_points applies. Above the cap, Reviera simplifies the points (ARC-TOPO-005) before triangulating and reports what it did. - Link Topography: linked civil surfaces (LandXML and IFC4X3 IfcGeographicElement/terrain). Linking is covered in the COL chapter.

    Behaviour & rules. - Geometry. The top surface is a TIN: a CDT of the boundary vertices, points and split lines (ARC-SHAPE-001), with heights taken from the points. - Boundary vertices that have no point take their height from the nearest triangle of the surrounding points, extrapolated linearly if needed. If there are no points at all, they take level + offset. - The solid is built from: the top TIN; the vertical side faces along the boundary; and a flat bottom at z_bot = min(top) − Σ layer thicknesses, or at the type's Default Thickness below the level if that is lower. - Layers: the topmost layers follow the top surface (offset straight down). The type's variable layer, which is the core by default, absorbs the varying depth. The layers below the variable layer are flat, parallel to the bottom. - OCCT builds the top as a shell of triangular faces sewn with the side and bottom faces (BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing, then BRepBuilderAPI_MakeSolid). - Hosting. Site components, parking components, railings, floor-based families and slab edges (curbs) can be hosted on the surface. - Surface pattern comes from the top layer's material. - Instance parameters: Level, Height Offset from Level, Room Bounding, Curved Edge Condition, Perimeter, Area, Volume (after cuts and excavations), Elevation at Top, Elevation at Bottom and phasing. - Type parameters: Structure (layers), Default Thickness, coarse fill, Contour Display (ARC-TOPO-004), Structural Material and thermal properties. - Display. Folding lines (the TIN edges) are hidden by default (V/G › Toposolid › Folding Lines) and are always suppressed while the toposolid is being shape-edited, so the contours stay readable; contours remain visible during editing when the view and the type show them. - Smooth shading (Massing & Site › Model Site › Toposolid Smooth Shading, a toggle): - When on, every toposolid in the project is drawn with per-vertex normals averaged over the adjacent top triangles (weighted by triangle angle), so the faceted TIN reads as a continuous surface. Side and bottom faces and sharp creases (dihedral angle above 30°, split lines and sub-division boundaries) keep hard normals. - It applies in the shaded visual styles (Shaded, Consistent Colors, Textures, Realistic). Hidden Line and Wireframe are unchanged, and contours, cut patterns and dimensions are unaffected because the geometry is unchanged. - Limitations while it is on: surface (model and drafting) patterns are not drawn on toposolid tops, decals cannot be placed on toposolids, and paint and graphic overrides of toposolid materials are not shown. The toggle's tooltip lists these. - It is a project-wide display setting stored in RXD document project/settings (site.smooth_shading, default off). It is not part of undo. Image, glTF and OBJ exports write the smoothed normals when it is on; IFC geometry is never smoothed.

    Regeneration. Edges out of the toposolid: host to the elements on it; cut from cutting and excavating elements into it (ARC-TOPO-002). Sub-divisions read the parent's surface.

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcGeographicElement (PredefinedType = TERRAIN, an IFC4 enumeration value), contained in IfcSite. - Body: an IfcPolygonalFaceSet (closed), or an IfcFacetedBrep for IFC4 consumers that do not support face sets. - IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage (AXIS3, NEGATIVE). - When the export option Site geometry on IfcSite is set, the top TIN is also written as the IfcSite's Body (an open IfcTriangulatedFaceSet), because many viewers expect terrain there. The option is on by default when there is exactly one toposolid. - The points, split lines and settings are stored in RXD element data (recipe.toposolid).

    Commands. - toposolid.create(type_id, boundary: loop, level_id, offset?, points?: [xyz], split_lines?: [[xyz]]) -> element_id - toposolid.create_from_import(type_id, source: ImportRef(element_id) | File(path), level_id, max_points?) -> element_id - toposolid.toggle_smooth(on? (default: toggle)) -> () switches smooth shading for the project (display setting, not undoable) - the shape.* commands (ARC-SHAPE-001)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A toposolid created from a CSV of 5 000 points produces a TIN with every point as a vertex. Its volume matches an independent prism-sum calculation within 0.1%. - [ ] Importing 60 000 points with the default cap produces at most 20 000 vertices, and the user is told about the simplification. - [ ] The IFC export opens in an independent viewer with the terrain visible, both under the IfcSite and as an IfcGeographicElement. - [ ] Turning smooth shading on changes the shaded display of every toposolid without changing its volume, contours or IFC body, and does not add an undo step; with it on, a toposolid's surface pattern is not drawn.

    3.11.5 Sub-divisions, split and excavation

    ID: ARC-TOPO-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §1 (2026), §12.2, §12.3 · screenshots/architecture/toposolid_subdivision_road.png · web: Merge Toposurfaces (2016); What's New in Revit Site Planning and Design 2024

    Behaviour & rules. - Sub-Divide (Modify | Toposolid › Toposolid Shaping): 1. The user sketches a region and chooses a sub-division toposolid type and a Sub-divide Offset: positive raises it, negative excavates the host, 0 is flush. 2. Geometry. The parent's TIN is clipped to the region. The region boundary is inserted as constraints, with heights sampled from the parent's surface, and the result is lifted by the offset to form the sub-division's top. Its layers come from its own type. - For offset > 0, the sub-division sits on the parent: its bottom is the parent's surface. - For offset < 0, the parent loses the volume between its surface and the sub-division's top within the region (BRepAlgoAPI_Cut of the parent with a prism from the lowered top up to the parent's top). The Excavation Volume is that volume. 3. The sub-division follows the parent's later edits. Edit Sketch changes the region. - Split Element on a toposolid: the user sketches a closed loop inside it, or an open chain whose two ends touch the boundary. The result is two independent toposolids, each keeping its own points. Sub-divisions that cross the split line stay with the part that holds the larger share of their area. Sub-divisions that lie wholly within a removed region are deleted, and the user is notified. - Excavate / Remove Excavation: - A floor, roof, building pad or another toposolid that intersects the host excavates it. - The cut tool is the cutter's solid plus a vertical prism of its plan footprint from the cutter's bottom up past the host's top. This is what lets a basement slab remove the soil above it. - The host's volume updates. Excavation is a cut edge. - Robustness. Reviera does not jitter void positions. It relies on OCCT's fuzzy Booleans (OCCT_FUZZY) and retries once with a fuzzy value 10× larger before reporting "Excavation failed". See Deviations. - Cut Geometry / Join Geometry with floors, walls, foundations and similar elements uses the general rules (ARC-MOD-016, ARC-MOD-017). - Merge Toposolids (Modify | Toposolid › Toposolid Shaping › Merge; see D16). It reverses a split and joins terrain pieces into one element: 1. The user selects two or more toposolids (or starts the tool and picks them one after another, then Finish). An option Remove points on common edges (on by default) is on the contextual tab. 2. Conditions. The toposolids must be on the same level, in the same phase and design option, and of the same type; in plan, their boundaries must share at least one edge segment longer than TOL_SHORT or overlap. Toposolids that only touch at a point, or are apart, are refused ("Toposolids must overlap or share an edge"). A different type is refused with the two type names; the user changes one first. 3. Result. The first picked toposolid survives and keeps its GlobalId, type, parameters and phase; the others are deleted. Its boundary becomes the union of the plan outlines (holes where the outlines enclose a gap). Its points are the union of all points; where two inputs overlap, the points of the first picked one win and the others' points inside the overlap are dropped. With Remove points on common edges on, points that lie on the former shared boundary (within TOL_POINT) and are not needed to keep the surface's height there within 1 mm are removed; this cleans up the extra points a split inserts. 4. Dependants. Sub-divisions, excavations, cuts, joins, graded-region links and hosted elements (site components, parking, railings, slab edges) of the deleted toposolids are moved to the survivor. Dimensions and tags that referenced deleted toposolids are removed and listed. 5. The merge is one undo step. In IFC the survivor keeps its IfcGeographicElement; the deleted ones disappear.

    Data (IFC mapping). - A sub-division is an IfcGeographicElement(TERRAIN) aggregated under its parent (IfcRelAggregates). - An excavation is written as an IfcOpeningElement in the host (IfcRelVoidsElement). In IFC4X3 the excavated soil is also written as an IfcEarthworksCut, when the IFC4X3 schema is selected. - The excavation volume is stored as a property value.

    Commands. - toposolid.subdivide(toposolid_id, loops, type_id, offset) -> element_id - toposolid.split(toposolid_id, curves: [curve]) -> [element_id] - toposolid.excavate(toposolid_id, cutter_ids) - toposolid.remove_excavation(toposolid_id, cutter_ids?) - toposolid.merge(toposolid_ids, remove_common_points?: bool = true) -> element_id returns the surviving toposolid (the first in the list)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A road sub-division with offset −0.3 m over a 100 m² flat region reports an excavation volume of 30 m³. - [ ] A 10 × 10 m basement floor with its top 3 m below a flat terrain removes 300 m³ plus the floor's own volume from the toposolid. - [ ] Splitting a toposolid with an open chain and merging the two parts again restores one element with the original GlobalId, the original volume within 0.1%, and no extra points on the former split line. - [ ] Merging two toposolids that touch only at a corner, or that use different types, is refused and changes nothing.

    3.11.6 Graded region

    ID: ARC-TOPO-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/02 §12.2

    Workflow. 1. The user starts Massing & Site › Modify Site › Graded Region and chooses either Create a new toposolid exactly like the existing one or based on perimeter points only. 2. The user picks a toposolid from an existing phase. 3. Reviera demolishes the original in the current phase (Phase Demolished = current phase) and creates a copy (Phase Created = current phase). The copy has either all the original points or only the perimeter points. 4. The user shape-edits the copy.

    Behaviour & rules. - Cut and fill. Selecting the graded toposolid shows Cut, Fill and Net cut/fill. Reviera computes them against the demolished original: 1. Overlay the two TINs in plan: take the union of their vertices and edges and build a CDT. 2. In each resulting triangle τ, Δz = z_new − z_old is linear. If Δz changes sign inside τ, split τ along the zero line. 3. Fill = Σ ∫_τ max(Δz, 0) and Cut = Σ ∫_τ max(−Δz, 0). Both are exact for piecewise-linear surfaces (triangle area × mean Δz on each part). Net = Fill − Cut. - The link between the original and the graded copy is stored in RXD element data (recipe.toposolid).

    Commands. toposolid.create_graded_region(toposolid_id, mode: Copy|PerimeterOnly) -> element_id and toposolid.cut_fill(toposolid_id) -> {cut, fill, net} (query).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Lowering one interior point by 1 m on a graded copy of a flat 20 × 20 m toposolid, triangulated so that the point's star covers 100 m², reports Cut = 33.33 m³ and Fill = 0.

    3.11.7 Contours, labels and site settings

    ID: ARC-TOPO-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §1 (2025), §12.2, §12.3 · web: Control Contour Display on Toposolids; Video: Configure Site Settings; Toposurface Settings; Property Line Data Settings

    Purpose. Contour lines and labels on toposolids, and the project-wide site settings that give contour defaults, section graphics for terrain and the angle format of property lines.

    Workflow. 1. Per type: select a toposolid › Edit Type › Contour Display › Edit… opens the Contour Display dialog for that type. 2. Project-wide: Massing & Site › Model Site panel › dialog launcher (Site Settings) opens the Site Settings dialog. 3. Labels: Massing & Site › Modify Site › Label Contours, then draw a line across the contours in a plan view.

    UI. - Contour Display dialog (type). A checkbox Use site settings for primary contours (on for new types) and a table of additional rows. Each row has: visible (checkbox), Start, Stop, Interval, Range Type (Single Value or Multiple Values), Subcategory (a Topography line subcategory, for example Primary or Secondary Contours). Buttons Insert, Delete, Up and Down. With Range Type = Single Value only Start is used. Validation: Interval > 0 for Multiple Values, Stop ≥ Start, and at most 10 000 contour heights per row ("Too many contours; increase the interval"); errors show inline and block OK. - Site Settings dialog (project), three groups: - Contour Line Display: At intervals of (checkbox and length, default 1 m or 5' in imperial templates), Passing through elevation (default 0, measured from the project's elevation base), and an Additional Contours table with the same columns as above. These are the primary contours of every type that uses site settings. - Section Graphics: Section cut material (default: the template's earth material) and Elevation of poché base (default −10 m). The material is the default for the core layer of new toposolid types and of types that Generate Toposolid creates (ARC-TOPO-006); surface-only imported terrain that has not been converted is drawn in sections as a fill of this material from the surface down to the poché base. - Property Data: Angle display: Degrees from N/S (bearings such as N 45°00'00" E, the default) or Degrees (a 360° azimuth clockwise from north); Units: Degrees-minutes-seconds (default) or Decimal degrees. They apply to the property-line table (ARC-SITE-001) and to property-line tags. - Validation: interval > 0, poché base below the lowest toposolid bottom (a warning, not an error, if it is not). OK applies everything as one undoable transaction; Cancel discards.

    Behaviour & rules. - Contour Display (a type property; dialog). Rows have Start, Stop, Interval, Range Type (Single Value or Multiple Values), Subcategory and visibility. There is one row set for primary contours and one for secondary contours. - Contour heights. With site settings in use, the primary heights are z = e0 + k·i for every integer k, where i is the interval and e0 the passing-through elevation (for i = 10 and e0 = 5: …, −15, −5, 5, 15, …). The type's rows add more heights. A height produced by several rows is drawn once, with the subcategory of the last row in the list. - Contour generation. Each triangle of the top TIN is sliced at every contour height z_k with a linear interpolation along its edges. The segments are chained into polylines, and closed contours are detected. Contours are recomputed lazily, per view, when they are displayed. - Contours are drawn on the top surface of toposolids and sub-divisions whose type shows them; a sub-division's type decides its own contours. They are not drawn on excavated or cut faces. - Label Contours (Modify Site): the user draws a label line, and labels are placed where that line crosses each contour. The labels are view annotation (DOC chapter). - V/G controls contours per view. - Changing site settings or a type's contour rows regenerates the contours of all affected toposolids in open views at once.

    Data (IFC mapping). Contours are not written to IFC (they are derived). The type's rows are stored in RXD type data of the toposolid type (params); the site settings are stored in RXD document project/settings (section site). Contour labels are view annotation (DOC chapter).

    Commands. - toposolidtype.set_contours(type_id, rows) and contour.label(view_id, line: Line, label_type_id?) -> element_id. - site.settings() -> () opens the Site Settings dialog (UI only). - site.set_settings(contour_interval?: f64 | None, passing_elevation?, additional_contours?: rows, section_material_id?, poche_base_elevation?, angle_display?: Bearing|Azimuth, angle_units?: DMS|Decimal) -> () applies the same values without the dialog.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A plane tilted 10% over 50 m with a 1 m contour interval shows five contours, evenly spaced 10 m apart. - [ ] With an interval of 10 m and a passing-through elevation of 5 m, a terrain from −20 m to +20 m shows contours at −15, −5, 5 and 15 m only. - [ ] Switching Angle display to Degrees shows a property-line segment previously listed as N 90°00'00" E as 90°, in the table and in its tag, without changing the geometry. - [ ] A Contour Display row with Interval 0 and Range Type Multiple Values blocks OK with an inline error.

    3.11.8 Simplify surface

    ID: ARC-TOPO-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §1 (2024), §12.2 · web: Simplify Topography

    Purpose. Reduce the number of points of a dense terrain (typically an import) so that editing, regeneration and navigation stay fast, while keeping the surface within a stated vertical error.

    Workflow. 1. The user selects one toposolid and chooses Modify | Toposolid › Shape Editing › Simplify. 2. The Simplify Toposolid dialog shows the current point count and offers either Target number of points (default: half the current count) or Maximum vertical error (default 50 mm). A Preview button computes the result and shows the resulting point count and the actual maximum vertical deviation; the view shows the simplified surface in a temporary overlay. 3. OK applies the result; Cancel discards the preview.

    Behaviour & rules. - Simplify Topography reduces the number of points to a target count, or to a vertical tolerance. - Algorithm. Greedy decimation: repeatedly remove the interior vertex whose removal changes the surface least (the vertical error of re-triangulating its star), using a priority queue, until the target is met. Boundary and split-line vertices are never removed. Points carrying a "locked" flag (for example, survey benchmarks) are never removed either. - Error measure. The vertical error of a removal is the largest |Δz| between the old and new surfaces at the removed vertex and at the vertices removed earlier inside the affected star, so the error is tracked against the original points, not only against the previous step. The reported maximum deviation is that tracked value. - Limits. The target cannot go below the number of protected vertices (boundary, split-line and locked) plus one; a lower request stops at that number and says so. A toposolid with fewer than 50 interior points cannot be simplified ("Nothing to simplify"). - Dependants. Sub-divisions, graded-region links, excavations and hosted elements regenerate on the new surface; hosted elements keep their (x, y) and take the new surface height. Cut and fill of a graded region (ARC-TOPO-003) changes accordingly and is recomputed. - The simplification is one undoable step. - Imports. Create from Import uses the same algorithm when an import exceeds the point cap (ARC-TOPO-001).

    Data (IFC mapping). The remaining points replace the old ones in RXD element data (recipe.toposolid); the body is regenerated. The tolerance used and the reported deviation are recorded in the element's RXD data for traceability.

    Commands. toposolid.simplify(toposolid_id, target_points? , max_vertical_error?); exactly one of the two must be given ("Specify a target or a tolerance, not both"). The command returns nothing; the resulting count and deviation are reported in the result message.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Simplifying a 20 000-point terrain to 5 000 points keeps the maximum vertical deviation at or below the reported value, and the boundary is unchanged. - [ ] Simplifying with a maximum vertical error of 0 removes only points that lie exactly on the plane of their neighbours, so a perfectly planar terrain is reduced to its boundary vertices plus one point. - [ ] Locked survey points are still present after simplifying to the minimum.

    3.11.9 Legacy toposurface and building pad

    ID: ARC-TOPO-006 · Priority: P3 · Ref: research/02 §1 (2024), §12.3 · web: Generate a Toposolid from a Toposurface

    Purpose. Bring surface-only terrain from other tools into the toposolid model without supporting the legacy element kinds themselves.

    Workflow. 1. On IFC import (or link-and-bind), Reviera detects surface-only terrain and lists it in the import report with a Generate Toposolid action. The user can also select such an element later (it is imported as a non-parametric element) and choose Modify › Generate Toposolid. 2. A dialog asks for the Base level (default: the level nearest below the surface's lowest point) and the Toposolid type (default: the project's default toposolid type). 3. OK creates the toposolid. The source surface stays in the model, unchanged, until the user deletes it.

    Behaviour & rules. - Reviera does not create surface-only terrains or building pads. Open alternative: a toposolid, plus a floor that excavates it. - On IFC import, a terrain that is a surface without thickness (an open TIN on IfcSite or an IfcGeographicElement) is offered for conversion with Generate Toposolid: a base level and type dialog, non-destructive, with the original kept as a reference until it is deleted. - Sub-regions (separate surface patches with other materials) become sub-divisions. - Site components are rehosted onto the new toposolid if they can be. Otherwise they are listed. - Railings are rehosted automatically. - Detection. A surface-only terrain is an IfcSite Body or an IfcGeographicElement(TERRAIN) whose representation is an open shell (IfcTriangulatedFaceSet with Closed = FALSE, an open IfcShellBasedSurfaceModel, or an IfcTriangulatedIrregularNetwork in IFC4X3). - Conversion. The surface's vertices become toposolid points, and its outer boundary (the free edges, chained) becomes the boundary loop. Inner free-edge loops become holes. Triangles are kept by inserting their edges as split lines only where the CDT of the points would differ by more than TOL_POINT, so the top matches the source. - Sub-regions. Each differently-styled patch becomes a sub-division with offset 0 and a new toposolid type named after the patch's material, with the material on its top layer and the default thickness. A patch with more than 100 boundary loops, or whose loops cannot be closed, is skipped and listed (for example a striped crossing modelled as one patch). - Pads. An imported IfcSlab(BASESLAB) that is flagged as a pad (its ObjectType or a pad property says so) becomes an ordinary floor that excavates the generated toposolid (ARC-TOPO-002). - Point cap. If the surface has more vertices than toposolid.max_points, it is simplified first (ARC-TOPO-005) and the user is told.

    Data (IFC mapping). The new toposolid is an ordinary IfcGeographicElement(TERRAIN) (ARC-TOPO-001). The link to the source surface is stored in its RXD element data (recipe.toposolid) until the source is deleted.

    Commands. toposolid.generate_from_surface(surface_element_id, type_id, level_id) -> element_id.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An IFC file with a TIN on IfcSite converts to a toposolid whose top matches the TIN within TOL_POINT. - [ ] A terrain with two differently styled patches produces one toposolid with two flush sub-divisions, each with its own new type. - [ ] The source surface is still present after conversion, and deleting it does not change the toposolid.

    3.11.10 Site components, parking and property lines

    ID: ARC-SITE-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §12.4

    Behaviour & rules. - Site Component (Model Site): trees (planting), entourage and site furniture. The user picks a type and clicks to place. Each component is hosted on the toposolid (its height is the surface height at the insertion point) or on a level. - Parking Component: placed on a toposolid or on a sub-division road. Parking components are usually arrayed. Pick New Host rehosts them, and they keep sitting on the surface when moved. - Property Line (Modify Site): - Create by sketching expects a closed loop. An open loop gives a warning that no area can be computed. - Create by entering distances and bearings uses a table. Each row has Distance, Bearing (N or S, degrees-minutes-seconds, E or W), Type (Line or Arc), Radius and L/R, with Insert, Delete, Up and Down. The user then clicks to place the result. Bearings are relative to True North (the project's site rotation). - A sketched property line can be converted to the table form. - Property lines report their area and can be tagged. - Surface hosting means that whenever the surface changes, the component's Z is set to the surface height at its (x, y) plus its offset.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Site components: the IFC class follows their category (planting → IfcGeographicElement, 4X3 VEGETATION; site furniture → IfcFurniture; entourage → IfcBuildingElementProxy), contained in IfcSite. - Parking components: IfcBuildingElementProxy (ObjectType = "Parking") or, when the family is flagged as a parking space, IfcSpace(PARKING). - Property lines: IfcAnnotation (ObjectType = "PropertyLine") contained in IfcSite, with an Annotation curve. Their area is written as a property, and the bearings table is stored in RXD element data (recipe.property_line).

    Commands. - sitecomponent.place(type_id, point, host_id?, rotation?) -> element_id - propertyline.create(loops | table: [{distance, bearing, kind, radius?, side?}], origin?) -> element_id - propertyline.to_table(element_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A property line entered as a table with four rows (N 0°E 30 m, N 90°E 20 m, S 0°E 30 m, S 90°W 20 m) closes and reports 600 m². - [ ] A tree on a toposolid moves up 1 m when the surface under it is raised 1 m.

    3.12 Modify tools

    These tools are on the Modify tab and are repeated on every Modify | <Element> contextual tab. All of them support both invocation orders (ARC-TOOL-001). Their options sit on the contextual tab and are remembered for the session. The common rules in ARC-MOD-000 apply to all of them.

    3.12.1 Common rules for modify operations

    ID: ARC-MOD-000 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §13 (Edge cases), §15.2, §17.12

    Behaviour & rules. - Pins. A pinned element cannot be moved, rotated, mirrored, scaled or deleted by a user operation. Trying gives "Element is pinned", and the command fails. Implicit moves still apply to pinned elements, because those changes come from the element's dependencies: following a host, a level change, Moves With Nearby Elements, or an array or group regeneration. - Constraints. Every geometric modification is applied to the target elements and then run through the constraint solver (ARC-CNST-002). - If satisfying the constraints needs other elements to move, they move too. For example, a locked alignment drags its partner. - If the constraints cannot be satisfied, the transaction is rolled back, and the "Constraints are not satisfied" dialog offers Remove Constraints (deletes the conflicting constraints and retries) or Unjoin Elements (where joins conflict). - Hosting. Hosted inserts move only along their host unless the command has disjoin = true. - 3D views. Rotate and Mirror in a 3D view work in the active work plane. The work plane must be set first. - Mirroring a family instance sets its read-only Mirrored flag (it can be scheduled and filtered). On hosted doors and windows, mirroring can flip hand or facing; Reviera stores the resulting hand and facing explicitly. - Groups. Modifying a member of a group instance outside the group editor is refused. The user is pointed to Edit Group (ARC-GRP-002). - Copy and Copy to Clipboard. Copy keeps elements on the same level and in the same view. Pasting to other levels is done with Paste Aligned (ARC-MOD-021). - Option memory. Tool settings (Multiple, Copy, Disjoin, Constrain, Graphical or Numerical, joint gap, Delete Inner Segment, array options, Prefer) are kept for the session and can be stored in the user settings.

    3.12.2 Modify tool requirements

    ID Tool Priority Shortcut Behaviour Commands
    ARC-MOD-001 Align P0 AL Options: Multiple Alignment (or hold Ctrl), Lock, Prefer (Wall faces, Wall centerlines, Faces of core or Center of core). The user picks the reference first, then the element edge, face or line that should move. The element is translated (or, for curves such as wall ends, extended) so that the picked geometry becomes coplanar or collinear with the reference. Lock creates an alignment constraint (ARC-CNST-002). Tab cycles references. Works in plan, elevation and 3D. Also aligns surface-pattern lines and extends wall or beam ends element.align(reference_ref, target_refs: [ref], lock?: bool)
    ARC-MOD-002 Offset P0 OF Graphical or Numerical (value), and Copy (Ctrl toggles it). Hovering an element or chain (Tab selects a chain of the same family) previews a parallel copy on the cursor side; a click creates it. Graphical mode picks a point, drags and accepts a listening dimension. Works for lines, walls, beams and braces. Walls are offset by their location line element.offset(element_ids, distance, side_point, copy: bool) -> [element_id]
    ARC-MOD-003 Mirror – Pick Axis / Draw Axis P0 MM / DM Copy (on by default). Pick Axis takes an existing line, reference plane, grid or wall face. Draw Axis takes a temporary two-point axis. Elements are reflected through the vertical plane that contains the axis (in plan), or through the plane through the axis that is perpendicular to the work plane (in 3D). Inserts can be mirrored without their hosts if a valid host lies at the mirrored position element.mirror(element_ids, axis: Line | ref, copy: bool) -> [element_id]
    ARC-MOD-004 Move P0 MV Constrain (orthogonal or along the element only), Disjoin, and Multiple. The user clicks a start point and an end point, or types a distance. Disjoin breaks joins and hosting: a hosted insert can move to another host, which gives it a new GlobalId, resets its Mark and loses its dimension references. Arrow keys nudge the selection by the zoom-dependent increment, and Shift+arrow by ten times that. Dragging moves too, with snapping element.move(element_ids, vector, disjoin?: bool) -> [element_id]
    ARC-MOD-005 Copy P0 CO / CC Copies the selection by a vector, staying in the same level and view context. Select first, or start the tool, select and press Enter. Options: Constrain (orthogonal directions only, or along the element when one linear element is selected), Disjoin (a copied hosted insert may land on another host, which it then joins; without it the copy stays on the source host and the vector is projected onto that host) and Multiple (after each destination the tool asks for another, each measured from the same base point, until Esc). The user picks a base point, then destinations, or types distances (ARC-DIM-002). Copies get new GlobalIds and the next free Mark; joins and constraints among copied elements are copied, those to uncopied elements are dropped. Copies stay on the source's level even when the destination lies at another level's height (use Paste Aligned, ARC-MOD-021). Pinned elements can be copied, and their copies are not pinned. A copied group member is refused outside the group editor element.copy(element_ids, vectors: [vector]) -> [[element_id]] (one inner list per destination, one undo step for all)
    ARC-MOD-006 Rotate P0 RO (R3 sets a new centre) Disjoin, Copy, Angle (typed; enabled after the first ray), Center of rotation: Place or Default. The centre control starts at the selection's bounding-box centre; the user can drag it, click it and pick, press Spacebar and pick, or use Place. The user clicks a first ray and a second ray, or types an angle. The axis is normal to the view (in 3D, normal to the work plane). Walls cannot be rotated in elevation. Hosted inserts cannot be rotated away from their wall element.rotate(element_ids, center: point, angle, axis?: vector, copy?: bool) -> [element_id]
    ARC-MOD-007 Trim/Extend to Corner P0 TR The user clicks two elements, each on the part to keep; Tab cycles overlapping candidates. Both curves are trimmed or extended to their intersection (for arcs, the intersection nearer to the click points). Works for walls (location lines; the end joins are re-solved into an L join), model and detail lines, beams and braces. Both elements must lie in the same plane (the plan, or the same work plane). Parallel elements give "Elements do not intersect" and nothing changes. Inserts that end up outside a trimmed wall are deleted after a warning. Pinned elements and group members are refused (ARC-MOD-000). The tool stays active for more pairs until Esc; each pair is one undo step element.trim_corner(a: (element_id, keep_point), b: (element_id, keep_point))
    ARC-MOD-008 Trim/Extend Single P0 — The user picks the boundary first: a line, wall face or location line, reference plane, grid, level (in elevation) or model edge; Tab cycles candidates. Then the user picks the element to change. If it crosses the boundary or its extension, the part on the clicked side is kept and the rest is removed; if it stops short, its nearer end is extended to the boundary. The boundary never changes and stays active, so more elements can be picked until Esc or until another trim mode is chosen (which clears the picks). Valid targets: walls, lines, beams, braces and MEP curves. An element parallel to the boundary is refused ("Element cannot be trimmed or extended to the boundary"). Joins at the moved end are re-solved element.trim_extend(boundary_ref, target: (element_id, keep_point))
    ARC-MOD-009 Trim/Extend Multiple P0 — The user picks a boundary, then clicks or box-selects targets. A crossing window (dragged right to left) selects the elements it touches. Works for walls, lines, beams, braces, ducts, pipes, conduit and cable tray. A window dragged left to right takes only elements fully inside it. For boxed elements, the kept part is the one on the side of the boundary where the box was started; for clicked elements, the clicked side. Elements that cannot reach the boundary (parallel, or in another plane) are skipped and listed in the status bar. Each click or box is one undo step. The same pin, group and join rules as Trim/Extend Single apply element.trim_extend_multiple(boundary_ref, targets: [(element_id, keep_point)])
    ARC-MOD-010 Split Element P0 SL Delete Inner Segment. Works for walls (ARC-WALL-011), lines, beams, MEP curves (MEP chapter: inserts unions or couplings according to routing preferences) and toposolids (by sketch, ARC-TOPO-002). A click on the element divides it there into two elements of the same type and parameters; with Delete Inner Segment the user clicks two points and the piece between them is removed. The original GlobalId stays with the piece that contains the start point. Hosted elements go to the piece that contains their insertion point; dimensions to the new ends are not created and dimensions spanning the cut keep their references. A click within TOL_SHORT of an end does nothing ("Element too short"). Walls can also be split horizontally in elevation and 3D (ARC-WALL-011). Pinned elements and group members are refused (ARC-MOD-000) element.split(element_id, point, delete_inner?: point2) -> [element_id]
    ARC-MOD-011 Split with Gap P1 — Joint Gap, between 1.6 and 305 mm. Works for walls, structural framing and columns. A click removes a gap of that width centred on the click point and leaves two elements; for structural columns the cut is horizontal (in elevation, section or 3D). The new ends get Disallow Join and a locked dimension that records the gap; the joint is closed by unlocking the dimension, allowing the joins and dragging the ends together. A value outside the range is refused with the range in the message; the last value is remembered for the session (default 20 mm). Not available for curtain walls, stacked walls, or slanted walls cut by a vertical plane. Hosted inserts that fall inside the gap are deleted after a warning element.split_with_gap(element_id, point, gap) -> [element_id]
    ARC-MOD-012 Scale P1 RE Graphical (origin, then two vectors whose length ratio is the factor) or Numerical (factor). Scaling is proportional about the origin. Only these elements can be scaled: walls (curve only; thickness unchanged), lines, images, imported CAD, reference planes and dimension positions. If any selected element cannot be scaled, the tool is disabled element.scale(element_ids, origin, factor)
    ARC-MOD-013 Pin / Unpin P0 PN / UP The pushpin control toggles the pin. Activate Controls (Modify | Multi-Select › Selection) shows pushpins on a large selection. Type-driven curtain grids and mullions are pinned automatically, and unpinning one makes it independent. A pinned element cannot be moved, rotated, mirrored, scaled, flipped or deleted by the user ("Element is pinned") but still follows implicit changes (host, level, Moves With Nearby Elements, arrays, groups; ARC-MOD-000). Clicking the pushpin unpins (the pushpin shows a red cross) and clicking again re-pins in the new position. Unpin also works from the tool (UP) on a selection. The Select Pinned Elements toggle can make pinned elements unselectable (ARC-SEL-001). Elements already in the requested state are ignored. The pin state is saved with the element and is undoable element.pin(element_ids), element.unpin(element_ids)
    ARC-MOD-014 Delete P0 DE / Del Deletes without using the clipboard. Cascades (hosted inserts, a level's views and hosted elements, group members) are listed in a confirmation dialog before commit. Deletes fail on pinned elements (ARC-MOD-000). The dependants collected also include openings, parts (ARC-PART-003), and dimensions and tags whose references disappear; the dialog lists them by category with counts and offers Delete or Cancel. With confirm_dependents = false (scripts and MCP) the cascade happens without asking and the result lists it. Deleting a placed room in a view unplaces it (ARC-ROOM-001). Deleting the last member of a group instance deletes the instance. Elements in links and members of group instances outside the group editor cannot be deleted element.delete(element_ids[], confirm_dependents?=true) -> element_ids[] (everything deleted, dependants included)
    ARC-MOD-015 Match Type Properties P1 MA A paintbrush cursor: the user clicks the source, then targets of the same category. Only the type is copied. Select Multiple lets the user box-select and then Finish. Esc once empties the brush; Esc twice exits. Works across tiled views, and a type in the Project Browser can be the source element.match_type(source_id, target_ids)
    ARC-MOD-016 Cut Geometry / Uncut P1 — Multiple Cut. The user picks the element to be cut, then the cutting element. Allowed pairs: toposolid, floors, ceilings, roofs, slab edges, fascias, gutters, soffits, walls, wall sweeps, structural foundations and mass voids; family voids flagged Cut with Voids When Loaded cut hosts. Creates a cut edge, and BRepAlgoAPI_Cut runs at regeneration. Stored in RXD document model/constraints, and in IFC as IfcRelInterferesElements (InterferenceType = "Cut", ImpliedOrder = TRUE) geometry.cut(target_id, cutter_ids), geometry.uncut(target_id, cutter_ids?)
    ARC-MOD-017 Join Geometry / Unjoin / Switch Join Order P0 — Multiple Join. Joining removes the visible edge between the elements and gives them a shared cut-pattern display. One element cuts the other, according to this precedence table: walls cut columns (architectural); structural elements cut non-structural hosts; floors, ceilings and roofs cut walls; gutters, fascias and slab edges cut their hosts; otherwise the first element picked cuts the second. Switch Join Order swaps them. The material of the first pick is applied to both in the merged cut display. In IFC: IfcRelConnectsElements (Name "JoinGeometry") plus IfcRelInterferesElements for the cut direction geometry.join(a_id, b_ids), geometry.unjoin(a_id, b_ids?), geometry.switch_join_order(a_id, b_id)
    ARC-MOD-018 Wall Joins P0 — Modify › Geometry › Wall Joins: hover a join (its node is marked by a square) and click it, or window-select several nodes. The contextual tab then offers Butt, Miter and Square Off (L joins only), Previous / Next to cycle which wall runs through (one node only), Display (Use View Setting, Clean Join, Don't Clean Join) and Allow / Disallow Join. Changes apply immediately and the tool stays on the node until Esc. Options that do not suit the selected nodes are disabled. The geometry rules, join limits and IFC mapping are in ARC-JOIN-001 wall.join_set_type(node_ref \| wall_end_refs, type: Butt\|Miter\|SquareOff), wall.join_cycle_order(node_ref, step: +1\|-1), wall.join_set_display(node_ref, display: ViewSetting\|Clean\|DontClean), wall.set_join_allowed(wall_id, end: Start\|End, allowed: bool)
    ARC-MOD-019 Split Face P1 SF The user picks a face (Tab cycles), sketches a closed loop inside it or an open chain ending on its edges, and presses Finish. The face is divided into regions that can be painted separately. The element's structure is unchanged. Not available on arc or elliptical walls. Deleting a split region removes it. Family instances (except columns) must be split in the family editor. OCCT: BRepFeat_SplitShape with the projected sketch edges face.split(face_ref, curves: [curve]) -> [face_key]
    ARC-MOD-020 Paint / Remove Paint P1 PT The Material Browser is available while Paint is active. The user hovers a face (Tab cycles) and clicks to apply a material. The status bar shows existing paint. Works on walls, floors, roofs, masses, columns and in-place families. Does not work on loadable component instances. Painting a face that has a model pattern makes the pattern lines dimensionable and alignable. Paint is stored per face sub-reference in RXD element data (paint), and exported as an IfcStyledItem on the faces, which IFC supports only per representation item: Reviera splits the painted faces into their own IfcFacetedBrep item when exporting face.paint(face_refs, material_id), face.remove_paint(face_refs)
    ARC-MOD-021 Copy, Cut and Paste (clipboard) P0 Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V The Paste menu offers: Paste from Clipboard (enters paste mode, where the elements can be moved before Finish or Cancel); Aligned to Selected Levels (a searchable multi-select list); Aligned to Selected Views (view-specific elements; similar view types only); Aligned to Current View; Aligned to Same Place (also between design options, worksets and models that share coordinates); and Aligned to Picked Level (elevation views: pick a level line). The clipboard holds an IFC fragment plus its RXD element data, so pasting between Reviera instances works clipboard.copy(element_ids), clipboard.cut(element_ids), clipboard.paste(mode: Free(vector)|Levels([id])|Views([id])|CurrentView|SamePlace|PickedLevel(id)) -> [element_id]
    ARC-MOD-022 Create Similar P0 CS Starts the placement tool for the selected element's type, with its instance parameters as the New defaults. For walls the height properties are copied, and the top constraint is adapted to the active level. Esc twice exits. Exactly one element must be selected (also from the context menu). Only parameters that the family or system element defines are copied (dimensions, offsets, heights, hosting and placement options); user parameters such as Comments and Mark are not. For walls these are Base Offset, Unconnected Height, Top/Base Extension Distance, Top Constraint and Top Offset; on another level the top constraint moves the same number of levels up. Slanted walls copy only their type. The defaults hold until the user changes the type in the Type Selector. Not available for elements without a placement tool (groups, links, imports, in-place families): "Create Similar is not available for this element" tool.create_similar(element_id)
    ARC-MOD-023 Measure P0 — Between Two References and Along Element. A temporary read-out; no element is created. Between Two References: click a start point or reference and an end point or reference (snaps apply; SP measures perpendicular to the target); the read-out shows the distance and, in plan and elevation, the angle from horizontal. In 3D views Ctrl constrains the second point to the plane through the first point perpendicular to the view direction. Option Chain: each click adds a segment, the status bar keeps a running total, and a double-click ends the chain. Along Element: click a wall, model line, beam or MEP curve (Tab takes a chain) to show its length; it is not available in 3D or for detail lines. Read-outs stay until the next measurement; Esc once clears, twice exits measure.between(ref_a, ref_b) -> {distance, dx, dy, dz, angle?} (query), measure.along(element_id) -> length (query), measure.chain(points: [point]) -> {segments: [f64], total} (query)
    ARC-MOD-024 Demolish P1 — A hammer cursor: each clicked element gets Phase Demolished = the view's phase, and its graphics follow the phase filter. Undone by setting Phase Demolished to None. Elements that can be demolished highlight on hover. The change is model data, so the element shows as demolished in every view of that phase. Elements created after the view's phase, or already demolished in an earlier phase, are refused with a status-bar message. Hosted inserts are demolished with their host. Nothing is deleted or unhosted, and rooms in later phases recompute without the element. Linked elements and annotation cannot be demolished. Esc or Modify exits; each click is one undo step element.demolish(element_ids[], phase_id? (default: the active view's phase), view_id?) -> ()
    ARC-MOD-025 Linework P1 LW A view-specific override of the line style of model edges. Specified in the DOC chapter. The user picks a line style on the contextual tab (including Invisible lines, and By Category to remove an override) and clicks edges, Tab cycling between coincident edges; dragging an edge's end controls limits the override to part of the edge. It works on projected and cut edges in plan, section, elevation and orthographic 3D views. The element itself is unchanged, and an override is dropped with a warning when its edge disappears (DOC-GFX-007) view.set_linework(view_id, edge_refs[], line_style_id?) (DOC)
    → ARC-MOD-026 Array P0 AR ARC-MOD-026 below element.array_linear, element.array_radial, array.set_count
    ARC-MOD-027 Repeat last command P0 RC / Enter Re-runs the last tool with its options. Enter repeats only when no tool is active and nothing is being edited; RC and the context-menu item Repeat [tool name] always repeat. The repeated tool starts with the options it had when it ended (Multiple, Copy, Disjoin, joint gap, and so on) and the same type, but with no selection, so select-first tools ask for a selection. Commands run from Lua or MCP are not recorded as "last"; view-navigation and selection commands are not either. After a session tool (sketch, group editor) the repeat starts a new session. If the last tool is unavailable in the current view, the status bar says so tool.repeat_last() -> session_id

    Acceptance criteria (modify tools). - [ ] Align with Lock between a wall face and a grid keeps the wall on the grid when the grid moves 1 m. - [ ] Moving a pinned wall with element.move fails with "Element is pinned", and the model is unchanged. Moving its base level still moves it. - [ ] Move with Disjoin from wall A to wall B rehosts a window, and its GlobalId changes. - [ ] Rotating four walls about a placed centre by 30° keeps every join between them. - [ ] Trim/Extend to Corner on two non-touching walls produces an L join with no gap. - [ ] Paste Aligned to Selected Levels (Levels 2–5) creates four copies, each based on its own level. - [ ] Join Geometry between a floor and a wall makes the floor cut the wall, and Switch Join Order reverses that. - [ ] Mirror with Copy of a right-handed door produces a left-handed door with Mirrored = true.

    3.12.3 Array

    ID: ARC-MOD-026 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §1 (2026), §13

    Workflow. - Options: Linear or Radial, Group and Associate, Number (including the original), Move To: 2nd or Last, Constrain, Angle (radial), and the centre of rotation (Place is the default for radial arrays). - Linear: click the start, then the second member (Move To: 2nd) or the last member (Move To: Last), or type a distance. - Radial: place the centre, pick the start ray, then pick the end ray or type an angle.

    Behaviour & rules. - Without Group and Associate, the copies are independent elements. - With Group and Associate: - Each member is a model-group instance of an automatically created group type (ARC-GRP-001), and the array is an array set that records the base vector or angle, the count, the Move To mode and the members. - Selecting the array shows an editable count label. - Changing the count with Append to End keeps the spacing and adds or removes members at the end. With Append to End off, the endpoints stay fixed and the spacing is redistributed (only when the array was created with Move To: Last). - Dimensions between array members can be given a parameter label (DOC chapter). - Detail elements and model elements cannot be arrayed together. - Regeneration. The array set is a node with group edges to its members. Changing the count adds or removes group instances in one transaction.

    Data (IFC mapping). Each member is an IfcGroup (ARC-GRP-001). The array set is an IfcGroup with ObjectType = "ArraySet" whose members are the member groups (IfcRelAssignsToGroup). The parameters are stored in RXD document model/groups.

    Commands. - element.array_linear(element_ids, vector, count, move_to: Second|Last, group_and_associate: bool, constrain?: bool) -> array_id | [element_id] - element.array_radial(element_ids, center, angle, count, move_to: Second|Last, axis?, group_and_associate: bool) -> array_id | [element_id] - array.set_count(array_id, count, append_to_end: bool)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A linear array of 5 chairs at 0.8 m, with Group and Associate on, can be changed to 7 by editing the count label, and the spacing stays 0.8 m. - [ ] A radial array of 8 columns over 360° (Move To: Last, 360°) places the columns 45° apart without duplicating the first one.

    3.13 Groups

    3.13.1 Group types and instances

    ID: ARC-GRP-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §14, §17.13

    Purpose. Reusable sets of elements whose instances stay identical.

    Workflow. - Create. The user selects elements and groups and chooses Create › Create Group (GP), enters a name, and optionally opens the group in the editor. Architecture › Model › Model Group › Create Group creates an empty group in the editor. - Place. Architecture › Model › Model Group › Place Model Group, or Annotate › Detail Group › Place Detail Group, or dragging from the Project Browser (Groups › Model or Detail), or right-click › Create Instance.

    Behaviour & rules. - Kinds: - model groups (model elements, which may include rooms); - detail groups (view-specific elements); - attached detail groups (a detail group bound to a model group for one view kind: plan, or section/elevation; never 3D).

    A group cannot mix model and detail elements. Selecting both and choosing Create Group makes a model group plus an attached detail group. - Dimensions, tags and keynotes can only be grouped together with the elements they refer to. Otherwise they go into an attached detail group. - Origin. A group has an origin with three drag controls: the centre moves the origin, and the arm ends rotate it about Z. When placing or pasting, the cursor holds the origin. Swapping the type keeps the origin's position. - Instance parameters: Reference Level, Origin Level Offset (the group's height above its level; unhosted components may not follow), Mirrored (RO), phase and similar. - Type operations: Duplicate, Rename and Swap (with the Type Selector). On swap, attached detail groups with the same name are mapped automatically and dependent references are re-targeted. Where that cannot be done, Reviera warns. - Nested groups are allowed and are selected with Tab. - Implementation model. - A group type holds a template: member elements in the group's local frame, each with a stable member key. - Each instance is a transform plus a set of excluded member keys. - Each instance's members are real elements with their own GlobalIds, created and regenerated from the template. They are linked by group edges. - Editing the template re-creates or updates the members of every instance, which preserves member GlobalIds by member key. - Member elements are read-only outside the group editor (ARC-MOD-000). - Hosted members. A member whose host is outside the group is rehosted, in each instance, onto the element at the corresponding transformed location if one exists. If none exists, the member is flagged "Host not found". - Members on several levels. A level-based member keeps its level offset relative to the group's reference level. If that level does not exist for an instance, the member uses the reference level plus an offset. - Constraints between group members and outside elements are removed when the group is created, with a warning.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Each group instance is an IfcGroup (ObjectType = the group type name) whose members are assigned with IfcRelAssignsToGroup. Nested groups are assigned the same way. - IFC has no group-type concept, so the template, the origin, the attached-detail-group bindings, the member keys and the exclusions are stored in RXD document model/groups. - Detail groups are IfcGroup objects whose members are view annotation (DOC chapter).
