    Commands. - group.create(element_ids, name, kind?: Model|Detail) -> {group_type_id, instance_id, attached_detail_type_id?} - group.place(group_type_id, point, rotation?, level_id?, origin_offset?) -> element_id - group.swap_type(instance_ids, group_type_id) - group.duplicate_type(group_type_id, name) -> group_type_id - group.rename_type(group_type_id, name) - group.ungroup(instance_ids) -> [element_id] - group.set_attached_detail_visible(instance_id, view_id, attached_type_ids)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Creating a group of a bathroom (walls, fixtures and a room) and placing three instances, then adding a fixture in the editor, adds that fixture to all four instances (the original plus three). - [ ] Ungroup leaves the elements in place as independent elements, and the group type remains in the project. - [ ] IFC export writes one IfcGroup per instance with the right members, and the file still opens in an IFC viewer after the RXD data has been stripped.

    3.13.2 Group editor

    ID: ARC-GRP-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §14

    Workflow. The user chooses Edit Group (EG), or double-clicks the group if that is enabled in Options. The group editor offers Add (AP), Remove (RG), Attach (AD; creates an attached detail group), Group Properties, Finish (FG) and Cancel.

    Behaviour & rules. - While the editor is open, the elements outside the group are shown in half-tone. - On Finish, the edits are propagated to all instances in one transaction group. - View-specific elements added to a model group stay in the view and are not added to the group. - Reviera warns when an instance has been changed outside the editor in a way that breaks identity, which can only happen through scripts that bypass the commands. The warning offers Restore or Make a new group type.

    Commands. - group.edit(instance_id) -> session_id - group.add_members(session_id, element_ids) - group.remove_members(session_id, element_ids) - group.attach_detail(session_id, view_kind, name) -> session_id - group.finish(session_id) - group.cancel(session_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Cancel in the group editor leaves every instance unchanged.

    3.13.3 Excluding members, saving, loading and converting to a link

    ID: ARC-GRP-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §14

    Behaviour & rules. - Exclude. The user tabs to a member of an instance and clicks the exclude icon (or right-click › Exclude). The member is hidden, is not scheduled and is not exported for that instance. Hosted elements are rehosted if possible. - Move to Project removes the member from that instance and turns it into an independent, editable element. - Restore Excluded Member (RB) and Restore All Excluded (RA) undo exclusions. - Save Group (right-click in the Project Browser) writes the group as a standalone .ifc file (with its RXD data). Load as Group (Insert tab) loads an .ifc file as a group type, with these options: attached details, include levels, include grids. A group saved this way can be edited as a separate project and loaded again into every open project (Load as Group into Open Projects). - Convert to link. Modify | Model Groups › Link offers Replace with a new project file (Save Group, then a link) or Replace with an existing project file. A name conflict prompts Yes, No or Cancel. The reverse is Bind a link into a group (COL chapter).

    Commands. - group.exclude_member(instance_id, member_key) - group.restore_member(instance_id, member_key | All) - group.move_member_to_project(instance_id, member_key) -> element_id - group.save(group_type_id, path) - group.load(path, options) -> group_type_id - group.convert_to_link(instance_ids, target: NewFile(path)|ExistingFile(path)) -> link_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An excluded member is absent from the schedule and the IFC export for that instance only. - [ ] A group saved to .ifc and loaded into another project produces the same members, with new GlobalIds.

    3.14 Temporary dimensions, constraints and selection

    Temporary dimensions are specified in ARC-DIM-001 and listening dimensions in ARC-DIM-002.

    3.14.1 Constraint model

    ID: ARC-CNST-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §15.2

    Purpose. Persistent geometric relationships between references.

    Behaviour & rules. - Explicit constraints: - locked dimensions (the padlock on a permanent linear, angular or radial dimension); - locked alignments (Align › Lock, pick-and-lock in sketches); - EQ equality (the EQ symbol on a multi-segment dimension). - Display. When the referenced elements are selected, explicit constraints are drawn as blue dashed lines. Reveal Constraints (View Control Bar) shows every constraint in the view in red. - Persistence. Constraints are model elements, not view-specific ones. They survive deletion of the dimension that created them: Reviera asks whether to keep or remove the constraints. - Looser constraints (unlocked dimensions and alignments) are dropped silently when they conflict. - Implied constraints (a wall attached to a roof, joined walls, hosted inserts, sketch lines locked to picked edges, Moves With Nearby Elements) are kept unless they conflict. - EQ display is a dimension setting: Value, Equality Text ("EQ") or Equality Formula (DOC chapter). - In worksharing mode, every element involved must be editable before a constraint can be added (COL chapter).

    Data (IFC mapping). Constraints are stored in RXD document model/constraints. Each record holds: kind (Distance, Alignment, Equality, Angle, Radius); references (GlobalId plus a named sub-reference, such as #face:ext or #refplane:Center); the locked value; and the ID of the dimension that created it, if any. IFC has no equivalent; IFC4 IfcConstraint is for requirements, not geometry.

    3.14.2 Constraint solving

    ID: ARC-CNST-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §13, §15.2

    Behaviour & rules. - Variables. Each constrained element contributes the degrees of freedom that its kind exposes: translation for families and inserts (along the host for hosted ones), endpoint and curve offsets for curve-driven elements, and the rotation angle where it applies. - Equations. - A distance constraint between two parallel references gives n·(p_b − p_a) = d. - An alignment constraint gives n·(p_b − p_a) = 0 with parallel normals. - An equality constraint gives d_1 = d_2 = … = d_k. - Solver. 1. A modification first proposes new values for the variables it touched. 2. The solver collects the connected component of constraints reachable from the modified elements. 3. It solves the component by least-change: minimise the weighted squared change of the untouched variables, subject to the equations. The proposed variables are fixed. It uses Gauss–Newton with a QR decomposition (the nalgebra crate, Apache-2.0). 4. Most constraint graphs are linear (translations), so the solve converges in one iteration. Rotations need up to 20 iterations with a tolerance of TOL_POINT. 5. Failure. If the system has no solution (inconsistent) or does not converge, Reviera reports "Constraints are not satisfied", lists the constraints involved, and offers Remove Constraints. 6. Looser constraints. Unlocked alignments are tried as soft equations with weight 1e-3 and dropped if the solve fails. Then the solve is retried. - Ordering. The solve runs inside the transaction, before geometry regeneration. Solved variable changes become ordinary parameter changes, which then dirty the regeneration graph.

    Commands. - constraint.lock_dimension(dimension_id, segment?: usize) - constraint.unlock_dimension(dimension_id, segment?) - constraint.lock_alignment(ref_a, ref_b) -> constraint_id - constraint.set_equality(dimension_id, on: bool) - constraint.delete(constraint_ids) - constraint.list(element_id?) -> [Constraint] (query) - view.reveal_constraints(view_id, on)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Three walls with an EQ dimension across them stay evenly spaced when the outer wall is moved. - [ ] Locking a 3000 mm dimension and then moving one wall drags the other wall by the same amount. - [ ] Locking two dimensions that contradict each other (3000 and 3500 between the same references) fails, and offers Remove Constraints. - [ ] Deleting a locked dimension prompts to keep or remove its constraint. Keeping it leaves a constraint that Reveal Constraints shows.

    3.14.3 Selection

    ID: ARC-SEL-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §15.3

    Behaviour & rules. - Basic actions. Click selects. Ctrl+click adds and Shift+click removes. - Window and crossing. A window dragged left to right selects only elements fully inside it. A crossing window dragged right to left selects elements it touches. - Tab cycles the candidates (ARC-KEY-001). - Select All Instances (SA): Visible in View or In Entire Project. - Filter dialog: category checkboxes with counts. - Select Previous: Ctrl+←. - Selection toggles (status bar and Modify › Select): Select Links, Select Underlay Elements, Select Pinned Elements, Select Elements by Face, Drag Elements on Selection. - Selection is local. It belongs to the session and is never written to the model. Lua and MCP can query and set the active selection.

    Commands. - selection.set(ids[], mode?: replace|add|remove (default replace)) -> () - selection.add(element_ids) - selection.remove(element_ids) - selection.get() -> {ids[], by_category} (query) - selection.select_all_instances(type_ids? (default: types of the current selection), scope: view|project) -> element_ids[] - selection.filter(category_ids[]) -> element_ids[] - selection.previous() -> () - selection.set_toggles(links?, underlay?, pinned?, by_face?, drag_on_select?)

    These commands are session-only and are not undoable.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A crossing window over the corner of a building selects every wall it touches, and a window over the same area selects only the walls that lie fully inside it. - [ ] With Select Pinned Elements off, pinned elements cannot be selected by clicking.

    3.14.4 Saved selections (selection sets)

    ID: ARC-SEL-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/02 §15.3

    Purpose. Name a set of elements once and recall it later for editing, checking or graphic overrides.

    Workflow. - With a selection active, the user chooses Modify | Multi-Select › Selection › Save (or Manage › Selection), and enters a name. - Load recalls a saved selection. - Edit opens Edit Filters, with Add to Selection, Remove from Selection and edit mode for adding or removing members.

    UI. - Save Selection dialog: a Name field, pre-filled with "Selection N". Names must be unique among selection sets and view filters (they share one name space, DOC chapter) and non-empty; a duplicate name offers Replace or Cancel. - Retrieve Filters (Load) dialog: the list of saved selection sets with their member counts, sorted by name, with a search box. Choosing one and OK replaces the current selection with its members that are visible in the current view; a check box Include elements not visible in this view selects the others too. - Edit Filters dialog: the list of saved sets with New, Duplicate, Rename and Delete. Choosing Edit for a selection set closes the dialog and enters Edit Selection mode in the active view: current members are highlighted, and the contextual tab offers Add to Selection, Remove from Selection and Finish Selection / Cancel. Clicks and window selections add or remove members according to the active button. The mode records add {ids}, remove {ids}, finish and cancel micro-operations so that an interrupted edit can be replayed (conventions §2.1).

    Behaviour & rules. - A saved selection is stored as a selection filter: an explicit list of GlobalIds. - What can be a member. Model and annotation elements in the current model, group instances (as a whole) and link instances (as a whole). Elements inside a linked model or inside a group instance cannot be members individually; such picks are ignored with a status-bar note. - Members that are deleted are dropped silently. - Copy and undo. Copying an element does not add the copy to its sets. Saving, editing, renaming and deleting a set are undoable model changes; loading a set only changes the session selection. - A saved selection can also be used as a view filter for graphic overrides (DOC chapter). Deleting a set that is used in a view or view template asks for confirmation and removes it from those views. - Collaboration. Sets are shared project data: in BIMserver mode they are merged by set ID like other RXD objects (02a §8), and two users adding members to the same set merge without conflict.

    Data (IFC mapping). Stored in RXD document model/selection_sets. The optional export setting Selection sets as IfcGroup also writes each set as an IfcGroup (ObjectType = "SelectionSet").

    Commands. - selectionset.save(name, element_ids) -> id - selectionset.load(id) -> [element_id] - selectionset.edit(id, add?: [element_id], remove?: [element_id]) - selectionset.delete(id) - selectionset.rename(id, name) and selectionset.list() -> [{id, name, count}] (query)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A saved set of 12 elements, one of which is later deleted, loads 11 elements without error. - [ ] Saving a set with the name of an existing view filter offers Replace or Cancel; Cancel changes nothing. - [ ] In Edit Selection mode, window-selecting three walls with Remove from Selection active and pressing Finish leaves the set three members smaller, as one undo step. - [ ] Exporting with Selection sets as IfcGroup gives one IfcGroup per set, whose IfcRelAssignsToGroup lists exactly the member elements.

    3.15 Regeneration dependencies and ordering

    3.15.1 Regeneration graph for architectural elements

    ID: ARC-REGEN-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/02 §17 (all items) · TECH_STACK.md §3.3

    Purpose. One deterministic, parallel recompute order for every element in this chapter.

    Behaviour & rules. - Two stages per element. Every curve-driven or sketch-driven element has a plan stage (location curves, sketch loops, datum references and resolved parameters) and a body stage (the 3D solid). Other elements may depend on either stage. Splitting the stages removes the cycles that would otherwise occur. Examples: a roof footprint locked to a wall reads only the wall's plan stage, while the wall attached to that roof reads the roof's body stage. A hosted wall reads its host's plan stage. - Phases within a transaction:

    Phase Work Parallelism
    R0 Parameters Apply the command's parameter changes and run formulas (DM chapter) Serial
    R1 Constraints Solve the affected constraint components (ARC-CNST-002) Parallel over independent components
    R2 Datums Levels, grids, reference planes, scope boxes, work planes Parallel
    R3 Plan stage Wall location curves (including hosted walls), sketch loops (resolving pick-locks), curtain grid layouts, stair recipes (riser counts, run paths), railing paths, group instance transforms and member templates Parallel, in topological order
    R4 Join resolution Detect wall joins and paint them (ARC-JOIN-001), per node Parallel over nodes that share no wall
    R5 Bodies (unclipped) Wall layer solids with join and profile applied; floors, roofs (skeleton), ceilings, stairs, ramps, railings, toposolids (TIN), families (mapped geometry), masses Parallel over elements; each worker builds its own OCCT shapes (no shared TopoDS across threads)
    R6 Interactions Attach clipping (target bodies → walls and columns), Join Geometry and Cut Geometry, embedded curtain-wall cuts, insert voids and wrapping, shafts and openings, excavation, Join Roof Parallel over connected components of the attach and cut graph; serial inside a component, in topological order
    R7 Derived Room and area boundaries, volumes, door From/To rooms, quantities (Qto_*), shape-edit cut/fill, contours (lazy) Parallel per (level, phase)
    R8 Commit Swap the new geometry and quantities in atomically, update spatial indices, mark the views dirty (DOC chapter) Serial
    • Edge summary (this chapter):
    From (producer) To (consumer) Kind Stage read
    Level Every element constrained to the level; plan views datum —
    Grid Columns with Moves With Grids; locked references datum —
    Reference plane, face Work-plane-based elements; locked sketch lines datum, sketch-lock plan or body
    Wall Join node join plan
    Join node Each wall in the node join —
    Wall (plan) Roof, floor or ceiling sketch locked to it; hosted wall; By-Room linings (creation only) sketch-lock, host plan
    Floor, roof, ceiling, reference plane, wall Attached walls and columns attach body
    Insert (void only) Host wall, floor or roof body cut —
    Host Insert placement host plan (walls), body (faces)
    Cutter (Cut Geometry, shaft, excavation, Join Geometry) Cut element cut body
    Wall type, floor type and other types Instances type —
    Room-bounding element Rooms and areas in its level band bound body (uncut)
    Toposolid Hosted site components, sub-divisions host body
    Group type Group instances; array sets group —
    Constraint The elements it references constraint —
    Mass Elements by face (only on Update to Face) (explicit) body
    • Cycle handling. Adding an edge that would close a cycle at the same stage is rejected, with the message "Circular reference: A → B → … → A", and the command that would create it fails. Examples: aligning a host to its own hosted wall; attaching wall A's top to wall B while B's base is attached to A at the same location.
    • Determinism. Inside each phase, the results do not depend on thread scheduling. Elements are processed in topological order, ties are broken by internal ID, and the floating-point Boolean operations run with fixed fuzzy values.
    • Failure isolation. If one element's geometry fails (an OCCT exception or an invalid solid detected by BRepCheck_Analyzer), that element keeps its last valid body, is flagged with a warning, and its dependants regenerate against the old body. The transaction still commits unless the failure came from the command's own target element and the command was interactive. In that case the user chooses whether to commit or roll back.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Moving one wall in a 500-wall model regenerates only that wall, its join nodes' walls, its inserts, the attached elements and the rooms on its level. This is verified with the instrumentation counter. - [ ] Regenerating a model twice from the same IFC and RXD data produces byte-identical geometry hashes. - [ ] Creating a two-element attach cycle is refused with the circular-reference message, and the model is unchanged.

    Open questions / deviations from reference

    Intentional deviations

    # Topic Reviera behaviour Reason
    D1 Options Bar None. Tool options live on the contextual tab or in the Properties New <Element> block (ARC-TOOL-001) Matches the reference's own 2027 direction, and gives one UI model for every tool and for tools added from Lua
    D2 Project format IFC4 is the native format. Parametric intent is stored as RXD (02a_extension_data_format.md) Required by TECH_STACK.md. Other IFC tools can read every element, and a tool that drops RXD still leaves valid geometry
    D3 Compound priority scale Reviera uses 1 (strongest) to 9. IFC4 IfcMaterialLayer.Priority uses 0–100 (higher is stronger), so export maps it with 100 − 10·(p−1). The exact value is kept in RXD IFC defines the opposite direction
    D4 Join limit Automatic detection is limited to 4 ends per node, as in the reference. The algorithm itself is general (ARC-JOIN-001 D.8) Keeps the expected behaviour while leaving room to raise the limit later
    D5 Curtain "Fixed Number" Defined as the number of interior grid lines (ARC-CW-003) The reference's wording is ambiguous, and Reviera states one meaning so the result is testable
    D6 Excavation robustness OCCT fuzzy Booleans with one retry, instead of randomly jittering void positions Deterministic regeneration (ARC-REGEN-001) rules out random perturbation
    D7 Import thresholds Point caps are ordinary settings (toposolid.max_points, toposolid.link_max_points), not an INI file Single settings system (DM chapter)
    D8 Legacy terrain No surface-only toposurface or building pad creation. Imported surface terrains are converted with Generate Toposolid (ARC-TOPO-006) Reviera has no legacy files to support. The toposolid workflow covers the same use cases
    D9 Group files Save Group and Load as Group use .ifc with embedded RXD, not a proprietary format Open format. The proprietary formats are out of scope (00_overview.md)
    D10 Stair by sketch No separate legacy tool. Sketching happens only inside the stair assembly (ARC-STAIR-002) Matches the reference's current behaviour, with a single code path
    D11 Divide Surface, patterns, adaptive components in the conceptual environment P3 (deferred). Masses support forms and editing only (ARC-MASS-001) Large scope that the core architectural workflows do not need. Lua-driven panelisation is an open alternative
    D12 Model text glyphs Rendered through FreeType from system or bundled fonts Licence-compatible font pipeline. Font availability varies by platform, so bundling an open font (for example DejaVu) is recommended
    D13 Room reference lines Initially through the centre of the boundary's bounding box Simple and deterministic
    D14 Paint on faces in IFC Painted faces are split into separate representation items so they can carry IfcStyledItem IFC styles apply per representation item, not per face
    D15 In-place copies Copying still creates a new in-place family, as in the reference. A later option may allow Convert to loadable family (DM chapter) Keeps instances independent, as users expect
    D16 Toposolid merge Reviera provides toposolid.merge, which joins toposolids that share an edge or overlap into one element (ARC-TOPO-002) The reference dropped Merge Surfaces with the move to toposolids and offers only Join Geometry, which leaves the seam visible; a true merge is the natural inverse of Split
    D17 Parts in IFC By default a source element with parts is exported without its own Body; its leaf parts carry the geometry as IfcBuildingElementPart through IfcRelAggregates (ARC-PART-001). An option writes both Avoids double counting in take-off and clash tools that read both the whole and its parts
    D18 Mirrored state Mirrored is set only by mirroring (Mirror tool or a family mirror control), never by Flip Hand / Flip Facing, and the flips are stored explicitly (ARC-FLIP-001) Keeps mirrored doors findable in schedules and makes the IFC reflection operator deterministic

    Open questions

    1. IFC4 IfcGrid with a single direction. IFC4 requires both UAxes and VAxes to be non-empty. When every grid line is parallel, should Reviera (a) put the last axis in VAxes (valid, but semantically wrong), (b) write one IfcGrid per axis plus a zero-length companion axis, or (c) use WAxes? The current draft follows (a), with a reconciliation note in the RXD data. This needs a decision together with the DM chapter's IFC validation rules.
    2. Slab edges in IFC. The draft uses IfcSlab(USERDEFINED "SLABEDGE"). The alternatives are IfcBuildingElementProxy and IfcMember, and the choice affects quantity take-off in other tools. A decision is needed together with the STR chapter, which owns thickened edges and curbs.
    3. Areas as IfcSpace. Writing areas from area schemes as IfcSpace (GFA or USERDEFINED) may make naive tools count spaces twice. One option is to export areas only when the user asks for them (the Export area schemes setting).
    4. Reference levels. Non-story levels are written as IfcAnnotation. IFC4X3 would allow IfcBuildingStorey with a "not a story" property, but other tools would still treat it as a storey. Confirm with COL, because BIMserver's storey-based queries are affected.
    5. ~~RXD kind names.~~ Resolved: every element and type kind used in this chapter is registered in 02a_extension_data_format.md §6.5 (Object Kind Registry).
    6. Room boundary performance targets. Proposed: placing a single room takes under 50 ms, and Place Rooms Automatically on a level with 500 rooms takes under 2 s on a 4-core reference machine. To be confirmed with the benchmarking plan.
    7. Winder distribution. The linear-angle "balanced" winder distribution (ARC-STAIR-004) is a reasonable default. Regional codes may need alternatives (for example, a fixed minimum inner width or kite winders), which could be added as a type option.
    8. Roof skeleton with slope arrows. The generalised wavefront handles arrows whose contour direction differs from the edge direction. Pathological inputs, such as arrows that make a face rise toward the footprint edge, need defined error messages, and a corpus of test footprints should be built.

    4CHChapter 4: Structure, Steel, Concrete/Precast, MEP Systems and Analysis

    Status: Draft 1 (2026-10-12) · Area codes: STR, MEP, ANA · Primary source: research/03_structure_mep.md (cited as research/03) · Architecture source: TECH_STACK.md Reference baseline: Revit 2026. Where Reviera follows the reference's 2027 direction, this is noted.

    This chapter covers the engineering disciplines built on Reviera's shared element, type and parameter kernel (chapter 2, DM-):

    • structural physical modeling and reinforcement
    • the structural analytical model
    • steel fabrication detailing
    • concrete and precast detailing
    • the MEP connector, system and routing framework
    • HVAC, piping and electrical design
    • MEP fabrication
    • spaces and system-zones
    • the analysis services on the Analyze tab

    Requirements are written in Reviera's own terms. The reference product is named only in "Reference" lines and in §4.17.

    Where data is stored (applies to the whole chapter)

    Compatibility comes first, so Reviera puts data in standard IFC wherever IFC can express it. That includes: - physical elements and rebar - structural analysis model entities, loads, load groups and boundary conditions - MEP segments, fittings, terminals, equipment and ports - distribution systems and circuits - spaces and zones - standard Pset_*/Qto_* values

    Data that IFC cannot express is Reviera Extension Data (RXD). Its format and carriers are defined in spec/02a_extension_data_format.md, and this chapter does not define them. By default RXD is embedded in the IFC file. Every element reference inside RXD uses the IFC GlobalId. This chapter uses two kinds of RXD:

    • RXD element data: per-element data, such as a rebar set's layout recipe or a column's attachment settings. Each block names the content area it belongs to, for example "RXD element data (constraints)".
    • RXD document <name>: project-level documents, such as MEP settings, electrical definitions or analysis settings.
    RXD content area Kind Contents used by this chapter
    constraints element data Constraints, attachments, joins, justification, layout rules and sketches. Examples: column attachments, beam-system layout, rebar handle constraints.
    rebar element data + document Element data: rebar layout-rule recipes, partition, number, splice and crank definitions, area/path/fabric system recipes, per-face cover assignments. Document: reinforcement settings, rounding, cover types and numbering sequences.
    mep_settings document Mechanical settings, routing preferences, size tables, pipe segments, fluids, slopes, conduit and cable-tray settings, system-type calculation options.
    electrical document Electrical settings, distribution systems and voltages, wiring types, conductor and cable tables, load classifications, demand factors, circuit naming schemes, panel schedule templates, the electrical analytical model.
    analysis document (+ element data) Analytical-model settings, load natures and code selection, automation logs, analysis provider settings, energy and route-analysis settings, and caches and indexes of result packages. Element data: analytical-element flags that IFC cannot hold.
    fabrication document The MEP fabrication content configuration (§4.10) and the precast configuration.
    families family recipes Rebar shape families, truss layouts, connection-library type recipes, deck profiles, fabrication part templates.
    structural (proposed addition, §4.17 Q1) element data + document Structural settings, structural-connection status data, steel part and assembly marks, precast piece provenance.

    4.0 Chapter-wide principles

    4.0.1 Three layers per discipline

    Ref: research/03 §0, §15.1–15.4

    Every discipline in this chapter is built from three layers:

    Layer What it is Examples
    Physical Typed occurrences with geometry, materials and discipline behaviour Column, beam, rebar set, duct, pipe, panelboard
    Logical / analytical Elements with no geometry, or idealised geometry, that capture how things connect or how they are idealised for calculation Analytical member, load, MEP system, electrical circuit, energy model, analytical duct segment
    Calculation services Asynchronous engines that read the first two layers and write results back as parameters or result packages Duct sizing, voltage drop, load roll-up, structural solve, energy simulation
    ID Priority Requirement
    STR-GEN-001 P1 Reviera shall store logical and analytical elements as first-class, independently persisted elements, not as derived caches. Deleting a physical element shall never silently delete an analytical element unless an explicit association rule says it should. Each such element has its own GlobalId, its own undo history and its own IFC entity (for example IfcStructuralCurveMember, IfcDistributionSystem), so it survives save, reload and BIMserver round trips with no physical counterpart. When a physical element with associated analytical elements is deleted, the confirmation lists them and offers Keep (the default) or Delete too; kept elements lose the association and are reported by STR-AM-007.
    STR-GEN-002 P1 Every hosted relationship in this chapter shall cascade deletes and report orphans as warnings, never silently. Examples are a load on an analytical element, rebar in a concrete host, a coupler on bar ends, and a boundary condition on a node. A delete that cascades shows one confirmation that counts the dependants per kind (for example "4 loads, 1 boundary condition") and removes them in the same transaction, so one undo restores everything. A host that stops qualifying without being deleted (for example a material change) leaves its dependants in place, flagged as orphaned, with a warning that selects them and offers re-host or delete. Scripted and MCP calls get the same counts in the command result's warnings[] and never prompt.
    ANA-GEN-001 P2 Calculation services shall run on the core worker pool in the background and never block the UI thread. Each run snapshots the model at a transaction boundary. Results are committed in a new transaction tagged with the service name, so they can be undone like any other change. If the model changed after the snapshot was taken, the results are flagged as stale and a re-run is offered.
    ANA-GEN-002 P2 Results computed per network or per member shall be stored on parameters or sub-elements that can be scheduled and tagged, not only in reports. Examples are analytical duct or pipe segments, circuit voltage drop and member forces. Each result parameter is read-only, carries the job ID and a stale flag (ANA-GEN-001), and is filterable in view filters. Standard values go to IFC psets where one exists; the rest are RXD element data (analysis). Deleting a result package clears its parameters in one undoable transaction.

    4.0.2 Optional external engines (plugin model)

    Ref: research/03 §4.6, §13.2–13.4, §15.4

    Several capabilities in the reference product depend on proprietary or cloud engines: a structural solver link, cloud lighting and solar analysis, online load-combination generation, a fabrication database, and P&ID cloud collaboration. Reviera replaces each of these with a provider interface defined in the core, and optional engine plugins that implement it.

    ID Priority Requirement
    ANA-PLUG-001 P2 Reviera shall define analysis provider interfaces in the command registry, one per analysis family: structural, energy, loads, daylight, solar, hydraulic, clash, route. Each provider declares its name, version and SPDX licence; its inputs (the model subset and the exchange format); its outputs (a result-package schema); and its capabilities, for example "linear static" or "modal". Families also include carbon (ANA-CARB-001). The manifest is a JSON file validated on analysis_provider.register; a manifest with an unknown kind, a missing licence or a licence outside the GPL-compatible allow-list (for in-process providers) is refused with the failing field named. Several providers per kind may be registered; one is the project default, stored in RXD document analysis.
    ANA-PLUG-002 P2 A provider may be an in-process Lua add-in or an external process that Reviera launches. External engines exchange files or standard I/O and are never linked into the binary. That keeps engines under BSD-style or custom permissive licences clear of linking questions. Engine licences shall still be checked against the GPL-3.0 allow-list before any official bundle ships one (TECH_STACK §4.2).
    ANA-PLUG-003 P2 Reviera shall ship working built-in reference providers for calculations that are simple and well defined: duct and pipe friction sizing, voltage drop, demand factors, the lumen method, 2D path of travel and embodied carbon (quantity × factor). Heavy engines are offered as plugins. Built-in providers register through the same manifest as plugins, appear in analysis_provider.list with licence GPL-3.0-or-later, and each has a verification test against a published hand-calculated case in the test suite. They work with no network access.

    Engine suggestions in this chapter are marked [Suggestion]. They are candidates to evaluate, not commitments. A summary is in §4.15.

    Commands. - analysis_provider.list(kind?) -> providers[] - analysis_provider.register(manifest_path) -> provider_id - analysis_job.status(job_id) -> {state, progress, messages} - analysis_job.cancel(job_id)

    4.0.3 UI conventions for this chapter

    Ref: research/03 §0 (2027 row, Options Bar removed), §15.7

    • There is no Options Bar. Placement options appear on the contextual "Modify | Place …" ribbon tab and in the Properties palette. Examples are size, elevation, justification, slope and level. This matches the reference product's 2027 direction and Reviera's UI chapter.
    • The chapter uses dockable palettes (wxAuiManager): System Browser, Fabrication Parts, Sizing Calculator, P&ID Line List and Results Explorer.
    • The chapter uses in-canvas controls: rebar segment lengths, connector glyphs, fitting "+/−" upgrade and downgrade, flip and rotate arrows, and shape handles.
    • Discipline settings dialogs are tree-structured and stored per project as RXD documents. They can be moved between projects with Transfer Project Standards (chapter 2).
    • Keyboard shortcuts in this chapter are proposed Reviera defaults. Users can remap them. They are not taken from any reference shortcut file.

    4.0.4 Ribbon layout (Reviera)

    Ref: research/03 §1.1–1.6

    Tab Panels and tools
    Structure Structure: Beam, Wall: Structural, Column, Floor: Structural, Truss, Brace, Beam System, Component. Connection: Connection, Connection Library, Show Warnings. Foundation: Isolated, Wall, Slab, Pile. Datum, Work Plane, Opening: shared with Architecture. Panel launcher: Structural Settings.
    Steel Connection: Connection, Connection Library, Automate. Fabrication Elements: Plate; Bolts split button (Bolts, Anchors, Holes, Shear Studs); Welds. Modifiers: Corner Cut, Cope Skewed, Shorten, Contour Cut. Parametric Cuts: Cope, Miter, Saw Cut (Flange/Web), Cut Through, Cut By, Uncope. Output: Numbering, NC Export [Suggestion].
    Concrete Reinforcement: Rebar, Area, Path, Fabric Area, Fabric Sheet, Coupler, Path Distribution, Morphed Distribution, Cover. Settings: Reinforcement Settings, Cover Settings, Reinforcement Numbers, Shape Browser. Precast Detailing: Split, Mounting Parts, Auto Reinforce, Shop Drawings, CAM Export.     4.1 Structural physical elements

    Common data model for structural framing. Columns, beams and braces are family-based occurrences (chapter 2) with these properties:

    • a structural material whose material for model behaviour is steel, concrete, precast concrete, wood or other
    • a section shape parameter set: hot-rolled, cold-formed or concrete dimensions, used by fabrication and analysis
    • a symbolic representation at Coarse detail: a stick line with cutback, drawn in the style set in Structural Settings
    • an optional association to analytical elements (§4.3)

    4.1.1 Structural columns

    ID: STR-COL-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §2.1, §1.1

    Purpose. Reviera shall provide load-bearing vertical columns. They join to beams, braces and isolated foundations, carry a structural material, can host rebar when they are concrete, and can be associated with an analytical member.

    Workflow (vertical). 1. Choose Structure › Structure › Column (proposed shortcut CL), or Architecture › Column › Structural Column. 2. Pick a type in the Type Selector. On the contextual tab choose: - Depth or Height - the top or bottom constraint: a level, or Unconnected with a length - Rotate after placement - in 3D views, the placement level 3. Click to place. The cursor snaps to grid intersections and highlights both grid lines. Spacebar turns the column to the directions of the intersecting grids, or by 90° when there is no grid.

    Workflow (multiple placement). - Multiple › At Grids: select grid lines with a window or Ctrl+click. Spacebar rotates all previews. Finish commits them as one transaction. - Multiple › At Columns puts a structural column inside each selected architectural column.

    UI. Contextual tab "Modify | Place Structural Column": Vertical/Slanted, Multiple (At Grids, At Columns), Tag on Placement, Rotate after placement, Level/Depth/Height. Properties palette: base and top level and offset, Moves With Grids, cut styles, extensions, attachment settings, structural material, and the analytical association (read-only).

    Behaviour & rules. - Column top and base can attach to floors, roofs, beams and reference planes (Attach Top/Base, Detach). Attachment options: - Attachment Justification: minimum intersection, column midline, maximum intersection, or tangent - Offset From Attachment - Base/Top Geometry Alignment: location line, or the top, centre or bottom of the beam - Cut style at each end is perpendicular, horizontal or vertical. Each end can carry an extension. - Moves With Grids locks the column to its grid intersection, so moving a grid regenerates the column. - A read-only Column Location Mark is derived from the nearest grid intersection, for example "C-4". - Concrete columns are valid rebar hosts (§4.2.1).

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcColumn with PredefinedType COLUMN. Types are IfcColumnType. - Body: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid over an IfcProfileDef subtype (IfcIShapeProfileDef, IfcRectangleProfileDef, …). Material: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage. - Property sets: Pset_ColumnCommon (LoadBearing = TRUE, IsExternal, FireRating) and Qto_ColumnBaseQuantities. - Containment: IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure to the base storey. Other storeys the column spans are recorded with IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure. - Attachments to floors, roofs and beams are IfcRelConnectsElements. - RXD element data (constraints) holds the attachment targets and justification, offsets, cut styles, extensions and the Moves With Grids lock. The location mark is computed, not stored.

    Commands. - column.place(type_id, point, base_level, top_constraint, base_offset, top_offset, rotation?) -> element_id - column.place_at_grids(type_id, grid_ids[], base_level, top_constraint, rotation?) -> element_id[] - column.place_in_columns(type_id, arch_column_ids[]) -> element_id[] - column.attach(column_ids[], end: top|base, target_id, style?, justification?, offset?) -> () - column.detach(column_ids[], end: top|base, target_ids?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With Moves With Grids on, moving a grid moves the columns on it. With it off, the columns stay put. - [ ] At Grids with 4 × 3 selected grids creates exactly 12 columns in one undo step. - [ ] A column attached to a sloped floor follows the floor when the floor slope changes, for each of the four attachment justifications. - [ ] Exported IFC validates against IFC4 ADD2 TC1, and the column carries Pset_ColumnCommon.LoadBearing = TRUE.

    4.1.2 Slanted columns

    ID: STR-COL-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §2.1

    Purpose. Inclined columns, for example raking columns and V-columns.

    Workflow. Choose Slanted Column on the contextual tab. In plan, give two clicks, each with its own level and offset (First Click, Second Click). In 3D or elevation, the clicks can snap to existing structural elements using 3D snapping.

    Behaviour & rules. - The top end must always be higher than the base. If an edit would invert them, Reviera swaps the ends and reports a warning. - Column Style is Vertical, Slanted – End Point Driven or Slanted – Angle Driven. Changing the style keeps the base point. - Slanted columns are excluded from graphical column schedules (chapter 5) and from Copy/Monitor (chapter 6). - In point-to-point steel mode (STR-BEAM-003), a slanted column runs to the full end of its system length.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcColumn with an Axis representation along the inclined line. RXD element data (constraints) holds the column style and the angle that drives it.

    Commands. column.place_slanted(type_id, p1, p1_level, p1_offset, p2, p2_level, p2_offset, style) -> element_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing an angle-driven column from 60° to 75° moves the top point and keeps the base fixed. - [ ] Dragging the base above the top produces a warning, and the column remains valid.

    4.1.3 Beams (structural framing)

    ID: STR-BEAM-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §2.2

    Purpose. Horizontal, sloped or curved framing members. A structural usage value controls coarse line style, scheduling and analytical role.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Structure › Beam (proposed BM). 2. On the contextual tab set the placement plane, structural usage (or Automatic), 3D Snapping, Chain and Tag on Placement. 3. Click a start point and an end point; a typed length is accepted. Use an arc tool for curved beams. 4. Multiple › On Grids places one beam on each selected grid line between consecutive supports (columns, walls or beams).

    UI. Contextual tab "Modify | Place Beam": draw tools (line, arc, pick lines), Multiple › On Grids, structural usage, 3D snapping, chain, tag. If a plan view's lower clip plane hides the new beam, Reviera shows a non-modal notice that offers to adjust the view range.

    Behaviour & rules. - Automatic structural usage:

    Supported by Usage assigned
    Walls or columns Girder
    Girders Joist
    Joists Purlin
    A brace, or a member framing into one Other
    Drawn as horizontal bracing Horizontal Bracing
    • Users can edit and lock the usage. A locked usage is not recalculated.
    • On sloped work planes, Orientation is Normal (the section stays perpendicular to the plane) or Horizontal (the section stays upright).
    • Cross-Section Rotation turns the profile about the member axis.

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcBeam with PredefinedType set from usage: BEAM with ObjectType "GIRDER" or "JOIST"; LINTEL; HOLLOWCORE; T_BEAM. - Purlins and horizontal bracing are IfcMember (PURLIN or BRACE). - Types are IfcBeamType and IfcMemberType. - Property sets: Pset_BeamCommon (Span, Slope, Roll, LoadBearing) and Qto_BeamBaseQuantities (Length = cut length, CrossSectionArea, NetVolume, GrossWeight). - RXD element data (constraints) holds the usage lock, start and end level offsets, orientation and stick-symbol location.

    Commands. - beam.create(type_id, curve, reference_level, usage?, orientation?, z_justification?, y_justification?) -> element_id - beam.create_on_grids(type_id, grid_ids[], level) -> element_id[] - beam.set_usage(beam_ids[], usage, lock?)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A beam drawn between two columns gets Girder. A beam framing into that girder gets Joist. A beam framing into the joist gets Purlin. - [ ] On Grids across 3 grid lines that each cross 4 columns creates 9 beams, one per bay. - [ ] A purlin exports as IfcMember with PredefinedType PURLIN.

    4.1.4 Framing justification, extensions, cutback and joins

    ID: STR-BEAM-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §2.2, §2.4

    Purpose. Control precisely where framing geometry sits relative to its location line, and how members meet.

    Behaviour & rules. - Justification: - yz Justification is Uniform or Independent per end. - y Justification is Origin, Left, Centre or Right, with a y offset. - z Justification is Origin, Top, Centre or Bottom, with a z offset. - Lateral justification is also available. - The ribbon's Justification Points tool picks one of nine section points graphically, alongside y and z offset tools. - Extensions: start and end extensions change the physical length without moving the analytical end. Shape handles do the same by dragging. - Cutback: steel members get an automatic gap at joins, set per end. In joins between different materials, concrete takes precedence and cuts steel or wood. - Join editor (Beam/Column Joins): arrows at each join choose which member runs through. Ends can be mitred or squared off, and Disjoin releases an end. Change Reference chooses which face of the joined member the end aligns to. - Openings in framing come from face-based openings (chapter 3) or from family voids.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Joins are IfcRelConnectsPathElements (ConnectionType ATSTART, ATEND or ATPATH). - Openings are IfcOpeningElement + IfcRelVoidsElement. - Body geometry always reflects the resolved justification, cutback and extensions. - RXD element data (constraints) holds justification, extensions, cutback, join priority, mitre and disjoin flags.

    Commands. - framing.set_justification(ids[], y_just, y_offset, z_just, z_offset, mode) - framing.set_extension(id, end, length) - framing.set_cutback(id, end, distance) - framing.join_edit(join_id, through_member_id?, miter?) - framing.disjoin(id, end) - framing.change_reference(id, end, reference)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] z Justification = Top with a −50 mm offset puts the top of steel 50 mm below the location line in section. - [ ] A concrete beam joined to a steel column cuts the column. Swapping the materials reverses the cut. - [ ] Disjoining an end removes the cutback at that end only.

    4.1.5 Point-to-point steel modeling

    ID: STR-BEAM-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §2.2 ("Point-to-point steel modeling")

    Purpose. A project setting that makes steel members run exactly between the points the user clicked, so that system length equals cut length. This suits fabrication-first workflows.

    Behaviour & rules. When Structural Settings › Structural Steel Elements › Disable automatic shortening during auto-join is on: - Steel beams and braces are no longer shortened at joins. - Start extension is locked, and start join cutback is removed. - Weight is recalculated. - Change Reference is unavailable. - Columns are still shortened. Slanted columns run to the full end of their system length.

    Turning the setting on or off regenerates every affected member in one transaction.

    Data (IFC mapping). Geometry and Qto_BeamBaseQuantities reflect the result. RXD document model/structural (settings.point_to_point_steel).

    Commands. structural_settings.set(key="point_to_point_steel", value)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With the setting on, a steel beam clicked from (0,0) to (6000,0) and joined to columns at both ends reports Cut Length = 6000 mm.

    4.1.6 Beam systems

    ID: STR-BSYS-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §2.3

    Purpose. A parametric host element that fills a bay with parallel beams according to a layout rule. The beams it creates are ordinary framing occurrences.

    Workflow (automatic). 1. In a plan or ceiling view, choose Structure › Beam System. 2. Hover over a bay enclosed by supports (walls or beams). The bay highlights, and the preview aligns parallel to the nearest support. Curved supports can bound the bay but cannot set the direction. 3. Click to create. Walls Define Slope lets sloped walls drive the elevation.

    Workflow (sketch). Choose Sketch Beam System. Draw with Line or Pick Lines, or use Pick Supports, which locks edges to their supports. Set the Beam Direction edge, then Finish.

    UI. Contextual tab: Automatic/Sketch, Walls Define Slope, Tag on Placement (system tag or framing tag), Layout Rule. Edit-mode tab: Boundary, Beam Direction, Pick Supports, Finish/Cancel.

    Behaviour & rules. - Layout rules:

    Rule Behaviour
    Fixed Distance Given centre spacing
    Fixed Number Given count
    Maximum Spacing Smallest count that keeps spacing at or below the value
    Clear Spacing Spacing measured between beam faces. Resizing a beam moves its neighbours.
    • Justification of the layout: Beginning, End, Centre or Direction Line.
    • Other parameters: beam type, elevation, and 3D (non-planar), where sketch-line elevations drive the beam elevations.
    • When supports move, a boundary locked to them regenerates, and the child beams are re-laid out.
    • A system should not span a bay crossed by other beams. If it does, Reviera warns and suggests splitting the system.
    • Remove Beam System deletes the host and keeps the beams as independent framing.
    • Copying or mirroring a system copies its sketch. Support locks that cannot be resolved are released, with a warning.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcElementAssembly with PredefinedType BEAM_GRID, aggregating its child IfcBeam/IfcMember elements through IfcRelAggregates. RXD element data (constraints) holds the layout rule, spacing or count, justification, elevation, non-planar flag, boundary sketch, direction edge and support locks.

    Commands. - beam_system.create_auto(view_id, pick_point, type_id, layout_rule, value, justification?) -> system_id - beam_system.create_sketch(boundary_curves[], direction_edge, type_id, layout_rule, value, lock_to_supports?) -> system_id - beam_system.set_layout(system_id, rule, value, justification) - beam_system.remove(system_id) -> beam_ids[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 6 m × 9 m bay with Maximum Spacing 1.2 m produces the smallest beam count whose spacing does not exceed 1.2 m. - [ ] Under Clear Spacing, changing one beam to a wider section moves its neighbours so that clear spacing stays the same. - [ ] Moving a support beam 300 mm moves the locked boundary edge and re-lays out the children in one regeneration. - [ ] Remove Beam System leaves all child beams in place and editable.

    4.1.7 Braces

    ID: STR-BRACE-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §2.4

    Purpose. Diagonal framing that joins to columns and beams.

    Workflow. - In a framing elevation: choose Structure › Brace (proposed BR), snap the start to a column or beam, then snap the end. - In plan: set start level and offset and end level and offset on the contextual tab, then click two points. - Chain (contextual tab toggle, off by default) starts the next brace at the end of the previous one, for K and chevron patterns. Esc ends the chain; a second Esc leaves the tool.

    UI. Contextual tab "Modify | Place Brace": Type Selector, Start Level/Offset, End Level/Offset (plan only), Chain, 3D Snapping. Properties: reference level, start and end attachment (the member and distance or ratio along it), cross-section rotation, structural material, structural usage (read-only) and the analytical association (read-only).

    Behaviour & rules. - Braces share the framing rules for justification, cutback, extensions and releases (STR-BEAM-002). - Attachment. An end snapped to a column or beam stores the target and the position along it, as a distance from the target's start or as a ratio (Properties choose which). The end follows the target when it moves, stretches or changes level; if the target is deleted the end stays where it was, becomes free, and a warning names the brace. - Usage. Usage is Other, or Horizontal Bracing when both ends lie in one horizontal plane within 1 mm. It is recomputed after each edit and cannot be overridden (unlike beams). - At Coarse detail a brace in a plan view is drawn with the brace plan symbol set in Structural Settings (STR-SET-001): parallel line offset, or none. Kicker braces (one end on a beam mid-span) use the kicker symbol. - A zero-length brace (start and end within 1 mm) is refused with an error. - Braces are valid rebar hosts when their material is concrete (STR-RBR-001). - Interactive placement journals each pick (start, end, chain toggle) as a micro-operation so that an unfinished chain is recovered after a crash (§2.1 of the conventions); replay re-runs the picks in order.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcMember with PredefinedType BRACE, typed by IfcMemberType (BRACE). Pset_MemberCommon (Reference, LoadBearing = TRUE, IsExternal, Slope). Axis representation as an IfcPolyline "Axis" item plus a swept body. Connections to the attached members: IfcRelConnectsPathElements (ATSTART/ATEND). End attachments (target GlobalId, distance or ratio): RXD element data (constraints).

    Commands. - brace.create(type_id, start_point, start_level, start_offset, end_point, end_level, end_offset) -> element_id

    Justification, extension, cutback and join edits use the framing.* commands of STR-BEAM-002.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A brace snapped to two column–beam intersections in an elevation stays joined when one column moves. - [ ] A brace exports as IfcMember (BRACE). - [ ] A brace attached at ratio 0.5 along a 6 m beam stays at mid-span when the beam is stretched to 8 m. - [ ] A brace drawn in plan with both ends at Level 2 + 0 shows usage Horizontal Bracing; moving one end to Level 3 changes it to Other. - [ ] Deleting the column at one end leaves the brace in place with a free end and one warning that names it.

    4.1.8 Trusses

    ID: STR-TRUSS-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §2.5

    Purpose. A truss family defines a layout of top chord, bottom chord, vertical web and diagonal web lines. Every type in the family shares that layout but assigns its own framing type to each member group.

    Workflow. Choose Structure › Truss, then draw a line or pick a line from start to end. The layout stretches to fit the span.

    UI. - Contextual "Modify | Truss" tab: Edit Profile (top and bottom chord shapes), Attach Top/Bottom (to a roof or structural floor), Detach, Remove Truss, Edit Family. - When selected, the truss shows as dashed lines. Its members can be selected individually with Tab. - A one-click action tags all members.

    Behaviour & rules. - Type parameters per group (top chords, bottom chords, vertical webs, diagonal webs): framing type, start and end release (Pinned, Fixed, Moment), and angle. Chords also carry an analytical vertical projection. - Construction parameters: webs have symbolic cutback, web orientation, bearing chord (top or bottom), truss height and non-bearing offset. - A member's type can be changed individually, but only within the sizes the truss family allows. - Remove Truss deletes the truss host and keeps the members as plain framing.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcElementAssembly with PredefinedType TRUSS, aggregating IfcMember elements: CHORD for chords, and STRUT or MEMBER for webs. The RXD family recipe holds the truss layout recipe. RXD element data (constraints) holds attachments and profile edits.

    Commands. - truss.create(type_id, start, end, level) -> truss_id - truss.edit_profile(truss_id, top_curves[], bottom_curves[]) - truss.attach(truss_id, chord: "top"|"bottom", target_id) - truss.detach(truss_id, chord) - truss.remove(truss_id) -> member_ids[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A Pratt truss drawn over 12 m and then stretched to 15 m keeps its panel count and re-proportions its webs. - [ ] Attaching the top chord to a sloped roof regenerates the chords and webs to the roof underside. - [ ] The export contains one IfcElementAssembly (TRUSS) that aggregates all chords and webs.

    4.1.9 Structural walls

    ID: STR-WALL-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §2.6

    Purpose. Load-bearing and shear walls, built on the architectural wall engine (chapter 3, ARC-WALL-*).

    Workflow. Structure › Wall › Wall: Structural offers the same options as the architectural wall tool (level, depth or height, location line, chain, offset, radius, join status), with Structural set to true.

    Behaviour & rules. - Structural Usage is Bearing, Shear, Structural Combined or Non-bearing. - A wall is a valid rebar host when its usage is not Non-bearing and it has a layer whose material behaviour is concrete or precast concrete. - Analytical automation does not create panels for slanted structural walls. Reviera warns when it skips one, and a panel can still be modelled by hand. - A wall foundation (STR-FND-002) can be attached beneath.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcWall with PredefinedType SHEAR (shear usage) or SOLIDWALL, and Pset_WallCommon.LoadBearing (TRUE except for Non-bearing). RXD element data (structural) keeps the exact usage value where IFC cannot tell the difference, for example "Structural Combined".

    Commands. wall.create(...) (chapter 3) with structural=true, structural_usage; wall.set_structural_usage(ids[], usage)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A concrete Bearing wall offers the Rebar tool on its contextual tab. After the change to Non-bearing it no longer does. - [ ] Bearing walls export with LoadBearing = TRUE.

    4.1.10 Structural floors and composite decks

    ID: STR-FLOOR-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §2.7

    Purpose. Structural slabs with a span direction, optionally on a profiled metal deck.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Structure › Floor › Floor: Structural. 2. Sketch a closed boundary with Boundary Line, Pick Walls or Pick Supports. 3. Set the Span Direction edge. A span symbol is placed. 4. Optionally use Extend into wall (to core). Finish.

    Behaviour & rules. - Composite deck: a floor type can include one Structural Deck layer. That layer references a deck profile family and a deck usage: - Bound Layer Above/Below: concrete fills the deck ribs - Standalone Deck: the deck is used on its own - The deck profile is drawn at Medium and Fine detail in sections cut perpendicular to the span. - Sub-tools, shared with chapter 3 where they apply: slab edges, thickened slabs, drop panels, cantilevers, openings, stiffeners at openings, sloped floors (slope arrow) and the span symbol. - A concrete structural floor is a valid rebar host.

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcSlab (FLOOR). Layers: IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage. The deck layer is an IfcMaterialLayer with Category "StructuralDeck". - The span direction is also expressed through the layer set's reference direction. - The RXD family recipe holds the deck profile recipe and deck usage on the floor type. RXD element data (constraints) holds the span-direction edge and sketch.

    Commands. - floor.create(type_id, loops, level_id, offset?, slope?: {line_key|curve, slope} | {arrow: SlopeArrow}, structural?, span_direction_edge?, room_bounding?, attach_walls_below?: bool, join_overlapping_walls?: bool) -> element_id - floor.set_span_direction(floor_id, edge_index | vector) - floor_type.set_deck_layer(type_id, layer_index, profile_family_id, usage)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A composite floor cut perpendicular to its span shows deck ribs at Fine detail and a plain layer at Coarse detail. - [ ] Rotating the span direction by 90° changes which sections show the rib profile.

    4.1.11 Foundations

    ID: STR-FND-001 / 002 / 003 / 004 · Priority: P1 (001–003), P2 (004) · Ref: research/03 §2.8

    ID Feature Workflow Behaviour & rules IFC / RXD Commands
    STR-FND-001 Isolated footing Foundation › Isolated: click in plan or 3D. Also Multiple › At Grids and At Columns. Joins to the column base above. A read-only Elevation at Bottom is available to tags. A foundation tag that shows elevation is supplied. IfcFooting PAD_FOOTING (or PILE_CAP when the family declares piles), IfcFootingType, Pset_FootingCommon footing.place(type_id, point, level, offset), footing.place_at_columns(type_id, column_ids[]), footing.place_at_grids(type_id, grid_ids[])
    STR-FND-002 Wall foundation Foundation › Wall: pick structural walls. Type kind: Retaining (toe length, heel length) or Bearing (width). Other parameters: thickness, default end extension and Do Not Break At Inserts. Follows the wall's length and its openings. IfcFooting STRIP_FOOTING; RXD family recipe (type kind and dimensions) and RXD element data constraints (wall host) wall_foundation.create(type_id, wall_ids[])
    STR-FND-003 Foundation slab Foundation › Slab: sketch one closed outer loop (plus inner loops for openings), or pick walls to generate the boundary. Offset from the level, and extend into wall (to the wall core) when picking walls. Its top face sits at the level plus offset and the slab extends below it, so it is visible only in views whose range reaches below the level. When no plan of that level has a view depth reaching the slab, the tool offers to create a foundation plan. Has no span direction. Thickness comes from the type's layers. Joins to wall foundations and isolated footings it overlaps (the slab is cut). Valid rebar host (STR-RBR-001). An open or self-intersecting loop is refused with the offending segment highlighted. IfcSlab BASESLAB, IfcSlabType, Pset_SlabCommon; the editable boundary sketch is RXD element data (constraints) foundation_slab.create(type_id, boundary, level, offset)
    STR-FND-004 Piles and pile caps Place a pile-cap family with nested piles, or a single pile family. Pile families declare count, length, diameter and kind (bored or driven). Each pile is a separate nested occurrence. This goes beyond the reference's generic foundation families, to give clean IFC. IfcPile (PredefinedType BORED, DRIVEN, …), IfcPileType, Pset_PileCommon, aggregated under the cap's IfcFooting PILE_CAP pile.place(type_id, point, level, length), pile_cap.place(type_id, point, level)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] At Columns with 20 selected columns places 20 isolated footings centred under them. - [ ] A retaining wall foundation with Toe 600 mm and Heel 1200 mm shows the correct asymmetric section. - [ ] A foundation slab at Level 1 is not visible in a Level 1 plan whose view depth ends at the level, and is visible in the generated foundation plan. - [ ] A four-pile cap exports one IfcFooting (PILE_CAP) that aggregates four IfcPile elements.

    4.1.12 Structural connections (information carriers)

    ID: STR-CONN-001 · Priority: P1 (generic) / P2 (detailed types, code checking) · Ref: research/03 §2.9 · screenshots/structure_mep/structural_connection_symbols.png

    Purpose. An element placed at a join of two or more framing members. It carries the information engineers, detailers and fabricators exchange about that join: connection type, connected members, geometry, design forces, materials, fabricator, code-check status, approval status and phase.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Structure › Connection or Steel › Connection. 2. Pick the members with Ctrl+click or a window, then press Enter or Spacebar. 3. If members were already selected, the generic connection is placed at once, or the last-used type.

    UI. - A generic connection is drawn as a symbolic circle with spokes at Coarse and Medium detail. - With a generic connection selected, the Type Selector lists recommended types first. They are filtered by member count, member shapes, member positions and which member is the main member. - Properties: Override by Instance, Approval Status, Code Check Status, Fabricator, Design Forces (per load case or combination).

    Behaviour & rules. - Detailed connection types come from the connection library (STR-STL-002). Library types offer Modify Parameters (a type editor with live preview) and Ranges of Applicability (rules used by automatic placement). - Sub-connections come from parametric cuts (STR-STL-008). They cannot be duplicated or retyped. - Override by Instance unlocks per-instance detail parameters and the code-check tab. - Other tools: - Propagate: copy a connection to joins that match it geometrically - Break: turn the connection into independent plates, bolts and welds - Customize: see STR-STL-003 - Connection Library: load and unload types, filtered by group - Unloading a type deletes its instances after a confirmation that states how many are affected.

    Connection warnings in views. A connection whose generator cannot produce valid geometry (unsupported section shape, wrong input order, parameters that do not fit the members, a member moved out of the type's ranges of applicability) keeps its data, shows its symbol only, and gets a status of Failed with a reason code and a one-line explanation. - Connection › Show Warnings is a per-view toggle (off by default, stored with the view). When on, each failed connection in the view is drawn with a warning marker (a triangle at the join, in the view's warning colour) and a tooltip that gives the reason and the input order the type expects. - Clicking the marker selects the connection; the Properties palette shows the reason and offers Modify Parameters. The same failures are always listed in the project warnings list (chapter 1), whether or not the toggle is on. - The toggle changes display only. It is not undoable and does not mark the model as changed.

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcElementAssembly (PredefinedType USERDEFINED, ObjectType "STRUCTURAL_CONNECTION") aggregates the connection's plates, fasteners and cuts. - Connected members are related with IfcRelConnectsWithRealizingElements: the RelatingElement is the main member, the RelatedElement is a secondary member, and the realizing elements are the plates and fasteners. - The analytical counterpart is an IfcStructuralPointConnection (§4.3). - RXD element data (structural) holds the connection type reference, approval status, code-check status and report path, fabricator, instance-override flag, main member and design-force references. All references are GlobalIds.

    Commands. - structural_connection.create(member_ids[], type_id?) -> connection_id - structural_connection.set_type(connection_id, type_id) - structural_connection.propagate(connection_id, target_join_ids[] | "matching") -> connection_ids[] - structural_connection.break(connection_id) -> element_ids[] - connection_library.load(type_ids[]) - connection_library.unload(type_ids[]) - structural_connection.show_warnings(view_id, on: bool)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Selecting a beam and a column and running the tool creates one generic connection symbol at the join. - [ ] For a beam-to-column-flange join, the Type Selector lists shear-plate and end-plate types ahead of base plates. - [ ] Unloading a type used by 7 connections asks for confirmation, states the count, and then removes all 7. - [ ] With Show Warnings on, an end-plate connection whose beam is deeper than the plate range shows a warning marker whose tooltip names the failing parameter; turning the toggle off removes the marker but the warning stays in the warnings list, and the undo stack is unchanged.

    4.1.13 Structural settings and symbolic representation

    ID: STR-SET-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §1.6, §15.5–15.6 · web: Analytical Model Settings

    Purpose. Project-wide structural settings, opened from Manage › Structural Settings or the Structure panel launcher.

    UI: the Structural Settings dialog. A modal, tree-structured dialog (§4.0.3). The left pane lists the pages below; the right pane edits the selected page. OK applies all pages in one transaction ("Structural Settings"); Cancel discards; Apply commits and keeps the dialog open. structural_settings.show(page?) opens it on a given page: structural (symbolic representation and steel), connection, analytical, boundary_conditions or load_display.

    Page What it lists and edits Validation
    Symbolic Representation (structural) Brace symbol in plan (parallel line with offset, or none) and its offset; kicker brace symbol; coarse cutback for beams, braces and trusses (default 3 mm, 1/8"); plan symbol for vertical braces above and below the cut plane Offsets and cutbacks 0–100 mm; negative values refused
    Connection (connection) Connection symbol family per connection type (generic, and each loaded library type); default for new types The symbol must be a loaded annotation family of the connection-symbol kind
    Structural Steel Elements (structural) Point-to-point mode (STR-BEAM-003): turn off automatic shortening of steel members when they auto-join —
    Load Cases / Load Combinations Read-only summaries with a button that opens the manager (STR-LC-001) on the matching tab —
    Analytical Model (analytical) Automatic checks on or off: Member supports and Analytical/physical consistency (both off by default). Tolerances: support distance (default 300 mm), analytical-to-physical distance (default 150 mm), node merge distance (default 5 mm), level and grid alignment distance used by automation (default 300 mm). Consistency criteria to include, each a check box (STR-AM-007). Circular support references check on or off Every tolerance > 0 and ≤ 2 000 mm; node merge distance must be smaller than support distance
    Boundary Conditions (boundary_conditions) Symbol family per state (Fixed, Pinned, Roller, User) for point, line and area conditions; spacing of line and area symbols (default 1 000 mm) Spacing > 0; family must be of the matching boundary-condition symbol kind
    Loads Scaling Display (load_display) Arrow length per force unit (for example 10 mm per 10 kN), per linear force, per area force and per moment unit; whether values are labelled Scale values > 0

    Each row in a page shows whether the value differs from the project template default, and Reset page restores the template values.

    Behaviour & rules. - Changes to symbolic settings regenerate Coarse views on commit; changes to tolerances do not move any element. They take effect on the next check or automation run. - Turning an automatic check on runs it once over the whole model and then after every transaction that touches structural or analytical elements (STR-AM-007). - The dialog is available in BIMserver client mode; settings are part of the model and follow check-in.

    Data (IFC mapping). No IFC equivalent. RXD document model/structural (settings.*), with symbol families referenced by type GlobalId. Analytical tolerances, check switches and load display scale go in RXD document model/analysis.

    Commands. structural_settings.get() -> table, structural_settings.set(key, value), structural_settings.show(page?). set applies the same validation as the dialog and returns an error naming the key and the allowed range.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing the coarse cutback from 3 mm to 10 mm updates all coarse plan views on the next regeneration. - [ ] Settings survive a save and reopen of the .ifc with its RXD data, and a BIMserver check-in and get-latest round trip. - [ ] structural_settings.show("analytical") opens the dialog on the Analytical Model page; entering a node merge distance of 400 mm with a support distance of 300 mm disables OK and shows the rule. - [ ] Changing three pages and pressing OK creates one undo item; undo restores all three.

    4.2 Reinforcement (rebar)

    Every reinforcement feature in this section is P2, as the priority tiers require, unless stated otherwise. Rebar tools live on the Concrete tab. They also appear on the contextual tab of any selected valid host.

    4.2.1 Rebar hosts

    ID: STR-RBR-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.1

    Purpose. Decide which elements can contain reinforcement.

    Behaviour & rules. - Valid hosts: structural framing, structural columns, foundations, structural connections, floors, walls, foundation slabs, wall foundations, slab edges and parts cut from concrete walls or floors. - Generic-model families become valid hosts when their family flag Can Host Rebar is set. - Material condition: the host material's model behaviour must be Concrete or Precast Concrete. Walls and floors must also be structural and contain a concrete layer. - If a host stops qualifying, its rebar is kept but flagged as orphaned, with a warning. A host can stop qualifying through a material change or through becoming non-structural. The user can re-host the rebar or delete it. - Rebar shall never be silently deleted, except when its host is deleted. In that case the delete cascades and the count is shown in the confirmation.

    Data (IFC mapping). Rebar elements are related to their host with IfcRelAggregates, where the host is the whole and the reinforcement is a part. The IFC4 reference-view convention also accepts IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure. Reviera writes IfcRelAggregates and also records the host GlobalId in RXD element data (rebar), so that the link survives round trips through tools that drop aggregates. Host eligibility is computed and is not stored.

    Commands. rebar.can_host(element_id) -> bool, rebar.rehost(rebar_ids[], host_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A floor whose concrete layer is changed to timber flags its rebar as orphaned and keeps it in place. - [ ] Deleting a host column with 3 rebar sets shows "3 reinforcement elements will be deleted" and removes them in the same transaction.

    4.2.2 Reinforcement settings, rounding and cover

    ID: STR-RBR-002 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.1

    Purpose. Project-level rules for reinforcement.

    Behaviour & rules. - Area and path reinforcement produce real rebar (one mode per project). - When the mode is on, area and path systems generate individual rebar sets. These can be scheduled and edited, and they survive removal of the system. - When it is off, the bars are internal to the system. - The mode is locked once any area or path system exists. - Hooks in shape definition (on or off). This must be decided before the first rebar is placed and is then locked. - Presentation defaults for new sets, and abbreviations for area and path tags. - Rounding: on or off. Method is Nearest, Up or Down. Separate increments apply to bar length, segment length and fabric-sheet dimensions. Bar types can override the project rounding. - The Properties palette shows rounded values as "exact [rounded]". - Cover: Cover tool. Pick elements or faces, then choose a named cover setting. The Cover Settings dialog creates, duplicates and deletes named cover types with offsets. Each host face stores its cover type, so cover can differ per face.

    UI: Reinforcement Settings dialog (Concrete › Settings › Reinforcement Settings, reinforcement_settings.show()). A tree dialog with four pages; OK commits all pages as one transaction. - General: Area and path reinforcement produce rebar and Include hooks in shape definition. Each is greyed out, with the reason in a tooltip, once it is locked (an area or path system exists; any rebar exists). - Presentation: default set presentation for new sets in plan, section and 3D views (Show All, First/Last, Middle), and the default for spliced sets. - Abbreviations: tag abbreviations for area and path reinforcement layers (for example "T1", "B2", "EF") and for the direction labels. Each abbreviation 1–8 characters, unique per layer. - Rounding: on or off; method (Nearest, Up, Down); increments for bar length, segment length and fabric-sheet dimensions (default 1 mm, 5 mm and 5 mm). Increments must be > 0 and ≤ 100 mm. Bar types with their own rounding are listed read-only with a link to the type.

    UI: Rebar Cover Settings dialog (Concrete › Settings › Cover Settings, rebar_cover_type.manage()). A grid with one row per cover type: name, offset and a usage count (how many host faces use it). - Add creates a row named "New cover N" with offset 25 mm; Duplicate copies the selected row; Delete is allowed only for unused types, or after picking a replacement type that all its faces are moved to. - Names must be unique and non-empty. Offsets must be ≥ 0 and ≤ 500 mm. Changing an offset regenerates every rebar constrained to faces using that type, and the dialog states how many hosts will update before OK. - New projects get the template's cover types; a project always has at least one.

    Data (IFC mapping). No IFC equivalent. - RXD document rebar: settings (HostRebarInAreaPath, HooksInShape, Rounding., Presentation.) and the cover-type table (name, offset). - RXD element data (rebar) on each host: per-face cover assignments (Top, Bottom, Exterior, Interior, Other as cover-type references, with per-face overrides keyed by stable face IDs).

    Commands. - reinforcement_settings.set(key, value) - reinforcement_settings.show() - rebar_cover_type.create(name, offset) -> id - rebar_cover_type.manage() - rebar_cover.assign(host_id, face_ref? , cover_type_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With Nearest/10 mm rounding, a computed bar length of 2 437 mm displays as "2437 [2440]", and schedules use 2 440 mm. - [ ] Trying to change the area/path mode after an area system exists is refused, with an explanation. - [ ] Deleting a cover type used by 12 faces asks for a replacement type; after OK the 12 faces use the replacement and their rebar regenerates in the same transaction. - [ ] Changing the offset of cover type "Interior 25" to 30 mm moves every bar constrained to faces of that type by 5 mm.

    4.2.3 Standard (shape-driven) rebar placement

    ID: STR-RBR-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.2

    Purpose. Place planar or multi-planar bars from a library of shape families into a host.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Concrete › Rebar, or pick it from a selected host's contextual tab. 2. Pick a shape on the contextual tab or in the Shape Browser palette (thumbnails of the loaded shapes). 3. Choose a placement method: - Expand to Host: the shape stretches to fill the host's cover box in the placement plane. - By Two Points: draw a rectangle, aligned to the view or to a picked reference, that the shape fills. This method also places cranked bars. - Sketch: draw the bar's centreline (STR-RBR-007). - Free Form: see STR-RBR-013. 4. Choose a placement plane: current work plane, near cover reference or far cover reference. 5. Choose an orientation: parallel to work plane, parallel to cover or perpendicular to cover. By Two Points adds Horizontal, Vertical and Perpendicular Segment. The [ and ] keys cycle orientations. 6. Choose the set layout (STR-RBR-004) and the set type, standard or varying. Click to place.

    UI. Contextual tab "Modify | Place Rebar" with panels Placement Method, Placement Plane, Placement Orientation, Rebar Set, Set Type, Family (Load Shapes) and Show Tooltip. The optional cursor tooltip lists the keys for rotate, flip and align. Multi-planar shapes such as stirrups with legs in two planes are placed in section views and offer extra orientations.
