    Behaviour & rules. - Placement respects host cover. If a bar cannot fit, Reviera refuses it and explains which dimension failed. - New bars are visible in the placement view and in all section views, and hidden in other views by default (STR-RBR-017).

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcReinforcingBar. PredefinedType comes from the shape style and role: MAIN for main bars, LIGATURE for stirrups and ties, SHEAR, EDGE, RING, ANCHORING, SPACEBAR or PUNCHING. - The type is IfcReinforcingBarType, with NominalDiameter, CrossSectionArea, BarLength, BarSurface (PLAIN or TEXTURED), BendingShapeCode and BendingParameters (the A, B, C… values, in order). - Body geometry: an IfcSweptDiskSolid along the bar centreline, one item per bar in the set, using IfcMappedItem for identical bars. - RXD element data (rebar) holds the layout recipe and identity: HostId, ShapeFamilyId, PlacementMethod, LayoutRule, Quantity, Spacing, ArrayLength, Partition, RebarNumber, Style (Standard or StirrupTie), StirrupTieAttachment, HookStart, HookEnd, HookRotation, EndTreatment, WorkshopInstructions (Bent or Straight) and OverrideHookLengths. - Mass and total length: a standard quantity set where the schema defines one. Otherwise they are computed on load and not stored.

    Commands. - rebar.place(host_id, shape_id, bar_type_id, method: "expand"|"two_points"|"sketch", plane, orientation, points?, layout?) -> rebar_id - rebar_shape_browser.show()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Expand-to-Host of a closed stirrup shape in a 300 × 600 column section with 40 mm cover produces a stirrup whose outer dimensions equal the host dimensions minus twice the cover. - [ ] A placed bar exports as IfcReinforcingBar with its type's BendingShapeCode equal to the shape code of the shape family.

    4.2.4 Rebar set layouts

    ID: STR-RBR-004 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.2 ("Rebar set layout rules")

    Purpose. Distribute identical bars along a direction.

    Behaviour & rules.

    Rule Input Behaviour
    Single — One bar
    Fixed Number n n bars spread evenly over the array length
    Maximum Spacing s Smallest count that keeps centre spacing at or below s
    Number with Spacing n, s n bars at spacing s; the array length follows
    Minimum Clear Spacing c Clear gap at least c; stays valid when bar size changes
    Custom Spacing formula Segment list such as 3x100; ?x200; 5x100. ? marks the one variable segment that absorbs the remaining length. A second syntax, 1400@100; 900@300, gives distance at spacing.
    • Sets are tagged and scheduled as one object with quantity and spacing.
    • Formula errors are reported inline: a non-numeric value, more than one ?, or a total longer than the array length.
    • Individual bars can be hidden or removed and later reset (STR-RBR-006).

    Data (IFC mapping). The IFC body carries one swept solid per bar, so other tools see the true count. RXD element data (rebar) holds the layout recipe: LayoutRule, Quantity, Spacing, ArrayLength and CustomSpacingFormula.

    Commands. rebar.set_layout(rebar_id, rule, n?, spacing?, clear?, formula?)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] 3x100; ?x200; 5x100 over 2 000 mm yields 3 spaces of 100 mm, then 6 of 200 mm, then 5 of 100 mm. That is 14 spaces filling 300 + 1 200 + 500 = 2 000 mm, so 15 bars, with the first bar at 0. - [ ] With Minimum Clear Spacing 50 mm, changing the bar diameter from 12 to 20 mm reduces the count where needed so the clear gap stays at least 50 mm.

    4.2.5 Varying rebar sets

    ID: STR-RBR-005 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.2 ("Varying rebar set")

    Purpose. Sets whose bar lengths change across inclined or skewed straight host faces.

    Workflow. 1. Start Rebar (STR-RBR-003) and choose Varying in the Set Type panel before placing; or select an existing standard set and choose Convert to Varying on its contextual tab. 2. Each bar in the set is re-fitted to the host cover faces at its own position along the array, so bar segments lengthen or shorten with the taper.

    Behaviour & rules. - Only straight inclined faces are supported, not arcs. Reviera explains the refusal when a face is curved. - An existing standard set can be converted to a varying set, and back where the geometry allows. Convert to Standard is refused, naming the bars that differ, when the bars no longer share one length within the rounding increment (STR-RBR-002). - Every layout rule of STR-RBR-004 works on varying sets. Spacing is measured along the array direction, not along the inclined face. - Bar handles constrained to the inclined faces stay constrained per bar; handles on parallel faces keep one shared constraint. - Numbering. Each distinct length (after rounding) is a separate identity for numbering (STR-RBR-016), so a varying set can carry several rebar numbers; tags show the range ("12–17"). - Schedules list each distinct length, or one row per set with minimum and maximum length when the schedule groups by set. - A varying set that regenerates to only one distinct length stays varying until converted.

    Data (IFC mapping). One IfcReinforcingBar per distinct length group, aggregated under one IfcElementAssembly (REINFORCEMENT_UNIT), with the varying flag in RXD element data (rebar). Each group's BarLength is its own length; the set-level layout recipe (STR-RBR-004) is stored once on the assembly.

    Commands. rebar.convert_to_varying(rebar_id), rebar.convert_to_standard(rebar_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A set in a tapered wall produces bars whose lengths follow the taper, and the schedule shows a length range. - [ ] Converting a varying set in a tapered wall back to standard is refused and the message names the number of differing lengths. - [ ] A varying set with five distinct rounded lengths exports one IfcElementAssembly (REINFORCEMENT_UNIT) aggregating five IfcReinforcingBar groups. - [ ] Placing a varying set against a curved wall face is refused with an explanation.

    4.2.6 Rebar editing, propagation and splitting

    ID: STR-RBR-006 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.2 ("Editing")

    Behaviour & rules. - Shape handles: circles at bar ends, triangles on edges, a handle for the bar plane and a handle for the set extent. - In-canvas segment length controls: editable, and rounded according to STR-RBR-002. Hook lengths are read-only unless Override Hook Lengths is on. - Pick New Host and Select Host. - Move Rebar in Set, Remove Bar, Reset Bars and Split Set at a chosen bar. - Propagate: copy and adapt selected bars to other hosts of the same category. Align by Host matches the host's local frame; Align by Face matches a picked face. Constraints are re-solved per target, and targets where they cannot be solved are reported.

    Commands. - rebar.set_segment_length(rebar_id, segment, length) - rebar.move_bar_in_set(rebar_id, bar_index, delta) - rebar.remove_bar(rebar_id, index) - rebar.reset_bars(rebar_id) - rebar.split_set(rebar_id, at_index) -> rebar_id - rebar.propagate(rebar_ids[], target_host_ids[], mode: "host"|"face", face_ref?) -> rebar_ids[] - rebar.pick_new_host(rebar_ids[], host_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Propagating a stirrup set from one beam to 10 beams of different lengths produces 10 sets, each spanning its own beam between covers. - [ ] Splitting a 20-bar set at bar 8 yields two sets of 8 and 12 bars with identical type and shape.

    4.2.7 Sketched rebar and rebar constraints

    ID: STR-RBR-007 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.2 ("Rebar constraints"), §3.2 "Shape matching"

    Purpose. Draw bar centrelines directly, and keep bars constrained to their host.

    Behaviour & rules. - Sketch Rebar: sketch lines and arcs in a plane inside the host. Reviera matches the result to a loaded shape (STR-RBR-008) or creates a new one. - Constraints: each handle can be constrained to a planar reference: - host cover - another bar - host surface (with an offset)

    The reference plane must be parallel to the handle, within 6° for end handles. Straight bars can attach to stirrup bend points at 45° increments. - Edit Constraints mode: - The bar being edited is highlighted in one colour and its constraint target in a second colour (theme tokens, not fixed colours). - The offset is shown as an editable dimension. - Constraints can be disabled, kept or reset to default. - Several sets, including cranked and spliced sets, can be edited together. - When the host changes, constrained handles follow and unconstrained handles keep their absolute positions.

    Data (IFC mapping). No IFC equivalent. RXD element data (constraints) holds one entry per handle: handle ID, target kind (Cover, Bar, Surface), target GlobalId or face reference, and offset.

    Commands. - rebar.sketch(host_id, plane, curves[], bar_type_id, style, hooks?) -> rebar_id - rebar.constrain(rebar_id, handle_id, target_kind, target_ref, offset) - rebar.reset_constraints(rebar_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A longitudinal bar constrained to the top cover moves when the cover type changes from 40 to 50 mm. - [ ] A constraint to a face 10° away from parallel is refused, with an explanation.

    4.2.8 Rebar shapes, shape codes and shape matching

    ID: STR-RBR-008 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.2 ("Rebar shapes and shape codes")

    Purpose. Reviera shall support a parametric family kind, the rebar shape family. It defines a bar's centreline and its dimensions, and a shape code that is used in tags, schedules and bending details.

    Behaviour & rules. - Shape family content: - a sketched centreline of rebar lines - dimension parameters named A, B, C… that become the shape-code segments - major segments - bend and hook definitions - a multi-planar flag - allowable bar types - a status checker that validates the sketch, its dimensions and its constraints, so the family can be used - Shape parameters: style, stirrup/tie attachment, start and end hook settings, shape image, spiral settings, shape code, and whether hooks are included in the shape. - Shape matching: a sketched or free-form bar maps to an existing shape when all of these match: - segment count - joined geometry - hook count and direction - hook bend dimensions - style

    Otherwise Reviera creates a new shape family. It is named with the next free number, which the user can rename. - National shape-code standards: Reviera ships open shape-code catalogues as data files that map a code to a segment pattern. Candidates are ISO 4066 and BS 8666 / ACI 315-style numbering. Each catalogue is authored from the published code structure and not copied from vendor templates. Users can add catalogues. - Shape families can be built in 3D by rotating hooks and cranks out of plane.

    Data (IFC mapping). - The shape code goes to IfcReinforcingBarType.BendingShapeCode, and the ordered A, B, C… values go to BendingParameters (IfcLengthMeasure and IfcPlaneAngleMeasure). - Where a standard pset exists, values are also written to it: Pset_ReinforcingBarBendingsBS8666Common, Pset_ReinforcingBarBendingsISOCD3766Common, Pset_ReinforcingBarBendingsDIN135610Common and Pset_ReinforcingBarBendingsBECCommon. - The shape family itself is an IfcReinforcingBarType. Its RXD family recipe holds the centreline sketch, parameter list and status.

    Commands. - rebar_shape.create_from_sketch(curves[], params, code?) -> shape_id - rebar_shape.match(rebar_id) -> shape_id | null - rebar_shape.check(shape_id) -> issues[] - rebar_shape_catalogue.load(path)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Sketching an L-bar that matches an existing L shape reuses that shape and does not create a new family. - [ ] Adding a 135° hook to the same sketch creates a new shape, because the hook count differs. - [ ] An exported bar carries the shape code and parameters in both IfcReinforcingBarType and the matching standard pset.

    4.2.9 Bar types, hooks and cranks

    ID: STR-RBR-009 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.2 ("Rebar instance and type data", "Hooks", "Cranks")

    Behaviour & rules. - Bar type: - deformation (deformed or plain) - material - bar diameter and model diameter - standard bend diameter, standard hook bend diameter and stirrup/tie bend diameter - a hook length table (one row per hook type) - maximum bend radius - rounding overrides - a graphics subcategory - Hook type: angle, extension multiplier and style. - Cranks: a crank is an offset inside a segment. It is defined by crank length, offset and angle, and is kept inside the cover. - Add Crank acts on an existing bar. Place with Crank uses By Two Points. - Adding a crank re-matches the bar to a shape, or creates one. - Constraints stay editable on cranked bars. - Spiral bars: height, pitch, and base and top finishing turns.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcReinforcingBarType attributes The RXD family recipe of the bar type holds what IFC cannot: ModelDiameter, BendDiameters, HookLengthTable and MaxBendRadius. Hook types are kept in RXD document rebar. Cranks are RXD element data (rebar): SegmentIndex, Position, Length, Offset and Angle.

    Commands. - rebar_bar_type.create(name, diameter, material_id, ...) -> type_id - rebar_hook_type.create(name, angle, extension_multiplier) -> id - rebar.add_crank(rebar_id, segment, position, length, offset, angle)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Adding a 75 mm crank to segment A of a straight bar produces a bar whose crank stays inside cover, and a matching cranked shape is used or created.

    4.2.10 Area reinforcement

    ID: STR-RBR-010 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.3

    Purpose. Lay out orthogonal bar layers over a region of a floor, wall or foundation slab.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Concrete › Area and select the host. 2. Sketch a closed boundary. The parallel-line symbol marks the major direction edge, which can be changed. 3. Click Finish. A reinforcement symbol and tag are placed.

    The Whole Host option uses the host outline as the boundary.

    Behaviour & rules. - Layout rule: Maximum Spacing or Fixed Number. - Additional top/exterior and bottom/interior cover offsets allow layers to be stacked. - Layers: Top/Bottom for floors, Exterior/Interior for walls, each × Major/Minor. Each layer has an on/off toggle, bar type, hook type, hook orientation and spacing. - Host openings cut the bars. - In "real rebar" mode (STR-RBR-002) the bars are rebar sets that can be seen in section. Remove Area System keeps them.

    Data (IFC mapping). - The system is an IfcElementAssembly with REINFORCEMENT_UNIT, with its recipe (Boundary, MajorDirection, LayoutRule, Layers[]) in RXD element data (rebar). - The bars are IfcReinforcingBar elements aggregated into the system. - The symbol is view-specific annotation (chapter 5).

    Commands. - area_reinforcement.create(host_id, boundary | "whole_host", major_edge, layers[], layout_rule) -> system_id - area_reinforcement.remove_system(system_id) -> rebar_ids[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 6 × 4 m slab region with top and bottom × major and minor at 200 mm produces four layers, cut around a 1 × 1 m opening. - [ ] Remove Area System in real-rebar mode leaves four rebar sets that can be scheduled.

    4.2.11 Path reinforcement

    ID: STR-RBR-011 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.4

    Purpose. Bars laid perpendicular to an open path along a slab or wall edge, for example edge U-bars and top bars over supports.

    Workflow. Choose Concrete › Path and sketch an open path. A flip control chooses the side. Finish.

    Behaviour & rules. - Parameters: layout rule, additional offset, face (top or bottom), bar spacing or number of bars. - Primary bar: type, length, shape (single segment or with perpendicular segments), and start and end hooks. - Optional alternating bars with their own type, length, shape and offset. - The reinforcement volume is calculated. - Path boundary visibility can be controlled through visibility/graphics overrides.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcElementAssembly REINFORCEMENT_UNIT with its recipe in RXD element data (rebar). The bars are IfcReinforcingBar.

    Commands. path_reinforcement.create(host_id, path_curves[], side, primary, alternating?, spacing | count, face) -> system_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 5 m path at 150 mm spacing with alternating bars offset by 300 mm produces primary and alternating bars in the correct pattern.

    4.2.12 Fabric (welded wire) reinforcement

    ID: STR-RBR-012 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.5 · screenshots/structure_mep/fabric_area_sheet_layout.png

    Purpose. Mesh sheets placed by area or one at a time.

    Behaviour & rules. - Fabric area: - Select a floor, wall or slab and sketch a closed boundary. The major direction sets sheet rotation. - Edge controls on the bounding rectangle set the start and end edges, sheet alignment and lap splices. Lap position is Aligned or Staggered. - Sheets are cut by the boundary and by host openings. - Single fabric sheet: sheets snap to cover, sheet edges, lap positions and midpoints. Cut by Host Cover clips them. - Bent fabric sheet: sketched from a cross-section profile. - Custom fabric sheets: user-edited wire layouts, or rule-generated sheets in precast (STR-PRE-004). - Fabric wire type: diameter and material. - Fabric sheet type: major and minor wire type, spacing, overhangs, layout pattern, unit weight, and sheet length and width.

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcReinforcingMesh (PredefinedType USERDEFINED or NOTDEFINED), typed by IfcReinforcingMeshType with MeshLength, MeshWidth, Longitudinal/TransverseBarNominalDiameter, Longitudinal/TransverseBarCrossSectionArea, Longitudinal/TransverseBarSpacing, BendingShapeCode and BendingParameters (for bent sheets). - The fabric area is an IfcElementAssembly REINFORCEMENT_UNIT with its recipe (Boundary, MajorDirection, LapSplicePosition, LapLengths) in RXD element data (rebar).

    Commands. - fabric_area.create(host_id, boundary, major_edge, sheet_type_id, lap_position, start_edge?) -> system_id - fabric_sheet.place(host_id, sheet_type_id, point, rotation, cut_by_cover?) -> id - fabric_sheet.create_bent(host_id, profile_curves[], sheet_type_id, extent) -> id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A fabric area over a slab with one opening produces sheets clipped by both the boundary and the opening, with the configured lap lengths. - [ ] Switching from Aligned to Staggered moves every second row of lap splices by half a sheet length.

    4.2.13 Free-form rebar

    ID: STR-RBR-013 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.6

    Purpose. Bars in hosts with complex or curved geometry, placed by picking host faces in 3D views.

    Behaviour & rules. - Surface distribution: - Non-planar bars are interpolated between a first bar and a last bar. Each of those is defined by where a start or end surface meets the host surface. - The bars follow the host surface and respect cover. Where faces have different covers, the largest cover is used. - Aligned distribution: - Planar bars. Each bar plane cuts the host surfaces, and the planes are aligned along a distribution path built from host edges. - Path constraints are edited as Path Surface 1/2 in Edit Constraints. - Each face's own cover is used. - This suits stirrups in members with varying sections. - Shape matching for free-form bars uses Workshop Instructions = Bent. If no shape can describe the geometry, the bar reports only its total length. - Free-form sets accept cranks and couplers.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcReinforcingBar. Bars use per-bar IfcSweptDiskSolid geometry along IfcIndexedPolyCurve or B-spline centrelines. RXD element data (rebar) records Distribution = "Surface" or "Aligned", with the constraint surfaces referenced by stable face IDs.

    Commands. rebar.place_free_form(host_id, kind: "surface"|"aligned", start_face, end_face, path_edges?, bar_type_id, layout) -> rebar_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A surface distribution on a doubly curved shell keeps every bar at the specified cover within 1 mm at sampled points. - [ ] An aligned distribution in a tapered beam produces stirrups whose sizes follow the taper.

    4.2.14 Path shape distribution and morphed distribution

    ID: STR-RBR-014 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.6 ("[2027] Path Free Form Rebar", "Morphed") · screenshots/structure_mep/rebar_3d_path_shape_distribution_2027.png · screenshots/structure_mep/rebar_morphed_longitudinal_distribution_2027.png

    Purpose. Two advanced distributions for infrastructure-type geometry such as bridges and tunnels.

    Behaviour & rules. - Path shape distribution: 1. Place a main bar in a section view by Two Points, Expand to Host or Sketch. 2. Click Path and select one or more continuous host edges. 3. Finish.

    Identical planar bars are then distributed along the double-curved edge path. Bar segments can be constrained to edges so that the set follows changes to the host. The distribution range and the main bar can be edited later, and bar lengths may vary. - Morphed distribution: select a transverse stirrup set (circular, spiral or multi-segment). Longitudinal bars are generated that follow the stirrup shape, and they update when the stirrups change.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcReinforcingBar. RXD element data (rebar) records Distribution = "Path" or "Morphed", with the driver set's GlobalId (morphed) or PathEdgeRefs (path).

    Commands. - rebar.distribute_along_path(main_rebar_id, edge_refs[], range?) -> rebar_id - rebar.distribute_morphed(driver_stirrup_set_id, bar_type_id, count | spacing) -> rebar_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing a driver stirrup set's diameter regenerates the morphed longitudinal bars inside the new stirrup outline. - [ ] A path distribution along a 3D-curved edge keeps each bar plane perpendicular to the path tangent.

    4.2.15 Splices and couplers

    ID: STR-RBR-015 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.7 · screenshots/structure_mep/rebar_couplers.png

    Behaviour & rules. - Splice: - Splice on a selected set, by Pick Line or By Length. - Lap and stagger lengths come from the splice type or from the bar type. - Spliced sets are constrained to each other and move together. - Splicing is supported only on straight segments of shape-driven rebar. It is refused for spiral, arc, multi-planar, area, path and free-form bars. Free-form longitudinal splicing is an open question (§4.17). - Coupler: - Concrete › Coupler: On Bar End or Between Two Bars. - The coupler type is sized to the bar automatically, and a type is created when none fits. - Tolerances: the bar ends must be no more than 10 bar diameters apart and offset by no more than 3 diameters. Arc bars must share a centre. - Couplers apply end treatments that shorten the bars. - Couplers can be scheduled, grouped, numbered per partition, tagged, and propagated across sets. - The coupler family option Align to View hides a coupler when the view direction is more than 75° from the bar axis. - Couplers always display as solids in 3D.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Couplers are IfcMechanicalFastener. In IFC4, PredefinedType is USERDEFINED with ObjectType "COUPLER"; in IFC4X3 it is COUPLER where available. The type is IfcMechanicalFastenerType. - The coupler is connected to both bars through IfcRelConnectsWithRealizingElements, with the bars as relating and related elements and the coupler as the realizing element. - Splices are stored in RXD element data (rebar): SpliceTypeId, LapLength, Stagger and partner GlobalIds.

    Commands. - rebar.splice(rebar_id, mode: "line"|"length", line? , length?, splice_type_id?) -> rebar_ids[] - rebar_coupler.place(bar_end_refs[1..2], type_id?) -> coupler_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Placing a coupler between two Ø25 bar ends 300 mm apart is refused, because the gap is more than 10 diameters (250 mm). - [ ] A spliced set exports two bars per splice location, connected by the configured lap length.

    4.2.16 Reinforcement numbering and partitions

    ID: STR-RBR-016 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.1 ("Reinforcement numbering and partitions") · screenshots/structure_mep/rebar_partitions_by_level.png

    Purpose. Give identical reinforcement elements identical numbers within a partition.

    Behaviour & rules. - Each rebar set, fabric sheet and coupler gets a Rebar Number. - Elements that are identical in type, size, material and shape, including segment values after rounding, share a number within the same Partition. - Partition is a free-text instance value, used for phase, host type, location, top or bottom, and so on. - Rebar, fabric and couplers each have their own number sequence. - Reinforcement Numbers dialog: list the sequences per partition, change a start number, remove gaps and renumber. - Numbers update on regeneration when an element's identity changes. Locked numbers (an option) do not.

    UI: Reinforcement Numbers dialog (Concrete › Settings › Reinforcement Numbers, reinforcement_numbering.show(partition?)). - A partition list on the left (every partition name in use, plus "(none)"), with a filter box. partition preselects one. - For the selected partition, three tabs (Rebar, Fabric, Couplers), each a grid with: number, element count, a short identity summary (bar type, shape code, main dimensions), locked flag, and a Select button that selects those elements in the model. - Per sequence: Start number (integer ≥ 1); Remove gaps; Renumber (reassigns numbers in creation order, keeping locked numbers fixed and skipping them). - Per row: change a number to a free value (refused, with the conflicting row highlighted, if the value is used by a different identity in the same sequence), lock or unlock. - All edits apply on OK as one transaction; Cancel discards them.

    Data (IFC mapping). The rebar number is written to IfcReinforcingBar.Tag, and to Pset_PrecastConcreteElementFabrication.PieceMark where an exchange requires it. Partition and lock flag: RXD element data (rebar). Sequences: RXD document model/rebar.

    Commands. - reinforcement_numbering.renumber(partition?, kind: "rebar"|"fabric"|"coupler", start?, remove_gaps?) - reinforcement_numbering.show(partition?) - rebar.set_partition(ids[], name)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Two identical stirrup sets in partition "L1" share number 5. Moving one to partition "L2" gives it a number in L2's sequence. - [ ] Remove gaps turns the sequence 1, 2, 4, 7 into 1, 2, 3, 4 without changing which elements share numbers. - [ ] In the dialog, typing number 3 for a row when 3 belongs to another identity in the same partition and kind is refused and the other row is highlighted. - [ ] Renumbering a sequence with number 4 locked keeps 4 on its elements and numbers the others 1, 2, 3, 5, ….

    4.2.17 Rebar visibility and presentation

    ID: STR-RBR-017 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.2 ("Rebar presentation", "View visibility"), §3.8

    Purpose. Control, per view, which bars of a set are drawn and whether they show through or as solids, so that drawings stay readable.

    Workflow. 1. Select one or more rebar sets (or area, path or fabric systems). 2. On the contextual tab, choose View Visibility States (a grid of the project's views with Unobscured and Solid check boxes per view; Solid is enabled only for 3D views), or choose a presentation mode in the Presentation panel, which applies to the active view. 3. For Select, click the bars to show; Enter finishes. The picks are journaled as micro-operations so an unfinished pick session is recovered after a crash (§2.1 of the conventions).

    Behaviour & rules. - Per-instance, per-view visibility states: - View unobscured: the bars show through the host. - View as solid: applies in 3D views at Fine detail. At Coarse and Medium detail bars are drawn as centrelines. - Default visibility: the placement view and all section views. Rebar cut by a section is always shown. - Set presentation per view: Show All, Show First/Last, Show Middle, or Select (pick the bars to show). - First/Last and Middle draw a set extent line with end ticks spanning the whole set, so the distribution is still shown. - The default for new sets comes from Reinforcement Settings (STR-RBR-002). - Select keeps bar indices; if the bar count later drops below a picked index, that pick is dropped and the view falls back to Show All when no picks remain. - Spliced set presentation: show representative bars per lap zone. - Presentation changes only what is drawn. Tags, schedules and IFC export always count every bar. - View templates (chapter 5) can carry a rebar presentation default that overrides the per-set mode in views using the template. - Visibility and presentation edits are view data and are undoable.

    Data (IFC mapping). View-dependent settings are stored with the view's own RXD data (chapter 5), as a map from rebar GlobalId to Unobscured, Solid and Presentation (mode plus selected indices). Nothing is written to the rebar's IFC entity.

    Commands. - rebar.set_view_visibility(rebar_ids[], view_id, unobscured?, solid?) - rebar.set_presentation(rebar_ids[], view_id, mode, selected_indices?)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Show Middle in a plan view draws one representative bar and the set extent line, and other views are not affected. - [ ] A set set to Unobscured in a 3D view is visible through its concrete host there, and stays hidden by the host in a second 3D view. - [ ] A set of 15 bars shown with Show First/Last still tags as quantity 15 and exports 15 bar bodies. - [ ] Solid cannot be ticked for a plan view in the View Visibility States grid.

    4.2.18 Rebar documentation

    ID: STR-RBR-018 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.8

    Purpose. Annotate and schedule reinforcement for placing drawings and bar bending schedules.

    Workflow. - Tag: Annotate › Tag by Category, click a set; the tag attaches to the set (or to the representative bar shown by STR-RBR-017). - Multi-rebar annotation: choose Aligned or Linear, pick one or more sets, place the dimension line, then the tag. Picks are journaled as micro-operations (§2.1 of the conventions). - Bending detail: select a set, choose Bending Detail, click to place in the view; the scale and rotation can be set before the click.

    Behaviour & rules. - Rebar tags read number, shape code, bar size, spacing and quantity. - Multi-rebar annotation: an aligned or linear dimension plus a tag that spans a set or several sets. - The dimension measures the set extent and the tag reads quantity, size and spacing (for example "15 Ø12 @ 150"). - Several sets are accepted only if they are parallel; otherwise the pick is refused with a message. - The annotation follows the sets when they move and is deleted with the last set it references. - Bending detail: a view-specific annotation that draws a bar's shape with its segment dimensions. It updates when the bar changes. - Segment labels and dimension values use the shape's A–R parameters after rounding (STR-RBR-002). Hooks are drawn with their angle. - Varying sets (STR-RBR-005) show the range of each varying segment ("1 200–1 650"). - Rebar schedule (chapter 5 schedule engine): bar number, shape code, segments A–R, quantity, total length and mass. It can be filtered by partition. - Mass is length × nominal mass per metre of the bar type. Totals use rounded lengths when rounding is on. - A bending-schedule template that groups by partition and bar number is shipped.

    Data (IFC mapping). Annotation entities as defined in chapter 5. Schedule fields read IfcReinforcingBar, IfcReinforcingBarType and RXD element data (rebar). Multi-rebar annotations and bending details store the GlobalIds of their referenced sets in their own view-specific RXD data.

    Commands. - rebar_tag.place(rebar_id, view_id, point, tag_type_id) -> id - multi_rebar_annotation.place(rebar_ids[], view_id, kind: "aligned"|"linear", line) -> id - bending_detail.place(rebar_id, view_id, point, scale?) -> id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing segment B of a bar updates its bending detail and the schedule's B column in the same regeneration. - [ ] A multi-rebar annotation on a set of 15 Ø12 bars at 150 mm reads "15 Ø12 @ 150" and its dimension equals the set extent (2 100 mm). - [ ] Picking two non-parallel sets for one multi-rebar annotation is refused with a message. - [ ] The schedule's mass column for 10 bars of 6 m Ø16 (1.578 kg/m) shows 94.7 kg.

    4.3 Structural analytical model, loads and analysis

    Design stance. Reviera's analytical model is independent, following the reference product's current design rather than its older automatic one. Analytical elements are stand-alone, persisted elements. They are optionally associated with physical elements, and they respond to physical changes only when asked (automation). The whole analytical model is one IfcStructuralAnalysisModel per analysis scenario. A default model named "Analytical Model" is created on first use.

    Ref: research/03 §4.1 · screenshots/structure_mep/analytical_automation_physical_to_analytical.png

    4.3.1 Analytical members

    ID: STR-AM-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §4.2

    Purpose. Line elements that idealise beams, columns and braces.

    Workflow. Choose Analyze › Structural Analytical Model › Analytical Member. - Top Point Definition: one click creates a vertical member between the current level and the level below. - Start/End Point Definition: draw a line or an arc, with 3D snapping and chain.

    Nodes are created at both ends (STR-AM-003).

    UI. Properties: - highest and lowest associated level - structural material and physical material asset - structural role: Beam, Column, Brace, Member or Tie - section type, filtered to loaded framing or column types - section shape - cross-section rotation - start and end releases: Fixed, Pinned or User (six DOF flags) - Analyze As - the associated physical element (read-only)

    Behaviour & rules. - A member exists without any physical element. - Changing the section type does not change any physical element until Analytical to Physical (STR-AM-006) is run. - The member's local coordinate system is set by its end nodes and the cross-section rotation.

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcStructuralCurveMember. PredefinedType: RIGID_JOINED_MEMBER by default, PIN_JOINED_MEMBER when both ends release all rotations, and TENSION_MEMBER or COMPRESSION_MEMBER from Analyze As. - Axis: IfcDirection. Topology: an IfcEdge representation between two IfcVertexPoints. - Material and section: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage with IfcRelAssociatesMaterial. - End releases: IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember to each end node, with AppliedCondition IfcBoundaryNodeCondition (translational and rotational stiffness per axis) and ConditionCoordinateSystem. - The member is included in the model through IfcRelAssignsToGroup (RelatingGroup = IfcStructuralAnalysisModel). - RXD element data (analysis): StructuralRole, HighestLevel, LowestLevel and AnalyzeAs, where the PredefinedType cannot express them.

    Commands. - analytical_member.create(curve, section_type_id, material_id, role, releases?) -> id - analytical_member.create_vertical(point, level, section_type_id) -> id - analytical_member.set_releases(id, end, dof_flags | preset)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A member created with no physical counterpart persists through save and reload as an IfcStructuralCurveMember with two IfcStructuralPointConnection ends. - [ ] Setting both ends to Pinned exports with zero rotational stiffness in the end conditions.

    4.3.2 Analytical panels and openings

    ID: STR-AM-002 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §4.2

    Purpose. Surface elements that idealise walls, floors and roofs.

    Workflow. - Panel by Boundary: a planar panel sketched on a reference plane. The plane can be changed later. - Panel by Extrusion: a curved panel. A profile drawn on a work plane is extruded perpendicular to it, by 3 m (10 ft) by default. - Analytical Opening: sketched inside a panel.

    Behaviour & rules. - Properties: thickness, material, structural role (floor, wall, roof), Analyze As (shell, membrane or bending plate) and openings. - Panels can be split along a line. - Cladding panels carry and transfer lateral wind and snow loads to their supports but add no stiffness. They are flagged and excluded from the stiffness matrix by providers. - Panels align to supports when automation creates them (STR-AM-006).

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcStructuralSurfaceMember. PredefinedType is SHELL, BENDING_ELEMENT or MEMBRANE_ELEMENT; cladding panels use USERDEFINED with ObjectType "CLADDING". - Thickness: the Thickness attribute. Geometry: an IfcFaceSurface topology representation. - Openings are inner bounds of the face, and their editable sketches are kept as RXD element data (constraints).

    Commands. - analytical_panel.create_by_boundary(plane, boundary_curves[], thickness, material_id, role) -> id - analytical_panel.create_by_extrusion(work_plane, profile_curves[], depth, thickness, material_id) -> id - analytical_panel.split(id, line) -> ids[] - analytical_opening.create(panel_id, boundary_curves[]) -> id - analytical_panel.set_cladding(id, bool)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A curved panel by extrusion exports as an IfcStructuralSurfaceMember on a cylindrical face. - [ ] A cladding panel loaded with an area wind load is reported to providers with stiffness excluded.

    4.3.3 Analytical nodes and links

    ID: STR-AM-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §4.2

    Behaviour & rules. - Nodes are never placed directly. - End nodes sit at member ends and panel corners. They merge when elements are joined within tolerance. - Hosted nodes sit inside a member or panel, are drawn smaller and are driven by the host. - Each node keeps an associated level plus offset, and follows level moves. Optionally it follows grids. - Nodes define the orientation of the local coordinate system. - Analytical links: a connection between two nodes, rigid by default. - Fixity is set per link type: translation and rotation per axis, fixed or released. - A link is deleted when either node is deleted. - Links cannot be associated with physical elements.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Nodes: IfcStructuralPointConnection with an IfcVertexPoint representation, plus RXD element data (analysis): Kind (End or Hosted), host GlobalId, level GlobalId, offset and FollowsGrids. - Links: IfcStructuralCurveMember with PredefinedType USERDEFINED and ObjectType "RIGID_LINK", with the link type in RXD element data (analysis). Fixity is expressed through IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember.AppliedCondition at each end. This open choice is recorded in §4.17.

    Commands. - analytical_link.create(node_a, node_b, link_type_id) -> id - analytical_link_type.create(name, fixity[6]) -> id - analytical_node.merge(tolerance?)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Moving a level by 200 mm moves all nodes associated with it by 200 mm, and the members attached to them follow. - [ ] Deleting a node deletes the links attached to it and reports the count.

    4.3.4 Physical–analytical association

    ID: STR-AM-004 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §4.2 ("Association")

    Behaviour & rules. - An association is a group that relates any number of physical elements to any number of analytical elements. Each element can belong to only one association. - Commands: Add, Highlight and Remove. - Assisted Association proposes matches by proximity, orientation and section similarity. The user accepts or rejects each one. - Any physical element can be associated, including in-place families and group members.

    Data (IFC mapping). - A one-to-many association uses IfcRelAssignsToProduct, with RelatingProduct = physical element and RelatedObjects = analytical items. - A many-to-many association uses an IfcGroup with ObjectType "AnalyticalAssociation" that contains all members through IfcRelAssignsToGroup. - Reviera reads both forms on import.

    Commands. - analytical_association.add(physical_ids[], analytical_ids[]) -> association_id - analytical_association.remove(association_id) - analytical_association.suggest(scope?) -> proposals[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Trying to add an element that already belongs to an association is refused, and the existing association is named. - [ ] Assisted Association on a 10-column grid frame proposes 10 one-to-one pairs.

    4.3.5 Loads

    ID: STR-LOAD-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §4.3

    Purpose. Point, line and area actions applied to analytical elements.

    Workflow. Choose Analyze › Analytical Loads › Loads, then pick one of: - Point load: on an end point, or at a picked position - Line load: on a host (a whole member or panel edge), or along a defined path - Area load: on a host (a whole panel), or inside a defined boundary, including sloped area loads

    Behaviour & rules. - Every load has exactly one analytical host. It follows the host and is deleted with it. A load may lie outside its host, with a warning. Is Constrained on Host records whether the load is constrained. - Properties: - load case; nature (read-only, from the case) - orientation: Project, Host Local CS or Work Plane - Fx, Fy, Fz, Mx, My, Mz. Line and area loads take start and end, or three-corner, values for linear variation. - Projected (for line and area loads) - Is Reaction - The display scale per force or moment unit comes from Structural Settings (STR-SET-001).

    Data (IFC mapping).

    Load Activity entity Applied load Notes
    Point IfcStructuralPointAction IfcStructuralLoadSingleForce —
    Line IfcStructuralCurveAction IfcStructuralLoadLinearForce ProjectedOrTrue = PROJECTED_LENGTH or TRUE_LENGTH; PredefinedType CONST or LINEAR
    Area IfcStructuralPlanarAction IfcStructuralLoadPlanarForce PredefinedType CONST, BILINEAR, …
    • The host link is IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity (RelatingElement = member, panel or node).
    • The load case is set by assigning the action to an IfcStructuralLoadCase through IfcRelAssignsToGroup.
    • Orientation is expressed through the action's coordinate system (GlobalOrLocal). IsConstrainedOnHost and IsReaction are RXD element data (analysis).

    Commands. - load.create_point(host_id, position?, case_id, forces[6], orientation) -> id - load.create_line(host_id, path?, case_id, start[6], end[6], orientation, projected?) -> id - load.create_area(host_id, boundary?, case_id, values[3][3], orientation, projected?) -> id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Deleting an analytical member deletes its 4 line loads, and the confirmation names the count. - [ ] A trapezoidal line load exports as IfcStructuralCurveAction with LINEAR distribution and the correct end values. - [ ] Changing a load's case updates its nature display immediately.

    4.3.6 Load cases, natures, combinations and usages

    ID: STR-LC-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §4.4 · screenshots/structure_mep/load_cases_and_combinations_dialog.png

    Purpose. A single dialog to define how loads are grouped and combined.

    UI. Analyze › Load Cases & Combinations (or the shortcut buttons in Structural Settings, STR-SET-001) opens one dialog, load_case.manage(tab?), with tabs (tab = code, natures, cases, combinations or usages): - Design Code: region and code selection, the template file in use and its version, and Load template… for a user template. - Load Natures: grid of name, IFC action source, action type (permanent, variable, accidental) and source (Code or User). Code natures are read-only except their display name. - Load Cases: grid of name, nature (drop-down), category, self-weight flag, and a read-only count of loads in the case. Add, Duplicate, Delete. - Load Combinations: grid of name, formula, limit state, usages, plus one factor column per case that can be shown instead of the formula. Generate… opens the proposals list described below. - Load Usages: list of usage tags with add, rename and delete; deleting a usage removes it from combinations.

    Grids support copy and paste with spreadsheets as tab-separated text.

    Validation in the dialog (shown inline per cell; OK is disabled while any error remains): - Names are unique within natures, cases, combinations and usages, are non-empty and contain no *, + or -, so formulas parse. - A formula references only existing cases or combinations, has numeric factors, and cannot reference itself directly or through another combination. - A case cannot be deleted from inside a formula; it must be deleted on the Load Cases tab, which shows the cascade counts (STR-GEN-002). - Every case must have a nature; a nature in use cannot be deleted.

    OK commits all tabs as one transaction ("Load Cases and Combinations"); Cancel discards everything, including generated proposals not yet added.

    Behaviour & rules. - Choosing a region and design code fills the load nature list from an open code template (a Lua or JSON data file shipped with Reviera). Example natures are dead, live, wind, snow, seismic, roof live, temperature and accidental. - Each nature records its source: Code or User. User natures are kept when the code changes. - Load cases have a name, nature and category. Deleting a case warns that its loads will be deleted and that it will be removed from combinations, and then does both. - Load combinations have: - a name - a formula such as 1.35*DL1 + 1.5*LL1, edited as text or as per-case factor columns - a limit state: Ultimate, Serviceability, Quasi-permanent, Frequent, Rare, Accidental or Special - usages, user-defined tags such as Gravity, Lateral or Combined - Automatic combination generation: a local, offline rule engine reads the selected code template and generates combinations. Candidate templates are EN 1990 equations 6.10/6.10a/b and the ASCE 7 basic combinations, written as editable data. Cases whose nature does not fit the template are flagged. The user reviews the proposals and picks Add to table.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Cases: IfcStructuralLoadCase (PredefinedType LOAD_CASE). ActionType: PERMANENT_G, VARIABLE_Q or EXTRAORDINARY_A. ActionSource from the nature: DEAD_LOAD_G, LIVE_LOAD_Q, SNOW_S, WIND_W, EARTHQUAKE_E, TEMPERATURE_T, … Self-weight coefficients where they apply. - Combinations: IfcStructuralLoadGroup with PredefinedType LOAD_COMBINATION. Each case is assigned with IfcRelAssignsToGroupByFactor, and its factor is the case coefficient. - Limit state is written to the group's Purpose. Usages are RXD element data (analysis). - Natures, code selection and combination templates: RXD document analysis. - All groups are related to the IfcStructuralAnalysisModel through LoadedBy.

    Commands. - load_case.create(name, nature, category) -> id - load_case.delete(id) - load_combination.create(name, formula, limit_state, usages[]) -> id - load_combination.generate(code_template_id, options) -> proposals[] - load_nature.create(name, action_source) -> id - structural_code.set(region, code_id) - load_case.manage(tab?) (opens the dialog; the edits it commits are undoable as one item)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Entering 1.35*G + 1.5*Q creates a combination with two IfcRelAssignsToGroupByFactor relations, with factors 1.35 and 1.5. - [ ] A combination formula 1.0*C1 where C1 is itself a combination that references the first one is flagged as circular and OK stays disabled. - [ ] load_case.manage("combinations") opens the dialog on the Load Combinations tab. - [ ] Deleting case Q warns that 12 loads and 3 combinations are affected, and after confirmation removes the loads and strips Q from the 3 formulas. - [ ] The EN 1990 template generates ULS and SLS combinations offline, with no network access.

    4.3.7 Boundary conditions

    ID: STR-BC-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §4.5 · screenshots/structure_mep/boundary_conditions_on_analytical_panel.png

    Workflow. Choose Analyze › Boundary Conditions, then Point, Line or Area. Pick the host. Point conditions can be positioned anywhere on the host with temporary dimensions.

    Behaviour & rules. - The state is Fixed, Pinned, Roller or User. User states set each translation and rotation DOF to Fixed, Released or Spring, with a spring modulus. - Each state has its own symbol family, set in Structural Settings, along with the spacing of line and area symbols. Default symbol families are open, Reviera-authored content. - Boundary conditions can be tagged, filtered and scheduled.

    Data (IFC mapping).

    Kind Connection entity Applied condition
    Point IfcStructuralPointConnection IfcBoundaryNodeCondition (TranslationalStiffnessX/Y/Z, RotationalStiffnessX/Y/Z as IfcBoolean for fixed or released, or a linear or rotational stiffness measure for springs)
    Line IfcStructuralCurveConnection IfcBoundaryEdgeCondition
    Area IfcStructuralSurfaceConnection IfcBoundaryFaceCondition

    All are connected to their host with IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember and record the named state (Fixed, Pinned, Roller, User) as RXD element data (analysis).

    Commands. boundary_condition.create(kind: "point"|"line"|"area", host_id, location?, state, dof?: {tx,ty,tz,rx,ry,rz}) -> id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A Pinned point condition exports with all three translations fixed and all rotations released. - [ ] A User condition with Tz = Spring of 5 000 kN/m exports TranslationalStiffnessZ = 5.0E6 N/m.

    4.3.8 Analytical automation

    ID: STR-AM-006 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §4.2 ("Automation"), §13.7

    Purpose. Generate or update one model from the other on demand.

    Behaviour & rules. - Physical → Analytical: runs on selected physical elements, or on all supported elements that have no association. - It creates members and panels, aligns them to levels and grids within tolerances, connects nodes, aligns panels to supports, and uses core-layer thickness. - It creates the associations. - It also re-runs on demand for elements that changed, including new openings. - Analytical → Physical: creates or updates columns, framing, walls and floors from analytical elements. That includes section changes that come from analysis results. - Rule packages are Lua scripts: Reviera's equivalent of the reference's visual-programming packages, and a candidate for the future Lua node editor. Users can copy and edit them through Automation Customization. The default package ships with Reviera under GPL-3.0-or-later. - Disconnect: removes the associations and leaves both models in place. - Every run writes a log with created, updated and skipped elements and the reason for each. - Updates skip analytical elements flagged as manually adjusted (STR-AM-008) unless the run option Overwrite manual adjustments is on; skipped elements are logged with that reason. After a run, the consistency check (STR-AM-007) runs on the touched elements when automatic checks are on.

    Data (IFC mapping). Runs create and update the entities in STR-AM-001 to 004. Run history (package, version, timestamp, counts): RXD document analysis.

    Commands. - analytical_automation.physical_to_analytical(element_ids[] | "unassociated", package_id?) -> report - analytical_automation.analytical_to_physical(element_ids[], package_id?) -> report - analytical_automation.disconnect(element_ids[])

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] On a 3-storey, 4 × 3-bay steel frame with slabs, Physical → Analytical creates members for every column and beam and panels for every slab. The nodes are connected, and the solver interface (ANA-FEA-001) reports no unconnected nodes. - [ ] Changing an analytical member's section and running Analytical → Physical changes the associated beam's type.

    4.3.9 Analytical model checks: supports and consistency

    ID: STR-AM-007 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §4.1–4.2, §15.1 · web: Analytical Model Settings · web: Modifying Elective Checking Criteria and Tolerances · web: Automatic Checks

    Purpose. Find problems in the analytical model, and between it and the physical model, before it is sent to an analysis provider: members that nothing supports, nodes that should meet but do not, analytical elements that have drifted from their physical counterparts, and hints of instability.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Analyze › Structural Analytical Model › Check Supports or Check Consistency. Choose the scope: whole model (default), current selection, or elements visible in the active view. 2. The check runs in the background (ANA-GEN-001) and opens the Analytical Checks palette with the results. 3. Review each issue: Select, Zoom to, Isolate (a temporary view isolation of the elements and their neighbours within the support distance), or Ignore with an optional reason. 4. Fix the model (for example with STR-AM-008 adjust, analytical_node.merge, or a boundary condition), then Re-check. Fixed issues drop off the list; issues still present keep their ignore state. 5. Automatic mode: when Member supports or Analytical/physical consistency is turned on in Structural Settings (STR-SET-001), the corresponding check runs incrementally after every committed transaction that adds, moves or deletes structural or analytical elements. It checks only the changed elements and their neighbours within the support distance, and posts new issues to the project warnings list (chapter 1) as well as the palette. Both modes are off by default, because early, incomplete models would produce many warnings.

    UI. Analytical Checks is a dockable palette (§4.0.3): - a toolbar with scope, Check Supports, Check Consistency, Re-check, a severity filter (Error, Warning, Hint, Info), Show ignored and Export CSV - a tree grouped by check, then by issue; each issue row shows severity, a message, the element names and IDs, and where relevant the measured distance against the tolerance (for example "node gap 42 mm > merge distance 5 mm") - in the canvas, issue locations are marked with a temporary graphic (a ring at the node or a highlight along the edge) while the palette is open.

    Behaviour & rules.

    Support check (check_supports). Each analytical member and panel (and each physical structural element that has no association, using its location line or core mid-plane) must be carried by something:

    Code Issue Rule Severity
    S1 Unsupported member A column's lower end, both ends of a beam or brace, and the bearing edge of a panel must each lie within the support distance of another structural element, an analytical link or a boundary condition. Columns and walls are supported from below; beams and braces at their ends; floors along at least one edge or at points. Warning
    S2 Circular support A chain of supports loops back on itself (beam A carried by beam B carried by beam A) without reaching a boundary condition or foundation. Can be turned off in Structural Settings. Warning
    S3 No supports in scope The scope contains no boundary condition at all. Error

    Consistency check (check_consistency). Each criterion can be turned on or off in Structural Settings; C1–C7 are on by default, C8 is off.

    Code Issue Rule Severity
    C1 Disconnected nodes Two end nodes, or an end node and a member or panel edge, lie closer than the support distance but farther than the node merge distance, so they look connected but are not. Also free member ends that touch nothing and carry no boundary condition. Warning
    C2 Isolated part A connected group of analytical elements has no boundary condition, link or support path to one; the solver would see a mechanism. Error
    C3 Physical/analytical mismatch For associated elements, the analytical axis or surface lies farther than the analytical-to-physical distance from the physical location line, core mid-plane or default analytical position. Also a different section type, material or thickness from the physical element. Warning
    C4 Analytical outside physical An associated member's axis, or a panel's surface, leaves the physical body by more than the analytical-to-physical distance. Warning
    C5 No counterpart An analytical member or panel with no physical association, or a physical structural element (load-bearing column, framing, structural wall or floor) with no analytical association. Analytical-only elements are allowed (STR-GEN-001), so this is informational. Elements that lost their association when the other side was deleted are reported as warnings. Info / Warning
    C6 Overlap not reflected Physical beam and slab (or wall and slab) intersect, but their analytical member and panel neither share nodes nor lie within the support distance of each other. Warning
    C7 Instability hints Heuristic checks, labelled as hints and never errors: a node where every connected member releases the same rotation and no boundary condition fixes it; a member with torsion (Mx) released at both ends; a member released in all rotations at both ends that is not a truss member; a panel supported only along one straight line with pinned supports. Hint
    C8 Missing properties An analytical element without a structural material, a physical material asset or a section type; a panel with zero thickness. Warning
    • Loads that lie outside their host (STR-LOAD-001) are listed under C1's group as a separate Load off host issue, and the stale-results state of STR-RES-001 is not part of this check.
    • Tolerances come from Structural Settings (STR-SET-001): support distance (default 300 mm), analytical-to-physical distance (150 mm), node merge distance (5 mm). The check stores the tolerance values it ran with in its report.
    • Issue identity. Each issue has a stable key: check code plus the sorted GlobalIds of the elements involved. Ignore is stored against the key and survives re-checks, saves and BIMserver round trips; it is cleared automatically when any involved element changes geometry.
    • Before analysis. structural_analysis.run (ANA-FEA-001) runs the consistency and support checks on its scope first. If errors (S3, C2) remain that are not ignored, the run is held and the user is asked Run anyway or Review; scripted runs fail with the issue list unless options.ignore_check_errors is true.
    • Checks never change the model. They are read-only queries and leave the undo stack unchanged; only Ignore and Un-ignore are undoable model edits.
    • Performance target: a full check of 10 000 analytical elements completes within 10 s on the reference machine; an incremental automatic check after a local edit completes within 1 s and never blocks the UI thread.

    Data (IFC mapping). No IFC equivalent; check results are not exported. The last report per check (timestamp, scope, tolerances used, issue list with keys and GlobalIds) and the ignore list (key, reason, user, date) are stored in RXD document model/analysis (checks.*). Check switches and tolerances are part of the analytical settings in the same document (STR-SET-001).

    Commands. - analytical_model.check_supports(scope?) -> report - analytical_model.check_consistency(scope?) -> report - analytical_model.ignore_issue(issue_key, ignore: bool, reason?)

    scope is "model" (default), "selection", "view:<view_id>" or a list of element IDs. A report is {run_at, tolerances, issues: [{key, code, severity, message, element_ids[], measured?, tolerance?, ignored}], counts_by_severity}.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A beam whose analytical end node stops 40 mm short of a column's analytical member is reported as C1 "Disconnected nodes" with the measured gap of 40 mm, and Zoom to frames the gap. - [ ] A two-storey frame with no boundary conditions reports S3 and C2 as errors, and Run Analysis is held with a Run anyway / Review prompt. - [ ] A beam supported at one end only is reported as S1; adding a pinned point boundary condition at the free end clears the issue on Re-check. - [ ] Moving a physical beam 200 mm sideways without re-running automation reports C3 on its associated analytical member, with 200 mm against the 150 mm tolerance. - [ ] An ignored C5 issue stays ignored after save, reopen and re-check, and reappears when the involved member is moved. - [ ] With automatic consistency checks on, drawing a new analytical beam that misses a column by 20 mm adds one warning to the warnings list within 1 s of the commit. - [ ] Running either check leaves the undo stack unchanged.

    4.3.10 Manual analytical adjustment and reset

    ID: STR-AM-008 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §4.2 ("Analytical Node", "Automation") · web: Modify an Analytical Model

    Purpose. Let the engineer move analytical nodes, edges and whole analytical elements to idealise the model (for example to bring a beam's analytical line to a column centreline) without changing any physical element, and later restore the default position derived from the physical element.

    Workflow (adjust). 1. Select an analytical member, panel or node (or a physical element with exactly one associated analytical element) and choose Analyze › Structural Analytical Model › Adjust, or Adjust on the contextual tab. 2. Reviera enters Adjust mode: every non-analytical element is drawn half-toned and cannot be selected; the analytical elements stay fully drawn. 3. Click a node to show a move control. For members the control is 3D, in the member's local coordinate system; Spacebar switches between local and global axes. For panels the control is 2D in the panel's plane; Tab selects an edge instead of a node; Spacebar cycles the panel's two local orientations and the global one. 4. Drag along an axis or type a distance in the temporary dimension. Nodes and edges snap to other analytical nodes, analytical members and panel edges, grids, levels and reference planes. 5. Drag an edge, or use Move, to shift a whole member or panel. 6. Finish commits all moves as one transaction ("Adjust analytical model"); Cancel discards them.

    Workflow (reset). Select one or more analytical elements (or associated physical elements) and choose Reset. Each element returns to the default position that the active automation rule package (STR-AM-006) computes from its associated physical element.

    Behaviour & rules. - Physical elements never move in Adjust mode. - End nodes are shared: moving a node moves the ends of every member and corner of every panel that uses it, and the analytical links attached to it. A node dragged onto another node within the node merge distance merges with it (STR-AM-003); the merge is listed in the status bar and is undone with the session if cancelled. - Hosted nodes can only slide along or within their host. - A node keeps its associated level: the level offset is recalculated so the node still follows later level moves. - Hosted loads and boundary conditions follow their host; a point load or condition placed by position keeps its relative position along the member or panel. - An element or node moved in Adjust mode is flagged manually adjusted (shown in Properties and available to filters and schedules). Automation updates skip flagged elements unless told to overwrite them (STR-AM-006). - Moving a member's node so far that the analytical-to-physical distance is exceeded is allowed; the consistency check reports it (STR-AM-007, C3). - Reset clears the manually adjusted flag and recomputes geometry from the physical element. It keeps the element's GlobalId, section, releases, loads and boundary conditions. Elements with no physical association have no default position: Reset refuses them and names them. Reset of a node shared with an element that is not being reset moves only the ends of the reset elements and disconnects the shared node; the result is reported so the user can re-run the consistency check. - Crash recovery. Adjust mode is an interactive session (§2.1 of the conventions). Its micro-operation schema is: enter(element_ids[]), pick(node_id | edge_ref), set_cs(local_a | local_b | global), move(target_ref, delta_vector), snap(target_ref, snap_kind), merge(node_a, node_b); finish and cancel close the session. Replay starts from the committed model state at enter and re-applies the moves in order, so an unfinished session is offered for resumption after a crash.

    Data (IFC mapping). Adjusted geometry is written to the same IFC entities as before (STR-AM-001 to 003); no extra entity is created. The manually adjusted flag (per element and per node) and the hash of the default geometry it departed from are RXD element data (analysis). Unfinished Adjust sessions live only in the live model store's session journal (chapter 2b §6.5), not in the IFC file.

    Commands. - analytical_model.adjust(element_id) -> tool_session (interactive; the session commits on Finish) - analytical_node.move(node_ids[], delta, cs?: "global"|"local") (the non-interactive equivalent for Lua and MCP; sets the manually adjusted flag) - analytical_model.reset(element_ids[])

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] In Adjust mode, moving a beam's end node 150 mm to a column's centreline moves the beam's analytical end and the column's top node together, leaves the physical beam and column unchanged, and creates one undo item on Finish. - [ ] Cancel after three node moves leaves the analytical model exactly as before. - [ ] Running Physical → Analytical on the adjusted beam without Overwrite manual adjustments leaves it in place and logs it as skipped; Reset then restores its default position and clears the flag. - [ ] Reset on an analytical member with no physical association is refused and names the member. - [ ] Killing the process during an Adjust session with two moves and restarting offers to resume the session with both moves re-applied. - [ ] analytical_node.move([n], {0,0,-100}, "global") lowers node n by 100 mm and flags it as manually adjusted.

    4.3.11 Structural analysis provider interface

    ID: ANA-FEA-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §4.6

    Purpose. Reviera shall run structural analyses through a pluggable structural analysis provider. This replaces the reference product's proprietary solver link.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Analyze › Structural Analysis › Run Analysis. 2. Choose the provider, scope (whole model or selection), analysis type (linear static; modal and others where the provider supports them), self-weight inclusion, member offsets, code and units. 3. Click Run. The job runs in the background (ANA-GEN-001). A notification appears when it completes, and the result package is stored.

    Behaviour & rules. - Pre-analysis checks. structural_analysis.run first runs the analytical model support and consistency checks (STR-AM-007) on the analysed scope. The run is refused while check errors remain, unless options.ignore_check_errors=true is passed; the ignored errors are then recorded with the result set. - Exchange format: - Reviera exports the analytical model as an IFC4 Structural Analysis View subset: members, panels, nodes, links, supports, loads, cases and combinations. - It also writes a compact neutral JSON (reviera-structural-model.json) for providers that do not read IFC. - Result package: a provider returns a package with these parts: - a manifest (provider, version, analysis type, model snapshot hash) - member forces (Fx, Fy, Fz, Mx, My, Mz) at stations - displacements at nodes and panel mesh points - reactions - panel stresses and moments - optionally required reinforcement areas and proposed sections - Packages are stored as .reviera-results archives that the model references (STR-RES-001). Update model applies proposed sections through STR-AM-006. - Partial model transfer: the scope can be a selection. Nodes on the boundary of the selection get default supports, and the user is warned. - [Suggestion] engines, each wrapped as an external-process provider, with licences to verify before bundling:

    Engine Scope Notes
    CalculiX General FEA GPL-2.0-or-later; can be used under GPL-3
    Code_Aster Advanced FEA GPL-3.0
    Kratos Multiphysics Multiphysics BSD-style
    PyNite Frames and plates MIT; a lightweight default for linear static frame analysis
    OpenSees Seismic and non-linear Custom licence; must be checked

    Data (IFC mapping). Results summaries: IfcStructuralResultGroup (TheoryType FIRST_ORDER_THEORY and so on, ResultForLoadGroup → combination or case, IsLinear). Reactions are written as IfcStructuralPointReaction on supports. The full result data is referenced through IfcDocumentReference and IfcRelAssociatesDocument. The package index (path, hash, stale flag) and results caches are kept in RXD document analysis.

    Commands. - structural_analysis.run(provider_id, scope, analysis_type, options) -> job_id - structural_analysis.export_model(path, format: "ifc"|"json", scope) - structural_analysis.import_results(path) -> package_id - structural_analysis.update_model(package_id, apply_sections?: bool) - analysis_provider.list(kind?) -> providers[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With the PyNite suggestion installed, a simply supported 6 m beam under a 10 kN/m line load returns a mid-span moment of 45 kN·m ± 0.5%. - [ ] Editing a load after the run marks the result package stale and shows a notice in Results Explorer. - [ ] The exported IFC structural model opens in a third-party IFC structural viewer with all members, supports and load cases present.

    4.3.12 Results Explorer and Results Manager

    ID: STR-RES-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §4.6 · screenshots/structure_mep/structural_results_explorer_presets_2027.png · screenshots/structure_mep/structural_results_analysis_insights_2027.png

    Purpose. Show and manage analysis results inside model views.

    UI. - Results Explorer is a dockable palette that is active when at least one result package exists. It contains: - package and analysis selection - case or combination selection - result type: member force diagrams for Fx–Mz, displacements (deformed shape), reactions, panel maps for stresses and moments, and required reinforcement - display style (ANA-ADS-001), units and scale - Result presets: at least 13 named presets, for example: - column axial forces - column bending moments - support reactions - beam moments with deformation - beam shear - transfer beam forces - wall in-plane forces in X and Y - wall deflection - floor moments with deformation in X and Y - floor shear - slab twisting moments

    Users can save their own presets. - Insights tab: extreme (minimum and maximum) values per selected result type, with zoom-to-element. - Results Manager: lists, imports, exports and deletes packages.

    Behaviour & rules. Results are view overlays and never change model geometry. A stale package shows a banner.

    Data (IFC mapping). Display settings are stored with the view's own RXD data (chapter 5). Presets are kept in RXD document model/analysis.

    Commands. - results.show(view_id, package_id, load_group_id, result_type, style_id?) - results.apply_preset(view_id, preset_id) - results.extremes(package_id, result_type, load_group_id) -> {min, max, element_ids} - results.delete_package(package_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] The "Support Reactions" preset shows reaction arrows with values at every support for the chosen combination. - [ ] Insights lists the element with the maximum beam moment, and clicking it zooms to that beam.

    4.4 Steel fabrication detailing

    All features in this section are P2. Steel fabrication elements are shown only at Fine detail and need framing families that declare full section shape parameters. Reviera ships an Upgrade Steel Families utility that adds missing section parameters to older content.

    Ref: research/03 §5.1

    4.4.1 Steel detailing prerequisites and visibility

    ID: STR-STL-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §5.1

    Purpose. Set the conditions under which steel fabrication elements can be created and shown, and give users a way to bring older framing content up to those conditions.

    Behaviour & rules. - Plates, bolts, welds, cuts and connection sub-elements are drawn only at Fine detail. At Coarse and Medium detail a connection shows its symbol (STR-CONN-001). The elements always exist in the model: they are scheduled, counted by numbering (STR-STL-010) and exported to IFC whatever the view's detail level. - Supported sections. Steel tools accept framing and columns whose type declares a section shape (I/H, channel, angle, T, rectangular and circular hollow, flat bar, cold-formed C and Z) with its section parameters (depth, width, web and flange thickness, root radius, and so on). Members without them are refused by connection, cut and fastener tools with a message that names the member and suggests the upgrade utility. - Upgrade utility (Steel › Upgrade Steel Families, steel_families.upgrade): scans framing and column families, infers the section shape from the profile geometry and type names, adds the missing section parameters, and fills them from the profile. Families it cannot classify are listed with the reason and left unchanged. The report lists upgraded, skipped and failed families. The run is one undoable transaction. - When placement fails because of an unsupported shape, the wrong input order or parameters that do not fit, Reviera explains the cause specifically. Tooltips on each connection type describe the required input order. - Unlike the reference product, Reviera's interference check (ANA-CLASH-001) includes detailed steel elements and fabrication parts. See §4.17. - The connection library is stored as open files, not in a local database server. - Steel elements of the Steel tab need a structural material whose model behaviour is steel; other materials are refused with a message.

    Data (IFC mapping). Section shape and parameters map to the type's IfcMaterialProfileSet with a parametrised profile (IfcIShapeProfileDef, IfcUShapeProfileDef, IfcLShapeProfileDef, IfcTShapeProfileDef, IfcRectangleHollowProfileDef, IfcCircleHollowProfileDef, IfcCShapeProfileDef, IfcZShapeProfileDef); shapes with no parametrised IFC profile use IfcArbitraryClosedProfileDef plus the section parameters in RXD family recipe data.

    Commands. steel_families.upgrade(family_ids[] | "all") -> report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A bolt group visible at Fine is not drawn at Medium in the same view, and the connection symbol is drawn instead. - [ ] A bolt group is counted in a schedule and exported to IFC when every view in the model is at Coarse detail. - [ ] Placing a shear-plate connection on a beam whose family lacks section parameters is refused with a message naming the beam and the upgrade utility. - [ ] Upgrading a legacy W-shape family adds its section parameters with values equal to the profile dimensions, and the type then exports an IfcIShapeProfileDef.

    4.4.2 Open parametric connection library

    ID: STR-STL-002 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §5.2

    Purpose. Reviera needs its own library of standard steel connections, because the reference product's connection engine and content are proprietary.

    Behaviour & rules. - Library format: a connection type is a package containing: - a manifest (name, group, SPDX licence, version) - an input signature: member count (1–3 inputs for standard types), member roles (main, secondary, brace), and supported section families (I, H, channel, angle, tube, CHS, flat) - a parameter schema: plates, bolts, welds, stiffeners and properties, grouped by tab - a Lua generator that produces plates, fasteners, welds and cuts from the inputs and parameters - optional ranges of applicability: rules on profile size and geometry - Initial library target (first release): grouped like the reference product's families, but authored from first principles. Groups and examples:

    Group Types
    Base plates Pinned and moment base plates with anchors
    Beam–column Shear plate (fin plate), end plate (flush and extended), double clip angle, seated beam, moment flange plates
    Beam–beam Notched shear plate, clip angle, splice (flange and web plates), end-plate splice
    Bracing Gusset plates for 1–4 diagonals, flat bracing with tension bolt, tube-end slotted plate
    Column Bolted and welded splices, stiffeners, web doubler, cap plate
    Frames Apex haunch, knee (eaves) haunch
    • Modify Parameters dialog: tabs generated from the parameter schema, with live 3D preview. The same dialog edits types and instance overrides.
    • Connection Library (the launcher on Steel › Connection) loads and unloads types, filtered by group. Community libraries can be added if their licence is GPL-compatible (TECH_STACK §4.2).

    Data (IFC mapping). See STR-CONN-001. Library packages are external, but the generated sub-elements are fully written to IFC, so a model opens without the library. The library package and version are recorded in RXD element data (structural), and the type recipe in an RXD family recipe.

    Commands. - connection_library.install(path) - connection_type.edit_parameters(type_id, params) - structural_connection.override(connection_id, params)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A shear-plate connection between a W-beam and a column flange creates a plate, a bolt group and welds at Fine detail. - [ ] Changing the bolt row count from 3 to 4 in the dialog regenerates the plate height. - [ ] A model whose library package has been removed still opens and shows all plates and bolts, with a warning that the connection cannot be edited.

    4.4.3 Custom connections

    ID: STR-STL-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §5.2 ("Custom connections") · screenshots/structure_mep/steel_custom_connections.png

    Workflow. 1. Select one or more standard or generic connections and their loose fabrication elements. 2. Choose Customize. 3. Name the connection, then Add or Remove sub-elements: plates, profiles, bolts, welds, parametric cuts and nested standard connections (stiffeners excepted). 4. Finish.

    UI. While customizing, Reviera is in a custom connection edit mode: the members and the selected elements stay fully drawn, everything else is half-toned, and the contextual tab offers Add, Remove, Finish and Cancel. The name is asked for first and must be unique among loaded connection types. Each Add or Remove pick is journaled as a micro-operation, so an unfinished session is recovered after a crash (§2.1 of the conventions); replay re-applies the picks in order.

    Behaviour & rules. - A custom connection allows at most three connected members. A fourth member in the selection is refused with a message. - The result is a new connection type. Nested parameters can be exposed as type parameters. - Welds cannot be attached to sub-elements of custom connections. They are allowed on sub-elements of standard connections. - What is stored. The type records each sub-element relative to the main member's local coordinate system (position, orientation, and the member face or end it is related to), plus the nested standard connections with their parameters. When placed on another join, sub-elements are re-positioned relative to that join's main member; nested standard connections regenerate for the new members. - Matching. A custom type can be placed only on joins with the same member count and roles and the same section families (for example I to I flange). Other joins are refused with the reason. - Editing the type. Add and Remove on an existing custom type change every instance of that type after a confirmation that states the instance count. - Exposed parameters (expose_parameter) appear in Modify Parameters (STR-STL-002) as type parameters with the nested element's current value as default; a path is <sub-element name>.<parameter>. An invalid path is refused. - Loose elements used to build the type are absorbed into the first instance; they are not duplicated. - Custom types are stored in the project. They can be exported as a connection-library package (STR-STL-002) for reuse in other projects.
