    Data (IFC mapping). Each instance is an IfcElementAssembly (USERDEFINED "STRUCTURAL_CONNECTION") like any connection (STR-CONN-001), with its plates, fasteners, welds and cuts written in full. The type recipe (sub-element list, relative placements, nested connections, exposed parameters) is an RXD family recipe; the instance records its type in RXD element data (structural).

    Commands. - structural_connection.customize(connection_ids[], element_ids[], name) -> type_id - custom_connection.add_elements(type_id, element_ids[]) - custom_connection.remove_elements(type_id, element_ids[]) - custom_connection.expose_parameter(type_id, path)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A custom connection built from an end plate and an extra stiffener can be placed on another matching join, where it recreates both. - [ ] Customizing a selection with four connected members is refused with a message. - [ ] Removing a plate from a custom type used by 5 instances asks for confirmation with the count, then removes the plate from all 5. - [ ] Exposing Stiffener 1.Thickness adds a type parameter whose change from 10 mm to 12 mm updates every instance.

    4.4.4 Connection automation

    ID: STR-STL-004 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §5.2 ("Connection automation")

    Purpose. Place connections on many joins at once from rules, instead of one by one.

    Workflow. 1. Select framing members or a region, or nothing for the whole model, and choose Steel › Connection › Automate. 2. In the dialog choose the rule set (the project default, or a loaded Lua or JSON rule set), what to do with joins that already have a connection (Skip, the default, or Replace generic only), and whether to run in preview mode. 3. Run. The job runs in the background (ANA-GEN-001). Preview shows the proposed type per join, colour-coded in the active view and listed in the log, without changing the model; Apply then commits it.

    Behaviour & rules. - Automate Connections applies connection types to the selected joins, or to all joins, using ranges of applicability. - Joins are found from framing end joins and member intersections within 1 mm, classified by member count, roles (main, secondary, brace) and section families. - Each join gets the first type whose rules match. - A rule set is an ordered list of rules. Each rule names a connection type and conditions on member roles, section families, profile size ranges (for example depth 200–400 mm), angles between members and material grade. - Ranges of applicability stored on library types (STR-STL-002) are used when the rule set does not override them. - Joins with an existing detailed connection are never changed. Joins where the generator fails keep a generic connection with a Failed status (STR-CONN-001). - A log lists placed, skipped and failed joins with reasons. It can be saved as CSV. - Rule sets that map profile sizes to connection types are Lua or JSON tables. - The applied run is one undoable transaction; its log is kept with the run history.

    Data (IFC mapping). Placed connections as in STR-CONN-001. Rule sets are project-level data in RXD document model/structural (settings.connection_rules), or external files referenced by path; run logs (date, rule set, counts) are kept there too.

    Commands. structural_connection.automate(scope, rule_set_id?, options?: {existing: "skip"|"replace_generic", preview: bool}) -> report. The report lists {join, members[], type_id?, status: placed|skipped|failed, reason} per join. A preview report can be applied with structural_connection.apply_automation(report_id).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Automating 200 beam–column joins places a type on every join whose profiles fall within a range, and logs the rest. - [ ] Re-running automation on the same joins with Skip changes nothing and logs all 200 as skipped (already connected). - [ ] Preview mode leaves the undo stack and model unchanged until Apply. - [ ] The log saved as CSV has one row per join with status and reason.

    4.4.5 Plates

    ID: STR-STL-005 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §5.3

    Workflow. 1. Choose Steel › Plate. Pick the placement plane: the current work plane, or a planar face of a steel element. 2. Sketch a single closed contour with lines and arcs (rectangle, polygon and circle tools are offered). Each sketch operation is journaled as a micro-operation, so an unfinished sketch is recovered after a crash (§2.1 of the conventions). 3. Finish. Reviera validates the contour and creates the plate.

    Behaviour & rules. - Parameters: thickness (default 10 mm, 1–200 mm), material (steel grade), coating and justification (Top, Centre or Bottom relative to the sketch plane), plus a free Part role (for example stiffener, gusset, cap plate) used by numbering and schedules. - The contour must be one closed, non-self-intersecting loop. Several loops or gaps are refused and the offending segment is highlighted. Holes in plates are made with hole patterns or contour cuts (STR-STL-006, STR-STL-008), not inner loops. - Arcs in the contour are approximated by corner cuts. - A plate sketched on a face is hosted by that face: it moves with the element and its sketch plane updates when the face moves. If the face disappears the plate stays in place, becomes unhosted and a warning names it. - Edit Contour reopens the sketch. Corner cuts (STR-STL-008) can be applied afterwards. - Folded plates are produced only by connections. After Break they become independent, and their sketch can no longer be edited. - Plates are drawn only at Fine detail (STR-STL-001), and are valid targets for bolts, welds and cuts.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcPlate (PredefinedType SHEET, or USERDEFINED "FOLDED"), typed by IfcPlateType. Pset_PlateCommon. Geometry: an extruded area solid from the contour. Material: IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage with one layer of the plate thickness. The editable contour, justification and host face reference are RXD element data (constraints).

    Commands. plate.create(work_plane | face_ref, contour_curves[], thickness, material_id, justification) -> id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A plate sketched on a column flange face exports as IfcPlate with the correct thickness. - [ ] A contour with a gap of 2 mm is refused at Finish and the open segment end is highlighted. - [ ] A 15 mm plate with Bottom justification on a flange face sits fully outside the flange, with its bottom face on the flange face. - [ ] Moving the hosting column moves the plate with it.

    4.4.6 Bolts, anchors, holes and shear studs

    ID: STR-STL-006 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §5.3 · screenshots/structure_mep/steel_fabrication_elements_plate_anchors.png

    Workflow. 1. Select the steel elements to join with Ctrl+click, then press Enter. 2. Pick the face the pattern is perpendicular to. 3. Sketch a rectangular or circular pattern. Finish.

    Behaviour & rules. - Bolts: - standard, grade, diameter and assembly (for example bolt + nut + 2 washers) - bolt length and grip length, both calculated - grip length increase - hole definition per connected element (type, tolerance, slotted) - inverted - finish calculation at gap - location (site or shop) and coating - count and spacing per direction, and edge distances - Anchors: the same flow, between concrete and steel. Parameters: standard, length and grade. - Holes: a pattern without fasteners. - Shear studs: a pattern on a steel element. Parameters: standard, diameter and length. - Bolt standards are open data tables (dimensions per standard). Reviera ships tables only where their content is not copyrighted, and users can add their own. - The shape of a pattern can be edited after placement.

    Data (IFC mapping).

    Element IFC
    Bolt IfcMechanicalFastener BOLT, NominalDiameter, NominalLength; Pset_MechanicalFastenerBolt (ThreadDiameter, ThreadLength, NutsCount, WashersCount, …)
    Anchor IfcMechanicalFastener ANCHORBOLT
    Shear stud IfcMechanicalFastener STUDSHEARCONNECTOR
    Hole IfcOpeningElement OPENING with IfcRelVoidsElement in each pierced element

    A pattern is an IfcElementAssembly USERDEFINED "FASTENER_GROUP" that aggregates its fasteners, or a single fastener with IfcMappedItem copies. The joined elements are related with IfcRelConnectsWithRealizingElements. Pattern parameters (kind, counts, spacings, grip, location, hole definitions) are RXD element data (constraints).

    Commands. - bolt_pattern.create(element_ids[], face_ref, pattern: "rect"|"circle", params) -> id - anchor_pattern.create(...) - hole_pattern.create(...) - shear_stud_pattern.create(...)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 2 × 3 M20 bolt pattern through a 15 mm plate and a 10 mm web reports a grip length of 25 mm and creates 6 holes in each element. - [ ] An exported bolt is an IfcMechanicalFastener with NominalDiameter = 20 mm.

    4.4.7 Welds

    ID: STR-STL-007 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §5.3

    Purpose. Record shop and site welds between steel elements, with the data a fabricator needs.

    Workflow. Choose Steel › Welds. Select the elements to weld (two or more steel elements, Ctrl+click), press Enter, then pick an available edge. Only edges where the selected elements touch within 1 mm are offered and highlighted. A cross symbol represents the weld. Picks are journaled as micro-operations (§2.1 of the conventions).

    Behaviour & rules. - Parameters: main and double weld type, thickness, location (site or shop), surface shape and preparation. Values come from data tables, not free text. - Weld types include fillet, butt (square, single-V, single-bevel, double-V), plug and spot; surface shapes flat, convex and concave. The tables are open data files that users can extend. - Thickness is the throat (a) or leg size, > 0 mm; length defaults to the picked edge and can be shortened; an Intermittent option takes segment length and pitch. - Welds do not move with their elements. When geometry changes they are flagged for review. - Review means: the weld keeps its position, a needs review status appears in Properties and in the warnings list, and Accept clears it once the user has checked or re-picked the edge. - If one of the welded elements is deleted, the weld is deleted with it (STR-GEN-002). - Welds cannot be placed on sub-elements of custom connections (STR-STL-003). - Shop welds join elements into one assembly for assembly marks (STR-STL-010); site welds do not. - Welds are drawn only at Fine detail. Weld symbols in drawings are annotations of chapter 5 that read the weld parameters.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcFastener with PredefinedType WELD, and Pset_FastenerWeld (Type1, Type2, Surface1, Surface2, Process, a, l, Intermittent, …). Related with IfcRelConnectsWithRealizingElements. The picked edge reference, location (site or shop) and review status are RXD element data (structural).

    Commands. weld.create(element_ids[], edge_ref, params) -> id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Moving a plate with a weld marks the weld "needs review" and leaves its position unchanged. - [ ] Picking an edge where the selected elements do not touch is not possible: the edge is not highlighted. - [ ] A 6 mm fillet weld exports as IfcFastener (WELD) with Pset_FastenerWeld.a = 6 mm. - [ ] A plate shop-welded to a beam gets the beam's assembly mark; the same plate site-welded does not.

    4.4.8 Modifiers and parametric cuts

    ID: STR-STL-008 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §5.4

    Tool Behaviour Command
    Corner Cut (plates) Convex or concave, straight or radius steel_modifier.corner_cut(plate_id, corner_ref, kind, size)
    Cope Skewed (framing) Skewed cope at a member end steel_modifier.cope_skewed(member_id, end, params)
    Shorten A cut at the nearest end; positive shortens, negative extends; angles across height and width give diagonal cuts steel_modifier.shorten(member_id, end, length, angle_h?, angle_w?)
    Contour Cut A sketched hole or notch through framing or plates, with gap width, radius, boring and boundary distances steel_modifier.contour_cut(element_id, face_ref, curves[], params)
    Cope (parametric) Select intersecting members, then Enter. A swap control chooses which member is cut. steel_cut.cope(member_ids[], cut_member_id?)
    Miter, Saw Cut – Flange, Saw Cut – Web End cuts between two members steel_cut.miter(a, b), steel_cut.saw(a, b, part: "flange"|"web")
    Cut Through Cuts one element by the shape of another, plus a gap steel_cut.cut_through(cut_id, cutter_id, gap)
    Cut By Cuts by the intersecting geometry steel_cut.cut_by(cut_id, cutter_id)

    Behaviour & rules. - Parametric cuts form a sub-connection (shown as a dashed box) that cannot be retyped. - Modifiers and cuts regenerate when their members move. Void cuts and connections can be combined. - Shape handles extend a member beyond its shorten modifier. - Uncope (Parametric Cuts › Uncope, steel_cut.uncope(member_ids[])): select one or more members that carry copes, then press Enter. Every parametric cope on those members is removed and their ends return to the uncut shape. A sub-connection left with no cuts is deleted; one that still holds other cuts (for example a miter) is kept. Copes that belong to a detailed connection (STR-CONN-001) are not removed; they are listed as skipped, because editing them belongs to the connection's parameters. Selecting members with no copes is reported as "nothing to remove" and makes no transaction. - Deleting a cut opening directly (selecting its dashed box contents) has the same effect for that single cut.

    Data (IFC mapping). Cuts are IfcOpeningElement (PredefinedType OPENING, or USERDEFINED "COPE", "MITER", …) with IfcRelVoidsElement. Their parameters are RXD element data (constraints). A sub-connection is an IfcElementAssembly USERDEFINED "SUB_CONNECTION".

    Commands. The commands are listed in the table above, plus steel_cut.uncope(member_ids[]).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A cope between a secondary beam and a girder removes the girder's flange zone from the secondary beam's end and updates when the girder depth changes. - [ ] Uncope on that secondary beam restores its full end profile, deletes the now-empty sub-connection and is undone in one step. - [ ] Uncope on a beam whose cope belongs to a shear-plate connection leaves the cope and reports it as skipped.

    4.4.9 Connection code checking (provider)

    ID: STR-STL-009 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §2.9 ("Code checking"), §5.2

    Purpose. Check detailed connections against a design code, and size them, through a pluggable provider rather than a built-in proprietary checker.

    Workflow. 1. Select one or more detailed connections whose instance has Override by Instance on (STR-CONN-001), so that the code-check tab is available. 2. In Modify Parameters, open the code-check tab: choose the provider, the design code the provider offers (for example a Eurocode 3 or AISC 360 module) and the design forces. Forces come from the connection's Design Forces property per load case or combination, or from the member end forces of a result package (STR-RES-001). 3. Choose Check, Presize or Report. Checks run in the background (ANA-GEN-001).

    Behaviour & rules. - Check, Presize and Report on connections go through a connection design provider (ANA-PLUG-001 kind structural, capability connection_check). - Provider input: member sections and materials, connection type and parameters (plates, bolts, welds), geometry of the join, and the design forces per load group. Output: per check item (for example bolt shear, bearing, block tearing, weld resistance) the resistance, the action, the utilisation ratio and pass or fail, plus an overall status and a report file (HTML or PDF). - Presize grows bolt diameter and plate and weld thickness step by step until the check passes. - Steps follow the bolt and plate tables (STR-STL-006). Presize stops with Failed after the largest size, or after 20 iterations, and reports which item still fails. - Presize changes connection parameters, so it is an undoable model edit; the provider never edits the model directly. - Status (NotCalculated, Failed or OK) and the report path are written to RXD element data (structural). - Any later change to the connection, its members or its design forces resets the status to NotCalculated (stale). - Connections without design forces are refused with a message naming them. - Reviera does not bundle a code checker in the first release. The provider interface and a sample Lua provider for simple bolt shear and bearing checks are supplied.

    Data (IFC mapping). No IFC equivalent for check results. Status, utilisation (the maximum ratio), code, provider, date and report path are RXD element data (structural) on the connection. The report file is referenced from the model with IfcDocumentReference through IfcRelAssociatesDocument.

    Commands. - structural_connection.check(connection_ids[], provider_id, code) -> report - structural_connection.presize(connection_ids[], provider_id, code)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With the sample provider, a bolt group whose design shear exceeds its capacity gets status Failed and a report that shows the utilisation ratio. - [ ] Presize on that connection increases the bolt diameter until the utilisation is ≤ 1.0, sets status OK, and is undone in one step. - [ ] Changing the beam size after a successful check resets the status to NotCalculated. - [ ] Checking a connection with no design forces is refused with a message naming it.

    4.4.10 Steel interoperability and fabrication output

    ID: STR-STL-010 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §5.5

    Behaviour & rules. - IFC is the primary exchange format with detailing software. Members, plates, fasteners, welds, openings and connection assemblies all round-trip as described above. - Part and assembly marks: - Steel › Numbering assigns part marks to identical parts and assembly marks to identical assemblies (main member plus everything welded to it in the shop). - The part mark is written to IfcElement.Tag. The assembly mark is written to the assembly's Tag. A copy of both is kept in RXD element data (structural) with the numbering options. - An assembly is an IfcElementAssembly USERDEFINED "STEEL_ASSEMBLY". - [Suggestion] NC export as a plugin: per-part CNC files in the openly documented DSTV NC1 format, generated from member profiles, holes, cuts and plates. - Proprietary exchange formats used by the reference product's detailing integration are not supported (§4.17).

    Commands. - steel_numbering.run(scope, options) -> report - steel_nc.export(scope, folder, format="dstv") (plugin)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Two identical beams with identical holes get the same part mark. Adding one hole to one beam gives it a new mark.

    4.5 Concrete detailing and precast

    All features in this section are P2. Precast tools are on Concrete › Precast Detailing and Precast Settings. Precast is a rule-driven pipeline: 1. split walls and slabs into pieces 2. reinforce the pieces and add mounting parts 3. generate shop drawings 4. export CAM data

    Ref: research/03 §6.1

    4.5.1 Precast configuration

    ID: STR-PRE-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §6.1

    Purpose. One tree-structured dialog holds all precast rules.

    UI. Concrete › Precast Settings › Configuration (precast_config.show()). Tree: - Concrete - Wall: Solid Wall, Double Wall - Slab: Solid, Hollow-core, Lattice-girder slab

    Each with Segmentation, Reinforcement, Connections (mounting parts) and Shop Drawing nodes. - Built-in parts: Annotations, Dimensioning - CAM Export - Data folder path for templates and families

    What each node edits:

    Node Contents Validation
    Segmentation The rules of STR-PRE-002: minimum and maximum length or width and height, maximum weight, joint gaps, minimum distance to openings, profile overlap; for hollow-core, the slab family, division profile, minimum width and strand diameter Minimum ≤ maximum; gaps 0–100 mm; maximum weight > 0 t; families must be loaded
    Reinforcement Reinforcement types per thickness range (area, edge, lattice girder), as used by STR-PRE-003; custom fabric sheet rules (STR-PRE-004) Thickness ranges must not overlap; bar and mesh types must exist
    Connections Mounting-part rules (STR-PRE-005): part family, count by weight bands, edge distances, symmetry Weight bands must be contiguous and ascending
    Shop Drawing Sheet template, centre-of-gravity symbol, dimension type and distances, descriptions (STR-PRE-006) Template must contain the required viewports
    Annotations / Dimensioning Tag family per category, dimension rules per category Tag families must be loaded
    CAM Export Writer per format, output folder and filename rule (STR-PRE-007) Filename rule must parse
    Data folder Path to templates and families Path must exist and be readable
    • Invalid values are marked in the tree node and in the cell, and OK is disabled until they are fixed.
    • OK commits as one transaction. The dialog shows how many existing assemblies were made with an older configuration version; Reviera does not re-split or re-reinforce them automatically, but offers Re-run on affected assemblies (STR-PRE-002 precast.resplit, STR-PRE-003).
    • Export… and Import… buttons call the commands below. Import replaces the whole configuration after a confirmation; references to families not loaded in the project are listed so they can be loaded.
    • A new project's configuration comes from its template; Reviera ships an open default configuration.

    Data (IFC mapping). No IFC equivalent. RXD document fabrication (precast configuration section), versioned. It can be exported and imported as a standalone file to share between projects. Each version increments on commit; the version used is recorded on each precast assembly (RXD element data structural, rule snapshot hash, STR-PRE-002). The standalone file is JSON with a schema version.

    Commands. - precast_config.get(path) -> value - precast_config.set(path, value) - precast_config.export(file) - precast_config.import(file) - precast_config.show()

    path addresses a node and key, for example wall.solid.segmentation.max_length. set applies the dialog's validation and returns an error naming the rule.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A configuration exported from one project and imported into another produces identical segmentation results on an identical wall. - [ ] Entering a minimum wall length of 9 m with a maximum of 8 m marks the Segmentation node invalid and disables OK. - [ ] After changing the maximum weight, the dialog reports how many existing assemblies used the previous version and offers to re-run on them. - [ ] precast_config.set("wall.solid.segmentation.max_length", -1) fails with a message naming the rule.

    4.5.2 Segmentation (split)

    ID: STR-PRE-002 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §6.2

    Workflow. 1. Choose Split, optionally with Multiple. 2. Select walls, floors or foundation slabs, then Finish. 3. For floors, choose the slab kind: Hollow-core, Solid or Lattice-girder.

    Behaviour & rules. - What Split does: creates parts (chapter 3 parts engine), divides them by the rules, places mounting parts and reinforcement (when automatic updates are on), and creates one assembly per piece. - Wall rules: minimum and maximum length, minimum and maximum height, maximum weight, horizontal and vertical joint gap, minimum distance to openings, and profile overlap height. - Slab rules: minimum and maximum width, maximum weight and joint gap. Hollow-core slabs add the hollow-core family, a division profile, minimum width, segmentation gap and strand diameter. - Re-splitting: after the source boundary changes, Split is re-run on the assembly. If it is run on the source element instead, Reviera detects the existing split and offers to redirect. - Automatic updates (a toggle) controls whether mounting parts and reinforcement are re-created when pieces change. - Double walls: a wall type with three layers (concrete, thermal or air, concrete) is split and reinforced as one double-wall piece. - Independent lattice girders can be sketched on lattice-girder slab assemblies.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Initial version (owner decision, 2026-10-12; open question Q13). The IFC relationship between the source wall or slab and its pieces is not written. IFC allows a piece only one decomposition parent, and that parent is its piece assembly (below). The source-to-piece link is kept in RXD element data only. Which IFC relationship, if any, carries it is decided later on expert advice. - Each piece is an IfcWall or IfcSlab (or an IfcBuildingElementPart with PRECASTPANEL) inside an IfcElementAssembly (USERDEFINED "PRECAST_ASSEMBLY") together with its reinforcement and mounting parts. - Pset_PrecastConcreteElementGeneral and Pset_PrecastConcreteElementFabrication (TypeDesignator, PieceMark, ProductionLotId, SerialNumber). - RXD element data (structural) holds the source element GlobalId, slab kind and rule snapshot hash.

    Commands. - precast.split(element_ids[], slab_kind?) -> assembly_ids[] - precast.resplit(assembly_ids[]) - precast.set_auto_update(bool)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 30 m × 3 m wall with maximum length 8 m and maximum weight 12 t is split into the fewest pieces that satisfy both limits, with the configured gaps. - [ ] No joint lies closer to an opening than the minimum distance. - [ ] Each piece exports as an IfcElementAssembly that contains the concrete element and its reinforcement.

    4.5.3 Automatic precast reinforcement

    ID: STR-PRE-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §6.3 · screenshots/structure_mep/precast_wall_auto_reinforcement.png

    Workflow. Choose Auto Reinforce. Select an assembly, or several assemblies of the same kind. Choose the area reinforcement type and, for walls, the edge reinforcement type. Click OK.

    Behaviour & rules. - Reinforcement types are defined per wall or slab thickness. Each covers: - area bars or mesh - edge bars around openings and edges (for example U-bars) - lattice girders for double walls and girder slabs - Editing a reinforcement type changes every default that refers to it. Reviera offers to re-run on the affected assemblies. - The dialog offers only the reinforcement types whose thickness range contains the piece thickness. Selecting assemblies of different kinds (for example a wall and a slab) is refused. - Re-running on an assembly that is already reinforced replaces only the reinforcement that the previous run generated (marked as generated, with the run's rule snapshot). Bars the user added by hand are kept; generated bars the user edited are kept and reported, so manual work is never lost silently. - With automatic updates on (STR-PRE-002), reinforcement is regenerated whenever a piece's geometry changes; with them off, the assembly is flagged as out of date. - Area reinforcement respects the host cover (STR-RBR-002) and is cut around openings with the configured clearance; edge bars wrap openings and free edges with the configured lap; lattice girders are laid parallel to the span at the configured spacing and edge distance. - Generated reinforcement gets partition = the assembly's piece mark, so numbering (STR-RBR-016) is per piece. - The report lists, per assembly, the bars, sheets and girders created, kept or skipped, and why.

    Data (IFC mapping). Generated rebar and mesh as in §4.2, aggregated into the piece assembly. Lattice girders are IfcReinforcingElement subtypes: IfcReinforcingBar chords and diagonals grouped in an IfcElementAssembly USERDEFINED "LATTICE_GIRDER". The generated flag, the reinforcement type used and the rule snapshot hash are RXD element data (rebar) on each generated element.

    Commands. precast.reinforce(assembly_ids[], area_type_id, edge_type_id?) -> report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Reinforcing a wall piece with a 1.2 × 2.1 m door opening places U-bars around the opening edges and mesh cut around it. - [ ] Re-running on that piece after the user added one extra bar keeps the extra bar and replaces only generated reinforcement. - [ ] A 200 mm wall piece is offered only reinforcement types whose thickness range contains 200 mm. - [ ] Generated bars carry the piece mark as their partition.

    4.5.4 Custom fabric sheets

    ID: STR-PRE-004 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §3.5, §6.3

    Purpose. Generate a fabric sheet shaped to each precast piece, instead of cutting standard sheets, so that the plant can produce one welded mesh per piece.

    Workflow. Select one or more precast assemblies and choose Concrete › Precast Detailing › Custom Fabric Sheets, optionally choosing a rule set other than the default. Rules are edited in Precast Settings › Custom Fabric Sheet Rules (part of the precast configuration, STR-PRE-001).

    Behaviour & rules. - Rule-generated custom sheets are cut around openings. The rules are wire spacing, edge distances, opening clearances and maximum sheet size, set in Custom Fabric Sheet Rules. The output is IfcReinforcingMesh with per-sheet wire geometry. - Rule set contents: wire diameter and spacing per direction, edge distance per edge kind (outer edge, joint edge), clearance around openings, minimum wire length (shorter wires are dropped), maximum sheet length and width (default 6.0 × 2.5 m), and which layer (near or far face) to fill. - A piece larger than the maximum sheet size gets several sheets, split along a line perpendicular to the main wires, with the configured lap. - Wires stop at the clearance line around each opening; wires that would be shorter than the minimum length are omitted, and the omitted count is reported. - Sheets are regenerated when the piece changes if automatic updates are on (STR-PRE-002); otherwise the piece is flagged as out of date. - Each sheet is numbered like any fabric sheet (STR-RBR-016); two pieces with identical sheets share a number.

    Data (IFC mapping). One IfcReinforcingMesh per sheet, aggregated into the piece assembly, with MeshLength, MeshWidth, the longitudinal and transverse bar diameters and spacings, and one swept body per wire. The rule set id and the generated flag are RXD element data (rebar); rule sets are part of the precast configuration in RXD document fabrication.

    Commands. precast.generate_custom_fabric(assembly_ids[], rule_id?)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A slab piece with two openings receives one custom sheet whose wires stop at the configured clearance from each opening. - [ ] A 9 m × 2.4 m wall piece with a 6 m maximum sheet length receives two sheets lapped by the configured lap length. - [ ] Two identical pieces get sheets with the same rebar number.

    4.5.5 Mounting parts

    ID: STR-PRE-005 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §6.1–6.2

    Purpose. Place the embedded parts that a precast piece needs for lifting, fixing and connecting, from rules rather than by hand.

    Workflow. Select precast assemblies and choose Concrete › Precast Detailing › Mounting Parts. Parts are also placed automatically by Split when automatic updates are on (STR-PRE-002). Individual parts can afterwards be moved, deleted or added by hand like any family occurrence.

    Behaviour & rules. - Rule-driven placement of lifting anchors, loops, bushings, connectors and lattice girders, per configuration. - Placement rules include count by weight, edge distances and centre-of-gravity symmetry. - Weight bands decide the count and family (for example up to 10 t: 2 anchors; up to 16 t: 4 anchors). A piece heavier than the last band is not given parts and is reported. - Weight is computed from the piece volume (openings removed) and the concrete density of the material (default 2 500 kg/m³). - Lifting anchors go on the top edge for walls and the top face for slabs, symmetric about the centre of gravity, at least the configured edge distance from ends and openings. If no symmetric position satisfies the distances, the closest valid positions are used and a warning is issued. - Mounting-part families can carry dimensioning references for shop drawings. - Re-running replaces only parts the rules generated; parts added or moved by hand are kept and reported. - Mounting parts host on the piece and move with it; deleting the piece deletes them (STR-GEN-002).

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcMechanicalFastener (USERDEFINED "LIFTING_ANCHOR", "BUSHING", …) or IfcDiscreteAccessory (USERDEFINED "CONNECTOR", or ANCHORPLATE), aggregated into the piece assembly. The generated flag and the rule that placed each part are RXD element data (structural). The piece weight is written as NetWeight in Qto_WallBaseQuantities or Qto_SlabBaseQuantities of the piece.

    Commands. precast.place_mounting_parts(assembly_ids[]) -> report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 9 t wall piece configured for "2 anchors up to 10 t" receives 2 lifting anchors placed symmetrically about the centre of gravity. - [ ] A 20 t piece with bands only up to 16 t receives no anchors and is listed in the report. - [ ] Re-running after the user moved one anchor keeps the moved anchor and reports it.

    4.5.6 Shop drawings

    ID: STR-PRE-006 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §6.4 · screenshots/structure_mep/precast_shop_drawing.png

    Workflow. Select assemblies and choose Shop Drawings. Reviera creates one sheet per assembly, or per group of identical assemblies, from the shop-drawing template configured for that element kind.

    Behaviour & rules. - Templates are Reviera assembly-sheet templates (chapter 5 sheets and assembly views). They define: - viewports: front, sections, 3D and reinforcement - a centre-of-gravity symbol - dimension type and dimension line distances - descriptions - schedules: bill of materials for concrete, rebar, mesh and mounting parts - per-category tags (Annotations) and per-category dimension rules (Dimensioning) - Similar pieces share dimension layouts. - Only title blocks that contain the required template viewports are accepted. Reviera ships open template title blocks. - Shop-drawing generation is a command, so Lua scripts and the MCP server can drive and customise it. This replaces the reference product's separate precast API.

    Commands. precast.shop_drawings(assembly_ids[], template_id?, group_identical?: bool) -> sheet_ids[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Generating shop drawings for 10 pieces, of which 4 are identical, with grouping on produces 7 sheets. Each has dimensioned views, a centre-of-gravity symbol and a BOM schedule.

    4.5.7 CAM export

    ID: STR-PRE-007 · Priority: P2 (framework) / P3 (specific proprietary formats) · Ref: research/03 §6.4

    Purpose. Hand precast pieces to plant production systems as machine-readable files.

    Workflow. Select precast assemblies (or none, for all assemblies in the project) and choose Concrete › Precast Detailing › CAM Export. Choose the writer and the output folder; the filename rule comes from the configuration (STR-PRE-001) and can be overridden for this run. The export runs in the background and ends with a summary.

    Behaviour & rules. - A CAM export framework with per-format writer plugins. - A writer is a provider (ANA-PLUG-001 style manifest with name, version, SPDX licence and file extension), implemented in Lua or as an external process. It receives the neutral piece model below and returns files. - cam_writer.list lists installed writers with their format and version. - Each writer node has an output filename rule built from variables: name with length, minimum length, padding and alignment; date; time; production number. - Syntax: {Var:Length:MinLength:Pad:Align}, where any trailing field may be omitted; variables are Name, ProdNo, Date (YYYYMMDD), Time (HHMMSS) and Mark. Unknown variables and malformed fields are rejected before export with the position of the error. - Names that would collide in the folder get a numeric suffix, and the summary lists them. - [Suggestion] writers: Unitechnik (versions 5.2/6.0/7.0) and PXML, as plugins. Implementations must be based on openly available format documentation. If such documentation is not available under acceptable terms, the format stays P3. - Reviera always provides a neutral JSON/CSV piece export (geometry outline, openings, embeds, reinforcement and piece marks) for custom CAM pipelines. - Coordinates are in millimetres in the piece's local production system (origin at the lower-left corner of the piece's front face, X along the length). - Pieces without a piece mark, or whose reinforcement or mounting parts are out of date (STR-PRE-003, STR-PRE-005), are exported only after a confirmation that lists them; scripted calls report them as warnings. - The export does not change the model.

    Data (IFC mapping). Reads the precast assemblies, pieces, reinforcement and mounting parts of STR-PRE-002 to 005 and Pset_PrecastConcreteElementFabrication (PieceMark, ProductionLotId, SerialNumber). Writer settings and filename rules are stored in the precast configuration (RXD document fabrication). Nothing is written back.

    Commands. - precast.cam_export(assembly_ids[], writer_id, folder, filename_rule?) -> files[] - cam_writer.list() -> writers[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] The rule {Name:12:4:0:left}_{ProdNo} names files with zero-padded, left-aligned piece names and the production number. - [ ] The rule {Nme}_{ProdNo} is rejected before any file is written, with the position of the unknown variable. - [ ] The neutral JSON export of a wall piece with one opening lists the outline, the opening, every bar with its shape and the lifting anchors, with coordinates in the piece's local system. - [ ] Exporting leaves the undo stack unchanged.

    4.6 MEP foundations: connectors, systems and settings

    4.6.1 Connectors

    ID: MEP-CONN-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §7.1

    Purpose. Connectors are the core MEP abstraction. Every MEP family carries typed connection points: equipment, terminals, fixtures, fittings, accessories, devices and lighting fixtures. Systems, routing and calculations are built from these points.

    Workflow. In the family editor (chapter 2), Create › Connector places a connector on a face or a plane in one of five domains: Duct, Pipe, Electrical, Cable Tray or Conduit. Connector parameters can be linked to family parameters.

    Behaviour & rules. - Duct and pipe connector parameters: - System classification, a fixed enumeration: - air: Supply Air, Return Air, Exhaust Air, Other Air - piping: Hydronic Supply, Hydronic Return, Domestic Hot Water, Domestic Cold Water, Sanitary, Vent - fire protection: Wet, Dry, Pre-Action, Other - Other - fittings only: Fitting, Global - Flow direction: In, Out or Bidirectional - Flow configuration: - Calculated: sums the flow downstream - Preset: a fixed value - System: a share of the system flow, set by a flow factor from 0 to 1 - Flow - Loss method: Not Defined, Coefficient or Specific Loss - Shape (round, rectangular or oval) and dimensions - Angle - Utility flag - Fixture units - Pipe connection type (threaded, welded, flanged and so on) - Electrical connector parameters: - System type: Power – Balanced, Power – Unbalanced, Data, Telephone, Security, Fire Alarm, Nurse Call, Controls or Communication - Voltage - Number of poles - Apparent load, per phase where unbalanced - Power factor and its state (lagging or leading) - Load classification and sub-classification - Motor flag - Cable tray and conduit connectors carry size and shape only. Conduit also supports surface connectors, which accept any number of conduits anywhere on a face. - Fittings declare a part type: Elbow, Tee, Cross, Transition, Wye, Tap, Union, Cap, Multi-port or Multi-shape Transition. Routing preferences use the part type to choose fittings automatically. - The connector origin and snap points are previewed in the family editor.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Each connector is an IfcDistributionPort nested in its element with IfcRelNests (the element is RelatingObject, the ports are RelatedObjects). - Port attributes: - FlowDirection: SINK for In, SOURCE for Out, SOURCEANDSINK for Bidirectional - PredefinedType: DUCT, PIPE, CABLE or CABLECARRIER - SystemType: an IfcDistributionSystemEnum value derived from the classification - Shape and size go in Pset_DistributionPortCommon and in the port-type psets (Pset_DistributionPortTypeDuct, Pset_DistributionPortTypePipe, Pset_DistributionPortTypeCable) where they are defined. - Electrical values go to the port, or to the element's Pset_ElectricalDeviceCommon (RatedVoltage, NumberOfPoles, PowerFactor, …). - Connector placement inside the family, the flow configuration and flow factor, and the loss method are kept in the RXD family recipe. The resolved flow values are written to standard psets.

    Commands. - connector.add(family_id, domain, face_ref | plane, params) -> connector_id (family editor) - connector.set(element_id, connector_index, params) - connector.list(element_id) -> connectors[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A VAV box family with one inlet and one outlet duct connector exports two IfcDistributionPorts nested with IfcRelNests, with SINK and SOURCE flow directions. - [ ] A fitting family whose part type is Tee is offered by routing preferences only in Junction rows.

    4.6.2 Physical connections and the connectivity graph

    ID: MEP-CONN-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §7.1–7.2, §15.2

    Purpose. Reviera shall keep a live connectivity graph of connected ports. Systems, sizing, checking and analysis all use it.

    Workflow. Connections are normally made implicitly: drawing a duct, pipe, tray or conduit from a connector, snapping an end grip onto an open connector, or inserting an inline fitting or accessory. Users can also connect or disconnect explicitly from the context menu of a selected connector glyph (Connect To…, Disconnect).

    Behaviour & rules. - Two ports are connected when they coincide in position, direction (anti-parallel), domain and compatible size, or when a connection command joins them explicitly. - Tolerances. Coincidence is tested within 0.5 mm in position and 0.5° in direction. Size is compatible when shape and nominal size match exactly; a mismatch is allowed only through a transition fitting, which mep.connect inserts from the routing preferences when one fits. Otherwise the command is refused with "Connectors differ in size or shape and no transition is available". - Domains. Ports of different domains (for example Duct and Pipe) are never connected. Electrical ports join only through circuits (§4.9), not through this graph's physical edges. - One partner per port. A duct, pipe, tray or conduit port has at most one partner. Conduit surface connectors (MEP-CONN-001) are the exception and accept any number. - The graph is updated incrementally on each transaction. Network IDs (connected components) are recomputed in parallel. Undo and redo restore the graph exactly, because edges are derived from stored relationships. - Open ports are tracked so that Show Disconnects (MEP-SYS-005) does not need a full scan. - Moving connected elements. Dragging an element drags its connected neighbours' ends with it where the geometry allows (segments stretch; fittings move). If the move would break the anti-parallel rule, the connection is dropped and a warning lists the newly open ports. - Linked models. Ports in linked models can be read for checking, but connections across a link are never created.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcRelConnectsPorts (RelatingPort, RelatedPort, optional RealizingElement for couplings). Network IDs are computed and not stored. On import, IfcRelConnectsPorts between ports whose positions differ by more than the tolerance are kept and flagged with a warning rather than dropped.

    Commands. - mep.connect(port_a, port_b): refused across domains or when a port already has a partner. - mep.disconnect(port_a, port_b) - mep.network_of(element_id) -> element_ids[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Drawing a duct from an equipment port creates IfcRelConnectsPorts between the equipment port and the duct's start port. - [ ] Deleting a fitting in a run leaves two open ports, which Show Disconnects reports. - [ ] mep.connect between a duct port and a pipe port is refused, and no relationship is written. - [ ] Undoing a connection and redoing it gives the same network ID membership for every element in the network.

    4.6.3 System classifications and system types

    ID: MEP-SYS-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §7.2

    Purpose. Group connected elements into logical systems. The classifications are fixed. System types are user-defined types within a classification.

    Behaviour & rules. - System types appear in the Project Browser under Families › Duct Systems / Piping Systems. They can be duplicated. - A system type has: - a graphics override (colour, line pattern) - a material - calculations: All, Flow Only, Performance or None - an abbreviation - rise and drop symbols - for piping: fluid type and temperature, and the flow-conversion method - The system kinds are duct systems, piping systems, electrical circuits (§4.9) and switch systems.

    Data (IFC mapping). - A system type is an IfcDistributionSystem occurrence template. Because IFC has no system type entity, Reviera writes the type definition to RXD document mep_settings (system types) and stamps each system occurrence with the type name in its ObjectType. - Each system is an IfcDistributionSystem with PredefinedType from the classification:

    Classification PredefinedType
    Supply Air AIRCONDITIONING or VENTILATION
    Return Air VENTILATION
    Exhaust Air EXHAUST
    Hydronic Supply / Return HEATING or CHILLEDWATER (chosen by fluid temperature, user-overridable)
    Domestic Cold Water DOMESTICCOLDWATER
    Domestic Hot Water DOMESTICHOTWATER
    Sanitary DRAINAGE or SEWAGE
    Vent VENT
    Fire protection (all) FIREPROTECTION
    Other USERDEFINED
    • Members are linked with IfcRelAssignsToGroup. The serviced building or storeys are linked with IfcRelServicesBuildings.
    • Pset_DistributionSystemCommon and, where it applies, Pset_DistributionSystemTypeVentilation.

    Commands. - system_type.create(classification, name, params) -> type_id - system_type.set(type_id, params)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing a system type's colour override recolours every element of every system of that type in all views. - [ ] A domestic cold water system exports as IfcDistributionSystem with PredefinedType DOMESTICCOLDWATER, assigned to its pipes, fittings and fixtures.

    4.6.4 Creating and editing systems

    ID: MEP-SYS-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §7.2

    Workflow. 1. Select terminals, fixtures or equipment. 2. Choose Create Systems › Duct / Piping / Power / Data / Switch …. 3. Set the system type and a system name (a name is proposed automatically). Optionally open the system in the System Editor.

    Drawing a duct or pipe from a component whose connector has a system type also creates a system or adds to one.

    UI. The System Editor mode (Modify | Duct/Piping Systems › Edit System) offers: - Add To System and Remove From System - Select Equipment - System Properties - Finish and Cancel

    Other tools: - Divide System: when one system contains several separate physical networks, it is split into "Name 1", "Name 2" and so on - Disconnect Equipment - Generate Layout (MEP-DUCT-008) - Generate Placeholder

    A System Selector drop-down on systems contextual tabs switches between the systems attached to the selected element.

    Behaviour & rules. - An element can belong to several systems through different connectors. - Components with no system are listed as Unassigned in the System Browser. - Only compatible classifications can be added. For example, a supply-air terminal cannot be added to a return-air system.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcRelAssignsToGroup membership. The equipment that serves a system is recorded through the port relationship, and its GlobalId is mirrored in RXD element data (mep_settings) on the system for fast lookup.

    Commands. - system.create(kind, element_ids[], system_type_id, name?) -> system_id - system.add(system_id, element_ids[]) - system.remove(system_id, element_ids[]) - system.select_equipment(system_id, equipment_id) - system.divide(system_id) -> system_ids[] - system.disconnect_equipment(system_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Creating a supply air system from 8 diffusers and then selecting an AHU as equipment gives a system with 9 members and the AHU as source. - [ ] Divide System on a system that spans two unconnected networks creates two systems with suffixes 1 and 2.

    4.6.5 System Browser

    ID: MEP-SYS-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §7.2 · screenshots/structure_mep/system_browser_analytical_systems.png

    UI. A dockable tree palette, toggled with a proposed F9. It has: - Views: - Systems, with a discipline filter: All, Mechanical, Piping or Electrical - Zones: system-zones and the spaces assigned to them - Analytical Systems: water loops, air systems, zone equipment, and the electrical analytical distribution tree - Columns chosen by the user: Flow, Size, Name, Type, Space and Phase. - An Unassigned node. - Context-menu commands: Select, Show, Pressure Loss Report, Delete and Properties. - Toolbar commands that add analytical systems and nodes. - A search box that filters the tree by name, mark or system abbreviation; matching branches expand automatically.

    Purpose. Give one place to see every system, its members and its unassigned components, and to act on them without hunting through views.

    Behaviour & rules. - Hierarchy. In the Systems view the tree is: discipline › system classification › system (name, type) › equipment › members, with fittings and segments under a collapsible Segments and fittings node so that large runs stay readable. An element that belongs to several systems appears under each of them. - Unassigned. Components with at least one connector that has no system are listed under Unassigned, grouped by domain. The node count updates live. - Selection is synchronised both ways with the canvas. Selecting a node selects its members in the active view; members not visible in that view stay selected but are counted in the status bar as "n not visible". Show opens or cycles through views where the selection is visible. - Columns. Column values are read-only except Name, which renames the system in place (validated against duplicate names within the same classification: "A system with this name already exists"). Column choice and widths are stored per user in ui/state. - Delete on a system node deletes the logical system only; its members become Unassigned. Physical elements are never deleted from the browser. - The tree is virtualised so it can show more than 100 000 elements. It refreshes incrementally from the transaction change set, not by rebuilding. - Linked models appear as read-only branches named after the link; their nodes can be selected for Show but not edited.

    Data (IFC mapping). None of its own: the browser reads IfcDistributionSystem/IfcDistributionCircuit groups and RXD element data. Its layout is user interface state (ui/state), not model data.

    Commands. system_browser.show(view: "systems"|"zones"|"analytical", discipline?). Context-menu items call existing commands: selection.set, pressure_loss_report.export (MEP-CALC-004), system.divide and element.delete.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Selecting a system node selects all its members in the active view. - [ ] The Unassigned node lists a newly placed diffuser that is not in any system. - [ ] Deleting a system from the browser leaves its 8 diffusers in the model and lists them under Unassigned. - [ ] Renaming a system to the name of another system of the same classification is refused with a message.

    4.6.6 Check Systems and Show Disconnects

    ID: MEP-SYS-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §8.6 · screenshots/structure_mep/check_pipe_systems_warning.png

    Behaviour & rules. - Check Duct Systems, Check Pipe Systems and Check Circuits are toggles that draw warning markers and dashed links for three kinds of problem: - systems that are not well connected - mismatches between flow and demand configuration - mismatches in flow direction - Show Disconnects marks open connectors on ducts, pipes, cable tray, conduit and electrical elements. - Each marker opens the related warning (chapter 2 warnings).

    Purpose. Find broken or inconsistent systems before sizing, calculation or fabrication conversion depend on them.

    UI. Analyze › Check Systems panel: three toggle buttons (Check Duct Systems, Check Pipe Systems, Check Circuits) and Show Disconnects, which opens a small dialog with a check box per domain (Duct, Pipe, Cable Tray, Conduit, Electrical). Toggle state is per view and survives closing and reopening the view during the session.

    Behaviour & rules. - Checks performed: - Not well connected: the system's members do not form one connected network from its equipment, or the system has no equipment. - Flow/demand mismatch: a terminal connector set to Preset sits on a branch whose equipment connector is also Preset with a different total, or a Calculated connector has nothing downstream. - Flow direction mismatch: two connected connectors are both In or both Out. - Circuits: a circuit has no panel, or a member's distribution system does not match the panel (MEP-ELEC-003). - Markers are view-specific overlays drawn with the theme warning token and a "!" glyph; they are never printed unless Print warning markers is set in the print dialog. Dashed links join the marker to the offending connector or element. - Markers update incrementally after every transaction (no manual refresh). In views with more than 5 000 issues, only the first 5 000 are drawn and the status bar shows the total. - Elements in linked models are checked but their markers cannot be acted on. - Check Systems does not alter the model, so toggling is not undoable.

    Data (IFC mapping). No model data. Issues are the standard persisted warnings (project/warnings, chapter 2).

    Commands. - mep_check.systems(kind: "duct"|"pipe"|"circuit", view_id, on: bool) -> issues[]: each issue is {kind, element_ids[], connector_refs[], message}. - mep_check.show_disconnects(view_id, domains[], on: bool) -> ports[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A pipe run with one unconnected end shows one disconnect marker. Connecting the end removes the marker without a manual refresh. - [ ] Two connected connectors both set to Out produce one flow direction mismatch issue naming both elements. - [ ] A supply-air system with no equipment selected is reported as not well connected. - [ ] Show Disconnects with only the Conduit domain ticked shows no markers on open duct ends.

    4.6.7 Mechanical settings

    ID: MEP-SET-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §7.3

    UI. Manage › MEP Settings › Mechanical Settings, or the HVAC and Plumbing panel launchers (mep_settings.show("mechanical"), common dialog behaviour in MEP-SET-004). Tree: - Hidden Line: whether MEP hidden lines are drawn, their line style, the inside and outside gap, and the single-line gap. - Duct Settings: - single-line fitting annotation scale and fitting annotation size - air density and air dynamic viscosity - size separators and suffixes, connector separator, flat-on-top and flat-on-bottom suffixes, rise/drop annotation size - Angles: any angle, an increment, or a list of specific angles - Conversion: main and branch duct type, offset and flex settings used by placeholder conversion and layout generation - Rectangular, Oval and Round size tables, with flags Used in Size Lists and Used in Sizing - Calculation: the friction method for straight segments (selectable equations, for example Colebrook or Altshul–Tsal) - Pipe Settings: - annotation sizes, suffix and separators - Angles and Conversion - Segments and Sizes: a segment is a material plus a schedule or class, with roughness and a size catalogue (nominal, inner and outer diameter), each flagged Used in Size Lists or Used in Sizing - Fluids: name, then a table of temperature, dynamic viscosity and density - Slopes: a list of allowed slope values; zero cannot be removed, and values above 45° give a warning - Calculation: background hydronic network analysis on or off; pressure-drop method (Colebrook or Haaland); fixture-unit-to-flow method

    Data (IFC mapping). RXD document mep_settings. Pipe segments are also written as IfcPipeSegmentType objects with Pset_PipeSegmentTypeCommon (NominalDiameter, InnerDiameter, OuterDiameter, Roughness), so other tools see the size catalogue.

    Commands. - mechanical_settings.get(path) -> value - mechanical_settings.set(path, value) - pipe_segment.create(material_id, schedule, roughness, sizes[]) -> id - fluid.create(name, table[]) -> id - duct_size_table.set(shape, sizes[])

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Removing a duct size from Used in Size Lists removes it from the size drop-down but keeps existing ducts of that size valid. - [ ] Trying to delete the zero slope is refused.

    4.6.8 Electrical settings

    ID: MEP-SET-002 · Priority: P1 (wiring, tray, conduit, voltages) / P2 (load calculations, circuit naming, panel schedules) · Ref: research/03 §7.3

    UI. Manage › MEP Settings › Electrical Settings (mep_settings.show("electrical"), common dialog behaviour in MEP-SET-004). Tree: - Hidden Line. - General: - connector separator - electrical data style - circuit description format - phase labels (A/B/C or L1/L2/L3) - capitalisation of load names - circuit sequence: numerical, or grouped by phase - default circuit rating - circuit path offset - Angles. - Wiring: - ambient temperature - gap at wire crossings - tick mark styles for hot, ground and neutral conductors - slanted line across tick marks - whether tick marks are shown - wire sizes, correction factors and ground conductors - wiring types: material, temperature rating, insulation, maximum size, neutral multiplier, whether a neutral is required, and conduit type - Voltage definitions: name, value, minimum and maximum. - Distribution systems: name, phase (single or three), configuration (wye or delta), number of wires (2–4), line-to-line voltage, line-to-ground voltage, and high-leg phase. - Cable tray and conduit settings: annotation, size separator and suffix, rise/drop symbols, size tables, and conduit standards. Reviera ships open tables for common standards and lets users add their own. - Load calculations: on/off for space load calculations, with links to load classifications and demand factors (MEP-ELEC-009/010). - Circuit naming schemes (MEP-ELEC-012). - Panel schedules: spare label, space label, whether spares count in totals, and whether multi-pole circuits are merged into one cell.

    Data (IFC mapping). RXD document electrical. Conduit and tray sizes are also written as IfcCableCarrierSegmentType objects with their nominal sizes.

    Commands. - electrical_settings.get(path) -> value - electrical_settings.set(path, value) - distribution_system.create(name, phase, config, wires, v_ll, v_lg) -> id - voltage.create(name, value, min, max) -> id - wiring_type.create(params) -> id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 400/230 V 3-phase 4-wire wye distribution system can be created and assigned to a panel, and only devices with a matching voltage definition can be circuited to it.

    4.6.9 Conductor and cable settings (international)

    ID: MEP-SET-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §7.3 · screenshots/structure_mep/electrical_conductor_and_cable_settings.png

    Behaviour & rules. Manage › MEP Settings › Conductor & Cable Settings is a tabbed dialog with searchable, sortable grids: - conductor materials - insulation materials - conductor sizes (name, cross-section area or gauge, diameter) - conductor details (material, size, insulation, ampacity) - cable sizes (number and size of phase conductors, plus ground and neutral) - cable types (assembled cables used by circuits)

    The dialog supports both IEC (mm²) and AWG/kcmil conventions. Reviera ships starter tables taken from openly published physical data such as cross-sections and resistivity. Ampacity tables are user-supplied or loaded from content packs, because code tables may be copyrighted (§4.17).

    Data (IFC mapping). RXD document electrical. Cable types are written as IfcCableSegmentType (CABLESEGMENT) with Pset_CableSegmentTypeCableSegment and Pset_CableSegmentTypeConductorSegment.

    Commands. - conductor_size.create(name, area_mm2 | gauge, diameter) -> id - cable_type.create(name, material_id, insulation_id, phase_conductors: {count, size_id}, neutral?: size_id, ground?: size_id) -> id - conductor_table.import(path)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 5 × 2.5 mm² Cu/PVC cable type can be defined and chosen on a circuit, and voltage drop uses its conductor resistance.

    4.6.10 MEP settings dialogs (common shell)

    ID: MEP-SET-004 · Priority: P1 (mechanical, electrical) / P2 (other kinds) · Ref: research/03 §1.6, §7.3, §10.4, §11, §12.1, §14

    Purpose. Give every MEP settings area one entry point, mep_settings.show(kind), and one dialog behaviour, so that the Manage › MEP Settings drop-down, the panel launchers on the Systems tab and Lua or MCP callers all reach the same editor.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Manage › MEP Settings › an item, a Systems-tab panel launcher (HVAC, Plumbing & Piping, Electrical, Fabrication, P&ID), or the proposed shortcuts MS, ES, BT, FS. 2. The dialog opens on the requested kind. A tree or tab strip on the left selects a page; the page grid or form is on the right. 3. Edit values. Every field validates as it loses focus; the page shows a red text hint and a theme warning glyph next to an invalid value. 4. OK commits all changed pages as one transaction named after the dialog ("Mechanical Settings"). Cancel discards everything. Apply is not offered, so a dialog session is always a single undo step.

    UI. The kind values and the dialog each opens:

    kind Dialog Pages and grids (detail in)
    mechanical Mechanical Settings Hidden Line, Duct Settings, Pipe Settings and their sub-pages (MEP-SET-001)
    electrical Electrical Settings General, Wiring, Voltage Definitions, Distribution Systems, Cable Tray and Conduit, Load Calculations, Circuit Naming, Panel Schedules (MEP-SET-002)
    conductor_cable Conductor & Cable Settings six searchable grids (MEP-SET-003)
    building_space_type Building/Space Type Settings two tabs, Building Types and Space Types (below)
    load_classification Load Classifications list of classifications (below)
    demand_factor Demand Factors list of definitions with a method editor (below)
    fabrication Fabrication Settings configuration, profile, services (MEP-FAB-002)
    pid P&ID Settings System Types and Object Mapping tabs (MEP-PID-002)
    • Building/Space Type Settings. Left: a list of types with New, Duplicate, Rename and Delete. Right: lighting load density, power load density, area per person, sensible and latent heat gain per person, plenum lighting contribution, occupancy, lighting and power schedules (picked from the ANA-EM-002 schedule library), heating and cooling set points, outside-air per person and per area, and opening and closing times. A type used by spaces cannot be deleted; the refusal states how many spaces use it.
    • Load Classifications. Left: the list, with Lighting, Power, HVAC, Motor and Other locked against deletion. Right: name, demand factor (drop-down with an edit button that jumps to the Demand Factors dialog) and the space-load option Use in space load calculation. Renaming updates every connector that refers to it.
    • Demand Factors. Left: definitions. Right: method (Constant, By quantity, By load), incremental check box, a range grid (from, to, percentage), the optional largest-motor table, and a live preview that evaluates a typed connected load. Ranges must be contiguous and non-overlapping, start at 0, and have percentages from 0 to 1 000%; the grid flags the first offending row.

    Behaviour & rules. - Only one MEP settings dialog is open at a time. Opening a second kind while one is open switches the open dialog to that kind after asking to keep or discard pending edits. - Settings are project-wide. In BIMserver mode the dialog warns that edits change shared project standards and merge like any other RXD change (02a §8). - Every page has Search, so long size tables and type lists can be filtered. - A value that is still referenced (a size, a slope, a voltage definition, a wiring type, a load classification) cannot be deleted; the refusal names one referencing element and the count. - Units follow the project units (chapter 2). Fields accept expressions and unit suffixes. - The same data can be set without the dialog through mechanical_settings.set, electrical_settings.set, space_type.create and the other commands of the requirements above.

    Data (IFC mapping). No IFC entity. The pages write to RXD documents mep_settings (mechanical, P&ID), electrical (electrical, conductors, load classifications, demand factors), analysis (building and space types) and fabrication.

    Commands. mep_settings.show(kind: "mechanical"|"electrical"|"conductor_cable"|"building_space_type"|"load_classification"|"demand_factor"|"fabrication"|"pid"). It only opens the dialog; the edits are recorded as the per-setting commands listed in each requirement, inside one transaction.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] mep_settings.show("demand_factor") opens the Demand Factors dialog, and from Lua or MCP the same call returns without error when no UI is attached (headless) by reporting ui_unavailable. - [ ] Editing three pages of Mechanical Settings and pressing OK adds exactly one entry to the undo stack; Undo reverts all three pages. - [ ] Deleting the space type "Office" while 12 spaces use it is refused with a message that names the count 12. - [ ] A demand-factor range grid with a gap between 10 and 12 kVA cannot be saved, and the row at 12 kVA is flagged.

    4.7 HVAC (ductwork)

    4.7.1 Duct placement

    ID: MEP-DUCT-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §8.1

    Purpose. Draw rigid ducts that insert fittings automatically according to the duct type's routing preferences.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Systems › HVAC › Duct (proposed DT). 2. In the Type Selector pick a duct type (rectangular, round or oval). On the contextual tab and in Properties set: - width and height, or diameter - middle elevation, with a history list, and an elevation lock - the reference level - the system type 3. Click a start point and an end point. Change the middle elevation and click Apply in the middle of a run to create a vertical riser. Risers that span levels, and the rise/drop symbols shown on them, are specified in MEP-DUCT-011.

    UI. Contextual "Modify | Place Duct" tab: - Justification (horizontal justification, horizontal offset, vertical justification) - Automatically Connect - Inherit Elevation and Inherit Size - sloped connection options Add Vertical and Change Slope - Tag on Placement - size and elevation fields (there is no Options Bar)

    On a selected duct the canvas shows end grips, editable size text, fitting "+" and "−" controls, flip and rotate. The context menu offers Draw Duct, Draw Flex Duct, Cap Open Ends and Select (Tab cycles through connected elements).

    Behaviour & rules. - Elbows, tees, transitions and taps are inserted automatically. The routing preferences (MEP-DUCT-002) choose them, and the Angles setting limits the angles. - Automatically Connect snaps to and connects with ducts it crosses. Junctions use the preferred junction type. - Size Lock stops a segment from being resized by sizing. - Vertical ducts are best drawn in section or elevation, or with Apply.

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcDuctSegment (RIGIDSEGMENT), typed by IfcDuctSegmentType, with two nested IfcDistributionPorts. - Properties: Pset_DuctSegmentTypeCommon (Shape, WorkingPressure, …) and Pset_DuctSegmentOccurrence (InteriorRoughnessCoefficient, HasLiner, Color). - Calculated flow values go to Pset_DuctSegmentOccurrence, or to an analytical segment (MEP-CALC-002). - Quantities: Qto_DuctSegmentBaseQuantities (Length, GrossCrossSectionArea, OuterSurfaceArea, GrossWeight). - RXD element data (constraints): justification, size lock and elevation lock.

    Commands. - duct.create(type_id, start, end, shape_size, middle_elevation, level_id, system_type_id?, justification?) -> element_ids[] (the segments and fittings created) - duct.set_size(ids[], size) - duct.cap_open_ends(ids[])

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Drawing an L-shaped 600 × 300 run inserts one elbow from the routing preferences. - [ ] Changing the middle elevation from 3.0 m to 3.6 m mid-draw and pressing Apply inserts two elbows and a vertical segment. - [ ] The exported run contains IfcDuctSegment and IfcDuctFitting elements linked by IfcRelConnectsPorts.

    4.7.2 Routing preferences

    ID: MEP-DUCT-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §8.1 ("Routing Preferences"), §15.3

    Purpose. An ordered list of parts per role and size range, used to choose segments and fittings automatically. This applies to duct, pipe, cable tray and conduit types.

    UI. Type Properties › Routing Preferences › Edit. A grid with one group per role: - Segment (pipe only: material and schedule) - Elbow - Junction (tee, tap or takeoff), with a preferred junction type of Tee or Tap - Cross - Transition - Union - Multi-shape Transition, for example rectangular to round - Cap

    Each row has a part and a minimum and maximum size. Rows are tried from top to bottom.

    Behaviour & rules. - When no row fits, Reviera inserts nothing, leaves the connection open and raises a warning that names the role and size. - Reapply Type re-runs fitting selection on existing runs after preferences change. Change Type swaps a run's type and reapplies the preferences.

    Data (IFC mapping). RXD document mep_settings (routing preferences per type GlobalId).

    Commands. - routing_preferences.get(type_id) -> table - routing_preferences.set(type_id, table) - mep_run.reapply_type(element_ids[]) - mep_run.change_type(element_ids[], type_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With Junction rows "Tap ≤ 300 mm, Tee > 300 mm", a 250 mm branch gets a tap and a 400 mm branch gets a tee. - [ ] After a row is removed, Reapply Type replaces the affected fittings and warns where no row fits.

    4.7.3 Duct fittings and fitting controls

    ID: MEP-DUCT-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §8.3

    Behaviour & rules. - Duct Fitting (proposed DF) places a fitting on a duct end or along a duct. A tee inserted in the middle of a run takes the run's size and elevation. - In-canvas controls: - size per leg; a transition is added automatically when it is needed - flip, relative to airflow - rotate - "+" upgrades an elbow to a tee, or a tee to a cross - "−" removes an unused leg - Damper visibility inside fittings is a family parameter.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcDuctFitting. PredefinedType: BEND for elbows, JUNCTION for tees, crosses and taps, TRANSITION, CONNECTOR for unions, OBSTRUCTION for caps, and ENTRY/EXIT. Types are IfcDuctFittingType. Pset_DuctFittingTypeCommon. Loss coefficients are written to Pset_DuctFittingOccurrence where they are defined.

    Commands. - duct_fitting.place(type_id, host_duct_id | point, params) -> id - mep_fitting.upgrade(id) - mep_fitting.downgrade(id, leg) - mep_fitting.flip(id) - mep_fitting.rotate(id, angle)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] "+" on an elbow whose run continues straight turns it into a tee with an open third leg. "−" on that unused leg turns it back.

    4.7.4 Duct accessories, insulation and lining

    ID: MEP-DUCT-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §8.1, §8.3

    Purpose. Insert inline duct components and apply external insulation or internal lining to duct runs.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Systems › HVAC › Duct Accessory (proposed DA) and pick a type in the Type Selector. 2. Hover a duct: the preview snaps to the centreline and orients the accessory along the flow. Click to insert, or click an open duct end to attach it there. 3. For insulation or lining, select ducts, fittings or accessories (Tab selects a whole run) and choose Modify | Ducts › Insulation › Add (or Lining › Add). A dialog asks for the type and the thickness; Edit changes them and Remove deletes them.

    Behaviour & rules. - Duct Accessory (proposed DA) inserts dampers, fire dampers, filters, coils and sound attenuators inline. Insertion splits the duct and connects both sides. - The accessory takes the duct's size and shape when its family has size parameters linked to its connectors. If it cannot match (for example a fixed-size round damper on a rectangular duct), transitions are added from the routing preferences; if none fits, the insert is refused with a message naming the size. - An accessory must fit between existing fittings: if the free straight length is shorter than the accessory, the insert is refused ("Not enough straight duct for this accessory"). - Deleting an inline accessory leaves the two duct ends open; Heal in the context menu rejoins them into one segment when they are collinear and the same size. - Add/Edit/Remove Insulation and Duct Lining take a type and a thickness. Insulation is included in interference checking. - Insulation and lining follow their host: they regenerate when the host is resized or moved and are deleted with it. Lining reduces the free cross-section used by pressure-drop calculations (MEP-CALC-002); insulation does not. - Default thicknesses: insulation 25 mm, lining 25 mm. Thickness must be greater than 0 and less than half the smallest duct dimension for lining; otherwise the dialog shows an inline error. - Insulation and lining types are ordinary types (material, roughness for lining) shown in the Project Browser and are drawn using their own object style (chapter 5).

    Data (IFC mapping).

    Item IFC
    Damper IfcDamper (FIREDAMPER, CONTROLDAMPER, BACKDRAFTDAMPER, …)
    Filter IfcFilter
    Coil IfcCoil
    Sound attenuator IfcDuctSilencer
    Insulation and lining IfcCovering with PredefinedType INSULATION or WRAPPING, related with IfcRelCoversBldgElements. Thickness on the covering.

    Commands. - duct_accessory.place(type_id, duct_id, point) -> id - mep_insulation.add(element_ids[], type_id, thickness) - mep_insulation.remove(element_ids[]) - mep_insulation.set(element_ids[], type_id?, thickness?) (Edit Insulation) - duct_lining.add(element_ids[], type_id, thickness) - duct_lining.remove(element_ids[])

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A fire damper inserted in a 400 mm round duct splits it into two segments connected through the damper. - [ ] Adding 50 mm insulation exports an IfcCovering (INSULATION) related to the duct. - [ ] Resizing an insulated 600 × 300 duct to 800 × 300 regenerates its insulation at the new size with the same thickness. - [ ] Adding 25 mm lining to a 400 × 200 duct lowers the free area used by the pressure-drop calculation to 350 × 150. - [ ] Inserting a 600 mm long silencer into a 400 mm straight between two elbows is refused with a message.

    4.7.5 Flexible duct

    ID: MEP-DUCT-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §8.3

    Purpose. Model the short flexible connections between rigid branches and terminals or equipment, so that layouts, quantities and pressure losses include them.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Systems › HVAC › Flex Duct (proposed FD), or Draw Flex Duct from the context menu of an open connector. 2. Pick the type and size (diameter, or width and height) on the contextual tab and in Properties. 3. Click the start (a connector, a duct centreline or a free point), then intermediate points, then the end. Ending on a connector connects it; double-click or Enter ends at a free point. 4. To convert existing runs, select terminals and choose Convert to Flex Duct (proposed CV), then enter the maximum length.

    Behaviour & rules. - Flex Duct (proposed FD) has round and rectangular types. It is drawn from a connector or a duct centreline, as a spline with vertex, tangent and end grips. Flex Duct Controls add and delete vertices. - Starting on a duct centreline inserts a takeoff (tap) chosen by the rigid duct's routing preferences; if none is defined for the size, the start is refused with a message naming the role and size. - The spline passes through every clicked point; end tangents follow the connector directions. Minimum bend radius is the type's Minimum Bend Radius (default 1 × diameter); a tighter shape is accepted but flagged with a warning. - Pressure loss. The type carries a roughness and an optional loss multiplier for compressed flex (default 1.0), used by MEP-CALC-002. - Plan display. Flex duct can show a type-defined flex pattern (a sine or wavy line) in single-line and two-line views. - Convert to Flex (proposed CV) converts the last segment before a terminal into flex duct, up to a maximum length. - Convert to Flex works per terminal: if the final rigid segment (plus the elbow at the terminal, if any) is longer than the limit, that terminal is skipped and listed in the report. Converted flex keeps the system and the size of the replaced segment. - Recovery. Drawing journals each click (flex.pick{point, snap_ref?}) and each size or type change (flex.set{param, value}) as micro-operations; replay re-applies them in order and reopens the session at the last point (conventions §2.1).

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcDuctSegment (FLEXIBLESEGMENT), with a swept-disk body along a B-spline. Length goes to Qto_DuctSegmentBaseQuantities.Length (spline length). Control points and tangents are RXD element data (sketch), so the spline is re-editable.

    Commands. - flex_duct.create(type_id, points[], start_port?, end_port?) -> id - duct.convert_to_flex(terminal_ids[], max_length) -> ids[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Convert to Flex with a 1.5 m limit converts only branches whose final segment is 1.5 m or shorter. - [ ] A flex duct drawn from a duct centreline to a diffuser inserts a tap from the routing preferences and connects at both ends. - [ ] The exported flex duct's Length equals the spline length within 1 mm. - [ ] After a simulated crash during drawing with three points picked, the recovered session resumes with the same three points.

    4.7.6 Justification editor

    ID: MEP-DUCT-006 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §8.1 ("Justify")

    Workflow. 1. Select a run with Tab. 2. Choose Justify. 3. Choose a control point: the start or end segment. 4. Pick one of 9 alignment points (top, middle or bottom × left, centre or right), or pick an alignment line in a wireframe 3D view. 5. Finish.

    Purpose. Align a run whose segments change size so that one face or edge stays continuous, for example a flat bottom for ceiling clearance or a flush side along a wall.

    UI. Contextual tab Justification Editor: Control Point (cycles between the run's first and last segment, shown by an arrow glyph), the 3 × 3 alignment buttons, Alignment Line (active only in a wireframe or hidden-line 3D view), Finish and Cancel. The current alignment point is drawn on the control segment's end face.

    Behaviour & rules. The run keeps its control segment fixed and re-aligns every segment to the chosen face or edge. Fittings regenerate. - Applies to ducts, pipes, cable tray and conduit runs. For round ducts and pipes, only top, middle and bottom are meaningful vertically; left and right align the outside diameter. - A run is a chain without branches selected with Tab.
