Selecting elements that do not form one chain is refused: "Justify needs a single run without branches". - Segments that are size-locked keep their size; only their position moves. Sloped segments keep their slope. - If re-alignment would disconnect a branch whose own run is not selected, the branch's connecting segment is stretched or moved so it stays connected; if that is impossible, the editor reports the branch and the change is not applied. - Alignment Line aligns the selected edge line of every segment to the picked edge of the control segment. - The justification chosen is written to each segment's justification settings, so later size changes keep the alignment. - Recovery. The editor journals justify.control{end}, justify.align{point | line_ref} as micro-operations; replay restores the pending choice before Finish (conventions §2.1). Finish commits in one transaction; Cancel discards it.

    Data (IFC mapping). Geometry changes only. Justification values are RXD element data (constraints) on each segment (MEP-DUCT-001).

    Commands. mep_run.justify(element_ids[], control_end, alignment: "TL"|"TC"|…|"BR" | line_ref)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Justifying a run that transitions from 600 to 400 mm wide to Bottom-Left makes the bottoms and left sides of all segments flush. - [ ] Selecting a run that includes a tee and its branch refuses Justify with the message above. - [ ] After justifying Bottom-Centre, changing one segment's height keeps its bottom flush with the others.

    4.7.7 Placeholders and conversion

    ID: MEP-DUCT-007 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §8.2

    Purpose. Let designers lay out duct and pipe routes quickly, early in design, and turn them into fully fitted runs later without redrawing.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Duct Placeholder or Pipe Placeholder (on the Duct and Pipe split buttons). Set type, size, middle elevation and system type as for real ducts or pipes (MEP-DUCT-001, MEP-PIPE-001). 2. Click points as for real ducts or pipes. Placeholders connect to each other end-to-end and to equipment connectors. 3. Select placeholders (Tab selects a connected set) and choose Convert Placeholder. 4. Review the conversion report: it lists every junction that could not be fitted and leaves those ends open.

    Behaviour & rules. - Duct and pipe placeholders are single-line elements without fittings, used for fast layout and coordination. They keep their size and system. - Placeholders join directly at corners and junctions: no elbows or tees exist, so a placeholder network is a graph of segments meeting at points. - They are drawn as single lines in every detail level and are included in system flow and Check Systems, but not in sizing, pressure-drop calculation or interference checking (a body is needed for those). - Justification settings are not available for placeholders; the line is always the centreline. - Convert Placeholder produces real ducts or pipes and fittings using the type's routing preferences. Conversion warnings are listed for review. - Conversion keeps each placeholder's GlobalId on the resulting segment and creates new fittings. Sloped pipe placeholders keep their slope. - A placeholder network that contains a junction of more than four legs, or legs meeting at an angle that the Angles setting does not allow, is converted up to that junction and the remaining ends are left open with a warning. - Real ducts and pipes cannot be converted back; Undo restores the placeholders.

    Data (IFC mapping). Placeholders are IfcDuctSegment or IfcPipeSegment with an Axis representation only (no Body). A placeholder flag is RXD element data (constraints). Other tools see a segment with no body.

    Commands. - duct_placeholder.create(type_id, start, end, size, elevation, level) -> id - pipe_placeholder.create(type_id, start, end, diameter, middle_elevation, level_id, system_type_id?, slope?) -> id - placeholder.convert(ids[]) -> element_ids[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Converting an L-shaped placeholder pair produces two segments and one elbow at the original elevation. - [ ] A converted placeholder segment keeps its GlobalId and system membership. - [ ] A five-leg placeholder junction converts every other junction and leaves that junction's ends open, listed in the report. - [ ] An exported placeholder has an Axis representation and no Body.

    4.7.8 Generate Layout (system-based auto-routing)

    ID: MEP-DUCT-008 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §8.2

    Workflow. 1. Select a system component and choose Generate Layout. 2. Reviera proposes several solutions, each a different trunk-and-branch arrangement: network, perimeter, intersections or custom. 3. Settings: main and branch type, offsets, and slope for pipe. 4. Edit Layout adjusts trunk positions. 5. Finish Layout creates placeholders or real elements.

    Purpose. Propose trunk-and-branch routes for an existing logical system, so a first layout can be produced from equipment and terminals alone.

    UI. Contextual tab Generate Layout: Solution Type drop-down (Network, Perimeter, Intersections), a solution counter with previous/next arrows ("Solution 2 of 5"), Settings, Edit Layout, Solutions, Finish Layout and Cancel Layout. The preview draws the trunk in one theme token and branches in another, both with text labels in the legend, plus warning glyphs where a component cannot be reached.

    Behaviour & rules. The router avoids nothing in the first release. It routes orthogonally in the layout plane, and clashes are left to the interference check. Obstacle-aware routing is an open question (§4.17). - Solution types: - Network: a trunk along the minimal rectangle enclosing the components, with branches to each one. - Perimeter: trunks around the bounding rectangle at an inset set in Settings (default 1 m). - Intersections: trunks along lines through the components in both directions, choosing intersections that minimise length. - Custom: any solution after Edit Layout has changed it. Solutions are ranked by total length; up to 10 per type are offered. - Settings dialog: duct or pipe type for main and branch, offset of the layout plane from the level (default: the equipment connector's elevation), and for pipe a slope from the allowed list. Changing settings regenerates solutions. - Edit Layout lets the user drag trunk lines and move branch connection points. Each drag is journalled as a micro-operation (layout.move_line{line_index, delta}, layout.move_point{point_index, position}); replay restores the edited solution (conventions §2.1). - The system must have equipment and at least one other member, and all must be on connectors of the same domain. Otherwise the tool is refused with a message naming the problem. - Finish Layout creates placeholders or real elements in one transaction and connects them to the components. Junctions that cannot be fitted are left open and reported (as for MEP-DUCT-007). - Unfinished solutions are session data and are discarded by Cancel Layout; nothing is written to the model before Finish.

    Data (IFC mapping). No data of its own. The result is ordinary ducts, pipes, placeholders and fittings.

    Commands. - mep_layout.generate(system_id, settings) -> solution_ids[] - mep_layout.edit(solution_id, moves[]) -> solution_id (each move is {line_index | point_index, delta | position}) - mep_layout.finish(solution_id, as: "placeholder"|"real") -> element_ids[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] For a system of one AHU and 6 diffusers, at least two solutions are offered, and Finish connects all 7 components. - [ ] Solutions within one type are listed in ascending order of total length. - [ ] Generate Layout on a system without equipment is refused with a message. - [ ] Moving a trunk line in Edit Layout and finishing creates elements along the moved line.

    4.7.9 Air terminals and mechanical equipment

    ID: MEP-DUCT-009 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §8.4

    Behaviour & rules. - Air Terminal (proposed AT) supports Tag on Placement. Air Terminal on Duct places the terminal on a duct face. The terminal's preset flow adds to the running supply, return or exhaust totals of the space it sits in. - Mechanical Equipment (proposed ME): AHUs, VAV boxes, fans, boilers, chillers, pumps and radiators. Spacebar rotates by 90°. Equipment connectors are Calculated by default. - Equipment sets group duty and standby pumps (Add and Remove pumps). Only duty units count toward flow. - Mechanical Control Device: thermostats and sensors, specified in MEP-DUCT-012. - Connect Into routes from a selected component's connector into an existing duct or pipe main.

    Data (IFC mapping).

    Item IFC
    Air terminal IfcAirTerminal (DIFFUSER, GRILLE, REGISTER, LOUVRE)
    VAV box IfcAirTerminalBox
    AHU IfcUnitaryEquipment (AIRHANDLER)
    Fan IfcFan
    Boiler IfcBoiler
    Chiller IfcChiller
    Pump IfcPump
    Radiator IfcSpaceHeater
    Controls IfcController, IfcSensor
    Equipment set IfcGroup with ObjectType "EquipmentSet"; duty and standby roles in RXD element data (mep_settings)

    Commands. - air_terminal.place(type_id, point | duct_face_ref, level, flow?) -> id - mech_equipment.place(type_id, point, level, rotation) -> id - equipment_set.create(equipment_ids[], duty_ids[]) -> id - mep.connect_into(element_id, connector_index, target_id) -> element_ids[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Placing three 100 L/s supply diffusers in a space sets its actual supply airflow to 300 L/s. - [ ] In a duty/standby set of two pumps, only the duty pump's flow appears in system totals.

    4.7.10 Duct and pipe color fill legends

    ID: MEP-DUCT-010 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §8.1 ("Color fill")

    Purpose. Show at a glance how a calculated or descriptive value varies across duct and pipe networks in a plan or section view.

    Workflow. 1. In a plan, ceiling plan or section view, choose Analyze › Color Fill › Duct Legend or Pipe Legend. 2. Click to place the legend. If the view has no scheme for that kind, a Choose Colour Scheme dialog lists the existing duct or pipe schemes and offers Edit. 3. Select the legend and choose Edit Scheme to change the parameter, the ranges and the colours.

    Behaviour & rules. Analyze › Color Fill › Duct Legend / Pipe Legend places a legend and colours runs by a chosen parameter, such as flow, velocity, friction, pressure or size. Colour schemes are shared with chapter 5's colour-fill engine. - Parameters offered: for ducts, flow, velocity, friction, pressure drop, size, system type and system name; for pipes, the same plus fluid temperature and slope. Calculated values need the system's Calculations to include them (MEP-SYS-001); elements without a value use the scheme's No value colour (default: none). - Scheme kinds: By value (each distinct value gets a colour) or By range (bands with editable boundaries, default 5 equal bands over the current min–max). Colours come from theme-aware palettes and every legend row carries a text label, so meaning does not depend on colour alone. - Fill applies to segments and, optionally, to fittings and accessories (scheme option Include fittings, default on). Insulation takes the colour of its host. - One duct legend and one pipe legend per view. Deleting the legend removes the fill from the view. The fill is a view setting and changes no element. - Values update when the network calculation finishes (MEP-CALC-002); stale results are drawn hatched until recalculation completes.

    Data (IFC mapping). No model data. Schemes are stored in views/color_schemes (kind colorscheme) and the legend as view annotation (anno.colorlegend), both chapter 5.

    Commands. mep_color_legend.place(view_id, kind: "duct"|"pipe", scheme_id, point) -> id. Schemes are created and edited with colorscheme.create (chapter 5).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A velocity scheme with bands at 4 and 8 m/s colours each segment in the band for its velocity. - [ ] Placing a second duct legend in the same view is refused; a pipe legend in the same view is accepted. - [ ] Deleting the legend removes all duct colouring from that view and from no other view. - [ ] A segment whose system has Calculations = None shows the No value colour in a velocity scheme.

    4.7.11 Duct and pipe sizing

    ID: MEP-CALC-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §8.5, §9.1

    Workflow. Select a run or system, choose Analysis › Duct/Pipe Sizing, pick a method and constraints, then OK.

    Behaviour & rules. - Duct methods: - Friction and/or Velocity, combined as Only, And or Or - Equal Friction, with a default target of 1 Pa/m (≈ 0.1 in. w.g. per 100 ft) - Static Regain - Pipe methods: Friction and/or Velocity (Only, And or Or). Pipe sizing is not offered for sanitary systems; drainage sizing is a separate open question. - Constraints: - Branch sizing: calculated size only, match connector size, or the larger of the two - Restrict Height and Restrict Width (and restrict inner diameter for pipe) - Size constraints win over flow targets. Each conflict raises a warning. - Sizing needs a connected system with valid flow. Size-locked segments are skipped. - Fitting loss data: loss coefficients come from each fitting type's data table. That is either a coefficient, a coefficient table by geometry ratio, or a specific loss. Reviera ships open coefficient tables built from public-domain sources and lets content authors supply their own. Reviera does not bundle any proprietary fitting-loss database (§4.17).

    Commands. mep.size(element_ids[] | system_id, method, targets: {friction?, velocity?}, combine, branch_rule, restrict?: {height?, width?, inner_diameter?}) -> report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Equal Friction at 1 Pa/m on a 3-branch supply system sizes each segment to the smallest size in the Used in Sizing table whose friction is at or below 1 Pa/m. - [ ] Restrict Height = 300 mm keeps every rectangular segment at or below 300 mm high and widens segments to compensate. - [ ] Size-locked segments keep their size, and the report lists them as skipped.

    4.7.12 Pressure drop and analytical segments

    ID: MEP-CALC-002 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §8.5 · screenshots/structure_mep/analytical_duct_segments_tag.png · screenshots/structure_mep/analytical_duct_segment_schedule_critical_path.png

    Purpose. A network calculation produces analytical segments: sub-elements that represent the flow path and carry results.

    Behaviour & rules. - Pressure drop is calculated from geometry, roughness, fluid properties (air density and viscosity, or the pipe fluid table) and fitting losses. The friction equation is the one selected in settings. - Each analytical duct or pipe segment carries flow, velocity, friction, pressure drop, network ID and a critical path flag. - Analytical segments can be selected with Tab, tagged and scheduled. They take per-segment overrides, for example a measured loss. They also work over fabrication parts (§4.10). - The calculation runs in the background (ANA-GEN-001) when a system's Calculations setting is All or Performance.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Results are written to the physical segments' standard occurrence psets: Pset_DuctSegmentOccurrence and Pset_PipeSegmentOccurrence, plus flow-performance values in Pset_DistributionPortCommon/port psets where they are defined. - Analytical segments themselves are computed sub-elements, not IFC entities. Their overrides and the critical-path cache are RXD element data (analysis) on the physical segment.

    Commands. - mep_network.calculate(system_id | "all") -> job_id - analytical_segment.list(system_id) -> segments[] - analytical_segment.override(segment_ref, params)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A schedule of analytical duct segments filtered by "critical path = yes" lists exactly the segments on the highest-loss path from the fan to a terminal. - [ ] Changing one segment's size marks the network results stale until recalculation completes.

    4.7.13 System Inspector

    ID: MEP-CALC-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §8.5 ("System Inspector")

    Purpose. Let the engineer explore a calculated duct or pipe system interactively in a view and see where pressure is lost.

    UI. Contextual tab System Inspector: Inspect (toggle), Properties (opens the selected section's values in a read-only panel), Exit. While active, the canvas shows flow arrows on every section, a hover tooltip, and a small legend explaining the critical-path highlight in words.

    Behaviour & rules. - Select a system and choose Analysis › System Inspector › Inspect. - Flow arrows are drawn. Hovering shows flow, static pressure and pressure loss for each section. - The critical path is highlighted, using a theme warning colour rather than a hard-coded red. Terminals show their excess pressure relative to the critical path. - The inspector needs a well-connected system. It is not offered for fire-protection systems. - A section is a stretch of the network with constant flow between two junctions; hovering any element of it shows the section's values. Values come from the latest network calculation (MEP-CALC-002); if results are stale, the inspector first starts a recalculation and shows a progress bar until it completes. - Preconditions and refusals: the system must have equipment, Calculations = All or Performance, and no open connectors; otherwise Inspect is refused with the first failing condition named ("System has open connectors: 3. Run Show Disconnects"). - The inspector is a view session: it changes no model data, and editing the model while it is active ends the session. - Units follow the project's HVAC or piping units (chapter 2 units).

    Data (IFC mapping). None. It reads analytical-segment results.

    Commands. - system_inspector.start(system_id, view_id) - system_inspector.stop() - Section values are also available to scripts through analytical_segment.list (MEP-CALC-002).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Hovering a branch segment shows its flow and static pressure, and the critical path is visually distinct. - [ ] Inspect on a system with an open connector is refused and the message gives the number of open connectors. - [ ] The excess pressure shown at a terminal equals the critical-path loss minus that terminal's path loss, within 1 Pa.

    4.7.14 Pressure loss report

    ID: MEP-CALC-004 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §8.5 ("Pressure Loss Report")

    Purpose. Produce a shareable, per-section record of a system's pressure losses for review, submittals and equipment selection.

    Workflow. 1. Open from Analyze › Reports & Schedules › Pressure Loss Report (duct or pipe), or right-click a system in the System Browser. 2. In Select Systems, tick systems; a filter limits the list by classification. Only systems with Calculations = All are selectable; others are shown greyed with the reason. 3. In Report Settings, choose the fields per table, the sections to include and the format, then Generate and choose a file path.

    Behaviour & rules. - Open from Analyze › Reports & Schedules › Pressure Loss Report, or right-click in the System Browser. - Choose systems, then the report settings: fields, system information, critical path and fitting detail. - Output is HTML or CSV. Systems must have Calculations = All. - Report sections: project information; system information (name, type, classification, total flow, equipment); a Total pressure loss table by section; Segment detail (length, size, flow, velocity, friction, loss); Fitting and accessory detail (part type, loss method, coefficient, loss); and Critical path (the ordered list of sections and its total). - Report settings can be saved as named presets in model/mep (mep_settings), so a team uses the same format. - Stale results are recalculated before the report is written. If recalculation fails, the report is not written and the error is shown. - HTML uses the project's units with a units line in the header; CSV writes values in SI base units with a header row naming units, so it can be re-imported by other tools. - Elements with user overrides (MEP-CALC-002) are flagged in an Overridden column.

    Data (IFC mapping). None in the model; the output is a file. Presets are RXD document mep_settings.

    Commands. pressure_loss_report.export(system_ids[], settings, path, format: "html"|"csv"). settings is {preset_id? | fields{}, sections[], include_critical_path, include_fittings}.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] The CSV report for a system lists every segment and fitting with flow, size, velocity and loss, and the totals match the System Inspector. - [ ] A system with Calculations = Flow Only cannot be ticked, and the dialog states why. - [ ] A segment with an overridden loss is marked in the Overridden column.

    4.7.15 Sizing Calculator palette

    ID: MEP-CALC-005 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §8.5 ("MEP Sizing Calculator palette")

    UI. A dockable palette with: - volumetric flow, taken from the selection or typed in - sizing basis: friction, velocity or aspect ratio, each with a tolerance slider - roughness - constraints: restrict height, width or inner diameter - Show Best Sizes: a sortable table of candidate sizes, with Swap Height/Width - Apply, which resizes the selected duct or pipe

    Open it from View › User Interface › Sizing Calculator or the right-click menu of a selected duct or pipe. It docks with the other palettes of this chapter (§4.0.3).

    Purpose. Size a single duct or pipe by hand, comparing candidate sizes against friction, velocity and aspect-ratio targets, without running system sizing.

    Behaviour & rules. - Inputs. With one duct or pipe selected, the palette reads its flow (calculated or preset), shape, type and roughness. User value lets the user type a flow instead. With nothing or several elements selected, the palette works in calculator mode and Apply is disabled. - Basis and tolerance. Friction target (default 1 Pa/m), velocity target (default 5 m/s for duct, 1.5 m/s for pipe) and, for rectangular and oval duct, aspect ratio (default 1:3 maximum). Each slider sets a ± tolerance from 0 to 50% (default 10%). Several bases can be ticked; a candidate must satisfy all ticked bases. - Candidates come from the Used in Sizing size tables (MEP-SET-001) for the element's shape, or for pipe from the segment's sizes. Friction uses the project's selected equation and fluid properties, as in MEP-CALC-002. - Table columns: size, friction, velocity, aspect ratio, equivalent diameter, and the deviation from each target. Sorting by any column; the row closest to the friction target is pre-selected. Swap Height/Width swaps rectangular candidates in the table. - If no size meets all bases, the table shows the three nearest sizes greyed with a note "No size within tolerance". - Apply resizes the selected element in one undoable transaction, with fittings regenerating. It is refused on size-locked elements ("Element is size-locked"). - Palette inputs are per-user session state; nothing is stored in the model.

    Data (IFC mapping). None, except the size change made by Apply, which is an ordinary geometry and pset update.

    Commands. - sizing_calculator.candidates(flow, basis, tolerance, roughness, constraints) -> sizes[] - pipe.set_size(ids[], diameter): the pipe counterpart of duct.set_size (MEP-DUCT-001). Apply calls one of the two; system sizing (mep.size) is not involved.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] For 1 000 L/s at 1 Pa/m ± 10%, the table lists only sizes whose friction falls in 0.9–1.1 Pa/m, and Apply resizes the selection. - [ ] With friction and aspect ratio (max 1:3) both ticked, no listed rectangular candidate has an aspect ratio above 1:3. - [ ] Apply on a size-locked duct is refused, and the duct keeps its size.

    4.7.16 Risers and rise/drop display

    ID: MEP-DUCT-011 · Priority: P2 (riser tool) / P1 (rise/drop display) · Ref: research/03 §7.2 (system type rise/drop symbols), §8.1, §9.1, §10.7 · web: Specify Rise Drop Symbols for a Piping System; Specifying Rise Drop Symbols for a Duct System

    Purpose. Create vertical duct, pipe, cable tray and conduit runs between levels from an open end, keep them bound to their levels, and show standard rise and drop symbols wherever a run turns up or down in a plan view.

    Workflow. 1. Select a duct, pipe, cable tray or conduit with an open end (or an equipment connector), then choose Systems › Risers › Create Riser. 2. Click the open connector to rise from. Only open connectors of the four routing domains are pickable. 3. In the contextual tab pick the target level and an offset from it (default 0). A target below the start gives a drop. 4. Press Finish. Reviera inserts an elbow from the routing preferences at the start, draws one vertical segment of the same type, size and system, and leaves the top end open.

    Risers can also be drawn by changing the middle elevation mid-run and pressing Apply (MEP-DUCT-001), or by drawing in a section or elevation; those risers are ordinary segments and are not level-bound unless the user binds them (below).

    UI. Contextual tab "Modify | Create Riser": target level drop-down, offset field, Bind top to level check box (on by default), Finish, Cancel. Selected riser segments show a Top Level and Top Offset in Properties.

    Behaviour & rules. - Level binding. A level-bound riser stores its top level and offset. When that level's elevation changes, the vertical segment stretches and the open end or connected fitting moves with it. Unbinding keeps the current geometry. - Errors: no elbow row fits the size ("No Elbow in routing preferences for 300 mm"), target equals the start elevation ("Riser length is zero"), or the connector is not vertical-capable (for example a face-based surface connector): the tool refuses and names the reason. Nothing is created. - Rise/drop display. In plan and ceiling plan views, a vertical segment is drawn with a rise symbol when it continues above the cut plane, or a drop symbol when it continues below the view's bottom, using the geometry, not the flow direction. A vertical branch from a tee uses tee up or tee down. - Symbol sets are chosen per system type (MEP-SYS-001) for ducts and pipes, with six slots: two-line rise, two-line drop, single-line rise, single-line drop, single-line tee up, single-line tee down. Cable tray and conduit take them from Electrical Settings (MEP-SET-002); fabrication parts use the system type of their service's system (MEP-FAB-007). - Single-line symbols are used at Coarse detail (and Medium for pipe); two-line symbols at the other levels. The symbol size is the rise/drop annotation size in Mechanical or Electrical Settings, scaled with the view. - Symbols are generated graphics: they are not selectable, cannot be deleted one at a time and follow visibility of their category's Rise/Drop subcategory.

    Micro-operation schema and replay (§2.1). riser.pick_connector{element_id, connector_index}, riser.set_target{level_id, offset, bind}, riser.finish, riser.cancel. Replay re-runs the ops in order against the recovered model; a pick whose connector is no longer open ends the replay with the session cancelled.

    Data (IFC mapping). Riser segments are normal IfcDuctSegment, IfcPipeSegment or IfcCableCarrierSegment occurrences with a vertical axis, connected by IfcRelConnectsPorts. Level binding (top level GlobalId, offset) is RXD element data (constraints). Symbol choices are in RXD document mep_settings (system types) and electrical. Symbols are never exported as IFC.

    Commands. mep_run.create_riser(element_id, connector_index, top_level, top_offset?) -> element_ids[] (the elbow and the vertical segment).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] From an open 200 mm pipe end on Level 1, mep_run.create_riser to Level 3 + 300 mm creates one elbow and one vertical pipe whose top is at Level 3 elevation + 300 mm. - [ ] Raising Level 3 by 500 mm lengthens the bound riser by 500 mm, and the run stays connected. - [ ] In a Level 1 plan, the riser shows the system type's single-line rise symbol at Coarse and the two-line rise symbol at Fine; in a Level 3 plan cut below its top it shows nothing extra, and in a plan above it shows a drop symbol. - [ ] A riser requested where no elbow row fits is refused, and no elements are created.

    4.7.17 Mechanical control devices

    ID: MEP-DUCT-012 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §1.4, §8.4 · web: Place Mechanical Control Device

    Purpose. Place thermostats, sensors (temperature, CO₂, humidity, occupancy, pressure) and humidistats, and relate each device to the equipment, terminal or system-zone it controls.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Systems › Mechanical › Mechanical Control Device and pick a type in the Type Selector. 2. Choose a placement mode on the contextual tab: Place on Vertical Face (default), Place on Face or Place on Work Plane. Set the offset or mounting height in Properties. 3. Optionally keep Tag on Placement on, with tag orientation (horizontal or vertical) and a leader length. 4. Click to place. Spacebar rotates the device by 90° before the click. 5. Optionally choose Assign Controlled Element and pick the equipment, VAV box, damper or system-zone the device controls.

    Behaviour & rules. - A face-hosted device moves with its host face and reports its offset from that face; when the host is deleted the device stays in place, unhosted, with a warning. - A device may carry an electrical connector (Controls or Power) so it can be circuited (MEP-ELEC-002), and a duct connector for duct-mounted sensors. Controls wiring is not modelled. - A device controls zero or more elements. Assigning a controlled element of another discipline is allowed; assigning the device to itself or to another control device is refused. - The space a device sits in is found by its room calculation point, as for lighting fixtures (MEP-ELEC-001). - Control devices are schedulable with their controlled elements and space.

    Data (IFC mapping). Thermostats and controllers are IfcController (PROGRAMMABLE, FLOATING, PROPORTIONAL, MULTIPOSITION, TWOPOSITION) or IfcUnitaryControlElement (THERMOSTAT, HUMIDISTAT); sensors are IfcSensor (TEMPERATURESENSOR, CO2SENSOR, HUMIDITYSENSOR, MOVEMENTSENSOR, PRESSURESENSOR, …), each with its type psets. The control relationship is IfcRelFlowControlElements (the device as RelatedControlElements, the controlled element as RelatingFlowElement). Control of a system-zone is stored as RXD element data (mep_settings).

    Commands. - mech_control_device.place(type_id, point, level, host_face_ref?) -> id - mech_control_device.assign(device_id, controlled_ids[])

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A thermostat placed on a wall at 1 500 mm offset exports as IfcUnitaryControlElement (THERMOSTAT) contained in the storey, hosted to the wall face. - [ ] Assigning the thermostat to a VAV box exports an IfcRelFlowControlElements relating them. - [ ] Deleting the host wall leaves the thermostat in place with a warning.

    4.8 Piping, plumbing and fire protection

    4.8.1 Pipe placement

    ID: MEP-PIPE-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §9.1

    Workflow. Choose Systems › Plumbing & Piping › Pipe (proposed PI) or Pipe Placeholder. Set the diameter, middle elevation and system type, then click points.

    UI. Contextual tab: - Justification - Automatically Connect - Inherit Elevation and Inherit Size - Slope Off / Slope Up / Slope Down and Slope Value - Show Slope Tooltip - Add Vertical or Change Slope, which decide how a sloped pipe connects - Tag on Placement

    Behaviour & rules. - Pipe types use routing preferences with Segment rows, which give the material and schedule per size range. - Fittings are inserted automatically. Vertical pipe is created by changing the elevation and pressing Apply, or by drawing in section or elevation.

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcPipeSegment (RIGIDSEGMENT), typed by IfcPipeSegmentType. - Property sets: Pset_PipeSegmentTypeCommon, Pset_PipeSegmentOccurrence (InteriorRoughnessCoefficient, Gradient = slope) and Qto_PipeSegmentBaseQuantities. - Material from the segment: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage with a circular hollow profile.

    Commands. pipe.create(type_id, start, end, diameter, middle_elevation, level_id, system_type_id?, slope?) -> element_ids[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Drawing a 50 mm copper pipe with an elbow uses the segment and elbow given by the routing preferences for 50 mm. - [ ] A pipe drawn at 1% Slope Down exports Gradient = 0.01.

    4.8.2 Sloped piping and the slope editor

    ID: MEP-PIPE-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §9.1 ("Sloped piping")

    Behaviour & rules. There are four ways to slope pipe: 1. Set a slope while drawing. 2. Use the slope controls on a segment. 3. Use the Slope Editor: 1. Tab-select a section and choose Slope. 2. Pick a value from the allowed slopes list. 3. Set the slope control point. The default is the lowest end. 4. Finish.

    The slope propagates through fittings, and connected branches adjust. 4. Draw at an angle in a section view.

    Allowed values come from Mechanical Settings › Slopes. Fabrication pipework can also be sloped (§4.10).

    Purpose. Give gravity drainage and other sloped pipework a controlled, consistent fall that survives later edits.

    UI. - While drawing: Slope Off / Slope Up / Slope Down and Slope Value on the contextual tab, with an optional slope tooltip that shows the slope and the end elevation at the cursor. - On a selected segment: a slope glyph with an editable value at its midpoint and an arrow that flips the direction of fall. - Slope Editor contextual tab: Slope Value (drop-down of allowed values), Slope Control Point (cycles the arrow glyph between the ends of the selected section), Finish and Cancel.

    Behaviour & rules. - Slope is stored as a ratio (rise ÷ run) and displayed in the project's slope unit (percent by default; ratio or degrees selectable in Project Units). - Propagation. The editor walks the selected section from the control point. Each segment gets the chosen slope; elbows and couplings move with it; tees keep their branches connected by moving the branch's first segment's end and recalculating that segment's slope if it is not in the selection. - If a branch connection cannot be kept (for example the branch is size-locked and level-locked, or would need a slope outside the allowed list), the editor shows the conflict on the canvas and Finish is disabled until the user removes that branch from the section or cancels. - Slopes not in the allowed list cannot be chosen in the editor. A slope typed directly on a segment that is not in the list is accepted with a warning, so imported models stay valid. - Vertical segments (≥ 45° when the warning threshold is crossed, MEP-SET-001) are excluded from propagation and keep their geometry. - Recovery. The editor journals slope.select{element_ids[]}, slope.value{ratio} and slope.control{end_ref} as micro-operations; replay restores the pending edit (conventions §2.1). Finish commits one transaction.

    Data (IFC mapping). Pset_PipeSegmentOccurrence.Gradient on each segment (MEP-PIPE-001). The section's control point is not stored after Finish.

    Commands. mep_run.set_slope(element_ids[], slope, control_point_ref): refused with "Selection is not a single connected section" when the elements do not form one run.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Applying 2% to a 20 m sanitary run with the control point at the downstream end raises the upstream end by 0.4 m, and branch connections remain connected. - [ ] Each segment of the run then exports Gradient = 0.02. - [ ] A slope value not in the allowed list is not offered in the Slope Editor. - [ ] A branch that cannot be kept connected blocks Finish and is highlighted.

    4.8.3 Parallel pipes

    ID: MEP-PIPE-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §9.1 ("Parallel Pipes")

    Purpose. Create banks of pipes that follow an existing run, such as supply and return pairs or several services on a shared rack, in one step.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Systems › Plumbing & Piping › Parallel Pipes. 2. On the contextual tab set Horizontal Number, Horizontal Offset, Vertical Number and Vertical Offset. 3. Hover a pipe: the preview shows the new runs on the side of the cursor (left/right in plan, above/below in section). Tab extends the hover to the whole run. 4. Click to create.

    Behaviour & rules. - Creates copies of an existing run with a horizontal count, vertical count and offsets. Tab selects the whole run. - Not allowed on runs that contain tees, crosses or valves. The refusal names the element that blocks it. - Counts include the original: a horizontal number of 3 adds two runs. Limits: 1–20 per direction; offsets must be at least the pipe's outer diameter plus insulation thickness, otherwise the command is refused ("Offset smaller than pipe outside size"). - Offsets are measured centre to centre. At bends, each new run is offset so it stays parallel; its elbows are chosen by routing preferences for the same size, so inner runs get tighter centre-line radii when the fitting allows, and the result is concentric. - New runs copy type, size, system type, slope and insulation, but get new system membership: each copy joins the original's system only if it is connected to equipment; otherwise it is left unassigned and reported. - Open ends are left open; the tool does not connect copies to equipment. - Parallel pipes are independent elements after creation; no link to the original is kept.

    Data (IFC mapping). Ordinary IfcPipeSegment and IfcPipeFitting elements (MEP-PIPE-001, MEP-PIPE-004).

    Commands. pipe.create_parallel(run_element_ids[], h_count, v_count, h_offset, v_offset) -> element_ids[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Parallel pipes of 3 × 1 at 150 mm on an L-shaped run produce three concentric L-runs with correct elbows. - [ ] A run containing a gate valve is refused, and the message names the valve. - [ ] An offset of 40 mm on a 50 mm pipe is refused. - [ ] Copies of a 1% sloped run have the same 1% slope.

    4.8.4 Pipe fittings, accessories, flanges, caps and flex

    ID: MEP-PIPE-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §9.1

    Purpose. Place and edit the parts that complete a pipe run: fittings, inline accessories, flanges, caps, insulation and flexible connections.

    Workflow. 1. Pipe Fitting (PF) or Pipe Accessory (PA): pick a type, hover a pipe end or centreline (in plan, section or elevation), click to place. 2. Flex Pipe (FP): click a start connector or point, intermediate points, and an end connector. 3. Cap Open Ends: select pipes and choose the command from the contextual tab or context menu.

    Behaviour & rules. - Pipe fittings (proposed PF) have size, flip, rotate and "+/−" controls, and Change Tee to Cross. - Pipe accessories (proposed PA): valves, strainers and meters, inserted by clicking on a pipe centreline. Valves can be placed in section or elevation. - Flanges are added automatically per routing preferences (union role), or manually. - Caps come from Cap Open Ends. - Insulation works as for ducts. - Flex pipe (proposed FP): spline with vertices. - Fitting placement. A fitting placed on a pipe end connects and takes the pipe's size. Placed along a pipe, a tee or cross splits the pipe; elbows and transitions can only go on ends ("Elbows must be placed at an open end"). A fitting placed in free space keeps its family's default size and is unconnected. - Accessory sizing. The accessory adopts the pipe's nominal size when its family links size to its connectors; a fixed-size accessory on a different pipe size gets transitions from routing preferences or is refused if none fits. - Flanges and unions. When the accessory's connection type (for example flanged) differs from the pipe segment's, the union-role row of the routing preferences supplies a matching flange or adapter on each side. Manually placed flanges replace the automatic ones and are not removed by Reapply Type. - Caps take the end's size and the cap row of the routing preferences; an end with no matching cap row is reported and left open. - Flex pipe uses the same spline rules, recovery micro-operations (flex.pick, flex.set) and length quantity as flex duct (MEP-DUCT-005). - Valve orientation (handle direction) can be rotated in 90° steps with Spacebar before placement and with the rotate control afterwards.

    Data (IFC mapping).

    Item IFC
    Fitting IfcPipeFitting (BEND, JUNCTION, TRANSITION, CONNECTOR, OBSTRUCTION, …)
    Valve IfcValve (ISOLATING, CHECK, GATE, GLOBE, …)
    Meter IfcFlowMeter
    Strainer IfcFilter (STRAINER)
    Flex pipe IfcPipeSegment (FLEXIBLESEGMENT)
    Insulation IfcCovering (INSULATION)

    Commands. - pipe_fitting.place(type_id, host_pipe_id | point, params) -> id (params: size?, rotation?, end_ref?) - pipe_accessory.place(type_id, pipe_id, point) -> id - mep_fitting.tee_to_cross(id) - flex_pipe.create(type_id, points[], start_port?, end_port?) -> id - Caps use duct.cap_open_ends' pipe counterpart pipe.cap_open_ends(ids[]); fitting controls use mep_fitting.* (MEP-DUCT-003); insulation uses mep_insulation.* (MEP-DUCT-004).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Inserting a gate valve into a 65 mm pipe splits the pipe and adds flanges from the union role on both sides. - [ ] Placing an elbow on the middle of a pipe is refused with a message. - [ ] Cap Open Ends on a run with three open ends adds three caps of matching size. - [ ] Change Tee to Cross on a tee adds a fourth open leg of the run size.

    4.8.5 Pipe sizing and fixture units

    ID: MEP-PIPE-005 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §9.1 ("Pipe sizing")

    Behaviour & rules. - Pipe sizing uses MEP-CALC-001 with the Friction and Velocity methods. It is not used for sanitary systems. - Domestic water flow can come from fixture units, converted to flow by a selectable method. Reviera's built-in method uses the probabilistic fixture-unit curves from public-domain sources, such as the original U.S. government reports on fixture-unit theory. Users can load their own tables for local codes. - Velocity limits can depend on annual operating hours, to control noise and erosion. - Pressure drop uses the Colebrook or Haaland equation.

    Purpose. Size domestic water and hydronic pipework from its flow, where domestic flow is derived from fixture units rather than summed directly.

    Behaviour & rules (detail). - Flow source. Fixture connectors carry fixture units (MEP-CONN-001). For domestic cold and hot water systems, each segment's design flow is the conversion of the sum of downstream fixture units, not the sum of fixture flows, because simultaneous use is probabilistic. Hydronic systems use summed connector flows. - Separate curves apply to systems dominated by flush tanks and by flush valves; the method picks the curve from a per-fixture flush valve flag. If a system mixes both, the flush-valve curve is used and a note is written to the sizing report. - Fixture-unit table format. A user table is a CSV with columns fixture_units, flow_tank, flow_valve in ascending order; flow is interpolated linearly between rows. Import validates monotonic rows and refuses others with the line number. The source and edition are stored with the table so the report can name them. - Velocity by operating hours. An optional table of hours_per_year, max_velocity (per material) caps velocity; the default table is empty, which means only the user's velocity target applies. - Fluids. Density and viscosity come from the system type's fluid and temperature (MEP-SET-001). A fluid temperature outside the fluid table is refused with "Temperature outside fluid table range". - Report. Sizing writes a report listing each segment's fixture units, design flow, chosen size, velocity and friction, and the conversion method used.

    Data (IFC mapping). Sizes are ordinary geometry and Pset_PipeSegmentTypeCommon/occurrence updates. Fixture units on sanitary terminals go to the terminal's type psets where defined, and otherwise RXD element data (mep_settings). The selected method and user tables are RXD document mep_settings.

    Commands. - fixture_unit_method.set(method_id | table_path) - mep.size(...) (shared with MEP-CALC-001)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] For a given fixture-unit total, the built-in method returns the documented flow within 2%. - [ ] Colebrook and Haaland agree within 2% for turbulent flow in 50 mm steel pipe. - [ ] A segment downstream of fixtures totalling 40 fixture units is sized for the converted flow of 40 units, not the sum of the fixtures' individual flows. - [ ] Importing a fixture-unit CSV with a non-ascending row is refused and the message names the line.

    4.8.6 Plumbing fixtures, equipment and sanitary workflow

    ID: MEP-PIPE-006 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §9.2

    Behaviour & rules. - Plumbing Fixture (proposed PX) is usually hosted, with Place on Vertical Face, Place on Face or Place on Work Plane. Spacebar rotates. - Plumbing Equipment (water heaters, pumps) is placed like mechanical equipment. - Sanitary workflow: 1. Select fixtures and use Create Systems › Piping, choosing Sanitary or another default (Domestic Cold Water, Domestic Hot Water, Other). 2. Optionally tile views (proposed WT). 3. Run Generate Layout with slope settings. 4. Add vents, traps and connections between levels by hand. - A plumbing plan view template is supplied (chapter 5).

    Purpose. Place sanitary fixtures and plumbing equipment with working connectors, and take them from placement to connected sanitary and domestic water systems.

    UI. Systems › Plumbing & Piping › Plumbing Fixture opens "Modify | Place Plumbing Fixture" with the placement buttons Place on Vertical Face, Place on Face and Place on Work Plane, Tag on Placement, and the elevation/offset in Properties. Tiled views (WT) are a window command (chapter 1).

    Behaviour & rules. - Hosting. A face-hosted fixture moves with its host face, including faces of linked models (it keeps a reference to the link face and warns if the link face disappears). A work-plane fixture keeps its offset from the plane. If the host is deleted, the fixture stays in place, becomes unhosted, and a warning is raised. - Connectors. Fixtures typically carry sanitary, vent, cold-water and hot-water connectors, each with its classification and fixture units. Creating a system from a selection only uses connectors of the chosen classification; fixtures without such a connector are skipped and listed. - Default systems. If a project has no system type for a needed classification, Reviera creates one named after the classification the first time it is needed. - Sanitary layout. Generate Layout for sanitary systems applies the slope chosen in its settings and runs downhill toward the equipment or stack connector; solutions that would require rising in the flow direction are discarded. - Vents and traps placed by hand join systems through their connectors like any other fitting or accessory. - Plumbing equipment behaves as mechanical equipment (MEP-DUCT-009): Spacebar rotates by 90°, connectors are Calculated by default.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcSanitaryTerminal (WASHHANDBASIN, WCSEAT, SINK, SHOWER, BATH, URINAL, …), IfcWasteTerminal (FLOORTRAP, GULLYTRAP, …) and IfcInterceptor. Water heaters are IfcBoiler (WATER) or IfcTank. Hosting on a face is RXD element data (hosting); the fixture is contained in the storey of its level.

    Commands. - plumbing_fixture.place(type_id, host_face_ref | work_plane, point, rotation) -> id - Plumbing equipment is placed with mech_equipment.place (MEP-DUCT-009); systems are created with system.create (MEP-SYS-002) and layouts with mep_layout.generate (MEP-DUCT-008).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Six basins placed on a wall and combined into a sanitary system appear under one Sanitary node in the System Browser. - [ ] Moving the host wall by 200 mm moves the six basins with it. - [ ] Creating a Domestic Hot Water system from a selection of a basin and a WC skips the WC (no hot-water connector) and lists it. - [ ] A sanitary Generate Layout solution never has a segment that rises in the flow direction.

    4.8.7 Fire protection (sprinklers)

    ID: MEP-PIPE-007 · Priority: P1 (placement) / P2 (hydraulic calculation) · Ref: research/03 §9.3

    Behaviour & rules. - Sprinkler (proposed SK): pendent heads hang below and are piped from above; upright heads are the reverse. Hosting options match plumbing fixtures. - The user chooses heads by temperature rating, response, K-factor and orifice. Reviera does not size or select heads automatically. - The fire-protection classifications are Wet, Dry, Pre-Action and Other. - [Suggestion] (P2) A sprinkler hydraulic-calculation provider (ANA-PLUG-001 kind hydraulic). It would cover Hazen–Williams friction, K-factor head discharge, and demand at the remote area. The reference product does not offer this, and it would fill an open-tool gap. The System Inspector and pressure loss report stay unavailable for fire-protection systems until a provider is installed.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcFireSuppressionTerminal (SPRINKLER), with Pset_FireSuppressionTerminalTypeSprinkler (ResponseTimeIndex, ActivationTemperature, CoverageArea, DischargeFlowRate, KFactor, …).

    Commands. sprinkler.place(type_id, point | host_face_ref, level) -> id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A sprinkler with K = 80 and 68 °C activation exports those values in Pset_FireSuppressionTerminalTypeSprinkler.

    4.8.8 Hydronic network analysis and hydraulic separation

    ID: MEP-PIPE-008 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §9.4 · screenshots/structure_mep/hydronic_network_primary_loop.png

    Behaviour & rules. - When hydronic network analysis is on, closed-loop networks report flow and pressure drop on their pumps. The switch is in Mechanical Settings › Pipe › Calculation. - A valid network needs all of the following: - one pump per loop - a source (boiler or chiller) - pipe segments - terminals in series or parallel - a direct or reverse return - Hydraulic separation (Modify | Pipes › Hydraulic Separation › Add/Remove) splits a network into primary, secondary and tertiary loops at a decoupler such as a close tee or a buffer tank. Each loop's pump reports only its own loop's pressure drop. Primary pumps add up the flows of the loops they serve. - [Suggestion] EPANET (public domain/MIT) could serve as an alternative hydraulic provider for large networks.

    Data (IFC mapping). Results on IfcPump go in Pset_PumpOccurrence and the pump performance psets where they are defined. Separation points are RXD element data (analysis) on the separating fitting.

    Commands. - hydronic.set_enabled(bool) - hydraulic_separation.add(fitting_or_pipe_id) - hydraulic_separation.remove(id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] After a separation is added between a primary chiller loop and a secondary AHU loop, the secondary pump's reported head excludes the chiller's pressure drop.

    4.8.9 Analytical pipe connections

    ID: MEP-PIPE-009 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §9.4 ("Analytical Pipe Connections")

    Behaviour & rules. - Create › Analytical Connections makes logical connections from equipment connectors to pipe curves or open pipe ends, without modelling the physical connection. They are used by the hydronic calculation. - A connection that cannot project perpendicularly onto a pipe attaches to the nearest pipe end. - Design to Fabrication (MEP-FAB-006) refuses selections that contain analytical connections.

    Purpose. Connect equipment to pipe mains for calculation early in design, before the short final connections (valve sets, flex hoses) are modelled.

    Workflow. 1. Select one or more pieces of mechanical equipment (or select pipes first and then pick equipment). 2. Choose Modify | Mechanical Equipment › Create › Analytical Connections. 3. Pick the target pipe for each open equipment connector, or let Reviera choose: each connector is matched to the nearest pipe of the same system classification within a search radius (default 3 m). 4. Review the preview (dashed lines from connector to attachment point) and Finish.

    Behaviour & rules. - Only pipe-domain connectors that are open and whose classification matches the pipe's system can be connected. Mismatches are skipped and listed ("Connector 2: Hydronic Return, pipe is Hydronic Supply"). - The attachment point is the perpendicular projection of the connector onto the pipe centreline; if it falls outside the pipe, the nearest pipe end is used. - An analytical connection carries flow in the hydronic calculation (MEP-PIPE-008) and system membership, but no geometry, no pressure loss of its own (an optional fixed loss can be set as a property), and no quantity. - It is drawn as a dashed annotation-weight line in plan and 3D, controlled by its own subcategory so that it can be hidden for documentation. - Moving the equipment or the pipe updates the attachment point. Deleting either deletes the connection. Replacing it with a physical connection (drawing a pipe from the same connector) deletes the analytical connection automatically. - Check Systems treats an analytical connection as connected; Show Disconnects does not flag the connector. - Recovery. Each pick is journalled as analytical_conn.pick{connector_ref, pipe_id}; replay restores the pending set (conventions §2.1).

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcRelConnectsPorts between the equipment port and a virtual port. The virtual port is an IfcDistributionPort nested in the pipe, with an RXD element data (analysis) flag "analytical", and no RealizingElement. The optional fixed loss is RXD element data (analysis).

    Commands. - analytical_pipe_connection.create(equipment_id, connector_index, pipe_id) -> id - Connections are deleted with element.delete.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A fan-coil connected only through analytical connections contributes its flow to the loop pump. - [ ] A connector whose projection falls beyond the end of the pipe attaches to the nearest pipe end. - [ ] Drawing a physical pipe from the same connector removes the analytical connection. - [ ] A hydronic return connector is not connected to a supply pipe, and the skip is listed.

    4.9 Electrical

    Placing electrical components, cable tray and conduit is P1. Circuiting, panel schedules, demand factors and the electrical analytical model are P2.

    4.9.1 Electrical equipment, devices and lighting fixtures

    ID: MEP-ELEC-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §10.1

    Behaviour & rules. - Electrical Equipment (proposed EE): panelboards, switchboards, transformers and motor control centres. They are wall-hosted or free-standing, with Tag on Placement. - Device split button: electrical fixtures (receptacles), communication, data, fire alarm, lighting (switches), nurse call, security and telephone. Most devices are face-hosted. - Lighting Fixture (proposed LF): usually ceiling- or wall-hosted. - The family's room calculation point decides which space the fixture belongs to, for schedules and lighting calculations. - Photometric web files (IES LM-63, and EULUMDAT as an addition) describe the light distribution. They are used by ANA-LIGHT-001/002 and by rendering.

    Data (IFC mapping).

    Item IFC
    Panelboard, switchboard, MCC IfcElectricDistributionBoard (DISTRIBUTIONBOARD, SWITCHBOARD, MOTORCONTROLCENTRE, CONSUMERUNIT) with Pset_ElectricDistributionBoardTypeCommon / Pset_ElectricDistributionBoardOccurrence
    Transformer IfcTransformer
    Receptacle and outlets IfcOutlet (POWEROUTLET, DATAOUTLET, TELEPHONEOUTLET, COMMUNICATIONSOUTLET, AUDIOVISUALOUTLET)
    Switch IfcSwitchingDevice (TOGGLESWITCH, DIMMERSWITCH, …)
    Fire alarm and security devices IfcAlarm, IfcSensor
    Lighting fixture IfcLightFixture (POINTSOURCE, DIRECTIONSOURCE) with Pset_LightFixtureTypeCommon
    Light source IfcLightSourceGoniometric, which references the photometric file through IfcExternalReference

    Commands. - electrical_equipment.place(type_id, point | host_face_ref, level) -> id - device.place(type_id, host_face_ref | point, level) -> id - lighting_fixture.place(type_id, host_face_ref | point, level) -> id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A lighting fixture whose calculation point lies inside Space 101 is listed under Space 101 even when its body crosses into Space 102. - [ ] A fixture with an IES file exports IfcLightSourceGoniometric that references the file.

    4.9.2 Creating circuits

    ID: MEP-ELEC-002 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.2

    Workflow. 1. Select devices or fixtures. 2. Choose Create Systems › Power, or Data, Telephone, Fire Alarm, Nurse Call, Security, Communication or Controls. 3. If the devices use instance-based distribution, a Circuit Information dialog asks for voltage and poles.

    The circuit is drawn as dashed lines from each device to the panel, or to a home-run arrow. Two in-canvas controls convert the circuit into permanent wiring, arc or chamfered.

    Behaviour & rules. - Every device on a power circuit must share a compatible distribution system (voltage and number of poles). Devices that are not compatible are skipped and listed. - Circuits are logical. Adding wires does not create circuits.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcDistributionCircuit (a subtype of IfcDistributionSystem) with PredefinedType ELECTRICAL, LIGHTING, DATA, COMMUNICATION, SECURITY, TELEPHONE, CONTROL or SIGNAL. Members via IfcRelAssignsToGroup. The panel and the protective device are related through ports (MEP-ELEC-006).

    Commands. circuit.create(kind, element_ids[], voltage?, poles?) -> circuit_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Six 230 V receptacles create one power circuit. A 400 V 3-phase motor in the same selection is skipped and reported. - [ ] The circuit exports as IfcDistributionCircuit with 6 assigned members.

    4.9.3 Circuit editor and panel selection

    ID: MEP-ELEC-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.2 ("Circuit Editor", "Panel connections")

    Purpose. Change the members of an existing circuit and choose the panel (or transformer) that feeds it, without deleting and re-creating the circuit.

    Workflow. 1. Select a circuit (Tab from a device, or pick it in the System Browser) and choose Modify | Electrical Circuits › Edit Circuit. 2. The mode greys out everything except the circuit members, the candidate devices and panels. 3. Toggle Add to Circuit or Remove from Circuit and click devices or fixtures. 4. Choose a panel from the Select Panel drop-down (with a search box) or click a panel in the canvas. 5. Finish commits all changes in one transaction; Cancel discards them.

    Disconnect Panel (outside the mode) removes the panel from the circuit and leaves the members circuited.

    UI. Contextual tab "Edit Circuit": Add to Circuit, Remove from Circuit, Select Panel (searchable list showing panel name, distribution system and free slots), Properties, Finish, Cancel. Members are drawn with the selection colour; candidates that cannot be added are drawn halftone, and hovering one shows the reason.

    Behaviour & rules. - A device can be added only when its connector system type matches the circuit kind (power, data, fire alarm…) and, for power, its voltage and pole count match the circuit's distribution system. Otherwise the click is refused with "Incompatible: <reason>". - A device already on another circuit through the same connector is moved, with a notice naming the old circuit. Devices with several electrical connectors ask which connector to use. - Removing the last member deletes the circuit on Finish, after confirmation. - The panel list offers only panels and transformers whose distribution system is compatible and that have enough free poles for the circuit. Panels in linked models are not offered. - Selecting a panel assigns the circuit to the first free slot that fits its pole count; circuit numbers follow the panel's naming scheme (MEP-ELEC-012). - Disconnect Panel frees the slot; the circuit keeps its members, loses its number and is listed as unassigned in the System Browser. - Micro-operations (§2.1): each add, remove and panel pick in the mode is journalled as {op: "add"|"remove"|"panel", element_id}. Replay after a crash re-applies the list to the circuit's state at mode entry and reopens the mode.

    Data (IFC mapping). Membership: IfcRelAssignsToGroup on the IfcDistributionCircuit. Panel: IfcRelConnectsPorts between the circuit's home-run port and the board's port (MEP-ELEC-006). Slot and pole positions are RXD element data (electrical) on the circuit.

    Commands. - circuit.add(circuit_id, element_ids[]) - circuit.remove(circuit_id, element_ids[]) - circuit.select_panel(circuit_id, panel_id) - circuit.disconnect_panel(circuit_id) - circuit.compatible_panels(circuit_id, search?) -> panels[]

    The edit mode itself runs as a tool session through tool.start, tool.finish and tool.cancel (Chapter 1).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A circuit cannot be assigned to a 120/208 V panel when its devices are 230 V. The search lists only compatible panels. - [ ] Adding a receptacle that is on circuit LP1-3 to circuit LP1-5 moves it, and LP1-3's load drops by the receptacle's load. - [ ] Cancel after three adds and one panel change leaves the circuit exactly as it was. - [ ] After Disconnect Panel the circuit has no number and appears as unassigned, and its members are unchanged.

    4.9.4 Circuit path and length

    ID: MEP-ELEC-004 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.2 ("Circuit path")

    Purpose. Give each circuit a measurable route from the panel to its devices, so that circuit length, voltage drop and cable sizing are based on a realistic distance rather than straight lines.

    Workflow. 1. Select a circuit and choose Modify | Electrical Circuits › Edit Path. The current path is drawn as a heavy dashed polyline with node grips, in plan or in 3D. 2. Pick a path mode on the contextual tab. 3. In Custom mode, drag nodes, add nodes by clicking a segment, delete nodes with Delete, and add risers by setting a node's elevation (a vertical segment is created between two nodes at the same plan position). 4. Set the path offset and click Finish (or Cancel).

    Behaviour & rules. - Path modes: - Farthest Device (default): the orthogonal route from the panel connector to the most distant device; other devices add no length. - All Devices: a daisy-chain through every device, ordered by nearest neighbour from the panel. - Custom: user-edited nodes, including risers (vertical segments). Custom paths do not update when devices move; they are flagged "path may be out of date" in the circuit's warnings until edited or reset. - Default routes are orthogonal (X, then Y, then Z) in the project coordinate system. - Path offset (default from Electrical Settings › General › Circuit Path Offset) lifts or lowers horizontal runs relative to the device connectors, for example to run in a ceiling void. Range ±10 m. - Reset Path (in Custom mode) recomputes the default route for the chosen base mode and discards the nodes. - Switching from Custom to another mode discards the nodes after confirmation. - A circuit without a panel has no path; Edit Path is disabled with the tooltip "Select a panel first". - Circuit length = path length + the runs' allowance for vertical drops at each device. It drives voltage drop and cable sizing (MEP-ELEC-005), which re-run when the length changes. - Micro-operations (§2.1): each node move, insert, delete, riser edit and mode change is journalled as {op, node_index, point?}. Replay re-applies them to the path saved at mode entry.

    Data (IFC mapping). The path (mode, nodes, offset) is RXD element data (electrical) on the circuit. The resulting length is written to a circuit length property in the electrical pset where IFC defines one, and otherwise to RXD. The path is not exported as geometry.

    Commands. - circuit.set_path(circuit_id, mode, nodes?[], offset?) - circuit.reset_path(circuit_id) - circuit.path(circuit_id) -> {mode, nodes[], length}

    The Edit Path mode runs as a tool session (tool.start/tool.finish/tool.cancel, Chapter 1).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Switching from Farthest Device to All Devices increases the reported length by the extra daisy-chain distance, and voltage drop updates. - [ ] Raising a 4-device circuit's offset by 1 m increases the Farthest Device length by 2 m (up and down), and nothing else changes. - [ ] Moving a device on a Custom-path circuit flags the path as possibly out of date; Reset Path clears the flag. - [ ] Adding a riser node 3 m above the previous node adds exactly 3 m to the circuit length.

    4.9.5 Circuit properties, cable sizing and voltage drop

    ID: MEP-ELEC-005 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.2 ("Circuit properties", "Wire sizing")

    Behaviour & rules. - Read-only (calculated) properties: - circuit naming index, phase label, way, start slot - circuit number - panel and system type - load classification - apparent load and current per phase - power factor - frame - length - voltage drop - number of elements - Editable properties: load name, rating, connection type (breaker or feed-through lugs), cable type, number of runs, and cable size. - Automatic cable sizing: - Reviera picks the smallest conductor that does both of these: carries the rated current after correction factors, and keeps voltage drop at or below a project limit (default 3%). - The calculation uses the wiring type or cable type tables. - A size the user enters is respected, with a warning if it fails the checks.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Pset_DistributionSystemTypeElectrical (MaximumAllowedVoltageDrop, NumberOfLiveConductors). - Protective device: IfcProtectiveDevice (CIRCUITBREAKER) with Pset_ProtectiveDeviceTypeCircuitBreaker. It is nested as a port-bearing component of the board, or written as a virtual device. The approach is chosen in §4.17 Q6. - Cable: an IfcCableSegment occurrence (or type only) with conductor data. - Calculated values that have no pset home are RXD element data (electrical).

    Commands. - circuit.set(circuit_id, {load_name?, rating?, cable_type?, runs?, cable_size?}) - circuit.size_cable(circuit_id, max_vd_percent?) -> size

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 16 A, 230 V single-phase circuit 40 m long with a 2 kW load gets the smallest conductor in the cable table whose voltage drop is ≤ 3%. The reported drop matches a hand calculation within 0.1 percentage points. - [ ] Editing Rating to 20 A re-runs cable sizing.

    4.9.6 Panel connections, feeders and transformers

    ID: MEP-ELEC-006 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.2 ("Panel connections")

    Purpose. Build the physical distribution hierarchy: switchboards feeding panels, panels feeding sub-panels, and transformers changing voltage between them, so that loads and demand roll up to the service entrance.

    Workflow. 1. Select a child panel (or transformer) and choose Create Systems › Power. A feeder circuit is created from the child's supply connector. 2. Choose Select Panel or Transformer and pick the parent. The search list shows only compatible parents. 3. Optionally set the feeder's connection type to Feed-Through Lugs (the parent must have Feed-Through Lugs turned on in its properties).

    Behaviour & rules. - Feeders: the child then becomes a load on its parent panel. Its connected load is the sum of its own circuits; the demand the parent sees is calculated with demand factors by load classification (MEP-ELEC-010), not by adding the child's demand figures. - Compatibility: the feeder's distribution system must match the parent's (phases, configuration, line-to-line voltage). A transformer bridges two systems: its primary must match the parent and its secondary distribution system (required; the feeder is refused with "Transformer has no secondary distribution system" until it is set) becomes the system for everything downstream. - Feed-through lugs: a feeder on lugs takes no breaker slot on the parent schedule and is listed in a separate Feed-through row. Only one lug feeder per parent is allowed unless the panel type says otherwise. - Loops are refused: a panel cannot feed itself directly or through any chain; the message names the chain. - A distribution element chooses its upstream supply with Select Supply. Changing it moves the feeder and all downstream loads; panel schedules of both old and new parents update. - Deleting a parent panel disconnects the feeder; the child keeps its circuits and reports "No supply". - Roll-up runs incrementally on each transaction and is parallel per branch of the tree.

    Data (IFC mapping). Feeders are IfcDistributionCircuit between the ports of two boards. Ports connect with IfcRelConnectsPorts. Hierarchy: IfcRelAssignsToGroup of the child board into the parent's circuit. Transformers are IfcTransformer with Pset_TransformerTypeCommon (PrimaryVoltage, SecondaryVoltage, MaximumApparentPower). Connection type, lug flag and the secondary distribution system are RXD element data (electrical).

    Commands. - panel.create_feeder(child_panel_id, parent_panel_id, connection: "breaker"|"lugs") -> circuit_id - panel.set_supply(panel_id, source_id) - transformer.set_secondary(transformer_id, distribution_system_id) - panel.hierarchy(root_id?) -> tree

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A sub-panel with 12 kVA of connected lighting load shows that load, with demand applied, on the parent panel's schedule summary. - [ ] A 120/208 V panel cannot be fed directly from a 480 V board, but is accepted when fed through a transformer whose secondary distribution system is 120/208 V. - [ ] Trying to make panel A feed panel B when B already feeds A is refused, and the message names both panels. - [ ] A lug-connected feeder occupies no slot in the parent's schedule.

    4.9.7 Wires

    ID: MEP-ELEC-007 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.2 ("Wiring")

    Purpose. Draw wiring on plans as documentation of how devices are connected, with conductor tick marks and home runs, independent of the logical circuit.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Systems › Electrical › Wire and a kind: arc (proposed EW), spline or chamfered. Pick a wire type in the Type Selector (it carries the wiring type and tick-mark style). 2. Click a device connector (snaps show connector points), then intermediate points, then the next connector. A spline or chamfered wire takes as many intermediate points as needed; an arc wire takes one mid point per span. 3. End on a connector to join two devices, or click in empty space to end with a home-run arrow. Press Esc to finish. 4. Alternatively, on a circuit, click the arc or chamfer control to generate permanent wiring for the whole circuit (MEP-ELEC-002).

    Behaviour & rules. - Adding wires does not create circuits and does not change circuit membership. A wire between devices on different circuits is allowed and flagged in Check Circuits only if the user turns on "wire/circuit mismatch". - Conductors: hot, neutral and ground counts default from the circuit's wiring type (for example 1/1/1 for a single-phase branch). They can be edited per wire; minimum 1 hot, maximum 12 of each. - Tick marks follow Electrical Settings › Wiring: one symbol per conductor kind, an optional slanted line across them, and a show/hide switch. Ticks are drawn at the middle of the longest span. - Home-run arrows show the panel and circuit number as a tag; the arrow count equals the number of circuits carried. - Wire crossings draw a gap of the size set in Wiring settings on the wire drawn later (the lower in draw order). - Wires are view-specific annotation. They can be tagged, have vertex and end grips, and stay attached to connectors when devices move; if a connector is deleted, the end becomes free and a warning is issued. - Micro-operations (§2.1): each click is journalled as {op: "point"|"connector", point | connector_ref}; replay redraws the unfinished wire in the same view.

    Data (IFC mapping). View-specific annotation (chapter 5), stored in views/annotation/<viewId> as wire objects with points, kind, connector references (GlobalId + connector index) and conductor counts. Conductor counts are RXD element data (electrical). Wires are not exported as model elements. Cable runs that must be modelled are created as IfcCableSegment (MEP-ELEC-005).

    Commands. - wire.create(view_id, kind: "arc"|"spline"|"chamfer", points[], connectors[], conductors?: {hot, neutral, ground}) -> id - wire.set_conductors(ids[], {hot?, neutral?, ground?}) - circuit.create_wiring(circuit_id, view_id, kind: "arc"|"chamfer") -> ids[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A wire drawn between two receptacles and ending in empty space shows a home-run arrow and tick marks that match its conductor counts. - [ ] Moving a receptacle drags the attached wire end with it. - [ ] Deleting a wire never changes any circuit's members or load. - [ ] Setting a wire to 2 hot, 1 neutral, 1 ground redraws four tick marks of the configured styles.

    4.9.8 Switch systems

    ID: MEP-ELEC-008 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.3

    Purpose. Record which switch controls which lighting fixtures, for lighting control documentation and switch-ID schedules, separately from the power circuits.

    Workflow. 1. Select lighting fixtures and choose Create Systems › Switch, or right-click a fixture connector and choose Create Switch System. 2. Reviera creates the system and opens Edit Switch System mode. 3. Use Add to System / Remove from System to click further fixtures, and Select Switch to click a lighting switch device. 4. Finish commits; Cancel discards.

    Behaviour & rules. - Switch systems are independent of circuits and wiring. Fixtures on one power circuit can belong to different switch systems, and one switch system can span several circuits and panels. - A fixture belongs to at most one switch system. Adding it to another moves it, with a notice naming the old system. - Only lighting fixtures (and devices whose family declares a switchable connector) can be members. Only switching devices of the Lighting device kind can be selected as the switch; other picks are refused with "Not a lighting switch". - A switch system may exist without a switch; it is then reported by Check Circuits as "switch system without switch" (information only). - The Switch ID parameter on fixtures and on the switch is set from the system name (default "$1", "$2"… per level, editable) and is schedulable and taggable. - Deleting the switch keeps the system and clears its switch. Deleting the last fixture deletes the system. - Micro-operations (§2.1): each add, remove and switch pick is journalled as {op, element_id}; replay re-opens the mode with the same state.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcDistributionSystem (LIGHTING, ObjectType "SwitchSystem"). Members via IfcRelAssignsToGroup. The controlling switch is related with IfcRelFlowControlElements where it applies, and otherwise recorded in RXD element data (electrical). The Switch ID is written to the system's Name and to each member's RXD.

    Commands. - switch_system.create(fixture_ids[], switch_id?) -> id - switch_system.select_switch(id, switch_id) - switch_system.add(id, fixture_ids[]) - switch_system.remove(id, fixture_ids[])

    The edit mode runs as a tool session (tool.start/tool.finish/tool.cancel, Chapter 1).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Two switch systems can contain fixtures that are on the same power circuit. - [ ] Adding a fixture that belongs to switch system $1 to $2 removes it from $1. - [ ] Selecting a receptacle as the switch is refused. - [ ] A schedule of lighting fixtures shows each fixture's Switch ID.

    4.9.9 Load classifications

    ID: MEP-ELEC-009 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.4

    Purpose. Group electrical loads by kind, so that panel schedules can summarise them and apply the right demand factor to each group.

    UI. Manage › MEP Settings › Load Classifications (mep_settings.show(kind: "load_classification")). A two-pane dialog: the list of classifications on the left (New, Duplicate, Rename, Delete), and on the right the selected classification's demand factor (drop-down, with a button that opens the Demand Factors dialog, MEP-ELEC-010), an optional space load flag, and an Other loads note. The dialog validates on OK.

    Behaviour & rules. - Defaults are Lighting, Power, HVAC, Motor and Other. Users can add their own, up to 256 per project. Names are unique (case-insensitive) and 1–64 characters. - Each classification refers to a demand factor definition. A new classification defaults to a constant 100% demand factor. - Classifications are assigned to electrical connectors in the family editor or on placed elements. A sub-classification (free text) can be added for finer grouping in schedules. Shared parameters for connector load classification can be created so the value can be scheduled. - Space load flag: when Load Calculations › run for spaces is on (MEP-SET-002), classifications with this flag contribute to space electrical load densities (for example lighting and power loads used by ANA-HCL-001). - Deleting a classification that connectors use asks for a replacement; Other is proposed. The five defaults can be renamed but not deleted. - Loads with no classification count as Other. - Changing a classification's demand factor re-runs panel roll-up (MEP-ELEC-006) in the background.

    Data (IFC mapping). RXD document electrical (definitions: id, name, demand factor id, space flag). On ports and devices, the classification name is also written to the element's electrical pset where one exists, for example Pset_ElectricalDeviceCommon and Pset_OutletTypeCommon.

    Commands. - load_classification.create(name, demand_factor_id) -> id - load_classification.set(id, {name?, demand_factor_id?, space_load?}) - load_classification.delete(id, replace_with) - connector.set(element_id, index, {load_classification})

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing a classification's demand factor changes every panel schedule summary row that uses it. - [ ] Deleting "Kitchen Equipment" while 12 connectors use it asks for a replacement, and afterwards all 12 show the replacement. - [ ] Deleting the default Lighting classification is refused. - [ ] Creating a second classification named "hvac" is refused as a duplicate.

    4.9.10 Demand factors

    ID: MEP-ELEC-010 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.4

    Behaviour & rules. Calculation methods:

    Method Variant Example
    Constant — 80%
    By quantity Whole total at one percentage, picked by count range 1–2 items: 100%; 3–10 items: 65%
    By quantity Incremental per range —
    By load Whole total at one percentage —
    By load Incremental per load range First 10 kVA at 100%, remainder at 50%
    • An optional largest-motor rule weights motors in descending order with configurable percentages, for example 125%, 100%, 75% and 50%.
    • Demand factors are applied when loads roll up to panels and feeders.

    Data (IFC mapping). RXD document electrical. Panels also write their total demand load to Pset_ElectricDistributionBoardOccurrence where the schema defines it.

    Commands. - demand_factor.create(name, method, ranges[], incremental?: bool) -> id - demand_factor.evaluate(id, loads[]) -> demand

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Incremental by load, with the first 10 kVA at 100% and the rest at 50%, gives 17.5 kVA for 25 kVA connected. - [ ] Constant 80% gives 8 kVA for 10 kVA connected.

    4.9.11 Circuit naming

    ID: MEP-ELEC-012 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.5

    Purpose. Generate circuit names (the "circuit number" shown on tags and panel schedules) from rules, so that projects can follow local conventions such as "1, 3, 5", "L1-3" or "DB2/7".
