    UI. Electrical Settings › Circuit Naming lists the schemes, with the project default marked. New/Edit opens the scheme editor: - a list of available parts: panel name, circuit naming index, phase label, way, start slot, and any text or number parameter of circuits or panels (including shared parameters); - the ordered list of chosen parts, each with its own prefix, suffix and separator; - a live preview for a sample three-phase and a sample single-phase circuit.

    Behaviour & rules. - The project's default naming scheme is set in Electrical Settings › Circuit Naming. Built-in schemes are Numerical, Prefixed and Panel Name + Number; built-ins can be duplicated but not edited or deleted. - A new scheme is made of parameters (panel name, naming index, phase label, way, start slot, shared parameters…) with a prefix, suffix and separators. A scheme needs at least one part that differs between circuits on one panel (index, way or start slot); otherwise saving is refused with "Names would not be unique". - Multi-pole circuits use the slots they occupy, joined with a comma ("1,3,5") unless the scheme sets First slot only. - Each panel's Circuit Naming is By Project or a named scheme. - Circuit numbers update when circuits move in a panel schedule, when the panel's scheme changes, and on Renumber or Update Names. Locked circuits (MEP-ELEC-015) keep their slot and hence their number. - If a referenced parameter is empty, the part is omitted together with its prefix and suffix, and the circuit is listed in a warning. - Deleting a scheme that panels use switches them to By Project after confirmation. - Names are resolved in the background after each transaction; tags and schedules read the resolved value.

    Data (IFC mapping). Schemes: RXD document electrical. The resolved circuit name is written to IfcDistributionCircuit.Name, and the full description (panel and load name) to LongName.

    Commands. - circuit_naming_scheme.create(name, parts[]) -> id - circuit_naming_scheme.set(id, {name?, parts?[]}) - circuit_naming_scheme.delete(id) - circuit_naming_scheme.preview(parts[], sample?) -> strings[] - panel.set_naming(panel_id, scheme_id | "project")

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] The scheme "{Panel}-{Index}" names circuit 7 on panel LP1 "LP1-7". After it moves to slot 9 it becomes "LP1-9". - [ ] A three-pole circuit in slots 13, 15 and 17 is named "13,15,17" by the Numerical scheme. - [ ] A scheme made only of the panel name cannot be saved. - [ ] Changing the project default updates every panel set to By Project and none of the panels set to a named scheme.

    4.9.12 Panel schedules

    ID: MEP-ELEC-013 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.6 · screenshots/structure_mep/panel_schedule_branch_two_column.png

    Workflow. 1. Set up load classifications, then demand factors, then assign classifications to connectors. 2. Format templates. 3. Create schedules: - Select panels of the same type and choose Create Panel Schedules, using the default template or a chosen one. - For many panels at once, use Analyze › Reports & Schedules › Panel Schedules (proposed PS). 4. Manage circuits on the schedule.

    Panel schedules appear in the Project Browser under Panel Schedules and are placed on sheets like other schedules (chapter 5).

    Behaviour & rules. - Default content: - header: panel, voltage, phases, wires, mains rating, mounting, enclosure, location - circuit table: load name, trip, poles, circuit number, load per phase, total - manufacturer and notes - a loads summary by load classification: connected load, demand factor and estimated demand - Schedules are live views of the circuits, not copies.

    Data (IFC mapping). The schedule view is a chapter 5 view object. Its definition is RXD data (chapter 5), and it references the panel's GlobalId.

    Commands. panel_schedule.create(panel_ids[], template_id?) -> view_ids[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A schedule for a panel with 18 circuits lists them in slot order, with per-phase totals that match the sum of the circuit loads. - [ ] Changing a circuit's load name in the model updates the schedule cell, and editing the cell updates the model.

    4.9.13 Panel schedule templates

    ID: MEP-ELEC-014 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.6 ("Templates")

    Purpose. Define how panel schedules look and what they show, once per project, so that every schedule of a panel kind is formatted the same way and can be re-formatted by switching template.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Manage › Panel Schedule Templates › Manage Templates (panel_schedule_template.manage). 2. On the Manage Templates tab pick a kind (Branch Panel, Data Panel, Switchboard), then select a template and use Duplicate, Rename, Delete, Set as Default or Open (edit). 3. On the Apply Templates tab pick panel schedules in the model and assign a template of the matching kind to them in one step. 4. Editing a template opens it in a schedule-like editor view. Set Template Options chooses sections, slot count and columns; cells are mapped to parameters; Finish Template saves it.

    UI. - Manage Templates dialog. Two tabs. Manage Templates: kind filter, template list with a default marker per kind, buttons as above. Apply Templates: a list of panel schedule views (filterable by panel kind and by current template) and a template picker; only templates of the schedule's kind are offered. - Template editor. Ribbon "Modify Panel Schedule Template": Set Template Options, Set Parameter (map the selected cell to a parameter of the panel, circuit or load summary), Combine Parameters (several parameters with separators in one cell), Edit Font, Borders, Shading, Insert/Delete Row and Column, Merge/Unmerge, Resize, Finish Template and Cancel. - Template Options pages: General Settings (section visibility for header, circuit table, loads summary and footer; total width; slot count, default 42, range 1–168; whether unused slots are shown), Circuit Table (column layout and per-phase load columns), Loads Summary (which load classifications are listed: all, or only those with connected load).

    Behaviour & rules. - Three kinds: - Branch panel: two columns with circuits across, two columns with circuits down, or one column - Data panel: a single circuit column - Switchboard: one row per feeder or distribution circuit - The editor works on these sections: header, circuit table, loads summary and footer. - Cells map to parameters, and formatting and merging are supported. A cell mapped to a parameter that a panel does not have shows blank, not an error. - Defaults are regional: two-column, circuits across, for imperial templates; one column for metric templates. Each kind has exactly one default template; the first template of a kind becomes the default. - Deleting a template used by schedules asks for a replacement template of the same kind; the default template of a kind cannot be deleted until another is set as default. - Template edits update every schedule that uses the template, on Finish Template, in one transaction. Per-schedule formatting overrides (MEP-ELEC-015) are kept unless they refer to removed rows or columns, which are reported. - A slot count smaller than the highest occupied slot of a panel that uses the template is refused, and the message names that panel.

    Data (IFC mapping). RXD document electrical (templates, kind defaults). Schedule-to-template assignment is part of the schedule view's RXD data (chapter 5).

    Commands. - panel_schedule_template.manage() (opens the Manage Templates dialog; no model change by itself) - panel_schedule_template.create(kind, name, options) -> id - panel_schedule_template.edit(id, cell_map, formatting) - panel_schedule_template.apply(template_id, schedule_view_ids[]) - panel_schedule_template.set_default(template_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Switching a schedule from a two-column to a one-column template keeps all circuits and re-lays them out. - [ ] Applying a Data Panel template to a Branch Panel schedule is not offered in Apply Templates, and the command form returns a kind-mismatch error. - [ ] Mapping a header cell to "Mains Rating" and finishing the template shows each panel's mains rating in all 5 schedules that use the template. - [ ] Setting the slot count to 24 on a template used by a panel with a circuit in slot 30 is refused, naming that panel.

    4.9.14 Editing circuits in a panel schedule

    ID: MEP-ELEC-015 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.6 ("Modify Panel Schedule ribbon") · screenshots/structure_mep/panel_schedule_modify_ribbon.png

    UI. Contextual "Modify Panel Schedule" tab: - Move Across and Move Up/Down - Assign Spare, Assign Space and Remove Spare/Space - Lock/Unlock (locked circuits do not move) - Group/Ungroup - Rebalance Loads across phases - Update Names - Change Template and Change Branch Panel - font, borders and shading - insert and delete rows - merge cells

    Workflow. Open a panel schedule view, select one or more circuit cells (or empty slots) and use the contextual tab. Moves can also be made by dragging a circuit row to another slot.

    Behaviour & rules. - Move Across swaps a circuit between the left and right columns of a two-column schedule; Move Up/Down moves it by one slot position on the same side, swapping with the neighbour. A move is refused when the target slots are locked, when a multi-pole circuit would cross the end of the panel, or when its poles would no longer land on distinct phases; the message names the blocking circuit. - Spares are reserved breakers with a rating and a load name (default label from Electrical Settings › Panel Schedules). Spaces are empty slots prepared for future breakers. Both occupy slots, can be locked, and count in totals only if Include Spares in Panel Totals is on. Remove Spare/Space frees the slot. - Lock/Unlock: locked circuits, spares and spaces are not moved by Move, Rebalance or Renumber. - Group/Ungroup: grouped circuits move together and keep their relative order; a group cannot mix sides of a two-column schedule. - Rebalance Loads moves unlocked circuits to reduce the phase imbalance. It uses a greedy assignment by descending load, then local swaps, and never changes a circuit's pole count. It reports the imbalance (maximum deviation from the mean phase load, in VA and %) before and after, and does nothing if it cannot improve it. - Update Names rebuilds load names from the load classification and the space name and number of the first device, for circuits whose load name has not been edited by hand (hand-edited names are kept unless Overwrite edited names is ticked). - Change Template re-lays the schedule with another template of the same kind (MEP-ELEC-014). Change Branch Panel switches the view to another panel of the same template kind. - Formatting (font, borders, shading, insert/delete rows, merge) applies to this schedule only and is stored as overrides of its template; Reset to Template removes them. - Every slot change re-runs circuit naming (MEP-ELEC-012).

    Data (IFC mapping). Slot positions, locks, groups, spares and spaces are RXD element data (electrical) on the panel. Formatting overrides are part of the schedule view's RXD (chapter 5). Spares are not exported as circuits; they are listed in the panel's RXD only.

    Commands. - panel_schedule.move(view_id, circuit_id, to_slot) - panel_schedule.move_across(view_id, circuit_ids[]) - panel_schedule.assign_spare(view_id, slot, rating?) - panel_schedule.assign_space(view_id, slot) - panel_schedule.remove_spare_space(view_id, slots[]) - panel_schedule.lock(view_id, circuit_ids[], bool) - panel_schedule.group(view_id, circuit_ids[], bool) - panel_schedule.rebalance(view_id) -> {before, after} - panel_schedule.update_names(view_id, overwrite_edited?) - panel_schedule.change_template(view_id, template_id) - panel_schedule.change_panel(view_id, panel_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Rebalancing a panel whose phase loads are 12/6/3 kVA, using movable single-pole circuits, reduces the maximum deviation from the mean and leaves locked circuits where they are. - [ ] Moving a 2-pole circuit so that its second pole would fall beyond the last slot is refused. - [ ] With Include Spares in Panel Totals off, a 20 A spare does not change the panel totals. - [ ] Update Names leaves a hand-edited load name unchanged unless Overwrite edited names is ticked.

    4.9.15 Cable tray

    ID: MEP-ELEC-016 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §10.7, §7.3 ("Cable Tray Settings"), §8.3 (fitting controls)

    Purpose. Model cable containment (tray and ladder) for coordination, with automatic and manual fittings, so that routes can be checked for clashes and scheduled by length and size.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Systems › Electrical › Cable Tray (proposed CT) and a type. 2. Set width, height, middle elevation and bend radius on the contextual tab or in Properties; set justification and Automatically Connect as for ducts (MEP-DUCT-001). 3. Click a start point and further points; bends, tees and crosses are inserted where the run turns or meets another tray. Changing the elevation and pressing Apply creates a vertical section (rise or drop, MEP-DUCT-011). 4. To place a fitting by hand, choose Systems › Electrical › Cable Tray Fitting (proposed TF), pick a fitting type and click on a tray end or along a tray.

    UI. On a selected tray: end grips, size text, "+"/"−" upgrade and downgrade on fittings, flip, rotate, and a bend-radius grip on bends. The context menu has Draw Cable Tray, Split and Select (Tab selects the run).

    Behaviour & rules. - Types: ladder, channel, solid bottom and trough, each with fittings (bends, tees and crosses are separate fitting elements chosen by routing preferences, MEP-DUCT-002) or without fittings (bends are drawn as curved portions of the segment itself, with no separate fitting elements; manual fitting placement is refused on these types). - The bend radius defaults to width × the type's bend radius multiplier (default 1.0). A bend radius below half the width is refused. - Manual fittings (cable_tray_fitting.place): placed on an open end, the fitting takes the end's size and elevation and connects; placed along a tray, a tee or cross splits the tray and keeps both parts connected. A transition (reducer) is inserted automatically where a fitting leg and the tray differ in width. - Fitting controls: elbow to tee and tee to cross ("+"), remove an unused leg ("−"), change angle (snaps to the Angles setting), change bend radius, flip and rotate. - Split cuts a straight at a point into two connected segments, with a union fitting if the type defines one. - Tray carries no circuit logic; cables are not modelled inside it in the first release. - Fill ratio is not calculated (open question for a later release).

    Micro-operation schema and replay (§2.1). tray.pick_point{xyz, snap_ref?}, tray.set_param{name, value}, tray.apply_elevation{value}, tray.finish, tray.cancel. Replay re-applies the ops in order and regenerates fittings from the routing preferences current at replay time.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcCableCarrierSegment (CABLETRAYSEGMENT, CABLELADDERSEGMENT or CABLETRUNKINGSEGMENT) with Pset_CableCarrierSegmentTypeCableTraySegment (or the ladder or trunking variant) and Qto_CableCarrierSegmentBaseQuantities. Fittings are IfcCableCarrierFitting (BEND, TEE, CROSS, REDUCER), typed by IfcCableCarrierFittingType, with nested IfcDistributionPorts (CABLECARRIER). A curved segment of a type without fittings is one IfcCableCarrierSegment with a swept body along a composite curve. Justification and bend-radius multiplier are RXD element data (constraints).

    Commands. - cable_tray.create(type_id, start, end, width, height, elevation, level) -> element_ids[] - cable_tray.split(id, point) -> ids[] - cable_tray_fitting.place(type_id, host_id?, point?, params) -> id (host_id is a tray or an open end's element; params holds angle, leg sizes and bend radius) - The shared fitting controls mep_fitting.upgrade, mep_fitting.downgrade, mep_fitting.flip and mep_fitting.rotate (MEP-DUCT-003) also apply to tray fittings.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A ladder tray drawn around a corner gets a bend whose radius is width × the type multiplier. - [ ] Placing a tee fitting along a 300 mm tray splits it into two segments, and all three elements are connected. - [ ] cable_tray_fitting.place on a type without fittings is refused with a message naming the type. - [ ] "+" on a bend whose run continues straight turns it into a tee with an open third leg.

    4.9.16 Conduit and parallel conduits

    ID: MEP-ELEC-017 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §10.7, §7.3 ("Conduit Settings")

    Workflow. Choose Systems › Electrical › Conduit (proposed CN), pick a type and a diameter from the active standard, set the elevation, then click points as for cable tray (MEP-ELEC-016). To add a fitting by hand, choose Conduit Fitting (proposed NF) and click on a conduit end or along a conduit.

    Behaviour & rules. - Conduit has types with or without fittings. Parameters: diameter, offset and bend radius. Standards and sizes come from Electrical Settings; only sizes of the type's standard are offered, and a size outside it is refused. - Rise and drop symbols appear automatically on vertical changes (MEP-DUCT-011). - Conduit fittings (conduit_fitting.place): elbows, tees, crosses, couplings (unions), reducers, boxes (pull and junction boxes with up to six connectors) and caps. Placed on an open end, the fitting takes the conduit's diameter and connects; placed along a conduit, a tee, cross, box or union splits it and keeps both parts connected. Manual fittings are refused on types without fittings, which draw bends as curved portions of the segment. - The fitting controls of MEP-DUCT-003 ("+", "−", flip, rotate) and change-angle apply to conduit fittings. A box has no "−" control. - The bend radius defaults to the standard's radius for the diameter, or the diameter × the type multiplier where the standard gives none. - Parallel Conduits offers Same Bend Radius or Concentric Bend Radius, plus horizontal and vertical counts and offsets. Concentric bends are only for conduit types without fittings. - Surface connectors let conduit leave equipment anywhere on a face (Connect Conduit to Equipment). Parallel conduits need a run connected through a surface connector or to cable tray.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcCableCarrierSegment (CONDUITSEGMENT) with Pset_CableCarrierSegmentTypeConduitSegment. Fittings are IfcCableCarrierFitting (BEND, TEE, CROSS, REDUCER; couplings and caps as USERDEFINED with ObjectType "COUPLING" or "CAP"), typed by IfcCableCarrierFittingType. Pull and junction boxes are IfcJunctionBox (POWER or DATA) with Pset_JunctionBoxTypeCommon. All carry nested CABLECARRIER ports. The conduit standard name is RXD element data (electrical) on the type. The cables a conduit carries can be related with IfcRelAggregates or IfcRelContainedIn… patterns where modelled; this is optional.

    Commands. - conduit.create(type_id, start, end, diameter, elevation, level) -> element_ids[] - conduit.create_parallel(run_ids[], h_count, v_count, h_offset, v_offset, bend: "same"|"concentric") -> element_ids[] - conduit_fitting.place(type_id, host_id?, point?, params) -> id (params holds angle, diameters per leg and, for boxes, the connector layout)

    The drawing tool uses the micro-operation schema of MEP-ELEC-016 with the conduit. prefix.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Concentric parallel conduits around a 90° bend have bend radii that increase by the offset for each conduit. - [ ] Concentric mode is refused on a conduit type with fittings. - [ ] A junction box placed along a 25 mm conduit splits it, and the box exports as IfcJunctionBox connected to both conduits. - [ ] A 32 mm conduit cannot be drawn with a type whose standard lists only 16, 20 and 25 mm.

    4.9.17 Electrical analytical loads (preliminary design)

    ID: MEP-ELEC-019 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.8

    Purpose. Plan loads before physical devices are placed. This works over linked models or imported plans.

    Behaviour & rules. - Area-based load boundaries: sketched, or derived from rooms or spaces. They can be shown or hidden. - Area-based loads (Electrical Analysis › Area-Based Load › Add Load Area): 1. Pick enclosed regions. 2. Assign an area-based load type: a load classification plus a power density in W/m² or W/ft². 3. True load = density × area. Apparent load = true load ÷ power factor (× quantity). 4. Loads can be divided. - Equipment loads: load classification, voltage, power factor and apparent load. - Load sets group loads. - The Electrical Analytical Load schedule category summarises area and equipment loads, with grouping and totals. - Like the reference product, the first release supports three-phase distribution only for analytical distribution elements.

    Data (IFC mapping). Load areas are IfcSpatialZone (USERDEFINED, ObjectType "ElectricalLoadArea") with a footprint representation, and load values in RXD element data (electrical). Equipment loads are RXD element data on a placeholder IfcSpatialZone or on the space they sit in. See §4.17 Q5.

    Commands. - electrical_load_area.create(boundary | space_ids[], load_type_id) -> id - electrical_load_area.divide(id, line) -> ids[] - equipment_load.create(point | space_id, classification, voltage, pf, apparent_load) -> id - electrical_load_type.create(name, classification, density) -> id - load_set.create(load_ids[]) -> id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 250 m² area with a 12 W/m² lighting load type reports a true load of 3 000 W. With PF 0.9 it reports about 3 333 VA apparent.

    4.9.18 Conceptual distribution system

    ID: MEP-ELEC-020 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.8 ("Conceptual distribution system")

    Behaviour & rules. - In the System Browser's Electrical Analytical Systems view, build a tree of these nodes: - power source (utility or generator) - bus (panelboard or switchboard) - transformer (needs a secondary distribution system) - transfer switch - loads - Children inherit the parent's distribution system, and incompatible children are refused. - Downstream connected phases maps single-phase children onto three-phase parents (an edit dialog per node). - Load totals and demand roll up through the tree.

    Data (IFC mapping). Nodes are geometry-less occurrences: IfcElectricDistributionBoard, IfcTransformer, IfcElectricGenerator and IfcSwitchingDevice (USERDEFINED "TRANSFERSWITCH") with no Representation and RXD element data flag "analytical". The tree is expressed with IfcDistributionCircuit groups. This is an open choice (§4.17 Q5).

    Commands. - electrical_analytical.add_node(kind, parent_id?, distribution_system_id?) -> id - electrical_analytical.set_phases(node_id, mapping) - electrical_analytical.rollup(root_id) -> report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Adding a 230 V single-phase bus under a 400/230 V three-phase bus asks which phase it connects to, and the parent's per-phase load reflects that choice.

    4.9.19 Circuit renumbering

    ID: MEP-ELEC-021 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.5, §10.6 ("Update Names", "Lock/Unlock") · web: Updating Circuit Names on a Panel

    Purpose. Close gaps in a panel's circuit numbering after circuits are deleted, moved or disconnected, without re-entering circuits one by one.

    Workflow. 1. Select a panel (or open its panel schedule) and choose Renumber Circuits (proposed RI) on the Electrical contextual tab or the Modify Panel Schedule tab. 2. A small dialog shows the start number (default 1) and a preview list: old number, new number, load name and phase, with changed rows highlighted by a text marker. 3. OK renumbers; Cancel leaves the panel unchanged.

    Behaviour & rules. - Circuits are moved to consecutive slots from the start number, keeping their current order. A multi-pole circuit keeps its pole count and occupies as many consecutive slots as before. - Locked circuits (MEP-ELEC-015) and spaces stay in their slots; other circuits flow around them. Spares are treated like circuits. - The slot count of the panel cannot be exceeded; if the start number would push a circuit past the last slot, the command is refused and names the first circuit that does not fit. - On a three-phase panel, moving a circuit changes its phase. The dialog shows the phase loads before and after, and warns when the maximum phase imbalance grows by more than 10 percentage points. It does not rebalance; Rebalance Loads is separate. - Circuit names are re-derived from the panel's circuit naming scheme (MEP-ELEC-012), as Update Names does. Load names typed by the user are not changed. - Wires, tags and schedules that show circuit numbers update in the same transaction. Feeders are renumbered like branch circuits. - A panel with no gaps and start number 1 is a no-op and adds no undo step.

    Data (IFC mapping). The new name is written to IfcDistributionCircuit.Name (as in MEP-ELEC-012). Slot and start-slot values are RXD element data (electrical) on each circuit.

    Commands. circuit.renumber(panel_id, start?) (renumbers the panel's circuit indexes and closes gaps).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] On a single-phase panel with circuits in slots 1, 2, 5 and 9, renumbering gives slots 1, 2, 3 and 4, and the scheme "{Panel}-{Index}" renames the last circuit "LP1-4". - [ ] A circuit locked in slot 7 is still in slot 7 after renumbering, and no other circuit is placed in it. - [ ] A 3-pole circuit keeps 3 consecutive slots after renumbering. - [ ] Renumbering with start 40 on a 42-slot panel holding 5 circuits is refused and names the first circuit that does not fit.

    4.10 MEP fabrication (open fabrication content)

    Design stance. The reference product's fabrication tools are driven by a proprietary configuration database and proprietary part files. Reviera does not read or write those formats. Instead it defines the Reviera Open Fabrication Content (ROFC) model. ROFC is a documented, versioned content format that anyone can author, publish and exchange under a licence of their choice. Fabrication models are written to IFC with full geometry, so a model never depends on its content library to be viewed. All features in this section are P2.

    Ref: research/03 §11 · screenshots/structure_mep/mep_fabrication_parts_model.png

    4.10.1 ROFC content model

    ID: MEP-FAB-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §11 ("Concept")

    Purpose. Define open fabrication content that covers what LOD 400 duct, pipe and containment detailing needs.

    Behaviour & rules. An ROFC configuration is a folder or ZIP package with:

    Component Content
    manifest Name, UUID, version, units, SPDX licence (content may use data licences such as CC-BY-4.0 or CC0), authors
    Materials and gauges Material, thickness or gauge tables by size, density for weight
    Specifications Gauge, insulation and connector rules by size range, for example "rectangular low-pressure galvanised"
    Connectors End-connection kinds (slip, flange, grooved, welded, threaded, press) with length allowances and gap rules
    Seams Longitudinal seam kinds and allowances
    Stiffeners and airturns Parametric definitions and placement rules
    Part templates Parametric patterns: straight, radius bend, segmented bend, offset, tee, wye, cross, transition, reducer, cap, tap, damper, valve body, hanger. Each has a dimension schema and a sandboxed Lua generator that produces geometry and connectors.
    Services Name, abbreviation, system classification mapping, default specification, and one or more palettes
    Palettes and buttons A button maps to one or more part templates with size conditions (ranges). Alternatives are shown on the button.
    Profiles Named subsets of services for a project or trade
    Fluids Fluid tables for pipework
    Reports Report and worksheet definitions (MEP-FAB-009)
    • A JSON Schema validates every file. Lua generators run in the restricted sandbox: no io, os or ffi.
    • A project uses one configuration at a time, optionally filtered by a profile. The configuration is identified by UUID and version.
    • Content packs can be local folders or HTTP URLs, for example a Git repository or a BIMserver-hosted package. Reviera caches them and verifies their checksums.
    • In BIMserver mode, a configuration change is a recorded model change. Collaborators are told to get the latest version before editing fabrication parts.

    Data (IFC mapping). RXD document fabrication records the active configuration UUID, version, profile, loaded services and checksums. Part templates are kept as RXD family recipes.

    Commands. - fabrication_config.load(path | url, profile?) -> config_id - fabrication_config.reload() - fabrication_config.validate(path) -> issues[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A configuration with a malformed part template fails validation, and the message names the file and the JSON path. - [ ] A model with fabrication parts opens and displays correctly when its configuration is unavailable. Editing those parts is disabled, with an explanation.

    4.10.2 Fabrication settings

    ID: MEP-FAB-002 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §11 ("Fabrication Settings") · screenshots/structure_mep/fabrication_settings_dialog.png

    Purpose. Choose the project's ROFC configuration and profile, and decide which services and extra parts are loaded, so that the Fabrication Parts palette offers only what the trade needs.

    UI. Systems › Fabrication launcher, the Settings button on the palette, or Manage › MEP Settings › Fabrication Settings (mep_settings.show(kind: "fabrication")). It contains: - configuration and profile pickers, with local and remote sources shown by a text label (not vendor icons); each entry shows name, version, licence and source path or URL - the services list: two columns, Unloaded and Loaded, with Add/Remove buttons, multi-select and a search box; each service shows its abbreviation and part count - additional parts outside services (single part templates that can be placed without a service) - Reload configuration, which re-reads the content from its source - tabs for connection indicators (how open and mismatched ends are drawn: symbol, size, colour token) and fluids (fluid tables from the configuration, read-only, with the option to copy one into Mechanical Settings)

    Behaviour & rules. - Changing the configuration in a model that already has fabrication parts asks whether to keep the parts; kept parts whose templates are missing in the new configuration become "out of step" and can be viewed but not edited (MEP-FAB-001). - Changing the profile filters the services shown; services that parts use stay loaded even if the new profile omits them, with a notice. - Unloading a service that parts in the model use is refused; the message gives the part count and offers Select parts. - Reload configuration compares checksums. Parts whose template changed are marked out of step and listed; Update parts regenerates them in one transaction. - Remote sources that cannot be reached fall back to the local cache, with a warning stating the cache date. - All changes apply on OK, in one undoable transaction.

    Data (IFC mapping). RXD document model/fabrication: configuration UUID and version, profile, loaded service IDs, extra parts, indicator settings and source checksums.

    Commands. - fabrication_settings.set_services(loaded_ids[]) - fabrication_settings.set_profile(profile_id) - fabrication_settings.set_parts(part_template_ids[]) - fabrication_settings.set_indicators(params) - fabrication_part.update_out_of_step(scope?) -> ids[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Unloading a service that parts in the model use is refused, and the dialog lists how many parts use it. - [ ] Switching to a profile without the "Plumbing" service keeps "Plumbing" loaded while 10 parts use it and shows a notice. - [ ] After a template file changes in the source, Reload configuration lists the affected parts as out of step, and Update parts regenerates them while keeping their connections. - [ ] With the remote source offline, the configuration loads from cache and a warning shows the cache date.

    4.10.3 Fabrication Parts palette and part placement

    ID: MEP-FAB-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §11 ("MEP Fabrication Parts palette", "Placement tools")

    UI. - Palette (proposed PB): service and palette drop-downs; part buttons, where an arrow lists alternatives and a tooltip shows the size-condition ranges; Settings; a Multi-Point Routing start button; and a model consistency check (parts out of step with content). - Contextual tab "Modify | Place Fabrication Part": - Edit Part: dimensions; components (connectors, seams, airturns, stiffeners); options such as the segment count for segmented bends. Double-clicking a part also opens it. Only connectors that are not connected can be edited. - Rotate Part: Spacebar. Shift+Space rotates tees and taps about the branch. Ctrl+Space rotates in vertical views. Rectangular parts step by 90° and round parts by 45°. - Toggle Connector (Up arrow) and Insert Part (a tee, valve or damper inline) - Elevation lock and slope (pipework)

    Data (IFC mapping). - Parts are standard MEP entities: IfcDuctSegment, IfcDuctFitting, IfcPipeSegment, IfcPipeFitting, IfcValve, IfcDamper, IfcCableCarrierSegment, … - Each part has full Body geometry, nested ports and a material. - RXD element data (fabrication) holds: service, button, template, template parameters, specification, gauge, connectors, seams, item number, spool, alias and product code. - Standard values are mirrored to psets where they exist: material, gauge as NominalThickness, insulation via IfcCovering, and weight in Qto_*BaseQuantities.GrossWeight.

    Commands. - fabrication_part.place(service_id, button_id, point, size, elevation, rotation?) -> id - fabrication_part.edit(id, dims?, components?, options?) - fabrication_part.insert(host_part_id, button_id, point) -> id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Placing a straight from a "Rect LP Duct" button at 600 × 400 gives the gauge that the specification sets for that size, and exports the matching material and thickness. - [ ] Setting a segmented bend to 5 segments regenerates it with 5 segments and keeps its connections.

    4.10.4 Multi-Point Routing

    ID: MEP-FAB-004 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §11 ("Multi-Point Routing")

    Purpose. Lay out a fabrication run quickly by clicking its path, letting Reviera choose straights, bends and branch fittings from the active service.

    Workflow. 1. Start Multi-Point Routing from the ribbon (Systems › Fabrication), from the palette's start button, or by right-clicking an open connector (Route from here). 2. Set service, size and elevation in Properties (the palette's service is the default). A route started from a connector takes that connector's service, size and elevation. 3. Click points in plan, section or 3D. Each click adds a straight; direction changes add a bend. 4. Change size, elevation or slope between clicks; Reviera inserts a transition or a vertical offset at the current point. 5. Click an open connector to finish onto it, or press Esc / Finish.

    Behaviour & rules. - Parts are chosen per role (straight, bend, tee, transition, offset) from the service's buttons whose size conditions contain the current size. The first matching button in palette order wins; alternatives can be set per role in a pop-up before routing. - Bend angles snap to the angles the service's bend templates support (for example 15°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°); off-angle clicks are snapped and a tooltip shows the snapped angle. - Straights longer than the template's maximum length are split into several straights with the configured connector between them. - Clicking a point on an existing straight of the same service inserts a tee or tap there. - When no button matches a role and size, the route stops at the last valid point and the message names the role and size. - Pipework routes can be sloped with the slope value on the contextual tab; slope is kept across bends. - Micro-operations (§2.1): each click and each property change during routing is journalled as {op: "point"|"set", point?, key?, value?}; replay rebuilds the unfinished route.

    Data (IFC mapping). Each created part is an MEP entity with RXD element data (fabrication) as in MEP-FAB-003. Parts are connected with IfcRelConnectsPorts.

    Commands. fabrication_route.multi_point(service_id, points[], size, elevation, start_connector?) -> element_ids[]

    The interactive mode runs as a tool session (tool.start/tool.finish/tool.cancel, Chapter 1); the command above is its scripted equivalent.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 4-point route makes 3 straights and 2 bends from the active service, all connected. - [ ] A 9 m straight leg with a 3 m maximum template length becomes three straights joined by the service connector. - [ ] Clicking a 50° change of direction with a service that has only 45° and 90° bends snaps to 45°. - [ ] A route started from a 400 mm open connector inherits 400 mm and that connector's elevation.

    4.10.5 Filling gaps

    ID: MEP-FAB-005 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §11 ("Filling gaps")

    Purpose. Close gaps between fabrication runs automatically, using parts from the services involved.

    Workflow. - Trim/Extend: pick the end of one run, then the end or side of another. - Quick Connect: drag a straight's end grip onto a connector. - Route and Fill: pick two open connectors. A dialog lists the candidate solutions with a preview in the canvas; filter them by required or excluded fittings, step through them, and Apply one.

    Behaviour & rules. - Trim/Extend joins two runs using the first solution found: it extends or shortens straights and adds one bend or tee. If no solution exists in at most two parts, it is refused with "No simple solution; use Route and Fill". - Quick Connect drags a straight to a connector, whatever its size, and inserts a transition. It needs the two connectors to be roughly aligned (within 5° and with an offset no larger than the transition template allows). - Route and Fill works between two open connectors in a single plane (the plane both connector axes lie in, within 1 mm). Connectors not in one plane are refused with "Connectors are not coplanar". It offers several solutions (up to 20, ordered by part count, then length), which can be filtered by fitting, and shows connection arrows at both ends. - Parts are taken from the service of the first connector; if the two connectors have different services, the user chooses which. - Exclude Parts from Auto Fill keeps chosen buttons out of these tools; the exclusion list is per project. - Applying a solution is one undoable transaction. The solution list is discarded after Apply or Cancel. - Micro-operations (§2.1): connector picks and the chosen solution index are journalled as {op: "pick"|"choose", connector_ref?, index?}; replay recomputes the solutions and reselects the chosen one.

    Commands. - fabrication_route.trim_extend(conn_a, conn_b) -> element_ids[] - fabrication_route.quick_connect(part_id, target_connector) -> element_ids[] - fabrication_route.route_and_fill(conn_a, conn_b) -> solutions[] - fabrication_route.apply(solution_id) -> element_ids[] - fabrication_autofill.exclude(button_ids[], excluded: bool)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Route and Fill between two offset open ends in one plane returns at least one solution, and applying it leaves no open connectors. - [ ] Route and Fill between two connectors in different planes is refused with the "not coplanar" message. - [ ] After a 45° bend button is excluded from auto fill, no offered solution contains that button. - [ ] Quick Connect from a 300 mm straight to a 400 mm connector inserts one transition and connects both ends.

    4.10.6 Design to Fabrication conversion

    ID: MEP-FAB-006 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §11 ("Design to Fabrication")

    Purpose. Turn a coordinated design-level model (generic ducts and pipes) into fabrication parts without redrawing it.

    Workflow. 1. Select design elements (Tab-select runs, or use a filter) and choose Modify › Fabrication › Design to Fabrication. 2. The dialog shows the mapping table for the selection: one row per design type or fitting part type found, with the target service and button. Unmapped rows are highlighted with a text label "Not mapped". 3. Edit rows or choose Use saved mapping, then Convert. 4. Review the conversion report (converted, skipped, warnings) and use Select skipped to inspect elements left unconverted.

    Behaviour & rules. - Converts generic design elements into fabrication parts: ducts, duct fittings, duct accessories, flex duct, air terminals, pipes, pipe fittings, pipe accessories and flex pipe. - A mapping table says which service and button replaces each design type or fitting part type. It is editable and stored in RXD document model/fabrication. Several named mappings can be saved; one is the project default. - Mapping rows can be qualified by system classification and size range, so that one duct type maps to a low-pressure service below 600 mm and a medium-pressure service above. - Conversion is refused when the selection contains analytical pipe connections; the message names them and offers Remove from selection. - Reviera recommends running Show Disconnects first and converting in small batches. The converter reports which elements it could not map. Batches larger than 2 000 elements ask for confirmation. - Geometry is kept: straights keep their centreline, size and elevation; fittings are replaced by the mapped button's part at the same connector positions. Where the fabrication part's length differs (for example a longer bend), adjacent straights are trimmed or extended. If that is impossible, the element is skipped and listed. - Conversion keeps system membership and GlobalIds where the element kind does not change. Otherwise it records the old GlobalIds for traceability (in RXD element data fabrication, key converted_from). - Tags and dimensions on converted elements are re-hosted to the new parts where the element kept its GlobalId; others are listed in the report. - The whole conversion is one undoable transaction and runs in the background with progress (ANA-GEN-001 job model).

    Commands. - fabrication.convert_design(element_ids[], mapping_id?) -> report - fabrication_mapping.set(rules[]) - fabrication_mapping.save(name, rules[], default?: bool) -> mapping_id - fabrication_mapping.preview(element_ids[], mapping_id?) -> rows[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Converting a 20-element duct run with a complete mapping yields 20 fabrication parts in the same system, and the run stays connected. - [ ] A selection with one unmapped fitting type converts everything else, and the report lists the unmapped fitting with Select skipped. - [ ] A selection containing an analytical pipe connection is refused before any change is made. - [ ] A 500 mm round duct converted with size-qualified rows uses the service of the row whose size range contains 500 mm.

    4.10.7 Fabrication editing tools

    ID: MEP-FAB-007 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §11 ("Editing")

    Purpose. Edit placed fabrication parts in bulk while keeping runs connected and consistent with their service.

    UI. Contextual tab "Modify | Fabrication Parts": Change Service, Change Size, Show Service, Edit Part (MEP-FAB-003), Spool (Create, Add, Remove), Slope, and the in-canvas length grip on straights.

    Behaviour & rules. - Change Service re-maps the selected parts to the equivalent buttons (same role and size condition) in another service. Parts with no equivalent are left unchanged and listed. Connections are kept; mismatched end connectors get a connection indicator. - Change Size, with an option to resize connected parts: without it, Reviera inserts transitions at the selection boundary; with it, the size change propagates through connected fittings and straights until a transition, a branch or equipment is met. Branch take-offs keep their branch size. - Modify length of a straight by grip or by typing; the length is limited by the template's minimum and maximum, and connected parts move with the free end only if they are not connected elsewhere, otherwise the edit is refused. - Show Service highlights all parts of the selected part's service in the view until the next selection change. - Rise and drop symbols for fabrication parts follow the system type's rise/drop symbol settings (MEP-SYS-001) and appear in plan for vertical parts, using the display rules of MEP-DUCT-011. - Dampers placed as inline parts can be opened or closed (a template option that changes the displayed blade). - Sloped pipework: the slope editor (MEP-PIPE-002) works on fabrication pipe; bends regenerate to the sloped angle where the template allows it, otherwise the edit is refused naming the part. - Spool assignment groups parts into prefabrication spools. A part belongs to at most one spool; spool names are unique per project and default to "<service abbreviation>-<n>". Spools must be connected sets; adding a disconnected part warns but is allowed.

    Data (IFC mapping). A spool is an IfcElementAssembly (USERDEFINED "SPOOL") aggregating its parts. An IfcPipeSegment with PredefinedType SPOOL is accepted on import. Service, button and spool name are RXD element data (fabrication).

    Commands. - fabrication_part.change_service(ids[], service_id) - fabrication_part.change_size(ids[], size, resize_connected?) - fabrication_part.set_length(id, length) - fabrication_part.show_service(view_id, part_id) - fabrication_spool.create(part_ids[], name) -> id - fabrication_spool.add(spool_id, part_ids[]) - fabrication_spool.remove(spool_id, part_ids[])

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing a main from 400 to 500 mm with resize connected updates the adjacent fittings, and the branch takeoffs stay connected. - [ ] Changing a 400 mm straight to 500 mm without resize connected inserts transitions at both ends. - [ ] Change Service on 30 parts where 2 have no equivalent button converts 28 and lists the 2. - [ ] Adding a part that is already in spool "PL-1" to spool "PL-2" removes it from "PL-1".

    4.10.8 Hangers and supports

    ID: MEP-FAB-008 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §11 ("Hangers")

    Purpose. Model the supports of fabrication runs so that rod lengths, quantities and anchor positions can be scheduled and set out on site.

    Workflow. 1. Choose a hanger button from the palette's hanger group (or Systems › Fabrication › Hanger). 2. Click a straight, a fitting extension or a sloped part to place one hanger; or select a run and choose Place Along Run with a spacing. 3. Adjust rod length, rod diameter and attach to structure in Properties. Press Spacebar before placing to flip the hanger.

    Behaviour & rules. - Hangers are placed on straights, on fitting extensions or on sloped parts. A hanger hosted on a part moves with it and is deleted with it (after a warning listing the hangers). - The hanger size follows the host part's outside size, including insulation when the template says so. - Parameters: rod length, rod diameter and attach to structure, which extends rods to the structure above. Bearer to bearer spacing places hangers along a run. - Attach to structure searches upwards (within 5 m by default) for the nearest face of structural floors, beams, roofs or structural framing, in the host model and in room-bounding links. If nothing is found, the rod keeps its typed length and a warning is issued. Rods re-extend when the structure moves. - Place along run spaces hangers at the given interval from the run start, keeps a minimum distance (template value, default 150 mm) from fittings and joints, and adds one hanger within the allowed end distance of each end. - Spacebar flips a hanger (swaps its rod side for trapeze or offset templates). - Hanger templates are ROFC part templates; they report the anchor point, rod lengths and ancillaries (nuts, washers) for reports (MEP-FAB-009).

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcDiscreteAccessory (USERDEFINED "HANGER") with IfcRelConnectsElements to the supported part and to the structural element. On IFC4X3 export, the specialised support entity is used where the schema offers one (to verify). Rod lengths and template parameters are RXD element data (fabrication); the anchor point is exported as a named representation point.

    Commands. - hanger.place(part_id, position, template_id, attach_to_structure?) -> id - hanger.place_along(run_ids[], spacing, template_id) -> ids[] - hanger.set(ids[], {rod_length?, rod_diameter?, attach_to_structure?, flipped?})

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With attach to structure on, a hanger under a slab gets a rod length equal to the distance from the hanger to the slab soffit. - [ ] Raising the slab by 200 mm lengthens the attached rods by 200 mm. - [ ] Place Along Run at 2 m on a 10 m straight with no fittings places 6 hangers including both ends, none closer than 150 mm to a joint. - [ ] A hanger with nothing structural within 5 m above keeps its typed rod length and raises a warning.

    4.10.9 Fabrication outputs

    ID: MEP-FAB-009 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §11 ("Outputs")

    Purpose. Hand fabrication data to the shop: part lists, ancillaries, cut lists and a machine-readable job, all in open formats.

    Workflow. Select parts or spools (or choose a scope: view, level, service, spool list), then Systems › Fabrication › Export Job, Fabrication Reports or Export Data. Choose the format, path and report definition, then Export.

    Behaviour & rules. - Open job export: fabrication parts, spools and hangers are exported as: - an IFC subset (IFC4, with spools as assemblies), and - an ROFC job file: JSON with parts, template parameters, cut lengths, flat-pattern data where the template provides it, and item numbers. The file names the configuration UUID and version, and is validated against the published ROFC job schema before it is written.

    Annotation is not included. - Exports refuse to run while parts in the scope are out of step with their content (MEP-FAB-002); the message offers Update parts or Export anyway (the latter writes a warning into the job file). - Parts without an item number get one assigned before export (MEP-FAB-010), with a notice. - Fabrication reports use the schedule engine with report definitions taken from the configuration: - item reports (one row per item number, with quantity, size, length, weight) - ancillary reports (fasteners, sealant, gaskets, hanger rods and fixings) aggregated from the templates' ancillary lists - linear nesting of straights into stock lengths A report can be placed as a schedule view on a sheet or written to a file. - Linear nesting uses first-fit decreasing by default, with a saw kerf (default 3 mm) and a minimum reusable offcut (default 300 mm); it reports bars used, parts per bar, offcuts and waste percentage. Parts longer than the stock length are listed as "cannot nest". - Data export as CSV (UTF-8, comma-separated, header row) or JSON, for items, ancillaries or nesting results. - Proprietary job formats are not supported (§4.17).

    Data (IFC mapping). The IFC subset uses the entities of MEP-FAB-003, MEP-FAB-007 and MEP-FAB-008. Report definitions come from the configuration; the last-used export settings are stored in RXD document model/fabrication.

    Commands. - fabrication.export_job(scope, path, format: "ifc"|"rofc-json") - fabrication.report(scope, report_id) -> view_id | file - fabrication.nest_linear(scope, stock_length) -> report - fabrication.export_data(scope, kind: "items"|"ancillaries"|"nesting", path, format: "csv"|"json")

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Linear nesting of twelve 2.3 m straights into 6 m stock produces 6 bars with 2 parts each and reports the offcut. - [ ] A job file exported for 2 spools validates against the ROFC job schema and lists every part with its item number and cut length. - [ ] A 7 m straight nested into 6 m stock is listed as "cannot nest". - [ ] The ancillary report for 10 hangers with two nuts each lists 20 nuts.

    4.10.10 Fabrication parameters

    ID: MEP-FAB-010 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §11 ("Parameters")

    Purpose. Make fabrication data available to schedules, tags, filters and scripts in the same way as any other parameter.

    Behaviour & rules. Every fabrication part exposes these read-only or editable parameters: - service name and abbreviation (read-only; changed with Change Service) - item number (editable; unique per project unless the parts are identical) - spool (read-only; changed with the spool tools) - material and gauge (read-only; from the specification) - insulation type and thickness (editable within the specification's allowed values) - weight, material weight and volume (read-only; computed from geometry and the material density in the configuration) - alias (editable free text) - product code and name (read-only; from the template) - part pattern number (read-only) - handle position (editable where the template has a handle)

    They are schedulable and filterable, can be used in view filters and tags, and are readable and writable from Lua and MCP through the generic parameter commands of Chapter 2 (param.get, param.set). Editing a read-only parameter is refused with "Set by fabrication content".

    • Item numbering: Number Items assigns item numbers to the parts in a scope, in run order from a start part, with a prefix and start value. Identical parts (same template, parameters and size) can share a number when Group identical is on.
    • Weights update in the background when parts change; schedules show a stale marker until done.

    Data (IFC mapping). Values are RXD element data (fabrication). Weight is mirrored to Qto_*BaseQuantities.GrossWeight, material and gauge as described in MEP-FAB-003, alias and item number to IfcElement.Tag (item number) and Description (alias).

    Commands. - fabrication_part.number_items(scope, start_part_id?, prefix?, start?, group_identical?: bool) -> count

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A schedule of fabrication parts grouped by service shows total weight per service, and the totals match the sum of the part weights. - [ ] Number Items with prefix "D-" and start 100 on a 5-part run numbers the parts D-100 to D-104 in run order. - [ ] With Group identical on, two identical straights get the same item number. - [ ] Setting the weight parameter through Lua is refused with "Set by fabrication content".

    4.11 Spaces and system-zones

    4.11.1 Spaces

    ID: MEP-SPACE-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §12.1

    Purpose. MEP volume elements, independent of architectural rooms. They hold load, airflow and lighting data for analysis and exchange. Reviera recommends placing them everywhere, including plenums, shafts, chases and thin "sliver" spaces.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Analyze › Spaces & Zones › Space. 2. Click inside bounded regions, or use Place Spaces Automatically. Automatic placement creates a space in every enclosed region larger than 0.025 m² and numbers them in sequence. 3. Highlight Boundaries shows the bounding elements. 4. Set the upper limit and offset on the contextual tab.

    Behaviour & rules. - Space extents: - up to the level above - up to the roof - up to the ceiling - plenum spaces - complex vertical extents - A space is marked Occupiable when a room exists at its location. - Linked models bound spaces only when the link is set to Room Bounding (chapter 6). - Space Naming copies names and numbers from the rooms in a linked or host model. - Editing: - space separator lines - combine, divide and move - unplace: the space stays in schedules as "Not Placed" until it is deleted - limits set through properties, drag controls or dimensions - Spaces are visible in plans and sections, not in elevations or 3D. Space volumes are shown in 3D only through the energy model.

    Data (IFC mapping). - IfcSpace (PredefinedType SPACE, or INTERNAL/EXTERNAL where known), with ObjectType "MEPSpace" to tell spaces apart from rooms. When a room and a space are in the same place, both are exported as separate IfcSpace objects. - Quantities: Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities (NetFloorArea, NetVolume, Height). - Property sets: Pset_SpaceCommon (IsExternal, ReferencedName), Pset_SpaceThermalRequirements, Pset_SpaceThermalLoad, Pset_SpaceOccupancyRequirements, Pset_SpaceLightingRequirements and Pset_SpaceThermalDesign (supply, return and exhaust airflow). - Space boundaries: IfcRelSpaceBoundary (level 1), and level 2 (IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel) when the energy model is created. - Containment in the storey.

    Commands. - space.place(view_id, point, upper_limit?, offset?) -> id - space.place_auto(level_id) -> ids[] - space_separator.create(view_id, curves[]) -> ids[] - space.unplace(ids[]) - space.name_from_rooms(scope, source_link_id?)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Place Spaces Automatically on a level with 25 enclosed regions creates 25 spaces, and marks occupiable the 20 that are under rooms. - [ ] Space Naming copies "101 Office" from a linked room to the space at the same location. - [ ] Each space exports as an IfcSpace with Qto_SpaceBaseQuantities.NetVolume correct to within 0.5%.

    4.11.2 Space properties and building/space type settings

    ID: MEP-SPACE-002 · Priority: P1 (properties) / P2 (type settings) · Ref: research/03 §12.1 ("Space properties")

    Behaviour & rules. - Space properties: - name and number - area and volume (the volume calculation setting is in chapter 5) - upper limit and offset - occupiable and condition type - space type and building type - people: area per person, sensible and latent heat gain per person - lighting and power loads: density, or actual values from the fixtures and devices in the space - airflow: specified, calculated and actual supply, return and exhaust - return-air plenum flag - ceiling, wall and floor reflectances - lighting calculation workplane height - average estimated illumination (ANA-LIGHT-001) - phase - Building/Space Type Settings (Manage › MEP Settings) define default densities, occupancy and operating schedules per type. Reviera ships open starter values. Schedules use the ANA-EM-002 schedule format. - Colour schemes on spaces show airflow, load or type. Space tags are supplied.

    Data (IFC mapping). The space psets listed in MEP-SPACE-001. Type definitions and schedules: RXD document analysis.

    Commands. - space.set(ids[], params) - space_type.create(name, params) -> id - building_type.create(name, params) -> id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Assigning the type "Office" sets lighting density, occupancy and schedules to the type defaults, and each value can be overridden per space.

    4.11.3 System-zones

    ID: MEP-ZONE-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §12.2 · screenshots/structure_mep/system_zones_plan.png

    Purpose. Graphic regions, sketched per level, that mark the areas served by analytical air systems, water loops and zone equipment. They also cover what HVAC zones used to do.

    Workflow. - System-Zone › By Sketch or By Level. - Add/Edit System-Zone. - Convert: turns legacy zones from imported models into system-zones.

    Behaviour & rules. - When the energy model is created (ANA-EM-003), every analytical space inside or touching a system-zone is assigned to it. - Each system-zone is assigned to a piece of zone equipment or an air system. - The relationships appear in the System Browser's Zones view. - System-zones and analytical spaces must be in the host model, not a link, and in the project phase being analysed. - Heating and cooling set points, humidity limits and outdoor-air rules are system-zone properties. They are kept so that legacy zone workflows can be converted.

    Data (IFC mapping). - The system-zone region is an IfcSpatialZone (THERMAL) with a footprint and body representation. - The grouping of spaces is an IfcZone (ObjectType "SystemZone"), with spaces linked by IfcRelAssignsToGroup. - Zone equipment is related with IfcRelServicesBuildings, or IfcRelAssignsToGroup of the equipment into the zone, plus Pset_ZoneCommon. - Set points are in Pset_SpaceThermalRequirements on each assigned space. - The equipment assignment is also kept as RXD element data (analysis).

    Commands. - system_zone.create(level_id, boundary | "whole_level") -> id - system_zone.assign(zone_id, equipment_or_system_id) - system_zone.convert_legacy(zone_ids[]) -> ids[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] After energy model creation, a system-zone that covers 6 analytical spaces lists those 6 in the System Browser under its zone equipment. - [ ] An imported IFC IfcZone with set points converts into a system-zone whose region envelopes its spaces.

    4.12 Analysis

    The analysis services in this section are P2 unless stated otherwise. They all run through ANA-GEN-001 (background jobs, stale-result flags) and the provider model (§4.0.2). Their results are drawn in views with the shared analysis display styles (ANA-ADS-001).

    4.12.1 Location and weather

    ID: ANA-EM-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §13.1 ("Location")

    Purpose. Give every energy, loads, daylight and solar calculation one site definition and one climate source, without any vendor weather service.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Analyze › Energy › Location. The dialog has two tabs, Location and Weather. 2. Location: type an address (resolved only if a geocoding add-in is installed), pick a city from a bundled list built from an openly licensed gazetteer, or enter latitude, longitude, elevation and time zone directly. This is the same project location as chapter 2. 3. Weather: Import EPW… from a file or a configured URL, or pick a previously imported file. The tab lists the station name, WMO number, distance from the site, period of record and the derived design conditions. 4. Optionally edit the design conditions table: heating dry-bulb (99.6%), cooling dry-bulb and mean coincident wet-bulb (0.4%), daily range, and clearness. Edited values are marked as user overrides.

    Behaviour & rules. - Energy › Location sets the site location (shared with chapter 2's project location) and a weather file. - Supported weather sources are EPW files (an open, widely published format), local or from user-configured URLs. - Design-day data comes from the weather file or from a user-entered design-conditions table. - No proprietary weather service is required. - An EPW file must hold 8 760 hourly records (8 784 in a leap year). A shorter or malformed file is refused, and the message names the first bad line. - A station more than 50 km away or with an elevation difference above 300 m from the site raises a warning, not a refusal. - When the weather file changes, energy, loads, daylight and solar results become stale (ANA-GEN-001). - The imported file is copied into the project's resource folder (or BIMserver extended data in client mode), so the project stays portable.

    Data (IFC mapping). IfcSite RefLatitude, RefLongitude and RefElevation. The weather file reference is an IfcDocumentReference. Design days are RXD document analysis.

    Commands. - energy_location.set(lat, lon, elevation?, weather_file?) - weather.import(path) -> id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Loading an EPW file fills the location and design temperatures, and they are shown in Energy Settings. - [ ] An EPW file truncated at 8 000 records is refused, and the message names the line where it ends. - [ ] Changing the weather file after a heating and cooling loads run marks that run stale. - [ ] A user override of the heating design temperature survives re-import of the same EPW file and is marked as an override.

    4.12.2 Energy settings

    ID: ANA-EM-002 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §13.1 ("Energy Settings", 2027 Energy Model Guide), §12.1

    UI. Energy › Energy Settings, laid out as a step-by-step "Energy Model Guide" panel and an advanced dialog: - Mode: conceptual masses and building elements (default), building elements only, masses only, or rooms/spaces. - Ground plane, project phase. - Analytical space resolution: default 457 mm, range 150 mm to 3 m. Gaps smaller than the value are bridged. Gaps larger than twice the value are never bridged. - Analytical surface resolution. - Perimeter zone depth and division, and core offset. - Advanced: - building type and operating schedule - HVAC system - outdoor air - export category (rooms or spaces) - conceptual constructions - target glazing percentage, sill height, shading, skylights - material thermal properties: schematic types, or detailed element layers - Schedules page: the operating, occupancy, lighting, equipment and HVAC availability schedules used by building and space types (MEP-SPACE-002). Each schedule is a named set of 24-hour profiles (fractions 0–1, or set-point temperatures) for weekday, Saturday, Sunday/holiday and design days, editable in a grid with a line-chart preview. Reviera ships open starter schedules.

    Workflow. 1. Choose Analyze › Energy › Energy Settings (energy_settings.show). The Energy Model Guide panel opens docked on the right with four steps: Location (ANA-EM-001), Model mode and resolution, Constructions and glazing, Create or update the energy model (ANA-EM-003). Each step shows a status (not started, complete, needs attention) and a button that opens the matching page. 2. Advanced… opens the full modal dialog with the pages above. 3. OK commits all changes in one transaction ("Energy Settings"). If an energy model exists, the dialog says which changes will make it stale and offers Update energy model now.

    Behaviour & rules. - Validation: analytical space resolution 150 mm–3 m; surface resolution 50 mm–1 m and not larger than the space resolution; perimeter zone depth 0–15 m; glazing percentage 0–95%; sill height 0–3 m. Out-of-range values are refused on the field with the allowed range shown. - The project phase must exist; the ground plane must be a level. Changing either marks the energy model stale. - Rooms or spaces mode needs at least one placed room or space of the chosen export category; the dialog warns if there is none. - Conceptual constructions pick from an open library of schematic constructions with U-values; detailed element layers use the material thermal assets (DM-MAT-004). - The Energy Model Guide is non-modal and updates its step status live; closing it does not discard settings. - Settings are per project and transferable with Transfer Project Standards.

    Data (IFC mapping). RXD document analysis (energy settings and schedules). Thermal properties of materials use Pset_MaterialThermal (SpecificHeatCapacity, ThermalConductivity) and Pset_MaterialCommon (MassDensity).

    Commands. - energy_settings.show() (opens the Energy Model Guide panel; the Advanced dialog is reached from it) - energy_settings.set(path, value) - energy_settings.get() -> table

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 300 mm gap between two walls is bridged at the default resolution. A 1 000 mm gap is never bridged. - [ ] Entering an analytical space resolution of 100 mm is refused with the range 150 mm–3 m shown. - [ ] Changing the project phase after the energy model was created marks it stale, and the guide shows step 4 as "needs attention". - [ ] Editing a weekday occupancy profile in the Schedules page changes the occupancy schedule used by every space of the type that refers to it.

    4.12.3 Energy model

    ID: ANA-EM-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §13.1 ("Energy (analytical) model") · screenshots/structure_mep/energy_model_analytical_spaces_3d.png

    Purpose. Build the analytical energy model: analytical spaces (air volumes), analytical surfaces (heat-transfer surfaces) and zones.

    Behaviour & rules. - Create Energy Model builds the model from masses, building elements, or both, using the settings above. It also creates the views System-Zone and Analytical Spaces. - Analytical surfaces are classified as exterior wall, roof, slab on grade, underground wall or slab, interior wall, interior floor, window, skylight, door, shading or air. - An existing energy model must be deleted before it is re-created (Delete Energy Model). Reviera also offers Update, which re-creates the model in one transaction and keeps the user's manual reassignments where the analytical spaces still match. - Building the model runs in parallel per level and per space, using OCCT boolean and offset operations.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Analytical spaces are IfcSpace (ObjectType "AnalyticalSpace") in an IfcGroup "EnergyModel". - Analytical surfaces are second-level space boundaries: IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel with PhysicalOrVirtualBoundary and InternalOrExternalBoundary, ConnectionGeometry, and CorrespondingBoundary pairs. - Shading surfaces are IfcShadingDevice (or IfcVirtualElement for air boundaries). - Reviera thus exports a building-energy-model-ready IFC.

    Commands. - energy_model.create(options?) -> job_id - energy_model.delete() - energy_model.update() -> job_id - energy_model.reassign_space(analytical_space_id, system_zone_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] For a two-storey box building with 8 rooms, the energy model has 8 analytical spaces, and every interior wall boundary has a corresponding boundary on the neighbouring space. - [ ] The exported IFC passes the buildingSMART space-boundary validation rules for second-level boundaries.

    4.12.4 gbXML exchange

    ID: ANA-EM-004 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §13.1 ("gbXML")

    Behaviour & rules. - File › Export › gbXML writes the energy model, or rooms/spaces in simple mode. gbXML is an open schema. - Insert › Import › gbXML reads load results computed by third-party tools and writes calculated values onto matching spaces (matched by ID, then by name and number). - Export dialog. Source (Energy model or Rooms/spaces), project phase, a 3D preview with a list of spaces and surfaces, and warnings (unbounded spaces, surfaces with no construction, overlapping spaces). Next writes the file. Export with the energy model as source requires an up-to-date energy model; if it is stale, the dialog offers to update it first. - Content. Campus, building, storeys, spaces (with area, volume, people, lighting and equipment loads from space types), surfaces with their adjacent spaces and openings, constructions and layers with material thermal values, the weather location, and schedules. IDs are derived from the IFC GlobalIds of the source spaces (prefixed with sp- and with $ replaced by -, so they are valid XML IDs), so a round trip can match them. - Export writes the gbXML schema version current at release (recorded in the file); units are SI unless the project uses imperial units. - Import. Only result values are read: design heating and cooling loads, airflows and peak times. Geometry in the file is ignored. Spaces that cannot be matched are listed in the report; no spaces are created. - Imported values are written as calculated results (ANA-GEN-002), tagged with the file name and date, and become stale when the spaces change.

    Data (IFC mapping). Imported loads go to Pset_SpaceThermalLoad and Pset_SpaceThermalDesign on the matched IfcSpace. The import source is an IfcDocumentReference indexed in RXD document analysis.

    Commands. - gbxml.export(path, source: "energy_model"|"spaces") - gbxml.import_loads(path) -> report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An exported file validates against the current gbXML schema. - [ ] Re-importing a file in which the loads were edited updates the calculated heating and cooling loads on the matching spaces. - [ ] A file with one space ID that matches nothing in the model imports the other spaces and lists the unmatched ID in the report. - [ ] Every exported Space element's id maps back to the GlobalId of its source space.

    4.12.5 Analytical HVAC systems

    ID: ANA-SYS-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §13.2 ("Add analytical systems")

    Behaviour & rules. Conceptual HVAC systems are defined in the System Browser's Analytical Systems view, with no physical modelling: - Water loops: - hot water - chilled water (air-cooled or water-cooled chiller, with a condenser loop) - condenser water - VRF - Air systems: heat-recovery exchanger, preheat coil, cooling coil, heating coil and fan, plus a DOAS flag. - Zone equipment: - VAV and CAV boxes - series and parallel fan-powered boxes - four-pipe fan coil - PTAC and PTHP - WSHP - VRF indoor unit - active and passive chilled beams - radiant panel - unit heater and unit ventilator

    Behaviour is One per Space or Group Spaces on Equipment. - Zone equipment is linked to system-zones (MEP-ZONE-001) and to water loops and air systems.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Loops and air systems are IfcDistributionSystem (HEATING, CHILLEDWATER, CONDENSERWATER, REFRIGERATION, VENTILATION, AIRCONDITIONING) with ObjectType "Analytical". - Zone equipment is a geometry-less IfcUnitaryEquipment, IfcAirTerminalBox, IfcSpaceHeater or similar occurrence, with an RXD element data (analysis) flag "analytical". - Component settings (coil types, efficiencies, DOAS) are RXD element data (analysis).

    Commands. - analytical_water_loop.create(kind, params) -> id - analytical_air_system.create(params) -> id - zone_equipment.create(kind, behavior, loop_ids[], air_system_id?) -> id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A chilled-water loop with a water-cooled chiller automatically creates its condenser loop, and both appear in the System Browser.

    4.12.6 Systems analysis (energy simulation)

    ID: ANA-SIM-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §13.2 · screenshots/structure_mep/systems_analysis_loads_report.png

    Workflow. 1. Create the energy model and the analytical systems, then assign the system-zones. 2. Choose Energy › Systems Analysis and pick a workflow: HVAC loads and sizing, or Annual building energy simulation. 3. Give a report name and folder, then Run.

    The job runs in the background with a notification. Spaces that no system serves get an ideal air-load system.

    Behaviour & rules. - [Suggestion] Default provider: EnergyPlus, driven through OpenStudio (both BSD-style, run as external processes). - Reviera translates the energy model, analytical systems, schedules and weather file to an OpenStudio model or EnergyPlus input. It runs the simulation and parses the outputs into a result package. - Workflows are scripts, Lua in Reviera, kept in a user-configurable folder. Users can add measures. - Loads report (HTML/PDF), with unit switching (SI, IP, project units): - zone load summary: peak cooling and heating per zone, with components (sensible instant and delayed, latent, total) - system load summary - design psychrometrics - plan and 3D panes and a system schematic - Annual simulation adds a detailed report: energy end uses, unmet hours, monthly profiles.

    Data (IFC mapping). Result package referenced through IfcDocumentReference. The package index is in RXD document analysis. Peak loads are written back to spaces (Pset_SpaceThermalLoad, Pset_SpaceThermalDesign) and to zone equipment.

    Commands. - systems_analysis.run(workflow_id, report_name, folder, provider_id?) -> job_id - systems_analysis.report(job_id) -> path

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With the EnergyPlus provider installed, running "HVAC loads and sizing" on a sample office model produces a report with zone peak cooling loads, and those loads are written to the spaces. - [ ] Editing the model after the run marks the results stale.

    4.12.7 Heating and cooling loads

    ID: ANA-HCL-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §13.3

    Purpose. A focused design-day loads calculation on the energy model, analytical spaces and system-zones. It is lighter than a full simulation.

    UI. Analyze › Reports & Schedules › Heating & Cooling Loads. The dialog asks whether to update the energy model or reuse it. Options: - building service - infiltration class: Loose, Medium, Tight or None. Defaults are 0.39, 0.19 and 0.10 L/s per m² of exterior surface, user-editable. - report type: Simple, Standard, Detailed or Compact - use load credits (negative loads) - Run Analysis

    Behaviour & rules. - Method: a radiant time series (RTS) calculation provider. It covers: - 24-hour design-day profiles - conduction through opaque elements with sol-air temperature - fenestration solar and conduction gains - the radiant/convective split and radiant time series - people, lighting and equipment gains - infiltration - plenum loads - psychrometrics, set points and humidification - peak hour and month search - [Suggestion] The RTS engine can be a native Rust provider written from the published method description in open literature, or the EnergyPlus provider's sizing run can be used. The project decides which ships by default (§4.17 Q8). - Reports are time-stamped under Reports in the Project Browser. Sections: project summary (location, weather, latitude and longitude, design temperatures), building summary, level and zone summaries, and space details. - Phase rule: system-zones and analytical spaces must match the analysed phase and must be in the host model.

    Data (IFC mapping). Peak values go to Pset_SpaceThermalLoad and Pset_SpaceThermalDesign (CoolingDesignAirflow, HeatingDesignAirflow, TotalSensibleHeatGain, TotalHeatGain, TotalHeatLoss). Reports are documents (IfcDocumentReference) indexed in RXD document analysis.

    Commands. - hc_loads.run(options) -> job_id - hc_loads.reports() -> report_ids[] - hc_loads.open(report_id)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] For a reference single-zone test case with published RTS results, the computed peak sensible cooling load is within 5% of the reference value. - [ ] Changing the infiltration class from Medium to Tight lowers the heating load, and the report states the class used.

    4.12.8 Average estimated illumination (lumen method)

    ID: ANA-LIGHT-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §10.1, §12.1, §15.4

    Behaviour & rules. - Reviera calculates average estimated illumination for each space with the lumen (zonal cavity) method: - room cavity ratio from the space geometry and the workplane height - reflectances from the space properties - coefficient of utilisation from the fixture's photometric data, or from a CU table in the family - light loss factor - fixtures counted by their room calculation point - This is a built-in provider (ANA-PLUG-003). It updates in the background when fixtures or spaces change. - Formula. E = N × Φ × CU × LLF ÷ A, where N is the fixture count, Φ the rated lumens per fixture (from the photometric file or the family's Initial Intensity parameter), and A the space floor area. - Room cavity ratio RCR = 5 × h_rc × (L + W) ÷ (L × W) for rectangles; for any other shape Reviera uses the general form RCR = 2.5 × h_rc × perimeter ÷ area. h_rc is the distance from the workplane (default 0.76 m, from the space's Lighting Calculation Workplane) to the fixture plane (the average fixture height in the space). - CU is interpolated from the fixture's CU table (rows by RCR 0–10, columns by ceiling, wall and floor reflectance).
