If the photometric file has no zonal data and the family has no CU table, the fixture is excluded and listed in the result with reason "no CU data". - LLF defaults to 0.8 and can be set per fixture type (light loss factor parameter) and overridden per space. - Defaults for reflectances when the space has none: ceiling 0.8, wall 0.5, floor 0.2. - Spaces with no fixtures report 0 lx; spaces with zero area or no upper limit are skipped and reported. - The result is compared with the target (Pset_SpaceLightingRequirements.Illuminance) and a Meets target yes/no parameter is set, usable in colour schemes.

    Data (IFC mapping). Pset_SpaceLightingRequirements.Illuminance (the target) and a calculated value in RXD element data (analysis), also exposed as a schedulable parameter.

    Commands. lighting.calc_average(space_ids[] | "all") -> results[]; each result holds space ID, illuminance, RCR, fixture count, excluded fixtures and meets target.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 6 × 5 × 3 m space with 6 fixtures of 3 000 lm each, CU = 0.6 and LLF = 0.8 reports 6 × 3 000 × 0.6 × 0.8 ÷ 30 = 288 lx. - [ ] For the same space with the workplane at 0.76 m and fixtures at 3.0 m, the reported RCR is 5 × 2.24 × 11 ÷ 30 ≈ 4.11. - [ ] Moving one fixture into the next space updates both spaces' values without a manual command, and marks no other space stale. - [ ] A fixture with no CU data is excluded and listed with the reason "no CU data".

    4.12.9 Daylight and electric lighting analysis

    ID: ANA-LIGHT-002 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §13.4 ("Lighting")

    Behaviour & rules. - Daylight & Solar › Lighting opens an analysis panel. Choose: - an analysis type: illuminance at a time, annual climate-based metrics (sDA/ASE) or daylight factor - levels - sensor-grid height and spacing - thresholds

    Then Run. - A model-preparation checklist covers rooms or spaces, material reflectance and transmittance, and glazing. - Results are drawn on grids in views with analysis display styles. - [Suggestion] Provider: Radiance, run as an external process with its permissive licence verified, possibly through an open daylight-simulation wrapper library. Reviera exports geometry, materials (reflectance and transmittance from material appearance and thermal data), sky definitions from the weather file, and luminaires from IES files. - No cloud service or subscription is required.

    Commands. - daylight.run(type, level_ids[], grid: {height, spacing}, thresholds, provider_id?) -> job_id - daylight.show(view_id, job_id, style_id?)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With the Radiance provider installed, a daylight-factor run on a single room with one window produces a grid result shown in a plan view with a legend.

    4.12.10 Solar analysis

    ID: ANA-SOLAR-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §13.4 ("Solar")

    Behaviour & rules. - Daylight & Solar › Solar: - study type: cumulative insolation over a date range, or PV potential - settings: PV panel efficiency, coverage and payback inputs - surfaces: all roof exterior surfaces, all mass faces, or a selection - Update

    Results are managed per view. - [Suggestion] Providers: a Radiance-based irradiance provider, or a built-in sky-patch cumulative method. An open PV-modelling library such as pvlib (BSD-3) could be used for PV yield. - Sun studies (still, single-day, multi-day and lighting) and the sun path display are view features in chapter 5. The solar analysis uses the same sun model. - Inputs. Site location and weather file (ANA-EM-001); the date range (default a full year) and hours (default sunrise to sunset); a grid spacing on each analysed face (default 1 m, range 0.1–10 m); and shading context, which is every model element and visible linked element in the 3D view the study is run from, unless a category is excluded. - Cumulative insolation. Results are kWh/m² per grid point over the period, plus per-face totals (kWh) and averages. The built-in provider splits the sky into patches, takes direct and diffuse irradiance from the weather file, and tests visibility from each grid point to each patch and to the sun positions by ray casting against the shading context. - PV potential. Per face: usable area (face area × coverage, default 80%), annual energy = insolation × usable area × panel efficiency (default 18%) × system derate (default 0.86), installed cost (cost per kW peak) and simple payback (cost ÷ (annual energy × energy price)). All defaults are editable in the settings and stored with the study. - Studies are per view. Each 3D view keeps a list of studies; Update re-runs the active one. Results draw with an analysis display style (ANA-ADS-001), with a legend. Results become stale when the model, the site or the weather file changes. - A face with no sun hours in the period (for example a north face in winter at high latitude) reports 0, not an error. Faces of elements in a link are analysed only if the link is visible. - Export: per-face results to CSV, and the grid values to the result package.

    Data (IFC mapping). The result package (grid points, values, per-face totals, inputs) is stored as a file referenced by IfcDocumentReference and indexed in RXD document analysis. Per-face totals are also schedulable result parameters (ANA-GEN-002) on the analysed elements.

    Commands. - solar.run(study_type, date_range, surfaces: "roofs"|"masses"|face_refs[], pv_settings?) -> job_id - solar.export(job_id, path) (CSV of per-face results)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Cumulative insolation on a south-facing roof face is higher than on a north-facing face of the same pitch for a northern-hemisphere site. - [ ] A roof face fully shaded by a taller neighbouring mass has at least 50% lower insolation than the same face with the mass hidden. - [ ] For a 100 m² face with 1 200 kWh/m² per year, 80% coverage, 18% efficiency and derate 0.86, PV potential reports 14 861 kWh per year (within 0.5%). - [ ] Moving the shading mass marks the study stale until Update completes.

    4.12.11 Analysis display styles (visualisation framework)

    ID: ANA-ADS-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §13.4 ("Analysis Display Styles"), §4.6 · web: Settings Tab for Analysis Display Styles

    UI: the Analysis Display Styles dialog (Manage › Additional Settings › Analysis Display Styles, analysis_style.manage). Left: the list of styles grouped by display kind, with New, Duplicate, Rename and Delete. Right: three tabs and a live preview swatch. - Settings (depends on the kind): - Colored surface: show grid lines, grid line weight (1–16) and colour - Contour: contour line count or interval, line weight, whether bands between lines are filled - Markers with text: marker shape (circle, square, triangle), marker size in sheet units (0.5–20 mm), labels (none, all, or only the points the provider marks as predefined), text type, rounding increment - Diagram: base line, scale (value per sheet mm), outline or filled, labels - Vector: arrow head, arrow line weight, scale, and whether arrow length follows magnitude - Color: gradient (2 or 3 colour stops) or ranges (bands with a colour each); auto range from the data, or fixed minimum and maximum; values outside the range use the end colours or a separate out-of-range colour. Colours come from theme-aware palettes, including colour-blind-safe sequential and diverging palettes; users may also enter colours. - Legend: show or hide, position (corner of the view or free), title, number of steps (2–20), units and decimal places, text type, and whether the provider description is shown.

    Behaviour & rules. - One shared visualisation framework is used by structural results, lighting, solar, airflow and loads overlays, and by Lua add-ins. - Add-ins publish results through the analysis_result.publish command. - A style has one display kind; result sets of a different kind cannot use it, and the view's style picker offers only compatible styles. - Each view has a default analysis display style (a view property); a published result uses the style passed to it, or the view default. - Editing a style redraws every view that uses it. Deleting a style in use asks for a replacement style of the same kind. - Results are view-specific graphics: they are not model elements, are not exported to IFC, and print and export to PDF and images like other view graphics. Reveal Obstacles (ANA-ROUTE-002) and results cannot be shown in the same view. - Hovering a result point shows its value and units in a tooltip.

    Data (IFC mapping). Styles are kept as RXD document analysis. Per-view assignments are part of the view's RXD data (chapter 5). Published values are kept in the result package of their job, not in the view.

    Commands. - analysis_style.manage() (opens the dialog) - analysis_style.create(name, settings) -> id - analysis_result.publish(view_id, element_or_face_refs[], values[], style_id) -> id - analysis_result.clear(view_id, id?)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A Lua script can publish scalar values on a floor's top face and see them in a gradient with a legend. - [ ] Changing a gradient style to five fixed bands updates every view that uses it without re-running the analysis. - [ ] Deleting a style used by two views asks for a replacement of the same kind, and both views then draw with it. - [ ] A Markers with text style with rounding 0.5 shows the value 3.26 as 3.5.

    4.12.12 Path of travel

    ID: ANA-ROUTE-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §13.5 · screenshots/structure_mep/path_of_travel_with_schedule.png

    Workflow. Choose Route Analysis › Path of Travel, then click a start and an end point in a plan view.

    Behaviour & rules. - Reviera computes the shortest path that avoids obstacles inside an analysis zone: a band between a bottom and a top offset from the level. - Obstacles are the elements of non-ignored categories whose geometry intersects the zone. Doors are passable. - Waypoints can be added and removed. Paths can be updated after the model changes, individually or all at once. - Paths are on one level only. Stairs and ramps are not followed in the first release (§4.17 Q9). - Path lines are view-specific elements that can be tagged and scheduled, with length and time (length ÷ walking speed). - Implementation: build a 2D obstacle map from plan-cut geometry, then search a visibility graph or a navigation mesh. An open navigation-mesh library under the zlib licence is a [Suggestion].

    Data (IFC mapping). View-specific annotation (chapter 5) with RXD element data (analysis): start, end, waypoints, length and time. When exported, paths can optionally be IfcAnnotation curves.

    Commands. - path_of_travel.create(view_id, start, end, waypoints?[]) -> id - path_of_travel.update(ids[] | "all_in_view") - path_of_travel.add_waypoint(id, point, index?)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] In a plan with a wall between start and end and one door, the path passes through the door, and its length is within 1% of the true shortest path that keeps the configured clearance. - [ ] A Path of Travel schedule lists length and time, and time = length ÷ walk speed.

    4.12.13 Route analysis settings, obstacles and people-flow tools

    ID: ANA-ROUTE-002 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §13.5

    Behaviour & rules. - Settings: - ignored categories; hidden, demolished and underlay elements are ignored by default, and a nested family needs both its own and its parent's category ignored - analysis-zone offsets - walking speed - clearance - Reveal Obstacles: a view mode that colours the elements counted as obstacles. It is unavailable in views that show analysis results. - Multiple Paths: several simultaneous routes, with a minimum separation. - One-Way Indicator: a family that routing respects. - People Content: occupancy families that block paths (specified in ANA-ROUTE-003). - Spatial Grid: a square or hexagonal filled-region grid over a room. It does not update with the room. - A sample Lua script "Longest Exit Distance" is supplied. It finds the most remote point in each room relative to the exits.

    Data (IFC mapping). RXD document analysis (route settings).

    Commands. - route_settings.set(params) - route.reveal_obstacles(view_id, on: bool) - path_of_travel.create_multiple(view_id, starts[], ends[], min_separation) -> ids[] - one_way_indicator.place(view_id, point, direction) -> id - spatial_grid.create(room_id, kind: "square"|"hex", size) -> id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A one-way indicator that points against the direct route forces the path to take an alternative door. - [ ] Ignoring the Furniture category lets paths pass through furniture.

    4.12.14 Interference check (cross-reference)

    ID: ANA-CLASH-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/03 §13.6

    Behaviour & rules. - The interference check is specified in chapter 6 (Collaboration, linking and coordination), together with BCF export. This chapter adds discipline requirements: - It shall support all categories in this chapter, including detailed steel elements (plates, bolts, welds) and fabrication parts. The reference product excludes these (§4.17). - Insulation and lining coverings are included. - Typical discipline pairs shall be offered as presets: framing–framing, structural–architectural columns, braces–walls and openings, roofs–floors, equipment–floors, ducts–beams, pipes–ducts, and host–links. - A clash provider interface (ANA-PLUG-001 clash) allows external engines. [Suggestion] OCCT-based distance and interference checks in parallel, with a bounding-volume hierarchy broad phase. - Discipline rules this chapter adds to the chapter 6 check: - Connected MEP elements (ports joined by IfcRelConnectsPorts) never clash with each other, and a fitting never clashes with the segments it connects. - A host and its own hosted or embedded elements are not reported: rebar inside its concrete host, welds and bolts in the parts they join, a duct accessory inside its duct, a hanger touching the part it supports. - Analytical elements (analytical members, nodes, analytical segments, energy model surfaces, geometry-less analytical equipment) are never tested. - Placeholders (MEP-DUCT-007) are tested using a swept body of their nominal size, so early coordination works before conversion. - Insulation and lining are tested as separate coverings, so a report can tell "insulation clash" from "duct clash". - An optional clearance per category pair (for example 50 mm between ducts and beams for access) reports near misses as soft clashes. - Presets are stored as named check definitions (RXD document coordination/clash, chapter 6) and can be edited and shared with Transfer Project Standards.

    Commands. See chapter 6 (interference.run, interference.report). The presets above are ordinary check definitions for those commands.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A bolt that intersects a duct is reported as a clash between Structural Fasteners and Ducts. - [ ] An elbow connected to two ducts produces no clash with either duct. - [ ] A rebar set fully inside its wall host produces no clash; the same rebar crossing a pipe does. - [ ] With a 50 mm clearance on Ducts–Structural Framing, a duct 30 mm below a beam is reported as a soft clash and one 80 mm below is not.

    4.12.15 People content for route analysis

    ID: ANA-ROUTE-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §13.5 ("People Flow Toolkit") · web: Revit 2022 – Enhanced Feature – People flow Toolkit

    Purpose. Represent standing, seated or queuing people in a plan so that path-of-travel routing treats them as obstacles, for occupancy, queuing and distancing studies.

    Workflow. 1. In a plan view choose Analyze › Route Analysis › People Content. 2. Pick a type in the Type Selector: Standing person, Seated person, Wheelchair user, Queue line (a row of people at a set spacing) or Group (people on a circle). 3. Click to place; Spacebar rotates by 90° before the click. For a queue line, click a start and an end point; the count follows from the spacing. 4. Update paths (path_of_travel.update) to see their effect, or let auto-update re-route paths in the view.

    Behaviour & rules. - People content is a model family category, People, with a body footprint (default standing 0.6 × 0.5 m, wheelchair 0.8 × 1.3 m), an optional personal-space radius (default 0, editable per type, for example 1.0 m for distancing studies) and a height for 3D display. - Route analysis treats the footprint plus personal-space radius as an obstacle in the analysis zone. Ignoring the People category in Route Analysis Settings (ANA-ROUTE-002) lets paths pass through them. - A path whose start or end lies inside a person's obstacle area is refused with "start point is blocked". - People are hosted on the level of the plan view, not on floors, and are visible in plan and 3D; they are excluded from material takeoffs, area and space calculations and interference checks by default. - People can be counted in schedules (by room or space), which gives a quick occupancy check against the occupant load of the room. - Starter types are authored from scratch and ship under the project's content licence.

    Data (IFC mapping). Exported, if the user enables the People category in the IFC export setup, as IfcFurnishingElement with ObjectType "PeopleContent" and IfcBuildingElementProxy as fallback; off by default. Personal-space radius and kind are RXD element data (analysis).

    Commands. people_content.place(view_id, type_id, point, rotation?) -> id (for a queue line, type_id is a queue type and point is the start; the end and spacing go in the type's instance parameters).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A standing person placed in a 1.2 m wide corridor with a 1.0 m personal-space radius blocks it, and the updated path takes the alternative route. - [ ] Ignoring the People category makes the same path go straight through. - [ ] A schedule of people by room lists 12 for a room holding a 12-person queue line.

    4.12.16 Embodied carbon analysis

    ID: ANA-CARB-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §0 (2027 version map: carbon data on materials), §15.4 · web: ÖKOBAUDAT; ICE Database FAQs; Introducing Forma Carbon Insights; CarboLifeCalc

    Purpose. Estimate the embodied carbon (global warming potential, kg CO₂e) of the model from its material quantities and emission factors taken from EPD data, by life-cycle stage, locally and without a vendor cloud service.

    Workflow. 1. Make sure materials carry carbon assets (DM-MAT-005): either type values in the Material Browser, or use Match materials in the analysis dialog. 2. Choose Analyze › Carbon › Embodied Carbon. The dialog has four steps: 1. Scope: whole model, current phase only (default: new construction, excluding existing and demolished), a selection, or a design option; categories to include; whether linked models count. 2. Data sources: the active emission-factor libraries in priority order. Reviera ships none of the commercial data sets; the user imports open data sets (for example ÖKOBAUDAT in ILCD+EPD format, or an openLCA export) or a CSV in the documented Reviera factor format. Data sets whose licence forbids embedding in software (for example the ICE database's individual licence) can only be used as a user-imported file on that user's machine. 3. Matching: a grid of project materials with match status (from material asset, matched, unmatched). Auto-match proposes factors by material class and name; the user confirms or picks manually. Unmatched materials are reported, not guessed. 4. Stages and options: stages to report (A1–A3 always; optional A4, A5, B1–B5, C1–C4 and module D shown separately), reference study period (default 50 years, for replacement counts in B4), gross floor area for normalisation (default from area plans), and Write results to IFC. 3. Run starts a background job (ANA-GEN-001). A notification links to the results.

    UI: Results. A dockable Carbon Results panel and an exportable report: - totals: kg CO₂e for the scope, per stage, and per m² of gross floor area - by category (walls, floors, structural framing, …) and by material, as sortable tables and bar charts; biogenic carbon and module D listed separately and never netted into the A–C total - by element: a schedulable Embodied carbon A1–A3 parameter and per-stage parameters, so schedules, colour schemes and view filters can show hot spots - a data quality column: factor source, generic or product-specific, EPD validity date (expired EPDs flagged) - Compare: two saved runs side by side (for example two design options), with the difference per category

    Behaviour & rules. - Quantity. For each element and material: volume from the geometry (layer thickness × area for layered types), area for factors declared per m², count for per-piece factors, mass = volume × density (Pset_MaterialCommon.MassDensity) for per-kg factors. A unit mismatch with no conversion path (for example a per-m² factor on a material with no area) excludes that material and reports it. - Calculation. GWP = quantity × factor per stage. B4 (replacement) = (A1–A3 + C1–C4) × replacements, with replacements = ceil(study period ÷ reference service life) − 1. Transport (A4) uses a distance and mode per material when given, otherwise is not reported. - Openings are subtracted; overlapping geometry is counted once per element; elements without materials are listed as no material. - Factors are snapshotted into the run so results stay reproducible after a library update; a library update marks the run stale. - This is a built-in provider (ANA-PLUG-003, family carbon); external LCA tools can register as providers of the same family. - Export: CSV and JSON of per-element and per-category results; HTML report; the run's input quantities in a neutral CSV for third-party LCA tools.

    Data (IFC mapping). When Write results to IFC is on, the factor per functional unit goes to Pset_EnvironmentalImpactIndicators.ClimateChangePerUnit (with FunctionalUnitReference) on the element type, and the element total to Pset_EnvironmentalImpactValues.ClimateChange on the occurrence, as DM-MAT-005 describes. The factor libraries, matching table, options and run index are RXD document analysis; the result package is a file referenced by IfcDocumentReference.

    Commands. - embodied_carbon.run(scope?, options?) -> job_id (scope: "model" | "phase" | element_ids[] | design_option_id; options: stages, libraries, study_period, gfa, write_ifc) - embodied_carbon.import_factors(path, format: "ilcd"|"csv") -> library_id - embodied_carbon.match(material_id, factor_ref) - embodied_carbon.export(job_id, path, format: "csv"|"json"|"html") - embodied_carbon.compare(job_id_a, job_id_b) -> report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 10 m³ concrete wall with density 2 400 kg/m³ and a factor of 0.10 kg CO₂e/kg reports 2 400 kg CO₂e for A1–A3. - [ ] With a study period of 60 years and a reference service life of 25 years, B4 counts 2 replacements. - [ ] A material with no factor is listed as unmatched, and the total states the share of model volume left unmatched. - [ ] Module D and biogenic carbon appear in separate columns and are not subtracted from the A–C total. - [ ] Editing a wall's thickness after a run marks the run stale; re-running changes only that wall's result.

    4.13 P&ID integration

    Design stance. The reference product's P&ID integration depends on a vendor cloud service. Reviera instead reads open P&ID exchange data: the DEXPI XML standard, which is based on ISO 15926 and the Proteus schema. It offers the same guided-modelling and validation workflow, working locally.

    4.13.1 P&ID line list and guided modelling

    ID: MEP-PID-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §14

    Workflow. 1. Choose Systems › P&ID › Line List and open a P&ID exchange file, DEXPI XML or a CSV line list. 2. The palette's top pane previews the diagram. DEXPI graphics are rendered as 2D; for CSV, an optional PDF of the diagram can be loaded. 3. The bottom pane lists pipeline segments, searchable by line number or component. A status glyph shows modelled, partially modelled or not modelled. The glyphs use theme tokens with text labels, so they never rely on colour alone. 4. Double-click a line to list its segments, inline components and from/to equipment. Hovering highlights items in the preview. 5. Model pipes and components in the 3D model, guided by the list. Starting a pipe from the palette sets its system type and size automatically. 6. Map P&ID items to existing model elements.

    Behaviour & rules. Model elements remember their P&ID tag. Re-loading an updated P&ID file keeps the mappings by tag.

    Data (IFC mapping). The P&ID tag is written to IfcElement.Tag, and pipelines to IfcDistributionSystem.Name. The mapping table and the source file reference are RXD document mep_settings (P&ID section). The source file is referenced with IfcDocumentReference.

    Commands. - pid.open(path) -> pid_id - pid.list_lines(pid_id, filter?) -> lines[] - pid.start_pipe(pid_id, line_id, segment_id) -> tool_session - pid.map(pid_item_id, element_ids[])

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Loading a DEXPI sample file lists every piping network segment with its line number, nominal size and from/to equipment. - [ ] Starting a pipe from a 50 mm line sets the pipe diameter to 50 mm and the system type from the service mapping.

    4.13.2 P&ID validation and mapping settings

    ID: MEP-PID-002 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/03 §14 ("Validate", "Mappings")

    Purpose. Check that the 3D piping model agrees with the P&ID, and define how P&ID classes and properties translate into Reviera types, families and parameters.

    Workflow. 1. Set up the mappings once in Systems › P&ID › P&ID Settings (also mep_settings.show(kind: "pid")). 2. Model from the line list (MEP-PID-001). 3. Choose Validate on the palette for one line, the selected lines, or the whole P&ID. Results appear as status labels in the line list and as a report. 4. Double-click a result to select and zoom to the model elements involved; use Ignore on a part that is intentionally different.

    Behaviour & rules. - Validate compares the model against the P&ID and marks each line: - fully modelled: every P&ID component on the line has a mapped model element, connected in the same order - mismatch, such as a size, spec or component difference (nominal size differs, pipe type differs from the spec mapping, or an inline component uses a different family than the mapping) - disconnected: the mapped elements of the line do not form one connected path (from the connectivity graph, MEP-CONN-002) - with ignored parts: differences the user marked Ignore, kept with the user name and date - with additional parts: model elements tagged with the line number that the P&ID does not contain (fittings and flanges added by routing preferences are not counted)

    Indicators use text and icons drawn from theme tokens. - Validation is read-only and runs in the background; it never changes the model. Results are stale once the model or the P&ID file changes. - P&ID Settings has two tabs, System Types and Object Mapping. They map: - piping services to pipe system types - pipe line specs to pipe types - inline assets to pipe accessory families - equipment classes to equipment families - P&ID properties to parameters (text, number and Yes/No; units converted where the P&ID states them) - Each tab is a two-column grid (P&ID item → Reviera target) with a search box, Auto-map by name and Import/Export as CSV. Rows with no target are labelled "Not mapped" and count as mismatches during validation. A target type or family that is deleted from the project makes its row invalid; OK is allowed but the dialog lists invalid rows. - Mappings can be saved as a named mapping set and reused across projects through Transfer Project Standards.

    Data (IFC mapping). Mappings, ignore records and the last validation result are stored in RXD document mep_settings (P&ID section). Line numbers on model elements are in IfcElement.Tag (MEP-PID-001).

    Commands. - pid.validate(pid_id, line_ids?[]) -> report - pid.ignore(pid_id, item_id, ignored: bool) - pid_settings.set_mapping(kind, rules[]) - pid_settings.auto_map(kind) -> rules[] - pid_settings.export_mapping(path), pid_settings.import_mapping(path)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing a modelled valve to a different family than the mapping specifies marks its line "mismatch", and the report names the valve. - [ ] Deleting a pipe segment in the middle of a fully modelled line changes its status to "disconnected" after re-validation. - [ ] A difference marked Ignore is reported under "ignored parts" and no longer causes a mismatch. - [ ] Auto-map by name maps the service "CW" to a pipe system type named "CW" and leaves unmatched services labelled "Not mapped".

    4.17 Open questions and deviations from the reference

    4.17.1 Intentional deviations

    # Area Reference behaviour Reviera behaviour Reason
    D1 UI Options Bar holds size, elevation and placement options (2026) No Options Bar. Everything is on the contextual ribbon and in Properties. Follows the reference's own 2027 direction and Reviera's UI chapter.
    D2 Ribbon Separate Precast tab (2026) One Concrete tab holds reinforcement and precast Follows the 2027 direction, with fewer tabs.
    D3 Structural solver Proprietary solver link and proprietary exchange file Provider interface with IFC Structural Analysis View and neutral JSON exchange. Open engines as plugins. No proprietary dependency; open standards (§4.3.11).
    D4 Load combinations Online generation that needs sign-in Offline, rule-based generation from editable code templates No cloud dependency, and works offline.
    D5 Analytical automation Visual-programming packages Lua rule packages, shipped under GPL Lua is Reviera's scripting layer (TECH_STACK §3.5).
    D6 Steel connections Proprietary connection engine and content in a local database server Open parametric connection library (manifest + Lua generator), stored as files Proprietary content cannot be used; a database server is unnecessary.
    D7 Steel interop Proprietary exchange formats with detailing software IFC as the primary exchange, plus an optional DSTV NC plugin Open formats only.
    D8 Interference check Excludes detailed steel elements and fabrication parts Includes them Reviera writes full geometry for both, so there is no technical reason to exclude them. This removes the need for an external tool.
    D9 MEP fabrication Proprietary configuration database and part files; proprietary job export ROFC open content model; open job export (IFC + JSON). Proprietary part files are not read or written. Proprietary formats are out of scope (00_overview).
    D10 Duct fitting losses Proprietary fitting-loss database Loss data per fitting type, with open coefficient tables from public-domain sources and user-supplied tables The proprietary database cannot be redistributed.
    D11 Fixture-unit conversion and ampacity Ships code tables from specific editions Built-in method from public-domain sources. Code tables are user-loaded content. Code tables may be copyrighted.
    D12 Lighting and solar analysis Cloud service with subscription Local providers (Radiance suggested) No vendor cloud (P3 policy).
    D13 Systems analysis Built-in simulation integration Same open engine (EnergyPlus) through OpenStudio, as an optional external provider Keeps the core GPL-clean, and the engine can be swapped.
    D14 P&ID Vendor cloud P&ID collaboration Local DEXPI (open standard) or CSV line-list import No vendor cloud; uses an open standard.
    D15 Precast CAM Built-in vendor-specific writers Neutral JSON/CSV export, plus format plugins where documentation allows Depends on the licensing terms of each format's documentation.
    D16 Legacy zones Hidden behind an ini switch No legacy loads tool. Legacy zones on import convert to system-zones. Simpler; matches the 2026/2027 direction.
    D17 Piles Generic foundation families Explicit pile and pile-cap support for clean IfcPile export IFC compatibility.
    D18 Sprinkler hydraulics Not supported Optional hydraulic-calculation provider Fills a common gap; optional.
    D19 Path of travel Single level only Same in the first release; multi-level is under consideration (Q9) Scope control.

    4.17.2 Open questions

    # Question Options / notes
    Q1 ~~RXD content areas~~ Resolved: model/structural (project document) and the structural element section are registered in 02a §6.4–§6.5.
    Q2 Analytical link representation. IFC4 has no dedicated rigid-link entity. A USERDEFINED curve member (chosen here) or a connection condition on IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember. Check against buildingSMART structural MVD guidance.
    Q3 Many-to-many physical/analytical association IfcGroup (chosen) versus several IfcRelAssignsToProduct relations. Check which form receiving tools understand.
    Q4 Coupler PredefinedType in IFC4 USERDEFINED "COUPLER" in IFC4; native COUPLER in IFC4X3 (to verify).
    Q5 Electrical analytical nodes and loads Geometry-less occurrences of real entity types (chosen) versus RXD-only nodes. The concern is other tools showing "phantom" equipment.
    Q6 Breakers per circuit Model each breaker as IfcProtectiveDevice nested in the board (more faithful, many more entities) or keep breaker data on the circuit.
    Q7 Free-form longitudinal splicing The reference extends this in 2027. Decide whether Reviera's first release includes it. Deferred to the post-Alpha/POC review (owner, 2026-10-12).
    Q8 Default heating/cooling loads engine A native Rust RTS implementation (fully built in, more work) or EnergyPlus sizing runs (needs an external install). Deferred to the post-Alpha/POC review (owner, 2026-10-12).
    Q9 Multi-level path of travel through stairs and ramps Needs a 3D navigation graph across levels; possibly P3. Deferred to the post-Alpha/POC review (owner, 2026-10-12).
    Q10 Obstacle-aware auto-routing for Generate Layout and Route and Fill Leave to clash checking (current), or add a 3D A router over an occupancy grid. Deferred to the post-Alpha/POC review (owner, 2026-10-12).*
    Q11 Bundled engines Which suggested engines, if any, ship with official installers. Each needs a licence review and a build for every target platform. Deferred to the post-Alpha/POC review (owner, 2026-10-12).
    Q12 ~~Cross-reference numbering~~ Resolved: collaboration is Chapter 6 and its file is 06_collaboration_coordination.md.
    Q13 Precast pieces and their source in IFC Deferred (owner, 2026-10-12): not implemented in the initial version. IFC allows one decomposition parent, so a piece cannot be aggregated by both its source element and its piece assembly. The initial version writes only the assembly aggregation and keeps the source link in RXD (STR-PRE-002). A real decision needs advice from an IFC and precast domain expert (buildingSMART precast/structural guidance, and how receiving tools behave). Candidate to evaluate: IfcRelAssignsToProduct from source to pieces.

    5CHChapter 5: Views, Graphics, Annotation, Schedules, Sheets and Output

    Area code: DOC · Status: Draft 1 (2026-10-12) · Primary source: research/04_documentation_collaboration.md (cited as research/04 §n) Related chapters: Chapter 1 (UI shell: ribbon, Project Browser, View Control Bar, keymap), Chapter 2 (DM: data model, families, parameters, formulas, file/IO), Chapter 2a (Reviera Extension Data, RXD), Chapter 3 (ARC: datums, rooms, areas), Chapter 6 (COL: worksharing display, links, positioning, BCF). Reference: Autodesk Revit 2026/2027 documentation and output features, used as the functional reference only.

    This chapter specifies how Reviera turns its IFC model into drawings and deliverables. It covers every view type, the rules that decide how each element is drawn in each view, model-reporting and drafting annotation, schedules, sheets, and every output channel. It also specifies how documentation objects persist inside the IFC file, and the hidden-line and GPU pipelines that produce the pictures.

    5.0 Core principles

    These principles apply to every requirement in this chapter.

    ID Principle Priority
    DOC-CORE-001 Views are live projections. A view stores only its definition (type, extents, camera, graphics settings, view-owned annotation). Projected model linework, cut poché and shaded images are always derived, and they are regenerated when the model changes. Derived results may be cached, but the cache is never the source of truth. Cache entries are keyed by element revision and view-definition revision (DOC-HLR-001); a cache miss or a corrupt entry only costs regeneration time, never a wrong drawing. Closing and reopening a project discards no definition data and may discard every cache. The only stored derived result is a saved rendering image (DOC-OUT-011). P0
    DOC-CORE-002 Paper-space sizing. Annotation symbols, text, tag heads, dimension text, line patterns, drafting fill patterns and annotation line weights are specified in paper millimetres. They render at paper size × view scale in model space, so that changing the view scale resizes them automatically. Model patterns (DOC-GFX-014), model text and model lines are the exception: they are sized in real units. Annotation positions are stored in view coordinates, so a scale change keeps each tag's anchor on its host while its head grows or shrinks around that anchor; leaders are re-elbowed, never re-routed. Sheets are always 1:1, so sheet annotation is the same in paper and model space. P0
    DOC-CORE-003 Model-reporting annotation is associative. Tags, dimensions, spot dimensions and element/material keynotes bind to model references (element GlobalId plus a stable geometric sub-reference). They update when the referenced element changes and become orphaned (kept, flagged, drawn in a warning colour) when the reference disappears. A reference is re-resolved on every regeneration of the view; when a sub-reference cannot be found but the element still exists, Reviera tries the named sub-reference rules of Chapter 2a (for example the same face role on a split wall) before orphaning. An orphan can be re-hosted with Pick new host or deleted; it never silently attaches to another element. P0
    DOC-CORE-004 View-owned elements. Text, detail lines, regions, detail components, revision clouds and similar drafting items belong to exactly one view (or sheet) and appear nowhere else, except through dependent views (DOC-VIEW-011). Deleting a view deletes its view-owned elements in the same undo step; the confirmation states how many there are. Copying them to another view is an explicit act (clipboard Paste aligned to selected views, Duplicate with Detailing, or detail groups) and always creates new objects with new ids. Model elements are never view-owned. P0
    DOC-CORE-005 One sheet per model view. A graphical model view (plan, section, elevation, callout, 3D, drafting, rendering) can be placed on at most one sheet. Schedules, legends, keynote legends, sheet lists, view lists and note blocks can be placed on any number of sheets. The rule is checked by sheet.place_view, viewport.swap_view and viewport.move_to_sheet, which fail with view.already_on_sheet (naming the sheet) instead of placing a second copy. To show the same area twice, the user duplicates the view, usually as a dependent (DOC-VIEW-011). Assembly views follow the same rule (§5.16). P0
    DOC-CORE-006 One draw list, many outputs. Every 2D result (on-screen hidden-line view, print, PDF, DXF/DWG, raster image) is produced from the same intermediate draw list (DOC-HLR-004). Output is what you see on screen, apart from the documented print options (DOC-OUT-001). The differences allowed between screen and output are exactly: temporary display state (DOC-GFX-008, temporary view properties, reveal hidden, displacement highlight) never prints; Thin lines is screen-only; the print options hide or recolour the items they name; raster processing (DOC-HLR-007) changes shaded content only. Any other difference is a defect. P0
    DOC-CORE-007 Everything is a command. Every creation, edit and output operation in this chapter is a registered command, so it is reachable from the ribbon, Lua and MCP. Read-only queries (for example graphics.explain) are commands too, flagged as not undoable. Commands that open a dialog (for example template.manage, revision.manage) are UI entry points only: every change made in the dialog is applied through the undoable commands of the same requirement, so a dialog session that changes five things records those five commands as one undo step named after the dialog. Without a UI (Lua, MCP, headless), dialog commands fail with ui.unavailable. P0
    DOC-CORE-008 RXD persistence. Every documentation object defined here persists as Reviera Extension Data (RXD, §5.1, Chapter 2a), embedded in the IFC file by default and keyed to the model by IFC GlobalIds. A project opened locally or downloaded from BIMserver therefore reproduces every view, sheet and annotation exactly, and the file remains valid standard IFC. When another tool has deleted or changed elements that RXD refers to, the reconciliation pass of Chapter 2a §7 runs on open: references to missing elements become orphans (DOC-CORE-003), and nothing is deleted without a report. Session-only state (temporary hide/isolate, highlight modes, render history) is never written to RXD. P0

    Acceptance criteria (core). - [ ] Changing a wall's thickness updates every plan, section, schedule and sheet that shows it, without the user refreshing anything. - [ ] Changing a plan from 1:100 to 1:50 halves the model-space height of every text note in it while its printed height stays the same. - [ ] Deleting a tagged door leaves the tag in the view marked as orphaned, and the warnings list reports it. - [ ] Saving a project with views, sheets, schedules and annotation, closing it and reopening it gives identical PDF output (byte-identical page content streams, excluding timestamps).

    5.1 Persistence of documentation objects

    ID: DOC-IFC-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §11; TECH_STACK §3.1, §3.7.3; spec/02a_extension_data_format.md

    Purpose. Views, sheets, schedules, graphic standards and annotation are not building data, and IFC entities cannot express them without loss. Reviera stores them as Reviera Extension Data (RXD): versioned JSON documents with stable object ids, defined in Chapter 2a (02a_extension_data_format.md). By default RXD is embedded in the IFC file as valid, standard IFC, so a single .ifc file carries the whole project. Chapter 2a defines the carrier (property sets, payload encoding, the alternative external carrier), the object envelope, the reference syntax and the merge rules. This chapter does not redefine any of that. It only names the RXD documents this chapter uses, and specifies how documentation is exported as IFC annotation for other tools.

    Behaviour & rules. - Loading. On open, views/index, sheets/index, views/templates, views/filters, views/types, views/color_schemes, the standards/* documents and the project/* documents load at once. views/<viewId>, views/annotation/<viewId>, schedules/<scheduleId> and sheets/<sheetId> load lazily, the first time the view, sheet or schedule is opened, printed, exported, scheduled (view lists, sheet lists) or queried through Lua or MCP. - Saving. Reviera tracks changes per RXD document. On save, only changed documents are serialised again; unchanged documents are written byte-identical, which keeps BIMserver revisions and text diffs small. - Damaged documents. A document that fails its schema check on load is quarantined: its view, sheet or schedule is listed as damaged in the Project Browser and cannot be opened, its raw JSON is kept unchanged and written back unchanged on save, and the problem is listed in the warnings list. The rest of the project opens normally. rxd.status (Chapter 2) reports quarantined documents. - Versions. Each document carries the RXD format version (Chapter 2a). Unknown fields from a newer minor version are kept and written back. A document from a newer major version opens read-only, with a banner naming the version. - Deleting model elements never deletes RXD annotation that refers to them; the annotation becomes an orphan (DOC-CORE-003). rxd.reconcile (Chapter 2a) can report or remove orphans in bulk.

    Commands. Persistence has no commands of its own: saving and opening use file.save, file.save_as and file.open (Chapter 2), and inspection uses rxd.get_document, rxd.status and rxd.reconcile (Chapters 2 and 2a). Acceptance criteria are in §5.1.3.

    5.1.1 What lives where

    Data Store Notes
    Elements, types, materials, levels, grids, spatial structure, standard Psets/Qtos, parameter values IFC entities Chapter 2. Never duplicated in RXD.
    Element-scoped documentation data (phase created/demolished, design option membership, per-element display flags) element-scoped RXD on the element (Chapter 2a) Also written as the standard Status property on export (DOC-GFX-017).
    Views (all kinds), view range, crop, camera, section box, per-view overrides, hidden elements RXD documents views/index and views/<viewId> One document per view, loaded lazily when the view opens.
    Navigation state: each view's latest camera and Home (UI-NAV-001) RXD document views/state Written with the next save; never makes the model modified.
    View templates, view filters, selection sets RXD documents views/templates, views/filters, model/selection_sets
    View-owned annotation (dimensions, spot dimensions, text, tags, keynotes, symbols, detail lines, regions, detail components, repeating details, insulation, revision clouds, plan regions, colour fill legends, matchlines, view references, elevation markers, legend components) RXD document views/annotation/<viewId> Kinds anno.*.
    Object styles, line weights, line styles, line patterns, fill patterns, text/dimension/tag styles, halftone settings, detail-level map, discipline profiles RXD documents standards/*
    Schedules (all kinds, including keynote legends, sheet lists, view lists, note blocks) RXD document schedules/<scheduleId>
    Sheets, title block instances, viewports, schedule instances, sheet annotation, guide grids, saved positions, sheet collections RXD documents sheets/index and sheets/<sheetId>
    Revisions and revision settings RXD document project/revisions
    Phases, phase filters, phase graphics RXD document project/phases
    Design option sets and options RXD document project/design_options
    Print, PDF, image and export setups; view/sheet sets RXD document project/settings (section output)
    Images (title block logos, image underlays, saved renderings, schedule images) RXD assets (Chapter 2a)

    Rules. - Every documentation object in this chapter is an RXD object with the common envelope (stable id, kind, per-object rev, name, data, ext). References to model objects use IFC GlobalIds, with named geometric sub-references (for example #face:core.ext) for dimensions and linework overrides. References between RXD objects use their stable ids. Index-based topology references are never stored. - Each object kind used below is registered in the Chapter 2a kind catalogue with a JSON Schema before implementation. The Data paragraph of each requirement names the RXD document and kind, and lists the payload fields this chapter depends on; the schema is normative. - Derived results (hidden-line linework, cut poché, schedule cell values, rendered pixels) are never stored in RXD. Saved renderings (DOC-OUT-011) are the one exception: they are stored as image assets. - Because RXD is merged per object by stable id (three-way, Chapter 2a and Chapter 6 COL-MRG-001), the documents are split so that two users editing different views, sheets or annotation do not conflict.

    5.1.2 IFC export of documentation as IFC annotation

    ID: DOC-IFC-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §6.4 (Export 2D plan view elements)

    Purpose. Other IFC tools do not read RXD. Viewers, facility-management tools and other authoring tools may still want drawings and annotation. The export setup option Include documentation as IFC annotation (DOC-OUT-006) writes them as standard IFC4 presentation entities. This is an interoperability export: Reviera never treats it as its own store. When Reviera opens a foreign IFC containing such annotation, it shows that annotation read-only as imported drafting (Chapter 6, COL-LNK-001).

    Behaviour & rules. When the option is on, for each view selected in the export setup: - Contexts. Reviera creates IfcGeometricRepresentationSubContext instances under the Plan and Model contexts with ContextIdentifier = 'Annotation', a TargetView of PLAN_VIEW, REFLECTED_PLAN_VIEW, SECTION_VIEW, ELEVATION_VIEW or MODEL_VIEW, and TargetScale equal to the view's scale (for example 0.01 for 1:100). Sheets, if exported, use a sub-context with TargetView = USERDEFINED and UserDefinedTargetView = 'Sheet', in paper millimetres. - Grouping. Each exported view becomes an IfcGroup (ObjectType = 'DRAWING', Name = view name) whose members (IfcRelAssignsToGroup) are that view's IfcAnnotation objects. Plan annotation may optionally be contained in the view's storey (IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure). - Annotation objects. Each annotation becomes one IfcAnnotation. In IFC4, its class is given by ObjectType (DIMENSION, TEXT, TAG, SYMBOL, DETAIL_LINE, FILLED_REGION, REVISION_CLOUD, MATCHLINE, …). In IFC4X3 exports, PredefinedType is set to the matching IfcAnnotationTypeEnum value where one exists, otherwise USERDEFINED with the same ObjectType. Model-reporting annotation is related to the element it reports on with IfcRelAssignsToProduct (RelatingProduct = the element), so consumers can tell which door a tag belongs to. - Curves. Lines, polylines, arcs and splines are items of an IfcGeometricCurveSet, using IfcPolyline, IfcIndexedPolyCurve (with arc segments), IfcTrimmedCurve of IfcCircle/IfcEllipse, and IfcBSplineCurveWithKnots. Representation identifier Annotation; representation type Annotation2D, or GeometricCurveSet when only curves are present. - Fills. Regions and poché use IfcAnnotationFillArea (outer and inner boundaries), styled by IfcFillAreaStyle containing IfcFillAreaStyleHatching (one per hatch line family), IfcColourRgb for solid and background fills, or IfcFillAreaStyleTiles where hatching cannot express the pattern. - Line appearance. IfcStyledItem → IfcCurveStyle with CurveWidth (paper mm scaled by the context scale), CurveColour, and CurveFont as an IfcCurveStyleFont built from the line pattern's dash and gap segments. - Text. IfcTextLiteralWithExtent (literal, placement, path, IfcPlanarExtent, box alignment) styled by IfcTextStyle with IfcTextStyleFontModel. Rich text is flattened to plain text, one literal per line. - Symbols. Repeated symbols (tag heads, arrowheads, section heads, title block artwork) use IfcRepresentationMap / IfcMappedItem. - Images. Logos and images use IfcBlobTexture (PNG or JPEG) on an IfcAnnotationFillArea, through IfcSurfaceStyleWithTextures. - Drawing linework. With the setup option Include 2D linework, the view's computed draw list (DOC-HLR-004) is also written: one IfcAnnotation (ObjectType = 'DRAWING_LINEWORK') per view, whose representation holds one IfcGeometricCurveSet per distinct line style (each with its IfcStyledItem), plus IfcAnnotationFillArea items for cut poché. Tools without hidden-line capability then get a finished 2D drawing. - Other documentation data written on export: phase status as the standard Status property (DOC-GFX-017); design options and worksets as IfcGroup (DOC-GFX-018; Chapter 6). - The same export setup can also strip RXD (a "clean" exchange file without Reviera data, DOC-OUT-006).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An IFC4 file exported with Include documentation as IFC annotation validates with IfcOpenShell's schema validator with no errors. - [ ] A third-party IFC viewer that displays Annotation sub-contexts shows the exported floor plan's dimensions and text at the correct position and size. - [ ] Each exported door tag is related to its door by IfcRelAssignsToProduct. - [ ] With Include 2D linework on, the exported plan linework overlays the model plan with no visible offset. - [ ] Opening a stripped export in Reviera creates no native annotation; the exported annotation appears only as read-only imported drafting.

    5.1.3 Acceptance criteria (persistence)

    • A saved project is one valid IFC file that, when reopened, restores every view, sheet, schedule and annotation (RXD embedded by default).
    • Switching the project to the external RXD carrier (Chapter 2a) and back gives identical documentation.
    • Opening a project with 500 views opens only the views that were open at the last save; rxd.status shows the other view documents as not loaded.
    • A view document edited by hand so that it fails its schema opens as damaged, the rest of the project opens, and saving writes the damaged JSON back unchanged.
    • Adding one text note to one view changes only that view's views/annotation/<viewId> RXD document (and the RXD index metadata defined in Chapter 2a).
    • Third-party IFC tools open a Reviera project file without errors, ignoring the RXD.

    5.2 Common view model

    Shared view properties and the Project Browser

    ID: DOC-VIEW-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §1 (intro table), §11; web: Edit Type Properties for View Tags, About Section Tag Visibility, Hide Section Tags, Find a Referring View

    Purpose. Give every graphical view one consistent set of properties, so that templates, schedules (View List), filters, Lua and MCP can treat views uniformly.

    Workflow. 1. The user creates a view with a View-tab tool, or by duplicating an existing view (DOC-VIEW-011). 2. The view appears in the Project Browser in the node chosen by the active browser organisation scheme. 3. With no element selected, the Properties palette shows the active view's properties; edits apply at once and regenerate the view.

    UI. View tab › Create panel: Plan Views ▾, Elevation ▾, Section, Callout ▾, 3D View ▾, Drafting View, Legends ▾, Schedules ▾, Scope Box, Duplicate View ▾. Project Browser context menu: Open, Duplicate View ▸, Apply/Create Template, Rename, Delete, Add to Sheet, Browser Organization. View Control Bar (Chapter 1): scale, detail level, visual style, sun/shadows, crop toggles, temporary hide/isolate, reveal hidden, temporary view properties, worksharing display, isolate annotations.

    Behaviour & rules. - Properties shared by all graphical views:

    Group Property Values / notes
    Graphics Scale Preset list (1:1 to 1:5000, plus imperial presets) or Custom (any positive ratio). Drives paper-space sizing (DOC-CORE-002).
    Display Model Normal / Halftone / Do not display. "Do not display" leaves only annotation and view-owned elements visible.
    Detail Level Coarse / Medium / Fine (DOC-GFX-010).
    Parts Visibility Show Parts / Show Original / Show Both.
    Visibility/Graphics Opens the view's graphics dialog (DOC-GFX-003).
    Graphic Display Options Opens DOC-GFX-012.
    Discipline Architectural / Structural / Mechanical / Electrical / Plumbing / Coordination. Each discipline has a category visibility profile and halftones non-discipline categories (DOC-GFX-016).
    Show Hidden Lines By Discipline / All / None.
    Color Scheme Location, Color Scheme Background / Foreground; scheme per space-like category (DOC-ANN-022).
    Sun Path On / Off (3D and plans).
    Underlay (plans) Base Level, Top Level, Orientation DOC-VR-004.
    Extents Crop View, Crop Region Visible, Annotation Crop, View Range (plans), Far Clipping and Far Clip Offset (sections, elevations), Depth Clipping (plans), Scope Box, Section Box (3D)
    Identity View Template, View Name, Dependency, Title on Sheet, Sheet Number and Sheet Name (read-only), Referencing Sheet / Referencing Detail (read-only), Sheet Collection / Referencing Sheet Collection (read-only)
    Phasing Phase, Phase Filter DOC-GFX-017.
    • View names are unique within a view kind (plans of the same plan type, sections, 3D views and so on). Renaming to a duplicate name is rejected with a clear message.
    • Browser organisation schemes group and sort views and sheets by any view or sheet parameter (for example Discipline, then View Type, then Phase). A scheme is a project-level definition; the active scheme is a user preference. Schemes persist in RXD document standards/browser.
    • Every view has a hidden, stable view kind (enumeration) and a view family type (user-defined types per kind, for example "Working Plan" or "Presentation Plan"). The type supplies the default template for new views, whether new views are bound to that template, and the marker symbol (callout tag, section head, elevation mark).
    • Per-user views: the default 3D view is created per user in BIMserver mode ({3D - <user>}), because one user orbiting a shared view must not change another user's view.
    • View tag settings. Manage › Additional Settings ▾ › Callout Tags / Elevation Tags / Section Tags (view_tag.settings) opens a type editor for the view tag types that marker symbols use. The dialog lists the tag types of the chosen kind (Duplicate, Rename, Delete; a type in use cannot be deleted until its users are moved to another type) and edits:
    • Section tags: section head symbol (an annotation family), section tail symbol (a symbol or None), and the broken-line display used by Gap mode (DOC-VIEW-004);
    • Callout tags: callout head symbol and the corner radius of the callout boundary (paper mm, 0 to 50);
    • Elevation tags: the marker body symbol (round, square or a custom annotation family) and the direction arrow symbol. Symbols are chosen from loaded annotation families of the matching category; a family whose labels lack the detail and sheet number is accepted with a warning. Edits are type edits: every marker of that type redraws at once. View family types (Section, Detail, Callout and Elevation types) refer to a view tag type, so the tag type is shared by all view types that use it.
    • View tag visibility. A section, callout or elevation marker is drawn in another view only when the marked view's extents intersect that view's range (plans: the view range slab; sections and elevations: the far clip volume), and when the viewing scale is not coarser than the marker's Hide at scales coarser than value. Print option Hide unreferenced view tags (DOC-OUT-001) drops markers whose view is not on a sheet.
    • Find referring views. Project Browser › right-click a view › Find Referring Views (view.find_referring) lists every view whose marker, callout boundary or view reference symbol points to the chosen view, and every sheet that holds it. The list opens in a Go to View dialog: double-click (or Open) opens the chosen view or sheet and zooms to the marker. A view nothing refers to gives an empty list with the message "No views refer to this view".

    Data (RXD). RXD documents views/index (id, kind, name, template, browser path) and views/<viewId> (kinds view.plan, view.ceiling, view.structural, view.area, view.section, view.elevation, view.callout, view.3d, view.camera, view.drafting, view.legend, view.walkthrough, view.rendering). Common payload: viewFamilyType, scale, displayModel, detailLevel, partsVisibility, discipline, showHiddenLines, colorSchemeLocation, colorSchemes, phase, phaseFilter, template, parent (dependent views), titleOnSheet, visualStyle, crop, annotationCrop, scopeBox, orientation, and the view's coordinate frame (origin, x and y axes, view direction). View family types: RXD document views/types, kind view.familytype (with tagType, the id of its view tag type). View tag types: RXD document views/types, kind view.tagtype (tagKind: section | callout | elevation, headSymbol, tailSymbol, cornerRadius, arrowSymbol). Browser schemes: RXD document standards/browser.

    Commands. view.set_property(view_id, name, value) -> () view.rename(view_id, new_name) -> () view.delete(view_ids[]) -> () view.open(view_id) -> () view.list(filter?) -> view_summary[] viewtype.create(kind, name, default_template_id?, bind_new_views?, marker_type_id?) -> view_family_type_id browser.set_organization(target: views|sheets, scheme_id) -> () browser.create_organization(name, target, group_by[], sort_by) -> scheme_id view_tag.settings(kind?: callout|elevation|section) -> () (opens the view tag type editor described above; the edits it makes are type edits through type.set_param, Chapter 2) view.find_referring(view_id) -> referrer[] (query; each entry is {id, kind: view|sheet, via: marker|callout|viewref|viewport, marker_id?})

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Every property in the table above can be read and written through view.set_property from Lua and from MCP. - [ ] Changing the head symbol of a section tag type redraws every section marker of that type in every view, in one undo step. - [ ] view.find_referring on a detail view referenced by two sections and placed on sheet A501 returns the two host views and A501. - [ ] Renaming a view to an existing name of the same kind fails with an error naming the clash; no change is made. - [ ] Switching browser organisation from "by type" to "by Discipline, then type" regroups the browser without changing any view.

    5.3 Plan views

    Creating plan views

    ID: DOC-VIEW-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §1.1

    Purpose. Create horizontal cut views (floor plan, reflected ceiling plan, structural plan, area plan) associated with a level.

    Workflow. 1. View tab › Create › Plan Views ▾ › Floor Plan / Reflected Ceiling Plan / Structural Plan / Area Plan. 2. In the New Plan dialog the user picks the view family type, one or more levels, and the scale. By default, levels that already have a plan of that type are not listed; clearing Do not duplicate existing views lists them too. 3. For an area plan the user also picks an area scheme (Chapter 3); Reviera offers to generate area boundary lines from walls. 4. OK creates one view per level and opens the last one.

    UI. New Plan dialog: Type selector, Edit Type…, level list (multi-select), Do not duplicate existing views, Scale. The level tool (Chapter 3) has a Make plan view option that calls the same command.

    Behaviour & rules. - A floor plan and a structural plan look down. A reflected ceiling plan looks up from its cut plane and is drawn mirror-correct (as if the ceiling were reflected in a mirror on the floor), so its left and right agree with the floor plan. - Structural plans default to a cut plane below the level, so that framing supporting the level is visible, and to the Structural discipline. - Each new view gets its view range defaults from its view family type (DOC-VR-001), and its template from the type's template for new views. - Deleting a level deletes its plan views after a confirmation that lists them.

    Data (RXD). views/<viewId> of kind view.plan, view.ceiling, view.structural or view.area, with level (ifc: GlobalId of the IfcBuildingStorey) and areaScheme (area plans).

    Commands. view.create_plan(kind, level_ids[], view_family_type_id?, scale?, allow_duplicates?, area_scheme_id?) -> view_id[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Selecting three levels creates three floor plans, named after their levels, in one undo step. - [ ] A reflected ceiling plan of the same level shows a door at the same paper position as the floor plan. - [ ] Creating an area plan with generate boundaries produces area boundary lines on the exterior wall faces chosen by the area scheme rules (Chapter 3).

    View range definition

    ID: DOC-VR-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §1.1 View Range · screenshots/documentation/view_range_dialog.png · screenshots/documentation/view_range_section_diagram.png

    Purpose. Define the vertical slice of the model that a plan shows: the cut plane, and the range above and below it.

    Workflow. 1. Properties › Extents › View Range › Edit… opens the View Range dialog. 2. For each of the four planes (Top, Cut Plane, Bottom, View Depth), the user picks a level reference and an offset. 3. A Show diagram toggle expands an explanatory section diagram that shows the four planes against the current level stack (drawn by Reviera; no reference artwork). 4. Apply or OK validates and regenerates.

    UI. View Range dialog: four rows (Plane, Level reference drop-down, Offset field); level references are Associated Level, Level Above, Level Below, Unlimited (Top and View Depth only) and every named level. Apply / OK / Cancel, diagram toggle.

    Behaviour & rules. - Each plane resolves to an absolute elevation z = elevation(level_ref) + offset. Unlimited resolves to +∞ (Top) or −∞ (View Depth). Level Above/Below resolve against the sorted level list at regeneration time, so adding a level in between changes the result. - Ordering constraint (floor and structural plans): Top ≥ Cut ≥ Bottom ≥ ViewDepth. Ceiling plans: the range is mirrored: Bottom ≤ Cut ≤ Top, and View Depth lies above Top (ViewDepth ≥ Top). - A combination that violates the ordering is rejected in the dialog (the offending row is highlighted) and through commands (error view_range.invalid_order). If a later level move makes a saved range invalid, the view keeps its previous valid result, shows a warning banner, and lists the problem in the warnings list until fixed. - Defaults for new floor plans: Top = Level Above, offset 0 (or Associated Level + 2300 mm when there is no level above); Cut = Associated Level + 1200 mm; Bottom = Associated Level, offset 0; View Depth = Associated Level, offset 0. Defaults are editable per view family type. - Selecting a plan's level marker in a section or elevation offers Show view range, which draws the four planes of that plan as temporary graphics in the section.

    Data (RXD). viewRange block of the view payload: top, cut, bottom, depth, each {level, offset}, where level is an ifc: storey reference or one of the tokens associated, above, below, unlimited.

    Commands. view.set_view_range(view_id, top, cut, bottom, depth) -> () where each plane is {level_ref, offset}; view.get_view_range(view_id) -> {planes, resolved_elevations}.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Setting Cut above Top is rejected with view_range.invalid_order and nothing changes. - [ ] Inserting a level between a plan's level and the next one changes the result of a Level Above top plane on the next regeneration. - [ ] view.get_view_range returns resolved elevations that match the dialog.

    View range classification algorithm

    ID: DOC-VR-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §1.1 View Range rules (a)–(d) · screenshots/documentation/view_range_cut_plane_diagram.png · screenshots/documentation/view_range_view_depth_diagram.png

    Purpose. Decide, deterministically and per element, which parts of an element a plan shows and with which graphic treatment.

    Behaviour & rules. For a floor or structural plan with resolved elevations T ≥ C ≥ B ≥ D (for a ceiling plan, mirror the vertical axis and swap the roles of above and below, then apply the same rules), the plan is generated as follows.

    1. Candidate selection. Query the spatial index for elements whose bounding box overlaps the plan's crop prism (crop polygon extruded from D to T, or from D − floor tolerance when step 6 applies). Drop elements that the graphics stack hides (§5.11) before any geometry work.
    2. Zones. The vertical axis is split into zones: - Above (z > T): never shown, except for symbolic plan linework (step 7). - Upper (C < z ≤ T): primary range above the cut plane. - Cut (z = C). - Lower (B ≤ z < C): primary range below the cut plane. - Beyond (D ≤ z < B): the view depth. - Below (z < D).
    3. Cut. For an element whose solid geometry crosses C, and whose category is cuttable (walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, columns, structural framing, stairs, railings, doors, windows, generic models, casework, curtain panels and mullions, MEP segments and others, as set in the category catalogue of Chapter 2): compute the planar section of the solid at C (§5.12, DOC-HLR-002). Draw the section's boundary with the element's cut line style and fill its interior with the cut pattern. Compound elements are cut layer by layer, and each layer uses its material's cut pattern. A non-cuttable category (for example furniture, plumbing fixtures, specialty equipment) that crosses C is drawn in projection, as if it were entirely in the Lower zone.
    4. Lower zone. Geometry in the Lower zone is projected straight down onto the view plane and run through hidden-line removal together with everything else visible from above. Visible edges use the projection line style; surfaces may carry the surface pattern (model patterns show at their real size).
    5. Upper zone. For each category the catalogue defines an above-cut behaviour: - Hide (the default for most categories); - Projection, drawn as in step 4 (default for windows, casework, generic models, and any family type whose author has set Show above cut plane); - Overhead, drawn with the <Overhead> line style (default for ceilings, soffits, upper cabinets drawn as dashed, and structural framing above the cut in structural plans). The table is project data, so offices can change it, and view filters may override it per view.
    6. Beyond zone. Geometry in the Beyond zone is drawn with the <Beyond> line style. Floor-like exception: floors, structural slabs, stairs, ramps, roofs and toposolids lying below B are drawn with their normal projection style (not <Beyond>) when their top surface lies within the floor tolerance below B (default 1220 mm, project setting), even if that is below D. This shows the floor of a sunken area or the slab under a level without forcing the user to deepen the view range.
    7. Symbolic plan linework. Family types may provide symbolic 2D linework for plan views (door swings, window sills, fixture symbols). When an element is visible by steps 3–6, its symbolic linework replaces or supplements its projected geometry according to the family's visibility settings. Symbolic linework is independent of the cut height.
    8. Partial elements. Elements that span several zones are split with OCCT half-space booleans at C, B and D, and each piece is treated by its own zone. Splitting happens on a temporary copy; the model is never modified.
    9. Hidden-line resolution. All pieces from steps 3–7 go through one hidden-line pass looking down (DOC-HLR-002). Cut poché occludes geometry beneath it. Pieces from the Upper zone shown as Overhead are not occluded by cut geometry (they are drawn over it, as overhead lines conventionally are).
    10. Show Hidden Lines. When the view's Show Hidden Lines is All, or By Discipline with the element's discipline matching the view, edges hidden by step 9 are drawn with the <Hidden> line style instead of being dropped.
    11. Linked models. Elements of linked models go through the same algorithm with the host plan's range (or with the linked view's range when the link's display setting is By Linked View, Chapter 6, COL-LNK-007).

    Data (RXD). The category catalogue (Chapter 2) gains cuttable, aboveCutBehaviour and floorLike attributes, stored per category in RXD document standards/object_styles. The floor tolerance is in project/settings. The family-type flag Show above cut plane is part of the family recipe (Chapter 2).

    Commands. category.set_view_range_behaviour(category, cuttable?, above_cut?: hide|projection|overhead, floor_like?) -> (); settings.set_floor_tolerance(length) -> (); view.classify_element(view_id, element_id) -> zone_report (query; returns which zones and styles apply, for debugging and for AI agents).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 3000 mm wall from the level, viewed with C = 1200 mm, is drawn as cut poché with cut lines; a 900 mm high wall is drawn in projection. - [ ] A window whose head is above C but whose sill is below it shows cut frame lines; a high window entirely above C (but below T) shows in projection; an upper wall cabinet shows dashed <Overhead> lines. - [ ] A column footing between B and D is drawn with <Beyond>; one below D is not drawn. - [ ] A sunken slab 600 mm below B and below D is drawn with projection lines; the same slab 1500 mm below B is not drawn (default tolerance 1220 mm). - [ ] With Show Hidden Lines = All, a beam hidden below a slab in a structural plan is drawn with the <Hidden> style. - [ ] view.classify_element reports the same zones that the drawing shows.

    Plan regions

    ID: DOC-VR-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §1.1 Plan Regions

    Purpose. Let part of a plan use a different view range (split levels, mezzanines, clerestory windows).

    Workflow. 1. View tab › Create › Plan Views ▾ › Plan Region enters sketch mode. 2. The user sketches one or more closed, non-intersecting loops and finishes. 3. In Properties the user edits the region's View Range (same dialog as DOC-VR-001).

    UI. Sketch mode with the standard draw tools (Chapter 1); Properties: View Range › Edit….

    Behaviour & rules. - The plan is partitioned into the region polygons and the remainder. Each part runs DOC-VR-002 with its own range, and the results are clipped to the part's polygon before they are combined into one draw list. Edges along the boundary are not drawn as model edges. - Plan regions in the same view must not overlap; an overlap is rejected at Finish. - Regions may extend beyond the crop region; only the part inside is used. - Region boundaries are view-owned annotation of category Plan Region and can be hidden through the graphics dialog. Regions can be copied to other plans with clipboard paste-aligned (Chapter 1).

    Data (RXD). Annotation object of kind anno.planregion in views/annotation/<viewId>: loops (view coordinates) and its own viewRange block.

    Commands. view.create_plan_region(view_id, loops[], view_range) -> element_id; planregion.set_view_range(region_id, top, cut, bottom, depth) -> ().

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A mezzanine plan region with C = 3800 mm cuts the mezzanine wall inside the region while the rest of the plan keeps C = 1200 mm. - [ ] Sketching two overlapping regions in one view fails at Finish with a message naming the overlap.

    Underlay

    ID: DOC-VR-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §1.1 Underlay

    Purpose. Show another level range in halftone beneath the current plan, for tracing and coordination.

    Workflow. In Properties › Underlay the user sets Base Level, Top Level and Orientation (Look down / Look up).

    Behaviour & rules. - The underlay range is from Base Level to Top Level (Top Level may be None, meaning the next level above Base). Its contents are generated by DOC-VR-002 with a synthetic range (T = Top Level, C = T, B = D = Base Level for Look down; mirrored for Look up) and drawn with the project's underlay line settings (DOC-GFX-009) beneath all other content. - Underlay elements are not selectable unless the Select underlay elements selection toggle (Chapter 1) is on. - Underlay is excluded from printing only if the print option Hide underlay is on (default off).

    Data (RXD). underlay block of the view payload: baseLevel, topLevel (ifc: storey references or null), orientation.

    Commands. view.set_underlay(view_id, base_level_id?, top_level_id?, orientation) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With Base Level = Level 1 in the Level 2 plan, Level 1 walls appear in halftone and cannot be selected with the toggle off.

    Depth clipping and far clipping

    ID: DOC-VR-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §1.1 Depth Clipping / Far Clipping

    Purpose. Limit how far a view sees past its view plane, with or without a boundary line.

    Behaviour & rules. - Depth Clipping (plans): No clip / Clip without line / Clip with line. When clipping is on, geometry beyond View Depth is removed even for floor-like categories (step 6 of DOC-VR-002 is suppressed). Clip with line draws the intersection of cut geometry with the depth plane using the <Beyond> style. - Far Clipping (sections, elevations, callouts): No clip / Clip with line / Clip without line, plus Far Clip Offset (distance from the view plane). With No clip, the view sees to infinity. Clip with line draws the intersection edges at the far plane. - Far clip and depth clipping are applied as an extra clipping half-space before hidden-line removal.

    Data (RXD). View payload fields depthClipping, farClipping, farClipOffset.

    Commands. view.set_far_clip(view_id, mode, offset?) -> (); view.set_depth_clipping(view_id, mode) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A section with Far Clip Offset 5000 mm does not show an elevation of walls 8000 mm behind the cut. - [ ] Clip with line draws the clipped outline of a slab that crosses the far plane.

    5.4 Elevations

    ID: DOC-VIEW-003 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §1.2

    Purpose. Orthographic views looking horizontally at the building, from outside (building elevations) or inside a room (interior elevations).

    Workflow. 1. View tab › Create › Elevation ▾ › Elevation; choose an elevation type (for example Building Elevation or Interior Elevation). 2. In a plan, the marker preview snaps its direction perpendicular to the nearest wall; Tab cycles candidate directions. Click to place. 3. A marker with one active direction creates one view. Selecting the marker body shows one checkbox per direction (up to four); ticking more checkboxes creates more views from the same marker. 4. Selecting a direction arrow shows that view's extents (view plane width, far clip line) with drag grips. 5. Framing Elevation: pick a grid line or reference plane; the view is aligned to it and its crop is limited to the selected grid bay.

    UI. Type Selector (elevation types), Edit Type (marker symbol, default template), placement preview, marker checkboxes, rotate control on the marker.

    Behaviour & rules. - Interior elevation markers placed inside a room size their crop to the room's bounding walls, floor and ceiling where they can be found; otherwise to a default size. - Rotating the marker gives non-orthogonal elevations. - Hide at scales coarser than hides the marker in views at coarser scales. - The marker head displays the detail and sheet number once the view is placed on a sheet; until then it shows a placeholder dash. - Deleting a marker deletes its views after confirmation; deleting the last view of a marker deletes the marker.

    Data (RXD). Marker: annotation object of kind anno.elevationmarker in the host plan's annotation document (position, rotation, marker type, views[4] slots holding rv: view ids or null). Each view: views/<viewId> of kind view.elevation, with marker and markerSlot (0–3); framing elevations add datum (ifc: grid or reference-plane reference) and bay.

    Commands. view.create_elevation(host_view_id, point, elevation_type_id, directions[], rotation?) -> {marker_id, view_ids[]} elevationmarker.set_directions(marker_id, directions[]) -> view_ids[] view.create_framing_elevation(host_view_id, datum_id, elevation_type_id, bay?) -> view_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Placing a marker next to a wall creates a view facing that wall. - [ ] Ticking all four boxes on an interior marker creates four views, each cropped to the room. - [ ] After placing the elevation on sheet A201 as detail 3, the marker head shows "3" and "A201".

    5.5 Sections

    ID: DOC-VIEW-004 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §1.3 · screenshots/documentation/section_view_building.png

    Purpose. Vertical cuts through the model.
