    Workflow. 1. View tab › Create › Section (also on the Quick Access Toolbar); choose Building Section, Wall Section or Detail. 2. Click the start point and the end point in a plan, elevation or section. The view looks to the right-hand side of the drawn direction; a flip control reverses it. 3. Drag the width (crop extents) and far clip grips. Cycle and flip controls at the head and tail change which ends show heads. 4. Jogged section: select the section, then use Split Segment on the contextual tab, click a point on the line, and drag the new segment. Only available in plans. 5. Gap display: the line's midpoint control toggles between a continuous line and a line that shows only its ends. 6. Reference section: with Reference other view on the contextual tab, the new section line points to an existing view (for example a typical detail in a drafting view) instead of creating a view.

    UI. Type Selector; contextual tab Modify | Views: Split Segment, Reference other view (with a view picker), Flip; Properties: Crop View, Crop Region Visible, Annotation Crop, Far Clipping, Far Clip Offset, Scope Box, Hide at scales coarser than, Reference Label, Detail Number, Sheet Number, Title on Sheet.

    Behaviour & rules. - Detail-type sections are listed under Detail Views, default to Fine detail level, and hide their section line in views coarser than a type-defined scale. - A jogged section is a single view: its cut is a polyline of segments perpendicular to the view direction, each with its own depth position. The cut at each segment is computed separately, and the jog edges are drawn as boundary lines. - The section head and tail symbols, and the gap display style (Continuous / Gap / Segmented), come from the section type. - Reference labels: reference sections, callouts, elevations and view references carry a Reference Label parameter (for example "SIM", "TYP", "OPP"). The type supplies a default; each instance can override it. Labels can include shared parameters and are edited in place on the canvas. - Moving or rotating the section line regenerates the section view.

    Data (RXD). views/<viewId> of kind view.section (or view.detail for detail sections): origin (section line start), direction, segments (list of offsets and lengths for jogs), width, farClipOffset, headEnd/tailEnd, gapMode, referenceView (reference sections), referenceLabel, hideAtScalesCoarserThan. The marker drawn in other views is generated from this definition and is not stored separately.

    Commands. view.create_section(host_view_id, start, end, section_type_id, width?, far_offset?, reference_view_id?) -> view_id section.split_segment(view_id, point, offset) -> () section.set_gap_mode(view_id, mode) -> () section.flip(view_id) -> () view.set_reference_label(view_id_or_marker_id, label?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Drawing a section across a building creates a section view showing cut walls, floors and roofs, and elevation linework of what lies beyond, up to the far clip. - [ ] Splitting a segment and dragging it 2 m produces one view with a jog line where the two cuts meet. - [ ] A reference section pointing to a drafting view shows that view's detail and sheet numbers in its head.

    5.6 Callouts

    ID: DOC-VIEW-005 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §1.4 · screenshots/documentation/callout_views_detail.png

    Purpose. Enlarged views of part of a parent view.

    Workflow. 1. View tab › Create › Callout ▾ › Rectangle or Sketch. 2. Rectangle: pick two corners in the parent view. Sketch: draw a closed loop and finish. 3. Drag the callout head and its leader to position them. 4. Double-click the callout head (or use Go to View from the context menu) to open the callout view.

    Behaviour & rules. - Detail callout (type of kind Detail): creates a detail view listed under Detail Views. In a plan it has no level association and owns its annotation independently. - View callout (type of the parent's kind, for example floor plan): creates a view of the parent's kind, with its own view range, associated with the parent's level. - Sketch callout: the crop region is the sketched (non-rectangular) loop. - Reference callout: Reference other view points the callout to an existing view. - The callout boundary in the parent and the crop region of the callout view are the same object: editing either updates the other. - New callouts take phase, detail level and template from their type, and default to a scale twice as large as the parent's (for example 1:50 from 1:100). - Callouts can be nested. - In a plan, a detail callout's view can show only annotation (Display Model = Do not display).

    Data (RXD). views/<viewId> of kind view.callout (or view.detail): parent, boundary (polyline in parent view coordinates, shared with the crop), head (point and leader points), referenceView.

    Commands. view.create_callout(parent_view_id, boundary, callout_type_id, reference_view_id?) -> view_id; callout.set_head(view_id, head_point, leader_points[]) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing the callout view's crop region moves the callout boundary in the parent view in the same undo step. - [ ] A sketch callout with an L-shaped loop produces an L-shaped crop.

    5.7 3D views, cameras and section boxes

    Default and orthographic 3D

    ID: DOC-VIEW-006 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §1.5; web: Add Tags and Keynotes in a 3D View

    Purpose. Show the model in 3D for modelling, coordination and presentation.

    Workflow. 1. View tab › Create › 3D View ▾ › Default 3D View (also on the Quick Access Toolbar). If the user's default 3D view exists it opens; otherwise it is created as an isometric view from the south-east. 2. The user navigates with the view cube, navigation bar and mouse (orbit, pan, zoom; Chapter 1). 3. Renaming the default view keeps it; the next Default 3D View command creates a new one.

    Behaviour & rules. - Toggling between parallel and perspective projection is available from the view cube context menu. - Lock / Unlock 3D view (View Control Bar lock menu) locks the camera so that tags, keynotes and text can be placed in the 3D view. Annotation in an unlocked view is disallowed. The menu has three items: - Save Orientation and Lock View stores the current camera as the view's locked orientation and locks it. The user's default 3D view cannot be locked: Reviera asks for a name and saves it as a new named view (save_as_name). If the view already has a saved orientation that differs and contains annotation, Reviera warns that the annotation placed at the old orientation will be deleted, and continues only on confirmation. - Restore Orientation and Lock View returns an unlocked view to its saved orientation and locks it again; annotation placed at that orientation shows again. - Unlock View allows orbiting. The view's annotation is kept but hidden (and excluded from print) until the orientation is restored. - In a locked view, orbit, pan-by-orbit and view cube rotation are refused; pan and zoom remain available. Perspective (camera) views can be locked, but tags and keynotes cannot be placed in them. Material tags, room, area and space tags are not allowed in any 3D view. - New tags in locked 3D views default to a free leader end (DOC-ANN-010). - Orient to view / direction: aligns the 3D camera to a plan, elevation or section, and sets the section box to that view's extents. - 3D views can be placed on sheets.

    Data (RXD). camera block of a view.3d payload: eye, target, up (model coordinates, metres), perspective, fieldOfView (horizontal, radians), parallelScale, locked, and lockedCamera (the saved orientation: eye, target, up, parallelScale; null until first locked).

    Commands. view.create_3d(kind: default|named, name?) -> view_id view.set_camera(view_id, eye, target, up, projection?: orthographic|perspective, fov?) -> () view.lock_3d(view_id, locked, save_as_name?) -> view_id (locked = true is Save Orientation and Lock View; it returns the new view's id when save_as_name is used on the default 3D view; locked = false is Unlock View) view.restore_orientation(view_id) -> () (Restore Orientation and Lock View; fails with view.no_saved_orientation when the view was never locked) view.orient_to(view_id, source_view_id_or_direction) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Two users in BIMserver mode each get a separate default 3D view; orbiting one does not change the other. - [ ] Placing a tag in an unlocked 3D view is refused with a prompt to lock the view. - [ ] Unlocking a locked view with five tags, orbiting, then Restore Orientation and Lock View shows the five tags again at their places. - [ ] Save Orientation and Lock View on the default 3D view asks for a name and creates a new locked view; the default view stays unlocked.

    Cameras and walkthroughs

    ID: DOC-VIEW-007 · Priority: P1 (camera), P2 (walkthrough) · Ref: research/04 §1.5 Camera, Walkthrough

    Purpose. Perspective views from a chosen eye point, and animated paths through the model.

    Workflow. 1. Camera: View tab › 3D View ▾ › Camera; click the eye position in a plan, then the target. 2. Properties: Eye Elevation, Target Elevation, Perspective, Far Clip. Size Crop sets the field of view as width and height (scaling proportionally if requested). Uncropped perspective views are allowed. 3. Walkthrough: 3D View ▾ › Walkthrough; click key-frame positions along a path in a plan; Finish. 4. Edit Walkthrough on the contextual tab: choose the active key frame, move camera and target, play, step frames. The frames dialog sets total frames, frames per second, total time, and uniform speed or per-key-frame timing.

    Behaviour & rules. - The camera's field of view is derived from the crop size and the camera distance; changing either keeps the other consistent. - A walkthrough is a spline path through the key frames; the camera interpolates position and target along it (Catmull–Rom by default). - Exporting a walkthrough is covered by DOC-OUT-012.

    Data (RXD). Camera: camera block as in DOC-VIEW-006 on a view.camera payload, plus cropSize. Walkthrough: view.walkthrough payload with keyframes[] (eye, target, time), totalFrames, fps, uniformSpeed.

    Commands. view.create_camera(host_view_id, eye, target, eye_elevation?, target_elevation?) -> view_id view.size_crop(view_id, width, height, proportional?) -> () view.create_walkthrough(host_view_id, keyframes[]) -> view_id walkthrough.set_keyframe(view_id, index, eye?, target?, time?) -> () walkthrough.set_timing(view_id, total_frames, fps, uniform_speed?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A camera placed in a plan opens a perspective view whose eye is at the clicked point and default eye elevation (1750 mm above the plan's level). - [ ] A five-key-frame walkthrough plays back at the set frame rate in the viewport.

    Section box

    ID: DOC-VIEW-008 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §1.5 Section Box · screenshots/documentation/3d_view_section_box.png

    Purpose. Clip a 3D view to a box.

    Workflow. 1. Properties › Extents › Section Box ✓ shows a box around the model. 2. Selecting the box shows six face grips and a rotation grip; dragging them clips the view in real time. 3. Selection Box (default shortcut BX): with elements selected, fits a section box tightly around them in the active 3D view, or in the user's default 3D view when the active view is not 3D.

    Behaviour & rules. - The box is an oriented box (a transform plus extents). The GPU viewport clips with six clip planes and fills cut faces with caps (DOC-HLR-006); hidden-line output cuts solids with OCCT and draws section poché on the cut faces when the view's Show cut faces property is on (default on). - The box outline is an annotation category (Section Boxes) that can be hidden; when hidden, it can still be selected by Tab or by the Properties checkbox. - Turning the box off keeps its last extents for when it is turned on again.

    Data (RXD). sectionBox block of a view.3d payload: enabled, transform (4×3 matrix), min, max, showCutFaces.

    Commands. view.set_section_box(view_id, enabled, transform?, min?, max?) -> () view.fit_section_box(element_ids[], view_id?, margin?) -> view_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Dragging a face grip updates the viewport at interactive frame rates (at least 30 fps on the reference model, Chapter 1 performance targets). - [ ] Selection Box on one room's furniture produces a box that contains all of it with the default margin (300 mm).

    Blueprint mode (3D slice to 2D drawing)

    ID: DOC-VIEW-013 · Priority: P1 · Ref: owner requirement (2026-10-12); builds on DOC-VIEW-002, DOC-VR-001, DOC-VIEW-008 and §5.12

    Purpose. Go from the 3D model to a conventional 2D drawing in one step. The user slices the model where they want to look, and Reviera turns the slice into the drawing an architect would draw there: a horizontal slice through a storey becomes a floor plan, and a vertical slice becomes a section. The transition is continuous, so the user can see how the drawing comes out of the model.

    Workflow. 1. In any 3D view the user turns on Blueprint mode: View Control Bar › Blueprint, or the default shortcut BP. 2. Reviera proposes a slice: - Horizontal (default): at the cut-plane height of the level nearest the camera target (the level's default view range, DOC-VR-001). - Vertical: when the camera looks more horizontal than down (pitch below 30°), at the section box face or the plane through the camera target facing the camera.

    The slice plane shows as a translucent plane with a grip. Dragging the grip moves the cut, Tab cycles horizontal and vertical, and clicking a level in the Project Browser snaps the cut to that level's cut plane. 3. The user confirms with Enter or by clicking Convert to drawing. The camera animates (about 0.6 s) to orthographic, looking straight at the slice: down onto a horizontal slice, or along the normal of a vertical one. The model above (or in front of) the cut is removed, and the graphics change to drawing conventions: - cut elements show cut patterns (poché) and cut line weights; - elements below the cut, within the view depth, show in projection; - elements beyond the view depth are hidden, or shown as underlay as the view range says; - hidden lines are removed (Hidden Line style, §5.12). 4. While in Blueprint mode the view behaves as a plan (or section) view: - annotation tools are available: dimensions, tags and text; - modelling tools work on the slice plane (the level's work plane for horizontal slices). 5. Exit (Esc, or the View Control Bar toggle) animates back to the previous 3D camera. 6. Save as view creates a real plan view (DOC-VIEW-002), or a section (DOC-VIEW-004), with the slice's level, view range or section line. Annotation placed during the session moves to the new view. Without saving, annotation placed in Blueprint mode stays with the 3D view's blueprint state (see Data).

    Behaviour & rules. - Drawing equivalence. A horizontal blueprint of a level, with the level's default view range, produces the same draw list (§5.12) as a new floor plan of that level with the default plan view template. The draw list includes linework, cut patterns, line weights, hidden-line results and which categories show. The acceptance criteria compare the two. - Slice choice. - A horizontal slice uses the level's view range: cut plane, top, bottom and view depth. The slice grip moves the cut plane only, and the other planes keep their offsets. - A vertical slice uses a section-like range: far clip at the section box, or the model extents. - Presentation style. The drawing uses the view's graphics (object styles, overrides and filters) in black on white by default. An optional Blueprint colour scheme draws white and cyan linework on a blueprint-blue background. It is a display setting for the view; printing and export use the normal print colours unless the user chooses otherwise. - Live model. - Edits made while in Blueprint mode regenerate the drawing at once: the GPU-assisted hidden-line path on screen, and the exact OCCT pipeline when printing. - Undoing past the moment Blueprint mode was entered does not leave the mode. - Navigation in the drawing. - Orbit is disabled. Pan and zoom work as in plan views. - Orbiting with the mouse, or clicking the ViewCube, offers to exit Blueprint mode. - Performance. Converting the reference model's typical storey to a drawing takes under 1 s on the reference hardware (Chapter 1 targets), animation included. Moving the slice grip updates the cut at interactive rates, at least 20 fps, using GPU clip planes and caps (DOC-HLR-006) before the exact drawing is computed when the grip is released.

    Data (RXD). blueprint block of a view.3d payload: - enabled - slice: {kind: horizontal, level_id, cut_offset} or {kind: vertical, origin, normal} - range (the view range used) - colourScheme: default or blueprint - savedCamera (the camera to return to) - annotations[] (ids of annotation placed in blueprint mode and not yet moved to a saved view)

    Commands. view.blueprint(view_id, on: bool, slice?: {kind, level_id?, cut_offset?, origin?, normal?}) -> () view.blueprint_set_slice(view_id, slice) -> () view.blueprint_save_as_view(view_id, name?) -> view_id view.blueprint_set_colour_scheme(view_id, scheme: default|blueprint) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] In the default 3D view of a two-storey model, Blueprint mode on the ground floor shows a floor plan whose draw list equals that of a new floor plan of that level with the same view range: same linework and cut patterns, within drawing tolerance. - [ ] Dragging the slice grip from 1200 mm to 900 mm above the level updates the cut at 20 fps or more, and on release the drawing shows windows with sills above 900 mm in projection rather than cut. - [ ] Save as view creates a plan named after the level. Two dimensions placed in Blueprint mode appear in the new plan and no longer in the 3D view. - [ ] Esc returns to the exact previous 3D camera (eye, target and projection). - [ ] With a section box enabled and a horizontal camera, Blueprint mode proposes a vertical slice on the box face nearest the camera, and the drawing matches a section through the same plane. - [ ] view.blueprint from Lua and MCP turns the mode on and off with the same result as the UI.

    Displaced elements (exploded views)

    ID: DOC-VIEW-012 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/04 §3.1 (modal display modes: Highlight Displacement); web: About Displacement Sets, About Displacement Set Paths, Create a Displacement Set, Edit a Displacement Set, Create Displacement Set Paths, Modify Displacement Set Path Style and Display, Reset a Displacement Set, Highlight Displacement Sets

    Purpose. Pull elements away from their true position in one view only, to make exploded axonometrics and assembly diagrams, and draw paths back to where they belong. The model is never moved.

    Workflow. 1. In a 3D view (orthographic or perspective), plan, section or elevation, select one or more model elements and choose Modify › View › Displace Elements. The selection becomes a displacement set with a drag gizmo of three arrows along the view's model X, Y and Z axes. 2. Drag an arrow, or type Displacement X/Y/Z in the Properties palette, to move the set. 3. To refine the set: select it, choose Edit on the Modify | Displacement Set tab, then Add to displacement or Remove from displacement and pick elements; Finish or Cancel. 4. To explode part of a set further, Tab-select an element inside a set and choose Displace Elements again: this creates a nested set whose offset is relative to its parent. 5. Path: hover an edge or vertex of a displaced element; a preview line shows the route back to the original position; click to place the path. 6. Reset returns the selected set (and its nested sets) to the true position and deletes them with their paths. 7. View Control Bar › Highlight Displacement Sets colours each set distinctly while the toggle is on.

    UI. Modify | Displacement Set contextual tab: Edit, Path, Reset. Edit mode panel: Add to displacement, Remove from displacement, Finish, Cancel. Properties of a set: Displacement X, Y, Z (length), Name. Properties of a path: Style (Straight or Jogged), Line style override. View Control Bar toggle: Highlight Displacement Sets (session state).

    Behaviour & rules. - Only model elements can be displaced. Annotation, view-owned drafting, datums (levels, grids, reference planes), rooms and links as a whole cannot; the command reports which picked items were skipped. Elements of a linked model can be displaced individually. - Each element belongs to at most one set per view (the innermost set when nested). Adding an element that is in another set moves it. - A displacement is a pure per-view translation applied after the model is evaluated and before stage 1 of the drawing pipeline (DOC-HLR-001). Constraints, joins, hosting and schedules ignore it, and so do other views. A hosted element (door, window) displaced without its host keeps its host's opening cut in the host; displacing the host alone leaves the inserts in place. - In 2D views the offset component along the view direction is kept but has no visible effect, except that it changes which zone of the view range (DOC-VR-002) the displaced geometry falls in; classification, cutting and hidden-line removal all use the displaced geometry. - Annotation on displaced elements. Tags, keynotes and spot dimensions may be placed on displaced elements and follow the displaced position. Dimensions cannot reference displaced elements (refused with dim.displaced_reference), because the measured distance would be false. Temporary dimensions are not shown for displaced elements. - Paths are view-owned annotation of category Displacement Path. A path joins a point on a displaced edge or vertex to the same point at its true position. Straight is one segment; Jogged follows the set's offset axes one after another (X, then Y, then Z, skipping zero components). Paths update when the set moves and are deleted when their element leaves the set. Line weight, colour and pattern come from the Displacement Path object style, overridable per view (DOC-GFX-003) and per path. - Highlight mode draws every set in its own colour from a distinct palette, halftones everything else, and frames the view in the highlight colour. It is session state: not saved, not printed (DOC-CORE-006). - Deleting an element removes it from its set; an empty set is deleted. Duplicating a view with detailing (DOC-VIEW-011) copies its displacement sets; plain duplicate does not. Dependent views share the parent's sets. - Displacement sets are part of the view definition, so they are not controlled by view templates. - Interactive tool. The set edit mode follows Conventions §2.1: its micro-operations are disp.add(element), disp.remove(element), disp.offset(vector) and disp.path(edge_ref, style), each logged with the set id; the replay function re-applies them to the set's state at the start of the session, so an interrupted edit is recovered after a crash (Chapter 2b, DM-LIVE-015).

    Data (RXD). View payload block displacementSets[], each with id, name, parent (optional), members[] (ifc: or link: references) and offset (a 3-vector in model coordinates, metres). Paths are annotation objects of kind anno.displacementpath in views/annotation/<viewId>: set, ref (edge or vertex sub-reference plus parameter), style (straight | jogged), lineStyle. Nothing is written to IFC; IFC annotation export (DOC-IFC-002) writes paths as IfcAnnotation curves with ObjectType = 'DISPLACEMENT_PATH' and displaced linework in the drawing linework.

    Commands. view.displace_elements(view_id, element_ids[], offset, displacement_set_id?) -> displacement_set_id (with displacement_set_id, the new set is nested in that set and offset is relative to it) displacement.edit(displacement_set_id, add_ids[], remove_ids[]) -> () displacement.set_offset(displacement_set_id, offset) -> () displacement.add_path(displacement_set_id, edge_ref, style?: straight|jogged) -> annotation_id displacement.set_path_style(annotation_ids[], style: straight|jogged, line_style_id?) -> () displacement.reset(displacement_set_ids[]) -> () view.highlight_displacement(view_id, on) -> () (session state, not undoable)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Displacing a roof 3 m upwards in an axonometric moves it in that view only; the plan, the roof's schedule row and its IFC placement are unchanged. - [ ] A nested set inside a displaced set moves with its parent and keeps its own relative offset. - [ ] A jogged path from a displaced beam corner follows the X, then Z offsets and redraws when the set moves. - [ ] Creating a dimension to a displaced element is refused with dim.displaced_reference; tagging it is allowed and the tag follows it. - [ ] Reset returns all members to their true positions, deletes the set and its paths, and is undone in one step. - [ ] Highlight mode never appears in a PDF export.

    5.8 Drafting views

    ID: DOC-VIEW-009 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §1.6; web: Insert a Drafting View from Another Project, Reuse Views and Sheets in Other Projects, Insert Detail Components from a Saved Detail View

    Purpose. 2D views with no model behind them, for standard details and diagrams.

    Workflow. 1. View tab › Create › Drafting View; enter a name and scale. 2. Draw with detail lines, regions, detail components, text, dimensions, symbols, and imported or linked CAD (Chapter 6). 3. Reference the view from sections and callouts (DOC-VIEW-004, DOC-VIEW-005). 4. Insert › Insert from File › Views from File copies drafting views from another IFC project; Save to Library › Views writes selected drafting views into a new IFC file containing only those views and the types they use.

    Behaviour & rules. - Dimensions in drafting views reference 2D geometry only. - When drafting views are inserted, conflicting type names are resolved by the duplicate-type dialog (Chapter 2). - Insert Views from File (Insert › Import › Insert from File ▾ › Insert Views from File, view.insert_from_file): after a file is chosen, the Insert Views dialog lists the source's insertable views with a kind filter (All, Drafting views, Schedules, Legends, Renderings, Sheets) and a preview. Insertable kinds are drafting views, schedules (definitions only; rows come from this project's model), legends, rendering views and sheets whose viewports hold only drafting views, legends, schedules or renderings. Model views (plans, sections, 3D) are not offered, because their content is the source model. Inserted views keep their names; a clash adds a numeric suffix (Detail 1 (2)). Types and styles the views use (text, dimension, region, line and fill pattern, detail component families) are copied when missing; when a type of the same name exists, the current project's definition is kept and the insert report lists every such case. - Insert 2D Elements from File (Insert from File ▾ › Insert 2D Elements from File, detail.insert_from_file): copies the view-owned elements (detail lines, filled and masking regions, detail components, repeating details, insulation, text, symbols, dimensions between copied elements) from one source view into the active view, as a group of new objects that the user positions with the cursor (or at position), then Finish. The result is selected so it can be moved at once. Model geometry is never copied. Elements that cannot be copied are skipped and listed: cut profiles (DOC-GFX-020), elements that create other views (callouts, sections), and annotation that references model elements (tags, keynotes, dimensions to model geometry), since their hosts do not exist in the target. - Sources can be any IFC file with Reviera RXD, including library files written by Save to Library and projects opened read-only by another user. Sources without RXD offer nothing and say why. In BIMserver mode, a source may also be a BIMserver project revision (Chapter 6). - Insertion is one undo step and assigns new ids to everything inserted; nothing keeps a link to the source.

    Data (RXD). views/<viewId> of kind view.drafting; its contents live in views/annotation/<viewId>. A library file written by Save to Library is an IFC file containing only the RXD for those views and the styles and types they use. Inserted objects record ext.insertedFrom (source file name and source object id) for traceability only.

    Commands. view.create_drafting(name, scale) -> view_id; view.insert_from_file(path, view_names[]?) -> view_id[] (with no view_names, the dialog opens; from Lua and MCP, view_names is required); view.save_to_library(view_ids[], path) -> (); detail.insert_from_file(path, source_view_name, target_view_id, position?) -> annotation_id[] (fails with view.kind_mismatch when the target is a 3D or schedule view).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A drafting view saved to a library file and inserted into another project reproduces its contents and line styles. - [ ] Inserting a drafting view whose text type "2.5 mm Arial" also exists in the target keeps the target's definition and lists the clash in the report. - [ ] Inserting 2D elements from a source detail view copies its regions, lines and text into the active section, skips its tags, and reports how many items were skipped. - [ ] A sheet holding only drafting views is offered in Insert Views; a sheet holding a floor plan is not.

    5.9 Legends and keynote legends

    ID: DOC-VIEW-010 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §1.7 · screenshots/documentation/keynote_legend_detail.png

    Purpose. Keys that explain the drawing: symbol legends built from real types, and lists of keynotes used.

    Workflow. 1. View tab › Legends ▾ › Legend: name and scale. 2. Annotate › Component ▾ › Legend Component: choose a family type, a view direction (plan, front elevation, back elevation, section where the type supports it), a detail level, and for hosted or linear types a host length. 3. Add text, detail lines, symbols and regions as needed. 4. Keynote Legend: View tab › Legends ▾ › Keynote Legend; set name, then fields (Key Value, Keynote Text) through the schedule properties (§5.14).

    Behaviour & rules. - A legend component draws the type's geometry, not a model element; editing the type updates every legend component of it. Legend components do not appear in schedules or counts. - Legends and keynote legends can be placed on many sheets (DOC-CORE-005). - A keynote legend lists the keynotes used in the project. With Filter by sheet, each placed instance lists only keynotes visible on its own sheet.

    Data (RXD). Legend: view.legend; legend components are annotation objects of kind anno.legendcomponent (type = ifc: reference to the family type object, direction, detailLevel, hostLength). Keynote legend: schedules/<scheduleId> of kind schedule.keynotelegend.

    Commands. view.create_legend(name, scale) -> view_id legend.place_component(view_id, type_id, direction, detail_level?, host_length?, point) -> element_id view.create_keynote_legend(name, fields[]?, filter_by_sheet?) -> schedule_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing a wall type's layer thickness updates its legend component. - [ ] A keynote legend with Filter by sheet placed on two sheets lists different rows matching each sheet's keynotes.

    5.10 Duplicating views and dependent views

    ID: DOC-VIEW-011 · Priority: P0 (Duplicate, With Detailing), P1 (Dependent) · Ref: research/04 §1.8

    Purpose. Reuse a view's set-up for another purpose, or split a large view across several sheets.

    Workflow. Project Browser › right-click a view › Duplicate View ▸ Duplicate / Duplicate with Detailing / Duplicate as Dependent; or View tab › Create › Duplicate View ▾.

    Behaviour & rules.

    Mode Copies view definition (extents, graphics, template) View-owned annotation Relationship afterwards
    Duplicate Yes Not copied Independent
    Duplicate with Detailing Yes Copied as new, independent elements (new GlobalIds) Independent
    Duplicate as Dependent Yes Shared with the parent and all siblings: an annotation placed in any of them belongs to the parent and is visible in all whose crop shows it Child of the parent; listed under it in the browser
    • A dependent view has its own crop region (and may follow a scope box) but takes scale, template, view range, detail level, visibility settings and phase from its parent. Those properties are read-only in the dependent.
    • Convert to independent view breaks the link: the dependent becomes an independent view and receives copies of the shared annotation that its crop shows.
    • Deleting a parent requires deleting or converting its dependents first; the dialog offers both.
    • Duplicate names follow the pattern <name> Copy n or, for dependents, <name> - Dependent n.

    Data (RXD). Dependent views: view payload parent with dependency = "dependent". Shared annotation is stored once, in the parent view's annotation document.

    Commands. view.duplicate(view_id, mode: plain|with_detailing|dependent, name?) -> view_id; view.convert_to_independent(view_id) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Duplicating with detailing yields annotation with new GlobalIds; moving a copied tag does not move the original. - [ ] A text note added in dependent view A appears in dependent view B when B's crop contains it, and in the parent. - [ ] Converting a dependent to independent leaves it with copies of the annotation inside its crop, and later edits to the parent's annotation no longer affect it.

    5.11 Graphics control

    The graphics override precedence model

    ID: DOC-GFX-001 · Priority: P0 (layers 0–1, 3, 6), P1 (layers 2, 4–5) · Ref: research/04 §3.1, §11 Key behaviours 5–6

    Purpose. Define one deterministic function that decides whether, and how, each element (and each sub-part of it) is drawn in a view. Every graphics feature in this chapter is a layer of this function.

    Behaviour & rules.

    The resolved appearance of an element in a view is a record of independent graphic attributes:

    Attribute Applies to
    visible whole element, or sub-category geometry
    projection_line = {pattern, colour, weight} edges seen in projection
    surface_pattern_fg / surface_pattern_bg = {visible, pattern, colour} projected faces
    surface_transparency (0–100 %) projected faces
    cut_line = {pattern, colour, weight} cut boundaries
    cut_pattern_fg / cut_pattern_bg = {visible, pattern, colour} cut faces
    halftone (boolean) all of the above
    detail_level which family/compound geometry is used

    Each attribute value can be set or unset ("by layer below"). The resolver walks the layers from lowest to highest. For each attribute, the highest layer that sets it wins. Three attributes combine differently: - visible: an element is drawn only if no layer hides it (logical AND), except that layer 6c (Reveal hidden) can show hidden elements in its highlight colour. - halftone: an element is halftone if any layer sets halftone (logical OR). - surface_transparency: highest layer that sets it wins, but a phase or design-option override that applies transparency is combined multiplicatively with it.

    Layers (lowest to highest):

    # Layer Scope Source
    0a Object styles project, per category and sub-category DOC-GFX-002
    0b Material graphics project, per material: surface and cut patterns, shading colour Chapter 2 materials
    0c Family geometry settings per family: sub-category assignment, visibility by detail level and by view direction Chapter 2 families
    1 View category overrides (including discipline profile, DOC-GFX-016) per view, or the view's template DOC-GFX-003
    2 View filters, in list order (the filter listed first wins conflicts) per view or template DOC-GFX-006
    3 Element overrides and per-edge linework per view, per element DOC-GFX-007
    4 Phase status graphics (via the view's phase filter) per view DOC-GFX-017
    5 Design option display, link display settings, workset visibility per view DOC-GFX-018, Chapter 6
    6a Worksharing display colours (when on) per view, temporary Chapter 6 COL-WS-004
    6b Temporary hide/isolate, isolate annotations per view, temporary DOC-GFX-008
    6c Reveal hidden per view, temporary DOC-GFX-008
    7 View-wide modifiers: Display Model = Halftone, underlay, halftone/underlay settings, visual style and graphic display options per view DOC-GFX-009, DOC-GFX-011, DOC-GFX-012

    Further rules: - Templates. When a view has an assigned template, every property included in the template is read from the template instead of the view. That includes the layer 1 and layer 2 tables when V/G overrides and Filters are included. The view's own values are kept, hidden, and become effective again if the template is removed or the property is excluded. - Linked models. Elements of linked models enter the resolver with the host's layers or the link's own layers, according to the link's display setting (Chapter 6, COL-LNK-007). - Sub-category geometry. Each piece of family geometry carries its sub-category, and the resolver runs per (element, sub-category) pair. - Phase "Not displayed" (layer 4) and design option not shown (layer 5) set visible = false. - The resolver is a pure function of (element state, view definition, project standards). Results are cached per view, keyed by element revision and view-definition revision, and recomputed in parallel (rayon) when invalidated.

    UI. The Graphics Inspector (context menu › Why does this look like this?) shows, for the picked element, each layer's contribution to each attribute and which layer won. This is a Reviera addition with no counterpart in the reference.

    Data (RXD). Layers 0a–0c are project and family data: RXD standards/object_styles, IFC materials plus their RXD graphics (Chapter 2), and family recipes. Layers 1–3 are the view payload blocks categoryOverrides (keyed by category and sub-category), filterOverrides (ordered list keyed by filter id) and elementOverrides / linework (keyed by GlobalId or GlobalId plus edge sub-reference). Because each entry has its own key, two users can change different overrides in one view and the three-way merge keeps both. Layer 6 is session state and is not saved; Apply hide/isolate to view writes layer 3 entries.

    Commands. graphics.explain(view_id, element_id, subcategory?) -> layer_trace (query); graphics.resolve(view_id, element_ids[]) -> resolved_attributes[] (query).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Object style sets wall projection lines to weight 3; a category override sets weight 5; a filter matching exterior walls sets weight 7; an element override on one wall sets weight 2. The resolved weights are 2 for that wall, 7 for other exterior walls, and 5 for interior walls. - [ ] Two filters both set colour; swapping their order swaps the result. - [ ] Hiding a category in the view and also setting an element override with visible = true leaves the element hidden (AND rule). - [ ] graphics.explain returns the same winning layer for every attribute as the drawing shows, for every element in the 50 test cases of the graphics conformance suite.

    Object styles

    ID: DOC-GFX-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §3.1 (1)

    Purpose. Project-wide default appearance per category and sub-category.

    Workflow. Manage tab › Settings › Object Styles opens a dialog with tabs Model Objects, Annotation Objects, Analytical Model Objects, Imported Objects. The user edits projection and cut line weight, line colour, line pattern and default material per row, and creates or deletes user sub-categories.

    Behaviour & rules. - Cut line weight is offered only for cuttable categories. - Imported-object rows are created automatically for each layer of an imported or linked CAD file (Chapter 6) and can be edited like other sub-categories. - Deleting a sub-category moves its geometry to the parent category after confirmation.

    Data (RXD). RXD document standards/object_styles, kind objectstyle, one object per (category, sub-category): projectionPen, cutPen, colour, linePattern, material, plus the view-range attributes of DOC-VR-002. On IFC export with Include presentation layers, each styled category is also written as an IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle (name = category or sub-category; styles = IfcCurveStyle and IfcFillAreaStyle) assigned to its elements' representation items.

    Commands. objectstyle.set(category, subcategory?, projection_weight?, cut_weight?, colour?, line_pattern_id?, material_id?) -> (); objectstyle.create_subcategory(category, name) -> subcategory_id; objectstyle.delete_subcategory(category, name) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing the Doors projection line weight changes every door in every view that has no override. - [ ] An exported IFC opened in another viewer shows doors on a presentation layer named "Doors".

    Visibility/Graphics dialog (view category overrides)

    ID: DOC-GFX-003 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §3.3 · screenshots/documentation/visibility_graphics_dialog_model_categories.png

    Purpose. Per-view visibility and appearance by category, filter, link, workset, design option, imported file and point cloud.

    Workflow. 1. View tab › Graphics › Visibility/Graphics (default shortcut VG or VV), or Properties › Visibility/Graphics › Edit. 2. The dialog title names the view. Tabs: Model Categories, Annotation Categories, Analytical Model Categories, Imported Categories, Filters, Links, Worksets (when worksets exist), Design Options (when options exist), Point Clouds (when clouds are linked), Coordination Models (when present). 3. In the category tabs, each row (category, expandable to sub-categories) has: Visible checkbox; Projection/Surface – Lines, Patterns, Transparency; Cut – Lines, Patterns; Halftone; Detail Level (By View / Coarse / Medium / Fine). 4. Clicking a cell opens the override editor for that attribute (line: pattern, colour, weight 1–16; pattern: foreground visible/pattern/colour and background visible/pattern/colour; transparency 0–100 %). 5. Footer controls: master Show categories in this view toggle, discipline filter, name search, All / None / Invert / Expand All, Override Host Layers (cut line styles per compound-layer function), Object Styles…, Edit…, Reset.

    Behaviour & rules. - If an assigned template controls a tab, that tab is read-only and a banner names the template. - Changes preview live in the view while the dialog is open; Cancel reverts. - Override Host Layers: for walls, floors, roofs and ceilings, the user can set the cut line style for each compound-layer function (Structure, Substrate, Thermal/Air, Finish 1, Finish 2, Membrane), and choose whether the outer boundary uses the category's cut line. - The Annotation Categories tab covers dimensions, grids, levels, sections, elevations, callouts, tags, text, scope boxes, section boxes, crop boundaries, reference planes, matchlines, revision clouds, plan regions and so on.

    Data (RXD). View payload categoryOverrides: per category and sub-category, visible, projectionLine, surfaceFg, surfaceBg, transparency, cutLine, cutFg, cutBg, halftone, detailLevel; and hostLayerCutStyles (per compound-layer function).

    Commands. view.set_category_visibility(view_id, categories[], visible) -> () view.set_category_override(view_id, category, subcategory?, override) -> () view.clear_category_override(view_id, category, subcategory?) -> () view.set_host_layer_cut_styles(view_id, function_styles{}) -> () view.visibility_graphics(view_id? (default: active)) -> () opens the dialog described above for the view (or for a template, when given a template id). The dialog is a UI entry point (DOC-CORE-007): OK applies all changed rows through the commands above as one undo step named "Visibility/Graphics"; Apply does the same and keeps the dialog open; Cancel discards. Validation: line weights 1–16, transparency 0–100 %, pattern ids must exist; an invalid cell is outlined and OK is disabled until it is fixed. A row controlled by the view's template, or a view that is a dependent, shows read-only rows with the reason.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Hiding Furniture in a plan hides every furniture element in that plan and nowhere else. - [ ] Setting a red cut pattern on Walls in a view applies to walls without a filter or element override. - [ ] When a template controls Model Categories, the tab is read-only and view.set_category_override on that view returns view.template_controlled.

    View templates

    ID: DOC-GFX-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §3.2

    Purpose. Standardise view settings across many views and keep them in step.

    Workflow. 1. View tab › Graphics › View Templates ▾ › Create Template from Current View / Apply Template Properties to Current View / Manage View Templates. 2. Manage dialog: list of templates (filter by view kind), property list with value and Include checkbox per property, Duplicate, Rename, Delete, Views using this template list. 3. To bind a view: Properties › View Template › pick a template (assign). To stamp once: Apply Template Properties (apply).

    Behaviour & rules. - Apply copies the included property values into the view once; there is no lasting link. - Assign creates a lasting link: included properties become read-only in the view and follow template edits immediately. - Templates have a view kind group: plans (floor, structural, area), ceiling plans, sections/elevations/details, 3D, drafting, schedules, walkthroughs, renderings. A template can be assigned only to views of a compatible kind. - Template-controllable properties: Scale, Display Model, Detail Level, Parts Visibility, V/G Model, V/G Annotation, V/G Analytical, V/G Imported, Filters, Links, Worksets, Design Options, Model Display (visual style), Shadows, Sketchy Lines, Lighting, Photographic Exposure, Background, Far Clipping, Phase, Phase Filter, Discipline, Show Hidden Lines, Colour Scheme Location, Colour Schemes, Depth Clipping, View Range, Orientation, Underlay Orientation, Section Box (3D), Schedule appearance (schedules). Crop and annotation crop are never template properties. - The view family type can name a template for new views and whether new views are bound to it. - Deleting a template used by views asks for a replacement or None; with None, views keep the values they had. - Templates can be copied between projects (DOC-MNT link: Chapter 6, COL-MNT-005 Transfer standards).

    Data (RXD). RXD document views/templates, kind view.template: appliesTo (view kind group), included (list of controlled property names), and the same payload blocks as a view for the included properties. The binding is the view's template field; a template keeps no list of its views (the list is computed), so assigning views never edits the template object.

    Commands. template.create_from_view(view_id, name) -> template_id template.apply(view_ids[], template_id) -> () template.assign(view_ids[], template_id?) -> () template.set_include(template_id, property, included) -> () template.set_property(template_id, name, value) -> () template.delete(template_id, replacement_id?) -> () template.manage() -> () opens the View Templates dialog: on the left, the template list with a kind filter (Show type: all, plans, ceiling plans, sections and elevations, 3D, drafting, schedules, walkthroughs, renderings) and a name search; at the bottom, Duplicate, Rename and Delete; in the centre, the property table (Parameter, Value, Include) of the selected template, where each value opens the same editor as in the view (for example Edit… for V/G and View Range); on the right, Views using this template (computed, with Open and Assign to selection). Validation: names must be unique among templates of the same kind group; values follow the rules of the corresponding view property (for example the view range ordering of DOC-VR-001); Delete of a template in use asks for a replacement or None. Changes are applied as one undo step on OK.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing the scale in a template changes the scale of every view assigned to it, in one undo step. - [ ] Unticking Include for Detail Level makes Detail Level editable in assigned views while other properties remain locked. - [ ] Assigning a 3D template to a plan is rejected.

    Temporary view properties

    ID: DOC-GFX-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §3.2 Temporary View Properties

    Purpose. Try out a template or change settings temporarily without altering the saved view.

    Workflow. 1. View Control Bar › Temporary View Properties ▾ › Enable Temporary View Properties, or Temporarily Apply Template Properties (a dialog lists templates compatible with the view's kind, with a preview of the properties each controls). 2. The user changes view properties, graphics overrides or filters as usual; the changes show at once. 3. Restore View Properties ends the mode and puts back the saved values.

    UI. View Control Bar menu (three items above). While the mode is on, the view has a coloured frame (default purple) and a label "Temporary View Properties" in its top-left corner. The Properties palette shows the temporary values with a marker.

    Behaviour & rules. - Reviera takes a snapshot of the view definition (every property, categoryOverrides, filterOverrides, elementOverrides, crop, view range) when the mode starts. Edits in the mode change a session copy; Restore discards the copy. - The edits are not undoable steps of the model, and they do not mark the project as changed. Undo inside the mode works on the session copy only. - If the view has an assigned template, Temporarily Apply Template Properties overrides the assigned template's included properties for the session; the assignment itself does not change. - Printing and export use the saved properties unless the user explicitly chooses As displayed in the output dialog. - Temporary state is per session, per view and per user: it is not saved, not sent to BIMserver, and is lost when the view is closed or the project is closed. Closing the view asks whether to Keep as view properties (applies the session copy through normal commands, one undo step) or discard it. - The mode is refused on dependent views whose properties come from the parent (DOC-VIEW-011), with a message naming the parent.

    Data. None; session state only (DOC-CORE-008).

    Commands. view.temporary_properties(view_id, mode: enable|apply_template|restore, template_id?) -> (). Keeping the temporary state as the view's properties uses view.set_property, view.set_category_override and the other per-view commands, grouped as one undo step.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] After temporarily applying a template and restoring, every view property equals its value before. - [ ] Changing the scale while the mode is on does not mark the project as modified, and a PDF export (not As displayed) uses the saved scale. - [ ] Closing the view with Keep as view properties creates one undo step that, when undone, restores the saved values.

    View filters

    ID: DOC-GFX-006 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §3.4; web: Filters Dialog · screenshots/documentation/view_filter_rules_nested_sets.png

    Purpose. Override graphics or hide elements by rule or by saved selection.

    Workflow. 1. View tab › Graphics › Filters opens the filter manager: list of filters, categories pane, rules pane. 2. Rule-based filter: choose categories; build rules parameter · operator · value grouped in nested sets, each set being All rules true (AND) or Any rule true (OR); Add Rule, Add Set, Delete. 3. Selection filter: select elements, then Modify › Selection › Save; edit later with Edit Selection (add/remove mode). 4. In the view's graphics dialog, Filters tab: Add, Remove, Up, Down; per row Enable, Visible, and the same override columns as categories.

    Behaviour & rules. - Operators: equals, does not equal, greater than, greater than or equal, less than, less than or equal, contains, does not contain, begins with, does not begin with, ends with, does not end with, has a value, has no value. Numeric comparisons are unit-aware and use a tolerance of half the display precision. - The parameter list offers parameters common to all chosen categories, including shared and project parameters, plus the pseudo-parameters Workset, Phase Created, Phase Demolished, Design Option, Sheet Collection, IFC Class and IFC PredefinedType. - Filters apply to linked elements when the link is displayed By host view or custom with host filters (Chapter 6). - Filter order in a view decides conflicts (first listed wins), as specified in DOC-GFX-001. - A filter definition is project data; applying it to a view stores only the view-specific overrides. - Rule evaluation is compiled once per filter into a predicate and run in parallel over candidate elements.

    Data (RXD). RXD document views/filters: kind filter.rule (categories, ruleTree of nested {op: and|or, children} and {parameter, operator, value, unit} nodes) and kind filter.selection (members: list of ifc: references). Per-view application is the view's filterOverrides list (DOC-GFX-001).

    Commands. filter.create_rule(name, categories[], rule_tree) -> filter_id filter.update_rule(filter_id, categories?, rule_tree?) -> () filter.create_selection(name, element_ids[]) -> filter_id filter.edit_selection(filter_id, add_ids[], remove_ids[]) -> () filter.delete(filter_id) -> () view.add_filter(view_id, filter_id, index?, visible?, enabled?, override?) -> () view.set_filter_override(view_id, filter_id, override, visible?, enabled?) -> () view.reorder_filters(view_id, filter_ids[]) -> () view.remove_filter(view_id, filter_id) -> () filter.evaluate(filter_id, view_id?) -> element_id[] (query) view.filters() -> () opens the filter manager (View tab › Graphics › Filters, or Edit/New… on the Filters tab of the graphics dialog). Left pane: all filters, rule-based and selection-based, with New, Duplicate, Rename and Delete. Middle pane (rule-based filters): category tree with a discipline filter, Hide un-checked categories, Check All and Check None. Right pane: the rule tree (Add Rule, Add Set, Delete, AND/OR per set, drawn as nested brackets). Selection filters show their member count and Edit selection. Validation: at least one category; each rule needs a parameter available for every chosen category, an operator valid for its data type and, except for has a value / has no value, a value in the parameter's unit; unchecking a category whose parameter a rule uses marks that rule invalid; names are unique. Delete removes the filter from every view and template that uses it, after a confirmation that counts them. A live count ("matches 124 elements in the active view") updates as rules change.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A filter "Walls where (Fire Rating = 60 OR Fire Rating = 90) AND Function = Interior" colours exactly the matching walls. - [ ] Disabling the filter in the view restores the previous appearance without removing the filter row. - [ ] filter.evaluate returns the same set the view highlights.

    Element and category overrides, hiding and linework

    ID: DOC-GFX-007 · Priority: P0 (hide), P1 (overrides, linework) · Ref: research/04 §3.5

    Purpose. Change the appearance of specific elements, or hide them, in one view.

    Workflow. 1. Select elements › right-click › Override Graphics in View ▸ By Element… / By Category… / By Filter… (By Filter creates a filter from the selection's categories and a common parameter the user picks). 2. The element override dialog has Visible, Halftone, Projection Lines, Surface Patterns (foreground/background), Surface Transparency, Cut Lines, Cut Patterns. 3. Hide in View ▸ Elements (EH) / Category (VH) / By Filter. 4. Modify › View › Linework (LW): pick a line style, then click edges to restyle them in this view only. <By Category> restores the default.

    Behaviour & rules. - Element overrides are view-specific and stored per element. - Linework overrides attach to an edge reference (element GlobalId plus a stable edge descriptor, Chapter 2). When regeneration can no longer find the edge, the override is dropped and a warning is logged. - Hiding an element in a view hides its hosted annotation (tags, dimensions referencing only that element) in that view too.

    Data (RXD). View payload elementOverrides (keyed by ifc: GlobalId), hidden (list of GlobalIds), hiddenCategories, and linework (keyed by ifc:<GlobalId>#<edge sub-reference> → line style id).

    Commands. view.override_elements(view_id, element_ids[], override) -> () view.clear_element_overrides(view_id, element_ids[]) -> () view.hide_elements(view_id, element_ids[]) -> () view.unhide_elements(view_id, element_ids[]) -> () view.set_linework(view_id, edge_refs[], line_style_id?) -> () filter.create_from_selection(view_id, element_ids[], parameter, name) -> filter_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Hiding one door hides its tag in that view only. - [ ] A linework override on a wall edge survives moving the wall; it is dropped with a warning if the edge disappears (for example the wall becomes curved).

    Hidden lines by element and cut profile

    ID: DOC-GFX-020 · Priority: P1 (hidden lines by element), P2 (cut profile) · Ref: research/04 §1 (Show Hidden Lines property), §3.5; web: Show Hidden Lines by Element, Change the Cut Profile of Elements

    Purpose. Two view-specific drafting corrections on model graphics: draw chosen hidden edges of one element behind another as hidden lines, and change the drawn shape of a cut face without changing the model.

    Workflow (hidden lines by element). 1. Set the view's Show Hidden Lines to By Discipline (the tool is disabled otherwise, with a tooltip saying why). 2. View tab › Graphics › Show Hidden Lines: pick the element in front (the obscuring element), then one or more elements behind it. With Multiple on the contextual tab, several obscuring elements can be picked first, then Enter. 3. The edges of the hidden elements that the obscuring elements cover are drawn in the <Hidden> style. 4. Remove Hidden Lines works the same way and removes the pair.

    Workflow (cut profile). 1. View tab › Graphics › Cut Profile, with the option Face (edit the whole cut face boundary) or Boundary between faces (edit the line between two adjoining cut faces, for example two layers or two elements). 2. Hover a cut face or boundary in a plan, ceiling plan, section, callout or detail view; click to enter sketch mode. 3. Sketch an open chain of lines and arcs that starts and ends on the face boundary. A flip arrow on the first segment shows the side that remains; click it to change sides. In Boundary between faces mode only the two end segments are sketched; Reviera adds the connecting segment along the old boundary. 4. Finish. To restore the original shape, select the profile and choose Remove Cut Profile.

    Behaviour & rules. - Hidden lines by element applies in plans, sections, elevations, callouts and orthographic 3D views. It is not available in perspective views, for linked elements, or when the view's discipline is Mechanical, Electrical or Plumbing. - Pairs are evaluated in the hidden-line stage (DOC-HLR-002 step 3, DOC-HLR-003): for a pair (A obscures B), edges of B hidden only by A are kept and classified as hidden edges; edges of B hidden by other elements stay hidden. The result uses the hidden-line sub-category of B's category, so object styles and V/G overrides apply. - Pairs of view-owned detail components work by draw order (DOC-ANN-020): the obscuring component must be in front of the hidden one, otherwise the pair has no effect and the command says so. - A pair whose element is deleted is removed silently; a pair whose elements no longer overlap in the view has no effect but is kept. - Cut profile changes only the 2D cut region of one element (or one compound layer) in one view. It is applied in stage 6 of the pipeline (DOC-HLR-001) as a 2D Boolean on the cut region: the sketched side is added to, or removed from, the region, and adjoining regions are trimmed so that no two cut regions overlap. Projection linework, 3D geometry, quantities, schedules and other views are unchanged. - Sketch validation at Finish: the chain must start and end on the selected boundary, must not form a closed loop, must not cross itself, and must not cross the starting boundary (in Face mode). An invalid sketch keeps the user in sketch mode with the offending segment highlighted. - When the element changes so that the cut face no longer exists (for example the wall is moved out of the cut plane), the profile is kept but inactive and is reported in the warnings list; it applies again if the face returns. - Cut profiles are not copied by Insert 2D Elements from File (DOC-VIEW-009) and are copied by Duplicate with Detailing (DOC-VIEW-011). - Interactive tool. The cut profile sketch follows Conventions §2.1: micro-operations cutprofile.segment(curve), cutprofile.delete(index), cutprofile.flip() with a replay function that rebuilds the sketch after a crash.

    Data (RXD). Hidden-line pairs: view payload hiddenLinePairs[] {obscuring, hidden} (ifc: or annotation references). Cut profiles: annotation objects of kind anno.cutprofile in views/annotation/<viewId>: target (element GlobalId plus face or layer sub-reference, or the two faces of a boundary), mode (face | boundary), sketch (curves in view coordinates), keepSide. Nothing is written to the model's IFC geometry; IFC annotation export (DOC-IFC-002) carries the result only in the drawing linework.

    Commands. view.show_hidden_lines(view_id, obscuring_ids[], hidden_ids[]) -> () (creates one pair per combination; fails with view.hidden_lines_not_by_discipline when the view setting is not By Discipline) view.remove_hidden_lines(view_id, element_ids[]) -> () (removes every pair in which a listed element is the hidden element) view.cut_profile(view_id, target_ref, loops[]) -> () (each loop is {curves[], keep_side: left|right, mode?: face|boundary}; creates or replaces the profile of that target) view.remove_cut_profile(view_id, target_ref) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] In a north elevation with Show Hidden Lines = By Discipline, pairing the north wall with the south entrance door draws the door outline dashed; switching the setting to None hides it. - [ ] The tool is disabled in a perspective view and in a Mechanical plan. - [ ] A cut profile that notches a slab edge in one section changes that section only; the slab's volume in schedules is unchanged. - [ ] A sketch that starts on the boundary but ends inside the face is refused at Finish with the open end highlighted.

    Temporary hide/isolate, reveal hidden, isolate annotations

    ID: DOC-GFX-008 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §3.5

    Purpose. Quick, non-persistent visibility tools while working.

    Behaviour & rules. - View Control Bar glasses menu: Hide Element (HH), Isolate Element (HI), Hide Category (HC), Isolate Category (IC), Reset (HR), Apply Hide/Isolate to View. While active, the view has a coloured border and label. - Temporary state does not print or export, and is not saved. - Apply Hide/Isolate to View converts the temporary state into permanent element or category hiding (layer 3). - Reveal Hidden Elements (light-bulb icon, RH): shows elements hidden by any layer in a highlight colour (default magenta), with the view framed in that colour; Unhide Element / Unhide Category act on the picked items and say which layer hid them. - Isolate Annotations: model elements are halftoned and unselectable so the user can work on annotation; an Include categories list (persisting per user across views) keeps chosen model categories selectable.

    Commands. view.temp_hide_isolate(view_id, mode: hide_element|isolate_element|hide_category|isolate_category, element_ids_or_categories[]) -> () view.temp_reset(view_id? (default: active)) -> () view.temp_apply(view_id? (default: active)) -> () view.reveal_hidden(view_id, on) -> () view.isolate_annotations(view_id, on, include_categories[]?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Temporarily isolating three walls, then printing, prints the full view. - [ ] In reveal-hidden mode, an element hidden by a filter shows in magenta and Unhide reports "hidden by filter <name>".

    Line weights, halftone and underlay settings

    ID: DOC-GFX-009 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §3.6

    Purpose. Map the 16 logical pens to printed widths.

    Workflow. Manage › Additional Settings ▾ › Line Weights: tabs Model Lines (16 pens × list of view scales), Perspective Lines (16 pens), Annotation Lines (16 pens); Add/Delete scale columns. Manage › Additional Settings › Halftone/Underlay: underlay line weight and pattern, halftone brightness (0–100).

    Behaviour & rules. - Model-line pen widths depend on the view scale: for a view scale not listed, Reviera uses the column of the nearest listed scale, measured by ratio (the larger of the two scale denominators divided by the smaller); ties go to the coarser scale. - Perspective and annotation pens do not depend on scale. - Widths are in paper millimetres and are used unchanged by every output (DOC-CORE-006). On screen, Thin lines mode (View Control Bar) draws all lines one pixel wide. - Halftone blends the resolved colour towards the background by the brightness percentage.

    Data (RXD). RXD document standards/line_weights (kind penset: model pens per scale, perspective pens, annotation pens) and the halftone section of project/settings.

    Commands. lineweight.set(table: model|perspective|annotation, pen, width_mm, scale?) -> (); lineweight.add_scale(scale) -> (); lineweight.remove_scale(scale) -> (); settings.set_halftone(brightness?, underlay_weight?, underlay_pattern_id?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With pen 5 at 0.50 mm for 1:50 and 0.35 mm for 1:200 (and no other scale columns), a 1:50 view prints pen 5 at 0.50 mm, a 1:200 view at 0.35 mm, and a 1:75 view uses the nearest column (1:50, 0.50 mm). If a 1:100 column is added, the 1:75 view uses it instead, because 1:100 is nearer by ratio (1.33 against 1.5). - [ ] A PDF printed from a view matches the on-screen line widths at 100 % zoom on a calibrated display (within one device pixel).

    Detail level

    ID: DOC-GFX-010 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §3.7 Detail Level

    Purpose. Choose how much geometric detail elements show.

    Workflow. View Control Bar › Detail Level (Coarse, Medium, Fine), or Properties › Graphics › Detail Level. Per category: Visibility/Graphics › Detail Level column (By View, Coarse, Medium, Fine).

    Behaviour & rules. - Coarse / Medium / Fine per view, overridable per category in the graphics dialog (layer 1) and by filter. The resolved detail level is an attribute of DOC-GFX-001, so the highest layer that sets it wins. - Family geometry declares which detail levels it appears at (Chapter 2). Geometry flagged for none of the levels is never drawn; Reviera warns about it in the family editor. - Walls, floors, roofs and ceilings show compound layers only at Medium and Fine; at Coarse they show their outline filled with the type's Coarse scale fill pattern and colour, with the category's cut line. - Structural framing and columns switch between a single-line symbol (Coarse) and their true section (Medium, Fine) as defined in Chapter 4. - MEP segments switch between single-line (Coarse) and double-line (Medium, Fine) as defined in Chapter 4. - Manage › Additional Settings › Detail Level maps scale ranges to the default detail level of new views. The default map: 1:1 to 1:20 Fine, 1:25 to 1:100 Medium, coarser than 1:100 Coarse. The map applies only when a view is created or its scale is set through the New dialog; changing an existing view's scale never changes its detail level. - Changing the detail level only re-runs stage 2 of the pipeline (representation choice, DOC-HLR-001) for affected elements; tessellations of each level are cached separately. - Dependent views and template-bound views take the detail level from their parent or template (read-only).

    Data (RXD). View payload detailLevel; per-category override in categoryOverrides[*].detailLevel; scale-to-detail-level map in project/settings (detailLevelMap[] {maxScale, level}). On IFC export, representations of different detail follow the sub-context convention of Chapter 2.

    Commands. view.set_detail_level(view_id, level) -> (); settings.set_detail_level_map(ranges[]) -> () (each range {max_scale_denominator, level}; ranges must cover all scales without gaps or overlaps, otherwise detail_level_map.invalid).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Switching a 1:100 plan from Coarse to Fine shows wall layers and door frame detail. - [ ] A category override of Fine for Doors in a Coarse plan draws doors at Fine and walls at Coarse. - [ ] Creating a 1:20 plan with the default map gives it Fine; changing its scale to 1:200 later leaves it at Fine. - [ ] A detail-level map with a gap between 1:50 and 1:75 is rejected with detail_level_map.invalid.

    Visual styles

    ID: DOC-GFX-011 · Priority: P0 (Wireframe, Hidden Line, Shaded, Consistent Colours), P1 (Textures, Realistic), P2 (Path traced) · Ref: research/04 §3.7 Visual Styles

    Purpose. Choose how surfaces and edges are drawn.

    Style Behaviour in Reviera
    Wireframe All edges, no surfaces; hidden edges shown.
    Hidden Line Visible edges only, surfaces in the background colour. This is the documentation style; for plans, sections and elevations it uses the exact HLR pipeline when printing and the GPU-assisted pipeline on screen (§5.12).
    Shaded Surfaces lit with the material's shading colour; edges optional.
    Consistent Colours Material shading colour without lighting.
    Textures Consistent colours with the material's texture maps.
    Realistic Physically based materials with real-time lighting, shadows and ambient occlusion.
    Path Traced Progressive path tracing in the viewport (optional renderer, DOC-OUT-011). Refines while the camera is still.

    UI. View Control Bar visual style menu; default shortcuts WF (wireframe), HL (hidden line), SD (shaded).

    Commands. view.set_visual_style(view_id, style) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Each style can be set from Lua and MCP and is saved with the view. - [ ] The Path Traced style is listed only when an optional renderer is installed; otherwise it is greyed out with a tooltip explaining why.

    Graphic display options

    ID: DOC-GFX-012 · Priority: P1 (P2 for sketchy lines, depth cueing, photographic exposure) · Ref: research/04 §3.7 Graphic Display Options; web: Define Sun Settings for a View

    Purpose. Fine-tune the rendering of a view.

    Behaviour & rules. The Graphic Display Options dialog (default shortcut GD) groups: - Model display: style, show edges, anti-aliasing, whole-view transparency (0–100 %), silhouette edges (line style). - Shadows: cast shadows, ambient shadows (screen-space ambient occlusion). - Sketchy lines: on/off, jitter (0–10), extension (0–10). Implemented by deterministic per-edge noise (the same edge always looks the same), applied in paper space, and therefore also printed. - Depth cueing (sections and elevations with far clipping): fade start and end (percent between near and far planes), fade limit (percent). - Lighting: scheme (exterior or interior; sun only, sun and artificial, artificial only), sun setting (date, time, location, or named preset), artificial light groups, sun intensity, ambient light, shadow darkness (each 0–100). - Photographic exposure (Realistic and Path Traced): automatic or manual exposure value, highlights, shadows, saturation, white point. - Background: none, sky, gradient (sky/horizon/ground colours), image (3D, sections, elevations). - Save as View Template….

    • Sun Settings dialog (sun.settings; opened from the View Control Bar sun path menu, Manage › Additional Settings › Sun Settings, the Lighting group above and the Render dialog). Left: a preset list (built-in presets such as summer and winter solstice and equinox at noon, plus user presets; In-session is the unsaved current setting), with Duplicate, Rename and Delete. Right, by mode:
    • Still, Single Day, Multi-Day (location-based): location (from the project's site location, Chapter 6; Browse opens the location dialog), date (start and end for multi-day), time (start and end for single and multi-day, or Sunrise to sunset), time interval (15 min, 30 min, 1 h, 1 day), and Ground plane at level with a level picker;
    • Lighting (direction-based): azimuth (0–360° from true north), altitude (0–90°), Relative to view (azimuth measured from the view's up direction instead of true north), and Ground plane at level. Validation: end date not before start date, end time after start time, interval shorter than the time range, azimuth and altitude within range. Apply previews in the active view; OK stores the chosen setting on the view; Save Settings stores a named preset. Solar study animation uses the same setting (DOC-OUT-012, solarstudy.set).
    • The ground plane receives shadows in shaded views only; rendered views need modelled ground (DOC-OUT-011).

    Data (RXD). graphicDisplay block of the view (or template) payload: edges, antiAlias, transparency, silhouette, shadows, ambientOcclusion, sketchy {jitter, extension}, depthCue {start, end, limit}, lighting (including sun {preset?, mode, date, endDate, time, endTime, interval, azimuth, altitude, relativeToView, groundPlaneLevel}), exposure, background. Sun presets: project/settings › sunPresets[].

    Commands. view.set_graphic_display(view_id, options) -> (); sun.settings() -> () (opens the dialog above for the active view; its changes are applied through view.set_graphic_display and solarstudy.set as one undo step)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Turning on sketchy lines in a hidden-line elevation shows the same jitter on screen and in the PDF. - [ ] Depth cueing fades a façade 30 m away more than one 5 m away. - [ ] A Lighting sun with azimuth 90° and altitude 30° casts shadows towards the west in a shaded 3D view, independent of the project date. - [ ] A multi-day setting with an end date before its start date cannot be confirmed.

    Line styles and line patterns

    ID: DOC-GFX-013 · Priority: P0 (styles), P1 (pattern editing) · Ref: research/04 §3.6

    Purpose. Named line appearances for drafting and overrides, and the dash patterns they use.

    Behaviour & rules. - Line styles are sub-categories of the Lines category: name, weight (pen), colour, pattern. Built-in styles that cannot be deleted: <Thin Lines>, <Medium Lines>, <Wide Lines>, <Hidden>, <Overhead>, <Beyond>, <Centerline>, <Demolished>, <Sketch>, <Area Boundary>, <Room Separation>, <Space Separation>, <Insulation Batting Lines>, <Lines>, <Invisible lines>, <Axis of rotation>. Users add their own. - Line patterns are sequences of dash, space and dot segments with lengths in paper millimetres. Patterns are applied along the whole polyline (continuing across vertices), so corners look consistent. A dot is drawn as a zero-length dash with round caps. - Deleting a style or pattern in use asks for a replacement.

    Data (RXD). RXD documents standards/object_styles (line styles are sub-categories of Lines) and standards/line_patterns (kind linepattern: ordered segments of {type: dash|space|dot, length_mm}). On IFC export, patterns become IfcCurveStyleFont with IfcCurveStyleFontPattern segments.

    Commands. linestyle.create(name, weight, colour, pattern_id?) -> style_id; linestyle.update(style_id, weight?, colour?, pattern_id?, name?) -> (); linestyle.delete(style_id, replacement_id) -> (); linepattern.create(name, segments[]) -> pattern_id; linepattern.update(pattern_id, segments[]) -> (); linepattern.delete(pattern_id, replacement_id?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A dash-dot pattern of 6 mm dash, 2 mm space, dot, 2 mm space prints with those lengths on paper at any view scale.

    Fill patterns

    ID: DOC-GFX-014 · Priority: P0 (simple), P1 (custom import, rotation) · Ref: research/04 §3.6

    Purpose. Hatches for surfaces, cuts and regions.

    Behaviour & rules. - Two kinds: Drafting patterns are sized in paper millimetres and scale with the view; Model patterns are sized in real units and stay attached to the geometry they cover (for example brick courses or tiles). - Simple patterns: parallel lines or crosshatch, with angle and spacing. - Custom patterns: imported from the open, widely used text .pat hatch definition format, with an import scale. Reviera implements its own parser and ships its own pattern library written for the project. - Orientation in host layers: Orient to view, Keep readable, Align with element. - Solid fill is a built-in drafting pattern. - Model patterns on a face can be aligned and moved: the user can tab-select a pattern line and use Align/Move to set the pattern origin and rotation for that face, stored per face. - Custom patterns can be rotated by any angle and saved as a new pattern.

    Data (RXD). RXD document standards/fill_patterns, kind fillpattern: kind (drafting|model), lineFamilies[] (angle, origin, offset, shift, dashes[]), hostOrientation. Per-face pattern alignment is element-scoped RXD on the element (face sub-reference → origin, angle). On IFC export: IfcFillAreaStyleHatching per line family (HatchLineAppearance, StartOfNextHatchLine, PointOfReferenceHatchLine, PatternStart, HatchLineAngle) inside an IfcFillAreaStyle (ModelOrDraughting = TRUE for model patterns).

    Commands. fillpattern.create(name, kind: drafting|model, definition) -> pattern_id; fillpattern.import_pat(path, pattern_name, kind, scale?) -> pattern_id; fillpattern.rotate_copy(pattern_id, angle, new_name) -> pattern_id; fillpattern.delete(pattern_id, replacement_id?) -> (); face.set_pattern_alignment(element_id, face_ref, origin, angle) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A drafting hatch at 3 mm spacing prints at 3 mm spacing at 1:50 and at 1:200. - [ ] A 225 × 75 mm brick model pattern shows real-size courses that move with the wall. - [ ] Importing a .pat file with 20 patterns lists all 20 for selection.

    Crop regions and annotation crop

    ID: DOC-GFX-015 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §3.8

    Purpose. Limit the area a view shows.

    Behaviour & rules. - Crop View (on/off) and Crop Region Visible are view properties and View Control Bar toggles. - The crop region can be dragged by its edges, edited as a non-rectangular sketch (Edit Crop), reset (Reset Crop), or sized numerically (Size Crop: model crop and annotation crop width/height, proportional option). - Crop breaks (sections and elevations): a break control splits the crop region into two parts that can be moved closer together to shorten a long view; the gap is shown by break lines. - Annotation crop: a second boundary outside the model crop, with an offset per side (paper mm). Annotation that crosses it is clipped; annotation that is entirely outside is hidden. Model-reporting annotation of elements outside the model crop is always hidden. - Rotating the crop region rotates the view's presentation (for example to set a plan square on the sheet). The plan property Orientation (Project North / True North) sets the base orientation (Chapter 6, COL-POS-001). - Crop changes on a callout or dependent view update the parent's callout boundary or matchline display accordingly.

    Data (RXD). crop block of the view payload: enabled, visible, boundary (polyline in view coordinates), breaks[], rotation; annotationCrop: enabled, offsets (four values in paper mm).
