    Commands. view.set_crop(view_id, enabled?, visible?, shape?) -> (); view.reset_crop(view_id) -> (); view.set_annotation_crop(view_id, enabled, offsets?) -> (); view.add_crop_break(view_id, axis, position, gap) -> (); view.remove_crop_break(view_id, index) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A tag whose host is outside the model crop is hidden even when the tag itself lies inside the annotation crop. - [ ] A crop break shortens a 60 m elevation by the gap distance and draws break lines at both cut edges.

    Discipline display

    ID: DOC-GFX-016 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §1 (Discipline property)

    Purpose. Tailor a view to a trade.

    Workflow. 1. Properties › Graphics › Discipline picks the view's discipline; the view regenerates. 2. Manage › Settings › Discipline Profiles opens a table with one column per discipline and one row per model category: Show, Halftone, Hidden lines (drawn when Show Hidden Lines = By Discipline). Reset restores Reviera's defaults.

    Behaviour & rules. - Each discipline (Architectural, Structural, Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing, Coordination) has a profile in project settings: categories hidden, categories halftoned, and whether Show Hidden Lines = By Discipline draws hidden lines for its own categories. - Default profiles: Structural hides non-structural categories and shows structural framing hidden lines; MEP disciplines halftone architectural and structural categories; Coordination shows everything normally. - The profile acts as part of layer 1 of the graphics model, below the view's explicit category overrides. An explicit Visible tick in the view's graphics dialog therefore shows a category the profile hides; the Graphics Inspector reports the profile as the losing layer. - Annotation categories are never hidden by a profile. - The discipline also groups the view in the Project Browser under the default organisation scheme, and is a filter field in view lists and view/sheet sets. - Profiles are project data, so changing one updates every view of that discipline. Templates can include the Discipline property (DOC-GFX-004). - Show Hidden Lines by element (DOC-GFX-020) works only when the view's Show Hidden Lines is By Discipline and the discipline is Architectural, Structural or Coordination, matching the reference product's limits.

    Data (RXD). Discipline profiles in RXD document standards/object_styles (kind discipline.profile: discipline, hidden[], halftone[], hiddenLines[] category keys); view payload discipline.

    Commands. view.set_discipline(view_id, discipline) -> (); discipline.set_profile(discipline, hidden_categories[], halftone_categories[], hidden_line_categories[]) -> (). An unknown category key fails with category.unknown.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Setting a plan to Mechanical halftones walls and shows ducts normally. - [ ] Ticking Furniture Visible in a Structural plan's graphics dialog shows furniture even though the Structural profile hides it. - [ ] Removing Floors from the Mechanical profile's halftone list draws floors normally in every Mechanical view at once.

    Phasing display

    ID: DOC-GFX-017 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §3.9

    Purpose. Show existing, new, demolished and temporary work correctly in each view.

    Workflow. 1. Manage › Phasing › Phases opens a dialog with tabs Project Phases (ordered list; insert before/after; combine with previous/next), Phase Filters, Graphic Overrides. 2. Each element has Phase Created and Phase Demolished. Modify › Geometry › Demolish sets Phase Demolished to the active view's phase for clicked elements. 3. Each view has a Phase and a Phase Filter.

    Behaviour & rules. - Status of an element in a view with phase P (phases ordered by index):

    Condition Status
    created after P not shown (always)
    created before P, not demolished or demolished after P Existing
    created before P, demolished in P Demolished
    created before P, demolished before P not shown (always)
    created in P, not demolished in P New
    created in P, demolished in P Temporary
    • Phase filters set, for each status, one of By category (normal graphics), Overridden (use the phase graphic overrides) or Not displayed. Built-in filters: Show All, Show Complete, Show Demo + New, Show New, Show Previous + Demo, Show Previous + New, Show Previous Phase, None. Users can add filters.
    • Phase graphic overrides per status: projection/surface lines and patterns, cut lines and patterns, halftone, and an optional material. Defaults: Existing = halftone; Demolished = <Demolished> dashed lines; New and Temporary = by category.
    • Phase graphics are layer 4 of DOC-GFX-001.
    • Rooms, areas, spaces and schedules are phase-specific (they belong to one phase).
    • Linked models map their phases to host phases (Chapter 6, COL-LNK-001).
    • The phase definitions themselves are project data owned by Chapter 2; this requirement defines their display.

    Data (RXD). RXD document project/phases: kinds phase (ordered), phase.filter, phase.override. Each element's Phase Created and Phase Demolished are element-scoped RXD (Chapter 2a) holding phase ids. On IFC export, Reviera writes the standard Status property of the element's common property set (NEW, EXISTING, DEMOLISH, TEMPORARY) as seen in the phase being exported, and may write phases as IfcTask objects ordered by IfcRelSequence (export option).

    Commands. phasefilter.create(name, settings{status: by_category|overridden|hidden}) -> filter_id phasefilter.update(filter_id, settings) -> () phase.set_graphic_override(status, override) -> () element.demolish(element_ids[], phase_id? (default: the active view's phase), view_id?) -> () view.set_phase(view_id, phase_id, phase_filter_id?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A wall created in Existing and demolished in New Construction shows dashed in the New Construction view with Show Demo + New, and is not shown in a later phase view. - [ ] A temporary element (created and demolished in the same phase) is hidden in views of later phases. - [ ] Exporting the New Construction phase writes Status = DEMOLISH for that wall.

    Design option display

    ID: DOC-GFX-018 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §3.10

    Purpose. Develop and present alternative designs in one model.

    Workflow. 1. Manage › Design Options › Design Options dialog: create option sets (for example "Entrance Canopy"), each with options; one option per set is primary. Buttons: New set, New option, Make Primary, Duplicate, Rename, Delete, Accept Primary. 2. Add to Set: assign selected elements to one or more options. 3. Pick to Edit / the active option drop-down on the status bar: choose the option being edited. New elements go into the active option; elements in other options are greyed and cannot be selected. 4. Per view, in the graphics dialog Design Options tab: for each set, Automatic (primary) or a specific option.

    Behaviour & rules. - The main model is always shown. For each set, a view shows exactly one option. - Elements may not join, host or be hosted across options, or between an option and the main model in ways that would make the main model depend on a secondary option; such edits are refused with a message. - Annotation that references an element in a non-primary option belongs to that option and is shown only when the option is displayed. - View-owned elements (detail lines, regions) can be edited while an option is active. - Accept Primary moves the primary option's elements into the main model and deletes the set and all other options (with confirmation). - Schedules show the primary option by default, or a chosen option per set.

    Data (RXD). RXD document project/design_options: kinds option.set and option (isPrimary, set). Membership is element-scoped RXD on each element (designOption = option id), so moving one element between options touches only that element. On IFC export, either only the main model plus chosen options are written, or (option Export design options as groups) each option becomes an IfcGroup with its elements assigned by IfcRelAssignsToGroup.

    Commands. designoption.create_set(name) -> set_id designoption.create_option(set_id, name) -> option_id designoption.make_primary(option_id) -> () designoption.add_elements(option_id, element_ids[]) -> () designoption.remove_elements(element_ids[]) -> () designoption.set_active(option_id?) -> () designoption.accept_primary(set_id) -> () designoption.delete(set_or_option_id) -> () view.set_design_option(view_id, set_id, option_id?) -> () designoption.manage() -> () opens the Design Options dialog: a tree of option sets and their options (the primary option marked "(primary)"), and buttons grouped as Edit (Edit Selected, Finish Editing, Cancel Editing), Option (New, Make Primary, Duplicate, Delete, Rename), Option Set (New, Accept Primary, Delete, Rename). The active option and the number of elements in each option are shown. Validation: option and set names are unique within their parent; the primary option cannot be deleted while other options exist (make another primary first); Accept Primary and Delete list what will be deleted and need confirmation; Make Primary is refused while an option is being edited. Each button calls the matching command above, so every action is its own undo step.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A view set to option B of a set shows option B's elements and hides option A's. - [ ] Accept Primary leaves the primary elements in the main model and deletes the others in one undo step.

    Scope boxes

    ID: DOC-GFX-019 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §3.8 Scope Boxes

    Purpose. One box that controls the crop of many views and the extents of datums.

    Workflow. 1. View tab › Create › Scope Box: draw a rectangle in a plan; set name and height. 2. Assign: view Properties › Scope Box; datum (level, grid, reference plane) Properties › Scope Box. 3. View Name Visibility: choose in which views the box itself is shown.

    Behaviour & rules. - A view assigned to a scope box has its crop set to the box's footprint (plans) or the matching face (sections and elevations that intersect it) and cannot edit its crop directly. - A datum assigned to a scope box has its extents limited to the box in every view. - Rotating the box rotates the crops of assigned plans. - Scope boxes print only if not hidden by the print option Hide scope boxes (default on).

    Data (RXD). Annotation-like project object of kind scopebox in RXD document views/index (name, rectangle, height, rotation, base level, visibleInViews). Views and datums refer to it by id; the datum's scope box reference is element-scoped RXD on the grid or level.

    Commands. scopebox.create(name, rectangle: {corner_a, corner_b, rotation?}, height, level_id?) -> element_id; scopebox.update(scopebox_id, rectangle?, height?, rotation?) -> (); view.set_scope_box(view_ids[], scopebox_id?) -> (); datum.set_scope_box(datum_ids[], scopebox_id?) -> (); scopebox.set_view_visibility(scopebox_id, view_ids[]) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Resizing a scope box resizes the crops of the four dependent plans assigned to it. - [ ] A grid assigned to a scope box stops at the box edge in every plan.

    5.12 Drawing generation: hidden-line pipeline and GPU viewport

    The reference product's rendering engine is not documented publicly, so this section is Reviera's own design. It is built on OpenCASCADE (OCCT) and a wgpu renderer, as set out in TECH_STACK §3.2 (the custom wgpu renderer fed by OCCT tessellation was adopted by the owner on 2026-10-12, TECH_STACK §5.2; OCCT's hidden-line algorithms provide the exact 2D output).

    Pipeline overview

    ID: DOC-HLR-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §11 Key behaviours 1, 3; TECH_STACK §3.2–3.3

    Purpose. Produce correct, printable 2D drawings (plans, sections, elevations, hidden-line 3D) and responsive interactive views from the same model, using all CPU cores.

    Behaviour & rules. Generating a view runs these stages. Stages 2–5 run in parallel per element on the rayon pool; each worker owns its OCCT shapes, and no mutable TopoDS state is shared between threads.

     model change ──► invalidation (element revision, view-definition revision)
        │
 1. Candidate query     spatial index (BVH of element boxes) ∩ view volume; graphics resolver (DOC-GFX-001) drops hidden elements
 2. Representation      choose geometry per detail level / view direction / symbolic linework (family recipe)
 3. Zone split & cut    OCCT half-space booleans at cut, bottom, depth, far-clip and section-box planes;
                        planar sections at the cut plane → cut regions per element and per compound layer
 4. Projection & HLR    interactive: GPU-assisted visibility (DOC-HLR-003)
                        print/export: exact OCCT HLR (DOC-HLR-002)
 5. Classification      each edge/region tagged {element, sub-category, zone, edge kind} → resolved style
 6. 2D clean-up         cut-region union per material and join rules, coincident-line removal, pattern phase
 7. Draw list           ordered display list of styled 2D primitives (DOC-HLR-004)
        │
        ├──► GPU viewport (2D renderer)        ├──► PDF / print        ├──► DXF / DWG        ├──► raster image
    • Results of stages 2–5 are cached per (element geometry hash, view direction, clipping planes, detail level), so that moving one element only recomputes that element plus the occlusion pass.
    • Regeneration is incremental and asynchronous. The viewport shows the previous result until the new one is ready, then swaps it atomically; a progress indicator appears after 250 ms.
    • Views that are not open, and are not being printed or exported, are not regenerated (lazy evaluation). Their caches are invalidated only.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Moving one door in a 2000-element plan updates the plan in under 200 ms on the reference machine (Chapter 1 performance targets). - [ ] Regenerating a large plan uses all available cores (CPU utilisation above 80 % on an 8-core machine during the HLR stage). - [ ] The cached and freshly computed draw lists of the same view are identical.

    Cut and exact hidden-line removal with OCCT

    ID: DOC-HLR-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §1.1 (cut plane), §3.6

    Purpose. Produce exact linework for printing and export.

    Behaviour & rules. 1. Cut regions. For each cuttable element crossing a cut plane (plan cut plane, section plane or plane segments of a jogged section, section box faces), compute the section of the solid with BRepAlgoAPI_Section, rebuild closed wires and faces from the section edges, and classify inner loops as holes. For compound elements, cut each layer solid separately so each layer gets its own material pattern. Results are 2D regions in view coordinates. 2. Clipping. Clip each solid to the view volume (crop prism between the near plane and far clip, or the zone slabs of DOC-VR-002) with BRepAlgoAPI_Common against a box or half-spaces. Unchanged elements that lie entirely inside the volume skip this step. 3. Hidden-line removal. Run OCCT's exact HLRBRep_Algo with an HLRAlgo_Projector set to the view's orthographic (or perspective, for camera views) projection. Feed it all clipped solids in the view, plus the cut regions as occluding planar faces. Extract visible sharp edges, visible smooth edges (only when the visual style shows smooth edges), visible outlines, and (when Show Hidden Lines applies) hidden edges with HLRBRep_HLRToShape. 4. Scaling up. Exact HLR is quadratic in the worst case. Reviera splits large views into screen tiles, runs HLR per tile in parallel with only the solids whose projected boxes overlap the tile (plus all solids in front of them), and stitches edges at tile borders. For very large views it may first run HLRBRep_PolyAlgo (mesh-based) to find which solids can occlude which, and then run the exact algorithm only on those. 5. Arcs and circles. Edges that project to circles, arcs or lines are recognised and emitted as exact 2D primitives (not polylines), so that DXF and PDF output keep true arcs. 6. Exact HLR is used for print, PDF, DXF/DWG and stored drawing linework. Interactive display may use DOC-HLR-003 while the exact result is computed in the background; once it is ready, the viewport switches to the exact draw list.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A section through a cavity wall shows one cut region per layer with each layer's pattern, and the layers' common edges are drawn once. - [ ] A circular column cut in plan is a true circle in the exported DXF (an arc entity, not a polyline). - [ ] On screen, the interactive and exact results of the same plan differ by no more than one device pixel along any edge at 100 % zoom.

    GPU-assisted interactive hidden-line display

    ID: DOC-HLR-003 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §1.5 (Accelerated Graphics as context)

    Purpose. Keep 2D views and hidden-line 3D views interactive on large models.

    Behaviour & rules. - Elements are tessellated by OCCT (BRepMesh_IncrementalMesh) with a chordal deflection based on detail level and on-screen size. Tessellations are cached per element and shared between views. - Edges come from the B-rep (feature edges), not from the mesh, so that the result is clean linework. - Visibility is resolved on the GPU: a depth pre-pass renders the triangles (cut by the clip planes and capped, DOC-HLR-006), then edges are drawn with a depth test using a small bias. Edges hidden by the depth test can be drawn again in the <Hidden> style when required. - Cut regions from DOC-HLR-002 step 1 are computed on the CPU (they are cheap) and drawn as filled polygons with the cut pattern. - When the camera moves, only the GPU passes rerun; no CPU geometry work is done.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Panning and zooming a 50 000-element plan stays above 30 fps on the reference GPU. - [ ] Orbiting a hidden-line 3D view of the same model stays above 20 fps.

    The draw list

    ID: DOC-HLR-004 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §6.1–6.3

    Purpose. One intermediate 2D representation shared by the screen and every output (DOC-CORE-006).

    Behaviour & rules. - A draw list is an ordered set of layers (back to front): background fills and underlay; model surface patterns; model projection linework; cut poché fills; cut linework; overhead and beyond linework; view-owned drafting (ordered by its draw order, DOC-ANN-020); annotation; crop frame. - Primitives: line, polyline, arc, circle, ellipse, spline (with a flattened copy), filled polygon (with holes) with a fill pattern reference, text run (font, size in paper mm, position, rotation, width factor, decorations), raster image (with clip polygon), and point symbol (a reference to a cached symbol draw list with a transform). - Each primitive carries a style key: resolved colour, pen width in paper mm, line pattern id and phase offset, halftone flag, transparency, and its source (element GlobalId, sub-category, zone, edge kind). The source lets the screen highlight and select, lets DXF choose layers (DOC-OUT-005), and lets PDF write tagged content. - Line patterns are applied in the consumers in paper space. The draw list keeps the pattern reference and the pattern phase (distance along the polyline), so that dashes continue across segment boundaries in every output. - Coincident lines: when two collinear overlapping segments with the same zone exist, the one with the heavier pen (or, on a tie, the higher-priority category per the object style table) is kept for the overlap, and the other is trimmed. The print option Region edges mask coincident lines applies the same rule between filled-region boundaries and model lines. - Draw lists are serialisable (for caching and for Lua and MCP inspection) but are never stored as RXD.

    Commands. view.get_draw_list(view_id, region?) -> draw_list (query, also exposed as the MCP resource reviera://view/{id}/drawlist).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] The PDF, PNG and DXF outputs of one view contain the same set of edges (compared after rasterising each at 300 dpi; at most 0.1 % differing pixels). - [ ] A dashed polyline with many short segments shows a continuous dash rhythm in all outputs.

    3D GPU viewport

    ID: DOC-HLR-005 · Priority: P0 (wireframe, hidden line, shaded, consistent colours), P1 (textures, realistic) · Ref: research/04 §3.7

    Purpose. Render 3D views in every visual style (DOC-GFX-011) at interactive rates.

    Behaviour & rules. - The renderer uses wgpu (Vulkan, Metal, Direct3D 12, or OpenGL ES fallback), drawing into the native child window that the wxWidgets view frame provides (TECH_STACK §3.4). - It is the built-in render backend (DOC-RBE-001): it consumes the same Render Scene and deltas as any plug-in backend, and is always present for editing, selection and 2D views. - It draws per-element instanced meshes from the OCCT tessellation cache. Family instances that share a type share their mesh. Large models use frustum culling, a BVH, and occlusion culling from the previous frame's depth. - Per-element resolved graphics (colour, transparency, halftone, visibility) live in a GPU buffer updated from the graphics resolver; a filter or override change updates the buffer without re-tessellating. - Visual-style features: edges from the B-rep edge cache; silhouettes from a depth/normal edge-detection pass; shadows by cascaded shadow maps; ambient shadows by screen-space ambient occlusion; sketchy lines and depth cueing in shaders using the same deterministic noise as print (DOC-GFX-012); transparency by weighted blended order-independent transparency; physically based shading (metallic/roughness) for Realistic, with materials taken from IfcSurfaceStyleRendering and the material's RXD appearance data (Chapter 2). - Selection uses an ID buffer (one render target holding element indices). - Large-coordinate safety: geometry is stored relative to per-tile origins and rendered relative to the camera (relative-to-eye) so that sites far from the internal origin (Chapter 6, COL-POS-001) do not jitter.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 500 000-triangle model orbits at 60 fps in Shaded style on the reference GPU. - [ ] Changing a filter colour updates the 3D view within one frame and causes no re-tessellation (checked by counters). - [ ] A model placed 30 km from the internal origin renders without visible vertex jitter at 1 mm zoom.

    Section box and clip-plane capping

    ID: DOC-HLR-006 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §1.5 Section Box

    Purpose. Show solid, patterned cut faces where section boxes and clip planes cut through elements.

    Behaviour & rules. - Interactive: clip planes in the vertex/fragment stage, and caps drawn with a stencil-parity technique per element, filled with the element's resolved cut pattern colour (a solid colour while dragging; the hatch pattern once dragging stops). - Compound elements are capped per layer, using each layer's material cut pattern; the layer boundaries come from the layer solids, not from the mesh, so adjacent layers share one edge. - Stencil parity needs closed (watertight) meshes. Elements whose tessellation is not closed (for example some imported Reference View geometry) are drawn clipped but uncapped, and the Graphics Inspector reports "not capped: open mesh". The exact print path caps them when OCCT can build a closed section, and otherwise leaves them open in print too. - Caps take the cut line and cut pattern of DOC-GFX-001 (so filters and overrides apply), and are drawn only when the 3D view's Show cut faces property is on (DOC-VIEW-008). - Caps are generated for host-model elements and for linked-model elements alike; transparent elements get transparent caps with the same alpha. - Up to six section-box planes plus one far-clip plane are supported per view; a single element cut by several planes gets one cap per plane, trimmed by the other planes.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Cutting a wall with a section box shows a closed cap with the wall's cut pattern, with no gaps at layer boundaries. - [ ] A filter that sets red cut patterns on exterior walls colours their caps red in the 3D view and in its PDF. - [ ] A box corner that cuts one column with two planes shows two caps that meet along one edge without overlap.

    Raster fallback for printing

    ID: DOC-HLR-007 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §6.1–6.2 (Vector / Raster processing)

    Purpose. Print views whose content cannot be expressed as vectors (shaded or realistic styles, transparency, shadows, images).

    Behaviour & rules. - A view is printed as raster when the user chooses Raster processing, or automatically when its visual style or content requires it (the output dialog says so). - Automatic raster is triggered by: visual styles Shaded, Consistent Colours, Textures, Realistic and Path Traced; surface transparency below 100 % opacity; cast or ambient shadows; sketchy lines with raster-only effects; images and point clouds; rendering views. Hidden Line and Wireframe views without these features stay vector. - The raster is rendered off-screen by the GPU renderer at the chosen raster quality (Low 72 dpi, Medium 150 dpi, High 300 dpi, Presentation 600 dpi), in tiles if the image exceeds GPU limits. - Tiles overlap by 16 pixels and are blended at the seams, so no tile border is visible. A GPU without enough memory for one tile at the chosen quality falls back to the next lower quality, and the output report says so. - Only the content inside each viewport's crop is rasterised; the raster is clipped to the crop polygon and placed at exact paper size. - Annotation and view-owned drafting on top of a raster view stay vector in PDF output. - Colour mode (DOC-OUT-001) is applied to the raster as well: Black lines turns non-white pixels of edges black but keeps shaded surfaces in greyscale; Greyscale converts the whole image. - Raster output is deterministic for a given model snapshot, quality and renderer version, so repeated exports compare equal.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A shaded 3D view on a sheet prints as a 300 dpi image, while its title and the title block remain vector (selectable text in the PDF). - [ ] An A0 sheet with a shaded viewport at Presentation quality prints without visible tile seams. - [ ] Exporting the same shaded sheet twice gives identical raster data.

    Pluggable render backends

    ID: DOC-RBE-001 · Priority: P0 (interface, with the built-in viewport as its first implementation), P2 (third-party backends) · Ref: owner directive 2026-10-12 (pluggable renderer for future photo-real and game-engine walkthroughs); TECH_STACK §3.2

    Purpose. Keep 3D presentation open to other renderers. A realistic offline renderer, a game engine or Blender can show a Reviera model without changes to the core. The built-in wgpu viewport (DOC-HLR-005) is the first backend behind the same interface, not a special case.

    Architecture.

     model transactions ──► graphics resolver (DOC-GFX-001) ──► Render Scene (render-agnostic)
                                                               │  snapshot + deltas
            ┌──────────────────────────┬───────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┐
            ▼                          ▼                       ▼                              ▼
   built-in wgpu viewport     in-process plug-in       out-of-process bridge          offline renderer
   (always present; editing,  (Rust/C ABI; GPL-       (Reviera Scene Protocol,       (stills, animations;
    picking, 2D views)         compatible only)        ADV-RSP-001; any engine)       DOC-OUT-011)
    • What is pluggable, and what is not. Only the 3D presentation of a scene is pluggable. The 2D drawing pipeline (cut, exact HLR, draw lists, DOC-HLR-001…004), printing and export stay in the core, so drawings are identical whichever backend is installed. Editing, selection, in-canvas controls and annotation always use the built-in viewport.
    • Render Scene. The core keeps one render-agnostic scene per open model, built from the graphics resolver and the OCCT tessellation cache:
    • nodes: one per visible element occurrence, with element GlobalId, category, sub-category, phase/design-option state and a world transform (relative to a tile origin, DOC-HLR-005)
    • meshes: shared per type and detail level (instancing), with normals, UVs, and optional feature edges as line sets
    • materials: the physically based description from Reviera appearance assets (base colour, metallic, roughness, transmission, IOR, emission, normal/bump/height maps, decals)
    • lights: lighting-fixture light sources with IES LM-63 photometry and light groups, sun from the project location and time, sky model, environment image
    • cameras: view cameras, section boxes and clip planes as metadata (a backend may ignore what it cannot show, see capabilities)
    • per-element resolved graphics: visibility, colour override, transparency, halftone
    • Deltas. Each committed transaction produces a scene delta (nodes, meshes or materials added, changed or removed; graphics changes; light and sun changes). Deltas are coalesced per frame for the built-in viewport and per sync interval (default 250 ms) for external backends.
    • Backend interface. A backend implements: describe() -> capabilities, open(scene_snapshot, target), apply(delta), set_camera(camera), render(request) -> frames/tiles (offline kinds), pick(x, y) -> GlobalId? (optional), and close(). A failing backend is unloaded, its views fall back to the built-in viewport, and the failure is reported. It never takes the model down with it.
    • Capabilities declared by each backend: kinds (interactive, walkthrough, offline_still, offline_animation, vr); clip planes and section boxes; feature-edge display; Reviera visual styles supported (DOC-GFX-011); IES lights; decals; picking; maximum scene size; colour pipeline (sRGB, HDR, ACES). The UI only offers a backend for tasks its capabilities cover. For example, a backend without clip planes is not offered for a view with an active section box, unless the user accepts "ignore section box".
    • Selecting a backend. Each 3D view has a Presentation backend property (default: built-in). Render (DOC-OUT-011) and walkthrough sessions (ADV-WALK-001) choose from the backends offering that kind. User preferences hold the default backend per kind.
    • Discovery. Backends are registered by add-in manifests (DM-ADDIN-001) with a render_backend entry (id, name, kinds, version, licence SPDX, entry point: library path or executable plus protocol version). render.backend.list() reports installed backends with their capabilities and health.

    Commands. render.backend.list() -> backend_info[] (query); render.backend.set_default(kind, backend_id) -> (); view.set_presentation_backend(view_id, backend_id?) -> () (none restores the built-in viewport); render.backend.test(backend_id) -> report (loads it against a sample scene and reports capabilities, timing and errors).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] The built-in viewport passes the same backend conformance suite as third-party backends (snapshot, 10 000 deltas, camera moves, picking). - [ ] Unloading or crashing a third-party backend returns its views to the built-in viewport within 2 s, with no model change and no lost undo history. - [ ] Printed and exported drawings are byte-identical whichever presentation backend the 3D views use. - [ ] A backend that lacks clip planes is not offered for a view with an active section box, unless the user explicitly accepts "ignore section box".

    Backend hosting and licensing

    ID: DOC-RBE-002 · Priority: P2 · Ref: owner directive 2026-10-12; TECH_STACK §4.2

    Purpose. Allow backends under different licences while keeping the GPL boundary clean.

    Behaviour & rules. - In-process plug-ins (dynamic library with a versioned C ABI wrapped by a Rust trait) run inside Reviera and are add-ins. They must carry a GPL-compatible SPDX licence (TECH_STACK §4.2, DM-ADDIN-003). Suitable for renderers such as Cycles (Apache-2.0), LuxCoreRender (Apache-2.0) or Mitsuba 3 (BSD-3-Clause). - Out-of-process bridges are separate programs that talk to Reviera only through the documented Reviera Scene Protocol (ADV-RSP-001), in the same way as MCP clients. Reviera ships no code of theirs and loads none. This is how game engines and other applications attach, for example a Blender add-on (Blender is GPL), a Godot (MIT) or Bevy (MIT/Apache-2.0) walkthrough application, or a user-built bridge to an engine under a proprietary licence that the user installs themselves. Whether a particular bridge stays at arm's length is for its authors; Reviera's obligation is to keep the protocol public and the boundary process-based. (Legal review recommended before any official bridge to a proprietary engine.) - Isolation. An external bridge receives a read-only scene. It can send back only: camera and walk-pose updates, pick results (GlobalIds), viewpoint captures (for BCF, COL-BCF-001) and render results (images for the render gallery). It can never send model edits. A bridge that also wants to edit must use the MCP server with its own token and permission class (DM-MCP-002), subject to the usual approvals. - Connection security. Bridges connect to a local endpoint (Unix domain socket or named pipe; loopback TCP only if enabled). A per-session token is handed over at launch or shown in the Connect backend dialog. Remote connections are off by default. When enabled they require TLS and a token, and the scene stream can be limited to the active view's visible elements. - Resource limits. Per bridge: maximum scene upload rate, maximum texture resolution sent (default 4096 px), and an option to send simplified meshes (a coarser detail level) for large models.

    Commands. render.bridge.launch(backend_id, view_id?, args?) -> session_id (starts the configured executable with a session token); render.bridge.connect_info() -> {endpoint, token} (for bridges started by hand; the token is shown in the UI and is never exposed through MCP resources); render.bridge.disconnect(session_id) -> (); render.bridge.list_sessions() -> session_info[] (query).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An in-process plug-in whose manifest licence is not on the GPL-compatible allow-list is refused at load time, with the reason shown. - [ ] An external bridge that sends a model-edit message is disconnected and the attempt is logged. The model is unchanged. - [ ] With remote connections disabled (the default), connecting from another host fails.

    5.13 Annotation

    All annotation tools are on the Annotate tab, in the panels Dimension, Detail, Text, Tag, Color Fill and Symbol. Reviera has no Options Bar: tool options appear in the tool's contextual ribbon tab and in the Properties palette (Chapter 1). Every annotation object is stored in the RXD annotation document of its owning view (views/annotation/<viewId>, kinds anno.*); references to model geometry use GlobalIds plus named sub-references (§5.1).

    Common annotation rules

    ID: DOC-ANN-000 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §4 intro, §11 Key behaviours 3–4

    Behaviour & rules. - Annotation types (text types, dimension types, tag families, arrowhead styles) are project standards stored in RXD document standards/text_styles. Changing a type changes every instance of it. - Fonts. Text renders with fonts found through the system font configuration. Reviera bundles a default family of open-licence fonts (SIL Open Font License) so that output is the same on every platform. PDF output embeds font subsets. A font missing on a machine is substituted, and the substitution is reported. - Orphans. When a reference can no longer be resolved, model-reporting annotation keeps its last position, is drawn in the orphaned colour (default orange; never printed differently unless the print option Print orphans in warning colour is on), and is listed in the warnings list (Chapter 6, COL-MNT-004). - Linked model references. References may point into linked models (link:<linkId>/ifc:<GlobalId>, Chapter 6). When the link is unloaded, such annotation is hidden, not deleted; it is orphaned only if the element is missing after a reload. - Read convention. Text in annotation stays readable: rotated text flips so that it reads from the bottom or the right of the sheet, unless the type says otherwise. - Annotation in 3D. Allowed only in locked 3D views (DOC-VIEW-006); the annotation plane is the view's projection plane.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Opening a project on a machine without the chosen font prints with the substitute font and logs one warning per missing font. - [ ] Unloading a link hides dimensions to its elements; reloading shows them again unchanged.

    Aligned dimensions

    ID: DOC-ANN-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §4.1

    Purpose. Dimension strings parallel to the measured references.

    Workflow. 1. Annotate › Dimension › Aligned (default shortcut DI; also on the Quick Access Toolbar). 2. In the contextual tab, choose Prefer (wall centrelines, wall faces, centre of core, faces of core) and Pick mode (individual references, or entire walls with options for opening centres, opening widths, intersecting walls and intersecting grids). 3. Click references one after another (Tab cycles candidates under the cursor), then click in empty space to place the dimension line.

    Behaviour & rules. - References can be faces, edges, centrelines, reference planes, grids, levels (in sections), family reference lines, detail lines and snap points, in the host model or linked models. - A dimension with n references has n − 1 segments. - Each reference is stored as a stable sub-reference; after regeneration, the dimension measures the new geometry. - Temporary dimensions shown during editing (Chapter 1) can be made permanent with their dimension control; the result is an aligned dimension.

    Data (RXD). Kind anno.dimension with mode = "aligned": style, refs[] (GlobalId sub-references), line (origin and direction in view coordinates), stringType, lockedSegments, equality, textOverrides[].

    Commands. dim.create_aligned(view_id, refs[], line_point, type_id?, prefer?, pick_mode?) -> dimension_id; dim.make_permanent(view_id, temporary_dimension_ref | {ref_a, ref_b}) -> dimension_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An aligned dimension between two wall faces updates its value when one wall moves. - [ ] Picking an entire wall with opening widths creates a string that includes every door and window opening.

    Linear dimensions

    ID: DOC-ANN-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §4.1

    Purpose. Horizontal or vertical dimensions between points, whatever the direction of the references.

    Workflow. Annotate › Dimension › Linear. Click two or more points (end points, intersections, arc centres, family reference points; Tab cycles candidates), then move the cursor to choose the axis and click to place the dimension line. Spacebar toggles between horizontal and vertical while placing.

    Behaviour & rules. - The dimension line is horizontal or vertical in the view (the user picks by cursor position or by pressing the spacebar). Measured values are projected onto that axis. References are points (end points, intersections, centres). - "Horizontal" and "vertical" are relative to the view's presentation, so rotating the crop region (DOC-GFX-015) rotates the axis with it. - References may be in the host model, in linked models (DOC-ANN-000) or on view-owned drafting. A point that becomes coincident with another along the axis gives a zero-length segment, which is drawn with its witness lines and the value 0 unless the type suppresses zero segments. - Linear dimensions use the same string types, equality, locks and text overrides as aligned dimensions (DOC-ANN-004, DOC-ANN-005). - Available in plans, ceiling plans, sections, elevations, callouts, drafting views and locked 3D views (where the axis is in the view plane).

    Data (RXD). anno.dimension with mode = "linear" and axis (horizontal | vertical, in view coordinates), plus the common dimension fields of DOC-ANN-001.

    Commands. dim.create_linear(view_id, point_refs[], line_point, axis?: horizontal|vertical, type_id?) -> dimension_id (fewer than two references fails with dim.too_few_references)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A linear dimension between the ends of a 45° wall shows its horizontal projection. - [ ] After rotating a plan's crop by 30°, a new vertical linear dimension is vertical on the sheet. - [ ] Moving one referenced column updates the linear dimension's value on the next regeneration.

    Angular, radial, diameter and arc-length dimensions

    ID: DOC-ANN-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §4.1

    Purpose. Dimension angles between lines and the size and length of curved geometry.

    Workflow. Annotate › Dimension › Angular / Radial / Diameter / Arc Length. Pick the references as described below (Tab cycles candidates), then click to place the dimension arc or text.

    Behaviour & rules. - Angular: between two non-parallel linear references; the user picks the quadrant by cursor position. More than two references that meet at one point give a chain of angles (picked in order). Parallel references are refused with dim.parallel_references. - Radial: radius of an arc or circle, with an optional centre mark; the leader goes from the centre or from the arc only, by type. The value text carries the type's radius prefix (default "R"). - Diameter: diameter of an arc or circle, with the diameter prefix symbol from the type. - Arc length: pick an arc, then the two radial references (end points or lines) that bound it. The value is the length along the arc between them; the type's arc-length symbol is shown above the value. - References can be curved walls, arcs in families, circular columns, detail arcs and, for angular dimensions, grids, reference planes and straight edges. - When the arc becomes a straight line (radius changed to infinite or the wall is made straight), radial, diameter and arc-length dimensions are orphaned (DOC-CORE-003). - Angular values use the project's angle format (decimal degrees or degrees–minutes–seconds) unless the type overrides it. Radial and diameter dimensions can drive the geometry (DOC-ANN-004) when the referenced element allows its radius to be edited.

    Data (RXD). anno.dimension with mode = angular | radial | diameter | arclength; angular adds quadrant; radial adds centreMark and leaderFrom (centre | arc); arc length adds endRefs[2].

    Commands. dim.create_angular(view_id, ref_a, ref_b, arc_point, type_id?) -> dimension_id; dim.create_radial(view_id, arc_ref, point, type_id?, centre_mark?) -> dimension_id; dim.create_diameter(view_id, arc_ref, point, type_id?) -> dimension_id; dim.create_arc_length(view_id, arc_ref, end_ref_a, end_ref_b, point, type_id?) -> dimension_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A radial dimension on a curved wall updates when the wall's radius changes. - [ ] An angular dimension between two grids at 60° shows 60.00° and changes when one grid is rotated. - [ ] Making a curved wall straight orphans its radial dimension and lists it in the warnings.

    Dimension string types, equality and locks

    ID: DOC-ANN-004 · Priority: P0 (continuous, locks), P1 (baseline, ordinate, equality) · Ref: research/04 §4.1

    Behaviour & rules. - String type (from the dimension type, switchable before placement): Continuous (chained segments), Baseline (each value measured from the first reference, stacked at the type's baseline spacing), Ordinate (a single line with running values from an origin, written at each reference). - Equality: the EQ control on a multi-segment string constrains all segments to be equal. Moving one reference redistributes the others. Equality display: Value, Equality Text (for example "EQ"), or Equality Formula (a type-defined formula such as "3 × 1200 = 3600"). - Locks: the padlock control on a segment creates a dimensional constraint (Chapter 2/3 constraint engine) that holds that distance. The lock is mirrored into RXD document model/constraints so that regeneration does not depend on annotation being loaded. - Driving dimensions: editing a segment's value moves the referenced element that is not locked (the element picked last, unless the user chooses otherwise with the move-element control). - Removing a dimension with locks asks whether to keep or remove its constraints.

    Data (RXD). anno.dimension fields stringType, equality, equalityDisplay, lockedSegments; constraints in model/constraints (constraint.lock, constraint.equal).

    Commands. dim.set_equality(dimension_id, on, display?) -> (); dim.lock_segment(dimension_id, segment_index, locked) -> (); dim.set_value(dimension_id, segment_index, value, move_ref?) -> (); dim.set_string_type(dimension_id, type: continuous|baseline|ordinate) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With EQ on a three-segment string between two fixed walls, moving the middle partition keeps the segments equal. - [ ] A locked segment cannot be changed by moving one of its walls; the move is refused with a constraint message. - [ ] Typing a new value into a segment moves the unlocked element by the difference.

    Dimension types, text overrides and witness lines

    ID: DOC-ANN-005 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §4.1 Dimension type properties, Instance, Behaviours

    Behaviour & rules. - Type properties: string type; leader type (arc or line) and leader tick; tick mark and interior tick mark; line and tick pens; dimension line extension (and flipped extension); witness line control (gap to element, or fixed to the dimension line), length, gap and extension; centreline symbol, pattern and tick; ordinate settings; colour; snap distance; text size, offset, font, background (opaque or transparent), bold/italic/underline, width factor; read convention; units format and alternate units (with format, prefix and suffix); show opening height; suppress spaces; equality text, formula and witness display. - Instance text: the value (read-only unless the dimension drives); Replace with text (only allowed for non-numeric text, so that a dimension cannot silently show a false number); prefix, suffix, text above and text below; segment leader visibility; label (bind to a global parameter, Chapter 2). - Witness lines: drag a witness grip to another reference; Edit Witness Lines adds or removes references; the gap grip shortens a witness line. - Moving text off its segment draws a leader when the type asks for one.

    Data (RXD). standards/text_styles kind dimstyle; instance fields textOverrides[] per segment (replace, prefix, suffix, above, below), witnessGaps[], textPositions[], label.

    • Dimension type editor (dimtype.edit; Annotate › Dimension ▾ › Linear / Angular / Radial / Diameter / Arc Length / Spot Elevation / Spot Coordinate / Spot Slope Dimension Types). It opens the Type Properties dialog filtered to the types of that dimension kind: type list with Duplicate, Rename and Delete (a type in use asks for a replacement), the grouped property grid listed above, and a live preview of a sample string. Validation: text size 0.5–100 mm, width factor 0.1–10, line extensions and witness gaps 0–50 mm (paper), units format must be valid for the dimension kind (length for linear kinds, angle for angular, slope for spot slope). OK applies all edits through dimtype.update as one undo step.

    Commands. dimtype.create(name, base_type_id?, properties) -> type_id; dimtype.update(type_id, properties) -> (); dimtype.edit(kind: linear|angular|radial|diameter|arc_length|spot_elevation|spot_coordinate|spot_slope) -> () (opens the editor above); dim.set_text(dimension_id, segment_index?, replace?, prefix?, suffix?, above?, below?) -> (); dim.edit_witness_lines(dimension_id, add_refs[], remove_refs[]) -> (); dim.set_label(dimension_id, global_parameter_id?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Replace with text refuses a numeric string such as "3000" and accepts "VARIES". - [ ] Alternate units show "3000 [9'-10\"]" style output when the type enables them.

    Spot elevations

    ID: DOC-ANN-006 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §4.1 Spot Elevation; web: Spot Dimensions, Spot Elevation Type Properties

    Purpose. Show the height of points on faces and edges in plans, sections, elevations and locked 3D views.

    Behaviour & rules. - Options: leader on/off, shoulder; Relative base: project base point, survey point, or a chosen level (relative elevations); Display: actual (picked point), top, bottom, top and bottom (for sloped or thick elements); prefix and suffix; single or top/bottom indicator; symbol from the type. - On a sloped surface the value follows the picked point and updates when the surface changes. - Elevations relative to the survey point use the shared coordinate system (Chapter 6, COL-POS-001). - Spot types. Each spot elevation type sets: Rotate with component; leader arrowhead, leader and arrowhead pens; colour; symbol (an annotation family, or none); text font, size, width factor, bold, italic, underline, background (opaque or transparent); text offset from leader and from symbol; text orientation (horizontal or vertical); text location (above, below, or in line with the leader; in-line hides the symbol); units format and alternate units (none, right or below, with format, prefix and suffix); Elevation origin (project base point, survey point or relative); elevation indicator, top indicator and bottom indicator texts, each as prefix or suffix. - Spot dimension settings (spot.settings; Manage › Additional Settings › Spot Dimensions) opens one dialog with three tabs, Spot Elevation Types, Spot Coordinate Types and Spot Slope Types. Each tab lists the types of that kind (Duplicate, Rename, Delete) and edits their properties as above, with the same validation and preview as the dimension type editor (DOC-ANN-005). The dialog also holds two project-wide settings: the default elevation origin for new spot types, and whether spot values in locked 3D views measure from the project base point or the survey point. - Spot elevations can be placed on faces and edges of model elements, on toposolids, and on linked elements; not on drafting lines or in drafting views.

    Data (RXD). anno.spot with spotKind = "elevation", ref (face or edge sub-reference plus parametric location on it), base, display, leader, shoulder, prefix, suffix. Spot types: standards/text_styles, kind dimstyle with dimKind = spot_elevation | spot_coordinate | spot_slope. Project-wide spot settings: project/settings › spot.

    Commands. spot.create_elevation(view_id, ref, point, leader_point?, type_id?, base?, display?) -> annotation_id; spot.settings() -> () (opens the Spot Dimensions dialog; type edits are applied through dimtype.update, and the dialog's changes, including the two project-wide settings, form one undo step)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A spot elevation relative to the survey point on a slab top shows the shared-coordinate elevation, and changes when the survey point is redefined. - [ ] A spot type with Display = Top and Bottom on a 250 mm slab shows two values 250 mm apart, each with its indicator text. - [ ] Changing the text location of a spot type to In line with leader hides the symbol on every spot of that type.

    Spot coordinates

    ID: DOC-ANN-007 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §4.1 Spot Coordinate

    Purpose. Report the plan coordinates of points (setting-out of grids, slab corners, site boundaries).

    Workflow. Annotate › Dimension › Spot Coordinate; click a point on an element (or a grid intersection), then the leader shoulder and text position.

    Behaviour & rules. - Shows north/south and east/west (and optionally elevation) of a point relative to the project base point or the survey point, with indicator texts and order from the type. - Type options: top and bottom value (north/south first or east/west first), indicator texts (default "N", "E", "EL"), indicator as prefix or suffix, whether elevation is included, units format, alternate units, and the text and leader settings shared with spot elevations (DOC-ANN-006). - Coordinates follow the shared coordinate system and true north (Chapter 6, COL-POS-001); rotating the survey point or redefining shared coordinates updates every spot coordinate. - Placeable in plans, ceiling plans, sections, elevations and locked 3D views; references are vertices, edge points or face points of model elements, grid intersections and toposolid points. - A value whose reference disappears is orphaned (DOC-CORE-003).

    Data (RXD). anno.spot with spotKind = "coordinate", ref, base (project | survey), includeElevation, leader, shoulder.

    Commands. spot.create_coordinate(view_id, ref, point, leader_point?, type_id?, base?) -> annotation_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A spot coordinate on a grid intersection matches the value reported by coord.report_point (Chapter 6). - [ ] Rotating the project to true north by 10° changes the spot coordinate values without moving the spot in the view.

    Spot slopes

    ID: DOC-ANN-008 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §4.1 Spot Slope

    Purpose. Report the slope of roofs, ramps, beams, pipes and paved surfaces.

    Workflow. Annotate › Dimension › Spot Slope; hover a sloped face or edge (the arrow previews the downhill direction), click to place. Representation (arrow or triangle) and Offset from reference are set on the contextual tab before placing.

    Behaviour & rules. - Shows the slope of a face or edge as an arrow or a triangle, with an offset from the reference, in the type's slope units (ratio, percent, degrees, or rise per run). - The arrow points downhill. In plan views it shows the slope arrow along the steepest descent of the face at the picked point; in sections and elevations it is drawn along the edge as seen, and the triangle form is available only there. - A horizontal face or edge shows 0 (or the type's text for flat, if set); a vertical face cannot carry a spot slope and is refused. - Type options: slope units and format, arrowhead, leader line length, text settings shared with DOC-ANN-006, and the triangle's run length (paper mm). - The value updates when the host slope changes; MEP segments use their own slope (Chapter 4).

    Data (RXD). anno.spot with spotKind = "slope", representation, offset, ref (face or edge sub-reference plus parameter).

    Commands. spot.create_slope(view_id, ref, point, type_id?, representation?: arrow|triangle) -> annotation_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A spot slope on a 2 % ramp shows "2 %" and updates when the ramp slope changes. - [ ] A spot slope on a roof plane in plan points downhill and flips when the roof's slope direction is reversed. - [ ] Placing a spot slope on a vertical wall face is refused.

    Text notes and leaders

    ID: DOC-ANN-009 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §4.2; web: Edit a Text Note, Text Note Type Properties, Check Spelling in Text Notes, Options Dialog: Check Spelling Tab

    Purpose. Free text in views and on sheets.

    Workflow. 1. Annotate › Text › Text (default shortcut TX). 2. Click for unwrapped text, or drag a box for wrapped text; choose leaders in the contextual tab (none, one segment, two segments, arc; left or right side; attached at top, middle or bottom). 3. Type in the in-place editor; finish by clicking outside.

    UI. Edit Text contextual tab: bold, italic, underline, subscript, superscript, all caps; lists (bullets, numbers, lowercase and uppercase letters) with indent levels; paragraph alignment; add/remove leaders; symbols; find and replace; spell check (in-place underlining with suggestions, using Hunspell dictionaries, LGPL/MPL); Close (finish editing). Default shortcuts in the editor: Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+U, Ctrl+Shift+A (all caps); Esc or a click outside finishes. Options on the Text panel: Show border when editing, Show opaque background when editing.

    Behaviour & rules. - Text types: colour, pen, background (opaque or transparent), border on/off and offset, leader arrowhead, font, size (paper mm), tab size, bold/italic/underline, width factor. - The frame width is the wrapping width; the box can be rotated. - Leaders end in the type's arrowhead and can be dragged; leaders are not associative (they do not follow elements). - Find and replace works across the current view, selected views or the whole project. - Formatting in the editor (text.format): a style toggles on the selected characters (or, with no selection, on the characters typed next). Bold, italic, underline, subscript, superscript and all caps combine freely, except that subscript and superscript exclude each other. All caps changes display only; the stored characters keep their case, so Find and replace matches the typed text. Formatting is stored as character-style runs in content. The whole edit session, from opening the editor to closing it, is one undo step. - Closing the editor (text.close_editor): commits the content with text.set_content and leaves edit mode. A note left empty is deleted. The editor is also closed by Esc, a click outside the note, or starting another command. - Text type editor (texttype.edit; Annotate › Text panel launcher, or Edit Type on a text note): the Type Properties dialog for text types, listing the type properties above plus line weight, leader/border offset and tab size, with Duplicate, Rename, Delete and a sample preview. Validation: size 0.5–100 mm (paper), width factor 0.1–10, tab size 0.5–100 mm, offset 0–20 mm; the font must be available or a substitute is named (DOC-ANN-000). A type in use cannot be deleted without choosing a replacement. - Spell check (text.check_spelling; Annotate › Text › Check Spelling, default shortcut F7): checks text notes in the selection or, with nothing selected, in the active view or sheet. Other text (parameter values, schedule cells, tag labels) is not checked. A dialog shows each unknown word in context with suggestions and Ignore, Ignore All, Add to dictionary, Change, Change All; changes are made through text.set_content and form one undo step. Text notes inside groups are skipped unless the group is being edited, and the dialog reports how many were skipped. In BIMserver mode, notes in views owned by someone else are skipped and reported (Chapter 6). - In-context spell check: while the editor is open, unknown words are underlined; the context menu offers suggestions and Add to dictionary. Underlining disappears when the editor closes. - Spelling options (Options › Check Spelling, a per-user preference): ignore words in capitals, ignore words with numbers, flag repeated words, main dictionary (any installed Hunspell dictionary; Reviera ships British and American English), and additional user dictionaries (plain word lists; a building-terms list is shipped). In-context checking can be switched off.

    Data (RXD). anno.text: style, position, rotation, width (null when unwrapped), content (portable rich-text runs: paragraphs, list levels, character styles bold, italic, underline, sub, sup, caps), leaders[], alignH, alignV. Text types: standards/text_styles, kind textstyle. User dictionaries are per-user files outside the project and are never written to RXD.

    Commands. text.create(view_id, position, content, type_id?, width?, rotation?) -> annotation_id; text.set_content(annotation_id, content) -> (); text.format(style: bold|italic|underline|all_caps|subscript|superscript) -> () (applies to the open editor's selection; fails with text.no_editor when no editor is open); text.close_editor() -> (); text.add_leader(annotation_id, side, attach, points[], shape?: straight|arc) -> (); text.remove_leaders(annotation_id) -> (); text.find_replace(scope, find, replace, match_case?, whole_word?) -> count; texttype.create(name, properties) -> type_id; texttype.edit(type_id?) -> () (opens the editor above); text.check_spelling(scope?: view|selection) -> spelling_issue[] (query; each issue is {annotation_id, offset, word, suggestions[]}; from Lua and MCP it only reports, and fixes are made with text.set_content)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A numbered list with two indent levels keeps its numbering after editing and in the PDF output. - [ ] Find and replace across the project reports the number of replacements and can be undone in one step. - [ ] Selecting a word and pressing Ctrl+B makes it bold; one Undo after closing the editor removes the whole edit session. - [ ] text.check_spelling on a view with the note "Concret slab" returns one issue for "Concret" with "Concrete" among the suggestions. - [ ] A text type with size 0 cannot be saved in the type editor.

    Tags by category, tag all and loaded tags

    ID: DOC-ANN-010 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §4.3

    Purpose. Label elements with values read live from their parameters.

    Workflow. 1. Annotate › Tag › Tag by Category (default shortcut TG): hover an element and click. Contextual options: orientation (horizontal, vertical, or model-aligned in 3D), leader on/off, leader end (attached or free), leader length. 2. Tag All Not Tagged: a dialog lists categories that have a loaded tag; choose all objects in the view or only selected ones, include linked elements, leader and orientation. 3. Loaded Tags and Symbols: per category, the default tag type.

    Behaviour & rules. - A tag is an instance of an annotation family whose labels name parameters (Chapter 2). Its text is computed from the host's current parameter values. - Editing a label in the tag edits the host parameter (for example door number), as a normal undoable parameter change, subject to ownership (Chapter 6). - A tag with an attached leader follows its host. A tag with a free leader end keeps its position. Leader start and leader end can each be free or attached; the attachment point can snap to snap references defined in the tag family. - Tags of linked elements stay bound to the link instance. - Tag All Not Tagged never creates a second tag of the same tag type for an element that already has one in the view. - Tag placement avoids overlapping existing annotation where possible (simple greedy search of candidate positions around the host).

    Data (RXD). anno.tag: tagType (family type reference), host (GlobalId or linked reference), position, orientation, angle, leader {start, end, elbow, startMode, endMode}, excludeFromLeaderOutline.

    Commands. tag.create(view_id, host_ref, position?, tag_type_id?, orientation?, leader?) -> annotation_id; tag.tag_all(view_id, categories[], scope: view|selection, include_links?, leader?, orientation?) -> annotation_id[]; tag.set_default_type(category, tag_type_id) -> (); tag.set_leader(annotation_id, start_mode?, end_mode?, points?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing a door's Mark from 101 to 102 updates every tag of that door at once. - [ ] Typing a new value into a door tag changes the door's Mark parameter. - [ ] Running Tag All Not Tagged twice creates no duplicates.

    Multi-category, material, room, area and space tags

    ID: DOC-ANN-011 · Priority: P0 (room tags), P1 (others) · Ref: research/04 §4.3

    Behaviour & rules. - Multi-category tag: tags elements of any category through parameters they share. It can be the default tag for any category in Loaded Tags and Symbols, and is then used by Tag by Category and Tag All. - Material tag: tags the material of the face or compound layer under the cursor (in plans and sections); the reference is the element plus the layer index sub-reference (#layer:<function>:<n>, Chapter 2a). - Room, area and space tags: placed with Architecture › Room & Area › Tag Room (default shortcut RT), Tag Area, and Analyze › Spaces › Tag Space. They show name, number, area and other values. The room tool can tag automatically on placement (Chapter 3). - A room tag outside its room shows a warning marker until moved back or given a leader.

    Data (RXD). anno.tag with tagKind = multicategory | material | room | area | space.

    Commands. tag.create_material(view_id, element_ref, layer_ref, position, tag_type_id?) -> annotation_id; tag.create_room(view_id, room_id, position?, tag_type_id?) -> annotation_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A material tag on the insulation layer of a wall in section shows the insulation material's name.

    Tag by example

    ID: DOC-ANN-012 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/04 §4.3 Tag by Example

    Purpose. Repeat an existing tag's set-up on many elements.

    Workflow. Select a reference tag › Tag by Example; choose target elements (all in view, selection, or by filter, including nested family instances); choose whether to replace existing tags of the same category; a live preview shows proposed tags; confirm.

    UI. Contextual tab Tag by Example: target scope (All in view, Selection, Filter with a filter picker), Include nested families, Replace existing tags, preview toggle, Finish, Cancel. The preview draws proposed tags in a highlight colour; clicking a proposed tag excludes it.

    Behaviour & rules. - New tags copy the reference tag's type, orientation, leader settings and its offset relative to the host's local axes. - Targets are elements of the reference tag's host category (or of any category the tag family supports, for multi-category tags) that are visible in the view. Elements already carrying a tag of the same type are skipped unless Replace existing tags is on, in which case their tags are deleted and recreated. - The host's local axes are its family placement axes (for walls and other linear elements, the location line direction). Mirrored hosts mirror the offset, so tags stay on the same side relative to the host's facing. - Where the copied position would overlap existing annotation, the tag is still placed (no automatic shifting), and the count of overlaps is reported so the user can review them. - Linked elements can be targets when the link is visible (DOC-ANN-000). - The command is one undo step.

    Data (RXD). Creates ordinary anno.tag objects (DOC-ANN-010); nothing records the example relation.

    Commands. tag.by_example(view_id, reference_tag_id, targets: all|selection|filter, filter_id?, replace_existing?) -> annotation_id[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Tagging 40 windows by example places each tag at the same relative offset as the reference tag. - [ ] Windows already tagged with the same tag type are skipped unless Replace existing tags is on. - [ ] A mirrored window receives its tag on the mirrored side.

    Stair, beam and other specialised tags

    ID: DOC-ANN-013 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §4.3, §4.5; web: Annotate the Stair Path, About Tagging Beam Systems

    Behaviour & rules. - Stair tread/riser numbers: numbers along a stair run, with start number, direction, orientation and visibility per run; they are included in Tag All. - Beam annotations: places tags and spot elevations at the ends and middle of selected structural beams by rule (Chapter 4 owns beam-specific settings). - Span direction, reinforcement symbols, stair path: symbols tied to structural floors, reinforcement and stairs (Chapters 3 and 4); they are annotation objects bound to their host like tags. - Beam system span tag (Annotate › Symbol › Beam, tag.beam_system): pick a beam system (Chapter 4, STR-BSYS-001) in a plan. The tag is a span arrow drawn perpendicular to the system's beams across the system boundary, with a label that by default reads "<beam type> @ <spacing>" (for fixed-number layouts, "<beam type> × <count>"). Its labels are ordinary tag labels, so the tag family can show other system parameters. The arrow length follows the boundary and the label updates when the layout changes. Framing tags on the individual beams are placed with Beam Annotations instead. - Stair path (Annotate › Symbol › Stair Path, tag.stair_path): pick a stair in a plan that does not show its path yet. The annotation draws the walk line along the stair's path (centre or offset line from the stair recipe, Chapter 3), a start symbol, an arrowhead at the end, and an "UP" or "DN" text that follows whether the view looks down on the stair from above or below its mid-height. Instance options: show up/down text, up and down text strings, text orientation, text offset, line start and end offsets, Full step arrow. Type options: arrow type, start symbol, line style, text font and size, and whether the path is drawn to the cut line only. One stair path per stair per view; placing a second is refused. - Reinforcement symbols (Annotate › Symbol › Area / Path / Fabric Reinforcement, tag.reinforcement_symbol): pick an area, path or fabric reinforcement system (Chapter 4). An area symbol draws the system boundary span arrows and a label listing the active layers (for example "T1 Ø12@200, B1 Ø10@150"); a path symbol draws the path with its bar size, spacing and number of bars; a fabric symbol shows the sheet type and lap. Symbols update when the system changes and are orphaned when it is deleted. - These annotations follow DOC-ANN-010 for leaders, ownership and linked hosts, and they are included in Tag All Not Tagged for their categories.

    Data (RXD). anno.tag with tagKind = stairnumber | beamsystem | stairpath | reinforcement (with reinforcementKind = area | path | fabric) | spandirection; host is the stair, run, beam system or reinforcement system GlobalId. Stair path instance options: showUpDown, upText, downText, startOffset, endOffset, fullStepArrow.

    Commands. tag.stair_numbers(view_id, run_ids[], start?, direction?) -> annotation_id[]; tag.beam_annotations(view_id, beam_ids[], settings) -> annotation_id[]; tag.beam_system(view_id, system_id, type_id?, position?) -> annotation_id; tag.stair_path(view_id, stair_id, type_id?) -> annotation_id; tag.reinforcement_symbol(view_id, system_id, kind: area|path|fabric, type_id?, position?) -> annotation_id. A host of the wrong kind fails with tag.host_kind_mismatch; these commands are refused in 3D views.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Stair tread numbers renumber when a run gains a tread. - [ ] A beam system span tag reads "W310x39 @ 1200" and changes to "@ 1500" when the system spacing changes. - [ ] A stair path in the plan of the stair's base level shows "UP"; the same stair in the plan above shows "DN". - [ ] Adding a top layer to an area reinforcement system adds it to the area reinforcement symbol's label.

    Keynotes

    ID: DOC-ANN-014 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §4.4 · screenshots/documentation/keynote_legend_detail.png

    Purpose. Short coded notes that refer to a project-wide keynote list.

    Workflow. 1. Annotate › Tag › Keynote ▾ › Element Keynote / Material Keynote / User Keynote / Keynoting Settings. 2. Keynoting Settings: keynote table source, path type (absolute, relative to the project, or in a library location), Reload, numbering method (By keynote, showing the key; By sheet, numbering keynotes sequentially per sheet). 3. Element keynote: click an element; it shows the keynote of the element's type. Material keynote: click a face or layer; it shows the material's keynote. User keynote: pick any key from the hierarchy browser.

    Behaviour & rules. - Keynote table format: Reviera reads a plain tab-separated text file with columns key, text and optional parent key, which builds a tree. It also accepts the same three columns as CSV. Reviera ships its own sample tables (not derived from vendor files). - The table can also be stored inside the project (RXD), which avoids missing-file problems in BIMserver mode. The settings choose external file or embedded; an external file can be embedded at any time. - A missing key shows "?" and is reported. - Keynote tag types: number only, text only, boxed number. - Keynote legends: DOC-VIEW-010.

    Data (RXD). anno.keynote: mode (element | material | user), host reference, key (user keynotes), position, leader. Settings and embedded table in standards/text_styles (kind keynote.settings, keynote.table).

    Commands. keynote.settings(source?, path_type?, numbering?: by_keynote|by_sheet, embed?) -> (); keynote.reload() -> (); keynote.create(view_id, mode, host_ref?, key?, position, tag_type_id?) -> annotation_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Editing a key's text in the table and reloading updates every keynote showing that key. - [ ] With By sheet numbering, the same key shows different numbers on two sheets, matching each sheet's keynote legend.

    Symbols

    ID: DOC-ANN-015 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §4.5

    Purpose. Place generic, non-reporting annotation symbols.

    Workflow. Annotate › Symbol › Symbol; choose a type in the Type Selector; set the number of leaders and Rotate after placement on the contextual tab; click to place (and click again to set the rotation when that option is on).

    Behaviour & rules. - Annotate › Symbol › Symbol places generic annotation family instances (north arrows, graphic scales, centrelines, note symbols). Symbols are sized in paper units and keep their printed size at any scale. - A north-arrow symbol can be set to point to true north; it then follows the project's true-north angle (Chapter 6). - A graphic-scale symbol reads the view scale automatically. - Symbol instances can be scheduled with note-block schedules (DOC-SCH-006). - Symbols are view-owned (DOC-CORE-004); they can be placed in any 2D view, on sheets, and in locked 3D views (on the view plane). Labels in the symbol family that use instance parameters are edited in place or in Properties. - Symbols may have any number of leaders (0–4 from the ribbon; more through Lua), each ending in the type's arrowhead and not associated with model elements. - Symbol families come from Reviera's annotation family library or the user's own families (Chapter 2); a symbol family must have category Generic Annotations or another annotation category marked as placeable. - Hide at scales coarser than is available per instance, as for view markers.

    Data (RXD). anno.symbol: type (family type reference), position, rotation, parameterValues, trueNorth flag, leaders[], hideCoarserThan.

    Commands. symbol.place(view_id, type_id, position, rotation?, parameters?) -> annotation_id (a type that is not an annotation family fails with symbol.not_annotation)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A graphic scale placed in a 1:100 view shows 1:100 divisions and updates when the scale changes to 1:50. - [ ] A true-north arrow rotates by 15° when the project's true-north angle changes by 15°. - [ ] A note-block schedule lists two symbols of the same note family placed on one sheet.

    Detail lines

    ID: DOC-ANN-016 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §4.6

    Behaviour & rules. - Annotate › Detail › Detail Line (default shortcut DL). Draw tools: line, rectangle, inscribed and circumscribed polygon, circle, arcs (three-point, centre-ends, tangent, fillet), spline, ellipse and partial ellipse, pick lines. Options: chain, offset, radius. - Each line has a line style (DOC-GFX-013). Detail lines are view-owned and appear only in their view. - Pick lines copies the geometry of model edges into detail lines (not associative). - Detail lines can be edited with the modify tools of Chapter 3 (move, copy, rotate, mirror, trim/extend, split, offset, align) and with their end-point grips. Joined end points (from Chain or snapping) move together when one is dragged, unless the join is broken with Disallow join. - Detail lines are drawn above model content and below annotation, in their draw order (DOC-ANN-020). They can be dimensioned and can host masking. - Changing the line style of a selection is one command; the style list shows only line styles of the Lines category (DOC-GFX-013). Detail lines can also be converted to model lines and back (Chapter 3), which moves them between view ownership and the model. - Zero-length segments are not created; a curve shorter than the project's short-curve tolerance (Chapter 2) is refused with a warning. - Interactive tool. Drawing follows Conventions §2.1: each finished segment is a micro-operation detail.segment(curve, style), so a crash loses at most the segment being drawn.

    Data (RXD). anno.detailline: style, curve (line, arc, circle, ellipse or spline in view coordinates), joins[] (ids of joined lines at each end), drawOrder.

    Commands. detail.line(view_id, curves[], line_style_id?) -> annotation_id[]; detail.set_line_style(annotation_ids[], line_style_id) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A chain of detail lines drawn with Chain on forms connected segments sharing end points. - [ ] Dragging a shared end point of a chain moves both joined lines. - [ ] A detail line in one plan does not appear in a duplicate of that plan made with plain Duplicate.

    Filled and masking regions

    ID: DOC-ANN-017 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §4.6

    Behaviour & rules. - Annotate › Detail › Region ▾ › Filled Region or Masking Region: sketch one or more closed loops (nested loops become holes). - Filled region type: foreground pattern and colour, background pattern and colour, masking (opaque) on/off, boundary pen. Each boundary edge has its own line style, which may be <Invisible lines>. - Masking region: an opaque region in the background colour that hides model and annotation beneath it in its view; boundary lines are optional. - Area of a filled region is reported as a read-only parameter. - Loops must be closed and must not self-intersect; nested loops alternate between region and hole; touching or overlapping sibling loops are refused at Finish with the problem edge highlighted. - Region fill patterns may be drafting patterns (scale with the view) or model patterns (real size, DOC-GFX-014). With Masking on in the type, the region hides everything beneath it in draw order, like a masking region, and still shows its own pattern. - Editing the boundary (Edit Boundary) re-enters sketch mode; the sketch follows Conventions §2.1 with micro-operations region.segment, region.delete, region.style and a replay function. - Region edges mask coincident lines (DOC-OUT-001) lets region boundaries hide model lines that lie exactly on them in print. - Filled regions can be placed in any 2D view, on sheets, in legends and in detail groups. IFC annotation export writes them as IfcAnnotationFillArea (DOC-IFC-002).

    Data (RXD). anno.region: regionKind (filled | masking), type, loops[], edgeStyles[], drawOrder. Region types: standards/text_styles, kind regiontype (fgPattern, fgColour, bgPattern, bgColour, masking, pen).

    Commands. region.create(view_id, loops[], kind: filled|masking, type_id?, edge_styles?) -> annotation_id (invalid loops fail with region.invalid_loops); regiontype.create(name, fg_pattern?, fg_colour?, bg_pattern?, bg_colour?, masking?, pen?) -> type_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A masking region hides the model linework beneath it on screen and in the PDF. - [ ] A filled region with an inner loop reports its area as the outer area minus the hole. - [ ] A sketch with two overlapping loops is refused at Finish.

    Detail components, repeating details, insulation and detail groups

    ID: DOC-ANN-018 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §4.6

    Behaviour & rules. - Detail component (Annotate › Detail › Component ▾, default shortcut CM): point-based or line-based detail item families (studs, bolts, flashings and so on), view-owned, taggable and keynotable. - Repeating detail: a line-based array of a detail component.
