Type: component, layout (fill available space, fixed distance, fixed number, maximum spacing), inside (whether end components stay inside the line), spacing, component rotation. - Insulation: batt insulation drawn along a line, with width and bulge-to-width ratio (1/x). - Detail group: a reusable named group of view-owned elements; instances update when the definition changes. Groups follow Chapter 3 group rules, restricted to view-owned elements.

    Data (RXD). anno.component (type, position, rotation, curve for line-based), anno.repeating (type, curve), anno.insulation (curve, width, bulgeRatio); detail groups in model/groups with scope = "detail".

    Commands. detail.component(view_id, type_id, position_or_curve, rotation?) -> annotation_id; detail.repeating(view_id, type_id, curve) -> annotation_id; detail.insulation(view_id, curve, width, bulge_ratio?) -> annotation_id; detail.create_group(view_id, annotation_ids[], name) -> group_id; detail.place_group(view_id, group_id, position) -> annotation_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Lengthening a repeating brick detail adds bricks according to the layout rule. - [ ] Editing a detail group definition updates all instances in all views.

    Draw order

    ID: DOC-ANN-020 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §4.6 Draw order

    Purpose. Control which view-owned drafting is drawn on top where items overlap.

    Workflow. Select drafting items › Modify › Arrange: Bring to Front, Bring Forward, Send to Back, Send Backward (default shortcuts: none; assignable in the keymap, Chapter 1).

    Behaviour & rules. - Modify › Arrange: Bring to Front, Bring Forward, Send to Back, Send Backward. Draw order applies among view-owned drafting (detail components, regions, detail lines) in the same view. Model content is always behind drafting; masking regions mask only what lies below them in this order. - Annotation (text, tags, dimensions, symbols) is always above drafting and is not ordered by this command; selecting annotation disables the Arrange buttons. - Forward and Backward move an item past the next item that overlaps it, not past items elsewhere in the view, so the result is visible after one click. - New drafting items are placed at the front. Copying preserves relative order within the copied set and places the set at the front of the target view. - Items in a detail group keep their order inside the group; the group as a whole is ordered among the other items. - Draw order is honoured in every output, because the draw list sorts view-owned drafting by it (DOC-HLR-004).

    Data (RXD). Each annotation object has an integer drawOrder; ties are broken by id. Reordering rewrites drawOrder only on the moved objects (gaps are used) so that concurrent edits of other items in the same view merge cleanly.

    Commands. detail.arrange(annotation_ids[], action: front|forward|back|backward) -> () (annotation ids of the wrong kind fail with detail.not_drafting)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Sending a filled region to the back makes a detail component above it visible in the PDF. - [ ] Bring Forward on a line under two overlapping regions puts it above the nearer region only. - [ ] Reordering one item changes only that item's RXD object.

    Revision clouds

    ID: DOC-ANN-021 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §4.6, §5.7

    Behaviour & rules. - Annotate › Detail › Revision Cloud: sketch lines, arcs or a rectangle in any view or on a sheet; the cloud's arcs are generated along the sketch with the project's arc length (paper mm). - Each cloud has a Revision property; it defaults to the latest revision that is not issued. - Clouds of an issued revision cannot be added, moved or edited (DOC-SHT-008). - The cloud's revision appears in the revision schedule of every sheet that shows the cloud (directly on the sheet, or in a view placed on it, if the cloud is inside the crop). - Revision tags are tags of the revision cloud category; they show the revision number (per project or per sheet, DOC-SHT-008).

    Data (RXD). anno.revcloud: revision id, loops[] (sketch), arcLength override (optional). Revisions in project/revisions.

    Commands. revcloud.create(view_id, loops[], revision_id?) -> annotation_id; revcloud.set_revision(annotation_ids[], revision_id) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Drawing a cloud in a plan that is placed on sheet A101 adds the revision to A101's revision schedule. - [ ] Moving a cloud of an issued revision is refused.

    Colour fill legends and colour schemes

    ID: DOC-ANN-022 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §4.6 Color schemes, Color Fill Legend

    Purpose. Colour rooms, areas, spaces, zones, ducts and pipes by parameter, with a legend.

    Workflow. 1. Annotate › Color Fill › Color Fill Legend: click in a plan or section; choose the space category and colour scheme. 2. Edit Scheme (from the legend or the view property Color Scheme): category, scheme title, Colour by parameter, By value or By range (range edges, units, stepping), include linked elements, per-value colour, fill pattern and visibility; the In use column shows values present in the model.

    Behaviour & rules. - A view uses one colour scheme per category; the view property Color Scheme Location puts fills behind (Background) or in front of (Foreground) model geometry. - New values found in the model get colours automatically from a perceptually distinct palette; the user can lock colours. - The legend lists the values present in the view (or all values, by legend type) and updates automatically.

    Data (RXD). Colour schemes in views/color_schemes (kind colorscheme: category, parameter, mode, entries[] of {value or range, colour, pattern, visible}); legends as anno.colorlegend (scheme, position, columns).

    • Colour scheme editor (colorscheme.edit; Edit Scheme on a selected legend, the view property Color Scheme, or Architecture › Room & Area ▾ › Color Schemes). Left: category picker and the list of schemes for that category (Duplicate, Rename, Delete). Right: title, Colour parameter, By value / By range, Include elements from links, and the entries table (Value or range, Visible, Colour, Fill pattern, Preview, In use) with Add, Remove, Move up and down. In range mode the table edits the range edges, units and the step used by Add. Validation: range edges must increase; a value can appear once; a scheme in use by a view cannot be deleted (the views are listed); changing the parameter of a scheme in use asks for confirmation because it rebuilds the entries. OK applies all changes through colorscheme.set_entry and related commands as one undo step.

    Commands. colorscheme.create(name, category, parameter, mode: value|range, ranges?) -> scheme_id; colorscheme.set_entry(scheme_id, value_or_range, colour?, pattern_id?, visible?) -> (); colorscheme.edit(scheme_id?) -> () (opens the editor above); view.set_color_scheme(view_id, category, scheme_id? (none clears), location?: background|foreground) -> (); colorlegend.place(view_id, scheme_id, position) -> annotation_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Colouring rooms by Department shows each department in its own colour, and adding a room with a new department adds a legend row.

    Matchlines

    ID: DOC-ANN-023 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §4.7, §1.8

    Purpose. Mark where a plan split across dependent views (and sheets) continues.

    Workflow. View tab › Sheet Composition › Matchline enters sketch mode; draw one or more lines (open polylines are allowed); set Top and Bottom constraints in Properties; Finish. Add view references beside it (DOC-ANN-024).

    Behaviour & rules. - View tab › Sheet Composition › Matchline: sketch one or more lines in a parent plan (or in a dependent view, which adds the matchline to the parent). - Matchlines are visible in the parent and in all its dependents. Their vertical extent (top and bottom constraints) controls which sections and elevations show them. - Appearance comes from the Matchline object style and the view's annotation category settings. - Top and Bottom are a level plus offset, or Unlimited; the default is the parent's level to the level above. Plans of other levels whose cut plane lies within that range also show the matchline when they are parents of dependents with the same scope boxes; otherwise matchlines belong to one parent only. - A matchline does not crop anything; the dependents' crop regions do. Reviera offers Fit crops to matchline on the contextual tab, which snaps the nearest crop edges of the dependents to the matchline (one undo step). - Editing a matchline (Edit Sketch) follows the sketch-mode rules of Conventions §2.1. Deleting the parent's last dependent leaves the matchline in place. - The matchline is printed with its view; Hide crop boundaries does not hide it.

    Data (RXD). anno.matchline in the parent view's annotation document: curves[], topLevel, bottomLevel, offsets.

    Commands. matchline.create(view_id, curves[], top?, bottom?) -> annotation_id (when view_id is a dependent view, the matchline is stored on its parent and the parent id is in the result's owner)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A matchline sketched in a parent plan appears in both of its dependent views. - [ ] A matchline with Top = Level 3 appears in a section through it between the parent level and Level 3 only. - [ ] Fit crops to matchline moves the facing crop edges of two dependents onto the matchline in one undo step.

    View references

    ID: DOC-ANN-024 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §4.7

    Behaviour & rules. - View tab › Sheet Composition › View Reference: choose the view kind and the target view; place the symbol (usually beside a matchline). - The symbol shows the target's detail number and sheet number, and may show the sheet collection and shared parameters. The reference label is per instance, with a type default (DOC-VIEW-004). - Double-clicking the symbol opens the target view. - When the target is not on a sheet, the symbol shows placeholder dashes. - The target list on the contextual tab is filtered by view kind (floor plans, ceiling plans, sections, elevations, drafting views, dependent views) and by name; dependents of the current view's parent are listed first. - When the target view is deleted, the view reference is orphaned (DOC-CORE-003) and shows "?"; Change target re-points it. - View references can be placed in plans, sections, elevations, callouts, drafting views and on sheets; they are view-owned and are copied by Duplicate with Detailing. - In combined PDF output they become internal links to the target's sheet (DOC-OUT-003). view.find_referring (DOC-VIEW-001) lists them as referrers of their target.

    Data (RXD). anno.viewref: target (view id), position, label, type, rotation.

    Commands. viewref.create(view_id, target_view_id, position, type_id?, label?) -> annotation_id; view.go_to_target(annotation_id) -> view_id (fails with viewref.orphaned when the target is gone)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] After the target dependent view is placed on sheet A103 as detail 2, the view reference reads "2 / A103". - [ ] Deleting the target view shows "?" in the symbol and lists it in the warnings. - [ ] In a combined PDF, clicking the view reference opens sheet A103.

    5.14 Schedules

    Schedules are tabular views of live model data. Every schedule definition is an RXD document schedules/<scheduleId> (kinds schedule.*). Cell values are always computed and never stored.

    Creating schedules

    ID: DOC-SCH-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §2 intro, §2.1, §2.4

    Purpose. List elements of a category (or of several categories) with chosen parameters.

    Workflow. 1. View tab › Create › Schedules ▾ › Schedule/Quantities (or another kind, DOC-SCH-006). 2. New Schedule dialog: discipline filter, category list (including Multi-Category, Sheets, Views, Sheet Collections, Revisions), Schedule building components or Schedule keys (with key name), name, phase, Include elements in links. 3. OK opens the Schedule Properties dialog (DOC-SCH-002 onwards); OK there opens the schedule view.

    Behaviour & rules. - A component schedule has one row per element (or per group of identical rows when Itemize every instance is off, DOC-SCH-005). - A multi-category schedule lists elements of all model categories and offers only parameters common to them (shared parameters, IFC common properties, and built-in identity fields). - Schedules are phase-specific: they list elements that exist in the schedule's phase, filtered by its phase filter (DOC-GFX-017). Design options: the primary option by default, or a chosen option per set. - Include elements in links adds rows from loaded linked models; those rows are read-only. - Evaluation is incremental: a parameter change re-evaluates only affected rows, totals and groups.

    Data (RXD). schedules/<id>, kind schedule.component (or schedule.keyschedule): category (or "multi"), phase, phaseFilter, designOptions, includeLinks, and the blocks fields, filters, sortGroup, formatting, appearance, embedded, layout (headers, merges, images, column widths).

    Commands. schedule.create(kind, category, name, phase_id?, include_links?, key_name?) -> schedule_id; schedule.get_table(schedule_id, include_hidden?) -> table (query; also MCP resource reviera://schedule/{id})

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A door schedule lists every door of the schedule's phase and gains a row when a door is placed. - [ ] schedule.get_table returns the same cell text the schedule view shows, including totals.

    Fields

    ID: DOC-SCH-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §2.2 Fields tab

    Behaviour & rules. - Fields tab: available fields on the left, scheduled fields on the right, with move up/down; Select available fields from: the category, related categories (for example the room a door opens from and to, the host level, the type), or a linked model; field search and filters by parameter kind. - Buttons: New parameter (creates a project parameter bound to the category, Chapter 2), Add calculated parameter, Combine parameters, Edit, Delete. - Combined parameters: concatenate several parameters into one column, each with prefix, suffix and separator; a sample preview is shown. - Built-in fields include Count, Family, Type, Family and Type, IFC GlobalId, IFC Class, Workset, Phase Created, Phase Demolished, Design Option, and element quantities (length, area, volume) from IFC quantity sets or computed by OCCT. - Removing a field also removes filters, sorting and formatting that use it, after confirmation.

    Data (RXD). fields[]: {id, source: param|related|calculated|combined|builtin, parameter, relation?, heading, ...}.

    Commands. schedule.add_field(schedule_id, field_source, index?) -> field_id; schedule.remove_field(schedule_id, field_id) -> (); schedule.move_field(schedule_id, field_id, index) -> (); schedule.combine_fields(schedule_id, parts[], name) -> field_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A door schedule with To Room: Name shows the name of the room each door opens into. - [ ] A combined field "Level-Number" with separator "-" shows "L1-101".

    Calculated values

    ID: DOC-SCH-003 · Priority: P0 (formula), P1 (percentage) · Ref: research/04 §2.2 Calculated values

    Behaviour & rules. - A calculated field has a name, discipline, value type (length, area, volume, number, integer, currency, yes/no, text, and so on), and either a formula or a percentage. - Formulas use the formula language of Chapter 2: arithmetic, comparison, if, and, or, not, trigonometric functions, round, roundup, rounddown, abs, sqrt, min, max, text concatenation, and unit-aware arithmetic (for example dividing an area by a length gives a length). A formula whose units do not match its value type is rejected with an explanation. - A percentage field gives one field's value as a percentage of its total within the current group or the grand total. - Calculated fields can be used for filtering, sorting, grouping and conditional formatting (an improvement over the reference, where some of these are limited).

    Data (RXD). fields[] entry with source = "calculated", valueType, formula or percentage {of, by: group|grandtotal}.

    Commands. schedule.add_calculated_field(schedule_id, name, value_type, formula?, percentage_of?, percentage_by?) -> field_id; schedule.update_calculated_field(schedule_id, field_id, formula?, value_type?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A calculated field Area * 1.2 of type Area shows values 20 % larger than Area. - [ ] Area / Width with value type Area is rejected because the result is a length.

    Filters

    ID: DOC-SCH-004 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §2.2 Filter tab · screenshots/documentation/schedule_properties_filter_tab.png

    Behaviour & rules. - Filter tab: a list of rules field · operator · value, combined with AND by default. Operators as in DOC-GFX-006. - Reviera removes the reference's limit of eight AND rules: the filter is a rule tree with nested AND/OR sets, using the same editor and evaluation engine as view filters (DOC-GFX-006). Hidden fields and calculated fields can be used. - Filter by sheet: when the schedule is placed on a sheet, each instance shows only elements visible in views placed on that sheet. - Rules can test any scheduled field, including hidden, calculated and combined fields, and any parameter of the category that is not scheduled (the editor lists them under Other parameters). Values are entered in display units; text comparisons follow the operator's case rule (case-insensitive by default, with a Match case option per rule). - A rule whose field is later removed from the schedule stays valid when it tests a category parameter; it is marked invalid when it tested a calculated field that no longer exists, and an invalid rule is ignored with a warning banner on the schedule view. - Elements of linked models are filtered with the same rules (DOC-SCH-001). - Filter by sheet evaluates visibility in each viewport's view after crop, view range, hidden elements and filters; temporary hiding is ignored. On a schedule view that is not on a sheet, the option has no effect and the schedule shows all rows. - Evaluation shares the compiled predicates of view filters (DOC-GFX-006) and is incremental: only elements whose tested parameters change are re-evaluated.

    Data (RXD). filters rule tree (same schema as filter.rule's ruleTree), filterBySheet.

    Commands. schedule.set_filter(schedule_id, rule_tree?, filter_by_sheet?) -> () (a rule naming an unknown field fails with schedule.unknown_field)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Filter "(Level = L1 OR Level = L2) AND Fire Rating has a value" lists exactly the matching doors. - [ ] A door schedule with Filter by sheet on sheet A101 lists only doors visible in views on A101. - [ ] A filter on a hidden calculated field "Area per person < 10 m²" hides the matching rows while the field stays hidden. - [ ] Hiding a door in a plan on A101 removes it from A101's filtered schedule instance; temporary hiding does not.

    Sorting, grouping and totals

    ID: DOC-SCH-005 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §2.2 Sorting/Grouping tab

    Behaviour & rules. - Sort by, then any number of Then by levels, each ascending or descending, with Header, Footer (title, count and totals / title and totals / count and totals / totals only) and Blank line options. - Grand totals with the same choices and a custom title. - Itemize every instance: when off, rows with identical values in all sorted fields collapse into one row; non-identical cells in that row are left blank, and Count shows the number of collapsed elements. - Sorting is natural (so "Door 2" comes before "Door 10") and unit-aware. - Totals are computed per field according to the field's calculation mode (DOC-SCH-007).

    Data (RXD). sortGroup[]: {field, descending, header, footer, blankLine}; grandTotals {mode, title}; itemize.

    Commands. schedule.set_sort_group(schedule_id, levels[], grand_totals?, itemize?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Grouping doors by Level with footer "Count and totals" shows a count per level and a grand total equal to the number of doors. - [ ] With itemize off, 12 identical door types on one level collapse to one row with Count = 12.

    Schedule kinds

    ID: DOC-SCH-006 · Priority: P0 (component, sheet list, revision schedule), P1 (key, material takeoff, view list, note block, keynote legend), P2 (graphical column schedule; panel schedules are specified in Chapter 4) · Ref: research/04 §2.4, §5.2, §5.6

    Kind (RXD kind) Rows Notes
    Component schedule.component elements of a category, or of all categories (multi-category) DOC-SCH-001.
    Key schedule schedule.keyschedule user-defined keys Each key row sets several parameters at once. Elements of the category gain a key parameter; choosing a key writes the key's values into the element's parameters (they become read-only on the element while the key is set). Rows are added with Insert data row.
    Material takeoff schedule.material one row per (element, material) Material fields (name, area, volume, cost, description, plus custom material parameters) combined with element fields. Areas and volumes are computed per compound layer or per solid with OCCT. As paint option for painted face materials.
    Sheet list schedule.sheetlist sheets and placeholder sheets Fields: sheet number and name, current revision, drawn/checked/approved/designed by, issue date, appears in sheet list, sheet collection, scale (or "As indicated"), sheet width and height, title-block parameters, primary title block. Insert data row adds a placeholder sheet (DOC-SHT-007).
    View list schedule.viewlist views View name, kind, scale, detail level, template, phase, sheet number, dependency, sheet collection. Some fields (such as name, scale, title on sheet) are editable from the list.
    Note block schedule.noteblock instances of a chosen generic annotation family Note number and text; filter by sheet.
    Keynote legend schedule.keynotelegend keynotes in use DOC-VIEW-010.
    Revision schedule schedule.revision revisions on the sheet Defined inside title block families (Chapter 2) and evaluated per sheet: sequence, number, description, date, issued to, issued by. Usually built bottom-up with a fixed height.
    Graphical column schedule schedule.graphicalcolumn grid × level matrix of structural columns Groups similar columns, shows level ranges and off-grid columns. Rendered as a drawing, not a table.
    Sheet collection schedule sheet collections Schedules the collection's custom parameters (DOC-SHT-006).

    Commands. Kinds are chosen in schedule.create. In addition: schedule.insert_data_row(schedule_id, values?) -> row_key (key schedules and sheet-list placeholders); schedule.delete_data_row(schedule_id, row_key) -> (); element.set_key(element_ids[], key_parameter, row_key?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Assigning key "Office Standard" to 30 rooms sets their four finish parameters in one undo step. - [ ] A material takeoff of walls reports a concrete volume matching the sum of the concrete layers' volumes within 0.1 %. - [ ] A sheet list shows placeholder rows next to real sheets, sorted by number.

    Formatting and conditional formatting

    ID: DOC-SCH-007 · Priority: P0 (formatting), P1 (conditional formatting) · Ref: research/04 §2.2 Formatting tab

    Behaviour & rules. - Per field: heading text, heading orientation (horizontal or vertical), alignment (left, centre, right), field format (units, rounding, unit symbol, digit grouping; or Use project settings), hidden field (kept for sorting and filtering, not shown), calculation (standard, totals, minimum, maximum, minimum and maximum). - Conditional format: rules per field, each test → cell background colour (and optionally text colour and bold). The test can use any field of the row, not just the formatted one. Rules are checked in order; the first match wins. Show conditional format on sheets controls whether colours print.

    Data (RXD). formatting per field: heading, orientation, align, format, hidden, calculation, conditional[] {ruleTree, background, textColour, bold}, showConditionalOnSheets.

    Commands. schedule.set_field_format(schedule_id, field_id, heading?, orientation?, align?, format?, hidden?, calculation?) -> (); schedule.add_conditional_format(schedule_id, field_id, rule_tree, background, text_colour?, bold?) -> rule_id; schedule.remove_conditional_format(schedule_id, rule_id) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A rule "Area < 10 m²" colours those cells red in the schedule view, and in print only when Show on sheets is on.

    Appearance

    ID: DOC-SCH-008 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §2.2 Appearance tab

    Purpose. Control how a schedule looks on sheets and in its view.

    Workflow. Schedule Properties › Appearance tab, or the Appearance panel of the Modify Schedule tab for cell-level styling (DOC-SCH-010).

    Behaviour & rules. - Build schedule top-down or bottom-up; grid lines (line style) and whether grid lines show in headers, footers and spacers; outline (line style); row height variable or user-defined; stripe rows (colour; whether they print); show title; show headers; text types for title, headers and body. - Blank row before data inserts one empty row between headers and data. - Text types are the project's text types (DOC-ANN-009); their size is in paper millimetres, so a schedule's printed size never depends on a view scale. - Row height: Variable fits the tallest wrapped cell; a fixed height (paper mm) clips longer text and marks the clipped cells in the schedule view. - The schedule view on screen shows the same fonts and grid as the sheet, but with alternating row shading only when Stripe rows is on and with interactive column letters and row numbers that never print. - Cell styles set in the schedule view (DOC-SCH-010) override the appearance settings for those cells. - Appearance may be included in a schedule view template (DOC-GFX-004).

    Data (RXD). appearance block: buildOrder (top_down | bottom_up), gridLines {style, inHeaders, inFooters, inSpacers}, outline, rowHeight (variable or mm), stripe {colour, print}, showTitle, showHeaders, blankRowBeforeData, textTypes {title, header, body}.

    Commands. schedule.set_appearance(schedule_id, appearance) -> () (a line style or text type that does not exist fails with schedule.unknown_style)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A bottom-up schedule lists its first row at the bottom, directly above the headers. - [ ] Changing the body text type from 2.5 mm to 3.5 mm enlarges the placed schedule on every sheet. - [ ] With Stripe rows on and print off, the PDF shows no stripes.

    Embedded schedules

    ID: DOC-SCH-009 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/04 §2.2 Embedded Schedule tab

    Purpose. Show, under each room or space, the elements it contains.

    Workflow. Schedule Properties › Embedded Schedule tab: tick Embedded schedule, choose the category, then Embedded Schedule Properties…, which opens a nested Fields / Filter / Sorting/Grouping / Formatting / Appearance dialog.

    Behaviour & rules. - Room and space schedules can embed a sub-schedule of a related category (for example the furniture in each room, or the air terminals in each space). The embedded schedule has its own fields, filter, sorting and formatting, and its rows appear under each parent row. - Containment is decided by the element's room or space calculation point (Chapter 3 room rules; Chapter 4 for spaces), in the schedule's phase. Elements in no room are not listed. - Parent schedules allowed: rooms, spaces, areas, and zones (HVAC). One level of embedding only. - Parent rows with no embedded rows show the parent row alone; Show empty parents can hide them. - Embedded rows are editable in the schedule view like normal rows (DOC-SCH-010); totals of the embedded schedule are per parent. - Export (DOC-SCH-012) writes embedded rows indented under their parent, with the embedded headers once per parent.

    Data (RXD). embedded: a nested schedule definition with relation (for example room-contents, space-contents), category, and its own fields, filters, sortGroup, formatting, showEmptyParents.

    Commands. schedule.set_embedded(schedule_id, category?, definition?) -> () (with no category, embedding is removed; a parent that is not a room, space, area or zone schedule fails with schedule.embed_not_supported)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A room schedule with embedded furniture shows each room's furniture rows below the room row. - [ ] Moving a chair from room 101 to room 102 moves its row to room 102. - [ ] Embedding in a door schedule is refused with schedule.embed_not_supported.

    Editing in the schedule view

    ID: DOC-SCH-010 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §2.3 · screenshots/documentation/schedule_view_room_finish_grouped_headers.png

    Purpose. Use the schedule as a spreadsheet-like editor for the model.

    UI. The schedule view is a grid with lettered columns. Contextual tab Modify Schedule: - Parameters: Format Unit, Calculated, Delete, Combine Parameters. - Columns: Insert, Delete, Resize, Hide, Unhide All. - Rows: Insert (title/header rows, or data rows for key schedules and sheet lists), Delete, Resize. - Titles & Headers: Merge/Unmerge, Insert Image, Clear Cell, Group, Ungroup. - Appearance: Shading, Borders, Reset, Font, horizontal and vertical alignment. - Element: Highlight in Model.

    Behaviour & rules. - Editing a cell writes the parameter of the underlying element through a normal parameter command (undoable, checked against ownership in BIMserver mode, Chapter 6). Editing a type parameter shows how many instances will change and asks for confirmation. A cell in a collapsed row (itemize off) edits all elements of the row. - Read-only cells (computed values, linked rows, values controlled by a key) are shown greyed. - Group headers: selecting several adjacent column headers and choosing Group adds a common parent header (for example "Finishes" over base, floor, wall and ceiling columns). - Selecting rows selects the elements; Highlight in Model opens or chooses a view that shows them and zooms to them. - Column widths set here apply to the schedule on every sheet. - Paste from the clipboard into a range of editable cells is supported (tab-separated text), as one undoable command.

    Data (RXD). layout: headerGroups[], merges[], images[] (asset references), columnWidths[], cellStyles[].

    Commands. schedule.set_cell(schedule_id, row_key, field_id, value) -> (); schedule.paste(schedule_id, top_left, tsv_text) -> (); schedule.group_headers(schedule_id, field_ids[], caption) -> (); schedule.ungroup_headers(schedule_id, group_id) -> (); schedule.merge_cells(schedule_id, range) -> (); schedule.insert_image(schedule_id, cell, image_asset) -> (); schedule.set_column_width(schedule_id, field_id, width_mm) -> (); schedule.highlight_in_model(schedule_id, row_keys[]) -> view_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing a door's Fire Rating in the schedule changes the door, and Undo restores it. - [ ] Pasting 20 rows of values from a spreadsheet application fills 20 rows in one undo step.

    Schedules on sheets

    ID: DOC-SCH-011 · Priority: P0 (place), P1 (split) · Ref: research/04 §2.5 · screenshots/documentation/schedule_room_finish_on_sheet.png

    Workflow. 1. Drag a schedule from the Project Browser onto a sheet. A schedule may be placed on any number of sheets. 2. Resize columns with the triangle grips (applies to the schedule everywhere). 3. Split: click the split control on the side of the placed schedule to split it at that row, or use Split & Place (number of segments, segment height), which places segments side by side on the same sheet. Drag a segment back onto the previous one to join them. 4. Rotate the schedule instance on the sheet (0°, 90°, −90°).

    Behaviour & rules. - Each segment has its own height and position; Repeat headers is a per-instance option. - When rows are added, the last segment grows. If it would run off the title block's drawing area, a warning marker appears on the segment. - Filter by sheet (DOC-SCH-004) uses the sheet of each placed instance. - Edit Schedule (context menu, with a default shortcut) opens the schedule view.

    Data (RXD). In sheets/<sheetId>: scheduleInstances[] {schedule, position, rotation, segments[] {startRow, height, position}, repeatHeaders}.

    Commands. sheet.place_schedule(sheet_id, schedule_id, position) -> instance_id; scheduleinstance.split(instance_id, segment_heights[], positions?) -> (); scheduleinstance.join(instance_id, segment_index) -> (); scheduleinstance.set_rotation(instance_id, angle) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Splitting a 90-row schedule into three segments of 30 rows each places three segments, each with headers when Repeat headers is on. - [ ] The same schedule placed on two sheets with Filter by sheet shows different rows on each.

    Schedule export

    ID: DOC-SCH-012 · Priority: P0 (CSV), P1 (XLSX, ODS) · Ref: research/04 §2.5 Other schedule capabilities

    Behaviour & rules. - File › Export › Reports › Schedule: delimited text (field delimiter, text qualifier, encoding UTF-8 with or without byte-order mark; export title, headers, group headers and footers, blank rows). - Spreadsheet export to XLSX (using a GPL-compatible writer such as rust_xlsxwriter, MIT/Apache) and OpenDocument ODS, keeping group headers, merges, column widths and conditional colours, with numbers written as numeric cells with units in the header. - Export schedules as IFC property sets is an IFC export option (DOC-OUT-006). - Export writes what the schedule shows: hidden fields are omitted, itemize and grouping are respected, conditional formats are kept only in XLSX and ODS, and images are omitted (a note lists them). Values are those of the model snapshot at the start of the command. - Delimited text writes values as displayed (with units when the format shows them), so it round-trips into the reference product and other tools; XLSX and ODS write numeric cells with the unit in the header, so formulas work. - Several schedules can be exported at once to one workbook (one sheet per schedule) through Lua or MCP; worksheet names are truncated to 31 characters and made unique. - An existing file is overwritten only after confirmation in the UI; from Lua and MCP, options.overwrite must be true. - Characters that a spreadsheet would treat as a formula at the start of a text cell (=, +, -, @) are escaped in delimited output, so exported text cannot run as a formula.

    Commands. schedule.export(schedule_id, path, format: csv|tsv|xlsx|ods, options?) -> () (options: delimiter, qualifier, bom, include {title, headers, groupHeaders, footers, blankRows}, overwrite)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An exported XLSX opens in a spreadsheet application with numeric area values that sum to the schedule's grand total. - [ ] A CSV export of a schedule with a hidden field has no column for that field. - [ ] A room name starting with "=" is written to CSV so that a spreadsheet shows it as text.

    5.15 Sheets, title blocks and revisions

    Sheets are paper-space views stored as RXD documents sheets/index and sheets/<sheetId> (kind sheet). Paper coordinates are millimetres from the sheet origin (lower-left corner of the title block's drawing area by default).

    Creating and duplicating sheets

    ID: DOC-SHT-001 · Priority: P0 (create), P1 (duplicate modes) · Ref: research/04 §5.1 · screenshots/documentation/sheet_with_elevation_viewports.png

    Workflow. 1. View tab › Sheet Composition › Sheet; or Project Browser › right-click Sheets or a sheet collection › New Sheet. 2. New Sheet dialog: title block types (with Load…, and None), and Select placeholder sheets (DOC-SHT-007). 3. OK creates the sheet, numbered by incrementing the last number used in the target collection (A101 → A102; numbers ending in letters increment the letter). 4. Duplicate Sheet ▸ Empty sheet / With sheet detailing / With views: for views, choose Duplicate, Duplicate with Detailing or Duplicate as Dependent (DOC-VIEW-011); the new views are placed at the same positions.

    Behaviour & rules. - Sheet properties: number, name, issue date, designed by, checked by, drawn by, approved by, Appears in sheet list, Revisions on sheet (DOC-SHT-008), current revision (read-only: number, date, description, issued by, issued to), sheet collection, guide grid, plus any custom sheet parameters (Chapter 2). - Sheet numbers are unique within a sheet collection (and among sheets not in a collection). A clash is rejected. - Deleting a sheet removes its viewports; the views are kept. - Sheet-owned annotation (text, lines, revision clouds, symbols, images) is stored in the sheet document. - Insert › Image places a raster image or PDF page on a sheet (stored as an RXD asset); Insert › Spreadsheet (P2) places a linked spreadsheet range as a table.

    Data (RXD). sheets/<sheetId>: number, name, collection, parameters{}, titleBlocks[], viewports[], scheduleInstances[], annotation[], revisionsOnSheet[], guideGrid, appearsInSheetList, isPlaceholder.

    Commands. sheet.create(title_block_type_id?, number?, name?, collection_id?, from_placeholder?) -> sheet_id; sheet.duplicate(sheet_id, mode: empty|detailing|views, view_mode?: plain|with_detailing|dependent) -> sheet_id; sheet.set_parameter(sheet_id, name, value) -> (); sheet.delete(sheet_ids[]) -> (); sheet.place_image(sheet_id, asset_or_path, position, size?) -> annotation_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Creating a sheet after A109 proposes A110. - [ ] Duplicating a sheet with views as dependents creates dependent views placed at the same viewport positions. - [ ] Creating sheet A101 in a collection where A101 already exists is rejected; creating it in another collection succeeds.

    Title blocks and project information

    ID: DOC-SHT-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §5.2 · screenshots/documentation/title_block_sheet_information.png

    Purpose. The sheet border and information panel, filled automatically from project, sheet and collection data.

    Behaviour & rules. - Title blocks are annotation families of category Title Blocks, created in the family editor (Chapter 2) from Reviera's own sheet-size templates (ISO A0–A4, ANSI A–E, ARCH A–E, and custom sizes). They contain lines, regions, images, logos and labels. - Label sources, in priority order for the same parameter name: sheet instance value; sheet collection value (DOC-SHT-006); project information value. Project information covers organisation name and description, building name, author, project issue date, status, client name, address, project name and number, plus custom project-information parameters. Where IFC has a home for a value (for example IfcProject.Name, IfcProject.LongName, IfcPostalAddress of the site or building, IfcOrganization of the owner history), Reviera stores it there and reads it back; the rest is RXD. - The Scale label shows the scale of the views on the sheet, or As indicated when they differ. The title block type can set a Scale override for multiple values text. - A sheet can hold several title block instances; the Primary title block flag decides which one supplies values to sheet list schedules. - The sheet's Sheet width and Sheet height come from the primary title block. - A title block family may embed a revision schedule (DOC-SCH-006). - Swap title block: choosing another type in the Type Selector keeps the sheet's viewports in place (they are positioned relative to the sheet origin). - Reset title block positions returns title blocks on selected sheets to the sheet origin.

    Data (RXD). titleBlocks[] {type, position, isPrimary, parameterValues}; project information as IFC attributes where available, otherwise project/settings (projectInfo).

    Commands. titleblock.place(sheet_id, type_id, position?) -> instance_id; titleblock.swap(instance_id, type_id) -> (); titleblock.set_primary(instance_id) -> (); titleblock.reset_positions(sheet_ids[]) -> (); project.set_info(name, value) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing the project name updates the label on every sheet. - [ ] A sheet with views at 1:50 and 1:100 shows "As indicated", or the type's override text when set. - [ ] Swapping an A1 title block for an A0 one keeps all viewports where they were.

    Placing views on sheets (viewports)

    ID: DOC-SHT-003 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §5.3

    Workflow. 1. Drag a view from the Project Browser onto an open sheet; or View tab › Sheet Composition › Place View (dialog listing views not yet placed); or right-click a view › Add to Sheet (choose the sheet). 2. Position the viewport; its view title follows (DOC-SHT-004). 3. Double-click inside a viewport, or use Activate View, to edit the view through the sheet (other sheet content is halftoned); double-click outside or Deactivate View to return. The double-click behaviour is a user option: Activate, Open in its own tab, or Do nothing. Open (context menu) opens the view in its own tab.

    Behaviour & rules. - A model view can be on only one sheet (DOC-CORE-005). Dragging an already placed model view offers to go to its sheet instead. - The viewport shows the view's crop region, or the extents of all visible content if the view is not cropped. Changing the view's crop or scale updates the viewport immediately. - Rotation on sheet: none, 90° clockwise, 90° counter-clockwise. - Swap view: on the Modify | Viewports tab, the view drop-down replaces the placed view with another unplaced view of the same kind group, keeping the position (by view origin or by the anchor, DOC-SHT-005). - Move aligned to sheet: moves selected viewports to another sheet, keeping their positions. - Viewports can be pinned; new viewports are pinned by default (user option). - The Detail number is unique per sheet; new viewports get the next free number. - Align views: while dragging, a viewport snaps so that its grids, levels and reference planes align with those of other viewports on the sheet or on a chosen guide grid. - Open hosting sheet: Project Browser › right-click a placed view › Open Sheet (sheet.open_for_view) opens the sheet that holds the view and selects its viewport. The item is disabled for views not on a sheet. A schedule or legend placed on several sheets opens a picker listing them. - Remove from sheet: Project Browser › expand a sheet › right-click a view under it › Remove from Sheet, or select the viewport and press Delete. Both call viewport.remove; the view itself is kept, its markers in other views lose their sheet and detail numbers (they show placeholder dashes), and any saved position assignment is kept for the next placement.

    Data (RXD). viewports[] {id, view, position, viewportType, rotation, detailNumber, anchor, savedPosition, titleOffset, titleLength, pinned}.

    Commands. sheet.place_view(sheet_id, view_id, position, viewport_type_id?) -> viewport_id; viewport.move(viewport_id, position) -> (); viewport.set_rotation(viewport_id, rotation) -> (); viewport.swap_view(viewport_id, view_id) -> (); viewport.move_to_sheet(viewport_ids[], sheet_id) -> (); viewport.activate(viewport_id, on) -> (); viewport.set_detail_number(viewport_id, number) -> (); viewport.remove(viewport_ids[]) -> (); sheet.open_for_view(view_id) -> sheet_id (fails with view.not_on_sheet; for views on several sheets, without a UI it returns the first by sheet number)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Placing a plan already on sheet A101 onto A102 is refused with an offer to open A101. - [ ] Changing the plan's scale from 1:100 to 1:50 doubles the viewport's size on the sheet. - [ ] Swapping a viewport's view keeps its sheet position when both views share the same view origin. - [ ] Remove from Sheet on a section's viewport keeps the section view and changes its marker head to placeholder dashes.

    Viewport types and view titles

    ID: DOC-SHT-004 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §5.4 · screenshots/documentation/viewport_types_view_titles_sheet.png

    Behaviour & rules. - Viewport type properties: title family (an annotation family whose labels can show view name or Title on sheet, detail number, sheet number, scale, sheet collection, reference label and shared parameters), Show title (yes, no, or only when the sheet has more than one viewport), Show extension line, extension line pen, colour and pattern, Preserve title position. - Instance: Title on sheet (overrides the view name on sheets), detail number, rotation; the title and extension line can be dragged; the extension length has a grip. - View titles snap to view boundaries, crop regions, title block edges and guide grid lines while dragged, without first selecting the viewport.

    Data (RXD). Viewport types in standards/text_styles (kind viewport.type); instance fields in viewports[].

    Commands. viewporttype.create(name, title_type_id?, show_title?, show_extension?, pen?, colour?, pattern_id?, preserve_title_position?) -> type_id; viewport.set_type(viewport_ids[], type_id) -> (); viewport.set_title(viewport_id, offset?, extension_length?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A viewport type with Show title: when multiple hides the title on a sheet with one viewport and shows it when a second viewport is added.

    Guide grids, saved positions and view anchors

    ID: DOC-SHT-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §5.3 Align views, View-to-Sheet Positioning · screenshots/documentation/positioning_view_ribbon_saved_positions_2026.png

    Purpose. Place views consistently across many sheets.

    Behaviour & rules. - Guide grid: View tab › Sheet Composition › Guide Grid; named, with spacing and extents; assigned to sheets through the sheet property. Viewport datums and view titles snap to it. Guide grids are not printed. - Saved positions: with a viewport selected, Save Position stores its sheet position under a name. Views can be assigned a saved position before they are placed; dropping them on any sheet places them at that position. Edit Position (with Finish/Cancel) moves the stored position and updates every viewport assigned to it. Manage Positions renames and deletes positions. - View anchor: View origin (default; ignores the crop, so plans of different levels line up from sheet to sheet), or Centre, Top left, Top right, Bottom right, Bottom left of the crop region (the viewport moves when the crop changes, so that the anchored point stays fixed; the annotation crop is ignored). - Legends and graphical column schedules placed on many sheets can share one saved position. - Saved positions can be transferred to other projects (Chapter 6, COL-MNT-005).

    Data (RXD). sheets/index: guideGrids[] {id, name, spacing, extents}, savedPositions[] {id, name, position, anchor}; viewport fields anchor, savedPosition.

    Commands. guidegrid.create(name, spacing, extents) -> guide_grid_id; sheet.set_guide_grid(sheet_ids[], guide_grid_id?) -> (); position.save(viewport_id, name) -> position_id; position.assign(view_ids[], position_id?) -> (); position.edit(position_id, position) -> (); position.delete(position_id) -> (); viewport.set_anchor(viewport_ids[], anchor) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Assigning a saved position to ten floor plans and placing them on ten sheets puts each at the same sheet coordinates, and the grids line up from sheet to sheet. - [ ] With anchor Top left, enlarging the crop to the right and down leaves the viewport's top-left corner where it was on the sheet.

    Sheet collections

    ID: DOC-SHT-006 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §5.5 · screenshots/documentation/sheet_collections_browser_print_set.png

    Purpose. Group sheets into issue packages, each with its own numbering and data.

    Behaviour & rules. - Project Browser › right-click Sheets › New Sheet Collection; rename; delete (sheets move to no collection). - Sheets move between collections by drag and drop in the browser or through the Sheet collection parameter. - Sheet numbers must be unique within a collection, not across collections. New sheets created in a collection continue its numbering. - Collections have custom parameters (category Sheet Collections), and they can be scheduled. A collection's values show (read-only) on its sheets and in their title block labels. Priority: sheet value, then collection value, then project information value. A parameter bound to both the Sheets and the Sheet Collections categories is two independent parameters. - Sheet collection and Referencing sheet collection parameters are available on views, in filters, schedules and labels (view titles, view references, callout heads, section and elevation marks, title blocks). - Print and export dialogs offer each collection as a selection filter (DOC-OUT-001).

    Data (RXD). sheets/index: collections[] {id, name, parameters{}}; sheet field collection.

    Commands. sheetcollection.create(name) -> collection_id; sheetcollection.rename(collection_id, name) -> (); sheetcollection.delete(collection_id) -> (); sheetcollection.move_sheets(sheet_ids[], collection_id?) -> (); sheetcollection.set_parameter(collection_id, name, value) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Two collections can each hold a sheet numbered G001. - [ ] Setting Issue purpose on a collection shows that text in the title blocks of all its sheets unless a sheet has its own value.

    Sheet list and placeholder sheets

    ID: DOC-SHT-007 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §5.6

    Purpose. List the whole drawing set, including drawings produced elsewhere, and turn planned drawings into real sheets.

    Workflow. 1. Create a sheet list (View tab › Schedules ▾ › Sheet List, DOC-SCH-006) and choose its fields. 2. In the sheet list view, Modify Schedule › Rows › Insert Data Row adds a placeholder; type its number, name and other values in the row. 3. Later, View tab › Sheet Composition › Sheet › Select placeholder sheets (multi-select) creates real sheets from them.

    Behaviour & rules. - A placeholder sheet is a row in a sheet list schedule with no real sheet behind it (for example a consultant's drawing). It is added with Insert data row and can belong to a sheet collection. - New Sheet › Select placeholder sheets turns placeholders into real sheets, keeping number, name and parameter values. - Sheet lists can be filtered (for example Appears in sheet list = yes and collection = X) and placed on a cover sheet. - Placeholder numbers obey the same uniqueness rule as sheets (DOC-SHT-001): a placeholder and a real sheet cannot share a number in one collection. - Placeholders appear in sheet lists, view/sheet sets and the Project Browser (under Sheets, with a placeholder icon), but cannot be opened, printed or exported; output commands skip them and report them. - Placeholders have no title block and no revisions; Current revision is blank unless typed into a custom parameter. - Deleting the placeholder row in a sheet list deletes the placeholder. Real sheets cannot be deleted from a sheet list (the row's Delete is disabled for them).

    Data (RXD). Placeholder sheets are entries in sheets/index with isPlaceholder = true, number, name, collection, parameters{}, and no sheet document. Converting one creates the sheets/<sheetId> document and clears the flag, keeping the same id, so references to it stay valid.

    Commands. sheet.create_placeholder(number, name, collection_id?, parameters?) -> sheet_id; sheet.convert_placeholders(sheet_ids[], title_block_type_id?) -> sheet_id[] (a real sheet in the list fails with sheet.not_placeholder)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Converting a placeholder keeps its number and name and removes the placeholder row. - [ ] Creating a placeholder numbered like an existing sheet in the same collection is refused. - [ ] A view/sheet set containing a placeholder exports the other sheets and reports the placeholder as skipped.

    Revisions

    ID: DOC-SHT-008 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §5.7, §4.6 Revision Cloud

    Purpose. Track issued changes on drawings.

    Workflow. 1. View tab › Sheet Composition › Revisions opens the Sheet Issues/Revisions dialog. 2. Table columns: sequence, revision number (derived), numbering sequence, date, description, issued (checkbox), issued to, issued by, show (cloud and tag / tag / none). Buttons: Add, Move Up/Down, Merge Up/Down, Delete. 3. Settings: numbering per project or per sheet; revision cloud arc length; numbering sequences (numeric with start value, minimum digits, prefix and suffix; alphanumeric with a custom list of values, for example A–Z without I and O). 4. Draw clouds (DOC-ANN-021), tag them, and tick Issued when the revision is issued.

    Behaviour & rules. - A sheet's revisions are the union of the revisions of clouds visible on it (on the sheet, or inside the crop of a view placed on it) and the revisions added manually through Revisions on sheet. - Current revision of a sheet is its highest-sequence revision. - Per-sheet numbering: each sheet numbers its own revisions in sequence order; a revision tag shows the number relevant to the sheet the cloud appears on. - Ticking Issued locks the revision: its clouds cannot be created, moved, edited or deleted, and its row cannot be edited, until it is unticked. - Merge combines a revision with the one above or below; clouds are reassigned. - Deleting a revision is allowed only when no cloud uses it, or after the user reassigns its clouds.

    Data (RXD). project/revisions: kind revision (sequence, numberingSequence, date, description, issued, issuedTo, issuedBy, show), kind revision.sequence, and settings (numberingMode, arcLength). Sheet field revisionsOnSheet[].

    Commands. revision.create(description?, date?, numbering_sequence_id?, index?) -> revision_id; revision.update(revision_id, fields) -> (); revision.set_issued(revision_id, issued) -> (); revision.merge(revision_id, direction: up|down) -> (); revision.reorder(revision_id, index) -> (); revision.delete(revision_id, reassign_to?) -> (); revision.set_settings(numbering?: per_project|per_sheet, arc_length?) -> (); revisionsequence.create(name, kind: numeric|alphanumeric, start?, min_digits?, prefix?, suffix?, values?) -> sequence_id; sheet.set_revisions_on_sheet(sheet_id, revision_ids[]) -> () revision.manage() -> () opens the Sheet Issues/Revisions dialog of the workflow above. Each table edit, button and setting calls the matching command, and OK commits the dialog session as one undo step named "Sheet Issues/Revisions". Validation: a revision row that is issued is read-only except for the Issued tick; Merge and Delete are disabled on issued rows and on the only row; numbering sequence values must be unique and non-empty, and an alphanumeric sequence needs at least one value; a numeric sequence needs a start value of 0 or more and minimum digits 1–6; the cloud arc length must be 1–50 mm (paper). Deleting a revision that clouds use asks for the revision to reassign them to.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A cloud for revision 3 placed in a view on sheet A201 makes revision 3 appear in A201's revision schedule and sets A201's current revision to 3. - [ ] With per-sheet numbering, a sheet whose only revisions are sequences 2 and 5 numbers them 1 and 2. - [ ] Editing a cloud of an issued revision is refused. - [ ] In the Sheet Issues/Revisions dialog, the Merge button is disabled on an issued revision.

    5.16 Assemblies, assembly views and assembly sheets

    An assembly is a named, typed set of model elements that is documented and fabricated as one piece: a precast panel with its reinforcement and lifting anchors, a steel column with its welded plates, a prefabricated bathroom pod, a stud-wall panel, a reception desk. Reviera stores it as an IfcElementAssembly that aggregates its members. This section owns the assembly element, its type, its views and its sheets. Chapter 4 creates assemblies automatically for precast pieces (STR-PRE-002) and steel shop assemblies (STR-STL-010 numbering) and uses the views and sheets defined here for shop drawings (STR-PRE-006). Chapter 2 (DM-ELEM-002) fixes the storage summary.

    The assembly element and assembly types

    ID: DOC-ASM-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/04 §3.6 (Assembly Code setting), §5.1 (assembly-specific sheet fields); web: About Assemblies, Create an Assembly, Assembly Instance Properties, Assembly Type Properties, IfcElementAssembly, IfcElementAssemblyType, IfcElementAssemblyTypeEnum, IfcAssemblyPlaceEnum

    Purpose. Group model elements into a unit that can be tagged, scheduled, filtered, counted and documented, and recognise repeated identical units as instances of one assembly type.

    Workflow. 1. Selection first: select elements, then Modify | <category> › Create › Create Assembly. Tool first: Modify › Create › Create Assembly enters a pick mode with Add (default) and Remove; pick elements, then Finish. 2. The New Assembly dialog shows the naming category (a drop-down of the categories of the picked elements; the category of the most numerous members is preselected), the type name, the IFC assembly type (PredefinedType, default User-defined) and Assembly place (Not defined, Site, Factory). 3. Reviera checks whether an identical assembly type already exists (DOC-ASM-002). If one exists, the dialog says so, the type name is read-only and OK creates another instance of that type. Otherwise the type name is editable, prefilled with the naming category's last type name plus the next number (for example "Walls 004"). 4. OK creates the assembly. The new type appears in the Project Browser under Assemblies, with its instances' count. 5. Create Instance (Project Browser › right-click an assembly type) places a copy of the type's members at a picked point, as a new instance of the same type.

    UI. Ribbon: Modify | <category> › Create › Create Assembly; Modify | Assemblies tab with panels Assembly (Edit Assembly, Disassemble, Create Views, Acquire Views, Compare) and the usual Modify tools. Properties of an instance: Naming Category, Mark, Comments, Assembly Place, Phase Created, Phase Demolished. Type properties: Keynote, Model, Manufacturer, Type Comments, URL, Description, Assembly Code and Assembly Description, Type Mark, Cost, IFC assembly type. Project Browser node Assemblies › type › views and sheets (Chapter 1 §1.13).

    Behaviour & rules. - Members. Most model elements can be members: walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, columns, framing, family instances, parts, MEP segments and fittings, generic models, rebar and fabric. These cannot: annotation and view-owned drafting; elements of a linked model; groups (ungroup first); rooms, areas and spaces; masses; model lines; imported or linked CAD and images; elements in a design option other than the one being edited, and mixtures of main-model and option elements; analytical elements and structural loads; datums. The command lists the rejected picks with the reason and creates the assembly from the rest, or fails with assembly.no_valid_members when nothing is left. - One parent only. An element can be a member of at most one assembly, because IFC allows an element to decompose only one whole. Picking a member of another assembly is refused (assembly.already_member), naming that assembly. - System aggregates as one member. Elements that already decompose a system element of Chapter 3 or 4 (beam system beams, truss chords and webs, curtain wall panels and mullions, stair runs and landings, railing segments, rebar of a reinforcement system, fasteners of a fastener group) cannot be picked individually. The system element itself (beam system, truss, curtain wall, stair, railing, reinforcement system, connection) can be a member as a whole, which nests one IfcElementAssembly (or other aggregate) inside another. This is a deliberate extension of the reference product, which refuses such elements; IFC allows nested assemblies. - Parts. IfcBuildingElementPart members (Chapter 3 parts) are already aggregated by their host. They can still be members: their membership is written as IfcRelAssignsToProduct from the part to the assembly (see Data), and RXD records it. - Ch 4 assemblies. Precast piece assemblies (PRECAST_ASSEMBLY, STR-PRE-002) and steel shop assemblies (STEEL_ASSEMBLY, STR-STL-010 numbering) are assemblies in the sense of this section: they get types, views and sheets here. Their membership is maintained by the Chapter 4 tools; editing their members by hand (DOC-ASM-003) is allowed but marks them modified by user, and the next re-split or re-numbering asks before overwriting. For steel assemblies, the assembly mark from Chapter 4 numbering and the assembly type name are kept equal: Chapter 4 numbering writes both. - Naming category is an instance property used only to name and match types (DOC-ASM-002). Changing it on an instance re-runs matching and may change the instance's type. - Assembly origin. Each instance has an origin (a local coordinate frame). By default it is placed at the minimum corner of the members' bounding box, aligned with the main member's local axes (the first member of the naming category, by member order); for walls this puts X along the wall, Y across it and Z up. The origin orients the assembly views (DOC-ASM-004) and is the frame in which identical assemblies are compared. - Mark. Instance Mark defaults to the next unused number within the type; a duplicate Mark within a type gives a warning but is allowed. Type Mark must be unique among assembly types; a duplicate gives a warning. - Level. The assembly is contained in the storey of its lowest member. Each member keeps its own level reference in RXD, so its level-based parameters keep working and disassembling restores the original containment. - Schedules and filters. Assemblies are a schedulable category (Assemblies), with fields from instance and type properties plus Count and member-derived quantities (sum of member volumes and areas, total weight from materials). Member schedules can show the assembly's type name and Mark through the related field Assembly (DOC-SCH-002). Filters and tags work on assemblies like any category. - Phasing and options. An assembly's phase created is the latest phase created of its members unless set explicitly; members can still be demolished individually. An assembly belongs to the design option of its members.

    Data (IFC mapping). - Instance: IfcElementAssembly with Name = type name, Tag = Mark (for steel assemblies, the Chapter 4 assembly mark), AssemblyPlace from the instance property (SITE, FACTORY or NOTDEFINED), ObjectPlacement = the assembly origin (an IfcLocalPlacement), and PredefinedType left unset when the type sets it. Chapter 4 assemblies keep their own PredefinedType and ObjectType (USERDEFINED with "PRECAST_ASSEMBLY" or "STEEL_ASSEMBLY"). - Members: one IfcRelAggregates (RelatingObject = the assembly, RelatedObjects = the members). Members that already decompose another element (parts) are related by IfcRelAssignsToProduct instead. Members' own IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure is removed while they are aggregated (IFC requires the whole, not its parts, to be contained) and restored on disassembly. - Type: IfcElementAssemblyType related by IfcRelDefinesByType, Name = type name, PredefinedType = the chosen value of IfcElementAssemblyTypeEnum (default USERDEFINED with ElementType = the naming category name, as the schema requires). Identity data go to Pset_ManufacturerTypeInformation and the assembly code to IfcClassificationReference through IfcRelAssociatesClassification, as for other types (Chapter 3). The assembly has no own geometry; viewers draw its members. - RXD: document model/assemblies, kind assembly.type (ifcType reference, namingCategory, signature (the matching hash of DOC-ASM-002), viewOwner (the instance that owns the views), views[], sheets[], template?) and kind assembly.instance (ifc reference, namingCategory, memberOrder[], assignedMembers[] (parts related by IfcRelAssignsToProduct), memberLevels{}, userModified for Chapter 4 assemblies). Category key cat.assemblies (Chapter 2).

    Commands. assembly.create(element_ids[], name?, naming_category?) -> assembly_id (name is the type name, used only when the assembly is unique) assembly.place_instance(assembly_type_id, position, rotation?) -> assembly_id assembly.set_naming_category(assembly_ids[], naming_category) -> () assembly.list(assembly_type_id?) -> assembly_summary[] (query: id, type, Mark, member count, whether it owns the views)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Selecting a wall and two windows in it and choosing Create Assembly with naming category Walls creates type "Walls 001" and one instance; the IFC file contains one IfcElementAssembly aggregating the three elements and typed by an IfcElementAssemblyType. - [ ] Picking a room together with walls creates the assembly from the walls and reports the room as rejected. - [ ] Picking a beam that belongs to a beam system is refused; picking the beam system itself adds it as one nested member. - [ ] A part of a layered wall can be a member; the export relates it by IfcRelAssignsToProduct and the IFC file validates. - [ ] Disassembling restores each member's original storey containment.

    Identical-assembly detection and comparison

    ID: DOC-ASM-002 · Priority: P2 · Ref: web: About Assemblies, Create an Assembly, Work with an Assembly

    Purpose. Decide reliably when two assemblies are the same product, so that they share one type and one set of drawings, and explain the difference when they are not.

    Behaviour & rules. - Two assemblies match when all of these hold: 1. the same naming category; 2. the same number of members, with the same category and type for each corresponding member; 3. the same values of every parameter that affects geometry or material (dimensions, offsets, profile, layer structure, material, rebar shape and size), compared in display precision; 4. each corresponding member occupies the same position and orientation relative to the assembly origin, within 1 mm and 0.01° (project setting Assembly match tolerance); 5. nested members (system aggregates) match recursively by the same rules. Identity data (Mark, comments), phase and workset are not compared. - Correspondence of members is found without relying on pick order: members are sorted by (category, type, position of their reference point in the origin frame), and nested assemblies by their own signature. The resulting order is stored as memberOrder and used for views and annotation mapping (DOC-ASM-005). - Reviera keeps a signature per assembly: a hash of the data in rules 1–5, with positions rounded to the tolerance grid. Signatures are compared first; instances with equal signatures are confirmed with the full comparison (to rule out rounding at the grid edges). - When matching runs: at creation; after any edit of an assembly's members or origin (DOC-ASM-003); after a change to a member that affects rules 2–4 (moving a member, changing its type or a geometric parameter); and after a change of naming category. Matching runs in the background and its result is applied as part of the edit that caused it. - Type changes after edits. When an edit makes an instance unique, it becomes an instance of a new type named "<old type name> (2)" (editable). When an edit makes it identical to another existing type, it joins that type. A type that loses its last instance is deleted, with its views and sheets unless they move with their owner instance (DOC-ASM-004). - Steel and precast numbering (Chapter 4) may use stricter or looser criteria for marks (for example ignoring holes). For those assemblies, Chapter 4 numbering decides the type, and the matching here only reports differences; it never re-types them. - Compare (assembly.compare; Modify | Assemblies › Compare, then pick a second assembly) shows a report of why two assemblies are or are not identical: naming category, member count per category and type, unmatched members, parameter differences per corresponding member (name, value A, value B) and position differences above the tolerance (with the distance). Each line can be clicked to select the members in the view. The same report is returned as data to Lua and MCP.

    Data (RXD). assembly.instance.memberOrder[] and assembly.type.signature in model/assemblies; the tolerance in project/settings › assemblies.matchTolerance {length, angle}.

    Commands. assembly.compare(assembly_id_a, assembly_id_b) -> comparison (query: {identical, naming_category_equal, unmatched_members[], parameter_differences[], position_differences[]}) assembly.find_identical(assembly_id) -> assembly_id[] (query: instances of other types that would match if re-typed, which can only differ by an earlier tolerance setting or by Chapter 4 numbering)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Two wall-and-window assemblies built separately from the same wall type, window type and window position become two instances of one type. - [ ] The same two assemblies with different naming categories become two types. - [ ] Moving the window in one instance by 50 mm makes that instance a new type, and assembly.compare reports the window's position difference of 50 mm. - [ ] Moving it back makes the instance rejoin the original type, and the temporary type is deleted. - [ ] Picking the same elements in a different order produces the same signature.

    Editing, disassembling and deleting assemblies

    ID: DOC-ASM-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: web: Work with an Assembly, Disassemble an Assembly, Delete an Assembly

    Purpose. Change an assembly's membership and orientation, change its type, and take it apart.

    Workflow. 1. Select an assembly (in a project view or an assembly view) › Modify | Assemblies › Edit Assembly (or double-click, depending on the user's double-click option, Chapter 1). 2. In edit mode, a floating panel offers Add, Remove, Finish and Cancel. Pick elements to add or remove. Elements created with any modelling tool while in edit mode join the assembly automatically. 3. The origin marker is shown; drag its arrows or rotate it with its controls to change the origin. 4. Finish applies the edit, re-runs matching (DOC-ASM-002) and reports any type change. 5. To change type: select one or more instances and pick another assembly type in the Type Selector; each instance's members are replaced by a copy of the target type's members placed at the instance's origin. 6. To edit one member without edit mode, Tab-select it inside the assembly and edit it normally. 7. Disassemble removes the assembly and leaves its members in the model. Delete removes the assembly and its members.

    Behaviour & rules. - Edit mode follows Conventions §2.1. Micro-operations: asm.add(element), asm.remove(element), asm.create(element) (an element created during the session), asm.origin(transform); the replay function applies them to the assembly's state at the start of the session so an interrupted edit can be recovered after a crash (Chapter 2b, DM-LIVE-015). Cancel discards the session, including elements created in it. - Removing the last member is refused; use Disassemble. - The member rules of DOC-ASM-001 apply to Add. - Changing the origin changes only the orientation of the assembly views and the comparison frame; members do not move. Because matching uses the origin frame, changing the origin of one instance usually makes it a new type; Reviera offers Apply origin to all instances of the type, which moves each instance's origin by the same relative transform and keeps the type. - Changing type replaces members: the old members are deleted and new ones created, so any annotation on the old members in project views is orphaned (DOC-CORE-003), and the confirmation says how many annotations are affected. Members cannot be swapped this way when they are hosts of elements outside the assembly (for example a wall hosting a door that is not a member); the command refuses with the list. - Disassemble deletes the IfcElementAssembly and its RXD instance object, restores the members' storey containment and their plain IFC relationships, and keeps their GlobalIds. If the instance owned the type's views (DOC-ASM-004) and other instances exist, ownership passes to the oldest remaining instance; if it was the last instance, the type and its views and sheets are deleted after a confirmation that lists them. - Delete of an instance deletes its members (one undo step). Delete of an assembly type (Project Browser › right-click › Delete) deletes all its instances, their members, and the type's views and sheets, after a confirmation that counts each. - In BIMserver mode, editing an assembly requires ownership of the assembly and of every member that changes (Chapter 6); Disassemble requires ownership of all members.

    Data (RXD). Edit sessions are not stored; their result changes IfcRelAggregates / IfcRelAssignsToProduct, the placement and the RXD objects of DOC-ASM-001.

    Commands. assembly.edit_members(assembly_id, add_ids[], remove_ids[]) -> assembly_type_id (returns the instance's type after matching) assembly.set_origin(assembly_id, transform, apply_to_type?) -> () assembly.set_type(assembly_ids[], assembly_type_id) -> () assembly.disassemble(assembly_ids[]) -> element_id[] (returns the freed members) assembly.delete_type(assembly_type_id) -> () Deleting an instance uses element.delete (Chapter 2).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Adding a shelf to one of three identical desk assemblies makes that one a new type; the other two keep the original type and its views. - [ ] A crash during Edit Assembly after two adds is recovered on restart with both adds pending, ready to Finish or Cancel. - [ ] Rotating the origin of one instance with Apply origin to all instances of the type keeps all instances in one type and rotates the type's elevation views. - [ ] Disassembling the only instance of a type with views asks for confirmation and then deletes the type, its views and its sheet; Undo restores all of them. - [ ] Deleting an instance deletes its members; disassembling keeps them with unchanged GlobalIds.

    Assembly views

    ID: DOC-ASM-004 · Priority: P2 · Ref: web: Create Assembly Views and Sheets, Delete an Assembly, Work with an Assembly

    Purpose. Create, in one step, the isolated drawings and lists needed to fabricate an assembly type.

    Workflow. 1. Select an assembly instance › Modify | Assemblies › Create Views, or Project Browser › right-click an assembly type › Create Assembly Views. 2. The Create Assembly Views dialog lists the view kinds with a checkbox, a view template and an Assign / Apply choice each: - 3D Ortho; - Detail Section A (horizontal cut through the middle of the assembly) and Detail Section B (vertical cut through the middle, along the origin's X axis); - Elevations Top, Bottom, Left, Right, Front and Back, looking at the six faces of the box around the assembly aligned with its origin; - Part List (a component schedule of the members); - Material Takeoff (a material takeoff of the members); - Sheet (with a title block type; DOC-ASM-005). It also sets one scale for all graphical views (default 1:10). Schedule templates offered are those whose category matches the members. The choices are remembered as the project default for next time. 3. OK creates the views in one undo step and lists them in the Project Browser under the assembly type. 4. Acquire Views (Modify | Assemblies) moves the type's views and sheets from their current owner instance to the selected instance of the same type.

    Behaviour & rules. - Ownership. Assembly views belong to the assembly type and are drawn from one owner instance of that type. Only one instance of a type owns views. Create Views is unavailable on an instance of a type whose views belong to another instance (the tooltip names it); Create from the Project Browser uses the oldest instance as owner. Because identical instances are identical in their origin frame, the owner's drawings document every instance of the type. - Isolation. An assembly view shows only the owner instance's members (including nested members) and the view's own annotation and drafting; everything else is excluded at the candidate query (stage 1, DOC-HLR-001), before any graphics layer. Members of other assemblies, links and datums are never shown. Annotation in the view may reference only members. - Geometry. Views are set up in the owner's origin frame: elevations and sections are orthographic and cropped to the member bounding box plus a margin (default 5 mm at paper scale on every side, so 50 mm at 1:10); detail sections cut through the box centre, with far clipping at the box; the 3D view is an isometric from the origin's (+X, −Y, +Z) octant with the section box off. Views can afterwards be edited like any view (crop, scale, rotation of the crop, extra annotation, templates). - Live update. When the owner's members change, its views regenerate; when the assembly origin changes, views are re-aligned and their crop regions re-fitted unless the user has edited the crop (then only re-aligned). Annotation stays attached to members by reference. - Type changes. Views go with their owner instance. If an edit moves the owner to another type that already has views, Reviera asks which set to keep (the reference product deletes one set without a choice); the other set is deleted after confirmation. - Extra views. Sections, callouts and duplicates created inside an assembly view inherit its assembly relation and isolation. Assembly views can be placed on assembly sheets or on ordinary sheets, once each (DOC-CORE-005). - Schedules. The part list and material takeoff are ordinary schedules (DOC-SCH-006) with a fixed filter Assembly = this type's owner instance that cannot be removed; their rows are the owner's members. Their Count column counts members of one instance; a Quantity per type field multiplies by the number of instances of the type. - Names. Views are named "<type name> - 3D Ortho", "<type name> - Detail Section A", "<type name> - Top", "<type name> - Part List" and so on; a clash adds a numeric suffix. Renaming the type renames views whose names still start with the old type name. - Tags in assembly views show the owner's values. Tags of instance parameters that differ between identical instances (Mark, Comments) may use the label option List all instances of the type, which shows the values of all instances separated by commas.

    Data (RXD). Views are ordinary views/<viewId> documents (kinds view.3d, view.section, view.elevation, view.detail) with an assembly block: type (the assembly.type id), owner (ifc: reference of the owner instance), role (3d | section_a | section_b | top | bottom | left | right | front | back | extra), cropFitted (true until the user edits the crop). Schedules: schedules/<id> with assembly set. assembly.type.views[] lists them; the defaults of the dialog are in project/settings › assemblies.viewDefaults.

    Commands. assembly.create_views(assembly_type_id, views[], scale?, templates?, sheet?: {title_block_type_id, number?, name?}) -> view_id[] (views[] from 3d, section_a, section_b, top, bottom, left, right, front, back, part_list, material_takeoff; templates maps a view kind to {template_id, mode: assign|apply}; when the type's views are owned by an instance other than the one the user chose, it fails with assembly.views_owned_elsewhere) assembly.acquire_views(assembly_id) -> ()
