    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Create Views with 3D, two sections, six elevations, part list and material takeoff at 1:10 creates eleven views in one undo step, listed under the type in the Project Browser. - [ ] The Front elevation of a precast wall piece shows only the piece, its rebar and its anchors, even where other walls stand in front of it in the model. - [ ] Moving a lifting anchor in the owner instance updates the Front elevation and the part list. - [ ] Acquire Views on a second instance of the type makes it the owner; deleting the first instance afterwards keeps the views. - [ ] Create Views on a non-owner instance is unavailable, and the tooltip names the owner.

    Assembly sheets, documentation templates and propagation

    ID: DOC-ASM-005 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/04 §5.1 (assembly-specific sheet fields); web: Create Assembly Views and Sheets; Chapter 4 STR-PRE-006

    Purpose. Produce one sheet per assembly type quickly and consistently, reuse a proven layout for other types, and carry views and annotation over to similar types.

    Workflow. 1. Tick Sheet in Create Assembly Views (DOC-ASM-004) and choose a title block type; or Project Browser › right-click an assembly type › Create Assembly Sheet. 2. Open the sheet (listed under the assembly type) and drag the type's views onto it; drafting views, legends and other project views may be placed on it too. 3. To reuse the arrangement: on a finished assembly sheet, Save as Assembly Template (sheet context menu) stores the layout. Later, select assembly types or instances › Apply Assembly Template, choose the template, and Reviera creates the views and the sheet and places everything as in the template. 4. To carry views to a similar type: Project Browser › right-click the documented type › Propagate Views…, choose target types, and choose whether to include annotation.

    Behaviour & rules. - Assembly sheets are ordinary sheets (DOC-SHT-001) with an assembly link to their type. They are listed under the assembly type in the Project Browser and also under Sheets when Show assembly sheets is on in the browser organisation. The default sheet number is the type's Type Mark (or its name when Type Mark is empty), and the default sheet name is the type name; numbers follow the uniqueness rule of DOC-SHT-001, with a numeric suffix on a clash. Title block labels can show assembly type and instance parameters (type name, Type Mark, Assembly Code, Description, number of instances, Marks of all instances). - One assembly type may have several assembly sheets. Deleting the type deletes them (DOC-ASM-003). - Identical instances need no propagation: they share the type's views and sheets by definition (DOC-ASM-004). The sheet's Instances label lists their Marks so the drawing states which pieces it covers. - Assembly documentation templates record: the view kinds and their templates, scale, crop margins, the sheet's title block type, each viewport's position (relative to the title block, by role), viewport types, schedule definitions for the part list and takeoff, and annotation rules: per-category tag types to place with Tag All in each view, and per-category dimension rules (overall dimensions, member-to-member dimension strings on faces of chosen categories, as in Chapter 4 shop drawings). Templates contain no element references, so they apply to any assembly type. Chapter 4 shop-drawing configuration (STR-PRE-006) chooses one of these templates per precast element kind. - Applying a template to several types creates one set of views and one sheet per type; with Group identical (the default), identical instances share one type and therefore one sheet. Viewports whose view kind is not in the template are left out. Reviera reports viewports that did not fit within the title block's drawing area and moves them into it if Fit to sheet is on. - Propagate views copies the source type's assembly views (definitions, crop, scale, templates, overrides) to each target type, and, if chosen, its annotation. Annotation is mapped through member correspondence (memberOrder, DOC-ASM-002): a tag or dimension whose references map to members of the same category and type in the target is copied; anything that cannot be mapped is skipped and listed in the report. Targets must have the same naming category; a target that already has views of the same role is skipped unless Replace existing is on. Propagation is one undo step. - Assembly sheets print and export like any sheet; the PDF naming rule can use assembly parameters (DOC-OUT-003).

    Data (RXD). Assembly sheets: sheets/<sheetId> with assembly (assembly.type id), listed in assembly.type.sheets[]. Documentation templates: RXD document model/assemblies, kind assembly.template (name, views[] {role, template, mode, scale, cropMargin}, titleBlockType, viewports[] {role, position, viewportType}, schedules[], tagRules[] {category, tagType, views[]}, dimensionRules[]).

    Commands. assembly.create_sheet(assembly_type_id, title_block_type_id?, number?, name?) -> sheet_id assemblytemplate.save(sheet_id, name) -> template_id (the sheet must be an assembly sheet) assembly.apply_template(assembly_ids_or_type_ids[], template_id, group_identical?=true, fit_to_sheet?=true) -> sheet_id[] assembly.propagate_views(source_type_id, target_type_ids[], include_annotation?=true, replace_existing?=false) -> report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Ticking Sheet in Create Assembly Views creates a sheet numbered with the type's Type Mark and lists it under the type. - [ ] Saving a template from a finished sheet and applying it to ten precast piece assemblies, four of them identical, creates seven sheets with the same viewport layout. - [ ] Propagating views with annotation from type A to a type B that has one extra member copies all tags and dimensions of the shared members and reports none skipped; the extra member gets no annotation. - [ ] The title block of an assembly sheet covering three identical instances lists the three Marks.

    5.17 Output: print, export and rendering

    All output commands work on an immutable model snapshot taken when the command starts, so they can run in the background (DOC-OUT-013) while the user keeps editing. All 2D output comes from the draw list (DOC-HLR-004). Output setups are project data stored in RXD document project/settings (section output), so they travel with the project and can be transferred to other projects (Chapter 6, COL-MNT-005).

    View/sheet sets and print options

    ID: DOC-OUT-001 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §6.1, §6.2 Options · screenshots/documentation/sheet_collections_browser_print_set.png

    Purpose. Choose what to output, and the options common to every 2D output.

    Behaviour & rules. - Range: current window; visible portion of current window; selected views/sheets. The View/Sheet Set dialog lists views and sheets with filters (sheets, views, view kind, sheet collection, name search) and saves the selection as a named set. Sets can also be rule-based (for example "all sheets in collection DD Issue with Appears in sheet list = yes"), so that new sheets join automatically. - Common options: view links in blue (colour output only); hide reference/work planes; hide unreferenced view tags; hide scope boxes; hide crop boundaries; replace halftone with thin lines; region edges mask coincident lines; hide underlay; print orphans in warning colour. - Colour mode: colour, black lines (all non-white lines and text black, fills kept as they are), greyscale. - Hidden-line processing: vector or raster (DOC-HLR-007).

    Data (RXD). project/settings › output.viewSheetSets[] ({id, name, members[] | rule}), output.commonOptions.

    Commands. viewset.save(name, view_and_sheet_ids[]?, rule?) -> set_id; viewset.delete(set_id) -> (); viewset.resolve(set_id) -> view_or_sheet_id[] (query)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A rule-based set of collection DD Issue includes a sheet added to that collection after the set was saved. - [ ] Hide scope boxes removes scope boxes from every output while they remain visible on screen.

    Print

    ID: DOC-OUT-002 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §6.1

    Workflow. File › Print (Ctrl+P). Print dialog: printer and its properties; Print to file; combine into one job or separate jobs; range (DOC-OUT-001); copies, reverse order, collate; Settings… (print setup); Preview; Print.

    Behaviour & rules. - Print setup (named, saved in the project): paper size and source, orientation, paper placement (centre, or offset from corner with x/y), zoom (fit to page, or a percentage; 100 % prints sheets at true size), raster quality, colour mode, options (DOC-OUT-001). Save, Save As, Revert, Rename, Delete. - Printing goes through the platform print system: Reviera renders each page to a vector page description (the same renderer as PDF) and hands it to the printer driver through the wxWidgets printing framework (Windows GDI/XPS, macOS Quartz, CUPS on Linux). - When a sheet is larger than the chosen paper and zoom is 100 %, the dialog warns that the output will be cropped. - Preview shows exactly what will be sent, page by page.

    Data (RXD). output.printSetups[].

    Commands. print.run(range, set_id?, printer?, setup_id?, copies?, combine?) -> job_id; print.setup_save(name, settings) -> setup_id; print.setup_delete(setup_id) -> (); print.preview(range, setup_id?) -> page_images[] (query)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An A1 sheet printed at 100 % on A1 paper measures within 0.5 mm of nominal size between title block corners. - [ ] Printing ten sheets as one job sends ten pages in the order of the view/sheet set.

    PDF export

    ID: DOC-OUT-003 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §6.2 · screenshots/documentation/pdf_export_dialog.png

    Purpose. Native, printer-independent PDF output.

    Workflow. File › Export › PDF (also on the Quick Access Toolbar). Dialog sections: Export range; Export setup (in-session or named; New, Duplicate, Rename, Delete, Save); File (combined file name, or separate files with a naming rule; location); Size (use sheet size, or a paper size; fit to page or zoom %); Paper placement (centre, or offset from corner with no margin / printer limit / user-defined x,y); Orientation (automatic, portrait, landscape); Appearance (raster quality, colour mode); Output (vector or raster processing); Options (DOC-OUT-001, plus Export in background, on by default). Export / Close.

    Behaviour & rules. - Naming rule: a file name pattern composed of parameters (sheet number, sheet name, project number, current revision, sheet collection, view name, custom parameters) with prefix, suffix and separators, and a live sample. Characters invalid in file names are replaced with _. - PDF content: PDF 1.7 written by Reviera's own writer (built on the MIT/Apache pdf-writer crate, with font subsetting). Text is real, searchable text with embedded font subsets. Lines keep their exact widths, caps and dash patterns. Fills use PDF tiling patterns for hatches, or explicit geometry when the pattern is too complex for tiling. - Hyperlinks: view reference symbols, section heads, callout heads and elevation marks on a sheet become internal links to the target sheet when it is in the same combined PDF. - Layers: optional PDF layers by category writes optional content groups per category (and sub-category), so that a PDF viewer can toggle them. - Metadata: title (sheet number and name), author, project name and number, and the Reviera version are written to the document information and XMP metadata. Optional PDF/A-2b output. - Combined files get one bookmark per sheet or view.

    Data (RXD). output.pdfSetups[].

    Commands. export.pdf(range, set_id?, setup_id?, path_or_folder, combine?, naming_rule?, background?) -> job_id; export.pdf_setup_save(name, settings) -> setup_id; export.pdf_setup_delete(setup_id) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Text in an exported PDF can be searched and copied. - [ ] Clicking a section head in a combined PDF jumps to the sheet holding that section. - [ ] Separate-file export of 20 sheets with naming rule <Project Number>-<Sheet Number>-<Current Revision> creates 20 correctly named files. - [ ] A PDF/A-2b export passes veraPDF validation.

    Raster image export

    ID: DOC-OUT-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §6.5 Images

    Purpose. Write views and sheets as raster images for presentations, web pages and documents.

    Workflow. File › Export › Images and Animations › Image. The dialog has: output file or folder with naming rule; range (DOC-OUT-001); image size; options; format; Export.

    Behaviour & rules. - File › Export › Images and Animations › Image: range; image size (fit to N pixels in a direction, or zoom % of real size); options (as DOC-OUT-001); shaded-view resolution (72–600 dpi); format PNG, JPEG (quality levels), TIFF, BMP, TGA, WebP; naming rule as for PDF. Hidden-line views are rasterised from the draw list with anti-aliasing; shaded views are rendered off-screen by the GPU renderer. - Fit to N pixels: N from 32 to 32 768 in the chosen direction (horizontal or vertical); the other dimension follows the view's aspect ratio. Zoom % (1–1000 %) of the printed size at the chosen dpi. Larger images are rendered in tiles (DOC-HLR-007). - The extents are the crop region of a cropped view, the sheet size for a sheet, and the extents of visible content for an uncropped view; Visible portion of current window exports exactly what the window shows. - Line widths keep their paper size at the image's dpi, so a 0.5 mm pen is 6 pixels wide at 300 dpi; Thin lines never applies. - PNG and TIFF can have a transparent background (option); JPEG uses the view background colour. TIFF and PNG embed the dpi. - Each image gets metadata: title (view or sheet name), software and project name, in the format's standard text fields. - The command runs as a background job (DOC-OUT-013).

    Commands. export.image(range, set_id?, path_or_folder, format, size, dpi?, options?) -> job_id (size is {fit: horizontal|vertical, pixels} or {zoom_percent}; out-of-range values fail with export.image_size_invalid)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Exporting a plan to a 4000-pixel-wide PNG produces an image exactly 4000 pixels wide whose linework matches the PDF output. - [ ] A PNG exported with a transparent background has alpha 0 outside drawn content. - [ ] Requesting a 50 000-pixel image fails with export.image_size_invalid.

    DXF and DWG export

    ID: DOC-OUT-005 · Priority: P1 (DXF), P2 (DWG) · Ref: research/04 §6.3

    Purpose. Exchange 2D drawings (and simple 3D) with CAD users.

    Workflow. File › Export › CAD Formats › DXF / DWG: choose an export setup (Modify Export Setup…), the range (current view/sheet or a view/sheet set), file naming (automatic long, automatic short, or manual), the file version, and whether views on sheets and links are exported as external references or bound.

    Behaviour & rules. The export setup dialog has these tabs: - Layers: per category and sub-category, a projection layer, a cut layer and colour numbers; layer modifiers (append category, sub-category, phase, workset, view kind and so on); Export layer options: properties by layer with overrides by entity, all by layer without overrides, or all by layer with new layers for overrides. Layer naming standards can be loaded from tables Reviera ships (ISO 13567 and other published conventions, written as Reviera's own tables). - Lines: line scaling mode (model space, paper space, or scaled definitions); mapping of line patterns to linetype names, with Reviera generating the .lin-style definitions it needs. - Patterns: mapping of fill patterns to hatch names; unmapped patterns are exported as explicit hatch definitions. - Text & fonts: font mapping; text treatment (keep visual fidelity, or keep editability). - Colours: indexed (255) or true colour. - Solids (3D views): polyface meshes only. Proprietary solid-kernel formats are not written; STEP (DOC-OUT-007) is the solid exchange route. - Units & coordinates: drawing unit; coordinate basis internal or shared (Chapter 6, COL-POS-001). - General: room/space/area boundaries on separate layers; non-plottable layer prefix; hide scope boxes, reference planes and unreferenced tags; preserve coincident lines; default version. - Sheets export to paper space layouts with each viewport as a model-space view at its scale (or flattened to paper space, by option). - Writers: DXF is written by Reviera's own writer (DXF is a published text format). DWG is written through LibreDWG (GPL-3.0-or-later), whose DWG writing is limited; Reviera therefore writes DWG only in the versions LibreDWG supports reliably and offers DXF as the recommended format. - Exact arcs, circles and ellipses from the draw list are written as true arc, circle and ellipse entities.

    Data (RXD). output.cadSetups[].

    Commands. export.dxf(range, set_id?, setup_id?, folder, naming?, version?, xrefs?) -> job_id; export.dwg(range, set_id?, setup_id?, folder, naming?, version?, xrefs?) -> job_id; export.cad_setup_save(name, settings) -> setup_id; export.cad_setup_load_layer_standard(setup_id, standard) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A DXF of a floor plan opens in LibreCAD and in another CAD application with walls on the configured cut layer and doors on their projection layer. - [ ] A circular column is exported as a CIRCLE entity. - [ ] Exporting a sheet produces one paper-space layout with a viewport at the view's scale.

    IFC export settings

    ID: DOC-OUT-006 · Priority: P0 (save-as variants), P1 (setups, MVD conversion) · Ref: research/04 §6.4

    Purpose. IFC is Reviera's native format, so "IFC export" means writing a derived IFC file tailored to a recipient: a different schema or model view definition, a filtered subset, or a clean file without Reviera data.

    Workflow. File › Export › IFC: file name; setup (in-session, or named setups including built-in ones for IFC4 Reference View, IFC4 Design Transfer View, IFC2X3 Coordination View 2.0, IFC4X3, and a handover/COBie-style setup); Modify setup…; Export linked models as separate files or federate into one file.

    Behaviour & rules. Setup tabs: - General: schema (IFC2X3, IFC4, IFC4X3); model view definition (Reference View writes tessellated geometry such as IfcTriangulatedFaceSet; Design Transfer View keeps parametric geometry such as extrusions and Boolean results); file type (.ifc, .ifcXML, .ifczip); phase to export (sets the standard Status property, DOC-GFX-017); space boundaries (none, first level, second level); coordinate base (internal origin, project base point, shared coordinates; Chapter 6, COL-POS-003); split walls, columns and ducts by storey; file header (author, organisation, authorisation). - Content: Include Reviera Extension Data (on by default; off produces a clean exchange file); Include documentation as IFC annotation (DOC-IFC-002) with Include 2D linework; export only elements visible in a chosen view; include rooms/areas/spaces as IfcSpace volumes; include linked models. - Properties: standard property sets; Reviera parameters as user property sets (with a mapping table from parameter to property set and property name, loadable from a text file); base quantities (computed by OCCT); schedules as property sets (each schedule's fields become a property set on its elements); classification references. - Level of detail: tessellation tolerance for curved geometry. - Advanced: export parts as building elements; use type name only for type objects; store exported GlobalIds back (not needed in Reviera because GlobalIds are native, so this option is absent); export bounding boxes. - Geographic reference: writes IfcMapConversion and IfcProjectedCRS from the project's positioning (Chapter 6, COL-POS-003). - Entity mapping: a per-category table of IFC class and predefined type used when a category's native class should be exported differently (for example exporting generic models as IfcBuildingElementProxy); family types can override it with an Export as parameter. - Schema conversion: IFC4 to IFC2X3 and IFC4 to IFC4X3 are done with IfcOpenShell's schema migration functions, followed by Reviera's own fix-ups for entities that have no counterpart. Losses are listed in an export report. - Validation: after writing, the file is validated with IfcOpenShell (schema and, where available, MVD rules); problems are listed in the export report.

    Data (RXD). output.ifcSetups[].

    Commands. export.ifc(path, setup? (name, id or inline settings), settings_override?, schema?, strip_rxd?=false, documentation?, background?) -> job_id; export.ifc_setup_save(name, settings) -> setup_id; export.ifc_setup_delete(setup_id) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A Reference View export contains no IfcExtrudedAreaSolid or IfcBooleanResult and opens in at least two other IFC viewers. - [ ] A clean export contains no Reviera Extension Data property sets and validates without errors. - [ ] An IFC2X3 Coordination View export of the sample project validates against the IFC2X3 schema, and the report lists every converted or dropped entity. - [ ] Schedules as property sets writes a property set named after the door schedule onto each door, containing that schedule's field values.

    3D exchange formats: glTF, OBJ, STEP, FBX

    ID: DOC-OUT-007 · Priority: P1 (glTF, OBJ), P2 (STEP), P3 (FBX) · Ref: research/04 §6.5 (FBX, ACIS SAT / STEP, Datasmith)

    Purpose. Hand 3D geometry and materials to visualisation, game-engine and CAD tools.

    Behaviour & rules. - glTF 2.0 (.gltf or binary .glb): the recommended visualisation format. Exports the visible contents of the active 3D view (respecting section box, visibility and phase), with physically based materials, texture maps, instancing for repeated family types, lights (KHR_lights_punctual), cameras, and per-node extras holding the element GlobalId, category and chosen parameters. Large coordinates are offset to a local origin stored in the asset's extras. - OBJ/MTL: simple mesh exchange, one group per element. - STEP AP214/AP242: solid exchange through OCCT's STEP writer, with one product per element, colours and names. - FBX: the format's official software kit is proprietary and cannot be used in a GPL program. Reviera does not plan an FBX writer; glTF is the supported alternative. A community writer for the documented ASCII FBX form may be considered later as an add-in. - Vendor live-link and proprietary visualisation formats are out of scope (P3). Open alternatives: glTF, USD (P2, through the Apache-licensed OpenUSD libraries, as a possible later addition).

    Commands. export.gltf(path, view_id?, binary?, options?) -> job_id; export.obj(path, view_id?, options?) -> job_id; export.step(path, view_id_or_element_ids, schema?: ap214|ap242) -> job_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A glTF export of a 3D view opens in a standard glTF viewer with correct materials, and each node's extras holds its element's GlobalId. - [ ] Repeated chairs are written as one mesh with many instances. - [ ] A STEP export reopens in a STEP viewer with one solid per element.

    gbXML export

    ID: DOC-OUT-008 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/04 §6.5 gbXML

    Purpose. Hand an energy model to open or third-party energy and load analysis tools.

    Workflow. File › Export › gbXML: choose the source (rooms, spaces or the energy analytical model), the phase, and options; Export. A preview lists spaces and surfaces with warnings before writing.

    Behaviour & rules. - Exports an energy model in gbXML, built either from rooms/spaces or from the analytical energy model of Chapter 4 (ANA). Spaces become Space elements; their bounding surfaces (computed from second-level space boundaries by OCCT) become Surface elements with openings, construction and adjacency; location comes from the project's site location. The export report lists surfaces that could not be classified. - Surface types are classified from the host element and adjacency: exterior wall, interior wall, roof, interior floor, slab on grade, underground wall and slab, ceiling, shade, air (room separation lines), with openings typed as operable window, fixed window, door or opening. - Constructions and materials are written from the host types' layers with thickness and thermal properties when present (Chapter 2 materials); missing thermal data is reported, not invented. - Options: export complexity (simple, or with shading surfaces), include unbounded rooms (default off), building type and space types (written as gbXML enumerations), and the coordinate base (internal or shared, Chapter 6). - Rooms that are not enclosed are skipped and reported. Spaces whose surfaces do not close within the tolerance (5 mm) are written but flagged in the report. - Units are SI (metres, square metres, cubic metres) unless the project's display units are imperial and the option Use project units is on.

    Commands. export.gbxml(path, source: rooms|spaces|energy_model, options?) -> job_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] The gbXML of a two-room sample validates against the gbXML schema, and the shared wall appears once with both spaces as adjacent. - [ ] A room that is not enclosed is listed in the report and not written. - [ ] A wall type without thermal data is exported with its layer thicknesses and named in the report as missing thermal properties.

    Reports and other exports

    ID: DOC-OUT-009 · Priority: P1 (schedule and room reports), P2 (database export), P3 (vendor formats) · Ref: research/04 §6.5

    Output Reviera behaviour Priority
    Schedule export DOC-SCH-012. P0–P1
    Room/area report HTML report listing each room or area with its boundary triangulation and computed area, for checking area calculations. P2
    Database export Exports elements, types and parameters to SQLite (one table per category plus a parameters table) or to CSV files. This replaces export to proprietary ODBC targets; SQLite files can be attached to other databases. P2
    Family type catalogue Exports a family's types and parameter values as a delimited text catalogue (Chapter 2). P1
    DWF/DWFx, DGN, NWC, Datasmith Proprietary or vendor-specific formats; not provided. Alternatives: PDF for review sets, DXF for CAD exchange, IFC plus BCF for coordination, glTF for visualisation. P3

    Commands. export.database(path, format: sqlite|csv, categories[]?) -> job_id; export.room_report(path, scope?) -> job_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A SQLite export contains one row per door in the Doors table, with one column per scheduled door parameter.

    Background jobs

    ID: DOC-OUT-013 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §6.2 Export in background

    Behaviour & rules. - Output commands return a job id at once and run on a background worker using the model snapshot taken at start. The user keeps editing; later edits do not affect the job. - A jobs panel and a status-bar indicator show progress and completion; a notification offers Open file or Open folder. Jobs can be cancelled. - Jobs started from Lua or MCP can be awaited (job.wait) or polled (job.status). - Several jobs can run at once, limited by a user setting (default: half the CPU cores). - Job states: queued, running (with percent and the current item, for example "Sheet A205"), succeeded, failed (with the error and the item it occurred on), cancelled. A job that fails on one item continues with the others when the output allows it (separate files) and reports the failures; a combined file fails as a whole. - Snapshot cost. The snapshot is copy-on-write (Chapter 2b), so starting a job does not copy the model; memory grows only with edits made while the job runs. - Files. Output is written to a temporary name in the target folder and renamed on success, so a cancelled or failed job never leaves a half-written file under the final name. - Closing the project while jobs run asks whether to wait or cancel them. Jobs never outlive the session; the jobs panel lists the last 50 finished jobs of the session. - Jobs started by one user in BIMserver mode run locally on that user's machine; they do not lock anything on the server.

    Commands. job.status(job_id) -> status (query; {state, percent, current_item?, errors[], outputs[]}); job.wait(job_id, timeout?) -> status (query; returns on completion or after timeout seconds with the current status); job.cancel(job_id) -> (); job.list() -> job_summary[] (query)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] While a 200-sheet PDF export runs, the user can move walls with no noticeable delay, and the exported sheets show the model as it was when the export started. - [ ] Cancelling a separate-file PDF export after 10 of 20 sheets leaves 10 complete files and no partial file. - [ ] job.wait with a 1-second timeout on a long job returns a running status with a percentage.

    Rendering

    ID: DOC-OUT-011 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/04 §6.6; web: Place a Decal in a View, Decal Type Properties, Decal Attributes · screenshots/documentation/rendered_image_raytracer.png

    Purpose. Photorealistic still images from 3D views, using open-source renderers.

    Workflow. 1. View tab › Presentation › Render (default shortcut RR) with a 3D view active. 2. Render dialog: renderer (from those installed); Render or Render region (drag a rectangle in the crop); quality preset (draft, low, medium, high, best) or custom (samples, or render time in minutes, or until stopped); output resolution (screen, or printer dpi with width and height); lighting scheme, sun setting and artificial light groups; background (sky model, colour, image, transparent) and haze; exposure (exposure value, highlights, mid-tones, shadows, white point, saturation). 3. While rendering, the image refines progressively; the user can stop at any time. 4. Save to project creates a rendering view (placeable on a sheet); Export writes PNG, JPEG, TIFF, or OpenEXR (high dynamic range).

    Behaviour & rules. - Renderer back-ends are render backends of kind offline_still/offline_animation (DOC-RBE-001). In-process ones are plug-ins behind the backend trait (scene in, image tiles out); external ones (for example a Blender bridge) attach through the Reviera Scene Protocol (ADV-RSP-001) and return images with render.result: - Reviera path tracer (built in, optional at build time): a progressive unidirectional path tracer in wgpu compute shaders, with a BVH built on the GPU, multiple importance sampling, and the same materials as the Realistic style. It also drives the Path Traced visual style (DOC-GFX-011). - Cycles (Apache-2.0), used as the standalone library, as an external render engine with CPU and GPU devices. - Others that fit the trait with GPL-compatible licences may be added, for example LuxCoreRender (Apache-2.0) or Mitsuba 3 (BSD-3-Clause). - Scene translation: tessellated geometry from the OCCT cache, with instancing; materials mapped from Reviera appearance data (base colour, metallic, roughness, transmission, IOR, emission, normal and bump maps) to a principled surface model; artificial lights from lighting fixture families with IES LM-63 photometric files and light groups (with dimming); sun position from the project location, date and time; physical sky model. - Denoising: optional Intel Open Image Denoise (Apache-2.0). - People and plant entourage use ordinary families with mesh geometry; no proprietary entourage formats. - Vendor cloud rendering services are out of scope (P3). - Decals (Insert › Link › Decal ▾ › Place Decal / Decal Types, decal.place). A decal is an image applied to a planar or cylindrical face, for signs, posters, paintings and screens. - Decal types hold the image (PNG, JPEG, BMP, or WebP, stored as an RXD asset) and its appearance: brightness (multiplier, default 1.0), reflectivity (0–1), transparency (0–1), finish (matte, satin, glossy, polished), luminance (cd/m², for screens and light boxes), bump pattern and amount (0–1), and cut-outs (none, rectangle, oval, or an image mask). The Decal Types dialog lists types with Duplicate, Rename, Delete (a type in use asks for a replacement) and a preview. Identity data (keynote, model, manufacturer, description, type mark, cost) are ordinary type parameters. - Placement: in a 2D view or an orthographic 3D view (not a perspective view), choose a type, set Width and Height (with Lock proportions, default on), then click a face. Elliptical faces and non-cylindrical curved faces are refused. The decal follows its host face when the host moves or changes size, keeping its position relative to the face's origin; it is deleted when the host is deleted. - Display: in Realistic, Path Traced and rendered output the image is mapped onto the face with the type's attributes; in all other styles the decal shows as a placeholder rectangle with a cross, which can be hidden with the Decals category. - Decals are taggable, schedulable (category Decals) and exported to glTF as textured quads offset 0.5 mm from the face (DOC-OUT-007). - Render gallery (render.gallery; View tab › Presentation › Render Gallery). A local browser of this user's render history for the open project: every finished or stopped render job is kept with its image (stored as 32-bit floating-point OpenEXR so exposure can be changed later), a thumbnail, the source view, renderer, settings, resolution, samples and render time. The gallery lists them newest first with filters by view and renderer, and offers: open full size, compare two side by side with a slider, Adjust exposure (re-tone-maps the stored image without rendering again), Render again with these settings, Save to project (render.save_to_project), Export (render.export), and delete. History is stored per user in the local application data folder, keyed by the project's GlobalId, with a size limit (default 2 GB; oldest entries are removed first). It is never written into the project, never shared through BIMserver and never uploaded anywhere; only renderings saved to the project become project data.

    Data (RXD). Render settings in the 3D view payload (render block). Saved renderings are views of kind view.rendering whose image is an RXD asset; the image is the only derived result stored (§5.1). Decal types: standards/materials, kind decal.type (image asset reference and the attributes above). Placed decals are element-scoped RXD on the host element (Reviera_Element section decals[]: id, type, face sub-reference, uv position, width, height, rotation), so moving or deleting the host carries them; they have no IFC entity of their own. On IFC export the host's face style is not changed; with Include Reviera Extension Data off, decals are lost and the export report says so.

    Commands. render.start(view_id, settings, renderer?, region?) -> job_id; render.stop(job_id) -> (); render.save_to_project(job_id, name) -> view_id; render.export(job_id_or_view_id, path, format) -> (); render.list_renderers() -> renderer_info[] (query); render.gallery() -> () (opens the gallery; session UI, not undoable); decal.place(view_id, decal_type_id, face_ref, position, width?, height?) -> element_id (returns the decal's id; a perspective view fails with decal.perspective_view, an unsupported face with decal.face_unsupported); decaltype.create(name, image_asset_or_path, attributes?) -> type_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With no renderer plug-in installed, the Render command explains how to install one and nothing crashes. - [ ] A rendering saved to the project can be placed on a sheet and printed. - [ ] Rendering the sample interior with Cycles and with the built-in path tracer gives images whose mean luminance differs by less than 10 % at equal exposure. - [ ] A decal placed on a wall moves with the wall, shows as a crossed rectangle in Shaded style and as the image in a rendering. - [ ] Placing a decal in a perspective camera view is refused. - [ ] After three renders of one view, the render gallery lists three entries; adjusting the exposure of one does not start a render, and none of them is in the saved IFC file.

    Walkthrough and solar study animation export

    ID: DOC-OUT-012 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/04 §1.5 Walkthrough, §6.5 Walkthrough / Solar Study

    Purpose. Export moving images of walkthroughs and of sun and shadow studies.

    Workflow. 1. Solar study: View Control Bar › Sun Path ▾ › Solar Study, or sun.settings (DOC-GFX-012), choose Single Day or Multi-Day, dates, times and interval; preview with the play controls on the contextual tab. 2. File › Export › Images and Animations › Walkthrough or Solar Study (the active view must be a walkthrough, or a 3D or plan view with a solar study set): frame range, frames per second, visual style, size, output format; Export.

    Behaviour & rules. - File › Export › Images and Animations › Walkthrough / Solar Study: frame range, frames per second, visual style (any style, including a renderer), image size; output as an image sequence (PNG) or a video file (WebM with VP9/AV1, or MP4 with AV1, through a GPL-compatible encoder; codecs with patent licensing are not bundled). Solar studies animate the sun over a day or several days at a chosen interval. - Frame range defaults to all frames; fps 1–60 (default 15 for solar studies, the walkthrough's own rate for walkthroughs); size by width and height in pixels (16–7680) or by zoom of the view size. - A solar study frame count is the number of intervals in the time range (single day) or in the date range (multi-day); the sun position per frame comes from the project location (Chapter 6). - With a renderer style, each frame is a render job with the view's render settings; the export can resume from the last finished frame after a cancel when writing an image sequence. - Image sequences are named <base>_0001.png onward with zero padding to the frame count's digits. - The export is a background job (DOC-OUT-013) and uses the model snapshot at its start.

    Data (RXD). Solar study settings are part of the view's graphicDisplay.lighting.sun block (DOC-GFX-012); export settings are not stored unless saved as a named animation setup in project/settings › output.animationSetups[].

    Commands. export.animation(view_id, kind: walkthrough|solar_study, path, frames?, fps?, size, style?, format: images|webm|mp4) -> job_id; solarstudy.set(view_id, kind: still|single_day|multi_day, date_range, time_range, interval) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 100-frame walkthrough exports 100 numbered PNG files at the chosen size. - [ ] A single-day solar study from 08:00 to 18:00 at one-hour intervals exports 11 frames whose shadows move from west to east. - [ ] A WebM export plays in a standard browser at the chosen frame rate.

    Publishing for review

    ID: DOC-OUT-014 · Priority: P3 (vendor cloud publishing), P2 (open alternative) · Ref: research/04 §6.7

    Purpose. Share a reviewable snapshot of the drawings and model without a vendor cloud.

    Workflow. File › Publish › Review Set: choose a view/sheet set (DOC-OUT-001), the 3D views to include, the 3D format (glTF or IFC), the target (folder, or the current BIMserver project in BIMserver mode), and the PDF setup; Publish.

    Behaviour & rules. - Publishing to a vendor cloud document service is out of scope. Open alternative: Publish review set writes a chosen view/sheet set as a combined PDF plus a glTF (or IFC) of chosen 3D views, and, in BIMserver mode, attaches them to the current BIMserver revision as revision extended data (Chapter 6; call names to verify against the deployed server), so that an open-source web viewer pointed at the server can show them. Issues raised on the published set travel as BCF (Chapter 6, COL-BCF-001). - A review set folder contains <set name>.pdf, one <view name>.glb (or .ifc) per 3D view, and a manifest.json listing every file with its SHA-256, the project name and number, the source revision (local save time or BIMserver revision id), the publishing user and the time. The manifest lets a reviewer check that files belong together and are unchanged. - The 3D files keep element GlobalIds (glTF extras, IFC natively), so BCF issues raised against them point at the right elements in Reviera. - In BIMserver mode, publishing requires write access to the project; without it, the command fails before writing anything. The upload is one job; partial uploads are rolled back where the server allows it and reported otherwise. - Publishing never changes the model; it is not undoable and does not create a project revision on its own.

    Commands. publish.review_set(set_id, include_3d_views[]?, target: folder|bimserver, path?) -> job_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Publishing a review set in Local mode writes a combined PDF and one glTF per selected 3D view to the chosen folder. - [ ] The manifest's SHA-256 values match the written files. - [ ] A user without write access in BIMserver mode gets an error before any file is uploaded.

    5.19 Open questions and deviations from the reference

    Deviations (intentional).

    # Topic Reviera behaviour Reason
    D5-1 Storage of documentation Views, sheets, schedules, standards and annotation are Reviera Extension Data (RXD) embedded in the IFC file by default (Chapter 2a), not a proprietary project database. Annotation is written as IfcAnnotation only on export. Native IFC with full compatibility; per-object three-way merge for BIMserver mode.
    D5-2 Options Bar None. Tool options are on the contextual ribbon tab and in the Properties palette. Matches the reference's own 2027 direction; one less UI surface to implement.
    D5-3 Schedule filters A nested AND/OR rule tree with no limit on the number of rules, shared with view filters; calculated and hidden fields can be used anywhere. The reference's eight AND-only rules are a common complaint; one engine for both is simpler.
    D5-4 Graphics Inspector graphics.explain and the Why does this look like this? command show which override layer won. Makes the precedence model transparent for users and AI agents.
    D5-5 View range category behaviour The above-cut behaviour and floor-like rule are a visible, editable per-category table rather than fixed internal rules. Predictability, and offices can match their conventions.
    D5-6 Keynote tables Plain tab- or comma-separated files, optionally embedded in the project. Avoids missing-file problems, especially in BIMserver mode.
    D5-7 Replace with text on dimensions Numeric replacement text is refused. Prevents drawings that silently show false dimensions.
    D5-8 DWG DXF is the primary CAD format. DWG is written only through LibreDWG and only in the versions it supports reliably; no proprietary DWG libraries. Licence compatibility (GPL-3.0-or-later).
    D5-9 FBX, DWF, DGN, NWC, Datasmith, ODBC, proprietary solid formats Not provided (P3). Alternatives: glTF, USD (later), STEP, PDF, DXF, IFC + BCF, SQLite/CSV. Proprietary formats or SDKs incompatible with the GPL.
    D5-10 Rendering Optional open renderers (built-in wgpu path tracer, Cycles; others such as LuxCoreRender or Mitsuba possible) behind one interface; no cloud rendering. No proprietary renderer can be shipped; vendor cloud services are out of scope.
    D5-11 Accelerated graphics There is only one GPU viewport (wgpu), always on, which supports every visual style, section boxes, halftone, transparency and links. Reviera starts with a modern renderer, so there is no legacy engine to toggle.
    D5-12 Publishing Publishing to a vendor cloud is replaced by review sets (PDF + glTF/IFC) written to a folder or attached to a BIMserver revision, with issues in BCF. Vendor cloud out of scope; open formats instead.
    D5-13 Walkthrough video WebM/AV1 or image sequences; no bundled patent-encumbered codecs. Licensing.
    D5-14 Unused IFC export option "Store IFC GlobalId in a parameter after export" does not exist. GlobalIds are native in Reviera.
    D5-15 Assembly members Whole system elements (beam systems, trusses, curtain walls, stairs, railings, reinforcement systems) may be members of an assembly as nested aggregates; parts are members through IfcRelAssignsToProduct (DOC-ASM-001). The reference refuses complex structures; IFC allows nested IfcElementAssembly, and precast and steel shop assemblies need it.
    D5-16 Assembly views after a type change When an edited owner instance joins a type that already has views, the user chooses which set to keep (DOC-ASM-004). The reference deletes one set without a choice.
    D5-17 Render gallery A local render history with exposure re-adjustment (DOC-OUT-011) replaces the reference's cloud render gallery. Vendor cloud services are out of scope (P3).
    D5-19 Pluggable presentation backends The reference product has one built-in renderer plus a vendor cloud service. Reviera puts all 3D presentation behind an open backend interface (DOC-RBE-001…002). The scene protocol, walkthroughs, the Godot translation layer for VR/AR and the reference bridges are specified in Chapter 7. Owner directive 2026-10-12: future photo-real, game-engine and Blender backends for simulated walkthroughs.
    D5-18 Displaced elements Displacement is a pure per-view transform, so constrained or hosted elements can be displaced; dimensions to displaced elements are refused instead (DOC-VIEW-012). The model is never moved, so constraints cannot be violated; a dimension would report a false distance.

    Open questions.

    # Question Owner
    Q5-1 Exact list of cuttable categories, above-cut behaviours and floor-like categories (DOC-VR-002) needs confirming against Chapter 2's category catalogue and against real drawing conventions. DOC + DM
    Q5-2 Performance targets for exact HLR on very large views (tile size, PolyAlgo pre-pass thresholds) must be set from prototypes. DOC
    Q5-3 Whether OCCT's HLRBRep_Algo is robust enough on IFC-derived tessellated geometry (Reference View imports) or whether mesh-based HLR must be the default for such elements. DOC
    Q5-4 IFC4X3 IfcAnnotationTypeEnum values to use for each annotation class on export need checking against the final schema. DOC
    Q5-5 PDF tiling-pattern support varies between PDF viewers; decide when hatches are written as explicit geometry instead. DOC
    Q5-6 ~~RXD document names and kinds must match Chapter 2a~~ Resolved: every kind used here is in the Object Kind Registry (02a §6.5); colour schemes are stored in views/color_schemes. DOC + DM
    Q5-7 Size limits for embedded RXD in very annotation-heavy projects (thousands of views) still need measuring. ~~Lazy loading per view with the embedded carrier~~ resolved: it works with both carriers (02a §3, §9). DM
    Q5-8 Which BIMserver extended-data calls are available for attaching review sets (DOC-OUT-014) on BIMserver 1.5.188, the target release. COL
    Q5-9 ~~Precast pieces with two IFC parents~~ Deferred: handled by Chapter 4 Q13. The initial version writes only the assembly aggregation and keeps the source link in RXD; a final decision needs expert advice. STR + DOC
    Q5-10 ~~New RXD kinds to be added to 02a~~ Resolved: registered in 02a §6.4–§6.5. DM

    6CHChapter 6: Collaboration, Linking and Coordination

    Area code: COL · Status: Draft 1 (2026-10-12) · Primary source: research/04_documentation_collaboration.md (cited as research/04 §n) Related chapters: Chapter 1 (UI shell, status bar, notifications), Chapter 2 (data model, file I/O), Chapter 2a (Reviera Extension Data, RXD: 02a_extension_data_format.md), Chapter 5 (views, graphics resolver, output), TECH_STACK §3.7 (Local and BIMserver modes). Reference: Autodesk Revit 2026/2027 worksharing, linking, positioning and coordination features, used as the functional reference only.

    This chapter specifies how several people and several models work together in Reviera. It covers the two operating modes (Local and Open Source BIMserver client), the mapping of the reference product's worksharing concepts onto BIMserver, the merge algorithm, advisory ownership, worksets, offline working copies, linked models and underlays, project positioning and coordinate systems, coordination tools (copy/monitor, coordination review, clash detection, BCF issues) and model maintenance.

    Storage rule for this chapter. As set out in Chapter 2a, everything IFC entities can express stays in IFC entities. Collaboration data that IFC cannot express (worksets, link registry, positioning extras, monitor pairs, clash tests, issues) is Reviera Extension Data (RXD), embedded in the IFC file by default, and named here as "RXD document <name>". The single exception is live ownership and lock state, which must change without creating model revisions; in BIMserver mode it travels as BIMserver extended data on the latest revision (COL-OWN-002). This chapter does not define the RXD carrier; Chapter 2a does.

    6.0 Principles

    ID Principle Priority
    COL-CORE-001 One editing engine, two stores. Editing, regeneration, undo, Lua and MCP behave identically in Local and BIMserver mode. Only open, save, synchronise, history and ownership differ, and they sit behind the ModelStore trait (TECH_STACK §3.7). No command has a mode-specific signature: a command that needs the server fails in Local mode with mode.not_available and changes nothing (COL-MODE-001). Undo history is local to the session in both modes; it is never shared through the server and is cleared by Get latest only for the steps that the merge invalidated (the user is told how many). P0
    COL-CORE-002 GlobalId is identity. Every rooted IFC object keeps its GlobalId for life. Copies get new GlobalIds. Merges, links, monitors, clashes and BCF issues all refer to elements by GlobalId; RXD objects are referred to by their stable ids. Moving an element to another storey, workset or type never changes its GlobalId. An imported file with duplicate or malformed GlobalIds is repaired by Audit (COL-MNT-002) before it can be published to BIMserver; publishing is refused with model.duplicate_globalid until then. References into links use link:<linkId>/ifc:<GlobalId> (Chapter 2a). P0
    COL-CORE-003 Never lose work silently. Every merge, conflict decision and ownership override is recorded in a sync report that the user can reopen (Collaborate › Show History › Sync reports; the last 50 are kept in the working copy). Changes that lose a conflict are kept in a recoverable conflict stash (COL-MRG-002) until the user discards them. Destructive actions on shared state (Discard local changes, Force relinquish, Discard working copy, Unload for everyone) need explicit confirmation naming what will be lost, and MCP agents may call them only with the model-edit permission and an explicit confirm: true. P1
    COL-CORE-004 Offline first. In BIMserver mode a local working copy is always kept, so users can open, edit and save without a connection (COL-OFF-001). Losing the connection never interrupts an edit; only Synchronise, Get latest, link reloads from the server and new borrows become queued or disabled. Reconnection is automatic and never merges without the user's go-ahead. P1
    COL-CORE-005 Credentials never leak. Server passwords and tokens (BIMserver, BCF API, OpenCDE and other server profiles, COL-API-001) are stored in the operating system's credential store. They are never written to RXD, IFC, the working-copy folder, logs, crash reports, sync reports, Lua-visible tables or MCP resources; log lines that would contain a token show <redacted>. MCP tools never accept a password or token as a parameter (COL-BIM-001). Signing out removes the stored token. P0

    Acceptance criteria (principles). - [ ] The same Lua script that creates and tags 100 doors produces identical IFC and RXD content in Local mode and in BIMserver mode (apart from the binding of the file to its server). - [ ] Searching the saved IFC file, the working-copy folder and the log files for the server password finds nothing. - [ ] bimserver.get_latest called in Local mode returns mode.not_available and leaves the undo stack unchanged. - [ ] Publishing a model that contains two objects with the same GlobalId is refused with model.duplicate_globalid.

    6.1 Operating modes

    Model stores and mode selection

    ID: COL-MODE-001 · Priority: P0 (Local), P1 (BIMserver) · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.7; research/04 §7.1, screenshots/documentation/worksharing_central_local_diagram.png

    Purpose. Let the same application work on a plain IFC file or on a shared BIMserver project.

    Workflow. 1. File › Open › IFC file opens a project in Local mode. 2. File › Open › From BIMserver… opens the server browser (COL-BIM-002) and opens a project in BIMserver mode. 3. The title bar and status bar show the mode: the file path in Local mode; the server, project name, base revision number and connection state in BIMserver mode.

    Behaviour & rules.

    Capability Local mode (LocalStore) BIMserver mode (BimServerStore)
    Storage .ifc or .ifczip with embedded RXD BIMserver project; the client keeps a working copy (COL-OFF-001)
    Save (Ctrl+S) Writes the file atomically (Chapter 2a), with rotating backups (COL-MNT-003) Writes the local working copy only; nothing is sent to the server
    Publish changes — Synchronise (COL-BIM-006)
    Get others' changes — Get latest (COL-BIM-005)
    History Local backups Server revision list (COL-BIM-008)
    Ownership Not used (single editor) Advisory ownership (§6.4)
    Worksets Available (organisation, visibility, open/close) Available, plus ownership by workset
    Equivalent in the reference A standalone, non-workshared model A workshared central model with local copies
    • The ModelStore trait has the operations open, save_working, get_latest, check_in, history, download_revision, ownership (a sub-interface, null in Local mode), and subscribe (change notifications, null in Local mode).
    • Commands that only make sense in BIMserver mode (for example bimserver.sync) fail in Local mode with mode.not_available, and their ribbon buttons are disabled.
    • Shared-folder protection (Local mode): when a Local project is opened, Reviera creates a lock file <name>.ifc.lock next to it, holding user, host, process id and time. If another user opens the same file, they are told who has it open and can open it read-only or as a copy. Stale locks (the process no longer exists on the same host, or older than 24 hours on another host) can be broken after confirmation. This is protection only; real multi-user editing is BIMserver mode.

    Data (IFC/RXD). In BIMserver mode, the server binding (server URL, project id poid, base revision id roid) is client state in the working-copy folder (COL-OFF-001), not project data; a project file moved to another machine does not carry a server binding.

    Commands. model.open_file(path, read_only?) -> model_id; model.mode() -> {mode, server?, poid?, base_roid?, connected?} (query)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A second user opening a Local project already open elsewhere is warned with the first user's name and can open it read-only. - [ ] bimserver.sync in Local mode returns mode.not_available and changes nothing.

    Moving between modes

    ID: COL-MODE-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.7 (Moving between modes); research/04 §7.2, §7.4 (Detach from central)

    Purpose. Start a project alone and share it later, or take a shared project out of the server.

    Workflow. 1. Publish to BIMserver (Collaborate › Share › Publish to BIMserver): log in, choose or create a project (or sub-project), enter a comment; Reviera checks in the current model as the project's first revision and switches to BIMserver mode with that revision as base. 2. Export local copy (Collaborate › Share › Export Local Copy): writes the current working copy as a standalone .ifc. Options: Keep worksets or Discard worksets (all elements move to no workset and the workset definitions are removed); ownership data is never included. This is the counterpart of "detach from central" and is used for archives and consultant issues.

    Behaviour & rules. - Publishing to a project that already has revisions is refused unless the user chooses Replace (which checks in a new revision and keeps the history) after a confirmation naming the project. - The schema of the server project must match the model schema (IFC4 by default; IFC4X3 only if the server offers a matching deserialiser, TECH_STACK §3.7.3). On mismatch Reviera offers to convert the model (Chapter 5, DOC-OUT-006 conversion) or to create a new project with the right schema.

    Commands. bimserver.publish_local(project: {poid}|{new_name, parent_poid?}, comment, replace?) -> {poid, roid}; model.export_local_copy(path, keep_worksets?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Publishing a Local project creates a server project whose first revision, downloaded by another user, opens with all views, sheets and annotation. - [ ] Exporting a local copy with Discard worksets produces a file that opens in Local mode with no worksets and no ownership data.

    6.2 BIMserver client

    All calls use the BIMserver JSON API as described in TECH_STACK §3.7.1: an HTTP POST to https://<host>[:port]/<context>/json with a body of the form {"token": "...", "request": {"interface": "...", "method": "...", "parameters": {...}}}, or several calls batched in a requests array. The client is asynchronous (reqwest + serde on tokio), so the UI never waits on the network. Interface and method names below are those of BIMserver 1.5 as published in its source; every name marked (verify) must be checked against the minimum supported server version (TECH_STACK §5, open decision 7) before implementation, and the client must look the methods up through the server's service metadata at connect time, failing with a clear message if one is missing.

    The JSON bodies below are illustrative. Tokens, ids and values are placeholders.

    Server profiles and login

    ID: COL-BIM-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.7.1

    Purpose. Connect to one or more BIMserver instances securely.

    Workflow. 1. Collaborate › BIMserver › Servers…: add a server profile (name, URL including context path, optional client certificate, Verify TLS certificates on by default). 2. Log in: user name and password; Remember me stores the password, or the token if the server allows long-lived tokens, in the OS credential store (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, Secret Service on Linux). 3. The status bar shows the connection state (connected, reconnecting, offline).

    Behaviour & rules. - Login flow: json POST /json {"request": {"interface": "AuthInterface", "method": "login", "parameters": {"username": "anna@example.org", "password": "••••"}}} → {"response": {"result": "<token>"}} The token is attached to every later call. AuthInterface.getLoggedInUser returns the user's server identity (user id and name), which Reviera uses as the owner identity for ownership (§6.4). Logout calls AuthInterface.logout. - When a call fails because the token expired, the client logs in again silently if credentials are stored, otherwise it prompts once and retries. - Plain http:// URLs are allowed only for localhost unless the user explicitly accepts the risk per profile. - Each profile records the server version and the list of serialisers and deserialisers it offers (looked up at connect time; COL-BIM-003, COL-BIM-004).

    Data. Server profiles are user preferences (never project data). Secrets live only in the OS credential store.

    Commands. bimserver.add_server(name, url, verify_tls?) -> server_id; bimserver.remove_server(server_id) -> (); bimserver.login(server_id, username, password?, remember?) -> session_info; bimserver.logout(server_id) -> ()

    The MCP tool for bimserver.login never accepts a password from an agent; it can only use stored credentials or ask the user interactively (COL-CORE-005).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] After Remember me, restarting Reviera reconnects without a prompt, and the password is not present in any Reviera file. - [ ] An expired token is renewed transparently during a long session. - [ ] Calling the MCP login tool with a password parameter is rejected.

    Project and revision browser

    ID: COL-BIM-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.7 (Open)

    Purpose. Find and open a project or a specific revision.

    Workflow. File › Open › From BIMserver… opens a dialog with the server list on the left, a project tree (projects and sub-projects) in the middle, and the selected project's revisions on the right (number, date, author, comment, size). Buttons: Open latest, Open revision, New project, New sub-project, Refresh.

    Behaviour & rules. - Project list: json {"token": "<token>", "request": {"interface": "ServiceInterface", "method": "getAllProjects", "parameters": {"onlyTopLevel": false, "onlyActive": true}}} The result gives each project's object id (oid, used as poid), name, schema, parent project, sub-projects and last revision id. The tree is built from the parent links. - Revision list: ServiceInterface.getAllRevisionsOfProject {"poid": …} returns each revision's object id (roid), sequence number, date, comment, user and size. User names are resolved with ServiceInterface.getUserByUoid (verify) and cached. - New project: ServiceInterface.addProject {"projectName": "...", "schema": "ifc4"}; sub-project: ServiceInterface.addProjectAsSubProject {"projectName": "...", "parentPoid": …, "schema": "ifc4"}. - Sub-projects are offered as a way to split a large job by discipline or building; each sub-project is a separate model that the others can link (COL-LNK-001). - Revisions whose check-in comment starts with [reviera:ownership] or [reviera:restore] are labelled accordingly.

    Commands. bimserver.list_projects(server_id) -> project_summary[] (query); bimserver.list_revisions(server_id, poid) -> revision_summary[] (query); bimserver.create_project(server_id, name, schema?, parent_poid?) -> poid

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] The browser lists projects and sub-projects as a tree matching the server's structure. - [ ] Creating a sub-project under "Hospital" shows it nested under that project immediately.

    Open and download

    ID: COL-BIM-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.7.1 (Download)

    Purpose. Bring a server revision onto the client as a working copy.

    Workflow. In the browser, choose Open latest or select a revision and Open revision. A revision that is not the latest opens read-only unless the user chooses Open as new working copy based on this revision (which will merge forward on the next sync).

    Behaviour & rules. 1. Find the serialiser for the project's schema: ServiceInterface.getSerializerByName (for example the server's IFC4 streaming serialiser) or ServiceInterface.getSerializerByContentType {"contentType": "application/ifc"} (verify). Cache its oid per server. 2. Start the download: json {"token": "<token>", "request": {"interface": "ServiceInterface", "method": "download", "parameters": {"roids": [65539], "query": "{}", "serializerOid": 3014707, "sync": false}}} → {"response": {"result": <topicId>}} 3. Wait for the result: progress through NotificationRegistryInterface.getProgress {"topicId": …} (or WebSocket progress events, COL-BIM-007). 4. Fetch the data: HTTP GET /download?token=…&topicId=… streams the IFC file. Reviera streams it to disk in the working-copy folder, then parses it with IfcOpenShell. The embedded RXD arrives as part of the IFC (Chapter 2a). 5. Clean up: ServiceInterface.cleanupLongAction {"topicId": …}. 6. Store the downloaded file as both base.ifc (immutable, for three-way merges) and working.ifc (COL-OFF-001), and record the base roid. 7. Fetch the live ownership document (COL-OWN-002) and subscribe to notifications (COL-BIM-007). - Downloads resume after a dropped connection when the server supports HTTP range requests; otherwise they restart. - If the working copy for that project already exists with unsynchronised changes, Open latest opens the working copy and offers Get latest; it never overwrites local work.

    Commands. bimserver.open(server_id, poid, roid?, as_working_copy?) -> model_id; bimserver.download_revision(server_id, roid, path) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Opening a 200 MB project shows download progress, can be cancelled, and leaves no partial working copy after cancel. - [ ] Re-opening a project with unsynchronised local changes opens the local working copy with those changes intact.

    Check in

    ID: COL-BIM-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.7.1 (Check-in)

    Purpose. Upload the working copy as a new server revision. Users normally do this through Synchronise (COL-BIM-006), which merges first; a bare check-in is used by synchronise and by Publish to BIMserver.

    Behaviour & rules. 1. Serialise the working copy (with embedded RXD) with IfcOpenShell to a temporary file. 2. Find the deserialiser: ServiceInterface.getSuggestedDeserializerForExtension {"extension": "ifc", "poid": …}; cache its oid. 3. Upload. Small models (below a configurable size, default 32 MB): json {"token": "<token>", "request": {"interface": "ServiceInterface", "method": "checkinSync", "parameters": {"poid": 131073, "comment": "Level 2 partitions", "deserializerOid": 2949171, "fileSize": 1234567, "fileName": "model.ifc", "data": "<base64>", "merge": false}}} (checkin with "sync": false returns a topic id instead, and progress is followed as for downloads.) Large models use the server's streamed upload endpoint: start the check-in to obtain a topic id (ServiceInterface.initiateCheckin, verify), then POST /upload as multipart form data with the token, topic id, deserialiser id, project id and comment (verify the endpoint and its fields). 4. merge is always false: Reviera uploads a complete, already merged model, and does not use the server's own merge. 5. On success, read the new revision id from the result (or from getProject's last revision id), record it as the new base, and copy working.ifc to base.ifc. 6. The comment is required (empty comments are refused) and is prefixed with nothing; Reviera appends a machine-readable trailer line with the Reviera version and the RXD format version.

    Commands. bimserver.check_in(comment) -> roid (used internally by sync and publish; exposed for scripts that manage their own merging)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 300 MB model checks in through the streamed endpoint without loading the whole file into memory twice (peak memory below model size + 100 MB). - [ ] After a successful check-in, the status bar shows the new revision number as base.

    Get latest

    ID: COL-BIM-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §7.1 (Reload Latest); TECH_STACK §3.7.2

    Purpose. Bring other users' changes into the working copy without publishing local changes (the counterpart of "reload latest").

    Workflow. Collaborate › Synchronise › Get Latest (default shortcut RL).

    Behaviour & rules. 1. Read the project's last revision id (ServiceInterface.getProjectByPoid). If it equals the base, report "Up to date" and stop. 2. Download the latest revision (COL-BIM-003 steps 1–5) to remote.ifc. 3. Three-way merge (§6.3) with base = base.ifc, local = working copy, remote = remote.ifc. 4. Resolve conflicts (COL-MRG-002), regenerate, show the sync report. 5. The new base becomes the downloaded revision; local unsynchronised changes remain local changes on top of it (the merged working copy is saved and remote.ifc becomes base.ifc).

    Commands. bimserver.get_latest() -> sync_report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] User B gets the 5 walls user A checked in, while B's own unsynchronised door edits stay in B's working copy and are not uploaded.

    Synchronise

    ID: COL-BIM-006 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §7.4 · screenshots/documentation/synchronize_with_central_dialog.png

    Purpose. Publish local changes and receive others' changes in one step (the counterpart of "synchronise with central").

    Workflow. 1. Collaborate › Synchronise › Synchronise and modify settings: dialog with server project (read-only), comment, relinquish options (worksets I own, elements I borrowed; standards, views and families are not special in Reviera, see deviations), Save working copy before and after; or Synchronise now, which uses the last settings and relinquishes borrowed elements. 2. Progress is shown in the status bar; the user can keep reading the model but edits are blocked during steps 3–7 (they would be lost from the upload).

    Behaviour & rules. 1. Save the working copy. 2. Acquire the sync lock (COL-OWN-002): a short-lived lock entry in the live ownership document, with a time-to-live (default 10 minutes, renewed while the sync is running). If another client holds it, wait and show "Project is being synchronised by <user>"; retry automatically. 3. Get latest and merge as in COL-BIM-005 (skipped if the base is still the latest). 4. If conflicts need user decisions, stop and show the conflict dialog (COL-MRG-002). Cancelling releases the lock and leaves the working copy merged but not uploaded. 5. Regenerate and validate (COL-MRG-003). 6. Check in (COL-BIM-004) with the comment. 7. Race check: list revisions again. If a revision other than Reviera's own appeared between the merged remote revision and the new one (someone checked in without respecting the lock, for example another client application), merge again with base = the merged remote revision, local = Reviera's revision, remote = the intruding revision, and check in a corrective revision with comment [reviera:merge] …. Report this in the sync report. 8. Relinquish ownership as chosen and release the sync lock (COL-OWN-002). 9. Save the working copy (base = new revision). - The sync history (Collaborate › Show History) lists revisions with time, user and comment (COL-BIM-008). - Reminders: a user option reminds the user to synchronise every N minutes (default 60) when there are unsynchronised changes. - Closing the project with unsynchronised changes or held ownership offers: Synchronise and relinquish, Relinquish without publishing (local changes stay in the working copy), Keep ownership (ownership stays until next session; others are told it is held), Discard local changes, Cancel.

    Commands. bimserver.sync(comment, relinquish?: {worksets?, elements?}, save_before?, save_after?) -> sync_report; bimserver.set_sync_reminder(minutes?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Two users each move different walls and synchronise in turn; afterwards both working copies contain both moves. - [ ] While user A is synchronising, user B's synchronise waits and completes after A's, with B's revision based on A's. - [ ] If a foreign client checks in during Reviera's synchronise, the sync report shows a corrective merge and the final latest revision contains all three users' changes.

    Notifications

    ID: COL-BIM-007 · Priority: P1 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.7.1 (Notification interfaces); research/04 §7.5 (update frequency)

    Purpose. Tell users promptly when the model or ownership changes on the server.

    Behaviour & rules. - Reviera opens a WebSocket to the server's notification endpoint (/stream, verify), receives an endpoint id, and registers for events on the open project: json {"token": "<token>", "request": {"interface": "NotificationRegistryInterface", "method": "registerNewRevisionOnSpecificProjectHandler", "parameters": {"endPointId": 7, "poid": 131073}}} and, for ownership changes, the handler for new extended data on the latest revision (registerNewExtendedDataOnRevisionHandler, verify). - Incoming new-revision events (NotificationInterface.newRevision with poid and roid) produce a status-bar balloon "Model updated by <user>: <comment>" with Get latest and Show changes, and update the Model updates display mode (COL-WS-004). - Incoming ownership events refresh the live ownership document (COL-OWN-002). - Fallback: if the WebSocket cannot be opened or drops, Reviera polls the project's last revision id and the ownership document every 30 seconds (user setting: manual, 5 s, 15 s, 30 s, 60 s), and reconnects with exponential back-off.

    Commands. bimserver.subscribe(events[]?) -> (); bimserver.unsubscribe() -> (); bimserver.set_update_frequency(seconds_or_manual) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] When user A checks in, user B sees the notification within 5 seconds with the WebSocket connected, and within the polling interval without it. - [ ] Unplugging the network and plugging it back re-establishes notifications without user action.

    History, compare and restore

    Updated 2026-10-12. Server revisions, local history and shared snapshots now appear in one combined History timeline, and named snapshots can be published to BIMserver without creating a new latest revision. Both are specified in Chapter 2b §8.6 (DM-LIVE-019, DM-LIVE-020). Where the text below conflicts with that section, Chapter 2b takes precedence. ID: COL-BIM-008 · Priority: P1 (history), P2 (compare) · Ref: research/04 §7.4 (Show History, Restore Backup)

    Purpose. Inspect, compare and roll back server revisions.

    Workflow. Collaborate › Show History lists revisions. Per revision: Download as file, Open read-only, Compare with base / with another revision, Restore as latest.

    Behaviour & rules. - Compare computes the change set between two revisions with the same fingerprinting used by the merge (§6.3): added, deleted, modified elements (with changed attributes and properties), and changed RXD objects (views, sheets, annotation). Results are shown in a changes palette and can be highlighted in views (colour by change kind) and exported as CSV or BCF topics. The server-side ServiceInterface.compare (verify) may be used as an accelerator when available, but Reviera's own comparison is authoritative. - Restore as latest downloads the chosen revision and checks it in as a new revision with comment [reviera:restore] Restored revision n: <reason>; history is never rewritten. Users with unsynchronised changes are told on their next sync that the model was restored, and their changes are merged onto the restored revision as usual.

    Commands. bimserver.history() -> revision_summary[] (query); bimserver.compare(roid_a, roid_b) -> change_set (query); bimserver.restore(roid, reason) -> roid

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Comparing two revisions lists exactly the elements changed between them, including a dimension text change in a view. - [ ] Restoring revision 12 creates revision 20 identical in content to revision 12, and revisions 13–19 remain in the history.

    6.3 Merging

    Three-way merge by GlobalId and RXD id

    ID: COL-MRG-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.7.2 (Get latest, conflicts found by comparing GlobalIds); spec/02a (RXD merge rules)

    Purpose. Combine local and remote changes reliably, at the finest practical granularity, so that people working on different things never conflict.

    Behaviour & rules.

    Inputs: B (base: the revision the working copy was last synchronised with, kept unmodified in base.ifc), L (local working copy), R (remote: the latest server revision). Each is an IFC model with embedded RXD.

    Step 1 — Index. Parse the three models (in parallel). Index every rooted IFC entity (every IfcRoot subtype: objects, types, relationships, property sets) by GlobalId. Index every RXD object by its stable id (Chapter 2a).

    Step 2 — Fingerprint. For each rooted entity, compute a canonical fingerprint of its owned closure: its own attributes plus every non-rooted entity reachable from it without passing through another rooted entity (placements, representations and their geometry items, property values, materials usage, and so on). In the canonical form: - references to other rooted entities are replaced by their GlobalIds, and STEP instance numbers are ignored; - real numbers are rounded to the model's length precision (default 1e-6 m) before hashing, so that a re-serialised but unchanged model has identical fingerprints; - the closure is split into named facets that can be merged separately: attributes (each direct attribute separately), placement, representation (as a whole), and, for property sets, one facet per property name; - hashing uses BLAKE3 and runs in parallel (rayon).

    Step 3 — Classify. For each GlobalId, compare B, L and R:

    B L R Result
    present same as B same as B unchanged
    present changed same as B take L
    present same as B changed take R
    present changed changed, same result as L take either (identical)
    present changed changed differently facet merge: facets changed on one side only are taken from that side; a facet changed on both sides differently is a conflict
    present deleted same as B delete
    present same as B deleted delete
    present deleted deleted delete
    present deleted changed conflict (delete/modify)
    present changed deleted conflict (modify/delete)
    absent added absent add L
    absent absent added add R
    absent added added (same GlobalId) identical → add once; different → conflict

    Step 4 — Relationship sets. Relationships whose meaning is a set of members are merged as sets, not as values, so that two users adding different elements to the same storey, group or assignment never conflict: IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure.RelatedElements, IfcRelAggregates.RelatedObjects, IfcRelNests.RelatedObjects (keeping order: local insertions first, then remote), IfcRelAssignsToGroup.RelatedObjects, IfcRelDefinesByType.RelatedObjects, IfcRelDefinesByProperties.RelatedObjects, IfcRelAssociatesMaterial.RelatedObjects, IfcRelAssociatesClassification.RelatedObjects. The merged set is (B ∪ added_L ∪ added_R) − removed_L − removed_R. A relationship whose set becomes empty is deleted.

    Step 5 — Exclusivity rules. After step 4, rules that IFC or Reviera require are checked: an element contained in exactly one spatial structure element; an occurrence typed by at most one type; an element in at most one workset (RXD). If the merged result breaks a rule (for example the element was moved to Level 2 locally and to Level 3 remotely), it becomes a conflict on that element.

    Step 6 — RXD. RXD objects are merged per Chapter 2a: by stable id, three-way against B, field by field; same-field changes on both sides are conflicts; delete/modify is a conflict. Keyed collections inside an object (for example per-category overrides in a view, or rows in a schedule's fields) are merged per key.

    Step 7 — Ownership-aware automatic resolution. Before a conflict is shown to the user, the live ownership document (§6.4) is consulted for the conflicting element or RXD object: - if the local user held ownership (borrowed it, or owned its workset) for the whole period since B, the local side wins automatically; - if another user held ownership, the remote side wins automatically, and the local change is put in the conflict stash (COL-CORE-003) and reported as "overridden: element was owned by <user>"; - otherwise the conflict goes to the user (COL-MRG-002). Ownership is advisory, so step 7 is what gives it force at merge time.

    Step 8 — Referential integrity. References to GlobalIds that no longer exist in the merged model are repaired: relationships lose the missing members (step 4 rule); a hosted element whose host was deleted (for example a door whose wall was deleted remotely while the door was edited locally) becomes a conflict; RXD references go through the reconciliation of Chapter 2a (annotation of deleted elements is orphaned or removed and listed).

    Step 9 — Write. The merged model is written with IfcOpenShell (new STEP instance numbers; GlobalIds unchanged). The merge is deterministic: the same B, L, R and decisions always give byte-identical output.
