    Commands. merge.preview(base_path?, remote_path?) -> merge_summary (query; counts of changes and conflicts without applying); merge.three_way(base_path, local_path, remote_path, out_path, policy?) -> merge_report (for scripts and tests; uses files, not the open model)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] User A changes a wall's fire rating property; user B changes the same wall's height. After both synchronise, the wall has both changes and no conflict was raised. - [ ] Users A and B both add new walls to Level 1; the merged containment relationship contains all walls from both, with no conflict. - [ ] A deletes a wall that B modified; the sync raises one delete/modify conflict. - [ ] Merging an unchanged model that was re-serialised by another tool produces zero changes. - [ ] Merging 100 000 elements with 1 000 changes on each side completes in under 30 seconds on the reference machine. - [ ] Running the same merge twice gives byte-identical output.

    Conflict resolution

    ID: COL-MRG-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §7.1 (Editing request, as the reference's way of avoiding conflicts)

    Purpose. Let the user decide conflicts clearly and safely.

    Workflow. When a merge has unresolved conflicts, the Conflicts dialog lists them, grouped by element and RXD object, with: what changed locally, what changed remotely (with the remote user and revision comment), and the base value. Per conflict: Keep mine, Take theirs, Show (zoom to the element in a suitable view, with local and remote versions shown as ghosts), and, for property facets, Edit merged value. Bulk actions: Keep all mine, Take all theirs for a filtered set. Finish applies the decisions; Cancel abandons the merge and restores the working copy to its state before the merge.

    Behaviour & rules. - Every decision is recorded in the sync report (user, time, element, choice). - The losing side of every conflict is stored in the conflict stash: a small IFC+RXD fragment per conflict, kept in the working-copy folder. Collaborate › Conflict Stash lists them; Re-apply re-applies the stashed change as a new local edit; Discard deletes it. The stash is never uploaded. - Scripts and agents can resolve conflicts through commands; MCP agents need the model-edit permission.

    Commands. merge.list_conflicts() -> conflict[] (query); merge.resolve(conflict_id, choice: mine|theirs|value, value?) -> (); merge.resolve_all(filter?, choice: mine|theirs) -> count; merge.finish() -> sync_report; merge.cancel() -> (); stash.list() -> stash_entry[] (query); stash.reapply(entry_id) -> (); stash.discard(entry_ids[]) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Choosing Take theirs for a conflict puts the local value in the stash; Re-apply from the stash restores the local value as an undoable edit. - [ ] Cancel in the Conflicts dialog leaves the working copy exactly as it was before the merge.

    Post-merge regeneration and validation

    ID: COL-MRG-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §9 (Review Warnings)

    Purpose. Make sure a merged model is consistent before it is used or uploaded, even though each side was consistent on its own.

    Workflow. 1. After the merge's step 9 (COL-MRG-001), Reviera regenerates and validates the merged working copy automatically; the status bar shows "Regenerating merged model (n of m)". 2. During Get latest the result is shown in the sync report. During Synchronise it runs before the check-in (COL-BIM-006 step 5): if validation finds blocking problems, the sync stops before uploading and shows them with Fix, Upload anyway (blocked for schema errors) and Cancel.

    Behaviour & rules. - After a merge, the regeneration graph is re-run for every changed element and its dependents (joins, hosted elements, rooms, schedules), so that, for example, two walls edited by different users still join correctly. - Seed set: every element or RXD object whose fingerprint differs from L (the local copy before merging), plus everything that depends on it in the dependency graph (Chapter 2, regeneration). Unchanged parts of the model are not regenerated, so the cost is proportional to the change, not to the model. - Regeneration runs in parallel on independent sub-graphs, like an ordinary edit (Chapter 2b). - Model validation runs on the merged result: IFC schema rules for changed entities, RXD schema validation, Reviera model rules (overlapping walls, duplicate instances, room boundary problems). New warnings caused by the merge are listed in the sync report and in the warnings list (COL-MNT-004). - Severity of findings: - Blocking (stop before check-in): IFC schema errors on changed entities (wrong types, missing required attributes), duplicate GlobalIds, RXD documents that fail their schema. - Warning (reported, check-in allowed): model rules such as overlapping walls, rooms not enclosed, elements that failed to regenerate. - If regeneration fails for an element, the merge still completes; the element keeps its merged IFC geometry and is flagged needs attention (a warning of kind col.merge.regen_failed naming the element and the two revisions involved). - Merge-caused warnings are tagged with the sync report id, so the warnings dialog can filter "caused by last sync" (COL-MNT-004). - Undo: the merge and its regeneration form one entry in the sync report, not in the undo stack; Ctrl+Z after Get latest does not undo other users' changes. The conflict stash (COL-MRG-002) is the way back for local changes that lost. - Cancel: cancelling during regeneration leaves the merged model in place but unvalidated; the next save or sync runs validation again.

    Data (IFC/RXD). Warnings found here are stored like other warnings in RXD document project/warnings (Chapter 2, DM-FAIL-001), with an extra syncReport field. The needs attention flag is a warning, not a separate field on the element.

    Commands. No new commands; validation runs inside bimserver.get_latest, bimserver.sync and merge.finish. Scripts can re-run it with model.audit(repair?) (COL-MNT-002).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Two users each extend one of two walls that meet at a corner; after both synchronise, the corner join is correct. - [ ] User A deletes a room separation line while user B moves a wall that bounds the same room; after both synchronise, the room area is recomputed and a "room not enclosed" warning, tagged with the sync, appears if the room is open. - [ ] A merge that produces an IFC schema error on a changed entity stops Synchronise before check-in, and Upload anyway is disabled. - [ ] Regenerating after a merge of 1 000 changed elements in a 100 000-element model touches only those elements and their dependents (checked by the regeneration log).

    6.4 Worksets and ownership

    Worksets

    ID: COL-WS-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §7.1–7.3 · screenshots/documentation/worksets_dialog.png

    Purpose. Divide the model into named collections of elements, for visibility control, partial loading and ownership by area of work.

    Behaviour & rules. - A workset has a name, a kind (user or view), visible by default in all views, and open by default. - Every element belongs to exactly one workset. Model elements are in user worksets. View-owned elements (annotation, detail items) belong to the view workset of their view, which is created automatically for each view and sheet and cannot be edited by hand. (Reviera does not need the reference's separate worksets for families and project standards: those are types and RXD standards objects, which follow ordinary per-object ownership, see deviations.) - A new project has the user worksets Shared Levels and Grids (levels, grids, reference planes, scope boxes) and Workset1 (everything else). Enabling worksets on a project without them (Collaborate › Worksets on first use) shows a dialog to rename these two. - Worksets work in Local mode as well (visibility, open/close); ownership applies only in BIMserver mode.

    Data (IFC/RXD). Workset definitions are RXD document project/worksets (kind workset). Each element's workset is element-scoped RXD on that element (Chapter 2a), so that moving one element to another workset changes only that element and merges cleanly. IFC export: with the export option Worksets as groups (default on for coordination setups), each user workset is written as an IfcGroup (ObjectType = 'WORKSET', Name = workset name) with its elements assigned by IfcRelAssignsToGroup, so other tools can filter by workset. This export form is never read back as the native store.

    Commands. workset.create(name, visible_by_default?, open_by_default?) -> workset_id; workset.rename(workset_id, name) -> (); workset.delete(workset_id, move_to_workset_id?|delete_elements?) -> (); workset.move_elements(element_ids[], workset_id) -> (); workset.list() -> workset_summary[] (query)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Deleting a workset requires choosing whether its elements move to another workset or are deleted. - [ ] An IFC export with Worksets as groups contains one IfcGroup per user workset with the correct members. - [ ] Two users each moving different elements to a new workset merge without conflict.

    Worksets dialog, active workset and element workset

    ID: COL-WS-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §7.3 · screenshots/documentation/worksets_dialog.png

    Purpose. One dialog to create, organise, open, close and take ownership of worksets, and to choose where new elements go.

    Workflow. Collaborate › Manage Collaboration › Worksets, or the status-bar workset button (workset.manage). The dialog shows the active workset, Grey inactive workset graphics, and a table: Name, Editable (owned by me), Owner, Borrowers, Opened, Visible in all views. Buttons: New, Delete, Rename, Open, Close, Editable, Non-editable. Show filter: user worksets, view worksets.

    UI (Worksets dialog). - Header: Active workset drop-down (user worksets only, sorted by name) and the Grey inactive workset graphics check box. - Table (one row per workset, multi-select, sortable by any column):

    Column Content Editable in the table
    Name Workset name Yes, for user worksets (in-place rename)
    Editable Yes if the current user owns the whole workset Yes (drop-down), BIMserver mode only
    Owner User name of the workset owner, blank if none No
    Borrowers Users borrowing elements of the workset; a drop-down when more than one No
    Opened Open or Closed Through Open/Close buttons
    Visible in all views Default visibility in views Yes (check box)
    Elements Element count (open worksets only; "–" when closed) No
    • Show filter: check boxes User worksets (default on) and View worksets (default off). View worksets are listed read-only with the view or sheet name; only Opened and Visible are meaningful for them, and they cannot be renamed, deleted or made editable here (ownership of a view is taken by borrowing the view, COL-OWN-001).
    • Buttons: New… (name, Visible in all views default on; the new workset is owned by its creator in BIMserver mode), Delete (asks where the elements go: another workset, or delete them with their count shown), Rename, Open, Close, Editable, Non-editable, and OK, Cancel, Help.
    • In Local mode the Editable, Owner and Borrowers columns and the Editable/Non-editable buttons are hidden.
    • The dialog refreshes live when ownership changes arrive (COL-BIM-007) while it is open.

    Validation. - Names are 1–128 characters, unique among worksets (case-insensitive), and must not start with the reserved prefix View:. Duplicates are refused inline with "A workset with this name already exists". - Delete is refused for the last remaining user workset, for the active workset (choose another active one first), and in BIMserver mode for a workset owned or borrowed from by another user (the message names them). - Rename and Delete in BIMserver mode need ownership of the workset definition; Reviera borrows the definition object automatically, as for any RXD object. - Close is refused for the active workset (choose another active workset first). Closing a workset that contains elements the user has borrowed asks for confirmation, because those elements cannot be edited until it is reopened; the borrows are kept. - Cancel discards all changes made in the dialog; ownership changes already written to the ownership document (Editable/Non-editable) are not undone by Cancel, and the dialog says so before closing.

    Behaviour & rules. - Active workset: new elements go into it. It is shown on the Collaborate tab and on the status bar, and can be a workset owned by someone else (new elements are then created as borrowed by the creator). - Grey inactive workset graphics halftones all elements not in the active workset in every view; it is display-only and never printed (layer 6 of Chapter 5, DOC-GFX-001). - Each element shows Workset (editable for model elements) and Edited by (read-only; the current borrower or the workset owner) in Properties. - Editable = Yes takes ownership of the whole workset (COL-OWN-001). It is refused when the user's base is older than the latest revision that changed any element of the workset; the user is offered Get latest first. - Editable only (status-bar toggle) restricts selection to elements the user may edit without requesting. - Per-view workset visibility (use global setting / show / hide) is part of the view's graphics settings (Chapter 5, DOC-GFX-003, Worksets tab).

    Data (IFC/RXD). Workset definitions, names and visible by default are in RXD document project/worksets (kind workset, COL-WS-001). The active workset, the grey-inactive setting and the open/closed choice are per-user client state (working-copy state.json), never project data. Editable/owner/borrower state is in the live ownership document (COL-OWN-002).

    Commands. workset.manage() -> () opens the Worksets dialog (UI only; each change made in it calls the commands below, so every change is scriptable and recorded); workset.set_active(workset_id) -> (); workset.set_editable(workset_ids[], editable) -> (); workset.set_visible_by_default(workset_id, visible) -> (); view.set_workset_visibility(view_id, workset_id, mode: global|show|hide) -> (); view.grey_inactive_worksets(on) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With Grey inactive workset graphics on, elements in other worksets are halftoned on screen but print normally. - [ ] Making a workset editable while another user borrows one of its elements fails and names the borrower. - [ ] Renaming a workset to the name of an existing one (different case) is refused inline, and Cancel leaves all workset names unchanged. - [ ] In Local mode the Worksets dialog shows no Editable, Owner or Borrowers columns. - [ ] Deleting the active workset is refused until another workset is made active.

    Opening and closing worksets

    ID: COL-WS-003 · Priority: P1 (closing for display), P2 (partial download) · Ref: research/04 §7.3 (Opened)

    Purpose. Improve performance by not loading parts of the model.

    Behaviour & rules. - A closed workset's elements are not displayed, not regenerated, not selectable and not included in schedules (a banner on the schedule says so). - At open time, Specify… lets the user choose which worksets to open; the choice is remembered per user and project (client state). - In P1, closed worksets are still downloaded and kept in the working copy; they are just not loaded into the editing session. In P2, Reviera downloads only open worksets, using a BIMserver query restricted to the GlobalIds of the open worksets' elements (verify query support), and fetches the rest when a workset is opened. - Elements of closed worksets still take part in merges (they are in the working copy file), so closing a workset never loses others' changes.

    Commands. workset.open(workset_ids[]) -> (); workset.close(workset_ids[]) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Closing the Furniture workset removes furniture from views and schedules, and reopening restores it without a download in P1.

    Advisory ownership and borrowing

    ID: COL-OWN-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §7.1 (Workset ownership, Element borrowing); TECH_STACK §3.7.2, §5 (open decision 8)

    Purpose. Avoid conflicts by letting users claim what they are working on, without needing a server-side lock service.

    Behaviour & rules. - Owner identity: the BIMserver user (COL-BIM-001) plus a client session id (so the same user on two machines is two owners). - Ownership units: an element (borrowing), a workset (taking it editable), or an RXD object (a view, a sheet, a schedule, a standards object; borrowed when edited, like an element). View-owned annotation is covered by its view: borrowing a view borrows its annotation. - Automatic borrowing: when a user starts an edit on something nobody owns, Reviera borrows it in the same action (no prompt). The borrow is written to the live ownership document (COL-OWN-002) before the edit is committed. If the write fails because someone else claimed it first, the edit is cancelled and the user is offered an editing request (COL-OWN-003). - Up-to-date rule: an element can be borrowed only if the user's base contains its latest server version. Reviera knows this from the notifications and the ownership document (each ownership entry carries the revision in which its holder last changed the element; each relinquish records it). If the element changed in a newer revision, the user is asked to Get latest first. - Owned by others: attempting to edit an element or object owned by someone else shows "<user> is editing this element" with Place request and Cancel (COL-OWN-003). Viewing and selecting are always allowed. - Relinquishing: happens at synchronise (by option), on Relinquish All Mine (Collaborate tab), on close (COL-BIM-006), or by an administrator's Force relinquish (server administrators only; logged and notified to the former owner). - Advisory nature: ownership is enforced by cooperating Reviera clients and by the merge (COL-MRG-001 step 7). A client that ignores it (for example another IFC tool checking in directly) cannot be stopped without a server plugin (COL-OWN-004); its changes are merged like any remote change. - Offline: while offline, edits to unowned things create provisional borrows that are queued and claimed on reconnection. If a provisional borrow is refused (someone else claimed the element meanwhile), the element is flagged and the merge will treat both edits as a conflict at the next sync.

    Commands. ownership.borrow(element_or_object_ids[]) -> result (normally implicit); ownership.relinquish(scope: all|elements|worksets, ids[]?) -> (); ownership.query(ids[]) -> ownership_info[] (query); ownership.force_relinquish(owner, ids[]?) -> () (administrators)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] User A moves a wall (borrowing it); user B trying to move it sees "A is editing this element" within the notification latency. - [ ] After A synchronises with relinquish, B can move the wall without a request. - [ ] B cannot borrow a wall changed in a revision B has not got yet; B is offered Get latest.

    Live ownership document and sync lock

    ID: COL-OWN-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.7.1–3.7.2; spec/02a (BIMserver transport)

    Purpose. Share ownership and lock state among clients immediately, without creating model revisions.

    Behaviour & rules. - Document: a small JSON document, the ownership document, with schema name org.reviera.ownership/1.0. Contents: version (integer), parentVersion, baseRoid (the revision it applies to), entries[] ({target: ifc:<GlobalId> | rv:<id> | workset:<id>, owner: {userId, userName, session}, since, lastChangedRoid}), requests[] (COL-OWN-003), and syncLock ({owner, acquired, expires} or null). It is not embedded in the IFC model and is never part of a check-in. - Transport (BIMserver extended data, call names from the public BIMserver service interface): 1. One-time per server: register the schema with ServiceInterface.addExtendedDataSchema (name org.reviera.ownership/1.0) if getExtendedDataSchemaByName does not find it. 2. Read: ServiceInterface.getLastExtendedDataOfRevisionAndSchema {"roid": <latest>, "schemaId": …} gives the newest ownership item on the latest revision; ServiceInterface.getFile {"fileId": …} returns its content. To resolve concurrent writers, the client reads all ownership items of the revision (getAllExtendedDataOfRevision, verify) and builds the chain described below. 3. Write: ServiceInterface.uploadFile with the new JSON (base64) returns a file id; ServiceInterface.addExtendedDataToRevision {"roid": <latest>, "extendedData": {"schemaId": …, "fileId": …, "title": "ownership v<N>"}} attaches it. - Optimistic concurrency with a deterministic chain: each write declares parentVersion = the version it was based on, and version = parentVersion + 1. When two clients write children of the same parent, the one attached first (lowest extended-data object id) wins; the others are rejected writes. Every client computes the same current state by following, from the root, the earliest child of each version. A client that sees its own write rejected re-reads, re-applies its change to the winning state if still valid (for example the element is still unowned), and writes again; otherwise it reports the refusal to the user (COL-OWN-001). - New revisions: the client that checks in a revision immediately writes the carried-forward ownership state (after its relinquishes) as the root (version 1, parentVersion null) on the new revision. Until a root exists on the newest revision, clients keep using the chain on the previous revision. - Refresh: clients refresh on new-revision and new-extended-data notifications (COL-BIM-007), and otherwise poll at the update frequency (default 30 s). Before any borrow, the client re-reads the document (not the cache). - Sync lock: the syncLock field implements the "central model in use" lock of COL-BIM-006: a client acquires it by a successful write with itself as holder and an expiry time; it renews by further writes; it releases it by writing null. An expired lock may be taken over by any client. - Growth: each revision accumulates ownership items; Reviera never deletes them (history is useful for audit), and a new revision starts a fresh chain. - Local mode: there is no ownership document; all ownership commands return mode.not_available.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Two clients borrowing the same element within 100 ms of each other: exactly one succeeds, and both clients agree on which one. - [ ] A client that crashes while holding the sync lock blocks others for no longer than the lock's time-to-live. - [ ] Borrowing and relinquishing elements does not create any new model revision. - [ ] After user A checks in, user B (who still has base = previous revision) still sees A's remaining borrows.

    Editing requests

    ID: COL-OWN-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §7.1, §7.5; web: Grant a Request to Borrow an Element; web: Granted, Denied, and Retracted Requests · screenshots/documentation/editing_request_received.png

    Purpose. Ask the owner to hand over an element, a workset or an RXD object.

    Workflow. 1. On a refused edit, the user chooses Place request (optionally with a message). 2. The owner receives a balloon "Editing request from <user>" with Show, Grant, Deny; the status bar shows a pending-requests count. 3. Collaborate › Editing Requests lists My pending requests (with Retract) and Requests to me (with Grant, Deny, Show). 4. When a request is granted, the requester is notified; if the owner had changed the element, the requester must Get latest (offered in the notification) before editing.

    UI (Editing Requests dialog). Opened by Collaborate › Communicate › Editing Requests, by the status-bar Editing Requests counter, or from a request balloon (editrequest.manage). It is modeless, so the user can keep working and use Show while it is open. - Two expandable groups: My pending requests (requests I placed) and Requests to me (requests for things I own). Each request row shows: requester or owner, targets (count, expandable to one row per element, workset or RXD object with category and name), message, time placed, state, and an indicator when a target has unsynchronised changes on the owner's side (*) or was deleted in a newer revision (^). - Buttons (enabled by selection): Grant and Deny (requests to me; Deny asks for an optional reply); Retract (my requests); Show (selects the targets and zooms to them in a suitable open view, opening one if needed; for targets in a closed workset it first asks to open that workset); Close. - History toggle: shows granted, denied, retracted and expired requests of the current revision chain with who decided and when; read-only. - The status-bar counter shows the number of Requests to me that are pending; it turns to the alert colour when there is at least one.

    Behaviour & rules. - Requests are entries in the ownership document's requests[] ({id, from, to, targets[], message, created, state: pending|granted|denied|retracted|expired, decided, reply}), written with the same chain mechanism. - Request scope: a request may name elements, worksets or RXD objects. A request for an element in a workset owned by someone else goes to the workset owner; a request for an element borrowed by someone goes to the borrower. If targets belong to several owners, one request is created per owner and the dialog groups them. - Grant relinquishes the targets to the requester. If the owner has unsynchronised changes to the targets, granting first runs a synchronise of those changes (the owner is asked to confirm), because handing over an element whose latest state is only on the owner's machine would lose work. The Grant button shows "Synchronise and grant" in that case. - Partial grant: the owner can expand a request and grant some targets; the request then stays pending for the rest. - Implicit grant: if the owner relinquishes requested targets in any other way (synchronise with relinquish, Relinquish All Mine), the request is marked granted automatically and the requester is notified. - Deleted targets: a target deleted in a newer revision is dropped from the request with a note; a request whose targets are all deleted becomes expired. - On grant, the requester's client borrows the targets automatically on its next ownership refresh, provided its base contains their latest version; otherwise it offers Get latest first (COL-OWN-001 up-to-date rule). The requester does not need to place the request again. - Advisory nature: a request is a message between cooperating clients; it gives no server-enforced right. Ignoring it is possible only by editing offline or with a foreign client, and the merge (COL-MRG-001 step 7) then settles the outcome. - Requests expire after 7 days (configurable per project, 1–90 days) and are then shown as expired. - Local mode: the dialog and every editrequest.* command return mode.not_available. - Offline: requests placed offline are queued (COL-OFF-001) and sent on reconnection; the dialog shows them as queued.

    Data. Ownership document requests[] only (COL-OWN-002); never IFC or RXD, and never part of a check-in.

    Commands. editrequest.manage() -> () opens the Editing Requests dialog; editrequest.create(targets[], message?) -> request_id; editrequest.grant(request_id) -> (); editrequest.deny(request_id, message?) -> (); editrequest.retract(request_id) -> (); editrequest.list() -> request[] (query; includes history entries with their state)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] B requests a wall owned by A; A grants; A's unsynchronised change to the wall is synchronised first; B is then able to edit the wall after getting latest. - [ ] A denied request shows the owner's message to the requester. - [ ] A request naming two walls, one borrowed by A and one by C, produces two requests, one to each owner, shown grouped in B's dialog. - [ ] A synchronising with relinquish borrowed elements marks B's pending request for one of those elements as granted, and B is notified. - [ ] The status-bar counter shows 2 when two requests to the user are pending, and 0 after both are decided.

    Request editing from the selection

    ID: COL-OWN-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §7.1 (Editing request, Place Request), §7.5; web: Grant a Request to Borrow an Element

    Purpose. Let a user ask for editing rights on selected elements owned by others before starting an edit, and see who owns them, within the advisory ownership model.

    Workflow. 1. Select one or more elements (or a view, sheet or schedule in the Project Browser) in BIMserver mode. When any of them is owned by someone else, the contextual ribbon shows the Ownership panel: Request Editing and Show Owner (Chapter 1). 2. Request Editing opens a small form: the list of selected items grouped by owner (items nobody owns are marked "free"), a message box (optional, up to 500 characters), and Request / Cancel. 3. On Request, items nobody owns are borrowed at once (as an automatic borrow, COL-OWN-001); for the others, one editing request per owner is placed (COL-OWN-003). The result is reported as "Borrowed 3, requested 5 from 2 users". 4. Show Owner shows a tooltip-style panel listing, per selected item, its workset, owner or borrower, since when, and whether the user's base is up to date for it; it uses ownership.query.

    Behaviour & rules. - Mapping onto the advisory model: a request is a message in the live ownership document; nothing is locked on the server (BIMserver has no locking, COL-OWN-004 is deferred). Requested items stay read-only in the requester's client until granted, exactly as for an edit refused by COL-OWN-001. - Items the user already owns are skipped and reported as "already yours". - Items whose latest version is newer than the user's base are still requested, but the result says Get latest will be needed before editing them. - Workset-level request: if the user ticks Request whole workset (shown when all selected items are in one workset owned by another user), the request targets the workset instead of the elements. - Linked elements cannot be requested (links are read-only); they are listed as "in link, not editable". - Local mode: the panel is hidden and the command returns mode.not_available. - Offline: the request is queued (COL-OFF-001) and the free items get provisional borrows. - MCP agents can call ownership.request; requests from an agent carry the logged-in user's identity plus the marker via agent in the message.

    Data. Borrows and requests are written to the ownership document (COL-OWN-002); no IFC or RXD change.

    Commands. ownership.request(element_or_object_ids[], message?, whole_workset?) -> {borrowed[], requests[], skipped[]}. Show Owner uses ownership.query(ids[]) -> ownership_info[] (COL-OWN-001).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Selecting five walls, two free and three borrowed by A, and choosing Request Editing borrows the two free walls and places one request to A for the other three. - [ ] Selecting an element in a linked model and choosing Request Editing places no request and reports it as not editable. - [ ] Show Owner on an element borrowed by A shows A's name and the time the borrow started.

    Enforced ownership through a server plugin (optional)

    ID: COL-OWN-004 · Priority: P3 · Ref: TECH_STACK §5 (decision 8)

    Purpose. For teams that need ownership to be binding even for other clients.

    Deferred (owner, 2026-10-12). Ownership follows what the target BIMserver release supports. Stock BIMserver has no locking, so Reviera's ownership is advisory (COL-OWN-001…003), and the Reviera project does not build or ship an enforcement plugin. The capability check below stays in P1 so that Reviera uses enforcement automatically if BIMserver itself, or a separately maintained plugin, ever provides it. The behaviour below describes what such a server-side facility must offer.

    Behaviour & rules. - An optional BIMserver service plugin (Java, distributed separately under a licence compatible with BIMserver's AGPL-3.0) provides: an atomic compare-and-set endpoint for the ownership document (replacing the optimistic chain), and a check-in validator that rejects revisions changing elements owned by someone other than the uploader (comparing the uploaded model with the previous revision by GlobalId). - Reviera detects the plugin through the server's plugin list and uses it automatically; otherwise it falls back to COL-OWN-002.

    Commands. No new commands; bimserver.capabilities() -> capability_set (query) reports whether enforcement is available.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With the plugin installed, a check-in from a non-Reviera client that modifies an element owned by a Reviera user is rejected by the server.

    Worksharing display modes

    ID: COL-WS-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §7.5 · screenshots/documentation/worksharing_display_worksets.png · screenshots/documentation/worksharing_display_owners.png

    Purpose. Show, in any view, who owns what, which elements are out of date, and which workset elements belong to.

    Workflow. View Control Bar › Worksharing Display: Off; Checkout status; Owners; Model updates; Worksets. Worksharing Display Settings sets colours per user, per workset and per status, and which ones are shown.

    Behaviour & rules. - Checkout status: owned by me / owned by others / not owned. - Owners: one colour per owner (stable, chosen from a distinct palette). - Model updates: up to date; changed in a newer server revision; deleted in a newer server revision. Reviera knows which elements changed from the notifications: after a new-revision event, the client downloads the revision in the background (or uses the server comparison where available) and compares fingerprints with its base (§6.3, steps 1–3), without merging. - Worksets: one colour per workset. - The mode is applied as layer 6a of the graphics model (Chapter 5, DOC-GFX-001): a temporary colour override that is not printed and not saved. - Tooltips over an element show its workset, owner, borrowers and update status.

    Commands. view.set_worksharing_display(view_id, mode: off|checkout|owners|updates|worksets) -> (); worksharing.set_display_colours(kind, key, colour) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] In Model updates mode, elements changed in a revision B has not got yet are coloured within the notification latency, before B gets latest. - [ ] Worksharing display colours never appear in PDF output.

    6.5 Offline working copies

    Working copy layout and offline editing

    Storage (updated 2026-10-12). The offline working copy is the project's live SQLite store (Chapter 2b §8.2). The downloaded base revision is kept in its base_entity and base_rxd tables for the three-way merge, and local edits are kept in its live tables and transaction journal. Crash recovery and offline work therefore share one mechanism. Where the layout described below conflicts with Chapter 2b, Chapter 2b takes precedence. ID: COL-OFF-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.7 (Save to a local working copy and cache (works offline))

    Purpose. Keep working when the server is unreachable, and never lose local work.

    Behaviour & rules. - Each opened BIMserver project has a working-copy folder in the user's data directory: <data>/reviera/bimserver/<server-id>/<poid>/ containing: - working.ifc: the working copy (IFC with embedded RXD), saved by Ctrl+S and by autosave; - base.ifc: the unmodified base revision, used for three-way merges; - state.json: client state (server profile id, poid, base roid, user, open/closed worksets, last sync time, queued ownership operations, queued editing requests); - journal/: an append-only log of committed commands since the last save, so that a crash loses nothing (the journal is replayed on reopen); - stash/: the conflict stash (COL-MRG-002); - cache/: downloaded linked models (COL-LNK-001) and ownership snapshots. - Offline detection: the connection state is shown on the status bar. When offline, the user can open the working copy, edit, save and close. Synchronise and Get latest are disabled with a tooltip. - Queued actions: borrows (provisional), relinquishes and editing requests made offline are queued and sent on reconnection, in order. - Reconnection: the client refreshes the ownership document, processes the queue, and if the server has newer revisions, offers Get latest (it never merges automatically without the user's go-ahead, because merges may need decisions). - Several working copies: a user can keep working copies for several projects and servers; the File › Open › From BIMserver dialog marks projects that have a local working copy and whether it has unsynchronised changes. - Discard: Discard working copy (with confirmation) deletes the folder, after offering to export it as a standalone .ifc.

    Commands. workingcopy.status() -> {base_roid, unsynced_changes, queued_ops, last_sync} (query); workingcopy.list() -> working_copy_summary[] (query); workingcopy.discard(poid, export_path?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With the network disconnected, a user opens a BIMserver project from the working copy, edits it, saves and closes; on reconnection, synchronise uploads the edits. - [ ] Killing the Reviera process after 10 unsaved edits and reopening restores all 10 from the journal. - [ ] A borrow made offline on an element that another user borrowed meanwhile is reported on reconnection, and the element is flagged for conflict review.

    6.6 Linking

    All links are registered in RXD document project/links (kinds link.ifc, link.cad, link.pointcloud, link.pdf, link.image). Each link has a link type (the source and how to load it) and one or more link instances (placement in the host). Linked content is read-only in the host.

    Common link fields: id, name, source (see each type), pathType (relative, absolute, or server), status (loaded, unloaded, not found, error), referenceType (attachment or overlay, IFC links only), and per instance transform (4×3 matrix in host internal coordinates), positioning (how it was placed), namedPosition (COL-POS-004), workset, pinned.

    IFC links

    ID: COL-LNK-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §8.1 (Revit link, IFC link); TECH_STACK §3.7.2 (Linked models)

    Purpose. Reference other models (consultants' models, other buildings, other sub-projects) for coordination and documentation.

    Workflow. 1. Insert › Link › Link IFC: choose the source: - Local file: an .ifc or .ifczip file; - BIMserver project: pick a server, project and either latest (follows new revisions) or a specific revision (pinned). 2. Choose positioning: Auto – origin to origin (internal origins aligned), Auto – project base point to project base point, Auto – by shared coordinates (requires both models to have map conversions, COL-POS-003), Auto – centre to centre, Manual – origin, Manual – base point, Manual – centre (the user clicks the insertion point). 3. Choose the workset for the link instance (BIMserver mode) and Attachment or Overlay.

    Behaviour & rules. - Loading: the linked file is parsed with IfcOpenShell into a read-only model in its own element space. If it carries Reviera Extension Data, its views and annotation are available for By linked view display (COL-LNK-007); other tools' IfcAnnotation content is shown as read-only drafting. - BIMserver sources: the link is downloaded like a revision (COL-BIM-003) into the working-copy cache/. For latest links, a new revision of the linked project triggers a notification "Link <name> has a new revision" with Reload. Source syntax: bimserver://<server-id>/<poid> (latest) or bimserver://<server-id>/<poid>/<roid> (pinned). - Local file sources: Reviera watches the file and offers Reload when it changes. - Selection and use: linked elements can be selected with Tab, or directly when the Select links toggle is on; they can be tagged, dimensioned, scheduled (Include elements in links), used as references for snapping and hosting of view annotation, copied into the host (as new elements with new GlobalIds), monitored (COL-CM-001) and clash-checked (COL-CLASH-001). References use link:<linkId>/ifc:<GlobalId> (Chapter 2a). - Room bounding: a link type option makes linked walls, floors and columns bound host rooms. - Phase mapping: each link type maps the linked model's phases (from its RXD, or from IFC status properties) to host phases; unmapped phases map to the nearest earlier host phase. - Nested links: links inside a linked project are shown if their reference type in that project is Attachment, and hidden if Overlay. - Multiple instances of the same link type are allowed (for example a repeated building), each with its own transform and named position. - Linking across modes: a Local project may link a BIMserver project (when the user is logged in), and a BIMserver project may link a local file; a server-sourced link is stored as a server reference, and a local file link as a path relative to the project when possible. - Performance: linked models are tessellated and indexed in parallel on load; the graphics resolver treats them as additional element sources (Chapter 5, DOC-HLR-001).

    Commands. link.add_ifc(source, positioning, point?, workset_id?, reference_type?: attachment|overlay) -> {link_id, instance_id}; link.add_instance(link_id, positioning, point?) -> instance_id; link.set_phase_map(link_id, map{}) -> (); link.set_room_bounding(link_id, on) -> (); link.copy_elements(instance_id, element_refs[]) -> element_id[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Linking a structural model from BIMserver (latest) shows it in the host; when the structural engineer checks in a new revision, the architect gets a notification and Reload shows the new geometry. - [ ] A host plan tags a linked column, and the tag survives a reload. - [ ] A linked model placed by shared coordinates lands at the correct position relative to the host within 1 mm.

    CAD links and imports

    ID: COL-LNK-002 · Priority: P1 (DXF), P1 (DWG through LibreDWG), P3 (DGN, SAT, SKP, 3DM) · Ref: research/04 §8.1 (CAD Link vs Import)

    Purpose. Use 2D and 3D CAD drawings as underlays and backgrounds.

    Workflow. Insert › Link › Link CAD (keeps a reference and reloads) or Insert › Import › Import CAD (copies the content into the project). Options: Current view only (the CAD becomes view-owned in that view) or all views; colours (black and white, preserve, invert); layers (all, visible only, specify); import units (auto-detect from the file header, or a chosen unit); Correct lines slightly off axis (snaps lines within 0.1° of the axes); positioning (as COL-LNK-001, plus Auto – by shared coordinates using the file's coordinates as shared coordinates); level to place at; orient to view.

    Behaviour & rules. - Readers: DXF through Reviera's own reader; DWG through LibreDWG (GPL-3.0-or-later), which reads the common DWG versions. Unsupported entities (for example proxy objects) are skipped and listed. - CAD layers become sub-categories of an Imported Objects category for that file (Chapter 5, DOC-GFX-002), with per-view visibility in the graphics dialog's Imported Categories tab. - Query reports the layer and entity type of a picked CAD element; Delete layers removes layers from an import. - Explode (imports only): Partial (one level of blocks) or Full, turning CAD geometry into detail lines, text and filled regions (view-specific imports) or model lines (all-view imports). - Snapping to CAD geometry (end points, mid points, intersections, centres) is supported. - Linked CAD is stored as a link (link.cad); imported CAD is stored as RXD drafting content of the view (current view only) or as an RXD import.cad object with its own geometry (all views). Imported CAD geometry is never written into IFC elements, except as export annotation when the user exports documentation (Chapter 5, DOC-IFC-002).

    Commands. link.add_cad(path, view_id?, colours?, layers?, units?, correct_off_axis?, positioning, level_id?) -> {link_id, instance_id}; import.cad(path, view_id?, options) -> import_id; import.explode(import_id, mode: partial|full) -> element_ids[]; import.delete_layers(import_id, layers[]) -> (); import.query(import_id, pick_ref) -> cad_entity_info (query)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A DWG site survey linked by shared coordinates appears at its survey coordinates. - [ ] Hiding a CAD layer in a view hides only that layer's geometry in that view. - [ ] Fully exploding a view-specific import produces detail lines with line styles derived from the CAD layers.

    Point clouds

    ID: COL-LNK-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/04 §8.1 (Point cloud)

    Purpose. Use laser scans of existing buildings as references.

    Workflow. Insert › Link › Point Cloud: choose E57, LAS, LAZ, COPC (cloud-optimised LAZ) or PLY files; positioning (as COL-LNK-001); Reviera indexes the file on first use.

    Behaviour & rules. - Readers: libE57Format (Boost licence) for E57; las/laz Rust crates (MIT/Apache) for LAS/LAZ; Reviera's own PLY reader. - Indexing: every cloud is converted once into an octree in the open COPC format (LAZ 1.4 with a hierarchical index), stored next to the source file or in the working-copy cache. Indexing runs in the background on all cores, with progress. Scans in a multi-scan E57 file become scan regions. - Display: the GPU viewport streams octree nodes by screen-space error within a point budget (default 5 million points), with point size and eye-dome lighting for depth perception. Colour modes: normal (RGB), single colour, by elevation, by intensity, by normal. - Point clouds are clipped by section boxes, crop regions and view ranges like model geometry; they appear in hidden-line views as points (not as linework). - Snapping: to points, and to planes and edges detected locally around the cursor (RANSAC plane fit in a small neighbourhood). - Per-view visibility per cloud and per scan region (graphics dialog, Point Clouds tab).

    Commands. link.add_pointcloud(path, positioning, point?) -> {link_id, instance_id}; pointcloud.reindex(link_id) -> job_id; view.set_pointcloud_display(view_id, link_id, visible?, colour_mode?, regions?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A 500-million-point E57 scan is indexed in the background and then orbits at 30 fps or more on the reference GPU with the default budget. - [ ] Snapping to a detected wall plane lets the user draw a wall aligned with the scan within 5 mm.

    PDF underlays

    ID: COL-LNK-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §8.1 (PDF / Image (underlay))

    Purpose. Trace over and measure from PDF drawings (surveys, consultants' plans, old drawings) in a plan, section, elevation or drafting view.

    Workflow. 1. Insert › Import › PDF: choose a file; a page picker shows thumbnails (multi-page files); choose the page, a resolution for raster content (72–1200 dpi, default 150), Link (reloadable, default) or Import (copied into the project assets), and the draw layer. 2. Click to place the page's centre in the current view (or press Enter to place it at the view centre). The page is placed at 1:1 paper size scaled by the view scale. 3. Optionally Calibrate: click two points on the underlay and type their real distance; the underlay is scaled about the first point.

    Behaviour & rules. - Pages are rendered with PDFium (BSD/Apache licence). Vector content is also extracted as geometry so that the user can snap to PDF lines and arcs, and scale-calibrate by picking two points and entering their real distance. - Draw layer: background (below model) or foreground. - A PDF underlay is view-owned; it can be hidden, moved, rotated, scaled, pinned. - Only plan, ceiling, section, elevation, drafting and detail views accept a PDF underlay; 3D views and schedules disable the command. Sheets use image placement (COL-LNK-005). - Rendering cache: the page is rasterised once per dpi and cached in the working-copy or project cache folder; zooming in beyond the cached resolution re-renders the visible tiles at higher resolution in the background, up to the chosen dpi × 4. - Vector extraction: paths are flattened to lines and arcs in page coordinates; text is not extracted. Pages with more than 2 million path segments keep snapping off and show a note. - Calibration keeps the aspect ratio. The real distance must be greater than zero and the two points at least 1 mm apart on paper; otherwise the command fails with underlay.bad_calibration. Calibration is undoable and can be repeated. - Linked PDFs: a changed source file is detected on open and on Reload (COL-LNK-006); a missing file shows the last cached raster greyed with "not found", and the underlay keeps its position and calibration. If the reloaded page has different paper dimensions, Reviera keeps the calibration scale and warns. - Imported PDFs are stored as RXD assets and do not depend on the source file. - The underlay never prints when the view property Show underlays in print is off (default on); it is never exported to IFC. - Interactive placement and calibration follow the micro-operation rule (conventions §2.1): micro-ops pdf.place_point{xy} and underlay.calib_point{index, xy}, underlay.calib_distance{value}; replay re-applies the recorded points and reopens the calibration prompt at the last missing step.

    Data (IFC/RXD). Linked PDF: RXD document project/links, kind link.pdf (source, page, dpi, pathType, status) with one instance per placement holding viewId, transform, layer and calibration scale. Imported PDF: the same kind with source pointing at an RXD asset. The underlay is not an IFC entity.

    Commands. link.add_pdf(path, page, view_id, dpi?, link?, position, layer?: background|foreground) -> underlay_id; underlay.calibrate(underlay_id, point_a, point_b, real_distance) -> (). Reload, reload from, unload and remove use the link commands of COL-LNK-006.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] After calibration with a known 10 m dimension, a 5 m line in the PDF measures 5 m (±0.5 %). - [ ] The cursor snaps to end points of PDF vector lines. - [ ] Deleting the source of a linked PDF shows the underlay greyed as "not found" at the same position; restoring the file and reloading shows it normally with its calibration kept. - [ ] Link PDF is disabled in a 3D view. - [ ] Killing Reviera after the first calibration point and reopening resumes calibration at the second point.

    Image underlays

    ID: COL-LNK-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §8.1 (PDF / Image)

    Purpose. Place raster images (site photos, scanned drawings, logos) as underlays in views or as artwork on sheets.

    Behaviour & rules. - Insert › Import › Image: PNG, JPEG, TIFF (single page; multi-page TIFF uses the first page and warns), BMP, WebP; link or import; placed in the current view (or on a sheet, Chapter 5, DOC-SHT-001); draw layer background or foreground; calibrate scale by two points (as COL-LNK-004, same underlay.calibrate and micro-ops). - Placement: two clicks for opposite corners, or one click with the image's own size (from its dpi metadata, 96 dpi if none) scaled to the view; Lock proportions is on by default. width sets the placed width in model units (or paper units on sheets). - Limits: images up to 16 384 × 16 384 pixels; larger images are refused with image.too_large and the user is offered to downscale on import. Colour images with alpha keep transparency. - Linked images reload when the source changes; a missing source shows a placeholder frame with "not found" and keeps size and position. - Imported images are stored as RXD assets (Chapter 2a), de-duplicated by SHA-256 hash, so placing the same image twice stores it once. - Manage Images (Insert › Import › Manage Images) lists every image asset and linked image: name, source path (for linked), pixel size, file size, number of placements and the views or sheets using them. Actions: Delete (an image in use asks to delete its placements too, or to replace it with another image via replace_with, which keeps every placement's size and position), Reload, Show (opens a view using it). - In BIMserver mode, image assets travel with the model and merge by asset hash; two users importing the same file produce one asset.

    Data (IFC/RXD). Kind link.image in RXD document project/links (linked) or RXD asset plus a placement record (imported); placements are view- or sheet-owned. Not written to IFC.

    Commands. link.add_image(path, view_id, link?, position, width?, layer?) -> underlay_id; image.manage_list() -> image_info[] (query); image.delete(image_ids[], replace_with?) -> (). The Manage Images dialog is shared with Chapter 2 (image.manage, DM-IMG-001); image.manage_list returns the same records as Chapter 2's image.list and is kept as an alias.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] An imported image still displays after the source file is deleted; a linked one shows "not found" in Manage Links. - [ ] Importing the same PNG into two views stores one asset, and Manage Images shows two placements. - [ ] Deleting an image in use with replace_with swaps the picture in every placement without changing their sizes or positions.

    Manage Links

    ID: COL-LNK-006 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §8.2 · screenshots/documentation/manage_links_new_dialog_type_filter.png

    Purpose. One place to see and control every link and import.

    Workflow. Insert › Link › Manage Links, or Manage › Manage Project › Manage Links (link.manage). The dialog is a single tree of all links and imports (IFC, CAD, point clouds, PDF, images) with a type filter, search, and a collapsible details panel.

    UI (Manage Links dialog). Modeless and resizable; it remembers its size, columns and filter per user. - Toolbar: Type filter (All, IFC, CAD, Point clouds, PDF, Images), search box (matches name and source), Show imported CAD check box, column chooser (gear), and the action buttons below. Actions that do not apply to the selected rows are disabled with a tooltip giving the reason. - Tree: one row per link (link type); its instances are child rows (name, placement summary, named position, workset). Nested links of an IFC link appear as grandchildren, read-only, marked nested (attachment); nested overlays are not listed because they are never loaded. - Details panel (collapsible, for the selected row): full source (copyable), resolved absolute path, file size and modification time, last load time and duration, element count, schema (IFC2X3, IFC4, IFC4X3), map conversion present yes/no, room bounding, phase map summary, and the error text for links in error state. - Context menu per row: the same actions plus Copy source, Open source folder (local files), Open in new window (IFC links: opens the source read-only as its own model).

    Behaviour & rules. - Columns (choosable): name, type, status (loaded, unloaded, not found, error), source (path or bimserver:// reference; copyable), path type (relative, absolute, server), reference type (attachment, overlay), revision (for BIMserver links: pinned revision or "latest", and whether a newer revision exists), positions not saved, size, instances. - Link kinds and what applies to each:

    Kind Sources Reference type Instances Positions Worksets Bind
    IFC (link.ifc) local .ifc/.ifczip, bimserver:// Attachment / Overlay Many Yes (COL-POS-004) Yes, if the link has worksets Yes
    CAD (link.cad) local .dxf/.dwg — Many (one per view for current view only) Yes (CAD shared coordinates) — No (use Import CAD, then Explode)
    Point cloud (link.pointcloud) local E57/LAS/LAZ/COPC/PLY — Many No — No
    PDF (link.pdf) local .pdf — One per view placement No — No (re-insert as Import)
    Image (link.image) local raster files — One per placement No — No
    Imported CAD (import.cad, shown with Show imported CAD) none (content is in the project) — One No — —
    • Status values:
    • Loaded: parsed and displayed.
    • Unloaded: deliberately not loaded; kept in the registry with all instances, tags and monitors, which reappear on reload.
    • Not found: the source cannot be resolved (missing file, unknown server profile, deleted server project or revision).
    • Error: the source was found but failed to load (parse error, unsupported schema, decryption failure, missing deserialiser); the details panel shows the message.
    • Loading…: transient, with progress; large links load in the background and the row shows a percentage.
    • BIMserver links also show Newer revision available (latest-following links) or Pinned in the revision column.
    • Actions (on one or many rows): Reload, Reload From… (a different file, or a different server project or revision), Unload, Remove, Add, Bind (IFC links: copy the linked elements into the host as new elements with new GlobalIds, after a warning), Save Positions (write a moved instance's position back as a named position, COL-POS-004), Show (select the instance or underlay in a view), Manage Worksets (open or close the linked model's worksets per instance).
    • Reload re-reads the source; elements are re-matched by GlobalId so that tags, dimensions, monitors, clash results and issues keep their references; references whose element disappeared are orphaned and listed (COL-CM-003 for hosted elements). After reload, monitored pairs are re-checked (COL-CM-002).
    • Reload From… changes the source and reloads. Changing between a local file and a server source is allowed. If fewer than 50 % of referenced GlobalIds are found in the new source, Reviera warns before committing ("this looks like a different model").
    • Unload keeps the link and its instances; annotation that refers to unloaded elements is hidden, not deleted.
    • Remove deletes the link type, all its instances, and asks what to do with annotation and monitor pairs that refer to it (Delete them or Keep as orphans); the confirmation states the counts.
    • Add opens the matching insert command (Link IFC, Link CAD, Point Cloud, PDF, Image) for the chosen type filter.
    • Bind is refused while the link is unloaded or not found, and for links with more than 200 000 elements unless confirmed twice.
    • Path type: Relative (to the project file's folder, or to the working-copy folder for BIMserver projects), Absolute, or Server (bimserver://, set automatically for server sources and not selectable for files). Changing to Relative is refused for a file on another drive or volume, and the row reports why. Local mode stores relative paths by default.
    • Reference type and nesting: Attachment means the link is carried along when this project is itself linked into another model; Overlay means it is ignored there. Only IFC links have a reference type (default Overlay, so that consultant models are not duplicated downstream). Nesting depth shown and loaded is limited to 4; deeper attachments are listed with a warning and not loaded. A circular link (A attaches B, B attaches A) is detected on load; the repeat is not loaded and a warning names the cycle.
    • Batch edit: change path type and reference type of many links at once.
    • Unload for me / for everyone: in BIMserver mode, Unload for me is a client preference; Unload for everyone changes the shared RXD link status (requires ownership of the link object).
    • Show imported CAD lists imports as well as links.
    • Selection in the dialog and selection in the canvas stay in step.
    • Undo: link registry edits (remove, path type, reference type, bind, open worksets) are one undo step per dialog action. Reload, Reload From and Unload change what is loaded, not project data (except the source of Reload From and the status of Unload for everyone), and are not undoable.

    Data (IFC/RXD). Everything listed is in RXD document project/links (kinds above; common fields in §6.6 introduction). Unload for me and per-instance open linked worksets for the current user are client state; Unload for everyone and the shared default of open linked worksets are RXD.

    Commands. link.manage() -> () opens the Manage Links dialog (UI only); link.show(link_or_instance_id) -> view_id (selects the instance or underlay and zooms to it in a suitable view, opening one if needed); link.list() -> link_summary[] (query); link.reload(link_ids[]) -> (); link.reload_from(link_id, new_source) -> (); link.unload(link_ids[], for_everyone?) -> (); link.remove(link_ids[]) -> (); link.bind(link_id) -> element_id[]; link.set_path_type(link_ids[], path_type) -> (); link.set_reference_type(link_ids[], reference_type) -> (); link.set_open_worksets(instance_id, workset_names[]) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Changing ten links from absolute to relative paths in one batch edit updates all ten in one undo step. - [ ] A link whose file was moved shows Not found, and Reload From with the new path restores it without losing tags on its elements. - [ ] A link set to Overlay in project B is not shown when B is linked into project C; switching it to Attachment and saving B makes it appear in C as a nested link after reload. - [ ] Two projects that attach each other load without hanging, and a warning names the cycle. - [ ] Unloading a link hides the tags on its elements; reloading shows them again unchanged. - [ ] Changing a link on drive D: to a relative path from a project on drive C: is refused with a reason.

    Link visibility and display settings

    ID: COL-LNK-007 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §3.3 (Revit Links tab), §8.2 (Visibility of links)

    Behaviour & rules. - In the graphics dialog's Links tab (Chapter 5, DOC-GFX-003), per link instance: visible, halftone, underlay, and Display settings: - By host view: linked elements go through the host view's graphics layers (categories, filters, phase, detail level); - By linked view: the link is drawn as a chosen view of the linked model shows it (requires the linked model's RXD; its view range, overrides, annotation categories and phase are used); - Custom: per tab, choose host, linked view or custom settings for model categories, annotation categories, filters, worksets, phase (with phase mapping), detail level and nested links. - Line weights from host or linked model: whether linked elements use the host's pen tables or the link's. - Host view filters can target linked elements when the link uses host or custom filter settings. - Visibility of a linked model's worksets is per instance (Manage Worksets).

    Data (RXD). In the host view's payload: linkOverrides keyed by link instance id.

    Commands. view.set_link_display(view_id, instance_id, mode: host|linked_view|custom, linked_view_id?, custom?, visible?, halftone?, underlay?, line_weights_from?: host|link) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With By linked view set to the structural model's Level 1 plan, the host plan shows the linked columns exactly as that structural plan does. - [ ] Halftoning a link instance halftones all of its elements in that view only.

    6.7 Positioning and coordinate systems

    Internal origin, project base point and survey point

    ID: COL-POS-001 · Priority: P0 (internal origin, project base point), P1 (survey point, shared coordinates) · Ref: research/04 §8.3

    Purpose. Locate the model in project terms and in the real world.

    Behaviour & rules. - Internal origin: the origin of the IFC model's world coordinate system (the WorldCoordinateSystem of the project's IfcGeometricRepresentationContext, normally at (0,0,0) with no rotation). All Reviera geometry is stored relative to it. It cannot be moved. It can be shown in views through the Site › Internal Origin sub-category. - Project base point (PBP): the origin of the project coordinate system that users dimension from and report spot coordinates against (Chapter 5, DOC-ANN-006/007). Its properties are its position relative to the internal origin and the angle to true north. Moving the PBP changes the project coordinate system only; the model does not move. Pinning prevents accidental moves. - Survey point (SP): a known point of the shared coordinate system, which is the real-world map grid (for example a national grid). Its properties are its shared coordinates (easting, northing, elevation). Moving the survey point graphically, or Specify coordinates at a point (COL-POS-004), redefines the shared coordinates of the whole model; the model does not move relative to the internal origin. - Distance warning: if model geometry lies more than a set distance from the internal origin (default 20 km, user setting), Reviera warns that geometric operations may lose precision, and offers to move the geometry and adjust the project base point and shared coordinates so that real-world positions are preserved. - Plan orientation: each plan has Orientation: Project North / True North (Chapter 5, DOC-GFX-015). - Rotate project north: rotates the project coordinate system (and so the presentation of every plan set to project north), for example to square the building on sheets. It changes the PBP angle; the model does not rotate relative to the internal origin. - Rotate true north: rotates the shared coordinate system relative to the project (changes the map conversion angle, COL-POS-003).

    Data (IFC/RXD). Project base point position and angle, and survey point marker position: RXD document project/settings (section positioning). Shared coordinates and true north: IFC entities, see COL-POS-003.

    Commands. coord.set_project_base_point(position?, angle_to_true_north?) -> (); coord.set_survey_point(internal_position?, shared_coordinates?) -> (); coord.rotate_project_north(angle) -> (); coord.rotate_true_north(angle) -> (); coord.relocate_to_origin(shift?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Moving the project base point changes spot coordinates relative to it but no element's internal position. - [ ] Rotating project north by 30° rotates every plan set to project north on screen and on sheets, while views set to true north are unchanged. - [ ] Geometry placed 25 km from the internal origin triggers the distance warning; accepting the relocation keeps every element's shared coordinates unchanged.

    Geographic location

    ID: COL-POS-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §8.3 (Location, Sites)

    Purpose. Record where on Earth the project is, for sun studies, climate data and georeferencing.

    Workflow. 1. Manage › Project Location › Location opens the Location dialog with three tabs: Location, Weather, Site. 2. Location tab: choose Define location by: Address (search box, results list), Coordinates (latitude, longitude in decimal degrees or D°M′S″), or Map (click the site on an online map). Elevation and time zone are filled from the result where known and can be edited. 3. Weather tab: pick a nearby weather station or a climate file (EPW) reference for analysis (Chapter 4). 4. OK writes the location; Cancel discards.

    Behaviour & rules. - Manage › Project Location › Location: set the site by address search (optional online geocoding service; user-configurable, off by default for privacy), by latitude and longitude, or by picking on a map (optional online map tiles). Elevation above sea level, time zone and a weather station or climate file reference (Chapter 4 analysis) are stored too. - Privacy: when the online service is off, the Address and Map options are disabled with a tooltip explaining how to enable them in Options; no request leaves the machine. The service URL is a user setting (any Nominatim-compatible geocoder and any XYZ tile server). - Validation: latitude −90…90°, longitude −180…180°, elevation −500…9 000 m; out-of-range values are refused inline. The time zone is an IANA name (for example Europe/London); daylight saving is derived from it. - Latitude, longitude and elevation are written to IfcSite.RefLatitude, RefLongitude and RefElevation. - IFC form: latitude and longitude are written as IfcCompoundPlaneAngleMeasure (degrees, minutes, seconds, millionths of a second, with a common sign). Reviera converts from decimal degrees with rounding to the nearest millionth of a second (about 0.03 mm) and reads both four- and three-part forms. - If the project has several IfcSite objects (several buildings), the location is written to the site chosen as project site (default: the first); the others keep their own values. - The location does not move the model and does not change shared coordinates. If a CRS is set (COL-POS-003), Reviera compares the location with the position implied by the map conversion and warns when they differ by more than 1 km ("Location and shared coordinates disagree"), offering to update either one. - The location drives sun position (Chapter 5, DOC-GFX-012, DOC-OUT-011) and, when a CRS is chosen, can be converted to and from map coordinates with PROJ (MIT licence).

    Data (IFC/RXD). IfcSite.RefLatitude, RefLongitude, RefElevation, and IfcPostalAddress (on IfcSite.SiteAddress) for the address. Time zone, weather station and climate file reference: RXD document project/location.

    Commands. coord.set_location(latitude, longitude, elevation?, time_zone?, address?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Setting latitude and longitude writes them to IfcSite in the IFC degree-minute-second-microsecond form and reads back the same values. - [ ] With the online service off, no network request is made when the Location dialog is opened and used. - [ ] Entering latitude 95° is refused inline. - [ ] Setting a location 5 km from the position implied by the project's map conversion shows the disagreement warning.

    IFC georeferencing: IfcMapConversion and IfcProjectedCRS

    ID: COL-POS-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §6.4 (Geographic Reference), §8.3

    Purpose. Store shared coordinates in standard IFC, so that every IFC tool places the model correctly.

    Behaviour & rules. - Coordinate reference system: Manage › Project Location › Coordinate System: choose a projected CRS by EPSG code or name search (from the PROJ database), plus a vertical datum. Reviera writes an IfcProjectedCRS with Name (for example EPSG:27700), Description, GeodeticDatum, VerticalDatum, MapProjection, MapZone and MapUnit (an IfcNamedUnit) where known. - Map conversion: shared coordinates are the image of internal coordinates under one similarity transform, written as an IfcMapConversion with SourceCRS = the project's 3D model IfcGeometricRepresentationContext, TargetCRS = the IfcProjectedCRS, and: - Eastings, Northings, OrthogonalHeight: the shared coordinates of the internal origin; - XAxisAbscissa, XAxisOrdinate: cosine and sine of the angle from the internal x axis to the map's easting axis (grid north rotation); - Scale: the ratio of map units to model length units, combined with the CRS's scale factor at the site if the user enables Apply grid scale factor (default off; IFC4X3 projects may use the scaled map-conversion entity where the schema provides one). - Deriving the conversion from the survey point: with survey point internal position s, its shared coordinates (E, N, H), and rotation θ, the translation is (E, N, H) − R(θ)·s, where R(θ) rotates about the vertical axis. Reviera recomputes and rewrites IfcMapConversion whenever the survey point, shared coordinates or true-north rotation change. - True north: IfcGeometricRepresentationContext.TrueNorth is set to the direction of geodetic true north in internal coordinates. Grid north (from the map conversion) and true north differ by the meridian convergence at the site, which Reviera computes with PROJ; the UI shows both and lets the user say which one Angle to true north means (default: grid north, which is what surveys normally give). - Reading: when a foreign IFC with IfcMapConversion is opened or linked, Reviera derives its shared coordinate system from it. IFC2X3 files with only the IFC2X3 property-set convention for georeferencing (ePSet_MapConversion / ePSet_ProjectedCRS) are read too. - Export coordinate base (Chapter 5, DOC-OUT-006): internal origin writes geometry unchanged with the map conversion; project base point or shared coordinates write the IFC with geometry shifted so that the chosen origin becomes (0,0,0), and adjust the map conversion so that real-world positions are unchanged.

    Commands. coord.set_crs(epsg_or_wkt, vertical_datum?, apply_scale_factor?) -> (); coord.get_georeference() -> {crs, map_conversion, true_north, grid_convergence} (query)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A model with CRS EPSG:27700 and survey point coordinates set opens in another IFC tool that supports georeferencing at the correct national-grid position (checked at three points, within 1 mm). - [ ] Changing the survey point's shared coordinates updates IfcMapConversion and leaves internal geometry unchanged. - [ ] Exporting with coordinate base shared coordinates produces geometry whose coordinates equal the survey-based shared coordinates.

    Acquire, publish, specify and report coordinates; named positions

    ID: COL-POS-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §8.3 (Coordinate tools, Positioning options, Reposition a link)

    Purpose. Agree on shared coordinates between linked models.

    Behaviour & rules. - Acquire coordinates: pick a link instance (IFC or CAD); the host adopts the shared coordinate system implied by the link's placement and the link's own shared coordinates (its map conversion, or for CAD the file's coordinates), so that the host's real-world position matches the link's. - Publish coordinates: pick a link instance; the host's shared coordinate system, expressed in the link's internal coordinates, is recorded as a named position for that link. For a local IFC link, Save positions writes the new map conversion into the linked file (after confirmation, and only if the file is writable and not open elsewhere). For a BIMserver link, saving positions means checking in a new revision of the linked project containing only the updated georeference (requires ownership of the linked project's georeference, through its ownership document). Until saved, Manage Links shows Positions not saved. - Specify coordinates at a point: click a point and enter its shared coordinates (easting, northing, elevation) and optionally the angle to true north; the survey point and map conversion are updated. - Report shared coordinates: click a point to read its shared coordinates (and project coordinates); also available as coord.report_point for scripts. - Reset shared coordinates: makes the shared coordinate system equal to the internal one (identity map conversion), after confirmation. - Named positions (sites): a project can hold several named shared positions (for example, the same building placed at two sites). Each link instance records which named position of the linked model it uses, and Auto – by shared coordinates asks which named position to use when the link has more than one. Only the current named position is written to the project's IfcMapConversion; the others are RXD (project/settings, section positioning.namedPositions). - Moving a link instance: after moving or rotating an instance placed by shared coordinates, Reviera asks on save whether to Record the new position in the link (as publish), Keep the old shared position (the instance becomes manually positioned), or Cancel.

    Commands. coord.acquire(instance_id) -> (); coord.publish(instance_id, position_name?) -> (); link.save_positions(link_ids[]) -> (); coord.specify_at_point(point, easting, northing, elevation, angle?) -> (); coord.report_point(point) -> {shared, project, internal} (query); coord.reset_shared() -> (); coord.create_named_position(name) -> position_id; coord.set_current_position(position_id) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] After acquiring coordinates from a survey DWG, a spot coordinate on a survey control point shows the survey's coordinates. - [ ] After publishing coordinates to a linked IFC and saving positions, re-linking that file by shared coordinates in a new project places it at the same real-world position as in the original host.

    6.8 Coordination

    Copy/Monitor

    ID: COL-CM-001 · Priority: P1 (levels, grids), P2 (columns, walls, floors, openings, MEP fixtures) · Ref: research/04 §8.4

    Purpose. Create host copies of key elements from a linked model (or pair existing elements) and watch the pairs for changes.

    Workflow. 1. Collaborate › Coordinate › Copy/Monitor ▾ › Select Link (pick a link instance) or Use Current Project (monitor two elements in the host). 2. Contextual tab Copy/Monitor: - Options: per category, a mapping from linked types to host types (levels, grids, columns, walls, floors), plus offsets (for example a level offset), name prefixes or suffixes, Copy hosted openings, doors and windows for walls, Split columns by level, and which parameters to monitor. - Copy: pick elements (or Multiple with a window selection, then Finish). Each copy is created in the host with the mapped type and a new GlobalId, at the linked element's position, and paired with it. - Monitor: pick a host element, then the linked (or host) element to pair it with. - Batch copy (MEP fixtures, P2): copy all fixtures of chosen categories that match mapping rules. - Finish. 3. Monitored host elements show a monitor badge in views.

    Behaviour & rules. - A monitor pair records the host element, the source element (link:<linkId>/ifc:<GlobalId> or a host GlobalId), the monitored aspects (position, orientation, extent, name or mark, chosen parameters) and a snapshot of the source's values as last accepted. - Pairs survive reloads, changes of link source (Reload From) when GlobalIds are kept, and BIMserver merges. - Stopping monitoring (Stop Monitoring on the host element) removes the pair but keeps the element. - Starting the mode (copymonitor.start): with a link_instance_id, the user picked a link instance (only loaded IFC link instances are pickable; CAD, point clouds and underlays are ignored by the pick filter); without it, the mode works inside the current project and Copy is disabled (only Monitor is available). Only one Copy/Monitor session can be active per model window. Starting it in a view where the link is hidden asks to show it temporarily. - Session behaviour: every Copy or Monitor pick inside the session is added to a pending list shown in the status bar ("3 copied, 1 monitored"). Finish commits all of them as one undoable transaction; Cancel discards them. Options changed in the session are saved immediately (they are settings, not part of the transaction). - Validation on Copy: an element whose category has no mapping or whose mapping is Do not copy is skipped with a note; an element already paired with a host element is not copied again (the existing pair is highlighted); a level or grid whose name would clash with an existing host name gets the mapping's prefix or suffix, then a numeric suffix if still not unique. - Validation on Monitor: both elements must be of the same category (levels with levels, grids with grids, and so on), the host element must not already be monitoring another element, and in BIMserver mode the host element is borrowed when the pair is created (COL-OWN-001). - Ownership: copied elements are created in the active workset and are borrowed by the creator; monitor pairs are RXD objects owned like any other. - Interactive tool rule (conventions §2.1): the session declares micro-ops cm.start{link_instance_id?}, cm.copy{source_ref, host_type_id, offsets}, cm.multiple{source_refs[]}, cm.monitor{host_element_id, source_ref}, cm.set_option{category, key, value} and cm.finish. Replay after a crash rebuilds the pending list from the recorded micro-ops against the reloaded link, skips sources that no longer exist (listed), and leaves the session open for the user to Finish or Cancel.
