    Data (RXD). RXD document coordination/monitors, kind monitor.pair: host, source, aspects[], snapshot{}, tolerances{}, status. Copy/Monitor options and coordination settings are kind monitor.settings in the same document (COL-CM-004). Copied elements are ordinary IFC elements with new GlobalIds.

    Commands. copymonitor.start(link_instance_id?) -> () enters the Copy/Monitor mode and shows its contextual tab (omitting the link means Use Current Project); copymonitor.finish() -> pair_id[]; copymonitor.cancel() -> (); copymonitor.set_options(link_instance_id?, category, mapping{}, options{}) -> (); copymonitor.copy(link_instance_id, element_refs[]) -> element_id[]; copymonitor.monitor(host_element_id, source_ref) -> pair_id; copymonitor.stop(pair_ids[]) -> (); copymonitor.batch_copy(link_instance_id, categories[], rules) -> element_id[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Copying all levels from a structural link creates host levels with the mapped level type, offsets and name suffix, each paired with its source. - [ ] Copying a wall with Copy hosted openings also copies its doors and windows, each monitored. - [ ] Cancel after copying five grids leaves the host without those grids and without monitor pairs; Finish followed by one Undo gives the same result. - [ ] Trying to monitor a host level against a linked grid is refused with a category-mismatch message. - [ ] Killing Reviera after three copies inside a session and reopening shows the session with the three pending copies.

    Coordination review

    ID: COL-CM-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §8.4 (Coordination Review); web: Actions for Coordination Review; web: Review Warnings for Monitored Elements

    Purpose. Show and settle changes found on monitored pairs.

    Workflow. 1. After a link reload (or when a host element is edited), Reviera checks every affected pair; if anything changed, a warning says "Coordination review needed for <link>". 2. Collaborate › Coordinate › Coordination Review ▾ › Select Link / Use Current Project opens the review dialog: a tree grouped by status and category, each item describing the change (moved by 120 mm; renamed from "Level 3" to "L03"; deleted; parameter X changed from a to b; type changed). 3. Per item: Postpone (leave for later), Reject (the change in the source is wrong; keep the host and record the rejection, which the source's author can see if they also run Reviera with this host linked), Accept difference (update the snapshot; keep the host as it is), Modify host (move, rename or edit the host element to match), and a comment. Show zooms to the pair. Create report writes an HTML or CSV report.

    UI (Coordination Review dialog). Opened with coordreview.show(link_instance_id?): with a link instance it reviews pairs whose source is in that link; without it, pairs inside the current project. Modeless, so Show can be used while it is open. - Header: the scope (link instance name or "Current project"), a Group by choice (status → category → change kind, the default; or category → status → change kind), and a filter for status (default: pending and postponed). - Tree rows (one per change): host element (category, name or mark), source element, change description, detected at, current action (drop-down), comment (editable cell), and last decided by. - Action drop-down, offering only the actions valid for that change kind:

    Change kind detected Actions offered (besides Postpone, Reject)
    Moved or rotated Accept difference, Move host to match
    Renamed Accept difference, Rename host to match
    Extent or type parameter changed (height, length, level offset, type) Accept difference, Update host extents / Change host type (via the type mapping)
    Monitored parameter changed Accept difference, Copy value to host
    Source deleted Accept difference (keep host, stop monitoring), Delete host element
    Host changed (edited in the host so it no longer matches) Accept difference, Restore host from source
    New hosted element in a monitored source wall (opening, door, window) Copy new element (copy and monitor it), Ignore new element
    Opening sketch changed Accept difference, Copy sketch

    Modify host in the commands covers every "…to match" action; the change kind decides what it does. - Buttons: Apply (carries out the chosen actions as one undoable transaction), Show (opens a suitable view and zooms to the host and source, with the source highlighted), Create report… (HTML or CSV of the listed items with their actions and comments), Create issue (BCF topic from the selected items, COL-BCF-001), Settings… (COL-CM-004), Close.

    Behaviour & rules. - Change detection compares the current source with the snapshot, using per-aspect tolerances (default: position 1 mm, angle 0.01°, extent 1 mm; user settings). - Modify host is an ordinary undoable edit, subject to ownership (§6.4). - Pairs with unresolved changes show a warning badge on the host element, and are listed in the warnings list (COL-MNT-004). - In BIMserver mode, decisions are RXD objects and are shared with other users at the next sync. - When detection runs: after each link load or reload, after Get latest (for pairs inside the host), and after any host edit to a monitored element (checked against the source in the same transaction, so that the warning appears at once). The trigger set can be narrowed in the settings (COL-CM-004). - Reject leaves both elements unchanged and keeps the item visible with status rejected until the source changes again (a new item is then raised) or someone chooses another action. It does not change the linked model. - Accept difference writes the current source values into the pair's snapshot. - Postponed items stay in the default view and keep the warning badge; rejected and accepted items leave the default view. - If a Modify host action fails (for example the target position collides with a constraint), the transaction rolls back that item only, marks it failed with the reason, and applies the others. - Unloaded or not found link: the dialog opens read-only with a banner; no actions can be applied until the link is loaded.

    Data (RXD). coordination/monitors: review[] entries per pair (change, detectedAt, status: pending|postponed|rejected|accepted|modified, comment, user).

    Commands. coordreview.show(link_instance_id?) -> () opens the dialog (UI only); coordreview.list(link_instance_id?, status?) -> review_item[] (query); coordreview.resolve(item_ids[], action: postpone|reject|accept|modify, comment?) -> (); coordreview.report(path, format: html|csv, filter?) -> (). Create issue uses bcf.create_topic.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Moving a grid by 300 mm in the linked model and reloading lists one moved item; Modify host moves the host grid by 300 mm and clears the item. - [ ] Accept difference clears the item and keeps the host grid where it was; a further 1 mm move of the source does not raise a new item if the tolerance is 1 mm. - [ ] Adding a door to a monitored linked wall raises a new hosted element item; Copy new element creates a monitored host door in the copied host wall. - [ ] The action drop-down for a renamed item does not offer Move host to match. - [ ] Opening the dialog for an unloaded link shows the items read-only with the banner.

    Reconcile hosting

    ID: COL-CM-003 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/04 §8.4 (Reconcile Hosting); web: Orphaned elements and the Reconcile Hosting browser

    Purpose. Find and repair host elements and annotation that lost the linked element or face they were hosted on.

    Workflow. 1. After a link reload that orphans anything, a warning says "n elements lost their host in <link>" with Reconcile. 2. Collaborate › Coordinate › Reconcile Hosting (hosting.reconcile) opens the Reconcile Hosting palette, docked on the right by default. 3. The user selects orphans and chooses an action; the list updates as orphans are resolved.

    UI (Reconcile Hosting palette). - A tree grouped by link instance, then by category, then one row per orphan: category, family and type, mark, the lost host (category and GlobalId of the linked element), the reason, and the view (for view-owned annotation such as tags). - Show orphans of: all links or one link instance (the link_instance_id parameter). - Actions (toolbar and context menu): Show (opens a suitable view and zooms to the orphan), Pick new host (pick a face or element in the canvas), Make unhosted, Delete. - Graphics…: Highlight orphans in views (on/off) with colour, line weight and fill pattern for the highlight (default: magenta, weight 5, no pattern). The highlight is display-only and never printed (Chapter 5 graphics layer 6a).

    Behaviour & rules. Host elements hosted on linked elements (for example face-based fixtures on a linked wall) keep their hosting reference. When a reload loses the host (the linked element was deleted or its face changed), they are listed in the Reconcile Hosting palette (Collaborate › Coordinate), grouped by link; the user can Pick new host, Make unhosted (keep in place, no host), or Delete. Orphaned hosted elements keep their last position until reconciled. - Causes of orphaning: the linked host element was deleted; its hosting face was removed or split so that the stored face reference no longer resolves; the linked element was recreated with a new GlobalId (for example by copy-paste or mirror in the source); the link instance was removed with Keep as orphans (COL-LNK-006). - What can be orphaned: face-hosted and work-plane-hosted host elements on linked geometry, and annotation (tags, dimensions, spot elevations) referencing linked elements. - Tags remember their lost host; if an element with that GlobalId reappears on a later reload, the tag re-attaches automatically and leaves the list. - Pick new host accepts a face of a linked or host element of a category the element can host on; the element keeps its offset from the face along the face normal and its in-plane position projected onto the new face. A pick on an incompatible face is refused with the reason. The action is undoable. - Make unhosted converts the element to a level- or work-plane-based placement at its current position (Chapter 3 placement rules); it is undoable. - Delete uses ordinary element deletion (element.delete) and is undoable. - An orphaned element is still displayed, scheduled and exported; it is flagged with a warning of kind col.hosting.orphaned (COL-MNT-004). - In BIMserver mode, re-hosting needs ownership of the orphan (COL-OWN-001). - Interactive tool rule (conventions §2.1): Pick new host records micro-ops rehost.pick_element{element_id} and rehost.pick_face{host_ref, face_ref}; replay re-runs the pick against the reloaded link or reports that the face no longer exists.

    Data (IFC/RXD). The host reference and the orphaned flag are in the element's RXD hosting section (Chapter 2a). The orphan highlight settings are user settings. No IFC relationship exists for hosting on a linked element.

    Commands. hosting.reconcile(link_instance_id?) -> () opens the palette (UI only); hosting.list_orphans(link_instance_id?) -> orphan[] (query); hosting.rehost(element_id, new_host_ref) -> (); hosting.unhost(element_ids[]) -> (); hosting.set_orphan_graphics(on, colour?, line_weight?, pattern_id?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Deleting a linked wall that hosts three host fixtures lists the three fixtures as orphans after reload, and re-hosting one onto another linked wall keeps its offset from the wall face. - [ ] A tag on a linked column that was deleted and restored (same GlobalId) re-attaches after reload and disappears from the palette. - [ ] With orphan highlighting on, orphans show in the chosen colour on screen and in normal colours in PDF output.

    Copy/Monitor and coordination review settings

    ID: COL-CM-004 · Priority: P1 (tolerances, triggers), P2 (MEP fixture copy behaviour) · Ref: research/04 §8.4 (Options, Coordination Settings); web: Specify Coordination Settings

    Purpose. Control how elements are copied and mapped by Copy/Monitor and how sensitive the coordination review is.

    Workflow. Settings… in the Coordination Review dialog, the Options button of the Copy/Monitor tab, or Collaborate › Coordinate › Coordination Settings (coordreview.settings) opens the Coordination Settings dialog.

    UI (Coordination Settings dialog). - Apply to: Defaults for new links or a chosen link instance (drop-down). A link instance without its own settings uses the defaults, shown greyed until Override for this link is ticked. - Categories tab: one row per category (levels, grids, columns, walls, floors, openings, and the MEP fixture categories in P2) with: - Copy behaviour: Allow batch copy (default for fixture categories), Copy individually (default for the others) or Ignore category; - Mapping behaviour: Copy original type (bring the source type in, creating it in the host if needed) or Specify type mapping; - when mapping: a type-map grid, source type → host type, where each row can be Copy original type, Do not copy this type or a chosen host type; - category options: offset (levels: vertical offset; others: none), name prefix and suffix, Copy hosted openings, doors and windows (walls), Split columns by level (columns), Reuse existing levels and grids with matching names (default on). - Review tab: - tolerances: position (0.1–1 000 mm, default 1 mm), angle (0.001–10°, default 0.01°), extent (0.1–1 000 mm, default 1 mm); - monitored aspects per category (position, orientation, extent, name or mark, type) and extra monitored parameters (picked from the category's parameters); - Check on: link reload (always), Get latest (default on), host edits (default on); - Notify when review needed: balloon, warning only, or none. - Buttons: OK, Cancel, Reset to defaults, Copy from link… (copy another instance's settings).

    Behaviour & rules. - Settings apply to future copies and future checks; existing pairs keep their aspects unless Apply to existing pairs is ticked on OK, which also re-checks all pairs of that scope. - Validation: tolerances outside their ranges are refused inline; a type map must not map a source type to a host type of another category; a host type deleted later turns its mapping rows into Copy original type with a warning. - In BIMserver mode settings are an RXD object owned like any other (borrowed on edit). - Settings changes are one undoable step per OK.

    Data (RXD). RXD document coordination/monitors, kind monitor.settings (one object for the defaults and one per overriding link instance): scope, categories{} (copy behaviour, mapping behaviour, typeMap{}, options), tolerances{}, aspects{}, triggers{}, notify.

    Commands. coordreview.settings() -> () opens the dialog (UI only); copymonitor.set_options(link_instance_id?, category, mapping{}, options{}) -> () (COL-CM-001) sets the Categories tab; coordreview.set_tolerances(link_instance_id?, position?, angle?, extent?, triggers?, apply_to_existing?) -> () sets the Review tab.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With Ignore category for columns, picking a linked column in Copy mode copies nothing and reports why. - [ ] Mapping linked level type "Structural Level" to host type "Architectural Level" gives every copied level the host type. - [ ] Raising the position tolerance to 5 mm and ticking Apply to existing pairs clears pending items for grids moved by 3 mm. - [ ] A tolerance of 0 mm is refused inline.

    Interference check

    ID: COL-CLASH-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §8.5

    Purpose. Find elements that occupy the same space, inside the host or between the host and links.

    Workflow. 1. Collaborate › Coordinate › Interference Check ▾ › Run Interference Check. 2. Dialog with two columns. Each column: Categories from (current project, current selection, or a link instance) and a category checklist. 3. OK runs the check (in the background with progress) and opens the report: grouped by category pair (either order); each row shows the two elements (category, family, type, GlobalId). Show opens a suitable view, zooms and highlights the pair; Export writes HTML, CSV or BCF (COL-BCF-001); Refresh re-checks the listed pairs; Close. Show Last Report reopens it.

    Behaviour & rules. - Broad phase: axis-aligned boxes of all candidate elements in a BVH; candidate pairs are found in parallel (rayon). - Narrow phase: triangle–triangle intersection on the tessellation cache to reject non-intersecting pairs quickly, then an exact OCCT check (BRepAlgoAPI_Common, keeping pairs whose common volume exceeds a tiny tolerance, default 1 cm³, so that touching faces do not count). - Pairs that the model treats as intended are excluded automatically: a host and its hosted elements (wall and door), joined elements (wall–wall joins, wall–floor joins), an element and its own parts, elements in different design options that are never shown together, and elements of the same element group instance that overlap by definition (for example curtain panels and mullions). - Linked elements are tested in their placed position.

    Data (RXD). The last report is stored in RXD document coordination/clash (kind clash.result, with test definition and pairs) so that it survives reopening and is shared in BIMserver mode.

    Commands. clash.run_basic(set_a{source, categories[]}, set_b{source, categories[]}) -> job_id; clash.last_report() -> clash_report (query); clash.refresh(report_id) -> job_id; clash.export_report(report_id, path, format: html|csv|bcf) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A duct passing through a beam is reported; a door in its host wall is not; two walls meeting at a joined corner are not. - [ ] The check of 20 000 MEP elements against 5 000 structural elements completes in under one minute on the reference machine.

    Clash tests with tolerances and status (beyond the reference)

    ID: COL-CLASH-002 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/04 §8.5 (Limitations), §7.6 (Model Coordination, as the cloud alternative the reference relies on)

    Purpose. Provide the clash workflow that the reference leaves to separate coordination products: saved tests, clearance checks, grouping and status tracking, all in open formats.

    Behaviour & rules. - Saved clash tests: name; set A and set B defined by sources (host, links, selection sets, view filters, search rules); test type hard (with penetration tolerance), clearance (elements closer than a distance, computed with OCCT BRepExtrema_DistShapeShape), or duplicate (identical geometry and position). - Results are kept between runs and matched by GlobalId pair. Each result has a status new, active, reviewed, approved or resolved (resolved automatically when a re-run no longer finds it), an assignee, comments, and the run in which it was first and last found. - Grouping: by element (all clashes of one element), by level, or by proximity (clustering within a distance), so that one duct run crossing ten beams can be handled as one item. - Issues: any result or group can be turned into a BCF topic (COL-BCF-001) with a generated viewpoint. - Tests can run automatically after Get latest or link reload (option per test).

    Data (RXD). coordination/clash: kinds clash.test and clash.result.

    Commands. clash.create_test(name, set_a, set_b, type: hard|clearance|duplicate, tolerance?, auto_run?) -> test_id; clash.update_test(test_id, fields) -> (); clash.run(test_ids[]) -> job_id; clash.set_status(result_ids[], status, assignee?, comment?) -> (); clash.group(test_id, mode: element|level|proximity, distance?) -> group_id[]; clash.to_bcf(result_or_group_ids[]) -> topic_id[]

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A clearance test of 50 mm between pipes and beams reports a pipe 30 mm below a beam and does not report one 80 mm below. - [ ] After the pipe is moved and the test re-run, the result's status becomes resolved automatically.

    6.9 BCF issues

    BCF topics, viewpoints and files

    ID: COL-BCF-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §6.7 (Integrated Issues, as the reference's cloud-based counterpart), §8.5

    Purpose. Exchange and manage model-based issues using buildingSMART's open BIM Collaboration Format (BCF).

    Workflow. 1. Collaborate › Issues opens the Issues palette (bcf.issues_pane, COL-BCF-004): a filterable list of topics (title, status, priority, type, assignee, labels, due date, stage, modified) with a detail pane (description, comments, viewpoints with snapshots, related elements, reference links). 2. New issue captures a viewpoint of the active view (with snapshot), the selected elements, and opens the editor. 3. Clicking a viewpoint restores it in a view (COL-BCF-003). 4. Import/Export: Import BCF (.bcfzip, versions 2.1 and 3.0) and Export BCF (selected or all topics, version chosen by the user).

    Behaviour & rules. - Topic fields follow BCF: GUID, title, description, type, status, priority, labels, assigned to, due date, stage, creation and modification author and date, related topics, document references, comments (with optional viewpoint), viewpoints. - Topic types, statuses, priorities and labels are project lists (BCF extensions), editable by the project administrator and exported with the file. - Issues are project data: they are stored as RXD (document coordination/issues, one object per topic, keyed by the topic GUID, with snapshots as RXD assets), so in BIMserver mode they travel with the model and merge per topic and per comment. Importing a BCF file merges by topic GUID (newer modification date wins per field; comments are merged by GUID). - Issues whose elements are deleted keep their GlobalIds and show "element not found". - Clash results (COL-CLASH-002) and coordination review items (COL-CM-002) can be turned into issues.

    Commands. bcf.create_topic(title, description?, fields?, view_id?, element_ids[]?) -> topic_id; bcf.update_topic(topic_id, fields) -> (); bcf.add_comment(topic_id, text, viewpoint?: current|none) -> comment_id; bcf.add_viewpoint(topic_id, view_id?) -> viewpoint_id; bcf.delete_topic(topic_ids[]) -> (); bcf.import(path) -> import_report; bcf.export(path, topic_ids[]?, version: 2.1|3.0) -> (); bcf.list(filter?) -> topic_summary[] (query)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A .bcfzip exported from Reviera imports into at least two other BCF-capable tools with titles, comments, snapshots and camera positions intact. - [ ] A BCF 2.1 file from another tool imports into Reviera and its viewpoints restore the camera and selection. - [ ] Two users commenting on the same topic in BIMserver mode both see both comments after synchronising.

    BCF issues pane

    ID: COL-BCF-004 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §6.7 (Integrated Issues), §8.5; COL-BCF-001

    Purpose. A dockable pane in which users browse, filter, create, edit and act on BCF issues next to the model.

    Workflow. 1. Collaborate › Issues › BCF Issues (bcf.issues_pane) shows the pane, docked on the right by default with the Properties palette; running the command again brings it to the front. 2. The user filters the list, selects a topic, reads or edits it in the detail area, and clicks a viewpoint to go to it. 3. New issue captures the active view and selection (COL-BCF-001 workflow step 2).

    UI (Issues pane). - Toolbar: New issue, Import BCF…, Export BCF…, Delete, Refresh, Manage lists… (types, statuses, priorities, labels, stages, users), and, when a BCF API server is bound (COL-BCF-002), Sync now with the last sync time. - Filter bar: text search (title, description, comments), and drop-down filters for status, type, priority, assignee (including Me), labels, stage, due date (overdue, this week, none), Has elements in this view, and Source (manual, clash test, coordination review, imported). Filters combine with AND; the active filter is remembered per user and project. - List: sortable columns: index number, title, status, priority, type, assignee, due date, modified; the first viewpoint's snapshot as a thumbnail (togglable). Overdue topics show the due date in the alert colour. - Detail area (for the selected topic): editable fields (title, description, type, status, priority, labels, assignee, due date, stage), comment thread (newest last; each comment may carry a viewpoint thumbnail; Add comment with Attach current view), viewpoints strip (click to restore, COL-BCF-003; Add viewpoint; Update viewpoint replaces one with the current view after confirmation), related elements (Select, Isolate, with "not found" markers), related topics, and document references (links open in the system browser after confirmation). - Context menu on a topic: Go to first viewpoint, Select related elements, Copy link (reviera://issue/<guid>), Export selected, Delete. - Canvas markers: optional pins at each open topic's first viewpoint target in 3D views (toggle in the pane); clicking a pin selects the topic.

    Behaviour & rules. - Editing: field edits commit when the field loses focus and are undoable (one step per field). Each edit updates the topic's modification author and date. - Validation: the title is required (1–255 characters); status, type, priority and labels must come from the project lists (an imported value not in the lists is shown in italics and added to the list on the user's confirmation); due date must be a valid date, and a date in the past is allowed but shown as overdue. - Manage lists edits the BCF extension lists (bcf.set_extensions); removing a value in use is refused unless the user chooses a replacement value for the topics that use it. While a BCF API project is bound, the lists are read-only and come from the server. - Deleting a topic needs confirmation; in BIMserver mode it is a normal RXD deletion merged at the next sync. - Performance: the list handles 10 000 topics with filtering under 200 ms; snapshots load lazily when visible. - The pane updates live after Get latest, BCF import and BCF API sync; topics changed by others are marked with a dot until opened. - Permissions for agents: MCP agents can read topics with bcf.list; creating, editing or deleting needs the model-edit permission.

    Data (IFC/RXD). Topics, comments, viewpoints and extension lists: RXD document coordination/issues (kind issue.topic per topic and issue.extensions for the lists), snapshots as RXD assets (COL-BCF-001). Pane layout and filters are user settings.

    Commands. bcf.issues_pane() -> () shows the pane (UI only); bcf.set_extensions(lists{types?, statuses?, priorities?, labels?, stages?, users?}, replacements?{}) -> (); the pane uses bcf.list, bcf.create_topic, bcf.update_topic, bcf.add_comment, bcf.add_viewpoint, bcf.delete_topic, bcf.import, bcf.export (COL-BCF-001) and bcf.apply_viewpoint (COL-BCF-003).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Filtering by Assignee = Me and Status = Open shows exactly the matching topics, and the filter is restored after reopening the project. - [ ] Editing a topic's status in the pane and pressing Ctrl+Z restores the previous status. - [ ] Removing the status value "In review" while three topics use it asks for a replacement and applies it to the three. - [ ] Clicking a viewpoint thumbnail restores that viewpoint in a view. - [ ] Saving a topic with an empty title is refused.

    BCF API client (OpenCDE)

    ID: COL-BCF-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §7.6 (multi-company issue exchange, as context); web: buildingSMART BCF-API (v3.0), OpenCDE Foundation API (v1.1), OpenCDE Documents API (v1.0) repositories (public, accessed 2026-10-12)

    Purpose. Use any issue server that implements the buildingSMART BCF API as the shared issue tracker for a project, so issues move between Reviera and other BIM tools live, not only as files.

    Workflow. 1. Collaborate › Issues › Connect issue server… (bcf.api_connect): enter the server URL. Reviera reads the server's supported versions and authentication methods through the OpenCDE Foundation API, then signs the user in (COL-API-001). 2. Choose a project from the server's project list (bcf.api_bind_project). The Issues pane (COL-BCF-004) now shows the server's topics. Lists (types, statuses, priorities, labels, stages, users) come from the server's project extensions and are read-only locally. 3. Work normally. Changes sync automatically (default every 2 minutes and on every local change, after 5 s of quiet) or with Sync now.

    Behaviour & rules. - Versions: BCF API 3.0 is the target; 2.1 is supported for older servers. The version is negotiated from the server's versions list. Behaviour that only exists in 3.0, such as events and some extension fields, is hidden on 2.1 servers. - Coverage: - project details and extensions - topics: create, read, update and delete - comments - viewpoints, with snapshots, bitmaps, components, colouring, visibility and clipping planes (mapped through COL-BCF-003) - related topics - document references, both internal documents and external URLs - documents (upload and download) - files information, which links a topic to the IFC model file and revision it refers to: the Reviera model's file name, IFC project GUID and, in BIMserver mode, the revision - topic and comment events (audit history, shown in the topic's History tab) - Server permissions: the per-project, per-topic and per-comment action flags the server returns (for example update, createComment, updateRelatedTopics) drive the UI. Disallowed actions are disabled, with the server's restriction as the tooltip, and are never attempted. - Paging and queries: lists use the server's OData query options ($filter, $orderby, $top, $skip). Incremental sync filters on modification date. Paging continues until done, with a progress indicator for large projects. - Sync and conflicts: - local edits are queued while offline and replayed in order when the connection returns - each local object records its server GUID and the server modification date it last saw - when a local change conflicts with a newer server value, the server value wins per field, the local value is kept in the topic's Conflicts list, and the user can re-apply it with one click - nothing is silently lost - Local copy: server topics are cached in RXD (coordination/issues) for offline reading, so a model file carries a snapshot of its issues. When a project is bound, the server is the source of truth. Unbinding keeps the local copy as ordinary local issues. - Several servers: one project can be bound to one BCF API project at a time. Topics can be copied between bindings, or to and from BCF files. - Agents: MCP agents use the same bcf.* commands. Server credentials are never exposed to them (COL-CORE-005).

    Data (IFC/RXD). Cached topics in coordination/issues (kinds issue.topic, issue.extensions), each with server: {connection, guid, modified}. Connection profiles and tokens are client state (COL-API-001), never stored in the model.

    Commands. bcf.api_connect(url, profile_name?) -> connection_id; bcf.api_list_projects(connection_id) -> project[] (query); bcf.api_bind_project(connection_id, project_id) -> (); bcf.api_unbind(keep_local_copy=true) -> (); bcf.api_sync(connection_id?) -> sync_report; bcf.api_status() -> {connection, last_sync, queued_changes, conflicts} (query); bcf.api_resolve_conflict(topic_id, field, use: server|local) -> (); bcf.api_disconnect(connection_id) -> ().

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Against the open-source reference implementation of the OpenCDE APIs and at least one commercial BCF API server, a topic with two viewpoints, a snapshot and a comment created in Reviera appears on the server with its camera, components and image. A comment added on the server appears in Reviera after the next sync. - [ ] Losing the connection mid-sync leaves both sides consistent, and the next sync completes the transfer without duplicates. - [ ] Ten edits made offline are pushed in order when the connection returns. - [ ] An action the server forbids (for example editing a closed topic) is disabled in the pane and never sent. - [ ] A conflicting status change keeps both values visible: the server's in the topic, Reviera's in Conflicts.

    Issue tracking workflow

    ID: COL-BCF-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §6.7 (Integrated Issues, as context), §8.5; web: buildingSMART BCF-API (v3.0); COL-BCF-001, COL-BCF-004

    Purpose. Make BCF issues a working tracker for coordination and design review, not only an exchange format.

    Behaviour & rules. - Workflow rules (optional, per project, in the issue lists): - allowed status transitions, for example Open → In progress → Resolved → Closed, with Reopened allowed from Closed - which statuses need an assignee or a due date - which roles may close a topic

    Invalid transitions are refused with the rule shown. When bound to a server, the server's rules and permissions take precedence (COL-BCF-002). - Sources of issues: - manual capture (COL-BCF-001) - clash results (COL-CLASH-002, one topic per clash group, with both elements as components) - coordination review items (COL-CM-002) - model warnings (COL-MNT-004) - walkthrough and VR captures (Ch 7 ADV-WALK-001) - view bookmarks (UI-SCEN-002)

    Each topic records its source, and the pane can filter by it. - Element linking: - selecting a topic highlights its components in all open views - the Properties palette shows a count of open issues for the selected element, with a link - deleting or replacing an element that open issues refer to warns first - issues follow elements across Copy/Monitor by GlobalId - Assignment and notifications: - assignees come from the project's user list - in-app notifications are raised when a topic is assigned to the user, commented on, changed, or becomes overdue - a daily summary is optional - on a BCF API server, notifications follow server events - e-mail and chat notifications are left to the server or to add-ins - Due dates and stages: overdue and due-this-week badges; stages (for example design phases) can be used to filter and report. - Reports: - bcf.report produces a PDF or HTML issue report (cover, summary counts by status, assignee and type, then one section per topic with fields, comments and snapshots), a CSV or XLSX list, or a BCF file - report templates are project settings - a schedule-like issue list can be placed on a sheet - Dashboard: counts by status, assignee, type and age, with a trend of open issues over time (from topic events, or local history when offline), shown in the Issues pane's Overview tab. - Bulk edit: change status, assignee, priority, labels or due date for several selected topics in one step; one undo step for local issues.

    Data (IFC/RXD). Workflow rules and report templates in coordination/issues (kind issue.extensions, keys workflow and reportTemplates). Notification preferences are user settings.

    Commands. bcf.set_workflow(rules) -> (); bcf.bulk_update(topic_ids[], fields) -> (); bcf.report(topic_ids[]? | filter?, format: pdf|html|csv|xlsx|bcf, template_id?, path) -> job_id; bcf.from_clash(clash_result_ids[], group_by?) -> topic_ids[]; bcf.issues_for_element(element_id) -> topic_summary[] (query); bcf.notifications(since?) -> notification[] (query).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With a workflow that forbids Open → Closed, closing an open topic is refused and the allowed next statuses are shown. - [ ] Creating topics from 12 clash results grouped by level produces one topic per level, each listing its clashing element pairs as components. - [ ] A PDF report of 50 topics contains every topic's fields, comments and first snapshot, with summary counts that match the list. - [ ] Selecting an element with two open issues shows "2 open issues" in Properties, and the link filters the pane to them.

    OpenCDE Documents API client

    ID: COL-CDE-001 · Priority: P2 · Ref: web: buildingSMART OpenCDE Documents API (v1.0) and Foundation API (v1.1) repositories (public, accessed 2026-10-12)

    Purpose. Open models from, and publish models and drawings to, any common data environment (CDE) that implements the OpenCDE Documents API, without a vendor-specific connector.

    Workflow. 1. Open from CDE: File › Open › From CDE… (cde.select_documents). Reviera starts a selection session. The CDE's own document picker opens in the system browser, and the user picks one or more files there. Reviera then downloads the chosen versions: IFC opens as a model, other files as links or attachments. 2. Publish to CDE: File › Export › Publish to CDE… (cde.upload_documents). Reviera starts an upload session for the files to publish (the IFC model, a clean IFC export, PDF sheet sets, BCF). The user enters the CDE's metadata in its own web form, and Reviera uploads the binary data in the chunks the CDE specifies. 3. Stay current: a document opened from a CDE remembers its document and version. Reviera polls the CDE's document-versions endpoint (with ETags) and shows "A newer version is available" with Open newer version.

    Behaviour & rules. - Sign-in and server profiles use COL-API-001. A CDE that also offers the BCF API can be bound for issues with the same profile (COL-BCF-002). - Downloads are verified against the CDE's reported size and hash where given. Partial downloads resume. - Publishing a model that has local unsaved changes asks whether to save first. Clean-IFC publishing uses export.ifc{strip_rxd=true}. - BCF files information and document references can point at CDE document versions, so issues link to the exact published file. - Works in Local mode. In BIMserver mode, the CDE is an additional publication target, and the BIMserver remains the model's working store.

    Commands. cde.connect(url, profile_name?) -> connection_id; cde.select_documents(connection_id) -> selection_session_id; cde.download(selection_session_id, target_folder?) -> files[]; cde.upload_documents(connection_id, files[]) -> upload_session_id; cde.upload_status(upload_session_id) -> status (query); cde.check_versions(document_ids[]?) -> version_info[] (query); cde.disconnect(connection_id) -> ().

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Against the open-source reference implementation, a user can pick an IFC file in the CDE's browser UI and Reviera opens that exact version. - [ ] Publishing an IFC and a PDF sheet set creates two documents in the CDE with the metadata entered in its form. - [ ] After someone uploads a newer version in the CDE, Reviera shows the newer-version notice within the polling interval (default 5 minutes).

    Viewpoint mapping

    ID: COL-BCF-003 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §1.5 (3D views, section box), §3.5 (hide/isolate)

    Behaviour & rules. - Capture: from a 3D view: perspective camera (eye, direction, up, field of view) or orthogonal camera (eye, direction, up, view-to-world scale or field width); section box faces as six clipping planes; visible, hidden and selected elements as BCF components by IFC GlobalId (using default visibility plus exceptions to keep files small); colour overrides as component colouring; a PNG snapshot. From a 2D view: an orthogonal camera looking along the view direction plus the view's crop as clipping planes, and a snapshot. - Restore: opens or creates a temporary 3D view named after the topic, sets the camera, creates a section box from clipping planes that form a box (other planes become a temporary multi-plane clip), applies temporary hide/isolate (Chapter 5, DOC-GFX-008) and colours, and selects the selected components. Components that are not found are listed. - Linked elements: components in linked models are matched by GlobalId across host and links.

    Commands. bcf.apply_viewpoint(viewpoint_id, target_view_id?) -> view_id

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Restoring a viewpoint with a section box reproduces the box within 1 mm and the camera within 0.1°. - [ ] A viewpoint that isolates three elements shows only those three when restored.

    6.9a Integration services

    Shared REST and authentication client

    ID: COL-API-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: TECH_STACK §3.7.1 (async HTTP client); web: OpenCDE Foundation API (v1.1) authentication conventions; COL-CORE-005

    Purpose. One network client for every server Reviera talks to (BIMserver JSON API, BCF API, OpenCDE Documents API, library and analysis services, add-ins), so authentication, proxies, security and reliability work the same everywhere.

    Behaviour & rules. - Stack: an asynchronous HTTP client (reqwest on tokio, TECH_STACK §3.7.1) running off the UI thread. The UI shows progress and allows cancelling any request that takes longer than 1 s. - Server profiles: each server is a named profile (URL, kind, authentication method, proxy override, certificate settings) kept in client state. Profiles can be exported, without secrets, for a team. - Authentication: - OAuth 2.0 authorisation code flow with PKCE in the system browser, using a loopback redirect. This is the default for OpenCDE servers and follows the server's Foundation API authentication description. - OAuth 2.0 device code flow, where offered, for headless and locked-down machines. - API tokens. - BIMserver session tokens (COL-BIM-001). - Tokens are refreshed automatically. Secrets live only in the OS credential store and are never written to logs, the model, the live store, profile exports or MCP resources (COL-CORE-005). - Network environment: system proxy settings and PAC scripts are honoured, and a per-profile override is allowed. TLS uses the OS trust store; custom CA certificates can be added per profile. Disabling verification needs an explicit per-profile choice, with a red warning in the status bar. - Reliability: - timeouts: 10 s to connect, 60 s to read, overridable per request - retries with exponential backoff and jitter for idempotent requests and for 429/503 responses, honouring Retry-After - ETag/If-None-Match caching for polling - resumable chunked transfer for large files - an offline queue for writes that can be replayed (used by COL-BCF-002) - Paging helpers: OData $top/$skip/$filter/$orderby and link-header paging, shared by all clients. - Diagnostics: a per-profile request log (method, URL path, status, timing; secrets and bodies redacted) under Help › Diagnostics, and api.profile.test checks reachability, TLS and authentication. - Scripting: - Lua scripts get reviera.http.request(...) only at trust level trusted or native (DM-LUA-007), and only to hosts on the script's declared allow-list in its manifest. - Requests made with a stored profile use that profile's authentication without exposing the token to the script. - MCP agents have no raw HTTP access. They use the commands of the services above.

    Commands. api.profile.add(name, url, kind, auth_method, options?) -> profile_id; api.profile.list() -> profile[] (query, no secrets); api.profile.remove(profile_id) -> (); api.profile.test(profile_id) -> report; api.signin(profile_id) -> status; api.signout(profile_id) -> (); api.log(profile_id, since?) -> entry[] (query, redacted); http.request(method, url, headers?, body?, profile_id?) -> response (Lua at trusted/native trust only; not exposed to MCP).

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Behind an authenticating corporate proxy configured by PAC, BIMserver, BCF API and CDE connections all work with no per-service setup. - [ ] A server answering 429 with Retry-After: 5 is retried after 5 s, and the user sees "waiting for server" rather than an error. - [ ] No token or password appears in the request log, the model file, the live store, a profile export or any MCP resource (checked by scanning for a known token value). - [ ] A Lua script at standard trust calling reviera.http.request is refused. At trusted trust, a call to a host not on its allow-list is refused.

    6.10 Model maintenance

    Purge unused

    ID: COL-MNT-001 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §9 (Purge Unused)

    Behaviour & rules. - Manage › Settings › Purge Unused (default shortcut PU) shows a tree of unused items by kind: family types and families, materials, styles (line, fill, text, dimension), line and fill patterns, view templates, filters, colour schemes, schedules not placed and not referenced, groups without instances, property sets without objects, unused IFC resources (orphaned representations, placements and styles left by other tools), and unused RXD objects. Check All, Check None, Purge. - Dependency-aware: an item is unused if nothing reachable from the model uses it. Reviera computes this transitively, so one pass removes nested unused items (no need to purge several times). - In BIMserver mode, purging items owned by others is not possible; they are shown greyed with the owner's name. - Purge is one undoable command.

    Commands. model.purge_preview() -> purge_tree (query); model.purge(item_ids[]?|all?) -> count

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A family type used only by an unused nested family is purged in the same pass as that nested family. - [ ] Purge followed by Undo restores every purged item.

    Audit and repair

    ID: COL-MNT-002 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §9 (Audit)

    Behaviour & rules. - File › Open › Audit option, or Manage › Inquiry › Audit Model at any time. - Checks: IFC schema validation (IfcOpenShell validator: types, cardinalities, WHERE rules where available); duplicate GlobalIds; relationships referring to missing objects; elements contained in more than one spatial structure element; property sets attached to nothing; RXD schema validation and reconciliation (Chapter 2a: references to missing GlobalIds, stale recipes); geometry that fails to build in OCCT; elements far from the origin. - Repair fixes what can be fixed safely (new GlobalIds for duplicates, keeping the one referenced by RXD; removing dangling references; detaching orphan property sets; rebuilding representations from RXD recipes) and lists what needs a user decision. The audit report can be saved as HTML. - Audit of a BIMserver working copy repairs the working copy; repairs are uploaded at the next sync like other changes.

    Commands. model.audit(repair?) -> audit_report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Opening a file with a duplicated GlobalId with Audit on reports it and, with repair, gives one of the two objects a new GlobalId. - [ ] Audit on a valid model reports no problems and changes nothing.

    Backups and restore

    ID: COL-MNT-003 · Priority: P0 (Local backups), P1 (BIMserver restore) · Ref: research/04 §9 (Backups, Compact)

    Behaviour & rules. - Local mode: each save keeps the previous file as a numbered backup (name.0001.ifc, name.0002.ifc, …) up to Maximum backups (default 3; project setting). Backups keep their embedded RXD, so each is a complete project. Restore backup (File › Backups) lists them with date and size and opens one or replaces the current file with it (after confirmation, keeping the current file as a new backup). - Autosave: every N minutes (default 10) to a recovery file in the user's data directory, removed after a successful save; offered on the next start after a crash. - BIMserver mode: the server's revisions are the history; Restore is COL-BIM-008. The working copy has its own journal (COL-OFF-001). - Compact: Reviera always writes files in full, so there is no separate compaction; Save As with Compressed (.ifczip) reduces size.

    Commands. model.set_backup_policy(max_backups, autosave_minutes?) -> (); model.list_backups() -> backup_info[] (query); model.restore_backup(backup_id, replace?) -> ()

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] With maximum backups = 3, five saves leave exactly three backups, the oldest removed first. - [ ] After killing Reviera, the next start offers the autosave recovery file.

    Warnings review

    ID: COL-MNT-004 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §9 (Review Warnings); spec/02 §2.7.4 (DM-FAIL-001)

    Purpose. One dialog to review, locate, fix, acknowledge and report every stored warning in the model, building on the failure handling of Chapter 2 (DM-FAIL-001).

    Workflow. 1. Manage › Inquiry › Review Warnings (warnings.review), or a click on the status-bar warning count, opens the Warnings dialog. 2. The user expands a warning kind, ticks elements, and uses Show, a resolution, Delete checked or Acknowledge. 3. Export… writes a report.

    UI (Warnings dialog). Modeless and resizable. - Filter bar: severity (warnings only by default; errors never persist, DM-FAIL-001), kind (drop-down of the kinds present, with counts), discipline or chapter area (ARC, STR, MEP, DOC, COL, DM), Only in active view, Only my elements (BIMserver: elements I own or borrow), Caused by last sync (COL-MRG-003), Show acknowledged (default off), text search. - Tree: warning kind (message and count) → one node per warning instance → the elements involved, each with a check box, category, family and type, mark, and GlobalId. Selecting an element row highlights it in the canvas. - Buttons: Show (selects the checked or selected elements and zooms to them in a suitable view, cycling through views that show them on repeated presses), Resolve… (offers the resolutions the failure definition provides, for example Unjoin, Delete newer, Disallow join), Delete checked (enabled when elements are ticked; confirmation lists the count), Acknowledge (with an optional note), Un-acknowledge, Export… (HTML or CSV), Close. - The status-bar warning count excludes acknowledged warnings and turns to the alert colour above a project threshold (default 500).

    Behaviour & rules. - Manage › Inquiry › Warnings lists every current warning: overlapping or duplicate elements, join problems, room and area boundary problems, orphaned annotation (Chapter 5), coordination review items (COL-CM-002), reconciliation results, regeneration failures, elements far from the origin. Warnings are grouped by kind, with the elements involved (GlobalIds). - Show selects and zooms; Delete checked (for duplicate instances); Export to HTML or CSV. - The warning count is shown on the status bar. - Storage: warnings are stored in RXD document project/warnings and re-checked whenever the elements involved regenerate, as specified in Chapter 2 (DM-FAIL-001); a warning disappears when its condition is gone. Acknowledgement is the dismissed state of that store, plus who acknowledged it, when, and the note, so it is shared with other users in BIMserver mode and merged per warning. - Acknowledgement is not a fix: acknowledged warnings remain in exports (marked) and in the statistics (COL-MNT-007). If the elements involved change, the acknowledgement is cleared and the warning reappears. - Delete checked and resolutions are ordinary undoable edits, subject to ownership (COL-OWN-001): elements owned by others are skipped and listed. - Linked models: warnings inside linked models are not listed; warnings about host elements related to links (orphans, review items) are. - Export includes for each warning: kind, severity, message, element GlobalIds, categories, acknowledged state and note, first-seen time; HTML output is a single self-contained file. - The list updates live while the dialog is open; a warning resolved by an edit disappears from the tree without closing it.

    Data (IFC/RXD). RXD document project/warnings (Chapter 2, DM-FAIL-001), with fields acknowledgedBy, acknowledgedAt, note and, for merge-caused warnings, syncReport.

    Commands. warnings.review() -> () opens the Warnings dialog (UI only); warnings.list(filter?: {kind?, severity?, element_ids?}) -> warning[] (query); warnings.acknowledge(warning_ids[], note?) -> (); warnings.export(path, format: html|csv) -> (). Show uses warnings.show(warning_id) and Delete checked uses element.delete (Chapter 2). warnings.acknowledge sets the same stored state as Chapter 2's warnings.dismiss, with a note.

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Placing two identical doors at the same position raises one duplicate-instance warning listing both. - [ ] Acknowledged warnings stay hidden from the default list after reopening the project. - [ ] Moving one of two overlapping walls away while the dialog is open removes that warning from the tree. - [ ] Editing an element of an acknowledged warning so that the warning still applies makes it reappear unacknowledged. - [ ] Delete checked on a duplicate door removes it, and Undo restores it with its warning. - [ ] The exported CSV contains one row per warning element with its GlobalId.

    Transfer project standards

    ID: COL-MNT-005 · Priority: P1 · Ref: research/04 §9 (Transfer Project Standards)

    Behaviour & rules. - Manage › Settings › Transfer Project Standards: choose a source (another open project or an IFC file on disk, including template files) and the kinds to copy: system types (walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, stairs, railings and so on), materials, object styles, line weights, line styles, line patterns, fill patterns, text, dimension and tag styles, view templates, view filters, colour schemes, print, PDF, CAD and IFC export setups, view/sheet sets, revision numbering sequences, saved viewport positions, phase filters and settings, keynote settings, browser organisation schemes. - Items whose names already exist in the target: Overwrite, New only (skip existing) or Rename (append a suffix). - Dependencies come along (a view template brings its filters, a wall type its materials and fill patterns). - The transfer is one undoable command.

    Commands. standards.transfer(source_document_id, selection[{kind, item_ids?}], on_conflict: overwrite|new_only|rename) -> transfer_report

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Transferring view templates also transfers the filters and line patterns they use, and assigned views in the target are unaffected unless overwritten templates change them.

    Package project for transmittal

    ID: COL-MNT-006 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/04 §9 (eTransmit)

    Purpose. Send a project to someone else as one self-contained package that opens without missing files.

    Workflow. 1. File › Package Project opens a wizard: Contents (the reference tree, below), Options, Destination (folder or .zip), Summary. 2. The user reviews what will be included and clicks Package; progress is shown and the job runs in the background. 3. On completion the transmittal report opens.

    Behaviour & rules. File › Package Project: collects the project file and everything it references (IFC links, CAD links, point cloud sources or their indexes, PDF and image underlays, keynote files, render plug-in assets) into a folder or ZIP, rewriting link paths as relative. Options: include BIMserver links as downloaded files (pinned to their current revision), purge unused, remove views and sheets not on a chosen set, export as a local copy (strip ownership and server binding, COL-MODE-002), include a transmittal report (file list with sizes and SHA-256 hashes). - Contents tree: every referenced file with its kind, size and status; the user can untick a file (its link is then kept but will show not found at the destination). Nested IFC links that are attachments are followed recursively (depth limit 4, COL-LNK-006); overlays are not. - Point clouds: Source, COPC index only (default, smaller and enough for display) or Exclude. - Layout: the project file at the package root; referenced files in sub-folders by kind (links/ifc, links/cad, pointclouds, underlays, keynotes); duplicate file names get a numeric suffix. Link paths in the packaged copy are rewritten to these relative locations; the original project is not changed. - The packaged project is a copy: all options (purge, removing views, stripping) are applied to the copy only. - Missing references (not found links) are listed in the summary and in the report; packaging continues unless the user cancels. - Size check: the summary shows the total size; packages over 4 GB are written as ZIP64. - BIMserver mode: the package always contains a local copy (server binding and ownership data are never included); the transmittal report records the server project and base revision for reference.

    Data. No project data changes. The transmittal report (transmittal.html and transmittal.csv) lists every file with relative path, size, SHA-256 and origin path, plus the Reviera version and date.

    Commands. model.package(path, zip?, options) -> transmittal_report (options: {include_bimserver_links?, pointclouds?: source|index|exclude, purge?, keep_view_set_id?, local_copy?, report?, exclude_paths?[]})

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] A packaged project opens on another machine with all links loaded and no broken paths. - [ ] The SHA-256 hashes in the transmittal report match the packaged files. - [ ] Packaging with purge unused leaves the original project unchanged. - [ ] A package of a BIMserver project contains no ownership data and no server binding.

    Model statistics

    ID: COL-MNT-007 · Priority: P2 · Ref: research/04 §9 (Model Analytics / Model Health)

    Purpose. Show the size and health of a model so that teams can find what makes it slow or large.

    Behaviour & rules. Manage › Inquiry › Model Statistics: element counts by category and workset, file size and the size of IFC geometry and RXD by document, warnings by kind, largest families, number of views, sheets and unplaced views, link sizes, regeneration time of the slowest elements. Exportable as CSV or JSON, and available to agents as an MCP resource. - Dialog sections: Summary (file size, element count, warning count, link count, last save and sync), Elements (by category, workset, level, phase), Storage (IFC entity count, size of geometry representations, size of each RXD document and of RXD assets), Families and types (by instance count and by size, unused types), Views and sheets (counts by view type, unplaced views, views without a template), Links (size and load time per link), Performance (the 20 slowest elements to regenerate, from the last full regeneration, and open time). - Counts cover open worksets only; a note gives the number of elements in closed worksets, which are counted from the working copy index without loading them. - Statistics are computed in the background in under 5 seconds for a 100 000-element model; the dialog shows Refresh and the time computed. - History (BIMserver mode): the summary values are also computed for each sync and kept in the working copy, so the dialog can chart file size, element count and warning count over the last 50 syncs. - Numbers are read-only; clicking a category or warning kind selects the elements (with confirmation above 10 000). - The MCP resource is reviera://model/statistics (read-only, JSON with the same structure as stats).

    Data. Derived; nothing is stored in IFC or RXD. Sync history values are client state.

    Commands. model.statistics() -> stats (query)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] The statistics' element counts equal the counts in a multi-category schedule of the same model. - [ ] The RXD document sizes add up to the total RXD size shown in the summary. - [ ] The JSON export validates against the published stats schema.

    Element lookup by id

    ID: COL-MNT-008 · Priority: P0 · Ref: research/04 §9 (Select by ID / IDs of Selection)

    Purpose. Find elements from ids in reports, warnings, clash lists or messages, and give others the ids of a selection.

    Behaviour & rules. Manage › Inquiry › Select by ID accepts GlobalIds or internal ids (comma or line separated) and selects them, opening a view that shows them if needed; IDs of Selection shows and copies the GlobalIds of the selection. - Input parsing: separators are commas, semicolons, spaces and line breaks. A 22-character token in the IFC base-64 alphabet is a GlobalId; a 36-character UUID is converted to a GlobalId; a decimal number is an internal id; link references link:<linkId>/ifc:<GlobalId> select linked elements. Duplicates are ignored. Up to 100 000 ids per call. - Not found: ids that match nothing are listed in a result panel ("12 of 50 not found") with Copy not found; found ids are still selected. - Hidden elements: if an element is in a closed workset, an unloaded link, or hidden in every open view, Reviera offers to open the workset or a suitable view (a 3D view with Reveal hidden if no other view shows it). - IDs of Selection shows a dialog with GlobalIds and internal ids side by side, Copy GlobalIds, Copy internal ids, Copy both (CSV). Internal ids are session-stable but GlobalIds are the ones to share (COL-CORE-002).

    Data. None; the commands only read the model and change the selection.

    Commands. select.by_ids(ids[]) -> element_id[]; select.ids_of_selection() -> {global_ids[], internal_ids[]} (query)

    Acceptance criteria. - [ ] Pasting 50 GlobalIds from a clash report selects those 50 elements. - [ ] A list with 3 unknown ids selects the others and lists the 3 as not found. - [ ] Selecting an element in a closed workset by id offers to open the workset.

    The new RXD documents introduced by this chapter (coordination/monitors, coordination/clash, coordination/issues) and the ownership extended-data schema must be added to the Chapter 2a catalogue, together with the kinds monitor.settings, issue.topic and issue.extensions, which are not yet in the Chapter 2a §6.5 kind registry.

    6.13 Open questions and deviations from the reference

    Deviations (intentional).

    # Topic Reviera behaviour Reason
    D7-1 Central model An Open Source BIMserver project replaces the file-based or vendor-cloud central model; Synchronise = get latest + merge + check in. Open, self-hostable server; no vendor cloud (TECH_STACK §3.7).
    D7-2 Element ownership Advisory ownership through a live extended-data document, given force by the merge's ownership rule. No enforcement plugin is shipped; ownership follows what BIMserver supports (COL-OWN-004 deferred). The reference enforces ownership in its central model. BIMserver has no native locking (TECH_STACK §5, decision 8).
    D7-3 Conflicts Reviera merges by GlobalId at facet level and asks the user about true conflicts, with a recoverable conflict stash. The reference avoids conflicts by strict ownership and has no merge UI. Optimistic merging fits a revision server and offline work.
    D7-4 System worksets No separate worksets for families, project standards and views as ownership units; types, standards objects and views are borrowed individually as objects, and each view's annotation belongs to an automatic view workset. Finer-grained, fewer conflicts; matches the RXD object model.
    D7-5 Worksets in IFC Worksets are RXD; they are written as IfcGroup only on export. Project-owner storage decision (Chapter 2a); IfcGroup remains available to other tools on export.
    D7-6 Offline working Full offline editing with queued ownership claims. The reference requires a connection to the central model to borrow.
    D7-7 Link formats IFC is the only model-link format (local or BIMserver). Proprietary model formats, coordination caches and vendor-cloud coordination models are not supported (P3). Open formats only; IFC + BCF cover coordination.
    D7-8 Point clouds Open formats (E57, LAS/LAZ, COPC, PLY) indexed to COPC; no proprietary scan formats. Licensing and openness.
    D7-9 CAD formats DXF and DWG (through LibreDWG) only; DGN, SAT, SKP, 3DM deferred (P3). No GPL-compatible readers of sufficient quality for some formats.
    D7-10 Clash detection Basic interference check (P1) plus saved tests with tolerances, clearance, status tracking and grouping (P2), with BCF output. The reference's in-product check is hard-clash only. Avoids depending on separate proprietary coordination products.
    D7-11 Issues BCF 2.1/3.0 files, the buildingSMART BCF API (3.0, with 2.1 fallback) and an issue-tracking workflow instead of a vendor issue service; OpenCDE Documents API for CDE exchange instead of a vendor cloud. Open standards (buildingSMART OpenCDE APIs).
    D7-12 Positioning storage Shared coordinates stored as standard IfcMapConversion / IfcProjectedCRS, with grid and true north distinguished explicitly. Standard georeferencing that other IFC tools read.
    D7-13 Compaction No compaction command: files are always written in full. IFC files have no free-space fragmentation.
    D7-14 Model history Restore creates a new revision; history is never rewritten. Auditable history; nothing is lost.

    Open questions.

    # Question
    Q6-1 ~~Minimum supported BIMserver version~~: resolved, the latest stable release, currently 1.5.188 (TECH_STACK §5, decision 7). Still open: confirmation on 1.5.188 of every method marked "(verify)": serialiser and deserialiser lookup, checkinSync/initiateCheckin and the /upload endpoint, the /download and /stream endpoints, getAllExtendedDataOfRevision, registerNewExtendedDataOnRevisionHandler, compare, and query support for partial downloads (TECH_STACK §5, open decision 7).
    Q6-2 Behaviour and performance of full-model check-ins for very large projects; whether LowLevelInterface object-level transactions should be used for small syncs (TECH_STACK §3.7.1 notes this as "to verify").
    Q6-3 Ordering guarantee of extended-data object ids on concurrent writes (the deterministic chain of COL-OWN-002 assumes ids are allocated in attach order). If not guaranteed, use server timestamps plus a client tie-break.
    Q6-4 Whether IFC4X3 deserialisers are available on BIMserver 1.5.188, the target release (TECH_STACK §3.7.3).
    Q6-5 ~~Whether to ship the optional enforcement plugin~~ Resolved (owner, 2026-10-12): no. Ownership follows what BIMserver supports, which is advisory only; COL-OWN-004 is deferred (P3).
    Q6-6 Size limits for RXD-embedded issues with many snapshots; whether snapshots should move to BIMserver extended data or an external store when large.
    Q6-7 ~~Chapter numbering~~ Resolved: the file is now 06_collaboration_coordination.md, matching the overview.
